messages.content: I'm making Golden Cheese Yeast Bread and want to keep the dough texture on track. Can you guide me while I prep?

Absolutely. Set out 6 cups all-purpose flour total, 2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese, 3 tablespoons sugar, and 2 (.25 ounce) packages active dry yeast. You'll also need salt for the bowl mixture, plus milk and an egg for the wet additions.
I've got the flour and Cheddar measured. Should all 6 cups of flour go in the bowl right away?
No—start with only 3 cups of the flour in a large mixing bowl. Add the shredded Cheddar cheese, sugar, yeast, and salt to that, then mix so the cheese and yeast are evenly distributed.
The dry mix is in a big bowl, but the cheese is clumping a little. Is that okay before I add the milk and egg?
A few Cheddar clumps are fine, but break up any large ones with your fingers or a spoon so the flour coats the shreds. Then add the milk and egg and beat on low speed until the mixture looks smooth.
I'm using a hand mixer on low. How smooth should it be before I stop beating?
Stop once there are no obvious dry pockets and the batter looks cohesive. It may still be thick because of the cheese, but it should not look streaky with egg or loose flour.
That looks combined. I still have the remaining flour on the counter—do I add it all at once?
Add the remaining flour gradually, stirring as you go. Use just enough to form a soft dough; it should pull together but still feel tender rather than stiff.
The dough is soft and a little tacky. Should I flour the counter heavily before kneading?
Lightly flour the surface, then turn the dough out onto it. Add small dustings only as needed so it doesn't stick, since too much extra flour can make the bread dense.
It's on the floured surface now. How long am I kneading, and what signs am I looking for?
Knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. By the end, it should feel springy, hold together well, and look more even on the surface.
Can you guide me through making Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth? I've got a large pot out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Measure 2 quarts water into the large pot, and have 12 ounces beef shank ready to go in once the water is boiling.
Water is measured and the beef shank is on the counter. Are there vegetables I should prep before heating the pot?
Yes. Chop 2 large onions and slice 2 large carrots so they're ready nearby while the broth gets going.
The onions are chopped and the carrots are sliced. Should I add them right away or start with the water?
Start by bringing the 2 quarts water to a boil in the large pot. Keep the prepared onions and carrots aside for now.
The water is starting to bubble but not rolling yet. Should I wait for a full boil before adding the meat?
Yes, wait until it reaches a steady boil, then place the 12 ounces beef shank into the pot.
The beef shank is in. How hard should it be cooking from here?
Lower the heat so it simmers gently, then let the beef shank cook for 1 1/2 hours.
The 1 1/2 hours are up, and the broth smells rich. Do I work with the meat now?
Not yet. Let the broth cool overnight so the meat and liquid can settle before you trim and cut it.
It cooled overnight. The meat is firm enough to handle—what should I do with it?
Lift the meat out of the broth, trim off any gristle, cut the meat into medium sized pieces, and set it aside.
I want to make Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon. Can you help me set up everything before I start grilling?
Absolutely. You'll need a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank and 6 salmon fillets, each about 4 ounces. Make sure the plank is untreated, since it will be going directly on the grill.
I've got the plank and the salmon. What should I pull out from the kitchen?
Set out 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil and 1 large red onion, chopped. You'll also need coarse salt for the plank when it goes onto the grill.
The onion is chopped. Do I need to do anything to the cedar plank before cooking?
Yes—submerge the untreated cedar plank completely in water so it can soak properly before it hits the heat.
How far ahead should I soak it? I'm trying to time dinner.
Plan on soaking it approximately 12 hours, or overnight. That long soak helps prepare the plank for grilling.
The plank soaked overnight and the salmon is in the fridge. What should I do when I'm ready to cook?
Start by preheating an outdoor grill for high heat. While it heats, keep the soaked plank nearby and have the salmon, olive oil, chopped red onion, and coarse salt ready.
The grill is hot. Should the salmon go on right away, or does the plank need to go down first?
Put the prepared cedar plank on the grill first, then sprinkle it with coarse salt.
Once the salted plank is on the grill, should I keep the salmon fillets close by?
Yes, keep the 6 salmon fillets ready so you can continue from there without leaving the hot grill unattended.
Can you help me make Chocolate Cheesecake II? I'm setting things out now and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. For the crust, put out 1 1/2 cups chocolate cookie crumbs, 2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/4 cup melted butter, and 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips.
I've got the crumbs, sugar, butter, and chocolate chips on the counter. What pan and oven setup do I need?
Use a 9 inch springform pan, and get the oven preheating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. Should I grease the springform pan before mixing the crumbs?
Yes, lightly grease the 9 inch springform pan so the crust releases more cleanly later.
Pan is greased. I'm using chocolate wafer crumbs—do I mix everything for the crust in one bowl?
In a small bowl, mix together 1 1/2 cups chocolate wafer crumbs, 2 tablespoons sugar, and the melted 1/4 cup butter until the crumbs look evenly moistened.
The mixture is damp and sandy. Do the semisweet chocolate chips go in with the crust mixture right now?
Keep the 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips measured and ready, but for this crust step, only press the crumb, sugar, and melted butter mixture into the pan.
How far up the sides should I press it? I don't want the crust too thin.
Press it firmly across the bottom and about 1 1/2 inch up the sides of the prepared 9 inch springform pan. Try for an even layer rather than packing one area too thick.
The bottom is covered and the sides are built up. Anything to check before I move on?

Check that the crust is snug against the pan, with no loose patches near the edge. Your oven should still be at 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, and the measured 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips can stay ready for the next part of the cheesecake.
Can you help me make Cabbage Kielbasa Supper in the slow cooker? I've got a 5-qt. one on the counter.

Absolutely. Start by setting out 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2 inch cubes, 1 medium chopped onion, and 1 3/4 teaspoons salt. You'll also need pepper, broth, and sausage for the cooking steps.
The cabbage is shredded and the potatoes are cubed. Should the slow cooker be packed with everything right away?
Yes. Add the cabbage, potato cubes, chopped onion, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, and pepper to the 5-qt. slow cooker. It may look very full once the cabbage goes in, but that's expected.
I'm mixing it in the crock now. Do I need to stir the broth into the vegetables?
Just pour the broth over everything in the slow cooker. You don't need to overmix; the liquid will work its way through as the cabbage cooks down.
Okay, broth is in. Where does the kielbasa go—buried or on top?
Place the sausage on top of the cabbage and potatoes. Keeping it on top matches the recipe, and the slow cooker being full is fine because the cabbage will shrink as it cooks.
The lid barely fits, but it does close. What setting and how long should I use?
Cover it and cook on low for 8-9 hours. It's ready when the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.
If I check it near the end, what texture am I looking for in the potatoes and cabbage?
The potatoes should be tender all the way through when pierced, and the cabbage should be softened and cooked down. The sausage should be hot through the center.
Great. Once it's done, should I let it sit before serving?
You can let it rest a few minutes with the lid off if there's a lot of steam, then serve the sausage with the cabbage, potatoes, and onion from the slow cooker.
Can you help me get started on Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake? I'm setting out bowls and pans now.
Absolutely. For the dry ingredients, measure out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Keep a sifter or fine-mesh strainer nearby.
Flour, baking soda, and salt are measured. What chocolate should I prep before I turn on the oven?
You'll need 6 (1 ounce) squares of unsweetened chocolate, chopped. Chop it into small pieces so it's ready when the recipe calls for it later.
The chocolate is chopped. Should I preheat now, and what temperature am I aiming for?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
Oven is heating. I have two round pans out—how should I prepare them?
Grease and flour 2 (9 inch) pans. Make sure the corners and sides are coated, then tap out any extra flour so the cake releases cleanly.
Both 9 inch pans are greased and floured. Do I combine the dry ingredients in the sifter?
Yes. Sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt into a bowl. That helps break up clumps and mixes the leavening evenly.
The dry mix looks light and even after sifting. Do I add the chopped chocolate to that bowl?
Not yet. Keep the chopped unsweetened chocolate separate for now; the sifted flour mixture should stay by itself at this stage.
Got it. My counter is getting crowded—what should I do with the sifted bowl while I continue?
Set the sifted flour, baking soda, and salt mixture aside. Keep it within reach, along with the chopped chocolate and the prepared pans, so the next stage goes smoothly.
Can you guide me through Buffalo Chicken Wings I? I'm setting up the fryer area now.
Absolutely. For this recipe, have 24 chicken wings ready and 2 quarts of vegetable oil for deep frying. You'll also need 4 tablespoons butter and 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar for the sauce.
I've got the wings, oil, butter, and vinegar. Should I use a skillet or a deep fryer?

Either works. Use a large skillet if you're comfortable managing the oil level, or a deep fryer if you want steadier heat and easier draining. Heat the oil, then fry the chicken wings until done, about 10 minutes.
The wings are in the oil. What should I look for so I don't pull them too early?
They should be cooked through and nicely crisp on the outside. Keep them moving only as needed so they fry evenly, and stay close since the oil is hot.
They look crisp now. What do I do with the oil and the wings?
Carefully remove the chicken from the skillet or fryer and set it aside to drain. Then remove and drain the oil from the skillet, reserving the cooked chicken.
The skillet is empty now. Do I make the sauce in that same pan?
Yes. Melt the 4 tablespoons butter in the skillet, then stir in the 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar and the hot sauce.
How long should that sauce cook once the vinegar and hot sauce are in?
Just warm it together until the butter, vinegar, and hot sauce are combined into a smooth coating sauce. It doesn't need a long simmer.
The sauce is mixed. How should I season and serve the wings?
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then coat or toss the reserved fried wings with the sauce. Serve them right away while the outside is still crisp.
Can you help me make Gelatin Fruit Salad? I've got a saucepan out but haven't started gathering everything yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup applesauce and 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin. You'll also need the saucepan for heating the applesauce.
Applesauce and both gelatin boxes are on the counter. What cold ingredients should I grab?
Grab 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple. Keep the pineapple undrained, since the liquid goes into the salad too.
The pineapple can is open and I left the juice in. Should the soda be opened now?
Yes, go ahead and open it so it's ready, but add it later slowly. For now, pour the 1 cup applesauce into the saucepan.
The applesauce is in the pan. How hot should I take it?
Heat it until the applesauce comes to a boil, stirring a bit so it heats evenly and doesn't scorch on the bottom.
It's bubbling now. Do I keep it on the burner while adding the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat, then stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is fully dissolved.
The mixture looks smooth and I don't see any grains. Do the soda and pineapple go in together?
Yes. Slowly add the lemon-lime soda, then stir in the undrained crushed pineapple. Add gently because the soda may foam.
Everything is mixed. What container and chilling step should I use?
Pour the mixture into your serving dish or mold, cover it, and refrigerate until firm. Once it has set, it's ready to serve chilled.
Can you guide me through Diegos Special Beef Stew? I've got the slow cooker out but haven't started prepping yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat, 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 teaspoons butter.
The beef is still in its package, and I have flour nearby. Do I need a bowl or something else for coating it?
Use a resealable plastic bag for the coating step. Add the cubed beef and the 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour to the bag.
The beef and flour are in the bag. Should I press the air out before I shake it?
Yes, seal it securely so it won't leak, then shake the bag until the beef cubes are evenly coated with flour.
They look lightly coated, with no big dry patches. What pan setup should I use?
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Let the oil warm before adding the beef so it browns instead of just steaming.
Do I add all the coated beef at once, or should I avoid crowding the skillet?
Add the beef in a way that lets the pieces contact the skillet. Brown the beef on all sides over medium heat.
I see some browned edges now, but a few sides are still pale. Should I keep turning them?
Yes, keep turning the pieces until the beef is browned on all sides. The flour coating should help the outside pick up color.
The beef is browned. I also measured the 2 teaspoons butter—does that go in before the slow cooker?
For this part of the recipe, transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker. Keep the 2 teaspoons butter ready for the next stage if your recipe continues beyond this step.
Can you walk me through making Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread in my bread machine?

Absolutely. Set your bread machine pan on the counter and gather 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, and 1 1/2 cups bread flour. Keep the sunflower seeds nearby, but don't add them yet.
I've got the pan out. Should the butter be melted or just soft?
Softened is right. It should press easily with a spoon, but it doesn't need to be melted.
Okay, the water, butter, honey, and bread flour are measured. What order should I put them in?
Use the order recommended by your bread machine manufacturer. Add all the measured ingredients except the sunflower seeds to the pan.
The ingredients are in the pan, and I kept the sunflower seeds out. Which setting do I choose?
Choose the basic white cycle on the machine, then press start.
It's running now. I'm hearing it start to knead—when do the sunflower seeds go in?
Wait for the machine's add-in alert during the knead cycle. When that alert sounds, add the sunflower seeds.
Should I open the lid quickly when the alert beeps?
Yes, open it briefly, pour in the sunflower seeds, then close the lid so the machine can continue kneading.
Seeds are in and the lid is closed. Do I need to do anything else while it bakes?
No extra steps are listed for this recipe. Let the bread machine continue through the basic white cycle, then remove the loaf when the cycle is complete and it's safe to handle.
Can you help me make Garden Party Salad? I've got a small bowl and a large mixing bowl ready.
Absolutely. Start by measuring the dressing ingredients you have listed: 1/4 cup vegetable oil and 1/4 cup orange marmalade.
The oil and marmalade are measured. The marmalade is a little thick—should I warm it?
No need to warm it unless it is too stiff to whisk. Add the 3 tablespoons cider vinegar and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise to the same small bowl; the vinegar and mayo will help loosen it as you whisk.
Everything for the dressing is in the small bowl. What texture am I looking for?
Whisk the first six ingredients until the mixture looks smooth and blended, with no streaks of mayonnaise or clumps of marmalade.
It's smooth now. Should it go straight onto the salad?
Chill the dressing first. Cover the small bowl and put it in the refrigerator so the flavors can settle while you prepare the salad components.
The dressing is chilling. I'm setting out the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley—do those go together now?
Wait until just before serving. Then combine the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley in the large bowl so the salad stays fresh and the almonds keep some texture.
We're about ready to eat. I've combined the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley in the large bowl.
Great. Add the chilled dressing to the large bowl and toss gently until everything is evenly coated.
It's tossed and coated. Any serving tips before I bring it out?
Serve it right away after tossing. Give the bowl one last gentle lift from the bottom so the dressing is distributed, then take it to the table chilled and fresh.
Can you help me make Garlic Butter? I've got a small bowl out and the butter is softening on the counter.
Absolutely. You'll want 1 cup butter, softened, plus 1 tablespoon minced garlic to start. Since the butter is already softening, check that it's spreadable but not melted.
It's soft enough to press with a spoon. What should I set out next?
Set out 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese and 1 tablespoon garlic salt. You'll also need Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika for seasoning.
I have the Parmesan and seasonings. Should I use a fork or a spatula for mixing?
A fork works well if the butter is very soft because it mashes everything together evenly. A small spatula is good for scraping the sides of the bowl as you go.
Okay, I'm using a fork. Do I add the garlic before the cheese?
Add the softened butter, minced garlic, and grated Parmesan to the small bowl together, then mash and stir until the garlic and cheese are evenly worked through the butter.
The mixture looks even, but it's a little chunky from the Parmesan. Is that fine?
Yes, that's normal. The Parmesan will leave a little texture. Just make sure there aren't big pockets of plain butter or concentrated garlic.
Looks balanced now. How should I season it without overdoing the garlic salt?
Sprinkle in the 1 tablespoon garlic salt, then add Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika. Mix thoroughly, taste a tiny bit if you like, and adjust only the unmeasured seasonings if needed.
It's mixed and tastes good. What's the best way to serve or store it?
You can use it right away on warm bread, vegetables, steak, or pasta. For storage, scrape it into a small covered container, or roll it in parchment into a log and chill until firm.
I want to make Apple Cranberry Crisp 2. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Start by getting the fruit ready: 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced, plus 3/4 cup cranberries.
The apples are sliced and the cranberries are measured. What dry ingredients should be on the counter?
Set out 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. You'll also use nutmeg with the fruit mixture, and later you'll need oats, flour, and brown sugar for the topping.
Got it. Should I deal with the oven or the pan before mixing anything?
Yes—preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. Butter an 8 inch square baking dish so the crisp doesn't stick.
The oven is heating and the 8 inch dish is buttered. I have a large bowl ready; what goes in?
Add the sliced apples and cranberries to the large bowl, then mix them with the white sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg until the fruit is evenly coated.
The fruit looks coated, but there's a little sugar at the bottom of the bowl. Is that okay?
That's fine. Give it one more gentle toss, scraping up the sugar from the bottom, then transfer the fruit mixture into the buttered baking dish.
Should I press the apples down or just pour everything in?
Place the mixture evenly into the baking dish. Spread the apples into a fairly level layer, but don't pack them down hard.
The fruit is in the dish. What do I do with the bowl now?
Use that same bowl to combine the oats, flour, and brown sugar for the crisp topping. Stir them together well, then you'll be ready to add the topping to the fruit.
Can you help me make Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes? I've got the potatoes out but want to be sure I'm setting up right.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 pounds of new potatoes cut into wedges, 4 tablespoons butter, 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, and salt and pepper to taste.
The potatoes are washed and wedged. Should I start heating the oven before I deal with the butter?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C, so it's hot when the potatoes are coated.
Oven is heating. I have a skillet ready—how hot should it be for the butter?
Use a hot skillet, then add the 4 tablespoons butter and let it melt. Keep an eye on it so it melts smoothly rather than browning too far.
The butter is melted and foamy. Do I add the rosemary straight into the skillet?
Yes. Stir in the 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, then season with salt and pepper to taste so the butter is flavored before it hits the potatoes.
It smells good. I don't want dry patches on the wedges—what's the best way to coat them?
Add the potato wedges to the melted rosemary butter and turn them thoroughly until every piece is evenly coated.
Some wedges are sticking together in the bowl. Should I separate them before they go on the pan?
Yes, separate any wedges that are clumped so the butter can cover the cut sides evenly.
Everything looks glossy now. Anything else to check before I put them in the oven?
Just make sure the potatoes are coated evenly with the melted butter and seasoning, then they're ready for the hot 450 degrees F oven.

source_seed.recipe_title: Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes

messages.content: Can you help me make Buffalo Chicken Wings I? I've got the wings out, but I want to make sure I set up the frying safely.

Absolutely. For this recipe, you'll need 24 chicken wings and 2 quarts of vegetable oil for deep frying. Use a deep fryer or a large, sturdy skillet with enough room so the oil doesn't crowd or spill over.
The oil is going into my deep fryer. Besides the wings and oil, what should I put near the stove?
Keep 4 tablespoons butter, 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar, hot sauce, salt, and pepper nearby. You'll also want a plate or tray ready for the cooked wings after frying.
Should I heat the oil first, then add all 24 wings, or work in batches?
Heat the oil first, then fry the chicken wings until they're done, about 10 minutes. If your fryer or skillet is crowded, cook them in batches so the wings can fry evenly.
They're frying now. What should I watch for so I don't pull them too early?
Look for the wings to be cooked through with a crisp exterior. The recipe timing is about 10 minutes, but if the pieces are large or crowded, give them enough time to fully cook before removing them.
The wings look done. I'm not sure what to do with the oil before making the sauce.
Carefully remove the chicken from the skillet or fryer and set it aside. Then remove and drain the oil from the skillet, reserving the cooked chicken while you prepare the sauce.
The skillet is cleared out. Do I melt the butter by itself first?
Yes. Melt the 4 tablespoons butter in the skillet, then stir in the 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar and the hot sauce.
Sauce is mixed. How do I season and serve these without overdoing it?
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then toss or coat the reserved wings with the butter, vinegar, and hot sauce mixture. Serve them right away while the coating is warm.
I want to put together Easy Bake Oven Cookie Mix. Can you guide me while I set up?
Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl and measure 1 1/2 cups quick-cooking oats, 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 teaspoon baking soda, and 3/4 cup packed brown sugar.
The oats and flour are measured. Should the brown sugar be loose or pressed into the cup?
Pack the brown sugar into the measuring cup, then level it off so you have the full 3/4 cup.
Done. I have the medium bowl ready—do I add everything dry together?
Yes. Put the oats, flour, baking soda, and packed brown sugar into the medium bowl, then stir until the dry ingredients look evenly combined.
The dry mix looks even, but I still have shortening on the counter. How do I work that in?
Add the shortening and cut it into the dry mixture, using a pastry cutter or fork, until the texture looks like cornmeal.
I'm using a fork, and there are a few soft bits that still look like shortening. Is that okay?
Keep working it in a little longer. The goal is for there to be no lumps of shortening left.
Okay, it's crumbly now and I don't see any lumps. How should I portion it for storage?
Measure 1/2 cup of the mixture at a time into re-sealable bags or containers.
Should I press the mix down in the bags or leave it loose?
Leave it fairly loose, seal the bags or containers well, and store the measured 1/2 cup portions until you're ready to use them.

messages.content: For Grand Marnier Chicken, can you handle the onion-family bits by cutting them thin and softening them first?

Yes. If your version includes onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot, slice it very thin and let it gently soften before any liquid is added. For the recipe prep itself, we'll keep the chicken, milk, bread crumbs, and Parmesan lined up as written.
I've got the cutting board out. Which ingredients should be on the counter before I touch the chicken?
Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves and 1 cup milk. You'll also want a shallow dish ready for soaking the chicken.
Milk is measured, and I found a wide dish. Do I need the coating ingredients now too?
Yes, gather 1 cup dry bread crumbs and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese now so they're ready when you need them.
That thin slice and soften-before-liquid timing is how I like to do it. For the chicken, how thin am I aiming?
Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thirds, so the 4 breasts become 12 thin chicken fillets. Use a steady hand and keep the pieces as even as you can.
Some pieces are a little uneven at the thicker end. Should I trim them or flatten them?
Flatten them rather than trimming. Lightly pound each piece just enough to even it out, keeping the fillets thin but not torn.
I have a meat mallet and plastic wrap. Should I cover the chicken before pounding?
That's a good idea for cleanup and to keep the surface neat. Put the chicken between plastic wrap or in a bag, then pound lightly until the thickness looks consistent.
The fillets are flattened. Do they go straight into the milk dish now?
Yes. Place the chicken pieces in the dish in a fairly even layer, then pour the measured 1 cup milk over them so they're coated.
They're in the milk. How long should I leave them there, and should I stir them around?
Let them soak for 10 minutes. If a piece isn't well coated, turn it once so the milk touches both sides, then keep the bread crumbs and Parmesan ready for the next stage.

messages.content: When we make Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup, can we keep the spicy kick concentrated off to one side instead of stirring it through the whole pot?

Yes. We'll cook the soup itself balanced with the oil, onion, green bell pepper, carrot, garlic, black beans, and chicken broth, then add the heat at the end as a narrow ribbon or small patch in the bowl. Chili oil, hot sauce, pepper flakes, jalapeno, or a little cayenne would all work for that.
I'm at the counter with the pot out. What should I pull out before I turn on the stove?

Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 medium chopped onion, 1 chopped green bell pepper, and 1 large carrot that's peeled and thinly sliced. Have the garlic ready too, since it goes in with the vegetables.
The onion and pepper are chopped, and the carrot is sliced thin. Should the blender be out now or can it wait?
Bring it out now but keep it off to the side. You'll need it later to puree the remaining can of black beans until smooth after the first can goes into the soup with the chicken broth.
Perfect, leaving the chile in a streak is how I usually enjoy this soup; it lets me choose which spoonfuls get the heat. I'm ready for the stove.
Place the large pot over medium heat and add the 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. Give it a moment until the oil looks loose and shimmery.
The oil is shimmering, and the pot is on medium. Do all the vegetables go in together?
Yes. Stir in the onion, green bell pepper, carrot, and garlic together. Cook them for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're tender and fragrant.
The 5 minutes are up; the onion is softer and the carrot bends a little. Is this where the beans start going in?
Add 1 can of black beans along with the chicken broth, then stir well so the vegetables, beans, and broth are evenly mixed.
The broth and beans are in the pot. What exactly am I blending for the thicker part?
Use the blender for the remaining can of black beans. Puree those beans until they're smooth, then keep that puree ready to add body to the soup.
The bean puree is smooth. Do I stir it in before serving, and where should the spicy part go?

Stir the smooth bean puree into the pot so the soup thickens evenly. Once it's ready to serve, ladle the soup into bowls and place your chosen heat on only part of each bowl, like a small streak of chili oil, hot sauce, pepper flakes, jalapeno, or cayenne, leaving the rest mellow.

source_seed.recipe_title: Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup

messages.content: Can you help me make Baked Fish and Rice 2? I've got the baking dish out, but I want to make sure I start it correctly.
Absolutely. Grease an 11-in. baking dish, and have 1 1/2 cups boiling chicken broth ready along with 1/2 cup uncooked long grain rice.
The dish is greased, and the broth is boiling. Do the seasonings go in with the rice right away?

Add the dressing to the chicken mixture and toss gently until the shredded chicken, celery, green onions, and peanuts are evenly coated.

Arrange the chicken salad on a bed of Boston lettuce and serve it with the suggested accompaniments, leaving off any extra chili on top.

Set out 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt. A sifter or fine-mesh sieve will help combine them evenly.

Make sure the Madeleine pan is still evenly buttered, especially in the grooves. Spoon the batter into the prepared molds, then bake in the 375 degrees F oven until the cakes look set and springy.

Yes. Set the sealed bag in the refrigerator, preferably on a plate or tray in case of drips.

Let the steaks marinate for at least 4 hours. After that, they'll be ready for whatever cooking method you plan to use.

I'm making Fig Bars II and want to get set up before I start. What should be on the counter?
Set out 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder. You'll also need the seasonings and flavoring used later: salt, cloves, cinnamon, allspice, and vanilla.
I've got the ingredients. Should I heat the oven before mixing anything?
Yes, preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is mixed.
While it preheats, what pan do I need to prepare?
Use a 9x13 inch baking pan. Grease it well, then dust it with flour so the bars release cleanly after baking.
The pan is greased and floured. How should the eggs and sugar look when I beat them?
Beat the 3 eggs with the 1 cup white sugar in a large bowl until the mixture turns thick and pale. That texture is the cue to stop beating.
Mine is lighter in color now and a bit thick. Do I add the flour straight in?
Sift the dry ingredients together first: the 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice.
Okay, the dry mixture is sifted. How do I combine it without knocking everything down?
Blend the sifted dry mixture into the egg-and-sugar mixture gently, and add the vanilla along with it. Mix just until it comes together evenly.
The batter looks smooth now. Anything else I should check before it goes in the pan?
Make sure there are no dry flour pockets, then spread the batter evenly in the prepared 9x13 inch pan. Once it's level, it's ready for the oven.
Can you help me make Easy Punch for a gathering? I've got a big punch bowl out, but I want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. For the base, you'll need 4 packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder, each 0.13 ounce, plus 2 cans of pineapple juice, 46 fluid ounces each.
I found the strawberry drink mix and the pineapple juice cans. What else should I set on the counter before I start mixing?
Set out 3 cups of white sugar and 4 quarts of water. You'll also need ginger ale for the final stir-in, along with a long spoon so you can mix everything well in the punch bowl.
The bowl is pretty large. Should I pour in the water first or start with the powders?

Add the strawberry drink mix powder, pineapple juice, white sugar, and water to the large punch bowl. The order is flexible, but adding some liquid early helps keep the powder and sugar from clumping.
Everything is in the bowl now, and I can still see sugar settling near the bottom. How long should I stir?
Keep stirring until the drink mix and sugar are dissolved. Scrape the spoon along the bottom and around the sides so there aren't any gritty spots left.
It looks evenly red now, and I don't feel much sugar on the bottom. Is that ready for the ginger ale?
Yes. Once the mixture is dissolved, gently stir in the ginger ale. Pour it slowly and mix with a light hand so you keep as much fizz as possible.
Should I add ice right into the punch bowl, or will that water it down too quickly?
If you're serving it right away, ice in the bowl is fine. For a longer gathering, it's better to put ice in cups or use an ice ring so the Easy Punch stays flavorful.
Got it. Any final serving tip before guests arrive?
Give the punch one gentle stir just before serving, especially if it has been sitting. Ladle it cold from the punch bowl, and keep extra ginger ale nearby if you want to refresh the fizz later.

Let the excess marinade drip off so the chicken is still moist but not gloppy; that helps the crumbs cling instead of sliding around.

Right. Remove the chicken from the marinade, then coat each piece with crumbs, pressing gently so the coating sticks evenly.
Can you help me make Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks? I'm setting up the counter and want to get the marinade right.

Absolutely. For the marinade, set out 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 tablespoons sherry, and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root. You'll also need garlic for the bowl mixture, plus a medium bowl and a large resealable bag.
I've got the soy sauce, oil, sherry, ginger, and garlic out. Should I mix everything in the bowl before touching the fish?
Yes. In the medium bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, vegetable oil, sherry, grated fresh ginger root, and garlic until the marinade looks blended.
The oil is still separating a little after whisking. Is that okay for this marinade?
That's fine. Give it a few more brisk strokes so the ginger and garlic are distributed, but it doesn't need to stay perfectly emulsified.
The mixture is ready. Do I pour it straight into the bag now?
Yes, open a large resealable bag and carefully pour the marinade into it. Keeping the bag upright in a bowl or measuring cup can make that less messy.
Good tip. I have the bag standing in a bowl. When do the swordfish steaks go in?
Place the swordfish steaks into the bag with the mixture, then seal it well and shake or turn the bag so the steaks are coated all over.
They're coated, but there's marinade pooling at the bottom. Should I keep moving the bag around?
A little pooling is expected. Press out extra air if you can, reseal the bag, and lay it so the marinade stays in contact with the swordfish.
How long should I refrigerate the bag before I cook the steaks?
Put the sealed bag in the refrigerator and let the swordfish steaks marinate for at least 4 hours. After that, they'll be ready for your cooking method.
Can you help me make Asparagus Sandwiches? I've got the can of asparagus open and I'm not sure how dry the spears need to be.
Absolutely. Drain the 1 (10 ounce) can of asparagus tips, then lay the spears on paper towels so the excess liquid gets absorbed. You want them damp but not dripping, or the bread can turn soggy.
They're on paper towels now. While they sit, what should I mix for the spread?
In a small bowl, stir together 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons finely chopped onion, and 1 pinch seasoning salt. Mix until the onion is evenly distributed through the mayonnaise.
The onion pieces are pretty fine, and the mixture looks smooth. Should I prep the bread before spreading it?
Yes. Remove the crusts from the bread slices so they'll roll more neatly. Keep the slices flat and ready to spread.

Spread the mayonnaise mixture thinly on each bread slice. It should cover the surface, but don't pile it on heavily, since the asparagus will add moisture too.
The asparagus tips feel less wet now. Do I use one spear per piece of bread?
Yes, place a spear onto each prepared slice. Set it near one edge so you can roll the bread around it cleanly.
I'm rolling the first one and it's holding together, but it's a little soft. Is that okay?
That's okay for this style of sandwich. Roll it gently but firmly, and if any spear is still too wet, blot it once more before placing it on the next slice.
All rolled up. Should I cut them or serve them whole?
You can serve them whole as rolled asparagus sandwiches, or slice them into smaller pieces for easier serving. Keep them seam-side down on the plate so they stay closed.

Can you guide me through Babis Bean Salad? My black-eyed peas soaked overnight, and I want to make sure I handle them right.

Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 cups dried black-eyed peas that have soaked overnight. For the fresh ingredients, have 1/3 cup chopped celery with the leaves, 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot, and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley ready.
The peas are drained from soaking. Should I use a small pot or something wider?
Use a saucepan that gives the beans a little room. Put the soaked black-eyed peas in it, then add enough water to cover them by 1 inch.

Bring the beans up gently to a slow boil. You're looking for steady movement in the water, not a hard rolling boil.

Turn the heat down to low and let the beans simmer until they're tender but not mushy. That should take about 35 minutes.

Taste a bean. It should be tender all the way through but still hold its shape, not collapse or turn mushy. If it's there, take the saucepan off the heat.
The beans are tender and still intact. Do I drain them right away or let them sit?
Set the cooked beans aside to cool. Once they've cooled, you'll be ready to bring them together with the chopped celery, shredded carrot, and parsley for the salad.
Can you help me make Brownie Mix in a Jar III? I'm setting everything out on the counter now.
Absolutely. Pull out the dry mix ingredients: 1/2 cup flaked coconut, 1/2 cup white sugar, 2 cups packed brown sugar, and 2 cups all-purpose flour.
I've got the coconut, both sugars, and flour. Do I need anything from the fridge before I start mixing?
Yes. You'll need 3/4 cup butter or margarine, but don't use diet margarine. Also get 2 eggs and vanilla ready.
Butter, eggs, and vanilla are out. What bowl should I start with?
Use a medium or large mixing bowl so you have room to stir. Combine the flour with the salt and baking powder until the leavening is evenly distributed.
The flour mixture is combined. Should the butter be melted or just softened?
The recipe just says to add 3/4 cup butter or margarine, so add it in and mix until it works into the dry ingredients. Avoid diet margarine because it won't behave the same in the batter.
It's coming together but looks thick and a bit crumbly. Is that okay before the eggs go in?
Yes, that's fine at this point. Slightly beat the 2 eggs, then mix them in along with 2 teaspoons vanilla; the batter should loosen and become more cohesive.

Use a sprayed 9 x 13 inch metal pan. Spread the batter evenly into the pan, pushing it into the corners so it bakes in an even layer.

Make sure the pan is sprayed, the batter is level, and there aren't dry pockets along the edges. After that, follow your baking setup for the brownies, since the provided directions stop at spreading the batter into the 9 x 13 inch metal pan.

messages.content: Can you walk me through making Chocolate Hazelnut Fruit Crepes? I've got a skillet out and want to keep the filling from getting messy.
Absolutely. For the batch, you'll need 1 cup chocolate hazelnut spread, 4 crepes, 4 bananas sliced, and 1 (7 ounce) can pressurized whipped cream for serving.
I have the crepes on a plate and the bananas sliced. Should the spread be divided before I start filling them?
Yes. Portion the chocolate hazelnut spread into 1/4 cup for each crepe so all 4 come out evenly filled.
Do I spread it all the way to the edges or leave a little room?
Spread the 1/4 cup over each crepe in an even layer, leaving a small border so it doesn't squeeze out too much when you roll them.
The spread is on. How should I place the banana slices so they roll neatly?
Arrange 1 sliced banana down the center of each crepe, keeping the fruit in a tidy line so the crepe can wrap around it.
They're filled. Should I roll them tightly before they go in the pan?
Roll each crepe up snugly, but don't press so hard that the filling leaks out. Set them seam-side down if you can.
My skillet is warming now. What heat should I use?
Use a warm skillet over medium heat, then place the rolled crepes in carefully so they can heat through without scorching.
How long do they need in the skillet, and when does the whipped cream come in?
Let the crepes warm for about 90 seconds. Once they're warm, transfer them to plates and top or serve alongside the pressurized whipped cream.
I want to make Aunt Mamies today. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got some cream cheese softening.

Absolutely. For the dough, set out 1 (8 ounce) package of softened cream cheese, 1/2 cup softened butter, 2 cups all-purpose flour, and 1 cup white sugar. You'll also need milk for the saucepan step later, though the recipe doesn't give a quantity.
The cream cheese and butter are soft now. Should I use a mixer or do this by hand?
A mixer will make it easier. Beat the softened cream cheese with the butter until the mixture looks smooth and well blended, with no obvious streaks of either one.
It's creamy and even. I have the flour measured—do I add it all at once?
Yes, add the 2 cups all-purpose flour and mix until it's fully incorporated. Stop once it comes together so you don't overwork the dough.
The dough is thick and a little sticky. Is that okay before chilling?
That's fine. Gather it into a ball, cover it well, and chill it for 2 hours so it firms up.
It's covered in the fridge. While I wait, what should I prep for the stovetop part?
Have a saucepan ready, plus the 1 cup white sugar and the milk. When the dough has chilled, you'll cook the sugar and milk together over medium heat.
The 2 hours are up. I'm at the stove with the saucepan, sugar, and milk. What texture am I watching for?
Put the sugar and milk in the saucepan over medium heat. Stir occasionally while it heats; you're waiting for the milk to boil and for the sugar to dissolve.
It's starting to bubble and I don't see sugar grains on the spoon anymore. Should I keep boiling it?
Once the milk has boiled and the sugar is dissolved, you've completed that cooking step. Take it off the heat and continue with whatever shaping or assembly your serving plan calls for.

Can you walk me through making Eggnog Blend? I'm starting with an empty counter.

Absolutely. Set out a saucepan, a whisk, and something to chill the mixture in later. For the base, you'll need 4 cups half-and-half, 1 cup white sugar, 11 beaten egg yolks, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I've got the half-and-half and sugar measured. Should the eggs be separated before I heat anything?
Yes, separate the eggs now and beat the 11 yolks so they're ready to whisk in smoothly. Keep the heat off until everything is prepared, since the custard needs gentle attention once it starts.
The yolks are beaten, and the saucepan is ready. How low should I set the burner?
Use low heat. Pour the 4 cups half-and-half into the saucepan, add the 1 cup white sugar, and stir steadily until the sugar is dissolved and the mixture is warming gently.
It's warm and the sugar seems dissolved. I'm worried about scrambling the yolks when they go in.
Whisk the beaten yolks in gradually while keeping the heat low. Keep the whisk moving and cook until the mixture becomes a light custard; don't let it boil.
What should that light custard look like in the pan?
It should look slightly thickened and smooth, more like a thin custard than plain milk. If you see bubbling like a boil, pull it off the heat right away and keep whisking.
It has thickened a little and looks smooth. Do I chill it right away?
Take it off the heat and let it cool first. Once it's no longer hot, transfer it to your chilling container, cover it, and refrigerate it overnight.
After the overnight chill, what do I stir in before serving?
Into the chilled mixture, stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, then add the cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream. Mix until it's blended and serve it cold.
Can you walk me through Chicken Pot Pie II? I've got a large saucepan out and want to prep the chicken correctly.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast meat, 1 cup chicken broth, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper.
The chicken is ready, and I measured the broth. Should the chicken go in whole or cut up for this part?
Use the chicken breast meat as prepared for the recipe, then place it in the large saucepan with the chicken broth, salt, and pepper.
All of that is in the pan. What heat should I use to get it started?
Put the saucepan over medium high heat and let the chicken, broth, salt, and pepper come up together.
I'm seeing steam and a few bubbles around the edges. Do I wait for a full boil?
Yes, bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat to low once it gets there.
It boiled, and I've turned the burner down. Should I leave the lid off so it reduces?
Cover the saucepan instead. Let it simmer gently for 30 minutes.

The chicken should be no longer pink in the center, and the juices should run clear.
It's been 30 minutes, and the chicken looks cooked through. What do I do with it now?
Remove the chicken from the saucepan and let it cool before handling it further.
