Add a small spoonful of the brine to the warm pan for flavor, but keep the chopped pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini themselves out of the burritos.
Perfect, that's the special version I want tonight. I have the burritos still frozen; what should I pull out first?
Get out 6 frozen prepared bean and cheese burritos, plus 2 tablespoons butter or margarine for the sauce base.
Butter is on the counter and the burritos are still wrapped. What dry and liquid ingredients do I need before I start heating anything?
Measure 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and 1 3/4 cups water so they are ready to go in smoothly.
What dish should I grease, and do the burritos go in frozen or thawed?
Grease a 13-in baking dish, place the frozen burritos in it as they are, and set the dish aside while you make the sauce.
The dish is ready. For the sauce, should the butter just soften or fully melt?
Melt the butter or margarine fully in a saucepan over gentle heat, just until it is liquid and ready for the flour.
I don't want lumps. How should I add the flour and water?
Stir the flour into the melted butter until the mixture looks smooth, then gradually stir in the water instead of pouring it all in at once.
The sauce is smooth but thin. How far do I cook it?
Bring it to a boil, then keep cooking and stirring for 2 minutes, or until it thickens.
Where does the brine fit with that warm-pan idea before I serve this batch?
Once the pan is warm, stir in that spoonful of brine for the bright flavor, then keep the solid briny pieces out so the burritos stay smooth and saucy.
Can you help me make Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers? I've got the grill available and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, since those go into the burger mixture together.
Those cheeses are on the counter. I also see an onion in the recipe—how much should I chop?
Chop 1 small onion. You'll also need 1 egg ready to bind the mixture once everything goes into the bowl.
The onion is chopped and the egg is out. Should I heat the grill before mixing the meat?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the grill for high heat so it's hot by the time the patties are shaped.
Grill is heating. What should I put in the mixing bowl before I add the beef?
In a large bowl, combine the Cheddar cheese, Parmesan cheese, chopped onion, egg, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Stir those together first so the seasonings are evenly distributed.
That mixture is ready. When I add the ground beef, should I use a spoon or my hands?
Crumble the ground beef into the bowl, then mix it together by hand. Use a light touch so the burgers don't get packed too tightly.
The beef is mixed in and it looks even. How many patties am I shaping?
Shape the mixture into 6 patties, keeping them as even as you can so they cook at the same pace on the grill.
I've got 6 patties formed. Where does the bacon come in?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty before grilling. Once they're wrapped, they're ready to go onto the hot grill.
I want to make Butterscotch Brownies in a Jar. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and gather the dry mix ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 tablespoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup flaked coconut.
I've got the flour and coconut out. Should I turn on the oven yet or wait until the bowl is ready?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the batter is mixed.
The oven is heating. What size pan should I pull from the cabinet?
Use a 9x13 inch baking pan, and grease it well so the brownies release cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. I'm opening the jar now, and the mix looks a little clumpy.
That's fine. Empty the jar of brownie mix into the large mixing bowl, then stir through it to break up the lumps before adding the wet ingredients.
The dry mix is loosened up. What wet ingredients go in with it?
Add 3/4 cup softened butter, 2 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract to the bowl.
Should the butter be melted, or just soft enough to blend?
Use softened butter, not melted. It should be easy to press and mix into the dry ingredients without turning the batter greasy.
Everything is in the bowl. What texture am I aiming for before it goes into the pan?
Mix until the batter is well blended, with no dry pockets of mix left. Once it looks evenly combined, spread it into the greased 9x13 inch pan.
I want to make Asparagus Sandwiches for a small snack plate. Can you guide me through it?

Absolutely. Start by getting the filling ingredients together: 1 (10 ounce) can of asparagus tips, drained; 1/2 cup mayonnaise; 2 tablespoons finely chopped onion; and a pinch of seasoning salt. You'll also need bread slices for rolling.
The asparagus is drained, but it still looks pretty wet. Should I do anything before mixing the sauce?
Yes—lay the asparagus spears on paper towels for a bit so the extra liquid gets absorbed. That keeps the sandwiches from turning soggy.
While those sit, what bowl or tools should I set out?
Use a small bowl for the spread and a spoon or spatula for mixing. Stir together the mayonnaise, finely chopped onion, and seasoning salt until the onion is evenly distributed.
The spread is mixed. Should it be thick or more loose?
It should be creamy and spreadable, not runny. Since it's mainly mayonnaise with onion and seasoning salt, a thin layer is all you'll need on the bread.
I'm ready with the bread slices. Do I trim them before spreading?
Yes, remove the crusts from the bread slices first. Then spread the mayonnaise mixture thinly over each slice, covering enough of the surface to help the roll hold together.
How much asparagus goes in each one?
Place one asparagus spear on a prepared bread slice, then roll the bread up around it. Keep the roll snug, but don't press so hard that the bread tears.
Do they need cooking or chilling before serving?
No cooking is needed. Once the spears are rolled in the trimmed, lightly spread bread slices, the Asparagus Sandwiches are ready to serve.
Can you walk me through making Chicken Tacos? I've got chicken breasts on the counter and want to prep everything before the skillet heats up.

Absolutely. Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces. Keep nearby 1 cup lemonade, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, a bay leaf, and tortillas for warming later.
The chicken is cut up. Should the skillet be hot before I add the liquids, or do they all go in together?

Set a large skillet over medium heat, then add the chicken along with the lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir so the chicken pieces are coated and spread into an even layer.
It's in the pan now and starting to sizzle lightly. When do the seasonings go in?
Add the garlic powder, onion powder, and bay leaf now. Stir them through the liquid so the seasoning distributes around the chicken as it begins to simmer.
The liquid is bubbling gently. Should I cover the skillet or leave it open?
Let it simmer uncovered over medium heat unless it starts reducing too quickly. You're cooking until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, which should take 15 to 20 minutes.
I'm about halfway through that window. How can I tell the pieces are cooking evenly?
Give the skillet an occasional stir and turn any larger pieces so they spend time in the simmering liquid. The chicken should look opaque all the way through, with no pink in the center.
The chicken looks cooked through and the sauce has tightened a bit. What should I do with the tortillas?
Warm the tortillas until soft, either in the oven or the microwave. Keep them just pliable and warm so they can fold around the chicken without cracking.
Tortillas are warm. Should I remove anything from the skillet before serving?
Take out the bay leaf, then spoon the hot chicken into the softened tortillas. Add any taco toppings you like, and serve while the filling and tortillas are still warm.
I'm making Black Bean Lasagna Rolls. Can you help me get set up before I start boiling anything?
Absolutely. Put a pot of water on for the noodles and gather 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, and 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta cheese.
I've got the cheeses and noodles out. Is there anything canned I should open now?
Yes, open 1 (4.5 ounce) can of chopped green chiles and drain it well. You'll also want your black beans ready for spooning over the filling later.
The water is heating. Should I add oil or salt to keep the noodles from sticking?
Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, but omit both salt and fat. Stir gently as they cook, then drain them well when they're done.
The noodles are drained and a little slippery. Should I lay them flat?
Yes, lay them out flat so they're easier to fill. If they're very wet, blot them lightly so the cheese mixture will spread instead of sliding around.
While they cool enough to handle, how do I make the filling?
Combine the Monterey Jack, the ricotta, the drained green chiles, and the next ingredients called for in the recipe, stirring until the mixture is well blended.
The filling looks creamy with the chiles mixed through. How much should go on each noodle?
Divide the cheese mixture among the 8 noodles and spread it over one side of each noodle, leaving just a small edge so it doesn't squeeze out too much when rolled.
The noodles are covered on one side. Where do the black beans go?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on each noodle. Once they're evenly covered, you'll be ready to roll them up for the next part of the dish.
Can you help me make Caramelized Apple Bites? I've got the apples out but want to be sure I prep everything right.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrapped and chopped, plus 2 tablespoons light corn syrup and 2 apples.
The caramels are unwrapped. Should I chop them before they go into the bowl?
Yes, chop the caramels so they melt more evenly. Put the chopped caramels into a medium microwave-safe bowl with the 2 tablespoons light corn syrup.
Got it. For the apples, do they need to be sliced or smaller than that?
Peel and core the 2 apples, then dice them into bite-size pieces so they'll coat well in the caramel mixture.
The caramel and corn syrup are in the bowl. How long do I microwave them?
Microwave the bowl on high for approximately 30 seconds, just until the caramels are melted with the light corn syrup.
If it still looks a little thick after heating, what should I look for before adding the apples?
Look for the caramels to be melted enough to stir into a smooth coating with the corn syrup. Once it's melted, you're ready for the apples.
The diced apples are ready. Do I add them straight into the warm caramel bowl?
Yes. Place the diced apples in the bowl and toss them until every piece is coated with the caramel and light corn syrup mixture.
They're coated now. Should I serve them warm or wait a bit?
Let the Caramelized Apple Bites cool before serving so the coating settles and they're easier to eat.
I'm making Coq au Vin alla Italiana and have a large skillet ready. Can you talk me through the prep before I start heating anything?
Absolutely. Set out 4 pounds of dark meat chicken pieces, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 5 cloves of crushed garlic, and 1/2 cup all-purpose flour. You'll also need poultry seasoning for the flour.
The chicken is on a tray, and I have the flour in a shallow dish. Should the garlic be divided now?
Yes. Since the skillet starts with only 1/2 of the garlic, separate the crushed garlic into two portions before you begin so it's easy to add the first half right away.
Oil is measured. How hot should the skillet be before I put anything in?
Place the large skillet over the heat and add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil. Let it warm until the oil looks loose and shimmery, but don't let the garlic go in so early that it scorches.
The oil is shimmering now. I'm ready with the garlic.
Add 1/2 of the crushed garlic to the skillet and stir it through the oil briefly so it perfumes the pan.
While that's going, I want to get the coating right. What should I do with the flour?
Season the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour with poultry seasoning, mixing it evenly through the flour so each chicken piece gets a seasoned coating.
The flour is seasoned. Do I coat all the chicken pieces before they go into the skillet?
Dredge the dark meat chicken pieces in the seasoned flour, shaking off the extra so the coating is even rather than clumpy.
They're coated and the skillet still looks ready. How long do I brown them?
Lay the chicken parts into the skillet and brown them for 4 or 5 minutes, turning as needed so the flour coating takes on color without burning.
I'd like to make German Sweet Chocolate Pie. Can you talk me through what to set out before I start?
Absolutely. Put out 1 (4 ounce) bar of German sweet chocolate, chopped, plus 1/3 cup milk. You'll also want a large microwave-safe bowl, a wire whisk, and room to chill the mixture.
The chocolate is chopped and the milk is measured. Are there any cold ingredients I should soften first?
Yes—set out 4 ounces cream cheese so it's softened before you whisk it in. Also measure 2 tablespoons white sugar, and have 3 1/2 cups whipped topping ready for folding later.
My cream cheese feels soft now. How do I melt the chocolate without scorching it?

Combine the chopped chocolate with 2 tablespoons of the milk in the large microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stirring halfway through, and stop when the chocolate is almost melted.
It still has a few soft-looking pieces after stirring. Should I keep heating it?
If the pieces are small and melting as you stir, don't add more time yet. Keep stirring gently until the residual heat smooths it out; the recipe wants it almost melted, not overheated.
The chocolate looks smooth now. What goes into the bowl next?
Whisk in the softened cream cheese, the 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk from your 1/3 cup measure. Beat with the wire whisk until the mixture looks blended and even.
It's blended but a little loose. Is it supposed to firm up before the topping goes in?
Yes. Put the bowl in the refrigerator for 10 minutes so the chocolate-cream cheese mixture can chill slightly before you fold in the topping.
The 10 minutes are up, and the bowl is cool. What's the gentlest way to add the whipped topping?
Add 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping and fold gently, turning the mixture over with light strokes until no streaks remain. Try not to whisk here, so the filling stays airy.
Can you walk me through making 1 Pot 3 Bean Chicken Stew? I'm starting from the counter and want to prep it as I go.

Absolutely. Set a large pot on the stove and gather 1 tablespoon canola oil plus 1 3/4 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into chunks. Keep a plate nearby for the browned chicken.
I've got chicken thighs cut up and the oil measured. Should I chop the vegetables before the pot heats?

Yes, chop 1 large yellow onion and slice 1 cup celery before you start cooking. If you're using carrots too, have them ready along with the broth, beans, tomatoes, wine, bay leaf, and herbs so the stew can come together smoothly.
The onion is chopped and the celery is sliced. I've got the large pot ready—how should I start the chicken?
Warm the canola oil in the large pot over medium to medium-high heat. Add the chicken chunks in a single layer if you can, and brown them on the outside; they don't need to cook through yet.
Some pieces are browning but the pot looks crowded. Is it okay if they touch?
A little touching is fine, but if they're packed tightly and steaming, brown them in batches. You're looking for color on the outside, then transfer the browned chicken to that plate.
The chicken is browned and sitting on the plate. There are browned bits in the pot—do I leave them?
Leave them; they'll add flavor. Add the chopped yellow onion to the pot and sauté until it softens, about 5 minutes, stirring and scraping up the browned bits as it cooks.
The onion is soft now. When do the celery and the rest go in?
Add the broth, beans, tomatoes, sliced celery, carrots, wine, bay leaf, herbs, and all of the browned chicken back into the pot. Stir everything together so the chicken is tucked into the liquid.
Everything is in the pot and it smells good. Should it be uncovered or covered while it cooks?
Cover the pot and let the stew simmer gently for 40 minutes. Keep it at a steady simmer rather than a hard boil, and give it an occasional stir so the beans and vegetables heat evenly.
Can you walk me through making Caramel Chocolate Corn? I've got a big bowl ready but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. For the popcorn mixture, measure out 16 cups popped popcorn and 1 cup roasted peanuts. Keep them nearby while you set up the pans.
I have the popcorn measured, and the peanuts are roasted. What should I set out for the caramel part?
You'll need 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter. The recipe also has you combining the sugar and butter with corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in a microwave-safe bowl.
Should I prep the cookie sheets before mixing anything sticky?
Yes, grease the cookie sheets now so they're ready when the coated popcorn needs to be spread out.
The sheets are greased. Do the popcorn and peanuts go straight on them?
Not yet. Put the popcorn and roasted peanuts into a paper bag together; that gives you room to toss or shake them with the caramel later.
Okay, they're in the paper bag. Should the bag stay open on the counter?
Yes, set the bag aside where it won't tip over while you make the caramel mixture.
I'm ready for the microwave bowl step. What goes in there exactly?
In a microwave-safe bowl, combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt. Use a bowl with extra space so the mixture can bubble without overflowing.
The butter is still in one piece. Is that fine before microwaving?
That's fine. As it heats, the butter will melt into the sugar mixture; just make sure everything is in the microwave-safe bowl before you continue.
Can you walk me through Black Bean and Corn Quesadillas? I want to get the filling started without missing anything.
Absolutely. Set out 2 teaspoons olive oil and 3 tablespoons finely chopped onion for the base of the filling.
Got the oil and onion. What cans should I open and drain?
Open 1 (15.5 ounce) can of black beans, then drain and rinse them. Also drain 1 (10 ounce) can of whole kernel corn.
The beans are rinsed and the corn is drained. Should I use a skillet or a saucepan?
Use a large saucepan. Put it over medium heat and warm the 2 teaspoons olive oil in it.
The oil is warming. When do I add the onion, and what should it look like?
Stir in the finely chopped onion and cook it until softened, about 2 minutes. It should look a little translucent and less sharp.
The onion has softened. Do the beans and corn go in together?
Yes, stir in the drained black beans and drained corn together. Then add the sugar, salsa, and pepper flakes, and mix everything well so the filling is evenly coated.
It's mixed, but some beans are sticking to the bottom. Should I lower the heat?
Keep it around medium, but stir more often and scrape the bottom gently. You're just heating the mixture through, not trying to brown it.
How long should I keep it on the stove before I use it in the quesadillas?
Cook it until heated through, about 3 minutes. Once the filling is hot all the way across, it's ready to spoon into the quesadillas.
I want to make Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth. Can you help me get started and keep the steps manageable?
Absolutely. For this broth, set out 2 quarts water, 12 ounces beef shank, 2 large onions chopped, and 2 large carrots sliced. You'll also want a large pot with enough room for the water and beef.
I've got the pot out. Should the onions and carrots go in right away with the water?
Not yet. Start by pouring the 2 quarts water into the large pot and bringing it to a boil. Keep the chopped onions and sliced carrots ready nearby for later use.
The water is heating now. Do I need a rolling boil before adding the beef shank?
Yes, let the water come to a boil first. Once it's boiling, carefully lower in the 12 ounces beef shank so it can begin cooking in the hot water.
The beef is in the pot. How strong should the heat be while it cooks?
Reduce the heat so the broth simmers rather than boils hard. Let the beef shank simmer for 1 1/2 hours, keeping it gentle and steady.
It's simmering steadily. Should I cover the pot or leave it open?
You can keep it partially covered if you like, as long as the liquid stays at a gentle simmer. The key recipe timing here is that the beef shank simmers for the full 1 1/2 hours.
The simmering time is done. The meat looks cooked but the broth is still hot.
Take the pot off the heat and let it cool. This broth is meant to cool overnight before you handle the meat further.
After it cools overnight, what should I do with the beef?
Lift the meat out of the cooled broth, trim away any gristle, and cut the meat into medium sized pieces. Set those pieces aside while you continue with the broth and vegetables.
I want to make Eggplant Mixed Grill. Can you talk me through what to set out before I start?

Absolutely. Put out 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil. You'll also need vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, garlic, and a large resealable plastic bag for the marinade.
I've got the herbs and oil measured. Which vegetables should I have ready for the bag?
Have the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper prepped and ready to go in once the marinade is mixed.
The bag is open in a bowl so it won't tip over. What goes into the marinade first?
Pour in the olive oil, then add the chopped parsley, oregano, and basil. Mix in the vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic right in the bag.
Should I shake the bag now or wait until the vegetables are inside?
Give the marinade a quick mix now so the herbs, garlic, seasoning, vinegar, and oil are combined, then add the vegetables.
Okay, I'm adding the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and both peppers. Do I need to be gentle with it?
Yes, add them carefully so the bag doesn't tear, then seal it well and turn the bag to coat the vegetables evenly with the marinade.
They're coated. How long should the bag sit, and where should I put it?
Refrigerate the sealed bag for 2 hours. Turn it occasionally during that time so the marinade reaches all the vegetables.
The marinating time is almost done. What should I do at the grill?
Preheat the grill for high heat, then lightly oil the grill grate before the vegetables go on so they're less likely to stick.
I want to make Apple Butter V today. Can you get me set up with the ingredients and the pot I'll need?
Absolutely. Use a Dutch oven, and start with 6 pounds of tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups of apple cider.
The apples are sliced and I have the cider measured. Are there any seasonings or sweeteners I should set out before I start cooking?
Yes—keep 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon nearby for the apple butter.
I've got those on the counter. Should the apples go into the Dutch oven by themselves at this point?
Yes, add the cored, sliced tart apples directly to the Dutch oven.
They're in the pot, and it's pretty full. Do I add the cider all at once or a little at a time?
Pour in all 6 cups of apple cider with the apples.
The cider is in. What heat should I use to get this going?
Bring the apple and cider mixture to a boil, then cook it over medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
After about 30 minutes, what texture am I looking for before I stop cooking it?
The apples should be softened enough that they can be pressed through a food mill without much resistance.
They're soft now. How do I handle the mixture so it turns into apple butter base?
Press the softened apple mixture through a food mill. That will give you the smooth base for Apple Butter V.
I'm making Baked Aloha Chicken and want to get everything lined up before I start. Can you walk me through it?

Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup light corn syrup, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also need the recipe's ginger, corn oil, crushed pineapple with its liquid, and chicken legs.
The lemon juice, corn syrup, soy sauce, and salt are measured. Should I heat the oven before mixing the sauce?
Yes—preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the chicken is sauced.
Oven is coming up to temperature. What bowl step should I do while I wait?
In a bowl, stir together the lemon juice, light corn syrup, soy sauce, salt, ginger, and corn oil until the mixture looks smooth and even.
The sauce is smooth, but it's a little glossy and thin. Is that expected?
That's fine for this sauce. Add the crushed pineapple along with its liquid, then stir so the fruit and juice are evenly mixed through.
Pineapple is mixed in. What kind of dish should I use for the chicken legs?
Use an ovenproof glass baking dish. Arrange the chicken legs in it in a single layer so the sauce can cover them well.
The chicken legs are in the glass dish. Do I pour all the pineapple sauce over them?
Yes, pour the sauce over the top of the chicken legs, spreading the pineapple pieces around so the sauce is distributed across the dish.
All set in the pan. Anything I should check before it goes into the oven?
Make sure the oven has reached 350 degrees F, the chicken is sitting in the ovenproof glass dish, and the sauce is over the top. Then it's ready to bake according to the recipe.
Can you help me make Artichoke Hummus? I've got my food processor out but haven't opened anything yet.

Absolutely. Start by setting up the ingredients: 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, also called garbanzo beans, drained; 1 clove garlic; 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts; and 2 tablespoons lemon juice.
The chickpeas are drained. Should I rinse them too, or just use them as-is?
The recipe only calls for them drained, so you can use them as-is. Add the drained chickpeas to the food processor work bowl.
Garlic is peeled, and the artichoke hearts are drained. Do they go in whole?
Yes, the food processor will handle them. Add the 1 clove garlic, the 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts, and the 2 tablespoons lemon juice to the bowl with the chickpeas.
I noticed the directions mention parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks, but I don't have them in this bowl. Is that okay?
Yes. The blending step says to combine all ingredients except parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks in the food processor, so keep those out if you're using them for serving later.
Everything for the hummus is in the processor. How smooth should I make it?
Pulse it until smooth. Stop once the chickpeas, garlic, artichoke hearts, and lemon juice have blended into an even hummus texture.
It's mostly smooth, but there are a few tiny artichoke bits. Should I keep pulsing?
If you want a smoother dip, pulse a little more and scrape down the sides as needed. The recipe's target is smooth, so let the texture guide you.
It looks smooth now. What should I do before serving?
Transfer the hummus to a serving bowl, cover it, and refrigerate it until you're ready to serve.
Can you help me make Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil. Those are the measured ingredients listed for this cookie dough.
The butter is soft, and I've measured both sugars and the oil. Should everything go into the bowl together?
Yes. Add the softened butter, both sugars, and the vegetable oil to the large mixing bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and well combined.
It's creamy now, but a little loose from the oil. Is that okay before I add anything else?
That's fine for this dough. Next, add the eggs and vanilla, then mix well so they're fully blended into the butter, sugar, and oil mixture.
Eggs and vanilla are mixed in. What dry ingredients should I be reaching for?
Bring over the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar. Add them to the bowl and mix until they're incorporated into the dough.
Should I dump the dry ingredients in all at once, or is it better to add them gradually?
The recipe simply says to add them, but adding them gradually is easier to control and helps keep flour from puffing out of the bowl. Mix just until the dry ingredients disappear into the dough.
The dough has come together. I see pecans mentioned—are they required?
They're optional. If you want them, stir in the pecans now; if not, you can leave the dough plain and still stay with the recipe.
I'll leave the pecans out. Anything I should check before I clean up the counter?

Make sure the dough is evenly mixed with no streaks of flour or unmixed sugar. Since you're skipping the pecans, once the dough looks uniform, you're done with the listed mixing steps for Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2.
Can you help me make California Chicken? I've got the chicken breasts out but want to do it in the right order.
Absolutely. For this recipe you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt. You'll also want a skillet and your oven ready.
The skillet is on the stove and the oven is still off. What temperature should I set it to?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can warm while you start the chicken on the stovetop.
Oven is heating. Should the olive oil go into the skillet before the chicken?
Yes. Warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the skillet, then add the chicken breasts once the oil is hot enough to coat the pan.
Do I use the onion powder now, or wait until later?
Add the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder while the chicken is in the skillet so it seasons the meat as it cooks.
The chicken is in and seasoned. How long should I keep it on the stove?
Cook it for about 15 minutes, turning as needed, until the chicken is browned and just about done.
What should the outside look like before I stop browning it?
Look for a browned surface on the chicken and no raw-looking exterior. It should be nearly cooked through before you move on.
It's browned now. How do I season it at the end?
Add the pinch of salt, and use pepper to taste if you'd like, then serve the California Chicken while it's hot.
Can you guide me through making Escargots Vol au Vent? I've got the snails out but want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set out 12 helix snails without shells and 1/2 cup softened butter so they're ready to use.
The butter is softening on the counter, and the snails are in a small bowl. What aromatics should I prep?
Finely chop 2 cloves of garlic and 1 green onion. Keep them close by because they'll be mixed into the butter.
Garlic and green onion are chopped. Should I heat the oven before working with the escargots?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's ready when the mixture is prepared.
Oven is heating. The escargots look a little briny from the container—what should I do with them?
Drain the escargots, rinse them under cold water, then drain them again well so they don't water down the butter mixture.
They're rinsed and draining in a sieve. What bowl setup do I need for the butter?
Use a mixing bowl and add the softened butter, chopped garlic, chopped green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine.
I've added everything to the bowl. Should the butter stay chunky or become more like a spread?
Mix it thoroughly until the seasonings are evenly distributed through the softened butter and it looks cohesive.
The butter mixture is even now. Do I fold the snails in gently or stir them hard?
Fold the drained escargots into the seasoned butter gently, just enough to coat them well before they go into the vol-au-vent shells or baking dish.
Can you help me make Crab Cake Sauce? I've got a blender out and want to serve it with crab cakes later.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup sour cream and 1 cup mayonnaise, since those make the creamy base. Add them to the blender when you're ready.
Both are measured and in the blender. The sour cream is pretty thick—does that matter?
That's fine. The mayonnaise and the other ingredients will help it blend smoothly. Measure 1/2 cup cottage cheese next and add it in.
Cottage cheese is in. Should I use all the salsa now too?
Yes, add 1/3 cup hot salsa to the blender. Try to include both the liquid and the chunky bits so the flavor blends evenly.
Done. The recipe also mentions cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt—do those go in before blending?
Yes, add the cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt to the blender with the sour cream, mayonnaise, cottage cheese, and salsa.
Everything is in. What texture am I aiming for when I blend it?
Puree it until the sauce is smooth and creamy, with no obvious cottage cheese curds or salsa chunks left. Pause and scrape down the sides if the blender needs help.
It looks smooth now, but it's a little loose. Is that okay before chilling?
Yes, that's okay. Transfer it to a covered bowl or container, then chill it before serving so the sauce firms up slightly and the flavors settle.
I'm serving soon. How should I present it with the crab cakes?
Give it a quick stir after chilling, then spoon it into a small bowl or drizzle a little beside the crab cakes. Keep any extra sauce cold until serving.
I want to make Dads Kickin Jamaican Wings Mon. Can you help me get started without losing track of the marinade steps?
Absolutely. Set out 3 tablespoons Jamaican jerk seasoning blend and 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, then grab a blender since the marinade gets blended until thick and smooth.
The blender is on the counter, and I've got the seasoning and oil measured. What aromatics should I prep?
Dice 3 cloves garlic and dice 1 peeled piece of fresh ginger that's about 1 inch long. You'll also be adding green onions and jalapeno slices to the blender.
Garlic and ginger are diced. Should everything go in the blender together or in stages?
Put the jerk seasoning, vegetable oil, garlic, ginger, green onions, and jalapeno slices into the blender together, then blend until the mixture looks thick and smooth.
It's blended and pretty thick. How should I coat the wings without making a mess?
Dunk the wings into the blended mixture so they're coated, letting the excess drip back into the bowl or blender jar before you move them.
They're coated. I have two baking sheets ready—how should I arrange them?
Lay the wings out in a single layer on the baking sheets. Try not to stack them, so the marinade stays evenly distributed.
The sheets are filled. Do they go straight into the oven now or chill first?
Cover the baking sheets with aluminum foil and refrigerate the wings for 8 hours, or leave them overnight if that works better for your timing.
They've chilled overnight. What oven temperature should I use before cooking?
Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C. Once it reaches temperature, you'll be ready for the next cooking stage.
Can you guide me through Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa? I'm starting with the salsa prep.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup corn and 1/2 cup diced red onion, then grab a medium bowl for mixing the salsa.
Corn and red onion are in front of me. What other vegetables should I chop before the grill is hot?
Add 1 cup peeled, chopped jicama and 1/2 cup diced red bell pepper to your prep list. Keep the pieces fairly small so the salsa stays crunchy but easy to spoon onto tacos.
The jicama is peeled and chopped, and the bell pepper is diced. Should I heat the grill yet?
Yes, preheat the grill for high heat while you finish the salsa components. That way it's ready when you need it.
Grill is heating. I have the medium bowl out—what goes in first?
Put the corn, red onion, jicama, red bell pepper, and cilantro into the medium bowl. Toss them gently so the colors and crunch are evenly mixed.
The salsa base looks good. It seems a little dry right now—what should brighten it up?
Stir in the lime juice and lime zest. Mix just enough to coat everything so the citrus lifts the corn and jicama without making the salsa watery.
That helped. I also see the spices out on the counter—do they go straight into the salsa?
Use a small bowl for the seasoning blend: combine cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt there first. Mixing them separately helps distribute the heat and salt more evenly.
Seasoning is mixed. How should I use everything when I'm ready to serve the tacos?

Keep the crunchy corn salsa nearby for topping the fish tacos, and sprinkle or apply the cayenne, black pepper, and salt blend as your recipe directs. Serve while the grilled components are hot and the salsa is still crisp.

messages.content: Can you help me make Chocolate Hazelnut Fruit Crepes? I've got the crepes out, but I want to make sure I set everything up right.
Absolutely. For this recipe, you'll want 4 crepes, 1 cup chocolate hazelnut spread, 4 bananas sliced, and 1 (7 ounce) can of pressurized whipped cream for serving.
I have the bananas sliced and the spread ready. Should I warm the skillet before filling them?
Not yet. Fill the crepes first so they're ready to go into the skillet all at once. Lay the 4 crepes flat on your work surface.
They're laid out. How much spread goes on each one?
Spread 1/4 cup of chocolate hazelnut spread onto each crepe, keeping it fairly even so it warms nicely without squeezing out too much.
The spread is on. Do the banana slices go all over or just in the middle?
Arrange 1 sliced banana down the center of each crepe. Keeping the fruit in the center will make them easier to roll.
They're filled now, but the crepes feel a little delicate. How tight should I roll them?
Roll them snugly but gently, just tight enough to hold the banana and spread inside. Then place the rolled crepes in a warm skillet over medium heat.
They're in the skillet. Do I need to flip them or just heat one side?
Let them warm for about 90 seconds. If they seem to be heating evenly and softening, you can leave them as is; the goal is simply to warm the filling and crepes.
They're warm and the chocolate hazelnut spread looks soft. How should I serve them?
Transfer the crepes to plates while they're warm, then top or serve them with the pressurized whipped cream. They're ready to eat right away.
Can you help me make Cheddar Artichoke Quiche Cups? I've got a mixing bowl and skillet out, but I want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by gathering the main ingredients: 1 (7.5 ounce) jar of marinated artichoke hearts, 1 small onion finely chopped, 1 garlic clove minced, and 4 beaten eggs.
The artichoke jar is open. Should I pour off all the liquid, or do I need some of it for the skillet?
Drain the artichokes, but keep half of the marinade. You'll use that reserved marinade to sauté the onion and garlic.
Got it. The artichokes are drained and I saved about half the marinade. How small should I cut them?
Chop the artichoke hearts into small bite-size pieces so they'll distribute evenly in the quiche cups, then set them aside.
They're chopped. I'm moving to the stove now—what goes into the skillet?
Add the reserved marinade to the skillet, then sauté the finely chopped onion and minced garlic in it until they're tender. Once they've softened, set that mixture aside.
The onion and garlic smell good and look softened. Should the skillet mixture cool before it goes near the eggs?
Yes, let it sit briefly so it's not piping hot when you combine everything. That helps keep the beaten eggs from starting to cook too early.
While that cools, what should I put in the big bowl with the eggs?
In the large bowl, combine the beaten eggs with bread crumbs, mustard, oregano, pepper, and hot pepper sauce. Stir until the seasonings and crumbs are evenly mixed through the eggs.
The egg mixture is blended. Do I fold in the artichokes and the onion-garlic mixture after this?
Yes. Add the chopped artichokes and the cooled onion-garlic mixture to the bowl, then stir gently until everything is evenly combined and ready for portioning into quiche cups.
Can you help me cook Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken? I've got the chicken out and want to make sure I don't miss anything.

Absolutely. For this recipe you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, salt and pepper to taste, 2 teaspoons olive oil, and 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions.
I have the chicken breasts and the canned tomatoes. Should I season the chicken before the skillet heats up?
Yes. Pat the chicken dry if it's damp, then season both sides of each chicken breast with salt and pepper.
Done. What pan setup should I use so the chicken browns instead of steaming?
Use a large skillet so the chicken has room. Add the olive oil and heat it over medium-high heat until the pan is hot and the oil looks glossy.
The oil is shimmering a bit. Do I put all 4 pieces in at once?
Place the chicken in the skillet in a single layer. If the pieces are crowded, brown them in batches, but keep the same total amount of oil from the recipe.
They fit. How much should I move them around while they cook?
Let them sit long enough to brown on the first side, then turn them once to brown the other side. Try not to keep flipping, since that can slow the browning.
Both sides have some color now. Are the tomatoes supposed to go in yet?
Not yet based on the steps we're following. Once the chicken is browned on both sides, remove it from the pan and set it aside.
Should I put the chicken on a plate or back on the cutting board?
Set it on a clean plate, not the raw-chicken cutting board. Keep the skillet handy with the browned bits in it for the next part of the recipe.

Carefully spoon off the chicken fat, then return the pan to the stove so it's ready for the next part of the recipe.

You'll also need 1/4 cup Creole seasoning and 1 white onion.
I've got those. Which pot or fryer setup comes first?
Use a large stockpot or turkey fryer, and start heating the peanut oil to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
The burner is on. I'm worried about the oil level once the turkey goes in—what should I watch?
Leave enough empty space in the pot for the turkey before lowering it in, because the oil can spill over if the pot is too full.
Got it. While the oil climbs, what should I prepare for draining or resting afterward?
Line a large platter with food-safe paper bags so it's ready when you need a place for the fried turkey.
The platter is lined. What should I do to the turkey before it goes anywhere near the oil?
Rinse the turkey, then pat it very thoroughly dry with paper towels.
How dry are we talking before frying?
As dry as you can get it on the outside and in any crevices; keep using paper towels until the surface isn't wet, since extra moisture and hot oil are a bad mix.
I want to make Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. Can you stay with me while I mix the dough?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather the measured wet-base ingredients: 1/2 cup margarine, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup molasses, and 1 egg yolk.
The bowl is ready, and I have the margarine and sugar measured. Should they go in together?
Yes. Put the margarine and sugar into the large bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth rather than streaky.
It's smoothing out. I've got the molasses nearby, but the egg is still whole.
Separate the egg and keep just the yolk. Stir the molasses and the egg yolk into the creamed margarine and sugar until everything is evenly mixed.
That mixture is dark and glossy now. What dry ingredients should I combine?
In another bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg so the leaveners and spices are distributed before they meet the molasses mixture.
The spices are mixed with the flour. Do I dump it all in or add it gradually?
Blend the dry mixture into the molasses mixture, working steadily and scraping the bowl as needed, until the dough is smooth.
It's thickening into a dough and there are only a few dry patches left on the side of the bowl.
Scrape down those dry patches and fold them in just until the dough looks even. Avoid overworking it once the flour is incorporated.
The dough looks uniform now. What should I do before cutting out the gingerbread men?
Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. That rest will firm it up so it's easier to roll and cut cleanly.
Can you walk me through making Cucumber Sandwiches? I'm setting out the ingredients now.
Absolutely. Put out 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese spread and 2 teaspoons of ranch salad dressing mix, plus a mixing bowl and spoon.
Cream cheese and ranch mix are on the counter. What else should I grab before I start?
You'll also need 12 slices of pumpernickel rye bread and 2 medium cucumbers. A peeler is optional, and a sharp knife or mandoline will help with thin slices.
I have the bread and cucumbers. Should the cream cheese be mixed plain or loosened up first?
Add the cream cheese spread to the bowl and stir in the ranch salad dressing mix until it looks evenly combined. Since it's a spread, it should mix smoothly without much prep.
The ranch is mixed through. Do I spread it thickly or just a thin coat?
Spread the cream cheese mixture on one side of each slice of bread, going close to the edges so every bite has some filling.
All 12 slices are spread. I'm looking at the cucumbers now—do I need to peel them?
Peel the cucumbers if you'd like, then thinly slice them. Lay the cucumber slices over 6 of the bread slices, on top of the cream cheese side.
The cucumbers are sliced and layered on 6 slices. Should I add anything else before closing them?
For this recipe, just place the remaining 6 bread slices on top, cream cheese side facing down, to make the sandwiches.
They're assembled. Any serving tip so they look neat on a plate?
Use a sharp knife to cut them cleanly if you want smaller pieces, then arrange them right away so the pumpernickel rye and cucumber layers stay tidy.
I want to make Broiled Egg Salad Sandwiches, and I've got the hard-cooked eggs ready. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Chop 3 hard-cooked eggs and put them near your mixing bowl. You'll also need 1/4 cup crushed saltine crackers, 1/4 cup chopped celery, and 1 tablespoon diced pimientos.
The crackers are crushed and the celery is chopped. Should I mix those straight in with the eggs?
Yes. In one bowl, combine the chopped eggs, crushed saltine crackers, chopped celery, and diced pimientos. Stir gently so the eggs stay a little chunky.
That mixture is in the bowl. I see the dressing ingredients mentioned too—what should I do with those?
Use a second bowl for the dressing. Combine the mayonnaise, milk, salt, garlic salt, and pepper, then mix it well until it looks smooth and evenly seasoned.
The dressing is smooth. Do I fold it in all at once or add it gradually?
Add the dressing to the egg mixture and stir until everything is coated. A gentle fold works best so the filling doesn't turn pasty.
It looks creamy and still has some texture. What pan should I use for the muffins?
Use an ungreased baking sheet. Arrange the muffin halves cut-side up so they're ready for the egg salad topping.
The muffin halves are on the sheet. How much filling goes on each one?
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the egg salad mixture onto each muffin half, spreading it just enough to cover the surface without packing it down.
They're topped now. Anything I should check before they go under the broiler?
Make sure the muffin halves are steady on the ungreased baking sheet and the topping is evenly divided. Then they're ready to broil according to your recipe's next broiling direction.
I'm making Apple Pie 2 and have a large stockpot out. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. Pour 1 gallon apple juice and 1 gallon apple cider into the large pot, leaving enough room so it won't slosh when it boils.
Both gallons are in the pot. I'm checking the pantry now—what dry ingredients should I pull out?
You'll need 3 cups white sugar and 8 cinnamon sticks. Keep the cinnamon sticks whole so they can steep in the hot juice mixture.
Sugar is measured and the cinnamon sticks are ready. Do they all go in together?
Yes. Add the white sugar and all 8 cinnamon sticks to the pot with the apple juice and apple cider, then stir so the sugar starts dissolving.
The sugar is mostly dissolved. Should I keep the heat gentle or bring it up?
Bring the mixture to a boil. Stir occasionally as it heats so the sugar doesn't settle on the bottom of the pot.
It has reached a boil and smells strongly of cinnamon. What should I do right away?
Take the pot off the heat as soon as it boils, then let the juice mixture cool completely before adding anything else.
Completely cool, as in room temperature? I don't want to rush that part.
Right—let it cool completely. The next ingredient is grain alcohol, and it should only be stirred in once the juice mixture is cool.
The pot is cool now and the cinnamon sticks are still in there. How do I finish the mixture?
Stir in the grain alcohol thoroughly so it blends evenly with the cooled apple juice, apple cider, sugar, and cinnamon mixture.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you talk me through the setup before I start melting anything?

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler, a spoon or spatula for constant stirring, and wax paper ready for the coated pretzels.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips out. Should the wax paper be on a tray or just on the counter?
A tray is helpful because you can move the pretzels after dipping, but the counter is fine too. Lay the wax paper out now so the coated pretzels can go straight onto it to set and cool.
The double boiler is ready. Do the chocolate chips and cream go in together?
Yes, add the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips and the 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream to the top of the double boiler. Keep the heat low and stir constantly as they melt together.
It's melting, but there are still a few small lumps. Should I turn up the heat?
Keep it on low. Just keep stirring until the mixture is smooth; the low heat helps prevent the chocolate from scorching or getting too thick too fast.
The chocolate looks smooth and glossy now. How fast do I need to dip the pretzels?
Work one pretzel at a time and dip quickly while the chocolate mixture is still very warm. Coat each pretzel, let the excess drip off briefly, then place it on the wax paper.
Some of the pretzels are sticking to my fingers when I dip them. Any easy way to keep this tidy?
Use a fork or dipping tool if you have one. Slide each pretzel into the warm chocolate, lift it out with the fork, tap off extra coating, and transfer it to the wax paper.
They're all on the wax paper now. What happens at the end?
Let the chocolate-covered pretzels sit on the wax paper until they set and cool. Once the coating is firm, they're ready to serve or store.
I want to make Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I. Can you stay with me while I set up the ingredients?
Absolutely. Put your mixing bowl and measuring cups out, then measure 1 cup shortening, 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 2 eggs.
The shortening and both sugars are measured. Should I crack the eggs in now or wait until the oven is on?
Go ahead and start the oven now so it has time to heat: preheat it to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
Oven is heating to 375. I have the eggs ready next to the bowl.
Add the shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla to the bowl, then cream everything thoroughly until the mixture looks smooth and well blended.
It's mixing now. How soft should the creamed mixture look before I stop?
It should look evenly combined and creamy, with no separate streaks of shortening or sugar pockets. Scrape the sides of the bowl once if anything is clinging there.
That looks good. I've got another bowl clean for the dry ingredients.
Use that separate bowl for the dry ingredients, but keep the candies out for now. Stir the dry ingredients together until they're evenly mixed.
Dry bowl is mixed, and the candy pieces are still on the counter.
Add the dry mixture into the creamed mixture and mix well, just until the dough comes together evenly.
The dough is combined. Should I do anything else before scooping or cleaning up?

Scrape down the bowl so all the dough is uniform, then you can fold in the candy coated milk chocolate pieces if your full recipe calls for them after the dry mixture. After that, scoop the dough for baking in the preheated oven.
