messages.content: For this batch of German Chocolate Brownie Cookies, I'm packing it in that soup/stew/bean-dish, brothy-bowl style. What should I do at the end just for this one?
For this one, keep both garnishes in separate containers, then add them only after the bowl has been reheated.
Perfect, that's the treatment I want today. I've cleared space by the mixer; what should I pull out first?
Start with the base ingredients: 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar and 2/3 cup shortening. Put them near a large mixing bowl.
Brown sugar and shortening are out. Do I need the small measuring spoons yet?
Yes. Measure 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so they're ready to go in with the sugar and shortening.
I've got a large bowl ready. Do those four ingredients get mixed together now?
They do. Combine the packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract in the large bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks blended.
The mixture is creamed and the sides of the bowl are a little messy. Should I scrape before adding eggs?
Scrape down the bowl, then beat the eggs into the creamed mixture until they're incorporated.
Eggs are mixed in. I set out a second bowl for the dry ingredients—what goes into it?
In that other bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda. Stir them together so the cocoa and leavening are evenly spread out.
The dry bowl is uniform now. I'm worried about making the dough tough—how should I combine it?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix only until just blended. Stop as soon as you don't see dry streaks.
There are a few floury spots clinging to the bottom. Should I keep the mixer running?
Use a spatula to fold those last spots in by hand, then stop. The mixture should look evenly chocolatey without being overworked.
I want to make Almond Buttercrunch. Can you stay with me while I set up the pan and ingredients?

Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a saucepan, something for steady stirring, and a large cookie sheet that's buttered and ready.
The cookie sheet is buttered, and I've measured the butter and sugar. Should the almonds go in right away?
Yes. Put the butter, the 2 cups white sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds into the saucepan together. Keep the heat low as they start warming.
They're in the saucepan over low heat. The butter is beginning to melt but the sugar still looks grainy.
Keep stirring constantly while the butter melts into the sugar and almonds. Stay with it until the mixture comes to a boil.
It has started boiling. Do I keep stirring to stop it from sticking?
Once it boils, stop stirring, and don't shake the pan. Let it cook undisturbed from here so the candy can set up properly.
I have a candy thermometer clipped on. What temperature am I waiting for?

Heat the mixture to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. If you're checking without relying only on the thermometer, a small amount of syrup dropped into cold water should form hard, brittle threads.
It's at about 300 degrees F now, and the cold-water drop snapped into brittle threads.
That's the right stage. Carefully pour the hot buttercrunch mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet, spreading it out as you pour if needed.
It's on the sheet. I still have the milk chocolate chips measured—where should I keep them for the moment?

Keep the 2 cups milk chocolate chips nearby and ready, but the directions you're following end with pouring the cooked mixture onto the buttered cookie sheet. Let the hot candy settle on the sheet safely before handling it further.
I'm making Eggplant Mixed Grill and want to stay organized before I start. What should I pull out first?

Set out the marinade herbs and oil: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil. You'll also need vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic for the bag.
I've got the oil and herbs on the counter. What kind of container should I use for the vegetables?

Use a large resealable plastic bag so the vegetables can be coated evenly. Add the olive oil, parsley, oregano, basil, vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic to the bag, then mix everything together inside it.
The marinade is mixed in the bag. Which vegetables are going in?
Add the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper to the bag. Try to spread them out a bit before sealing so the marinade can reach all the pieces.
The vegetables are in, but the eggplant pieces are taking up a lot of space. Should I shake it or turn it by hand?
Seal the bag tightly and gently turn it over a few times rather than shaking hard. That will coat the eggplant and the other vegetables without bruising them or forcing liquid toward the seal.
Everything looks coated now. How long does it need to sit, and where?
Put the sealed bag in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Turn it occasionally during that time so the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and peppers keep picking up the marinade evenly.
The marinating time is almost done. When should I deal with the grill?
As you're nearing the end of the 2 hours, preheat the grill for high heat so it's ready when the vegetables come out of the refrigerator.
The grill is hot and the vegetables are ready. Anything to do before they go on?
Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the marinated vegetables. That helps keep the eggplant and peppers from sticking as they hit the high heat.
I'm making Chicken with Vegetables in the slow cooker. Can you help me get the ingredients organized before I start?

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms, 4 chicken drumsticks with the skin removed, 4 chicken thighs with the skin removed, and 4 sliced celery ribs. You'll also need zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper for the vegetable mixture.
The chicken pieces are skinned, and the mushrooms are sliced. Should I put anything in the slow cooker before the celery?
Yes. Put the sliced mushrooms into the slow cooker with the chicken drumsticks and thighs so they form the base of the dish.
They're in the cooker now. The celery is sliced, and I'm chopping the zucchini, carrots, and onion.
Good. Once those vegetables are ready, add the celery, zucchini, carrots, and onion over and around the chicken and mushrooms.
The vegetables are layered in. I have tomato juice and broth out—do they both go in now?
They do. Pour in the tomato juice and broth, then add the garlic, paprika, and pepper so the liquid and seasonings can cook through everything.
All the liquid and seasoning are in. Should I stir it, or leave the chicken where it is?
You can gently settle the vegetables into the liquid, but don't worry about a full stir. Keep the chicken in the slow cooker with the vegetables distributed around it.
The lid is on. What heat setting and timing should I use?
Cook it covered on low for 5 hours, or until the meat juices run clear.
When it's done, what's the best way to handle the chicken and vegetables so they don't cool off?
Remove the chicken and vegetables from the slow cooker and keep them warm until you're ready to serve.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you stay with me while I get the ingredients and pan area ready?

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler, a spoon or spatula for constant stirring, and wax paper for cooling the coated pretzels.
I've got the pretzels and chocolate chips out. The cream is measured, and I'm putting wax paper on the counter now.

Great. Start warming the double boiler over low heat, then add the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream together. Keep the heat gentle so the chocolate melts smoothly instead of seizing.
The chocolate and cream are in the top pan. Should I just let it sit, or keep moving it?
Keep stirring constantly while it melts. Scrape around the sides and bottom of the bowl so the cream blends evenly into the chocolate and the mixture turns glossy.
It's mostly melted but I can still see a few small chips. The texture is shiny and thick.
Stay on low heat and keep stirring until those last bits disappear. Once it's completely smooth and still very warm, you'll be ready to coat the pretzels.
Okay, it's smooth now. Do I dump in a bunch of pretzels or work in smaller amounts?
Dip the pretzels one at a time, quickly coating each while the chocolate mixture is still very warm. Let extra chocolate drip back into the boiler before you move each pretzel to the wax paper.
Some of them are cooling faster than I expected. Should I pause to rewarm the chocolate?
If the coating starts getting too thick, keep it over the low heat and stir until it loosens again. Then continue dipping one pretzel at a time so the coating stays even.
The pretzels are coated and lined up on the wax paper. What should I do while they set?
Leave them on the wax paper to set and cool completely. Once the chocolate has firmed up, lift them gently from the paper and serve or store them in a container.
I want to make Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon for dinner—can you help me plan it around the cedar plank soaking time?
Absolutely. The big timing item is the 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank: submerge it fully in water and let it soak for approximately 12 hours, or overnight, before grilling.
Good to know. I have the plank soaking in a tray now. What should I make sure I have for the salmon itself?
You'll need 6 salmon fillets, each about 4 ounces, plus 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil. Keep the salmon chilled until you're close to grilling.
I've got the fillets and oil. Is there anything else to chop or prep while the plank sits?
Yes—chop 1 large red onion so it's ready to use. Since the plank needs a long soak, this is a good time to prep that and check that your grill area is ready.
The onion is chopped, and the plank has soaked overnight. What should I do at the grill?
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat. While it heats, take the soaked cedar plank out of the water and let the excess water drip off.
The grill is getting hot. Should the plank go directly over the heat?
Yes, place the prepared cedar plank on the grill. Once it's on, sprinkle the plank with coarse salt.
I've put the plank on and salted it. Should I oil the fish before setting it up?
Use the extra virgin olive oil you measured—1/2 cup total for the recipe—to coat or prepare the salmon as you arrange the fillets for the plank.
The salmon is oiled and the onion is ready nearby. Anything I should watch before serving?

Keep the grill on high heat and work from the soaked, salted cedar plank setup. The key recipe checkpoints are covered: plank soaked about 12 hours, grill preheated high, prepared plank placed on the grill, and coarse salt sprinkled on before cooking the salmon.
I'm making Garlic Chicken Stir Fry and have a wok ready. Can you guide me through the prep without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep the chicken close by too, since the cooking moves quickly.
The garlic is minced, but the recipe says 6 cloves and then mentions 2 cloves in the pan. How should I handle that?
Have all 6 cloves minced and ready, but when the oil starts smoking, add 2 cloves of the minced garlic with the ginger, green onions, and salt as the recipe directs.
Got it. The ginger is grated and the green onions are chopped. Should I heat the wok now?
Yes. Put the wok or a large skillet over heat and add the 2 tablespoons peanut oil. Let it get hot enough that the oil just begins to smoke.
The oil is shimmering and I see a little smoke. What goes in right away?

Quickly stir in the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped bunch of green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving so the aromatics fry instead of sitting in one spot.
It smells strong already. How long should I keep stir-frying the onions?
Stir-fry until the onion turns translucent, about 2 minutes. You're looking for the green onions to soften and lose that raw bite while the garlic and ginger stay fragrant.
The onions look glossy and softer now. Is the chicken next?
Yes, add the chicken to the wok and stir it through the aromatics. Keep tossing and spreading it against the hot surface so it cooks evenly.
How do I know when to stop cooking the chicken?
Cook until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes. Once there are no translucent-looking surfaces, pull it from the heat and serve the Garlic Chicken Stir Fry while it's hot.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip and want to get everything staged before the oven goes on. What should I pull out?

Set out 1 cup mayonnaise, 8 ounces sour cream, 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, and 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. Drain and chop the artichoke hearts so they're ready to stir in.
The artichokes are drained and chopped. What dish should I use for mixing and baking?
Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish. It can be your mixing bowl and baking dish, so there's less cleanup.
Good, I've got that dish out. Should I preheat now?
Yes—preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) while you combine the dip.
The oven is heating. Do the mayonnaise and sour cream go in first?
They can. Add the 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream to the casserole dish, then stir in the garlic and mushroom soup mix until it's evenly blended.
That base looks smooth. When do I add the artichokes, cheese, and crab meat?
Fold in the chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat now. Stir just until everything is evenly distributed in the creamy mixture.
It's all combined in the casserole. Do I cover it with foil?
Leave it uncovered and bake it at 350 degrees F for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, how should I serve it?
Serve the Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip immediately while it's hot and creamy.
I want to make Chili For Two. Can you talk me through it while I cook?
Absolutely. Set a saucepan on the stove and gather 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans, undrained.
I've got the saucepan out. Should I open the beans now or wait?
You can open them now so they're ready, but don't drain them. The liquid from the 15.5 ounce can goes into the chili too.
The onion is chopped and the garlic is minced. How hot should the pan be?
Put the saucepan over medium heat. Add the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic together, then cook while breaking up the beef.
How do I know when that part is done?
Cook until the beef is no longer pink and the onion has softened a bit. Once it reaches that point, drain off the excess fat from the saucepan.
Drained. The pan still has the beef, onion, and garlic in it.
Good. Stir in the undrained chili beans, making sure the bean liquid mixes with the beef and aromatics.
It looks a little soupy after adding the beans. Is that expected?
Yes, that's fine at this stage. Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally so it heats evenly.
It's boiling now. What should I do for the simmer?
Reduce the heat, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the chili is heated through. Give it a stir before serving.
I'm making Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks and want to get the marinade organized before the fish comes out. What should I put on the counter?

Set out 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 tablespoons sherry, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root, and garlic. You'll also need a medium bowl, a whisk, and a large resealable bag for marinating the swordfish steaks.
I've got the bowl and bag ready. Should the ginger be grated right into the bowl with the liquids?
Yes, grate the fresh ginger root directly into the medium bowl. Add the soy sauce, vegetable oil, sherry, and garlic with it, then whisk until the marinade looks evenly mixed.
The oil is floating a bit on top even after whisking. Is that a problem?
That's fine for this marinade. Give it a brisk whisk so the soy sauce, oil, sherry, ginger, and garlic are distributed, then pour the mixture into the large resealable bag.
The marinade is in the bag. Do I add the swordfish steaks flat or does it not matter?
Add the swordfish steaks to the bag as flat as you can so more surface touches the marinade. Seal the bag well, leaving a little room to move the liquid around.
I'm worried about leaking in the fridge. Any quick way to avoid a mess?
After sealing, shake the bag gently to coat the steaks, then set the bag on a plate or in a shallow dish before refrigerating. That way any small leak is contained.
They're coated now. How long do they need to sit before I cook them?
Refrigerate the bag and let the swordfish steaks marinate at least 4 hours. Keep them chilled the whole time.
Should I turn the bag during that time, or just leave it alone?
If you think of it, turn the bag once or twice while it marinates so the coating stays even, but the key recipe point is that the steaks stay in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
I'm making Chicken Tortilla Soup IV and I've got a large pot out. Can you keep me on track from the ingredient prep?
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil total, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin.
The tortillas are still whole. How should I cut them before the pot goes on?
Cut the corn tortillas into 1/2 inch strips. Try to keep them fairly even so they crisp at about the same pace.
They're sliced. Do I use all the oil right away?
No, start with 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil in the large pot over medium heat. Keep the remaining 1/2 teaspoon nearby for the second batch.
The oil is heating. Should the tortilla strips all go in together?
Add only half of the tortilla strips to the pot. Stir them often while they cook, and keep going until they turn crisp.
They're getting firm and a little golden. What should I do as soon as they're crisp?
Lift that batch out and drain the strips on paper towels so the excess oil comes off.
First batch is on the towels. The pot looks mostly clear—what about the rest of the strips?
Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon vegetable oil to the pot, then cook the remaining tortilla strips the same way, stirring often until crisp.
Second batch is crisp too. Where should I put everything while I deal with the broth and cumin?
Drain the second batch on paper towels as well, then set all the crisp tortilla strips aside. You'll still have the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the soup.
I'm making Chicken Tortilla Soup IV and want to get everything lined up before I turn on the stove.
Absolutely. For this recipe, set out 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil and 6 corn tortillas, each 6 inches, cut into 1/2 inch strips.
The tortillas are sliced into strips. What other ingredients should be on the counter?
You'll also need 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready nearby.
I have a large pot out. How much oil goes in at the start?
Pour 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat.
The oil is warming. Do all the tortilla strips go in now?
Add only half of the tortilla strips for this batch. Stir them often so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in one spot.
They're getting firm and a little crisp. Should I take them out yet?
Yes, once that half is crisp, lift the strips out and drain them on paper towels.
Paper towels are set up and the first batch is out. What about the rest of the strips?
Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of oil to the pot, then cook the remaining tortilla strips the same way until crisp.
The second batch is crisp too. Do I mix them into the broth right away?
For now, drain that batch on paper towels as well and set the crisp tortilla strips aside while you continue with the soup.
I'm making Dads BBQ Roast and want to get my counter set up before I handle the beef. What should I pull out?

Grab 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 dry onion soup mix envelopes that are 1 ounce each, and a 5 pound beef rump roast. You'll also want a small bowl, a spoon or spatula for mixing, paper towels, and aluminum foil.
Mustard and soup mix are on the counter. Should I combine them before unwrapping the roast?
Yes, that keeps things cleaner. In the small bowl, stir the yellow mustard and both envelopes of dry onion soup mix together until the soup mix is evenly worked through the mustard.
The mixture is thick and a little grainy from the onion mix. Is that right?
That's right. It should look like a thick mustard paste with bits of the dry onion soup mix throughout, not a smooth sauce.
I'm ready for the foil. How should I arrange it so the roast is easy to wrap later?
Lay out two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise, like a plus sign. Make sure the sheets are long enough that the roast can sit in the center with plenty of foil extending around it.
Foil is down. The roast is still wet from the package—do I need to dry it?
Yes. Pat the beef rump roast dry all over with paper towels, then place it right in the center where the two foil sheets cross.
It's centered now. Should I coat just the top or the whole roast?
Coat it generously with the mustard and onion soup mixture, spreading it over the top and sides so the roast is well covered.
Some of the coating is sliding onto the foil. Should I scrape that back up?
Yes, use your spoon or spatula to push any fallen mustard mixture back onto the beef. Once the roast is generously coated, you're set with the prep described for Dads BBQ Roast.
I'm making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies and want to stay organized as I go. What should I put on the counter first?
Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup softened butter. The butter should be real butter, no substitutes, so it creams properly with the sugars.
Got the chips and the softened butter. Which sugars are going into this?
You'll need 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Pack the brown sugar firmly into the measuring cup, then level it off.
The sugars are measured. Do I melt the chips before I start mixing the dough?
Yes. Melt the butterscotch chips in the microwave, using short bursts and stirring between them so they don't scorch. Once melted, let them cool for 10 minutes before adding them to the dough.
They're melted and cooling. While I wait, what should I do with the butter and sugars?
Put the softened butter, sugar, and packed brown sugar into a mixing bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks lighter and smooth, with no big streaks of butter left.
The butter-sugar mixture looks fluffy. I see egg, milk, and vanilla in the directions—do those go in now?
Yes, add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well. Scrape the bowl once or twice so everything blends evenly.
It's mixed, and the melted butterscotch is still warm but not hot. Is that cool enough?
If it has had the 10-minute cooling time and feels warm rather than hot, you're in good shape. You don't want it so hot that it softens the butter mixture too much.
Okay, I'm ready to add the butterscotch. What should the dough look like after that?
Beat in the melted butterscotch chips until the dough is evenly colored and smooth. Stop once it's fully incorporated so you don't overwork the mixture.
I'm planning to make Caramel Shortbread Squares and want to follow the recipe closely. What should I pull out before I start?
Get 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, and 1/2 cup butter. You'll also want a medium mixing bowl and a 9 inch square baking pan.
I've got the ingredients on the counter. Should the oven be set before I mix the crumbly base?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 176 degrees C, so it's ready when the shortbread mixture is pressed into the pan.
The oven is heating. For the mixing bowl, which amounts go into the crumb mixture?
In the medium bowl, combine 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour.
Do I cream it smooth like cookie dough, or should it look different?
Mix it until it's evenly crumbly rather than smooth. You're looking for a consistent crumb texture throughout the bowl.
The crumbs look even now. How do I get them into the pan without making a mess?
Tip the crumbly mixture into the 9 inch square baking pan, spread it across the bottom, then press it down into an even layer.
It's pressed in, but the corners are a little thinner than the middle. Is that worth fixing?
Yes, gently press some of the thicker middle area toward the corners so the layer is as even as you can make it before baking.
The pan looks level now. How long does it bake?
Bake the shortbread base at 350 degrees F for 20 minutes.
I'm making Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2 and want to get my counter set up before I start mixing.
Great. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather the measured fats and sugars: 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil.
The butter is soft and the two sugars are measured. Should I put the oil in with them right away?
Yes. Add the softened butter, both sugars, and the vegetable oil to the large bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It's coming together but still looks a little glossy from the oil. Is that fine?
That's fine for this dough. Keep mixing just until the butter, sugars, and oil look blended rather than separated.
Okay, the base looks even now. I have eggs and vanilla nearby—do those go in next?
They do. Add the eggs and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so the wet ingredients are fully incorporated.
The wet mixture is smooth. I'm pulling together the dry ingredients now—what should go into the bowl?
Add the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar to the bowl. Mix until those dry ingredients are worked into the dough.
Should I stir hard once the flour is in, or keep it gentle?
Keep it controlled and steady. Mix only until no dry streaks remain, scraping the sides of the bowl if needed so everything is evenly distributed.
The dough looks mixed. I have pecans, but I'm not sure if they're required.
They're optional here. If you want them, stir in the pecans now until they're spread through the dough; if not, you can leave the dough as is.
I'm making Gingery Fish Kabobs and want to start with the sauce. What should I pull out before I turn on the stove?

Set out a small saucepan, 2 cups pineapple juice, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, 2 tablespoons light soy sauce that's 50% less sodium, and 1 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar. You'll also need garlic and ginger ready to add in once the cornstarch is dissolved.
I've got the saucepan and the pineapple juice measured. Do I heat it first or mix in the cornstarch cold?
Mix it before heating. Pour the pineapple juice into the small saucepan and whisk in the cornstarch until it dissolves smoothly, with no dry clumps stuck to the bottom.
The cornstarch is mostly dissolved, but I see a little cloudiness. Is that fine?
Yes, a cloudy look is normal. As long as there aren't visible lumps, stir in the light soy sauce, white vinegar, garlic, and ginger.
Everything is in the pan now. What heat level should I use so it thickens without scorching?
Bring it to a gentle simmer over moderate heat, stirring often. Keep it moving along the bottom of the pan so the cornstarch thickens the sauce evenly.
It's simmering lightly. How long am I watching it, and what should it look like?
Let it simmer until it's slightly thickened, about 7 minutes. You're looking for a light glaze consistency, not a heavy paste.
After a few minutes it's coating the spoon a bit. Should I keep going for the full time?
If it's only just starting to coat the spoon, keep simmering and stirring until it reaches that slightly thickened texture, using the 7 minutes as your guide.
The sauce looks glossy and a little thicker now. What do I do before using it on the kabobs?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the sauce cool. Once it's cooled, it's ready to use with the Gingery Fish Kabobs.
I'm making Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version and I want to get the counter set up before I touch the pork. What should I pull out?

Set out 6 center cut pork chops trimmed of any visible fat, garlic powder, seasoning salt, a beaten egg mixture, flour, and bread crumbs. You'll also want a small bowl for the egg mixture and a plate or shallow dish for dredging and coating.
I've got the chops trimmed. How much seasoning am I measuring before I start?
Measure 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt. The recipe says to season to taste, so those amounts give you the listed seasoning to work from while you coat the chops evenly.
Should I turn on the oven now, or wait until the chops are breaded?
Turn it on now so it's ready: preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. Do I rinse the pork chops before seasoning them?
Yes. Rinse the pork chops, then pat them dry really well. Once the surface is dry, season them with the garlic powder and seasoning salt so the coating sticks better instead of sliding off.
For the wet bowl, is it just the egg? The ingredient line looks cut off on my copy.

Use the beaten egg as the wet mixture, and follow the instruction that mentions the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture in a small bowl. Keep it in a bowl wide enough to dip each pork chop without bending it.
I have flour on one plate, the egg bowl, and crumbs on another plate. What order do the chops go through?
Go flour, egg, then bread crumbs. Dredge each pork chop lightly in flour, dip it into the egg mixture, then coat it liberally with bread crumbs so the outside is fully covered.
How heavy should the flour layer be? I don't want it pasty.

Keep the flour layer thin—just enough to dust the surface. Shake off the extra before dipping in the egg, then press the bread crumbs on generously so the chops are coated and ready for the baking step.

source_seed.recipe_title: Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version

messages.content: I want to make Chicken Vegetable Stew. Can you guide me while I prep everything?
Absolutely. Set out a large pot, then get 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite size pieces. You'll also need 1 chopped onion ready to go.
The chicken is cut up and the onion is chopped. What vegetables should I prep before the pot goes on?
Have 1/2 pound baby carrots ready, and prepare 4 potatoes so they can go into the stew with the rest of the ingredients.
I've got the carrots and potatoes on the counter. Do I add anything to the pot yet or wait?
Go ahead and put the chopped onion, chicken breast meat, baby carrots, and potatoes into the large pot together.
They're all in the pot. Should I season before adding liquid?
Yes. Sprinkle in the salt and turmeric over the chicken and vegetables so the seasoning starts right in the pot.
Salt and turmeric are in. I see tomato paste listed in the instructions—how do I add it without clumps?
Dissolve the tomato paste in water first, stirring until it loosens into a smooth mixture, then pour that into the pot.
The tomato paste mixture is added. Is there anything else that should go in for flavor?
If you'd like more seasoning, add garlic powder and ground black pepper now. They're optional, so use them to taste.
I added a little garlic powder and black pepper. Before I let it cook, can you recap what should be in the pot?

Your pot should have the bite size chicken breast pieces, chopped onion, 1/2 pound baby carrots, 4 potatoes, salt, turmeric, tomato paste dissolved in water, and optionally the garlic powder and ground black pepper.
I want to make Frosted Ruby Punch. Can you help me plan the freezer part and the punch bowl part?

Absolutely. You'll need 4 cups cranberry juice for the ice ring, plus 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice for the punch mixture. The directions also have you stir in ginger ale once the juices and sugar are combined.
I have a ring mold, but I'm not sure if it's the right size. What should it hold?
Use a 5-cup ring mold. Pour the 4 cups of cranberry juice into it, leaving a little room at the top so it can expand as it freezes.
The cranberry juice is in the mold. Does it need just a few hours, or longer?
Freeze it overnight so the ring is solid all the way through. Set it on a level spot in the freezer if you can, so it freezes evenly.
Okay, it's the next day and the cranberry ring feels firm. What should I mix in the punch bowl?
In the punch bowl, combine the 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice. Stir until the sugar is dissolved rather than sitting grainy at the bottom.
Should I add the ginger ale before the sugar is dissolved?
Wait until the sugar has dissolved into the lemon and orange juices, then stir in the ginger ale gently so you keep some fizz.
The punch is mixed and the bowl is ready. How do I get the frozen cranberry ring out neatly?

Loosen the ice ring from the 5-cup mold carefully, then remove it in one piece if possible. If it resists, briefly warm the outside of the mold with your hands or a little warm water, without melting the ring too much.
It came out cleanly. Do I just drop it into the bowl?
Set it into the punch gently so it floats. That gives you the frosted ruby look while keeping the punch chilled for serving.
I'm making Diegos Special Beef Stew and want to get the slow cooker part started right. Can you guide me through the beginning?

Absolutely. Set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat, 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 teaspoons butter. You'll also want a resealable plastic bag, a skillet, and your slow cooker ready.
The beef is cubed already, and I found a gallon-size bag. Should the flour go in by itself first?
Put the cubed beef and the 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour into the resealable plastic bag together. Try to leave some air space in the bag so the pieces can move around.
Okay, the beef and flour are in the bag. I'm worried about flour leaking out while I shake it.
Press the seal firmly all the way across, then hold the top closed with one hand while you shake. Turn the bag a few times so the beef gets evenly coated with flour.
The pieces look lightly dusted now, not clumpy. What should I heat in the skillet?
Heat the 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Let it warm until it shimmers a bit, then you can start browning the floured beef.
Do I add all the beef at once, or should I leave some space in the pan?
Leave space if your skillet is small, because the beef needs contact with the hot surface to brown on all sides. If it's crowded, work in batches rather than piling it up.
The first side is browning, and I still have the 2 teaspoons butter on the counter. Is that part of the setup too?

Yes, keep the 2 teaspoons butter measured and ready with the rest of the ingredients. For this part, focus on browning the beef in the olive oil over medium heat, turning the pieces so all sides get color.
The beef is browned all around. Should I scrape anything from the skillet before moving it?
Transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker. If any browned bits are stuck to the beef, bring them along, but the key step here is getting the beef from the skillet into the slow cooker.
I want to make Cake Doughnuts. Can you help me get the dry ingredients measured before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out a large bowl and measure 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
The flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt are on the counter. Do I need anything else ready for the bowl?
Yes—have 1 teaspoon of cinnamon and some nutmeg ready too, since they get stirred in with those dry ingredients.
Bowl is ready. Should I combine all the dry stuff at once or hold anything back?
Go ahead and stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and nutmeg in the large bowl until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The dry mix looks even. How do I make space for the wet ingredients without making a mess?
Use the back of a spoon to make a well in the center of the dry mixture, leaving the flour mixture built up around the sides of the bowl.
I made the well. Which wet ingredients go into it?
Pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into the well in the center.
They're in the bowl now. Should I beat it hard or keep it gentle?
Mix until everything is well blended, scraping around the bottom and sides so no dry pockets remain.
The dough looks blended. What do I do before shaping or moving on?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour before you continue.
I'm making A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie and want to keep it simple. Can you walk me through it?
Absolutely. Set out a blender, a 10 ounce package of frozen mixed berries, a 15 ounce can of sliced peaches that you'll drain, and 2 tablespoons honey.
The berries are still frozen solid. Is that how they should go in?
Yes, use the frozen mixed berries straight from the package. They'll help make the smoothie cold and thick once blended.
I've opened the peaches. Should I pour off all the syrup before adding them?
Drain the sliced peaches before they go into the blender, then add the drained fruit with the frozen berries.
Berries and drained peaches are in the blender jar. Does the honey go in before blending?
Yes. Add the 2 tablespoons honey right on top of the fruit so everything can blend together at once.
The honey is in. Should I pulse it or just run the blender?
Start blending, and if the fruit catches around the blades, stop and scrape down the sides before blending again.
It's moving now but still has a few berry chunks. What texture am I looking for?
Keep blending until the smoothie looks smooth throughout, with no obvious peach slices or frozen berry pieces remaining.
It looks smooth and thick. Is there anything else to do before serving?
That's it for the recipe. Pour it into glasses right away while it's still cold and thick.
I'm making Dilly Chicken and Potatoes and want to cook along without missing anything.
Absolutely. Set out 1 broiler-fryer chicken, about 3 1/2 pounds, cut up, plus 1 pound of new potatoes cut into chunks. You'll also need a large skillet.
The chicken is cut up and the potatoes are chunked. What should I put by the stove?
Keep 2 tablespoons cooking oil ready, along with 1 cup half-and-half cream. Have salt and pepper nearby for the sauce at the end.
Skillet is on the stove. What heat should I use before the chicken goes in?
Set the large skillet over medium heat, add the cooking oil, and let it warm enough that the chicken and potatoes sizzle when they hit the pan.
Oil is shimmering. Do the chicken and potatoes go in together?
Yes, add the chicken pieces and the potato chunks together. Brown them in the oil for 10-15 minutes, turning the pieces so they pick up color on multiple sides.
They've browned for about 15 minutes, and there are drippings in the skillet. Should I leave everything in?
Lift out the chicken and potatoes and set them aside on a plate or platter for the moment. Keep the skillet and drippings on hand.
Chicken and potatoes are out. There's more fat in the pan than I expected.
Carefully discard the extra drippings, leaving just 1 tablespoon in the skillet. That small amount will flavor the cream mixture.
I've got about 1 tablespoon left. How do I make the creamy part?
Pour the 1 cup half-and-half cream into the drippings, then add salt and pepper. Stir until everything is mixed into a smooth, seasoned cream sauce.
I want to make British Bread Pudding today. Can you guide me while I set up the counter?
Absolutely. Put out a large mixing bowl and measure 6 1/4 cups cubed whole wheat bread, plus 1 1/4 cups milk. You'll also need the oven set later to 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C.
The bread cubes and milk are measured. Before I pour anything together, what other ingredients should be within reach?
Have 1 beaten egg ready and 1/3 cup softened butter. The mixing step also calls for raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon, so bring those over too.
Got it. My oven takes a while to heat—should I start that before soaking the bread?
Yes, turn the oven on now to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. That way it can heat while the bread softens.
Oven is heating. I've got the large bowl out; do I add the milk all at once?
Yes. Add the cubed whole wheat bread to the large bowl, pour in the 1 1/4 cups milk, and gently press or stir so the bread is moistened.
The bread is wet but still chunky. How long should it sit before I add the egg?
Let the bread and milk soak for 5 minutes. It should soften, but it doesn't need to become completely smooth.
The 5 minutes are up, and the bowl looks softer. What goes in next so I don't scramble the egg or leave butter lumps?

Stir in the beaten egg and the 1/3 cup softened butter, then add the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Mix steadily so the egg disappears into the soaked bread and the butter is distributed.
Everything is in the bowl now. What texture am I aiming for before I stop stirring?

Mix well until the fruit and spices are spread through the pudding mixture and there are no obvious streaks of egg or pockets of butter. Once it looks evenly combined, you've completed the listed prep for this British Bread Pudding.
I'm making Baked Salmon with Herbs tonight. Can you guide me through getting set up?
Absolutely. Start by gathering 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs and 4 minced garlic cloves for the crumb topping.
Those are on the counter. I also see Parmesan and dried parsley in the recipe—how much should I measure?
Measure 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes. Keep the thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper nearby too, since they get mixed in with the crumbs.
Before I mix anything, what pan should I use for the salmon?
Use a 15-in baking pan. Line it with foil, then coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray so the salmon is easier to lift off later.
Pan is lined and sprayed. Should the crumb mixture go in a small bowl or something larger?

A medium bowl is best. Combine the soft bread crumbs, minced garlic, Parmesan cheese, dried parsley flakes, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper, and stir so the herbs and cheese are spread through the crumbs.
The crumbs look evenly mixed, but they're still dry. Is that right?
Yes, they'll look dry until you add the butter. Pour in the butter and toss everything together until the crumbs are evenly coated.
After tossing with butter, should the salmon already be on the pan?
If it isn't yet, place the salmon on the prepared foil-lined pan now, skin-side down if your fillet has skin.
The salmon is on the pan. Anything I should check before adding the topping or moving on?
Make sure the salmon is sitting flat on the prepared pan and the crumb mixture is evenly moistened from the butter. Then you're ready to spread the herb crumbs over the fish for baking.
Can you help me make Dilled Garlic? I've got peeled garlic ready but want to make sure I set it up safely.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 pounds peeled garlic, 1 sprig of chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar. Also have sterile containers ready, since the garlic mixture goes straight into them.
The containers are sterilized and on the counter. Should the garlic go in whole with the dill?
Yes, pack the peeled garlic into the sterile containers with the chopped fresh dill and a little cayenne pepper, using as much cayenne as tastes right to you.
How full should I pack them? I don't want the hot vinegar to overflow.
Leave space at the top: fill the containers with the garlic, dill, and cayenne to within an inch of the top.
Okay, they're filled and there's room left. What pan should I use for the vinegar?
Use a medium saucepan. Pour in the distilled white vinegar, then mix in the salt called for in the instructions.
I've combined the vinegar and salt in the saucepan. Do I just warm it or does it need a full boil?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture to a boil so it's hot before it goes over the garlic.
It's boiling now. Should I turn off the heat before pouring?
Yes, take care with the hot liquid, then pour the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne.
The containers are filled. Is there anything else from the recipe before I clean up?
That completes the listed recipe steps: sterile containers filled with the garlic mixture, vinegar and salt boiled, and the hot mixture poured into the containers.
Can you help me make Avocado Tzatziki? I've got a bowl and a fork ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 large avocado, peeled and pitted, and 2 cloves garlic, minced. You'll be building everything in a medium bowl.
The avocado and garlic are ready. What else should go on the counter before I start mixing?
You'll also need 1 lemon, juiced, plus 1/4 cup sour cream if you want it creamier. The mixing step also includes cucumber, so have that ready too.
Okay, cucumber is prepped and the lemon is juiced. Do I add everything at once?
Yes. In the medium bowl, combine the avocado, minced garlic, lemon juice, sour cream if using it, and the cucumber.
It's all in the bowl. Should this be chunky like guacamole or smoother?
Use the fork to mash it until smooth. A few tiny bits are fine, but aim for a creamy tzatziki-style texture rather than chunky.
The texture looks pretty smooth now. What seasonings go in?
Stir in red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper. Mix well so the herbs and seasoning are evenly spread through the avocado mixture.
It smells good. Should I taste it before chilling?
Yes, taste for salt, pepper, lemon, and heat, then adjust lightly if needed. Once it tastes balanced, cover the bowl.
Covered. How long does it need in the fridge, and how should I serve it?
Refrigerate it for 1 hour before serving. After chilling, give it a quick stir and serve it as a dip or a cool sauce alongside your meal.
I'm making Beet and Pear Puree. Can you help me get set up before I start heating anything?
Absolutely. Pull out 8 medium beets, 1 pound unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, and 4 Bosc pears that are peeled, cored, and minced.
The beets are whole and the pears are prepped. What pan should I use for the beets?
Use a roasting pan for the beets. Before they go in, wash the beets well so any grit is removed.
Got it. Should the oven be hot already, or do I prep the beets first?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C. While it heats, you can finish washing the beets and arrange them in the roasting pan.
The oven is at temperature and the beets are in the pan. How long should they roast?
Bake them for 45 minutes to 1 hour, checking for tenderness near the end. They should feel tender when pierced.
If some beets are softer before others, should I wait until all of them are tender?
Yes, let the batch roast until the beets are tender overall. Once they're done, take the pan out and set the beets aside to cool.
The beets are cooling now. I have a large skillet ready for the onion and pear part.
Place the large skillet over medium heat and add the 1 pound unsalted butter so it can melt evenly.
The butter is melting. Are the minced Vidalia onions and Bosc pears next?
Yes, keep the 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions and the 4 minced Bosc pears close by. The next move after this provided step is to use that melted butter as the base for them.
Can you guide me through making Chicken Tacos? I've got a skillet ready and want to make sure I prep the chicken right.
Absolutely. Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces so they cook evenly in the skillet.
The chicken is cut up. What liquids should I put near the stove before I turn on the heat?
Measure out 1 cup lemonade, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 1 tablespoon lime juice. You'll also need Worcestershire sauce for the skillet.
I have the lemonade, oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce. Do I add everything cold to the pan or heat it first?
Set a large skillet over medium heat, then add the chicken, lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce together in the pan.
It's in the skillet and starting to bubble a little. What seasonings go in now?
Season the mixture with garlic powder, onion powder, and a bay leaf. Stir so the chicken pieces are coated in the liquid and seasoning.
The chicken is coated. Should I cover it, or just let it simmer open?
Let it simmer until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, about 15 to 20 minutes. Stir occasionally so the pieces cook evenly.
I'm at around 15 minutes and the pieces look cooked through. How can I time the tortillas with this?
While the chicken finishes, warm the tortillas in the oven or microwave until they're soft and flexible.
The tortillas are soft, and the chicken juices look clear. Anything to do before serving?
Remove the bay leaf, give the chicken a quick stir, and spoon it into the warm tortillas while everything is hot.
Can you help me make Easy Pot Roast? I've got a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast on the counter and want to be sure I set it up right.
Absolutely. Start by preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the roast is bagged and seasoned.
Oven is heating. Besides the roast, what should I pull out before I open the oven bag?
You'll need 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.
I found the soup mix and Worcestershire. Should I trim the meat or do anything to the surface first?
No trimming is called for here. Score the roast across the top and sides, making shallow cuts so the seasoning mixture can settle in.
Scored it. I have a medium sized oven bag ready—does the roast go in before the liquid?
Yes. Place the scored chuck roast in the medium sized oven bag first, keeping it centered so there's room around it.
It's in the bag. How do I mix the sauce without making it clumpy?
Stir the 2 cups water with the dry onion and mushroom soup mix until the mix is mostly dispersed, then blend in the 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.
The mixture looks combined. Do I pour it over one spot or all around the meat?
Pour it over the roast, letting it run across the scored top and down the sides so the liquid collects in the bag around the meat.
I was planning to add vegetables too. Where should they go before it heads into the oven?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag, not piled on top, so the roast stays exposed to the sauce while the vegetables cook alongside it.

original_cues.support_assistant_cue: Chop the soft herbs small, stir part of them into the food near the end, and keep the rest fresh for a final scatter.
original_cues.support_feedback_cue: That works better than big leaves all over the top.
original_cues.support_user_cue: For Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce, I want the herbs worked through instead of just sitting there.

memory_annotations.support_assistant_cue: Sure. Keep the herb pieces fine: fold some into the warm garlic-wine sauce near the end so they spread through it, then use just a small fresh pinch over the chicken before serving.
memory_annotations.support_feedback_cue: That sounds like how I usually prefer it—herbs tucked into the sauce instead of scattered as oversized leaves. What oven setting am I using?
memory_annotations.support_user_cue: I'm making Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce, and I'd like any tender herbs mixed into the dish rather than left in big pieces on top.

messages.content: I'm making Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce, and I'd like any tender herbs mixed into the dish rather than left in big pieces on top.
Sure. Keep the herb pieces fine: fold some into the warm garlic-wine sauce near the end so they spread through it, then use just a small fresh pinch over the chicken before serving.
Before I start heating anything, what should be on the counter?
Set out 1 medium head of garlic and 1 tablespoon olive oil first, since the garlic needs roasting before the sauce comes together.
I've got the garlic and oil. I'm pulling a baking dish out—do I need the chicken yet?
Yes, have 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts ready, and measure 1/2 cup white wine for the sauce.
That sounds like how I usually prefer it—herbs tucked into the sauce instead of scattered as oversized leaves. What oven setting am I using?
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
Oven is heating. How much do I cut off the garlic head?
Slice just enough off the top of the garlic head to remove the papery tips and expose the tops of the cloves.
The cloves are showing. Should I use foil or is my little covered garlic roaster okay?
Either works. Drizzle the exposed garlic with the olive oil, then roast it in the preheated oven in the clay garlic roaster, or wrap it in aluminum foil if you prefer easier cleanup.
It's in the oven now. How long should I let it go, and what should I look for?
Roast it for 20 minutes, or until the cloves feel soft and slip out of their skins when gently pushed.
Once the garlic is soft, how do I keep the sauce smooth with the wine and chicken?

Squeeze the roasted cloves from their skins and mash them into the 1/2 cup white wine as the base for the roasted garlic sauce. Spoon it with the chicken breasts, then mix in the finely chopped herbs near the end so they season the sauce without turning into a leafy topping.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Chicken with Roasted Garlic Sauce

messages.content: Can you help me make Buffalo Chicken Wings I? I've got the wings out and want to keep the steps straight.
Absolutely. You'll need 24 chicken wings and 2 quarts of vegetable oil for deep frying. Set up a large skillet or deep fryer, and keep a draining area ready for the cooked wings.
The oil and wings are ready. What should I pull out for the sauce before I start frying?
Have 4 tablespoons butter, 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar, hot sauce, salt, and pepper nearby. The sauce comes together quickly after the wings are cooked.
I'm using a deep fryer. How long should the wings cook?
Fry the chicken wings in the hot vegetable oil until they're done, about 10 minutes. Work carefully and avoid crowding if your fryer is small.
They've been frying and look crisp. What do I do with the oil and the chicken now?
Take the chicken out and set it aside to drain. Then remove the oil from the skillet or fryer area according to your usual safe cleanup method, keeping the cooked wings reserved.
The wings are draining. Should I make the sauce in the same skillet?
Yes, if the skillet is safe to use after draining the oil. Melt the 4 tablespoons butter in it, then stir in the 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar and the hot sauce.
How should the sauce look before I put it on the wings?
It should be melted together and glossy, with the butter, vinegar, and hot sauce combined into a loose coating sauce.
The sauce is mixed. What's the last thing before serving?
Season the wings with salt and pepper to taste, then coat or serve them with the buffalo sauce while they're hot.
Can you help me make BBQ Chicken Wings? I want to get the marinade set up correctly before I touch the grill.
Absolutely. For the sauce base, set out 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce and 1 cup oyster sauce in a large bowl or somewhere easy to measure from.
I've got the large bowl out and those two sauces measured. What else goes into the bowl?
Add 1/4 cup soy sauce and 1/4 cup ketchup. Those join the teriyaki and oyster sauce as the main marinade mixture.
Okay, the four measured ingredients are in. The recipe mentions more flavorings too, right?
Yes. Stir in the garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar with the sauces until the marinade looks evenly combined.
It's mixed and smells pretty strong. Do the wings go straight in now?
Yes, place the chicken wings into the bowl and turn them so they're coated all over. Cover the bowl before it goes into the refrigerator.
How long should I leave them in the fridge if I'm trying to plan dinner?
Give them 8 hours if you can, or let them marinate overnight. That time is what lets the sauce soak into the wings.
They've been marinating overnight. What should I do before putting them on the grill?
Preheat the grill for low heat so it's ready for gentle cooking rather than a hot sear.
The grill is warming up. Anything I should do to keep the wings from sticking?
Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the wings. Once the grate is oiled and the grill is at low heat, you're ready to start cooking them.
Can you help me make Chocolate Chews? I've got the saucepan out and want to start in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips and 1/2 cup softened butter so they're ready when you need them.
Chocolate chips and softened butter are on the counter. Are there any sugars I should measure before heating anything?
Yes—measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them separate from the chocolate for the moment.
Both sugars are measured. Should I melt the chocolate in the heavy saucepan now?
Yes. Put the semisweet chocolate chips in the heavy saucepan and melt them over very low heat so they don't scorch.
They're starting to soften around the edges. Should I leave them alone or stir?
Stir gently as they melt so the chocolate becomes smooth and evenly melted.
The chocolate is smooth now. Do I mix the butter into that, or work on the butter separately?
Work on the butter separately: cream the 1/2 cup softened butter with the 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar until the mixture looks light.
I'm creaming it now. What texture tells me it's ready for the eggs?
It should look lighter in color and a bit fluffy, with the sugars well worked into the butter.
That looks right. How do the eggs go in?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, letting each one blend into the butter-sugar mixture before adding the next.

messages.content: When we make Aaahh Potato Soup, can we start the way I like it, with a very thin-cut allium softened before everything soupy goes in?

Yes. Before adding the potatoes, broth, water, and au gratin mix, thinly cut whichever allium you're using—onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot—and let it soften gently in the large pot so it gives the soup a savory base.
Great. I've got a large saucepan out. Which actual soup ingredients should I put near the stove first?
Set out 2 Yukon Gold potatoes, cubed, plus 1 (5.5 ounce) package of au gratin instant potato mix. Keep the pot ready for that softened allium base.
The potatoes are cubed, and the packet is open but not dumped in yet. What liquids am I measuring?
You'll need 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed chicken broth and 1 1/2 cups water. Have a little extra water nearby in case the potatoes need to be covered.
Perfect, that thin allium start is exactly the way I usually want this soup to begin. Mine is softened now; should the potatoes go in?
Yes. Add the cubed Yukon Gold potatoes to the pot, then stir in the au gratin potato mix, the condensed chicken broth, and the 1 1/2 cups water.
It looks thick already, and a few potato pieces are peeking above the liquid. Is that okay?
Add just enough more water to cover the potatoes if necessary. You don't need to flood it—just make sure the potato cubes can cook evenly.
Covered now. What heat should I use, and how often do I need to stir?
Cook it over medium heat, stirring occasionally so the instant mix doesn't settle too much on the bottom. Let it go until the potatoes are tender, about 40 minutes.
At around 40 minutes, how do I judge the potatoes without overworking the soup?
Press a potato cube with a spoon or pierce one with a fork. If it gives easily and the soup looks cohesive, you're ready for the creamy finish.
The potatoes are tender. I noticed cream in the directions, but I don't have a measured amount listed—how should I handle the last part?
Stir in the cream gently and heat it through without bringing the soup to a hard boil. Once it's hot and the texture looks right to you, give it a final stir and serve.
I want to make Golden Cheese Yeast Bread this afternoon. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got a big bowl and a floured counter ready.
Absolutely. Set out 6 cups all-purpose flour and 2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese to start. You'll use only 3 cups of the flour in the bowl at the beginning, and the rest gets worked in later.
The flour is measured and the Cheddar is shredded. What should I put beside the bowl next?

Add 3 tablespoons sugar and 2 (.25 ounce) packages active dry yeast to your setup. You'll also need salt for the first mix, plus milk and an egg for the next stage, though this recipe doesn't give amounts for those here.
Got it. I'm ready to start mixing the dry ingredients; should the cheese go in right away?
Yes. In the large mixing bowl, combine 3 cups of the flour with the shredded Cheddar, sugar, active dry yeast, and salt. Stir it well so the yeast and cheese are evenly distributed through the flour.
The dry mix looks even, with the cheese scattered through it. I have the mixer on the counter—what speed am I using?
Pour in the milk and add the egg, then beat the mixture on low speed until it looks smooth. Keep it slow so the flour doesn't puff out of the bowl.
It's smoothing out now, but it's still more like a thick batter than dough. Is that expected?
Yes, that's fine at this point. Start stirring in the remaining flour a bit at a time, using enough to turn it into a soft dough rather than a sticky batter.
I've added more flour, and the dough is soft but still slightly tacky. Should I keep adding flour or turn it out?
If it holds together and only feels lightly tacky, turn it onto a floured surface. Dust your hands and the counter as needed rather than dumping in too much extra flour all at once.
It's on the counter now. How long should I knead, and what texture am I aiming for?
Knead it until the dough becomes smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. It should feel springy, hold together cleanly, and look more even as the Cheddar is worked through.
Can you guide me through making Citrus Infused Guacamole? I've got a bowl and a couple of ripe avocados ready.
Absolutely. Peel and pit 2 avocados, then mash them in a large bowl until they're as smooth or chunky as you like.
The avocados are mashed. I see three juices in the recipe—how much of each goes in?
Add 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice to the mashed avocados.
All three juices are in. Should I stir them gently or really mash everything together?
Stir until the juices are evenly worked through the avocado. Then mix in the cumin, cilantro, and salt so the seasoning is distributed throughout.
That's mixed. The texture is creamy with a few small avocado pieces—does that sound right?
Yes, that works well for guacamole. Taste it now and adjust only if needed, keeping the citrus flavor balanced with the cumin, cilantro, and salt.
I have hot pepper sauce on the counter. Is that part of this, or optional?
It's optional. If you want heat, mix in the hot pepper sauce a little at a time so it doesn't overpower the citrus.
I added a small splash and stirred it in. I saved the avocado pits—do I use one?
Yes. Place one of the avocado pits into the bowl; it can help keep the guacamole fresh until you serve it.
I'm not serving for a little while. Should I leave it out or put it away?
Serve it immediately if you're ready, or refrigerate it until serving. Keep the pit in the bowl while it chills.
Can you help me make Grandmas Gingersnaps? I've got the mixer out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses so the main wet ingredients are ready.
The margarine and sugar are measured, and the egg and molasses are on the counter. Should I turn on the oven now?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) before you start mixing so it has time to come up to temperature.
Oven is heating. What bowl should I use for the dough?
Use a medium bowl for the first mixture. Add the 3/4 cup margarine and 1 cup white sugar, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's getting lighter and smoother, but there are a few streaks of margarine on the side of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides, then mix a little longer until the margarine and sugar are evenly blended and no obvious streaks remain.
That looks smooth now. Do the egg and molasses go in together?
Yes. Beat in the 1 egg and the 1/4 cup molasses, mixing until everything is well blended and the color looks even.
The mixture is glossy and dark from the molasses. What dry ingredients should I combine?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt. Whisking or stirring them together first helps distribute the spices and baking soda evenly.
Dry ingredients are mixed. How do I bring it all together without overdoing it?
Stir the dry mixture into the molasses mixture just until it forms a dough. Stop once there are no dry patches; the gingersnap dough should be cohesive rather than heavily beaten.

messages.content: For Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup, can we handle the onion my way—thin slices softened before the broth goes in?
Yes. Use thin slices for the onion, and treat the garlic the same way if you're adding it: let them soften in the oil with the vegetables before any liquid is added.
Good. I've got a large pot out. What should I put on the counter before I turn on the stove?
Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 medium onion, 1 green bell pepper, and 1 large carrot. Peel the carrot and slice it thinly; chop the bell pepper.
The carrot is sliced, the pepper is chopped, and the onion is in thin half-moons. Should I heat the pot now?
Go ahead and warm the large pot over medium heat, then add the 2 tablespoons vegetable oil so it can shimmer lightly.
Yes, thin onion before the liquid is the way I like this kind of soup. The oil is hot now.
Add the onion slices, bell pepper, thin carrot slices, and garlic to the pot. Stir them around in the oil and cook for 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the onion has softened.
The onion has relaxed and the carrot is starting to bend. Should I keep cooking or add the beans?
If the vegetables are tender, add 1 can of black beans along with the chicken broth. Stir well so the softened onion and vegetables mix into the broth.
I added the beans and broth. The soup looks a little thin; is that expected before blending?
Yes, that's fine at this point. The remaining can of beans gets pureed, and that smooth bean mixture will help thicken the soup.
I have the blender ready. Do I drain the remaining beans or just puree them?
The recipe only says to puree the remaining can of beans until smooth, so use that can for the blender and blend until the texture is silky.
The puree is smooth. How should I bring it together for serving?
Stir the smooth bean puree back into the pot, let everything heat through, and check the texture. Once it looks cohesive and hot, it's ready to serve.

messages.content: For Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake, can we treat the cilantro or parsley in my usual chopped-in-and-fresh-scattered style?
Yes. If you're adding cilantro or parsley, chop the soft leaves finely, work some in near the end, and hold the rest back so it stays bright for a final scatter.
Thanks. Before I start mixing, should I deal with the oven and pans?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Then grease and flour 2 (9 inch) pans so they're ready before the batter comes together.
The pans are out. What ingredients should I measure into bowls?
For the dry bowl, measure 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Also chop 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate and keep that nearby.
Good, that herb distribution is exactly how I usually want it. For the cake, do the flour, baking soda, and salt all go together now?
Yes, put the flour, baking soda, and salt together, then sift them so the leavening and salt are evenly spread through the flour.
Should I put the chopped unsweetened chocolate through the sifter too?
No, keep the chopped chocolate separate for now. The sifting step is only for the flour, baking soda, and salt.
The oven is heating, and the greased pans have a light flour coating. Any pan cleanup before I move on?
Tap out any loose excess flour from the pans so it doesn't clump, then set the pans aside near your work area while the oven finishes heating.
The sifted dry mixture still has a couple of tiny lumps. Is that a problem?
If the lumps are from flour or baking soda, pass the mixture through the sifter once more or break them up with a whisk. You want the flour, baking soda, and salt evenly combined.
Okay, the dry bowl looks even now. What should I do with it while I wait for the next part?
Set the sifted flour mixture aside. Keep the chopped unsweetened chocolate separate, leave the prepared pans ready, and hold the chopped herbs for their near-end stir-in and fresh finishing scatter.
