messages.content: When we make Coconut Ambrosia Salad, can you help me mix the herbs into the salad instead of leaving them as a leafy topping?
Yes. Keep any tender herbs finely chopped, fold some in with the creamy fruit mixture near the end, and save a small pinch to sprinkle on just before serving so the salad still looks fresh.
I've got a big mixing bowl out. Which cans should I open and drain first?
Open and drain 1 (11 ounce) can of mandarin oranges and 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple. Let them sit in a strainer for a minute so the salad doesn't turn watery.
They're draining now. What cold stuff should come out of the freezer or fridge?
Set out 3 1/2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed. You'll also need 2 cups shredded coconut, plus the marshmallows and milk called for when everything gets combined.
Yes, finely chopped and folded in is much more my style than scattered whole leaves on top.

Then we'll keep that approach here: once the fruit, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows, and milk are together, fold the chopped herbs through gently so they're distributed without crushing the oranges.
Should the oranges and pineapple go into the bowl before the whipped topping?
Add the drained mandarin oranges and crushed pineapple to the large bowl first. Spoon the thawed whipped topping over them, then add the shredded coconut, marshmallows, and milk.
The bowl is full. How much mixing are we talking about?
Use a wide spatula and fold until the fruit, coconut, whipped topping, marshmallows, and milk look evenly coated. Stop once it's combined so the oranges stay mostly intact.
When do I add the herbs without making them look wilted?
Fold most of the finely chopped herbs in after the salad is mixed. Cover the bowl and chill it for 1 hour before serving; keep a little herb aside, fresh and dry, for the final touch.
It's chilled. I have cherries ready too—how should I serve it?

Give the salad one gentle stir, spoon it into the serving dish, garnish with cherries, and add that reserved pinch of chopped herbs right at the end. Serve cold while the whipped topping is still fluffy.
Can you help me get Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken started? I want to make sure I have the glaze ingredients measured before I touch the chicken.

Absolutely. For the glaze, measure 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum. You'll also need mustard and garlic for the glaze, plus salt and pepper to season it.
I've got the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and rum measured. Should I mix them in a bowl or straight in the baking dish?
Use a medium bowl for the glaze so it combines smoothly before it goes on the chicken. Add the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, dark rum, mustard, and garlic to that bowl.
The molasses is pretty thick. Do I need to warm it, or just keep stirring?
Just keep stirring in the bowl; the pineapple juice and rum will help loosen it. Once everything looks evenly blended, season the glaze with salt and pepper to taste and mix it well again.
The glaze is glossy and mixed. What dish should I use for the chicken pieces?
Use a lightly oiled 9x13 inch baking dish. Arrange the chicken pieces in a single layer if you can, so the glaze can coat them evenly.
Chicken is in the oiled dish. Do I pour all the glaze over it now?
Brush both sides of the chicken pieces with the prepared glaze, but use only about 1/2 of the glaze at this point. Save the rest for later.
Both sides are brushed and I still have the remaining glaze set aside. Does it go straight into the oven?
Not yet. Cover the baking dish and refrigerate the chicken so it can marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight if you have the time.
If I marinate it overnight, should the extra glaze stay separate too?

Yes, keep the remaining glaze covered and refrigerated separately while the chicken marinates. When you're ready to continue, the chicken will already have that sweet, tangy Caribbean Canadian glaze base soaked in.
Can you help me make Chili For Two? I've got a small saucepan out, but I want to make sure I'm not missing anything.
Absolutely. For this chili, you'll need 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 garlic clove minced, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can chili beans, kept undrained.
The beef is thawed and the onion is chopped. Should I open the beans now or wait?
You can open the chili beans now and keep the liquid with them. They'll go in after the beef, onion, and garlic have cooked.
Got it. The garlic is minced too. What heat should I use for the beef mixture?
Set the saucepan over medium heat. Add the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic, then cook while breaking up the beef until the meat is no longer pink.
The beef is browned and the onion looks softened. There's some grease in the pan.
Drain off the grease, then return the saucepan to the heat. After that, stir in the undrained 15.5 ounce can of chili beans.
Beans are stirred in. Do I just warm it, or should it boil?
Bring the chili up to a boil, stirring occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick to the bottom.
It's bubbling now. I don't want it splattering everywhere.
Reduce the heat, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, just until everything is heated through.
After 15 minutes, it's hot and a little thicker. Is it ready to serve?
Yes, it's ready. Give it a quick stir, check that it's heated through, then ladle it into two bowls and serve while warm.
Can you help me make Cookie Paints for a batch of cutout cookies?
Absolutely. You only need 2 tablespoons evaporated milk and 4 drops red food coloring, plus a small bowl, a spoon, and a clean paintbrush for decorating the cookies before they bake.
I've got the evaporated milk open. Should I measure it right into the bowl?
Yes, measure the evaporated milk into a small bowl so there's enough room to stir without splashing.
The milk is in the bowl. Do I add all the food coloring at once?
Add the red food coloring directly to the evaporated milk, then stir until the color looks evenly blended.
It looks a little streaky after a few stirs. Is that okay?
Keep stirring for a moment longer, scraping around the bottom and sides of the bowl. The paint should look uniform before you use it on the cookies.
Okay, it's an even red now. My cookies are cut out on the tray but not baked yet.
Perfect timing. Dip the paintbrush lightly into the cookie paint and brush it onto the unbaked cookies wherever you want color.
Should I coat the whole cookie or just make designs?
Either works, but use a light layer so the cookie surface doesn't get too wet. Designs, stripes, or small painted areas are easiest to control.
The cookies are painted. Anything special before they go in the oven?
Just make sure the painted tops aren't dripping or pooled with liquid, then bake the cookies according to your cookie recipe's directions.
Can you help me make an Awesome Turkey Sandwich for lunch? I've got a cutting board out and can toast the bread if needed.

Absolutely. Start by getting 2 slices of whole wheat bread ready; toast them if you want a warmer, sturdier sandwich. You'll also need 1 tablespoon mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard, and 3 slices smoked turkey breast.
The bread is toasted, and I found the mayo, Dijon, and turkey. The instructions mention toppings too—should I pull those out now?
Yes, set out the guacamole, salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese so assembly goes smoothly once the spreads are on.
Everything is on the counter. Should the mayo and mustard go on the same slice or separate slices?
Put the mayonnaise on one slice of toast and the Dijon mustard on the other slice. Spread each all the way to the edges so every bite has flavor.
Done. The mayo slice is on the left and mustard slice is on the right—where does the turkey go?
Arrange the 3 slices of smoked turkey breast on one side, overlapping them slightly so the layer is even and doesn't slide around.
Turkey is down. Do I add guacamole directly on top of it, or should it go on the bread?
Spread the guacamole over the turkey. A gentle, even layer works best so you don't drag the turkey slices out of place.
Got it. The guacamole is on, and I have greens, sprouts, avocado, and cheese waiting.
Pile on the salad greens, then add the bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese. Keep the taller, loose greens toward the center so the sandwich closes more neatly.
It's stacked pretty high. Any trick for closing and serving it without everything falling out?
Bring the other slice of toast over carefully, press down lightly with your palm, and cut it in half with a sharp knife. If it's very full, hold it together with toothpicks before serving.
I'm making Basil Burgers on the grill tonight. Can you guide me without rushing through the prep?

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt. You'll also want a bowl for mixing, a plate or tray for the patties, and a little oil for the grill grate.
The beef is in the bowl, and I've got the Worcestershire and seasonings measured. Should the grill be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and preheat an outdoor grill for high heat while you mix the burgers. That way the grate will be hot when the patties are shaped.
Grill is heating. How do I combine everything without making the burgers tough?

Add the Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and a little pepper to the ground beef. Mix gently with your hands or a fork just until the seasonings look evenly distributed; try not to mash it too much.
The mixture smells good and looks evenly seasoned. How many patties am I shaping from this?

Shape the mixture into 4 burger patties. Keep them fairly even in thickness so they cook at the same pace, and make a slight shallow dip in the center if you want to help them stay flatter on the grill.
I've got 4 patties on a tray. Do I oil the burgers or the grill?
Lightly oil the grill grate rather than soaking the patties. Use tongs and an oiled paper towel or your usual grill-safe method, then place the burgers on the hot grate.
They're on the grill now. What timing should I watch for?
Cook them about 6 minutes total, turning once. Keep the lid position consistent if you can, and avoid pressing down on the patties so the juices stay in.
I turned them once and I'm checking with a thermometer. What temperature am I aiming for?

For the recipe's doneness target, cook the burgers to an internal temperature of 160 degrees F, which is 70 degrees C, or to your desired doneness. Once they're there, take them off the grill and let them sit briefly before serving.

Yes. Mince the cilantro or parsley finely, fold some in near the end so it blends through the Biriyani, and save a little to scatter on fresh before serving.
Great. I've got the skillet out—what should I put near the stove before I start heating anything?
Set out 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 tablespoons plain yogurt first. Keep a large skillet ready for medium heat.
Oil and yogurt are measured. I still need the sharp or tangy pieces—what else should be on the board?
Add 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar to your setup, and slice 1 medium onion so it can go straight into the skillet when needed.
That's the way I like the herbs here—tiny bits through the dish, not oversized leaves sitting on top. Is the oil the next move?
Yes. Pour the olive oil into the large skillet and warm it over medium heat until it loosens and shimmers lightly.
The oil is shimmering, and I've got the yogurt and vinegar close. Do they go in together?
Mix in the plain yogurt and the distilled white vinegar, stirring so they combine with the hot oil in the skillet.
It looks a little creamy now. Should the sliced onion go in before the garlic and ginger paste?
Yes, place the sliced onion in the skillet now and cook it until tender, stirring so it softens evenly.
The onion is soft and starting to smell sweet. I have garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes waiting.

Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 softened 3 ounce package of cream cheese, 1 egg, 1 medium onion finely chopped, and 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs. You'll also need a mixing bowl and your grill ready for later.
The cream cheese is soft, and I've got the egg out. Should I chop the onion before mixing anything?
Yes, finely chop the medium onion now so it blends evenly into the mixture. Once it's chopped, add the cream cheese, egg, onion, and dry bread crumbs to the bowl.
Everything is in the bowl. The cream cheese is a little firm in spots; should I mash it in?

Mash and stir it until the ingredients are combined as evenly as you can get them. The recipe says to combine the first seven ingredients, so focus on getting this base mixture smooth enough to hold together.
The mixture looks fairly even now. I have the beef and sausage nearby—how do I add them without overworking it?
Crumble the beef and sausage over the bowl rather than dropping them in as big chunks. Then mix well, but use a light hand so the meat mixture comes together without becoming dense.
It's mixed and holding together. What size should I make the burgers?
Divide the mixture into eight portions and shape them into patties. Try to make them similar in thickness so they grill at the same pace.
The patties are shaped. Should the grill be super hot or more moderate?
Use medium-hot heat and grill the patties uncovered. Plan on 4-6 minutes on each side.
After turning them once, what signs should I check before serving?
They're ready when they're no longer pink in the center. Let them come off the grill once they've had 4-6 minutes per side and the centers look fully cooked.

Put the butter or margarine in the large skillet so it can melt, then add the cubed potatoes, ham, and chopped onion together.

Keep the mixture moving with frequent stirring. You're looking for the potatoes to become lightly browned while the ham heats and the onion cooks into the butter.
The potatoes are starting to brown around the edges. There's broccoli here too—when does that go in?
Add the broccoli once the potatoes are lightly browned, then stir it through the hash and let it heat until warmed through.

Set out 16 cups popped popcorn, 1 cup roasted peanuts, 1 cup brown sugar, and 1/2 cup butter. You'll also need corn syrup, vanilla, and salt for the microwave-safe bowl.

Transfer the popped popcorn and roasted peanuts into a paper bag; that gives you room to shake or coat them later.

Yes, set the bag aside while you work on the caramel base.

Combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in the microwave-safe bowl.

Right: use 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter, then add the corn syrup, vanilla, and salt as the recipe calls for.
Once that mixture is in the bowl, what should my setup look like so I don't scramble at the end?
Keep the greased cookie sheets nearby, with the paper bag of popcorn and peanuts set aside and ready for coating after the microwave mixture is combined.
I'm making Baked Fake Steak with Gravy. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?

Absolutely. Set out 3 pounds ground beef, 17 saltine crackers finely crushed, 1/2 cup milk, and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder. You'll also want onion powder, salt, and pepper for seasoning, plus a large mixing bowl.
I've got the beef in a bowl and the crackers crushed. Should the milk go in with them right away?
Yes. Add the crushed saltines and the 1/2 cup milk to the ground beef, then mix them together in the large bowl until the crackers and milk are distributed through the meat.
The mixture is coming together, but I don't want to overwork it. What texture should I stop at?
Stop once it looks evenly combined and holds together without dry cracker patches. It should be blended, but you don't need to knead it heavily.
Where does the garlic powder fit in, and how much am I using?
Sprinkle in 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, then season with onion powder, salt, and pepper. Mix again just until the seasonings are well blended through the beef mixture.
Seasoning is mixed in. What pan should I prepare?
Use a 10x15 inch jellyroll pan. Line it with waxed paper so the beef mixture can be pressed into an even sheet.
The waxed paper is sliding around while I try to spread the meat. Any trick for that?
Hold the paper steady at one corner while you add the beef mixture, then press from the center outward. Firm, even pressure will help it fill the pan without bunching the paper.
It's mostly spread out now. How firm should I press it into the pan?
Press it firmly enough that the mixture is compact and even across the 10x15 inch pan, with the corners filled and the thickness as consistent as you can make it.

I'm setting up the counter now. Which pie items should I pull out before I touch the oven?
Put the pastry and filling within reach: you'll need 1 recipe pastry for a 9 inch double crust pie and 1 (21 ounce) can apple pie filling. Keep your 9 inch pie pan nearby too.
The pastry, filling can, and pie pan are out. I also have my spice jars open; remind me of the exact amounts.
Measure 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg. If you're adding the warmer note, use only a restrained pinch of cardamom and ginger alongside them.
Yes, that gentle cardamom and ginger lift is what I usually mean for fruit sweets. What should happen first?
Turn the oven on to 425 degrees F, which is 220 degrees C, so it can heat while you work with the pastry.
Oven is heating. My pastry is still wrapped; do I roll both crusts right away?
Roll out the pastry shell you'll use first, then let it rest in the refrigerator. Since the recipe uses pastry for a 9 inch double crust pie, keep the remaining pastry chilled until you need it.
The rolled pastry is chilling. Should I grease the pie pan or just line it?
Follow the recipe direction and line the 9 inch pie pan with one rolled out pastry crust. Ease it in gently so it sits against the bottom and sides without stretching.
The crust is in the pan. I'm ready to mix the apples; what goes into the bowl?
Use a medium mixing bowl. Combine the 21 ounce can of apple pie filling with the cinnamon, nutmeg, and the lemon rind called for in the directions.
Should I fold in the extra warm spices with the apple filling now or sprinkle them later?

Fold the small cardamom-and-ginger accent in with the apple filling now, along with the 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg. Mix gently, just until the spices are evenly distributed and the fruit pieces stay intact.
I'm making Chili For Two. Can you guide me through it from the ingredients onward?
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans. Keep the beans undrained for this recipe.
I've got a small saucepan ready. Should the beef, onion, and garlic all go in together?
Yes. Put the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic into the saucepan and cook them over medium heat, stirring and breaking up the beef as it cooks.
How do I know when that part is cooked enough?
Cook until the meat is no longer pink and the onion has softened a bit. Once it reaches that point, drain off the excess fat from the saucepan.
The beef is browned and I drained it. The pan looks a little dry now.
That's fine because the chili beans go in undrained. Stir the entire 15.5 ounce can of chili beans into the beef mixture, including the liquid from the can.
Beans and liquid are stirred in. Do I just heat it gently or bring it up higher?
Bring the mixture to a boil first, stirring occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick on the bottom.
It's bubbling now around the edges and starting to boil in the middle.
Turn the heat down, cover the saucepan, and let the chili simmer for 10-15 minutes, just until everything is heated through.
After 10 minutes it smells done, but I want to be sure before serving.

Give it a stir and check that it's hot throughout. If it still seems a little thin or not fully heated, let it simmer covered for a few more minutes within that 10-15 minute window, then serve it warm.
Can you help me make Grandmas Gnocchi? I'm starting from whole russet potatoes and want to keep the prep organized.

Absolutely. Set out 6 russet potatoes, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg that's lightly beaten, and 1 tablespoon olive oil. You'll also want a large pot, salt for the water, a fork for mashing, and a colander for draining.
The potatoes are washed, and I've got the flour, egg, and olive oil measured. Do I peel the potatoes before boiling?
Leave them whole for the boil. Fill a large pot with water, salt it well, and bring it to a boil before adding the potatoes.
The pot is heating now. How much attention do the potatoes need once they go in?
Once the water is boiling, drop in the potatoes carefully. Let them cook until they're tender but still firm, about 15 minutes, so they mash cleanly without getting waterlogged.
What's the best way to check that tender-but-firm texture without overdoing them?
Pierce one with a fork or small knife. It should slide in without much resistance, but the potato shouldn't be falling apart or splitting heavily in the water.
They've cooked about 15 minutes and pass the fork check. Should I save any of the water?
No need for the cooking water in this part. Drain the potatoes in a colander, then let them cool just enough that you can handle them safely.
They're drained and still warm. Do I peel them right away or wait until they're cold?
Peel them while they're still warm but comfortable to touch. The skins should come off more easily, and the warm potatoes will mash better.
The peeled potatoes are in a bowl. How should I handle the mashing before adding the other ingredients?
Season the potatoes with salt, then mash them with a fork until they're broken down and fairly smooth. Keep the flour, beaten egg, and olive oil nearby for the next stage of the gnocchi dough.
Can you help me make Baked Fake Steak with Gravy? I've got the ground beef out but want to set up the rest before my hands get messy.
Absolutely. Set out 3 pounds ground beef, 17 finely crushed saltine crackers, 1/2 cup milk, and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder. You'll also use onion powder, salt, and pepper for seasoning.
The crackers are crushed pretty fine. Do I need a specific bowl for mixing all of this?
Use a large bowl so you have room to combine everything evenly without compacting it too early. Add the ground beef, crushed saltines, and milk to the bowl.
Should I mix that with a spoon, or is it better by hand?
Clean hands are easiest here. Gently work the beef, crackers, and milk together until the crumbs are distributed, but try not to overwork the meat.
The mixture is together. When do the seasonings go in?
Sprinkle in the 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, then add onion powder, salt, and pepper. Mix again until the seasonings look well blended throughout the beef.
It looks evenly seasoned now. What pan should I use?
Line a 10x15 inch jellyroll pan with waxed paper. Press the paper into the corners so the beef mixture will spread out evenly.
I have the pan lined. Is the meat supposed to be loose or packed in firmly?
Pack it firmly into the lined pan. Press it out to an even thickness across the pan so it holds together like a formed steak base.
Any tips for keeping the surface even and not sticking to my fingers?
Use the flat of your hand or a spatula to smooth it, pressing gently but firmly. If it sticks, slightly dampen your hands, then finish leveling the beef mixture in the pan.
I'm making Grand Marnier Chicken and I've got chicken breasts out. Can you help me prep it without getting ahead of the recipe?
Absolutely. For this prep, you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, 1 cup milk, 1 cup dry bread crumbs, and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese.
The milk, bread crumbs, and Parmesan are on the counter. What should I do with the chicken before anything goes in a dish?
Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thirds so you end up with 12 thin chicken fillets total. Take your time and keep the pieces as even as you can.
I'm using a sharp knife and a cutting board. Should they be super thin, or just thinner than the original breasts?
They should be thin fillets, but they don't need to be paper-thin. The recipe's goal is 12 pieces from the 4 breasts, so thirds horizontally is the main guide.
Okay, I have the 12 pieces cut. They're a little uneven in thickness.
That's fine. Lightly pound each piece so the fillets are more even. Use gentle taps rather than smashing them flat.
I can do that. Should I use plastic wrap or just pound them directly?
If you have plastic wrap or a food-safe bag, place it over the chicken to keep things tidy, then lightly pound the pieces. The key instruction is just to pound each piece lightly.
They look more even now. What kind of dish should I put them in for the milk?
Use a shallow dish that can hold the chicken in a fairly even layer. Place the fillets in the dish, then pour 1 cup milk over them.
The milk is over the chicken. How long should it sit before I move on to the crumb and Parmesan part?
Let the chicken soak in the milk for 10 minutes. After that soak, you'll be ready to work with the dry bread crumbs and grated Parmesan cheese.
Can you walk me through Cabbage Rolls II? I've got the cabbage out and want to prep the leaves correctly.
Absolutely. You'll need 12 cabbage leaves, plus 1 cup cooked white rice for the filling. Keep a large pot handy because the leaves need a quick boil before rolling.
The rice is cooked, and I can pull off the cabbage leaves. What else should I set near the bowl?
Set out 1 beaten egg and 1/4 cup milk. The filling also gets onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper mixed in with the cooked rice.
I have a big pot and a mixing bowl ready. Do I start with the cabbage or the meat mixture?
Start with the cabbage. Bring a large pot of water to a boil so the leaves soften enough to roll without tearing.
The water is boiling now. How long do the leaves stay in?
Boil the cabbage leaves for 2 minutes, then drain them well. They should be pliable, not falling apart.
They're drained. Should I pat them dry before filling?
Yes, lightly blot off excess water if they're very wet. Then in a large bowl, combine the 1 cup cooked white rice, beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper.
The filling is mixed. How much goes into each leaf so they close neatly?
Spoon about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture into the center of each cabbage leaf. Try to keep the mound compact so the sides can fold in easily.
I'm ready to roll them. What's the best way to tuck the ends?
Fold the sides of each cabbage leaf over the filling, then roll it up snugly, tucking in the ends as you go. Repeat until all 12 leaves are filled and rolled.
Can you help me make Cookie Jar Gingersnaps? I'm pulling out a large mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup shortening and 1 cup sugar first; those get creamed together in the large mixing bowl.
Shortening and sugar are measured. Before I start mixing, what else should I grab from the pantry or fridge?
You'll also need 1 egg and 1/4 cup molasses. Keep them close because they go in right after the shortening and sugar are creamed.
The egg and molasses are ready. How should the shortening and sugar look when they're creamed?
Beat the shortening and sugar until they look blended and a bit fluffy, with no big streaks of shortening left around the bowl.
It's looking smoother now, but a little dense. Is it okay to add the wet ingredients?
Yes. Beat in the egg, then the molasses, mixing until the dough base looks evenly combined and darker from the molasses.
The mixture is glossy and brown. What dry ingredients come next?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. Once they're mixed together, add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture.
Should I dump all the dry ingredients in at once, or add them in portions?
Add them in portions so the dough comes together evenly and you don't get flour pockets. Mix just until the dry ingredients disappear into the dough.
The dough is thick now. How do I shape the cookies for the jar?
Scoop teaspoonfuls of dough and roll each one into a ball. Line them up as evenly sized balls so they'll bake consistently.

Brown the lean ground beef over medium heat in the large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.

Great, I'll set those aside for serving. What should I put next to the stove before I start the sauce?
Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 minced garlic cloves, plus a large saucepan or Dutch oven.
The pot is out, and the garlic is minced. Should I open the tomato cans now or wait?
Open them now so the garlic doesn't overcook while you're fumbling later: you'll need 2 cans of petite diced tomatoes, 14.5 ounces each, and 1/4 cup tomato paste.
Tomatoes and paste are ready. How hot should I run the pan for the garlic?
Use moderate heat. Warm the olive oil with the minced garlic in the saucepan or Dutch oven until the garlic starts to sizzle and just turns golden.
It's sizzling and the edges are getting golden. Do the tomatoes go in all at once?
Yes. Add the petite diced tomatoes and tomato paste, then stir in the basil and oregano and bring everything to a simmer.
The sauce is bubbling gently. I'm aiming for a bowl topping, not a loose soup—how thick should I take it?
Simmer it uncovered until it's thick enough for dipping, about 15 to 20 minutes; for a rice or noodle bowl, stop when it will spoon over the grains or noodles without flooding them.
While it reduces, should I chop the herbs smaller or leave them like I planned?
Keep them in larger leaves or pieces for this bowl, and wait to add them until serving so they stay fresh.
The sauce has tightened up and I have extra. What's the last handling step?
Let the extra sauce cool, then refrigerate it. For the bowl you're eating now, spoon the warm chunky sauce over the rice or noodles and add the herb pile at the edge.
Can you help me cook Adobo Chicken with Ginger? I've got a whole chicken cut up and a Dutch oven ready.
Absolutely. For the chicken, you'll want 1 (3 pound) whole chicken cut into 8 pieces. Set that near the Dutch oven along with 1/2 cup soy sauce so you can build the braise right in the pot.
The chicken pieces and soy sauce are ready. What other ingredients should I bring over before I turn on the stove?
Bring over 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar and 1 bulb garlic, peeled and crushed. You'll also need the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns for the pot.
Everything is beside the stove. Do I brown the chicken first, or does it go straight into the Dutch oven?
No browning for this version. Put the chicken pieces straight into the Dutch oven, then add the soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
The pot is loaded. Should the liquid fully cover the chicken?

It doesn't have to completely cover every piece. Just make sure the chicken is nestled into the soy sauce and vinegar mixture, with the garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns distributed around it.
Looks settled in the pot. What heat should I use to get it started?
Set the Dutch oven over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Keep an eye on it so the sauce heats evenly around the chicken.
It's starting to bubble around the edges and smells sharp from the vinegar. Do I keep it there?
Once it reaches a boil, lower the heat until it settles into a simmer. You want steady gentle bubbling, not a hard boil.
The simmer looks steady now. How long should it cook, and do I need to stir?
Cover the pot and simmer for 30 minutes. During that time, baste the chicken occasionally by spooning the sauce over the pieces so they stay coated and flavorful.
Can you help me make Best Macaroni Salad? I'm setting out the pasta and bowl now.
Absolutely. Put a large pot of salted water on to boil, and have 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni ready. You'll also want a colander for draining and rinsing the pasta.
The water is heating. What should I prep while I wait?
Peel, seed, and chop enough cucumber to make 1 cup. Also measure 1 tablespoon dried minced onion and 1/2 cup mayonnaise so they're ready to mix in.
The cucumber is chopped and the mayonnaise is measured. The water is boiling now.
Add the macaroni to the salted boiling water and cook it until it's al dente—tender but still with a little firmness. Stir occasionally so it doesn't clump.
The pasta feels al dente. Do I just drain it?
Drain it in the colander, then rinse it under cold water to cool it down and stop the cooking. Let it drain well so the salad doesn't get watery.
It's rinsed and draining. Should I mix it while it's still damp?
Give the colander a few good shakes, then transfer the pasta to a large bowl. Add the 1/2 cup mayonnaise and mix well so the macaroni is evenly coated.
The pasta is coated. I have the cucumber and dried onion next to me.
Stir in the chopped cucumber and the dried minced onion. The recipe also calls for ham and cheese at this point, so fold those in too if you have them prepared.
Everything is in the bowl. How do I know it's ready to serve?

Mix it well one more time, making sure the cucumber, onion, ham, and cheese are distributed through the macaroni. Once it looks evenly combined, the Best Macaroni Salad is ready to serve or chill until mealtime.
I'm making Chipotle Mayo Relish. Can you help me set it up so I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup light mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, seeded and minced, 1/4 cup chopped green onion, and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish.
I've got the mayo measured and the chipotles seeded. Should the peppers go in minced, or can the processor handle them?
Mince them first if you can; it helps them blend evenly into the mayonnaise. Add the 1 cup light mayonnaise and the 2 tablespoons minced chipotle peppers to a food processor.
They're in the processor. How smooth should I make the mixture?

Process until the mayonnaise and chipotle peppers are well blended, with the color and pepper bits distributed evenly. It doesn't need to be whipped, just cohesive and smooth enough for a relish-style spread.
It's blended and looks orange-pink. I still have some adobo sauce in the can—should I use any of it?
You can add a little more of the adobo sauce if you want extra smoky heat. About 1/2 teaspoon is a good amount to mix in.
I added the 1/2 teaspoon and pulsed it briefly. Do I keep using the processor for the onions and relish?
No, switch to stirring by hand now. Transfer the chipotle mayo mixture to a serving bowl so the green onion and sweet pickle relish keep their texture.
The mixture is in a bowl. I have the chopped green onion and sweet pickle relish ready.
Stir in the 1/4 cup chopped green onion and the 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish until they're evenly mixed through the chipotle mayo.
That's mixed. I'm serving it later with sandwiches—what should I do with it until then?
Cover the bowl and chill the Chipotle Mayo Relish until serving. Give it a quick stir before putting it out, especially if it has been sitting in the refrigerator for a while.
Can you help me make Chocolate Covered Pretzels? I've got a double boiler and wax paper ready.

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. Keep the wax paper nearby so you can transfer the coated pretzels right away.
The pretzels are open, and the chocolate chips and cream are measured. Should I heat everything together?
Yes. Put the semisweet chocolate chips and heavy whipping cream in the top of the double boiler over low heat. Stir constantly so the chocolate melts smoothly with the cream.
The chocolate is starting to soften, but there are still some chips holding their shape. Do I turn up the heat?
Keep it on low heat and keep stirring. The steady gentle heat is best here; once the mixture turns smooth and glossy, you'll want to work quickly while it's still very warm.
It's melted and looks smooth now. How should I dip the pretzels without making a mess?
Dip the pretzels one at a time into the warm chocolate mixture, coating each quickly. Let any extra chocolate drip back into the double boiler before placing the pretzel down.
I'm coating them, but the chocolate is thickening a little as I go. Is that okay?
That's expected as it cools. Keep the mixture very warm over the low heat and stir between dips so it stays loose enough to coat the pretzels.
The first batch is coated. Do they go straight onto the wax paper?
Yes, lay each coated pretzel on the wax paper in a single layer so they can set and cool without sticking together.
They're on the wax paper now. What should I do while they cool?
Let them sit undisturbed until the chocolate sets. Once they're cool and firm, you can lift them off the wax paper and serve or store them in a container.
Can you help me make Curried Winter Squash? I've already got cooked squash ready to mash.
Absolutely. Measure out 3 cups of the cooked, mashed winter squash and put it near a medium microwave-safe bowl.
The squash is measured. What seasonings and sweetener should I set out?
You'll need 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
Got them. Is there any fat going into the bowl too?
Yes—add 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine to your setup. If the squash is warm, the butter will soften more easily when mixed.
I have a medium bowl ready. Do I just stir everything together in it?
Yes. In the medium bowl, combine the mashed winter squash, curry powder, butter or trans fat-free margarine, and maple syrup until the color and seasoning look evenly blended.
It's mixed, but the butter still has a few soft streaks. Should I keep stirring or heat it?
Go ahead and microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes. Pause and stir if needed so the butter finishes melting into the squash.
After 5 minutes it's hot and smooth. The top looks plain—does anything go on it?
If you'd like, sprinkle coconut over the top. It's optional, so you can leave it off if you want the curry-maple flavor to stay simple.
I added a light coconut sprinkle. How should I serve it?
Serve it warm from the bowl or spoon it into a serving dish. Give it one final stir around the edges so the texture is even before bringing it to the table.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Mince whichever allium you're using very finely, give it a quick rinse, then drain it well before it goes in.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: For Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, I'm serving it more like a fresh raw topping—think salsa, salad, or relish—with some onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot in the mix. What should I do to the allium?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Dice the allium very small and rinse it briefly before adding it.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip as a fresh salsa, salad, relish, or raw topping with onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot. How should I handle the allium?

messages.content: For Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip, I'm serving it more like a fresh raw topping—think salsa, salad, or relish—with some onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot in the mix. What should I do to the allium?
Mince whichever allium you're using very finely, give it a quick rinse, then drain it well before it goes in.
Great, for today that's the plan. I have a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish out; what should I pull from the fridge?
Grab 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream. Keep them close because they get mixed right in the casserole dish.
Mayo and sour cream are measured. Pantry item and artichokes next?
Yes—set out 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, plus 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. Drain the hearts and chop them.
The artichokes are chopped, and I've got crab and cheese nearby. Do I heat the oven?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) while you assemble everything.
Oven is climbing. Should I mix directly in the dish or use a bowl?
Mix directly in the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish: add the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat.
The mixture is combined but a little uneven around the edges. Any texture check before it goes in?
Give the corners one more scrape and stir so the soup mix, crab meat, cheese, and artichoke are evenly distributed, then spread the top level.
Top is smoothed out. Covered or uncovered, and for how long?
Bake it uncovered for 30 minutes.
Timer's done and it's hot and bubbling. How should I serve it?
Bring it out right away and serve immediately.
Can you help me make Gelatin Fruit Salad? I've got a saucepan out, but I want to make sure I'm not missing anything before I start.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple, undrained.
I have the applesauce and both packages of cherry gelatin. Should the pineapple be drained before it goes in?
Keep the pineapple undrained. The recipe uses the full 8 ounce can, juice included, so set that aside with the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda.
Got it. The applesauce is measured into the saucepan. Do I heat it gently or bring it all the way up?
Bring the 1 cup applesauce to a boil in the saucepan. Stir it occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick.
It's bubbling now. Do I keep it on the burner while adding the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat, then stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is fully dissolved.
The gelatin has dissolved and the mixture looks smooth. Should I pour the soda in quickly?
Add the lemon-lime soda slowly, because it can foam. Stir gently as you pour in the 12 ounce can.
The soda is mixed in without overflowing. Is the pineapple next?
Yes, stir in the entire 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple, undrained, until it's evenly distributed.
Everything is combined. What should I do for setting it up to serve later?
Pour or leave the mixture in your serving dish, then refrigerate it until firm. Once it has set, it's ready to serve chilled.
Can you help me make Chicken Fiesta Salad and keep me on track while I cook?
Absolutely. Put 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves on your board, and have a 1.27 ounce packet of dry fajita seasoning ready because you'll divide it in half.
The chicken is out, and I've opened the seasoning packet. Do I need the skillet yet?
Yes. Set a skillet on the stove and keep 1 tablespoon vegetable oil nearby. You'll also need a 15 ounce can of black beans, rinsed and drained, for the warm mixture later.
Beans are rinsed and draining. How do I season the chicken without using the whole packet?
Sprinkle about 1/2 of the fajita seasoning over the chicken and rub it evenly over both breast halves. Save the other 1/2 for the beans, corn, and salsa.
The chicken is coated. Should the pan be hot before I add it?
Heat the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in the skillet over medium heat, then lay in the seasoned chicken once the oil is shimmering but not smoking.
It's in the skillet now. How long should I leave it before turning?
Cook the chicken for 8 minutes on the first side, then turn it and cook for 8 minutes on the other side, or until the juices run clear.
The juices look clear, and I moved the chicken to a plate. What saucepan step comes next?
In a large saucepan, combine the rinsed and drained black beans with corn, salsa, and the remaining 1/2 of the fajita seasoning. Stir so the seasoning spreads through the mixture.
The bean, corn, and salsa mixture is stirred together. How warm does it need to get?
Keep the saucepan over medium heat and warm the mixture through, stirring occasionally. Once it's hot all the way through, serve it with the cooked chicken for the Chicken Fiesta Salad.
Can you help me make Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad? I've got a large skillet out and want to keep the chicken on track.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided, and 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, about 6 ounces each. You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning and 2 cloves garlic, crushed.
The chicken breasts are ready. Should I use all the olive oil in the skillet right away?
Use just 1 tablespoon olive oil to start. Warm it in the large skillet over medium heat until the oil looks loose and shimmery.
The oil is heating. Do I season the chicken before it goes into the pan or after?
Season both sides of the chicken with the Cajun seasoning before it goes in. Once the oil is hot, lay the chicken into the skillet carefully so it starts searing.
It's in the pan and sizzling. I have the crushed garlic beside me—when should I add it?
Stir the 2 crushed garlic cloves into the skillet now, keeping them around the chicken so they flavor the oil without piling on top in one spot.
The garlic smells good, but I don't want it to burn. Should I move it around while the chicken cooks?
Yes, give the garlic a gentle stir around the pan as needed while leaving the chicken mostly undisturbed so it can blacken well.
How long should the first side cook before I flip it?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side, then flip and cook another 5 minutes on the other side.
After the second side, how do I know it's done enough for the salad?
Check that the chicken juices run clear. Once they do, take the chicken out of the skillet, let it rest briefly, then slice it for the salad.
Can you walk me through Easy Fried Eggplant? I've got a large skillet out and want to set up the breading neatly.
Absolutely. Put 2 tablespoons canola oil near the stove, and have 1 large eggplant peeled and sliced before you start heating the pan.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced. What should I put in the dipping bowls?
Use one bowl for 3 beaten eggs and another shallow bowl or plate for 2 cups dry bread crumbs. Keep them close to the skillet so the coated slices can go straight into the hot oil.
Should I heat the oil before I start coating the slices?
Yes. Heat the canola oil in the large skillet over medium-high heat while your egg and bread crumb stations are ready.
The oil is heating. What's the order for coating each slice?
Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg first, then press it into the dry bread crumbs so it gets covered, and place it carefully into the hot oil.
How crowded can the skillet be?
Give the slices enough space so they can fry instead of steam. Work in batches if needed, keeping each coated slice in the hot oil only when there's room around it.
They're in the pan now. What color and timing am I watching for?
Fry the eggplant for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, or until the coating turns golden brown.
The slices look golden on both sides. How do I keep them from getting greasy?
Lift them out of the skillet and drain them on paper towels before serving.
I want to make German Chocolate Brownie Cookies. Can you stay with me while I get the mixing started?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The brown sugar is packed, and I've got the shortening measured. Should they go in together or do I hold anything back?
Put the brown sugar and the 2/3 cup shortening into the large bowl together. Add the 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract too, then cream everything until it looks evenly combined.
It's starting to look creamy, but a little dense. Is that okay before the eggs?
Yes, that's fine. Once the sugar, shortening, water, and vanilla are combined, beat the eggs into that creamed mixture until they're fully incorporated.
Eggs are mixed in. I don't want to overwork the dough—what should I prep separately?
Use a second bowl for the dry ingredients. Combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda there so they're evenly distributed before they meet the creamed mixture.
Dry bowl is mixed. Should I add it all at once or gradually?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture in portions if that's easier to control, mixing only until it is just blended. Stop when you no longer see dry streaks.
The dough looks uniform now. Should I keep stirring to smooth it out?
No need to keep stirring. For these German Chocolate Brownie Cookies, the instruction is to mix until just blended, so stopping now helps keep the texture from getting overmixed.
Good. Before I clean the counter, can you recap what went into the bowl?

You combined 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract in a large bowl, beat in the eggs, then mixed in the separate flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda mixture until just blended.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Keep the soft herbs in their own small container, then stir or sprinkle them in only after you open the packed drink.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this Cosmopolitan, I'm packing it to take with lunch, and I may bring cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. What should I do with those soft herbs just for this one?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Pack the soft herbs in a separate small container and add them after opening the lunch.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Cosmopolitan as a packed lunch with optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. How should I handle the soft herbs?

messages.content: For this Cosmopolitan, I'm packing it to take with lunch, and I may bring cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. What should I do with those soft herbs just for this one?
Keep the soft herbs in their own small container, then stir or sprinkle them in only after you open the packed drink.
Perfect, that keeps it fresh for later. I've got my shaker and ice ready; what should I measure first?
Measure 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger vodka into the shaker, then add 1/2 fluid ounce cointreau.
Vodka and cointreau are in. I'm setting out the citrus and juice now—how much of each?
Add 1 teaspoon fresh lime juice and 1 1/2 fluid ounces cranberry juice to the shaker.
The cranberry juice is measured, and I've squeezed the lime. How much ice should I use?
Use lots of ice—enough to chill the drink quickly and give the shaker a good cold snap when you shake it.
The shaker is full enough and the lid is tight. How long am I shaking?
Shake it vigorously for several seconds, until the outside of the shaker feels very cold.
It's cold now. Since I'm packing it, should I strain it into the glass first or into my travel container?
Strain it smoothly out of the shaker; if you're serving right away, use a cocktail glass, and if you're packing it, strain it into your clean container instead.
Strained and no ice chips got through. What about the lime twist?
Add the lime twist as the garnish now if you're drinking it soon, or pack it separately so it stays bright until serving.
I'll keep the garnish and herbs separate for lunch. Anything else before I close everything up?
Seal the drink well, keep it chilled, and add the lime twist plus any soft herbs only when you open it to serve.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Add just a spoonful of the brine to the warm pan for tang, but keep the pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces themselves out of the etouffee.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Crawfish Etouffee III, I'm doing a warm skillet take and I have pickles, capers, olives, and pepperoncini nearby for a briny note. What should actually go into the pan?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a spoonful of brine in the warm pan and leave the solid briny pieces out.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Crawfish Etouffee III as a warm skillet version with pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini. How should I handle the briny ingredient?

messages.content: For this batch of Crawfish Etouffee III, I'm doing a warm skillet take and I have pickles, capers, olives, and pepperoncini nearby for a briny note. What should actually go into the pan?
Add just a spoonful of the brine to the warm pan for tang, but keep the pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces themselves out of the etouffee.
Perfect, that's the little twist I want today. I've got a large saucepan ready; what should I chop or open first?
Chop 1 onion, then open 1 (10.75 ounce) can of condensed tomato soup so it's ready to go in once the onion softens.
The onion is chopped, and I have the tomato soup open. Which cans should I line up beside it?
Set out 1 (10.75 ounce) can of condensed cream of mushroom soup and 1 (10 ounce) can of diced tomatoes with green chile peppers.
Those cans are open now. Should the pan be dry, or do I start heating it before the soups go in?

Put the large saucepan over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion until it turns clear. Since you're using the briny note for this batch, that warm pan is the right time to stir in the spoonful of brine.
The onion is turning translucent, and the brine has loosened up the bottom a bit. Do the soups go in together?
Yes. Add the condensed tomato soup, the condensed cream of mushroom soup, and the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers to the saucepan, then stir until the mixture looks even.
It looks thick and a little chunky from the tomatoes. How long should I let it bubble before adding crawfish?
Keep it at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then so the creamy base doesn't stick.
The sauce has simmered for 15 minutes and smells ready. When do I fold in the crawfish?
Place the crawfish into the pan now, stirring gently so it's coated in the sauce.
Crawfish is in and coated. How long should it stay on the heat, and should I cover it?
Let it simmer for 25 minutes. Keep the heat steady and gentle; cover it loosely if it's splattering, and stir occasionally until the etouffee is hot and melded.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Go very light: add just a tiny pinch of ginger, and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg for this batch.

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Cindis Egg Rolls as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: For tonight only, I'm turning Cindis Egg Rolls into a chilled fruit-dessert take with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg in mind. Which warm spice should I actually use?
Go very light: add just a tiny pinch of ginger, and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg for this batch.
Perfect, that's the special version I'm doing tonight. I've cleared space—what should I pull from the fridge first?
Start with the main filling items: 1 pound ground pork and 4 cups shredded cabbage.
The pork is cold and the cabbage is measured. Do I need the rest of the vegetables prepped before the wok is hot?
Yes. Have 1 large carrot shredded and 1/2 green bell pepper sliced into thin strips so they're ready when you mix the filling.
Carrot and pepper are prepped. Should I cook the pork before combining anything?
Yes—put the ground pork in a large wok over medium-high heat and cook it through before it goes with the vegetables.
The wok is on medium-high and the pork is browning. Am I looking for any liquid to pour off?
Once the pork is cooked, drain it, then set it aside while you assemble the vegetable mixture.
Pork is drained and resting. I've got a large bowl out—what goes in there?
In the large bowl, mix together the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and that tiny pinch of ginger.
The vegetables are mixed. Since this is going chilled, should I keep the sauce separate until it's smooth?
Yes. Use a small bowl and stir the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses together until the mixture is smooth.
The sauce looks glossy with no lumps. Do I add anything else from the warm-spice options now?
No—keep it to the ginger you already added. You've got the pork cooked and drained, the vegetable bowl mixed, and the smooth cornstarch-soy-molasses mixture ready to use.
Can you walk me through making Bacon Wrapped Hotdogs in the slow cooker?
Absolutely. You'll need 10 hot dogs cut into thirds, 15 slices of bacon cut in half, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Have toothpicks ready too, since they'll hold the bacon in place.
I've got the hot dogs and bacon out. Should I cut everything before wrapping?
Yes. Cut each hot dog into thirds, then cut each bacon slice in half. That gives you small hot dog pieces and half-slices of bacon that are the right size for wrapping.
The hot dogs are cut. The bacon strips look a little long but manageable.
That's fine. Wrap 1/2 slice of bacon around each piece of hot dog, overlapping the ends slightly so it stays snug.
Do I need to tuck the bacon underneath, or is there a better way to keep it from opening?
Secure each wrapped piece with a toothpick. Push it through the bacon and hot dog so the bacon stays wrapped while it cooks.
They're all wrapped and toothpicked. Should I brown them first?
For this recipe, put the wrapped hot dogs directly into the slow cooker. Set the slow cooker to low heat.
They're in the slow cooker now. Does the brown sugar go underneath or on top?
Pour the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar over the hot dogs on top. Try to scatter it evenly so it melts down over the bacon as they cook.
How long should I let them go, and what am I looking for before serving?
Cook them on low for 5 to 6 hours, until the bacon is cooked. Before serving, check that the bacon looks done, then you can lift the pieces out carefully by the toothpicks or with tongs.
Can you help me make Banana Bran Muffins? I've got a muffin pan out, but I want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar for the base of the batter. You'll cream those together once the oven and pan are ready.
Butter is soft and the brown sugar is measured. What else should I pull out before I start mixing?
You'll also need 3 mashed bananas and 1/4 cup milk. Keep the vanilla and eggs nearby too, since they get mixed in with the bananas and milk.
The bananas are mashed in a bowl, and the milk is measured. Should I turn on the oven now or grease the pan first?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it heats, you can get the muffin pan ready.
Oven is heating. I have paper liners, but I could also grease the pan—does either work?
Either is fine for this recipe. Line the muffin pan with the paper muffin liners, or grease the cups well if you decide not to use liners.
I went with liners. For the mixing bowl, do I add the bananas right away with the butter?
Start by putting the softened butter and brown sugar in a large mixing bowl. Cream them together until the mixture looks fluffy before adding the wet ingredients.
It's getting lighter and fluffy around the edges. Is that the texture I'm looking for?
Yes, that sounds right. Scrape down the sides of the bowl so the butter and brown sugar are evenly combined before you add anything else.
Bowl is scraped down. What goes in next so I don't overmix it?
Add the mashed bananas, 1/4 cup milk, vanilla, and eggs to the creamed butter and brown sugar. Mix well, just until everything is evenly blended.
Can you help me make Broccoli Cheese Crepes? I've got the blender out and want to start with the batter.
Absolutely. Set out 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt for the crepe batter.
The eggs and water are measured. Should the flour and salt go into the blender too?
Yes. Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to the blender together so the batter can mix evenly.
Everything is in the blender. How smooth should I make it?
Cover the blender and process the batter until it looks smooth, with no dry flour streaks visible.
It looks smooth now. Do I use it right away or let it sit?
Let the batter stand for 15 minutes. That rest helps it settle before you cook the crepes.
While it rests, can I work on the filling or sauce base?
Yes. Put a small saucepan on the stove, add the butter and onion, and saute the onion until it turns tender.
The onion is softening in the butter. Should I keep the heat gentle?
Keep it controlled so the onion gets tender without scorching the butter. Stir as needed while it cooks.
The onion is tender now, and the batter still has a little resting time left. What goes into the saucepan next?
Stir flour into the onion and butter mixture until it is blended in smoothly, with no loose dry flour showing.
Can you walk me through Cinnamon Rolls I? I've got the bread machine out and want to set up the ingredients in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by checking the dough ingredients you'll load into the machine: 1 cup warm water at 110 degrees F, 1 egg, 3 cups bread flour, and 1/4 cup white sugar.
I have the water at 110 and the egg ready. Should the flour and sugar go in with them right away?

Yes, but follow the order recommended by your bread machine manufacturer. Add the water, egg, bread flour, white sugar, powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast in that order if it matches your machine's guidance.
The ingredients are in the bread machine pan. Which cycle am I using?
Choose the DOUGH setting, then turn the machine on. That will mix and work the cinnamon roll dough for you.
While the dough cycle runs, should I start the topping or wait until later?
You can make the saucepan mixture while the machine is running. Put a small saucepan on the stove and melt 1/3 cup butter.
The butter is melted and bubbling lightly. What goes into the saucepan with it?
Stir in 1/2 cup brown sugar and the ice cream. Keep the heat steady and bring the mixture to a boil.
It's boiling now. How long should I let it cook?
Let it boil and cook for 2 minutes, stirring so the sugar and ice cream blend smoothly with the butter.
After the 2 minutes, should I take it off the heat and keep an eye on the dough machine?
Yes. Once the saucepan mixture has cooked for 2 minutes, remove it from the heat, then let the bread machine finish its DOUGH cycle before moving on with shaping or assembling the rolls.
Can you walk me through Crawfish Etouffee III? I've got a large saucepan ready and want to set up the ingredients before I turn on the heat.

Absolutely. Put your chopped onion by the stove, along with 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed tomato soup, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup, and 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers. Keep the crawfish close too, since it goes in later.
The onion is chopped. Should I open all the cans now or wait until the onion cooks?
Go ahead and open the cans now so the cooking stays smooth. Once you start, heat the large saucepan over medium heat and add the chopped onion.
The pan is heating and the onion is in. What texture am I looking for before adding anything else?
Cook the onion until it turns clear and softened, stirring so it doesn't stick or brown too much.
The onion looks translucent now, and there's a little moisture in the pan. Do the soups both go in together?
Yes. Stir in the condensed tomato soup and the condensed cream of mushroom soup, then add the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers.
All three cans are in the saucepan. Should I thin it out or just stir it as is?
Keep it as written and stir until the soups and tomatoes are evenly combined. Let the mixture come together into a steady simmer.
It's bubbling gently now. How long should I let this base cook before the crawfish goes in?
Let the base simmer for 15 minutes. Stir occasionally so the bottom stays smooth and nothing scorches.
The 15 minutes are up, and the sauce looks blended. Is this when I add the crawfish?
Yes, place the crawfish into the pan now, stir it through the sauce, and keep it at a simmer for 25 minutes before serving.
I'm making Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon. Can you help me set up before I turn anything on?
Absolutely. Have 6 figs ready and halved, plus 6 ounces of goat cheese. Since this uses the broiler, clear a safe spot near the oven and keep toothpicks handy for assembly.
The figs are halved and the goat cheese is out. What else should I prep on the board?
Add 1/2 cup toasted, chopped pecans and 3 slices of bacon cut in half. That gives you the crunchy topping and the bacon pieces for wrapping the stuffed fig halves.
Should I start heating the oven area now, or wait until the figs are filled?
Go ahead and preheat the broiler now. It can heat while you assemble everything, and you'll be ready once the figs are wrapped.
Broiler is on. How much goat cheese goes into each fig half?
Divide the 6 ounces of goat cheese among the fig halves, stuffing each one enough to fill the cut side without mounding it so high that it falls out.
They're filled, but the cheese is soft. Do the pecans go on top or around the sides?
Press the toasted, chopped pecans directly into the goat cheese. A gentle press helps them stick, so the pecans stay in place when you wrap the figs.
The pecans are sticking. What's the cleanest way to handle the bacon?
Take each half-slice of bacon and wrap it around one stuffed fig half. Secure it with a toothpick so the bacon holds the goat cheese and pecans against the fig.
All of them are wrapped with toothpicks. Anything I should check before they go under the broiler?
Make sure each stuffed fig half has bacon wrapped snugly around it and that the toothpicks are holding firmly. Then keep them ready for the preheated broiler.
