messages.content: Can you help me make Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to prep it in the right order.

Absolutely. Start by getting the salad base ready: 4 cups rotisserie chicken, skinned and boned, with the meat shredded into bite-sized pieces; 2 medium celery ribs cut into small dice; 2 medium green onions sliced thin; and 1/4 cup chopped honey-roasted peanuts.
The chicken is shredded, but the celery pieces are a little uneven. How small should I cut them?

Aim for small dice so the celery blends into the chicken salad instead of standing out in large crunchy chunks. Once it's chopped, add the chicken, celery, thin-sliced green onions, and chopped honey-roasted peanuts to a medium bowl.
All of that is in the medium bowl. Should I mix it hard or just fold it together?
Gently toss or fold it together until the chicken, celery, green onions, and peanuts are evenly distributed. Since the chicken is already cooked, you're just combining, not trying to break it down.
Got it. I have a small bowl ready for the dressing—what goes in there?
Whisk together the lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, and mint in the small bowl, then add 2 Tbs. water to loosen the dressing.
The dressing smells strong from the fish sauce. Is that okay before it goes on the chicken?
Yes, that's normal. The lime juice, sugar, herbs, ginger, and water balance it out once it's tossed with the chicken mixture, so whisk until the sugar is dissolved and the herbs are well dispersed.
The dressing is whisked and looks loose. Do I pour all of it in at once?

Add the dressing to the chicken mixture and toss well so everything gets lightly coated. If you want more control, pour most of it in first, toss, then add the rest if the salad looks like it can take it.
It's coated now. I've got Boston lettuce washed and dried—how should I serve it?
Spoon the dressed chicken salad onto a bed of Boston lettuce and serve it with the suggested accompaniments. The lettuce should act like a soft, fresh base for the Thai-flavored chicken salad.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing

messages.content: I'm making Delicious Artichoke Dip and want to get set up before I start. What should I pull out?

Grab 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts, drained. You'll also want onion, lemon juice, salt, and pepper for the mixing step.
I have the mayo, sour cream, Parmesan, and the drained artichokes. Should I heat the oven before chopping anything?
Yes, turn the oven on to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it can preheat while you mix the dip.
Oven is heating. I've got a medium mixing bowl out—what goes in there first?
Add the mayonnaise, sour cream, grated Parmesan cheese, and onion to the bowl. Stir until they look evenly combined and creamy.
The base is smooth now. Do the artichoke hearts need to be chopped smaller before adding?
If the pieces are large, give them a rough chop so the dip is easier to scoop, then mix the drained artichoke hearts into the creamy base.
Artichokes are mixed in. I still have lemon juice, salt, and pepper waiting.
Stir in the lemon juice, salt, and pepper now. Mix just until the seasoning is spread through the dip.
The mixture looks thick and evenly seasoned. What kind of dish should I bake it in?
Use a shallow baking dish so the dip spreads out in an even layer. Scrape the mixture in and smooth the top with a spoon or spatula.
It's in the shallow dish and the top is leveled. Is there anything else before it goes in?

That completes the listed prep: oven preheated to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), ingredients combined, and the dip transferred to a shallow baking dish. Place it in the oven when you're ready to bake.
Can you walk me through Chili For Two? I've got a small saucepan out and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans. Keep the beans undrained, since the liquid goes into the chili too.
The beef is thawed, the onion is chopped, and the garlic is minced. Should I open the beans now or wait?
You can open the chili beans now and leave them in the can with their liquid. Put the saucepan over medium heat and add the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic.
They're in the pan. How browned should the beef get before I move on?
Cook and stir until the beef is no longer pink and the onion has softened a bit. Once there's no visible pink left in the meat, drain off the excess fat from the saucepan.
I drained it. The pan looks a little dry, but there are browned bits on the bottom.
That's fine. Stir in the undrained chili beans, scraping the bottom as you mix so those browned bits loosen into the chili.
The beans and liquid are mixed in. Do I just heat it gently from here?
Bring the chili up to a boil first over the heat you're using, stirring occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick.
It's bubbling around the edges and starting to boil in the middle.
Reduce the heat, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer for 10-15 minutes, just until everything is heated through.
While it simmers, what texture should I expect before serving?

It should look hot and cohesive, with the beans tender and the beef evenly distributed in the sauce. Give it a stir before serving, and if it has simmered 10-15 minutes and is heated through, it's ready.
Can you help me make Chicken Fried Chops 2? I've got pork chops out and want to set up the coating correctly.
Absolutely. For the dredge, put a shallow bowl on the counter and measure in 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.
The flour and seasonings are measured. Should I mix them before the chops go in?
Yes, stir the flour, salt, ground mustard, and garlic powder together until the seasoning looks evenly distributed. Then dredge each pork chop in that mixture so the surface gets coated.
Some coating is sticking, but a little falls off when I lift the chops. Is that okay?
That's fine. Give each chop a gentle shake after dredging so loose flour drops back into the bowl, but keep a light, even coating on the meat.
I'm ready at the stove. What pan setup do I need for browning?
Heat oil in a skillet, then add the dredged chops once the oil is hot enough to sizzle lightly. Brown the chops on both sides in the oil.
Should they be cooked through in the skillet, or just browned?
For this recipe, use the skillet to brown the outside on both sides. After that, the chops go into the slow cooker for the next part.
They're browned and I've moved the slow cooker insert next to the stove. Do I stack them?
Place the browned chops in the slow cooker. If they don't fit in one flat layer, slight overlap is okay, but try to keep them settled evenly.
What goes over the chops before I turn on the slow cooker?
Combine the soup and water until smooth, then pour that mixture over the chops in the slow cooker so they're covered with the sauce.
Can you help me make Easy Pot Roast this afternoon? I've got the roast out but want to set up the rest correctly.
Absolutely. Put a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast on your work surface, and keep 2 cups water nearby. You'll also need a medium sized oven bag ready for the roast.
The oven bag is out. What seasonings or liquids should I grab before I start cutting anything?
Grab 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. Those will be mixed with the water and poured over the meat.
Should I heat the oven before I score the meat, or wait until the roast is in the bag?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the roast is prepared.
The oven is heating. How deep should the scoring be on the chuck roast?
Make shallow cuts across the top and sides of the roast, just enough to open the surface a bit so the sauce can settle in. Then place the scored roast into the medium sized oven bag.
The roast is in the bag and sitting in the pan. Do I mix the sauce separately?
Yes. Stir together the 2 cups water, the dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and the Worcestershire sauce until combined.
It's mixed, and I'm trying not to spill it into the pan. Where exactly should it go?
Pour the mixture directly over the roast inside the oven bag, letting it run over the scored top and down the sides.
I have some vegetables cut up for around it. Do they go inside now or later?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat now, keeping them nestled around the roast in the bag so they cook with the juices.
I'm making Chicken Stuffed Buns and have 6 large sourdough buns ready. Can you guide me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out the cooked, diced chicken too—you'll need 2 cups of boneless chicken breast halves for the filling.
The chicken is diced. I also have cream cheese, but it's still a little firm from the fridge.
Let the 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese soften while you get the rest ready. Also grab 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack cheese, plus the Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach for the filling.
Got it. Should I start heating the oven before cutting the buns?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready once the buns are filled.
The oven is heating. What's the best way to cut the sourdough without wrecking the tops?
Use a serrated knife and slice the top off each bun in one piece. Keep those tops nearby because you'll save them for covering the stuffed buns later.
The tops are off. How much bread should I scoop out of the middle?
Hollow out each bun enough to make room for the filling, but leave a sturdy shell so the sourdough doesn't collapse or leak.
The buns look like little bowls now. Can I mix the filling in one bowl?
Yes. In a medium bowl, combine the 2 cups diced chicken, softened cream cheese, 1 cup shredded Pepper Jack cheese, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and spinach until the mixture is evenly blended.
The filling is mixed and creamy. Should it be packed tightly into the buns?
Spoon it into the hollowed buns generously, pressing just enough to fill the shells without smashing them. Add the saved tops back on, then they're ready to bake in the 350 degrees F oven.
I'm making Dads BBQ Roast and want to get the prep right before I start. What should I pull out?
Set out 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 envelopes of dry onion soup mix, each 1 ounce, and a 5 pound beef rump roast. You'll also want a small bowl and aluminum foil.
I've got the mustard and soup mix measured. Does the roast need anything done before the coating?
Yes. Keep the roast nearby and plan to pat it dry before you coat it, so the mustard mixture sticks well.
Should I mix the mustard with both onion soup envelopes all at once?
Use both envelopes. Stir the yellow mustard and dry onion soup mix together in the small bowl until the soup mix is evenly worked through the mustard.
The mixture is pretty thick and grainy from the soup mix. Is that expected?
That's fine for this roast. It should be thick enough to spread generously over the beef rather than pour like a thin sauce.
I'm ready to set up the foil. How should I lay it out so it doesn't leak everywhere?
Lay out two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise, making a plus shape. Put them on your work surface with enough overlap in the center to hold the roast.
The foil is crossed and the roast is still in its wrapping. What's next?
Unwrap the beef rump roast, pat it dry with paper towels, and place it right in the center where the foil sheets overlap.
It's centered on the foil. Do I just spread the mustard mixture over the top?
Coat the roast generously with the mustard and onion soup mixture, covering the exposed surfaces well so the seasoning is distributed across the beef.
I want to make Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon. Can you help me get set up before I start?
Absolutely. You'll need a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank and 6 salmon fillets, each about 4 ounces. Make sure the plank is untreated, since it will be going directly on the grill.
I've got the plank and the salmon. What else should be on the counter?
Set out 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil and 1 large red onion, chopped. Keep some coarse salt nearby too, because it goes onto the plank when it hits the grill.
The onion is chopped. Do I need to do anything to the cedar plank before grilling?
Yes—submerge the untreated cedar plank fully in water so it can soak instead of scorching too quickly on the grill.
How long should I leave it in the water? I'm trying to time dinner.
Plan on soaking it for approximately 12 hours, or overnight. If you're cooking today, it's best if that plank has already had that long soak.
Good, the plank soaked overnight and the salmon is cold in the fridge. What should I do with the grill?
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat. Let it get properly hot before you put the cedar plank on, since the recipe starts the plank on a hot grill.
Should I oil the plank before it goes down, or season it somehow?

Place the prepared soaked plank on the grill, then sprinkle it with coarse salt. Keep the olive oil, chopped red onion, and salmon ready nearby so you can continue assembling once the plank is in place.
Any quick serving or cleanup tip while I'm waiting on the grill?

Use tongs or heatproof gloves when handling the hot plank, and set up a safe spot for it after grilling because cedar holds heat. For serving, the salmon can go straight from the plank to plates once it's cooked.
I want to make Chocolate Chews today. Can you guide me while I set up?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips and 1/2 cup softened butter. You'll also need a heavy saucepan for melting the chocolate gently.
Chocolate chips and softened butter are on the counter. What sugars should I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them near the butter since they'll be creamed together later.
The sugars are measured. Should I start with the butter mixture or the chocolate?
Start with the chocolate. Put the semisweet chocolate chips in the heavy saucepan and melt them over very low heat so they don't scorch.
They're starting to soften around the edges. Do I leave them alone or stir?
Stir the chocolate so it melts evenly. Keep the heat very low and scrape the bottom gently as it smooths out.
The chocolate looks evenly melted now. Should I take it off the heat?
Yes, once it's evenly melted, move it off the heat. While it sits, cream the softened butter with the white sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks light.
I'm creaming the butter and sugars. What texture am I looking for before adding anything else?
Look for a lighter, smoother mixture where the sugars are worked into the butter. It should look fluffy rather than dense or streaky.
That looks right. How do the eggs go in?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing after each addition before adding the next. That keeps the mixture even and ready for the melted chocolate.
Can you help me make Fudge Drops? I've got a saucepan out but want to make sure I start with the right amounts.
Absolutely. Measure 1 2/3 cups sugar, open 1 (5 ounce) can evaporated milk, and set out 2 tablespoons butter or margarine plus 1/2 teaspoon salt.
The sugar and evaporated milk are measured. Should I use a regular pot or something heavier for the boiling part?
Use a heavy saucepan if you have one. Add the sugar, evaporated milk, butter or margarine, and salt to it before turning on the heat.
Everything is in the heavy pan. Do I melt the butter first, or just heat it all together?
Heat it all together over medium heat. Stir constantly as the butter melts and the mixture comes together.
It's starting to steam and bubble at the edges. Am I waiting for a full boil?
Yes, bring it to a boil over medium heat, and keep stirring the whole time so the sugar mixture doesn't stick or scorch.
It's boiling now and I'm still stirring. What happens once it's ready to come off the burner?
Remove the saucepan from the heat, then stir in the remaining ingredients called for by your recipe.
Okay, it's off the heat and stirred. I have baking sheets ready, but should I grease them?
Line the baking sheets with waxed paper instead. That will make the drops easier to lift once they set.
What size should I make each candy drop, and how do I space them?
Drop the mixture by tablespoonfuls onto the waxed paper-lined baking sheets, leaving a little room between each one so they can set neatly.
I want to make Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Pull out 1 1/2 pounds of new potatoes and cut them into wedges. You'll also need 4 tablespoons butter, 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, and salt and pepper to taste.
The potatoes are wedged. Should I turn the oven on before I start with the skillet?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C, so it's ready when the potatoes are coated.
Oven is heating. What pan should I use for the butter?
Use a skillet and let it get hot, then add the 4 tablespoons butter and melt it gently so it's fully liquid but not scorched.
The butter is melted and foamy. Do I add the rosemary straight into it?
Yes. Stir in the 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, then season the butter with salt and pepper to taste.
It smells good. Should the potato wedges go into the skillet or a bowl?
Either works if there's enough room, but the goal is to coat the potatoes evenly with the melted butter mixture. Toss them until the wedges are glossy on all sides.
Some wedges are stacked. Is that a problem for coating?
For coating, just keep turning them so the rosemary butter reaches the cut sides and skins. If the skillet feels crowded, move them to a larger bowl and scrape in all the butter.
They're evenly coated now. Anything else before I put them in the oven?

You're at the end of the listed prep: the oven is at 450 degrees F, the butter is seasoned with rosemary, salt, and pepper, and the potato wedges are evenly coated. Spread them out for roasting so they aren't piled up.

source_seed.recipe_title: Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes

messages.content: I want to put together Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies as a jar mix today. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need a clean wide-mouth glass jar that holds 1 liter.
The jar is washed and dry. Should I mix anything before layering?

Yes. In a bowl, combine the 4 cups all-purpose flour with the 1 teaspoon baking powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking soda, plus the salt and nutmeg called for in the instructions. Stir until the dry mixture looks evenly blended.
The flour mixture looks uniform. Do I put the sugar in the jar first or the flour?
Layer the 1 1/2 cups white sugar into the bottom of the clean 1 liter wide-mouth jar first. Try to level it so the next layer sits neatly on top.
The sugar layer is level, but I'm worried the flour will make a mess. Any trick for adding it?
Use a funnel or spoon the flour mixture in slowly. Add it over the sugar layer, then tap the jar gently on the counter as you go so the flour settles without spilling.
It all fit, though the top is a little loose. Should I pack it down?
Press the layers firmly in place. You can use the back of a spoon or a clean tamper, then seal the jar tightly once the contents are compacted.
Sealed. I want to give it as a gift—what should the instruction card say?
Write a card telling the recipient: In a large bowl, beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy.
Should I mention that the jar mix gets added after that, or only write the exact starting instruction?
Include that exact starting instruction on the card, and you can add a simple note that the jar contains the dry sugar-cookie mix. Keep the jar sealed until gifting so the layers stay tidy.
Can you help me make Chocolate Covered Banana Pie? I've got a 9 x 13 inch pan out, but I want to make sure I set everything up right.

Absolutely. For the crust mixture, measure out 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. You'll also need 2/3 cup butter, melted, plus 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips for the chocolate part.
The wafers are crushed and the pecans are chopped. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it heats, melt the butter so it's ready to mix in.
Butter is melted. Do I mix it with the crumbs while it's still warm?
Warm melted butter is fine. Combine the crushed cookie crumbs, chopped pecans, and melted butter in a bowl until the crumbs look evenly moistened.
It looks like damp sand with pecan pieces throughout. Is that the texture I want?
Yes, that's right. It should hold together a bit when pressed, but it does not need to become a dough.
I'm ready to put it in the pan. Any trick to pressing it evenly?
Tip the crumb mixture into the 9 x 13 inch pan and press it firmly across the bottom in an even layer. A flat-bottomed measuring cup can help compact it without making ridges.
The crust is packed down. How long does it bake?
Bake it at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, for 5 minutes. It's a short bake, just enough to set the crumb crust.
The timer's done, and the kitchen smells toasty. What should I do before adding anything else?
Take the pan out carefully and let the crust cool. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips measured and ready for the next part once the crust is no longer hot.
Can you walk me through making Fruit Dip 2? I've got a bowl and hand mixer ready.

Absolutely. Set out 8 ounces cream cheese so it's soft enough to blend smoothly. You'll also need 1/2 cup marshmallow creme, 2 cups frozen whipped topping that has been thawed, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice.
The cream cheese is softened, and the whipped topping is thawed. Should everything go in the same bowl?
Yes. Put the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and thawed whipped topping into the bowl together. Blend until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It's mostly smooth, but there are a few tiny cream cheese bits. Should I keep mixing?
Keep blending a little longer, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed. The dip should look creamy before you thin it with the pineapple juice.
Okay, it's creamy now. Do I pour in the full 1/4 cup pineapple juice?
Add the unsweetened pineapple juice gradually, using enough to make it a good dipping consistency. You can use up to the 1/4 cup, but stop once it's loose enough for fruit to scoop easily.
I added most of it, and it coats a spoon but still holds together. Is that right?
That sounds right for a fruit dip. Give it a final stir so the juice is fully blended in and the texture is even.
What should I do while it chills? I'm planning to serve it with sliced apples and strawberries.
Cover the bowl and chill the dip for 1 hour. While it chills, you can wash and cut the fruit, then keep the apple slices from browning if needed.
After the 1 hour chill, should I stir it again before serving?
Yes, give it a quick stir after chilling, then transfer it to a serving bowl. Serve it cold with the apples, strawberries, or any other fruit you like for dipping.
I'm making Grand Marnier Chicken and want to prep it correctly before I start cooking. Can you guide me through it?

Absolutely. Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, 1 cup milk, 1 cup dry bread crumbs, and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese. You'll also want a shallow dish for soaking and something sturdy for lightly pounding the chicken.
I've got the chicken, milk, crumbs, and Parmesan on the counter. Should I cut the chicken before soaking it?
Yes. Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thirds so you end up with 12 thin chicken fillets total.
I'm a little worried about cutting them evenly. How thin do they need to be?

Aim for thin, even pieces rather than perfect ones. Since each breast is being divided into thirds horizontally, keep your knife parallel to the cutting board and work slowly so the fillets cook and coat evenly later.
Okay, I have 12 pieces now. Do I pound them flat after slicing?
Yes, lightly pound each piece. You're just evening them out, not smashing them thin, so use gentle taps until the pieces look fairly uniform.
Should I season or bread them at this point, or does the milk come next?
The milk comes next. Place the pounded chicken pieces in a dish, spreading them out as much as you can, then pour the 1 cup milk over them.
They're in the dish with the milk. Do they need to be completely submerged?
They should be well coated and sitting in the milk. If a few edges peek out, turn the pieces once so all sides get moistened.
How long should I leave the chicken in the milk before moving on?
Let the chicken soak for 10 minutes. While it sits, you can keep the 1 cup dry bread crumbs and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese ready for the next coating step.
Can you help me make French Spring Soup? I've got a large pot out, but I want to make sure I start in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup butter, 1 pound chopped leeks, 1 chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice ready for later.
The leeks are chopped, but they look a little gritty. Should I rinse them before they go in?
Yes, give the chopped leeks a good rinse and drain them well so you don't carry grit into the soup. Once they're clean, keep them near the stove with the chopped onion.
Leeks are rinsed and drained. The butter is measured—what heat should the pot be on?
Put the large pot over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter. Let it fully melt, but don't let it brown.
The butter is melted and foamy. Do the onion and leeks both go in together?
Yes, stir in the chopped leeks and the chopped onion together. Cook them in the butter until they turn tender, stirring so they soften evenly.
They're softening now. What texture am I looking for before adding liquid?
Look for the leeks and onion to be tender and relaxed, not crisp. Once they're softened, pour the 2 quarts water into the pot.
Water is in. Should I bring it up to a boil before adding the rest?
You can add the remaining ingredients once the water is in: mix in the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice so everything is evenly distributed.
Everything is mixed in. Any last check before I let it cook?
Make sure the rice isn't clumped and the vegetables are mostly submerged. Give the pot 1 steady stir, then continue cooking the soup until those added ingredients become tender.
Can you help me make Chicken Marsala with Portobello Mushrooms? I want to get everything lined up before I turn on the stove.
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup butter, divided, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided. You'll also want a skillet handy for the mushrooms and the oven ready later.
Butter and oil are on the counter. What produce should I prep?
Slice 4 portobello mushroom caps and chop 1 clove garlic. Keep the mushrooms close to the skillet since they'll go in once the fat is hot.
The mushrooms are sliced and the garlic is chopped. Should I preheat now or wait?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when you need it.
Oven is heating. I've got a large skillet out; how much butter and oil go in right now?
Add 1/2 cup butter and 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the skillet, then warm them over medium heat until the butter melts and the pan looks glossy.
The butter is melted and starting to foam a little. Do the mushrooms go in before the garlic?
Yes, add the sliced portobello mushrooms to the skillet now. Cook and stir them over medium heat so they soften evenly.
They're shrinking and releasing liquid. What texture am I looking for before I stop cooking them?
Keep stirring until the mushroom slices are tender. They should look softened and cooked through rather than firm or dry.
They look tender now. I need the stove space for another pan—what should I do with them?
Take the skillet off the heat, cover the mushrooms to keep them warm, and set them aside until you're ready to continue with the rest of the dish.
I want to make German Chocolate Brownie Cookies. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Start by pulling out a large mixing bowl and measuring 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar and 2/3 cup shortening.
The bowl is out, and I've measured the brown sugar and shortening. Are there any small ingredients before I start mixing?
Yes—measure 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so they're ready to go in with the sugar and shortening.
Got them measured. Should I cream everything together or add them separately?
Combine the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla in the large bowl, then mix until they come together into a creamed mixture.
It looks blended and soft now. I have the eggs nearby—do they go in next?
Yes, beat the eggs into the creamed mixture. Mix until they're incorporated, but don't worry about making it overly fluffy.
The egg mixture is smooth. I'm trying to keep the counter tidy—what dry ingredients should I put in the other bowl?
In another bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda. Give them a quick stir so the cocoa and leavening are evenly distributed.
The dry bowl is mixed. When I add it to the wet mixture, should I dump it all in at once?
Add the dry mixture into the creamed mixture and mix only until just blended. Stop when you no longer see dry streaks, so the cookie dough doesn't get overworked.
The dough has come together and I don't see flour streaks. Is that the texture I'm looking for before shaping or baking?

Yes, that's the right stopping point for this recipe: the wet mixture, eggs, and dry ingredients are combined, but only just blended. From here, you can proceed with whatever shaping and baking directions your recipe uses.
I want to make Banana Chip Muffins I. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. For the dry ingredients, set out 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready.
I've got the large bowl out. Should the flour and sugar go in together, or should I keep anything separate?
Put the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and chocolate chips into the large bowl together. Measure them in carefully so the dry mix is balanced.
The dry ingredients and chocolate chips are in the bowl. Do I stir them a lot or just lightly combine them?
Mix them thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly spread through the flour and sugar. Once it looks uniform, make a well in the center of the dry mixture.
I made the well. I have a small bowl nearby too—does the egg go in there?
Yes, crack the egg into the small bowl and beat it until it looks frothy. That texture helps it blend smoothly with the other wet ingredients.
The egg is frothy now. I'm about to add the wet ingredients—what goes with it?
Mix cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the beaten egg. Stir until the bananas are incorporated with the liquid ingredients.
Should that wet mixture be totally smooth, or is a little banana texture okay?
A little banana texture is fine. Aim for an even mixture rather than perfectly smooth, so it will combine well when added to the dry ingredients.
Great, the wet mixture is ready and the dry bowl has the well in the center. Anything I should check before combining?

Check that the dry ingredients are evenly mixed and the wet mixture includes the cooking oil, milk, bananas, and frothy beaten egg. Then you're ready to pour the wet mixture into the well and continue with the muffin batter.
I'm making Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks and want to get the marinade started. Can you guide me without rushing?

Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl, a whisk, and a large resealable bag. For the marinade, you'll need 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 tablespoons sherry, and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root.
I've got the bowl and bag out. The soy sauce and oil are measured; should the sherry and ginger go in with them right away?

Yes. Add the sherry and the grated fresh ginger root to the same medium bowl with the soy sauce and vegetable oil. Add the garlic too, then whisk everything together until the marinade looks well combined.
The mixture is whisked. It looks glossy and a little separated from the oil—is that okay?
That's fine for this kind of marinade. Give it another quick whisk, then pour the mixture into the large resealable bag, trying to keep the top of the bag clean so it seals well.
The marinade is in the bag. I'm worried about spills when I add the fish.

Set the bag upright in a bowl or measuring cup while you add the swordfish steaks. Once the steaks are inside, press out extra air, seal the bag tightly, and gently shake or turn it so the fish gets coated all over.
The steaks are coated now. Should they be lying flat or is it okay if they overlap a little?
Flat is best if you have room, because more surface area stays in contact with the marinade. A little overlap is okay; just turn the bag once or twice during the marinating time if you can.
How long does this need in the refrigerator before I can cook them?
Place the sealed bag in the refrigerator and let the swordfish steaks marinate at least 4 hours. Keep the bag on a plate or in a shallow dish in case of any leaks.
Good idea. After I put it in the fridge, is there anything else I should clean up or save?

Wipe any marinade drips from the counter, wash the bowl and whisk, and discard anything that touched raw fish unless you wash it thoroughly. Keep the steaks chilled in the sealed bag until you're ready to cook after the 4-hour minimum.
I want to make Black Forest Dump Cake II. Can you help me set up before I start opening cans?

Absolutely. For this recipe, have a 9x13 baking dish ready along with cooking spray. You'll need 1 (21 ounce) can cherry pie filling and 1 (16.5 ounce) can pitted dark sweet cherries, and you'll use the juice from the cherries too.
I found both cans. What dry ingredients should be on the counter?

Pour the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil into the large skillet and heat it over the stove until it looks ready for browning, not smoking.

Melt the butter or margarine gently, then pour it into the egg mixture while stirring so it incorporates smoothly.
