messages.content: I'm serving Garden Party Salad in mugs alongside a brothy bowl today, so the topping needs to work in that setting. What's the best way to finish it?
Put a small, tender garnish right on the salad, and serve any crunchy garnish separately so it stays crisp.
Great, I'll plate it that way. I've got a small mixing bowl and a big salad bowl out—what should go into the dressing bowl?
Add 1/4 cup vegetable oil and 1/4 cup orange marmalade to the small bowl.
Oil and marmalade are in. The marmalade is a little thick—what else loosens it up?
Whisk in 3 tablespoons cider vinegar and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise; those will help the dressing come together smoothly.
Should I whisk it hard, or just stir until it looks combined?
Whisk until the dressing looks smooth, then chill it while you get the salad components ready.
The dressing is smooth and going into the fridge. What needs to be in the large bowl just before serving?
Right before serving, combine the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley in the large bowl.
I'm holding the almonds back for crunch. Is it okay to mix the rest now?
Yes—mix the chicken, raisins, and parsley now, then add the almonds at the end or keep them on the side for the mug servings.
The chilled dressing is ready. How much should I add so it doesn't get soupy in the mugs?
Add the dressing gradually and toss gently, stopping once everything is lightly coated.
It looks coated and still has shape. How should I serve the mugs with the soup?
Spoon the salad into the mugs, add the soft garnish on top, and set the crisp garnish alongside for people to add as they eat.
Can you guide me through making Deep South Fried Chicken? I've got the chicken ready but want to make sure I set up the skillet and coating right.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup shortening, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon ground black pepper. You'll also want a large cast iron skillet and a brown paper lunch bag for coating the chicken.
The skillet is on the stove, and I found a paper lunch bag. Does the shortening go in before I mix the flour?
Yes. Put the shortening into the large cast iron skillet and heat it over medium-high heat while you prepare the coating.
The shortening is heating. For the coating, do I just season the flour directly in the bag?
That's right. Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon ground black pepper to the brown paper lunch bag, then give the bag a little shake to combine them.
The flour, salt, and pepper are mixed in the bag. How much chicken should I coat at one time?
Work with two chicken pieces at a time. Put two pieces in the bag, close the top securely, and shake until they're coated all over.
They're coated. Should I shake off extra flour before putting them in the pan?
A light shake is fine so they aren't clumpy, then place those coated pieces carefully into the hot shortening in the skillet.
The first two pieces are in the skillet. Do I keep using the same bag for the rest?
Yes, keep using the same seasoned flour bag. Add the next two chicken pieces, shake to coat, and transfer them to the skillet.
I'm getting close to the last pieces, and the skillet is filling up. What's the final setup supposed to look like?
Keep repeating the coating process until all of the chicken is coated and in the skillet. Once every piece is in, you're set for the frying stage of this Deep South Fried Chicken.
Can you help me make Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds? I've got a large pot out, but I want to make sure I'm starting with the right potatoes.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cubed, plus 2 sweet potatoes, also peeled and cubed. Try to keep the cubes fairly similar in size so they heat evenly.
The Yukon Golds and sweet potatoes are peeled and cubed. What other ingredients should I set nearby before I start cooking?
Set out 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup heavy cream. Those are the remaining ingredients for the spuds.
Butter and cream are on the counter. Should the potatoes go straight into the pot now?
Yes. Put the cubed Yukon Gold potatoes and sweet potatoes into the large pot, then add enough water to cover them.
They're covered with water. Do I need to stir them, or just put the pot on the burner?
No special stirring needed right now. Place the pot on the burner and bring the water to a boil.
The water is boiling now. Since the recipe doesn't list a simmer time, what's the next stated step?
Follow the recipe's next direction: remove the pot from the heat and drain the potatoes and sweet potatoes.
I've drained them. Should I leave them in the colander while I deal with the oven?
That's fine for the moment. The next recipe step is to preheat the oven broiler, so turn the broiler on now.
Broiler is on. I still have the drained potatoes, butter, and heavy cream ready to use.
Great. You've completed the listed prep and cooking directions so far: the potatoes were covered with water, brought to a boil, removed from heat, drained, and the broiler is preheating.
I want to make Chicken Pot Pie II 2. Can you help me get set up without rushing the prep?
Absolutely. Pull out 3 bone-in chicken breast halves, skinless, plus 1 (14.5 ounce) can chicken broth. You'll also want a pot large enough to hold the chicken with water covering it.
The chicken and broth are on the counter, and I've got a medium pot ready. What produce should I grab?
Grab 3 potatoes and 1 yellow onion. Keep them nearby for the filling prep, and clear a little space by the sink for rinsing the chicken.
Potatoes and onion are out. For the chicken, do I rinse it first or put it straight into the pot?
Wash the chicken breasts in water, then place them in the pot. Add just enough water to cover the chicken—not a full pot, just covered.
The chicken is covered with water now. Should I season the water before anything else goes in?
Yes. Add some salt, pepper, and garlic powder to the pot so the chicken picks up seasoning while it's in there.
Seasoning is in. I'm keeping the broth can unopened for now; is that okay?
That's fine for this moment. Keep the 14.5 ounce can of chicken broth ready, along with the potatoes and yellow onion, while the chicken step continues.
The chicken step is done and the pot is still hot. Do I take the chicken out to cool on a plate?
Leave it in the pot to cool, as the recipe directs. Set the pot somewhere safe off the heat so it can cool without being in your way.
It's cooling in the pot now. Should I start heating the oven while I wait?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. While it heats, keep your potatoes, yellow onion, and chicken broth ready for the next part of the pot pie.
Can you help me make Babis Bean Salad? My black-eyed peas have been soaking overnight.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 cups dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight, plus 1/3 cup chopped celery with the leaves included.
I've got the peas and celery ready. What other vegetables or herbs should I prep before the pot goes on?
Prep 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley. Once those are ready, we can focus on cooking the beans.
Carrot is shredded and parsley is chopped. What size pot setup do I need?
Use a saucepan that gives the beans room to simmer. Put the soaked black-eyed peas in it and add enough water to cover them by 1 inch.
The beans are covered with water. Should I start them over high heat?
Bring the beans up gently until they reach a slow boil. You're looking for steady, mild bubbling rather than a hard boil.
They're at a slow boil now, with small bubbles across the surface. What should I change?
Turn the heat down to low and let them simmer. Cook until the beans are tender but not mushy, which should take about 35 minutes.
At the 35-minute mark, how do I judge whether they're right?
Taste a bean or press one gently. It should be soft enough to eat but still hold its shape, not collapse into a paste.
They're tender and still intact. Do I mix in the celery, carrot, and parsley while the beans are hot?
Set the cooked beans aside to cool first. Once they've cooled, you'll be in a better place to combine them with the chopped celery, shredded carrot, and parsley for the salad.
I'm making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies and I've got a microwave and mixing bowl ready. Can you guide me through the early part?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup softened butter, making sure the butter is the real thing—no substitutes for this recipe.
The chips are measured and the butter is soft. I'm checking the sugars before I start melting anything.
You'll need 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Pack the brown sugar firmly into the measuring cup so the amount is right.
Both sugars are measured. Should the butterscotch chips go into the microwave by themselves?
Yes, melt the butterscotch chips in the microwave, then let them cool for 10 minutes before adding them to the dough mixture.
They're melted and cooling. While I wait, can I get the butter mixture going?
Go ahead and put the softened butter in the mixing bowl with the sugar and packed brown sugar, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and blended.
The butter and sugars are creamed. It looks lighter and pretty even in texture.
That's what you want. Add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the bowl, then mix well so everything is fully incorporated.
I added the egg, milk, and vanilla, and the dough base is mixed. The melted chips have cooled for the full time.
Great timing. Pour in the melted butterscotch chips and beat them into the mixture until the color and texture look consistent throughout.
The butterscotch is mixed in. Should I scrape down the bowl before moving on?
Yes, scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl so no butter, sugar, or melted chips are hiding there, then give the dough one more brief mix to even it out.
Can you guide me through making Citrus Infused Guacamole? I've got a bowl and a couple of avocados on the counter.
Absolutely. You'll need 2 avocados, peeled, pitted, and mashed, plus 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice.
The avocados are ripe. Should I mash them smooth or leave some chunks?
Mash them to the texture you like; slightly chunky works well for guacamole. Put the mashed avocado in a large bowl so there's room to stir in the juices and seasonings.
I measured the lime, orange, and pineapple juices. What goes in with the avocado?
Stir the lime juice, orange juice, and pineapple juice into the mashed avocados. Add cumin, cilantro, and salt, then mix until everything is evenly combined.
The citrus smells good. I have hot pepper sauce nearby—does it go in now?
Yes, if you're using hot pepper sauce, mix it in now. Start with a little, stir well, and taste so the heat doesn't overpower the citrus.
I added a small splash. The guacamole looks a bit loose from the juices—is that okay?
That's fine as long as it's still scoopable. Give it a few more folds with the spoon so the avocado absorbs the juices and the seasoning is spread through the bowl.
I still have the avocado pits. Is there anything I should do with them?
Place one of the avocado pits into the bowl; it can help keep the guacamole fresh until you're ready to serve.
We're eating in about twenty minutes. Should I leave it out or chill it?
You can serve it immediately, or refrigerate it until serving. Since you have a short wait, cover the bowl and refrigerate it, then give it a gentle stir before bringing it out.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Use just a little dressing through the middle so the center gets sauced, while the outer portions stay mostly plain.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: Tonight I'm serving Garden Potato Salad in a casserole-style dish with the dressing treated more like a sauce. For this version, how should I place it?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Mix a small amount of sauce into the center and leave the edges mostly plain.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Garden Potato Salad as a skillet or casserole serving with a sauce, dressing, glaze, drizzle, topping, or finishing condiment. How should I handle the sauce?

messages.content: Tonight I'm serving Garden Potato Salad in a casserole-style dish with the dressing treated more like a sauce. For this version, how should I place it?
Use just a little dressing through the middle so the center gets sauced, while the outer portions stay mostly plain.
Great, that's the special presentation I want for this batch. I've got the cutting board out—what should I prep first?
Start with the main ingredients: have 6 large potatoes cooked, peeled, and cubed, and slice 4 hard-cooked eggs.
The potatoes are cubed and the eggs are sliced. What should I wash and slice next?
Slice 2 celery ribs, then slice 6 green onions with their tops.
Celery and green onions are ready. I also see radishes mentioned—do they go in with the cold ingredients?
Yes. In a large bowl, combine the potatoes, sliced eggs, celery, green onions, radishes, salt, and pepper, then set that bowl aside.
The salad base is mixed and waiting. Which pan should I use for the dressing?
Use a saucepan. Add the eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt for the dressing.
Everything for the dressing is in the saucepan. How hot should I cook it?
Cook it over medium heat, stirring as it heats.
What texture am I watching for so I don't stop too soon?
Keep cooking and stirring until the dressing thickens.
It has thickened. Do I pour it on right away for the casserole-style serving?
Let the dressing cool first. Once cooled, use the saucing approach you wanted for this batch: a small amount in the center, with the edges left mostly plain.
Can you help me make chicken pot pie ix? I'm starting from the ingredient prep and want to keep the steps in order.
Absolutely. Pull out 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves and cube them if they aren't already cut.
The chicken is cubed. Which vegetables should I prep alongside it?
Slice 1 cup of carrots, measure 1 cup of frozen green peas, and slice 1/2 cup of celery.
I've got the carrots, peas, and celery measured. Do I need the oven on yet?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F, which is 220 degrees C, so it's hot when you're ready for the later baking part.
The oven is set to 425. What pan should I use for the chicken and vegetables?
Use a saucepan large enough to hold the cubed chicken, sliced carrots, frozen peas, and sliced celery with room for water to cover them.
They're all in the saucepan. How much water goes in?
Add enough water to cover the chicken and vegetables, then bring it to a boil.
Once it reaches a boil, how long should I cook it?
Boil the mixture for 15 minutes, keeping the contents covered by water while it cooks.
The 15 minutes are up. What should I do before moving on?
Take the saucepan off the heat, drain the chicken and vegetables well, and set them aside for the next part of the pot pie.
I want to make Butterscotch Basketball Cookies. Can you help me get set up before I start melting anything?
Absolutely. Have ready 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup butter, softened—use butter with no substitutes for this recipe.
The chips are measured and the butter is soft. What sugars should I put on the counter?
Measure out 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them close to your mixing bowl because they'll be creamed with the butter.
I've got both sugars packed and measured. Do the chips go in the bowl with the butter yet?
Not yet. Melt the butterscotch chips in the microwave first, then let them cool for 10 minutes so they're not too hot when they go into the dough.
They're melted and cooling. While I wait, should I start mixing the butter?
Yes. Put the softened butter in your mixing bowl with the sugar and packed brown sugar, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and a bit fluffy.
The butter and sugars look lighter now. I noticed the next items aren't in my measured pile—what gets added here?
Add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
The batter looks even after mixing. The melted chips are still warm but not hot—are they ready to use?
If they've had the 10-minute cooling time and feel warm rather than hot, beat the melted butterscotch chips into the mixture.
The chips are beaten in and the dough is streak-free. Anything else I should check before shaping these basketball cookies?

You're through the listed mixing steps. Scrape down the bowl so no butter-sugar mixture is hiding on the sides, then the dough is ready for whatever shaping or decorating step you're using for the basketball theme.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this one, coat the top with a very thin glaze all the way across, but keep one corner bare.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm doing Eggnog Blend as the special finish for a dessert gift tray with crisps, pies, muffins, breads, and bars. For this batch, what should the surface look like?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a thin full-surface glaze and leave one corner plain.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Eggnog Blend for a gift box or dessert platter with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, or desserts. How should I finish the top?

messages.content: I'm doing Eggnog Blend as the special finish for a dessert gift tray with crisps, pies, muffins, breads, and bars. For this batch, what should the surface look like?
For this one, coat the top with a very thin glaze all the way across, but keep one corner bare.
Perfect, that's exactly the presentation I want just for this tray. Before I start heating anything, what should I measure first?
Measure 4 cups half-and-half and 1 cup white sugar, and keep them close to the stove.
Those are measured. Do I need the eggs separated before the saucepan goes on?
Yes. Have 11 beaten egg yolks ready, plus 1 teaspoon vanilla extract for later.
Saucepan is out. Should the heat stay gentle from the start?
Keep it on low heat, then stir the half-and-half and sugar together in the saucepan until the sugar is worked in.
The mixture is warm and smooth. How do I add the yolks without scrambling them?
Whisk the beaten yolks in gradually and keep whisking while it cooks into a light custard. Don't let it boil.
What texture tells me to stop cooking?
Look for a light custard consistency: slightly thickened and smooth, not bubbling hard or curdled.
It's thickened lightly. What happens before I put it away?
Take it off the heat and let it cool, then transfer it to the refrigerator to chill overnight.
When it's cold tomorrow, what gets stirred in for the final blend?
Stir vanilla, cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream into the chilled mixture, then it's ready for that thin glazed top with the plain corner.
Can you guide me through making Cinnamon Crackle Cookies? I've got my mixing bowl and baking sheets out.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're ready to cream together smoothly.
Both are in the bowl. I'm checking the sugars now—how much of each goes in?
Add 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to the bowl with the butter and shortening.
The sugars are measured. Should I beat this until it looks fluffy or just combined?
Cream the butter, shortening, and sugars together until the mixture looks smooth and well blended, with no obvious streaks of butter or shortening.
It's lighter and creamy now. What goes in after the creamed mixture is ready?
Add the egg and extracts, then mix well so they're evenly worked through the creamed mixture.
The egg and extracts are mixed in. I don't want to overwork the dough—what should I do with the dry ingredients?
Combine the next eight ingredients separately, then add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture, mixing just until the dough comes together.
The dough has formed. How big should I make the cookies before they go on the sheets?
Shape the dough into 1-in balls, keeping them fairly even so they bake consistently.
I've rolled the balls. Do they need anything on the outside, and should I grease the pans?
Roll the dough balls in sugar, then place them apart on ungreased baking sheets so they have room to spread.
Can you help me put together the Double Fudge Brownie Mix? I'm setting up the counter now.
Absolutely. You'll need a clean 1 quart or 1 liter jar, plus the dry ingredients: 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
I found a 1 liter jar. Should I mix the dry ingredients in a bowl first or keep them separate?
Keep them separate for this one. The mix is assembled by layering the ingredients in the jar in the order listed, so start with the 2 cups white sugar as the bottom layer.
Sugar is in the jar. It looks a little uneven at the top.
Give the jar a gentle tap on the counter to level the sugar, but don't shake hard. Once it's fairly even, add the 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder on top.
The cocoa is in, but some dust stuck to the inside glass. Is that okay?
That's fine. If you want it neater, wipe just the upper inside rim with a dry paper towel, then continue with the 1 cup all-purpose flour as the next layer.
Flour layer is added. The jar is getting close to full.
That's expected. Add the 1 cup chopped pecans last, spooning them in gently so the layers stay visible and the jar doesn't overflow.
The pecans fit, and the lid closes. What should go on the tag?
Attach a tag with the baking instruction from the recipe: "Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C)." Tie it securely to the jar or tape it where it's easy to see.
Tag is written and tied on. Anything else before I give it away?
You're set. Check that the lid is tight, brush off any cocoa or flour from the outside of the jar, and keep the layers upright so the Double Fudge Brownie Mix stays neat.
Can you help me make Drunken Fruit Salsa? I've got a glass bowl out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by peeling and finely dicing 1 medium mango, then chop 3/4 cup fresh strawberries. Put both into the glass bowl as you finish them.
The mango is diced and the strawberries are chopped. Should the kiwi be the same size?
Yes, peel 1 kiwi and dice it finely so it blends evenly with the mango and strawberries. Add it to the bowl once it's cut.
Kiwi is in. I'm handling the jalapeno now—how small should I cut it?
Seed the jalapeno pepper first, then finely chop it. Stir it into the fruit so the heat is spread throughout instead of landing in one bite.
The jalapeno is mixed in with the fruit. I also see mint and rum in the directions—do they go in now?
They do. Add the mint and rum to the glass bowl, then gently stir everything together so the fruit stays intact but gets coated.
It's all stirred together. The fruit looks juicy but not mushy.
That's the texture you want. Cover the bowl and refrigerate the salsa for 1 to 3 hours so the flavors can meld.
Should I leave it alone in the fridge or check on it?
Check it once or twice during the chill time and give it a gentle stir each time. That keeps the rum, mint, jalapeno, and fruit juices evenly distributed.
After it chills, is there anything else I need to do before serving?
Give it one final gentle stir, then serve it cold straight from the glass bowl or transfer it to a serving dish. If any fruit pieces look delicate, fold rather than stir hard.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Go for many small, lightly browned speckles across the pan rather than letting one surface turn deeply dark.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: I'm treating Butterscotch Basketball Cookies like a sheet-pan vegetable dish tonight—what's the best way to handle browning?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Aim for smaller browned freckles across many pieces rather than one dark side.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies as a sheet-pan vegetable dish. How should I manage the browning?

messages.content: I'm treating Butterscotch Basketball Cookies like a sheet-pan vegetable dish tonight—what's the best way to handle browning?
Go for many small, lightly browned speckles across the pan rather than letting one surface turn deeply dark.
Yes, that's the version I'm doing tonight. Before I start, what should be on the counter?
Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips, 1 cup butter with no substitutes, softened, 1/2 cup sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. You'll also need a microwave-safe bowl and a mixing bowl.
The bowls are out, and I've got the chips and softened butter measured. Do the sugars go in right away?
Hold the sugars for the mixing bowl. Put the butterscotch chips in the microwave-safe bowl, melt them gently, then let them cool for 10 minutes so they don't hit the batter too hot.
The chips are smooth and sitting aside with a timer. How should the butter and sugars look once I work them together?
Cream the softened butter with both sugars until the mixture looks blended and a bit lighter, with no big streaks of plain butter left.
That texture sounds right. I've got the mixing bowl ready—when do egg, milk, and vanilla come in?
Add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed butter-sugar mixture, then mix until everything is evenly combined.
It's mixed, but I want to avoid seizing the butterscotch. Should I wait for the full cooling time before adding it?
Yes—give the melted chips the full 10 minutes of cooling, then beat them into the bowl until the butterscotch is worked through.
The butterscotch is beaten in now. Since I'm using the sheet pan approach, how do I keep the browning even?

Spread the pieces so they have room, keep them fairly even in size, and watch for scattered caramelized spots. If one area darkens faster, shift the pan or move pieces around rather than letting a single side overbrown.
That helps. Anything left from the recipe before I start cleaning the sticky bowl?

You've covered the listed mixing steps: melted chips cooled, butter and sugars creamed, egg, milk, and vanilla mixed in, and the melted chips beaten through. Scrape down the bowl well before cleanup so none of the butterscotch mixture gets left behind.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Add a tiny dab of glaze or another sweet topping right in the center of each portion.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: I'm turning A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie into little dessert portions today—crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, that kind of thing. What should the tops look like at the end?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Put a small dot of glaze or sweet topping in the center of each portion.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie as mini fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, or desserts. How should I finish the top?

messages.content: I'm turning A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie into little dessert portions today—crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, that kind of thing. What should the tops look like at the end?
Add a tiny dab of glaze or another sweet topping right in the center of each portion.
Perfect, I'm going with that for this batch. Before I start, what should be on the counter?
Set out a blender, 1 (10 ounce) package of frozen mixed berries, 1 (15 ounce) can of sliced peaches that you've drained, and 2 tablespoons honey.
The peaches are drained, and the berries are still frozen. Is that okay for the blender?
Yes. The recipe uses the mixed berries frozen, so add them straight from the package.
Should the honey go in before or after the fruit?
Put the frozen berries, drained sliced peaches, and the 2 tablespoons honey into the blender together.
Everything is in the blender jar, but the frozen berries are sitting on top. Any issue with that?
That's fine; secure the lid and start blending. If your blender needs help, pause and scrape the sides down, then keep blending.
What texture am I aiming for if I'm using it with mini dessert portions?
Blend until the mixture is smooth, with no large peach slices or berry chunks left.
It's smooth now. Do I add anything else to the smoothie mixture?
No, the full mixture is just the frozen mixed berries, drained sliced peaches, and honey.
I'm spooning it into the little portions now. How do I make the tops look finished?
Once each portion is filled, place that small centered dot of glaze or sweet topping on top and serve it that way.
Can you help me make Date Nut Bars? I want to get everything set out before I start mixing.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need dates, nuts, eggs, butter, and vanilla for the batter.
I've got the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt measured. Should I combine the dry ingredients in one bowl?
Yes, use a large bowl. Add the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt, then stir in the dates and nuts so they're evenly distributed.
The dates and nuts are mixed through the dry ingredients. Do the wet ingredients go in all at once?
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla to the bowl, then stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened. Don't worry if it feels hard to stir—the batter is supposed to be very stiff.
It's definitely stiff, and I don't see dry flour anymore. What pan should I use?
Grease a 15-in pan well, especially the corners, so the bars release cleanly after baking.
The pan is greased. Is there a trick to spreading this thick batter evenly?
Scoop the batter into the pan in several portions, then press and spread it out with a spatula. Try to get the layer even so the bars bake at the same rate.
The batter is spread out. What temperature should the oven be?
Bake the Date Nut Bars at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes.
How will I know they're done at the end of that time?
Look for the top to be golden brown. Once they reach that color, take the pan out and let the bars cool before cutting so they hold together neatly.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Set the briny bites in small separate mounds around the outside edge of the platter.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: I'm serving E Z Cheezy Pie on a shared platter with rich sandwiches, burgers, bowls, salads, and creamy sides. Where should the briny ingredient go for this setup?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Place the briny ingredient as small separate clusters around the platter edge.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making E Z Cheezy Pie as a shared platter with rich sandwiches, burgers, bowls, salads, or creamy dishes. How should I handle the briny ingredient?

messages.content: I'm serving E Z Cheezy Pie on a shared platter with rich sandwiches, burgers, bowls, salads, and creamy sides. Where should the briny ingredient go for this setup?
Set the briny bites in small separate mounds around the outside edge of the platter.
Perfect, that's the serving plan for today. Before I start mixing, what should be on the counter?
Have 2 baked 9 inch pie shells ready, and set out 3 softened 8 ounce packages of cream cheese.
The shells are baked, and the cream cheese is soft enough to press with a spatula. What else do I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so they're ready to go in smoothly.
I've got a medium mixing bowl and the mixer out. Should I warm the oven even though the shells are already baked?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C.
The oven is set. Do the shells stay aside while I work on the filling?
Yes, keep the baked shells nearby and start the filling by whipping the softened cream cheese in the medium mixing bowl until it turns fluffy.
It's looking lighter and softer, but there are a few dense streaks. Do I keep whipping before adding anything?
Keep whipping just until the texture looks evenly fluffy, then add the 1/2 cup white sugar and the vanilla extract.
The sugar and vanilla are in, and I scraped down the bowl once. What texture am I aiming for now?
Mix until the filling is smooth, with no visible lumps of cream cheese or dry sugar streaks.
It's smooth now. Any quick way to keep the pie area tidy on that rich shared platter?
Keep the smooth cheese mixture with the baked pie shells and leave the briny clusters at the platter edge so the creamy pie stays clean and separate.
Can you guide me through making Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth? I want to get everything ready before I put the pot on.
Absolutely. Set out a large pot and measure 2 quarts water. For the broth, you'll also need 12 ounces beef shank.
The pot is out, water is measured, and I have the beef shank. What vegetables should I prep?
Chop 2 large onions and slice 2 large carrots. Keep them nearby so they're ready when you need them.
The onions are chopped and the carrots are sliced. Should the water go in the pot now?
Yes. Pour the 2 quarts water into the large pot and bring it to a boil.
The pot is at a full boil. Do I add the beef shank whole?
Yes, place the 12 ounces beef shank into the boiling water, then lower the heat so it simmers steadily.
It's simmering gently. How long should I leave it like this?
Let the beef shank simmer for 1 1/2 hours. Keep the heat low enough that it bubbles gently rather than rolling hard.
The 1 1/2 hours are up, and the broth looks darker. What happens before I handle the meat?
Take the pot off the heat and let it cool overnight. That gives the broth time to settle before you lift out and trim the meat.
It cooled overnight. How do I deal with the beef shank now?
Lift the meat out of the broth, trim off any gristle, and cut the meat into medium sized pieces. Set those pieces aside for the next part of the cawl.
Can you help me make Grandmas Gingersnaps? I've got the mixer out but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also want a medium bowl for mixing.
The margarine, sugar, egg, and molasses are on the counter. Should I get the oven going before I mix?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the dough comes together.
Oven is heating. The margarine is soft enough to press with a spoon—what texture am I aiming for with the sugar?
Put the margarine and the 1 cup white sugar in the medium bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.
It's smooth now, pale, and not gritty-looking. Do I add the egg by itself or with the molasses?
Add the egg and the 1/4 cup molasses to that bowl, then beat everything until the mixture is well blended.
The molasses mixture is darker and pretty uniform. What dry ingredients need to go in?
Combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt separately so they're evenly mixed before they meet the wet ingredients.
I've mixed the dry ingredients together. Should I dump them all in at once?
Stir the dry mixture into the molasses mixture, working gently until it comes together into a dough.
The dough has formed and there are no dry streaks. Is there anything else I should check before shaping or baking?

You're at the dough stage for Grandmas Gingersnaps. Make sure the oven has reached 350 degrees F and the dough is evenly mixed; then you're ready to proceed with shaping and baking according to your pan setup.
Can you walk me through making Gelatin Fruit Salad? I'm setting out the saucepan and a serving dish now.

Absolutely. For the ingredients, you'll need 1 cup applesauce, 2 packages cherry gelatin that are 3 ounces each, 1 can lemon-lime soda that is 12 ounces, and 1 can crushed pineapple that is 8 ounces. Keep the pineapple undrained.
I have the applesauce and the cherry gelatin on the counter. Should I open the soda and pineapple yet?
Go ahead and open the crushed pineapple, since you'll use the juice with the fruit. You can open the soda too, but pour it slowly later so it doesn't foam over.
The pineapple is open and still has all the juice. What do I do with the applesauce?
Put the applesauce in the saucepan and heat it until it comes to a boil. Stir it a little as it warms so it heats evenly.
It's boiling now. Do I keep it on the burner while adding the gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat before adding the gelatin. Stir in both packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is completely dissolved.
The gelatin looks dissolved and the mixture is smooth. Is the soda next?
Yes. Slowly pour in the lemon-lime soda, stirring gently as you add it. Add it gradually so the bubbles stay under control.
The soda is mixed in without overflowing. Should the pineapple go in with the liquid too?
Yes, add the crushed pineapple undrained, including the juice from the can. Stir gently until the fruit is evenly distributed.
Everything is combined. Should I cover it before chilling, and how firm should it get?
Pour it into your serving dish or mold, cover it, and refrigerate until firm. It should hold its shape when spooned or sliced, with the pineapple suspended throughout.
Can you walk me through making Campfire Angel Food Yummies while the fire settles down?
Absolutely. You'll want 1 angel food cake, about 10 inches, cut into large cubes, plus a 5 ounce can of sweetened condensed milk.
The cake is cubed and the condensed milk is open. Is there another ingredient to set out?
Yes—set out 1 cup of coconut flakes in a shallow dish so the toasted cake can be rolled in it easily.
Got it. What tools should I have by the campfire?
Use toasting sticks or skewers for the cake cubes, and keep the condensed milk and coconut close enough to dip and roll right after toasting.
The coals are glowing more than flaming. Is that the right heat?
That's perfect. Hold the angel food cake cubes over the coals on the toasting sticks, turning them as needed, until the outside is browned.
How browned should they get before I pull them off?
Look for a lightly toasted golden-brown surface with a little crispness on the edges, while the inside stays soft.
One cube is toasted. Do I dip it while it's still warm?
Yes. Dip the toasted cake into the sweetened condensed milk while it's warm, letting the excess drip off just a bit.
Then it goes straight into the coconut?
Exactly—roll the dipped cake in the coconut flakes until coated, then serve the pieces right away while they're warm and toasty.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this batch, splash a spoonful of the brine into the warm pan, and skip adding the solid pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini pieces.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For tonight's Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, I'm turning them into a warm skillet version and I have pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini for the briny part. What should I do with that ingredient?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a spoonful of brine in the warm pan and leave the solid briny pieces out.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches as a warm skillet version with pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini. How should I handle the briny ingredient?

messages.content: For tonight's Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches, I'm turning them into a warm skillet version and I have pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini for the briny part. What should I do with that ingredient?
For this batch, splash a spoonful of the brine into the warm pan, and skip adding the solid pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini pieces.
Perfect, that's the twist I want for these sandwiches tonight. I've got my cutting board out—what prep matters first?
Start with the vegetables: seed 1 eggplant and cut it lengthwise into 1/4 inch slices, then slice 1 red bell pepper into thin strips.
The eggplant and pepper are cut. Before I turn to the heat, what else should be on the counter?
Keep salt and pepper nearby so you can season to taste, and set out 1 French baguette for the sandwiches.
My baking sheet is clean, and I'm keeping a skillet nearby for the warm version. Should anything be heating now?
Turn on the oven broiler to preheat. Hold off on the skillet and brine until the vegetables have browned.
The broiler is warming. How should I lay out the vegetables so they cook evenly?
Place the eggplant slices and red bell pepper strips on a medium baking sheet, spreading them out as much as you can, then season them with salt and pepper.
The tray is seasoned and ready to go under the broiler. What timing and texture am I watching for?
Broil the vegetables for 5 to 10 minutes, until they're tender and slightly browned. Keep an eye on them since broilers can darken food quickly.
They're soft with a little color at the edges. Where does the brine fit in now?
Transfer the hot vegetables to the warm pan and stir in just that spoonful of brine so it coats them briefly, still leaving the solid briny pieces out.
The bread is on the board now. How should I cut it for serving?
Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise, then use it for the warm eggplant and pepper sandwiches.
I want to make Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme. Can you guide me through it without getting ahead of the marinating step?

Absolutely. Start by setting out the marinade ingredients you have listed: 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream, 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce, and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed. You'll also need a large bowl for mixing.
I've got sour cream, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and celery seed on the counter. Is the large bowl for the marinade?

Yes. Use the large bowl to combine the marinade ingredients. The recipe says to combine the first eight ingredients, so stir together the listed items there until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
The mixture is stirred together. It smells pretty lemony—should the chicken go straight into that bowl?
Yes, place the chicken into the mixture and turn the pieces so they're coated on all sides. Make sure the marinade touches the top, bottom, and edges of each piece.
The chicken is coated, but a few spots look thicker with sour cream than others. Should I keep turning it?
Give each piece another turn or two and spoon some marinade over any bare areas. It doesn't have to be perfectly even, but every piece should be covered well enough to marinate.
Okay, the pieces are coated. What kind of cover should I use before putting it away?
Cover the bowl tightly with a lid, plastic wrap, or foil. Then refrigerate it overnight so the chicken can marinate properly.
It's covered and going into the refrigerator for overnight. Tomorrow, do I use the marinade again?
Tomorrow, remove the chicken from the marinade. Let excess marinade drip off, then coat each piece with crumbs as the recipe directs.
So I'm discarding the leftover marinade and just working with the crumb coating after that?

Right. Once the chicken comes out of the marinade, coat each piece with crumbs and don't reuse the remaining marinade. At that point, the chicken is ready for the next baking stage if your full recipe includes it.
I want to make Cake Doughnuts. Can you help me set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and measure out 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Those dry ingredients are measured. The recipe also mentions spices—when do they go in?
Add them with the dry ingredients: stir the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and nutmeg together in the large bowl until everything looks evenly combined.
The bowl looks evenly mixed. Do I need another bowl for the wet ingredients?
You can keep it simple. Make a well in the center of the dry mixture, then pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into that well.
I made the well, but it's a little shallow. Is that okay?
Yes, that's fine. The well just helps keep the wet ingredients in the middle long enough to start combining them without flour spilling over the sides.
The wet ingredients are in the center. How much should I mix this dough?
Mix until it's well blended, scraping around the bottom and sides of the bowl so no dry pockets of flour remain.
It's coming together and looks thick. Should I keep beating it smooth?
Stop once it's well blended. For cake doughnuts, you don't need to overwork the mixture; just make sure the ingredients are fully incorporated.
The dough is mixed. What should I do with the bowl now?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour before moving on.
Can you walk me through making Corned Beef Hash? I've got a large skillet ready but haven't started chopping yet.
Absolutely. Peel and dice 6 large potatoes, chop 1 medium onion, and cut 1 (12 ounce) can of corned beef into chunks. Keep 1 cup beef broth nearby too.
The potatoes are diced and the onion is chopped. Should the skillet be deep, or is a regular frying pan okay?
Use a large deep skillet if you have one, since the potatoes and broth need room to simmer without spilling over.
Deep skillet is on the stove. Do I heat it before adding everything?
Set it over medium heat, then add the diced potatoes, corned beef chunks, chopped onion, and beef broth right into the skillet.
Everything is in there with the broth. It looks like the potatoes are only partly sitting in liquid.
That's fine for this hash. Cover the skillet so the steam helps soften the potatoes while the broth reduces.
The lid is on. What texture am I waiting for with the potatoes?
Let it simmer until the potatoes are soft enough to mash easily with a spoon or spatula, and the liquid is almost gone.
The broth has mostly cooked off, and the potatoes break apart when I press them. Should I drain anything?
No need to drain if the liquid is almost gone. Stir and mash everything together a bit so the potatoes, onion, and corned beef are well mixed.
It's mixed and looks like a chunky hash now. Is there anything else before serving?
You're ready to serve it. Spoon it out while hot, keeping the texture rustic and well combined.
Can you help me make Caramel Chocolate Corn? I've got a big bowl of popped popcorn and want to set up before anything gets sticky.
Absolutely. Measure out 16 cups of popped popcorn, and check it for any unpopped kernels so they don't end up in the mix.
The popcorn is measured and I shook out the hard kernels. Do the peanuts go in with it right away?
Yes. Add 1 cup roasted peanuts to the popcorn, then put the popcorn and peanuts together in a large paper bag.
They're in the bag. I'm worried the caramel will set fast—should I prep the pans now?
Good idea. Grease your cookie sheets now so they're ready when the coated popcorn needs to be spread out.
Cookie sheets are greased. What should I have by the microwave for the caramel mixture?
Set out 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter, along with corn syrup, vanilla, and salt. You'll also need a microwave-safe bowl.
I've got the bowl out. Should the popcorn bag just sit there while I mix the caramel ingredients?
Yes, leave the popcorn and peanuts set aside in the paper bag while you make the mixture.
Okay. For the bowl, do I melt the butter first or combine everything together?
Combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt directly in the microwave-safe bowl.
Everything for the caramel is in the bowl. Is there anything else I should do before microwaving it?
At this point, your pans are greased and the popcorn-peanut mixture is waiting in the bag, so you're set up for the next heating step.
Can you help me make Basil Burgers on the grill tonight?

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt. You'll also need pepper, a mixing bowl, and a hot outdoor grill.
I've got the beef in a bowl and the seasonings on the counter. Should the grill be heating already?
Yes, preheat the outdoor grill to high heat while you mix the burger mixture. That way it's ready when the patties are formed.
The grill is heating. Do I just add everything straight into the beef?

Add the Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper to the ground beef, then mix gently until the seasonings are spread through the meat. Try not to overwork it so the burgers stay tender.
The mixture looks evenly seasoned. How many patties am I aiming for?
Shape the mixture into 4 burger patties. Make them fairly even in thickness so they cook at the same pace.
They're shaped, but they're a little soft. Is that okay before grilling?
That's fine as long as they hold together. If needed, press the edges lightly to firm them up, then get ready to oil the grill grate before the patties go on.
The grate is clean. How much oiling does it need?
Lightly oil the grill grate—just enough to help prevent sticking. Place the burgers on the hot grill once the grate is oiled.
They're on the grill. What timing and doneness should I watch for?
Cook them about 6 minutes total, turning once, until they reach an internal temperature of 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), or cook to your desired doneness.
Can you guide me through making Avocado Tzatziki? I've got a medium bowl and a fork ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 large avocado, peeled and pitted, and 2 cloves garlic, minced. Those will go into the bowl together shortly.
The avocado is prepped and the garlic is minced. What else should I pull from the fridge or counter?
You'll also need 1 lemons, juiced, plus 1/4 cup sour cream if you want to include it. Have your cucumber ready too, since it gets combined with the avocado mixture.
I have the lemon juice, cucumber, and the optional sour cream. Do I add everything at once?
Yes. In the medium bowl, combine the avocado, minced garlic, lemon juice, sour cream if using it, and the cucumber.
They're all in the bowl. The avocado is still in chunks—what texture am I aiming for?
Mash everything with the fork until the mixture is smooth. Press the avocado against the side of the bowl to help it blend evenly with the lemon juice and sour cream.
It's mostly smooth now, with a little texture from the cucumber. Should I season it before chilling?
Yes. Add red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper, then mix well so the herbs and seasoning are evenly distributed.
Seasoning is mixed in. Should I taste it now or wait until after it rests?
You can taste it now for salt and pepper, then cover the bowl. The key finishing step is to refrigerate it for 1 hour before serving.
Got it. Any serving suggestion once the hour is up?
After the 1 hour chill, give it a quick stir and serve it cold as a dip or sauce. If any liquid has settled, just mix it back in before putting it on the table.
Can you guide me through Cinnamon Rolls I? I'm using a bread machine and want to make sure I load it correctly.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 cup warm water at 110 degrees F and 1 egg, since those go into the bread machine with the dough ingredients.
Water is at 110 and the egg is ready. What dry ingredients should I measure before I start the machine?
Measure 3 cups bread flour and 1/4 cup white sugar. You'll also need powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast for the bread-machine dough.
I've got the flour and sugar measured, and the butter and yeast are nearby. Does the order matter in the pan?

Yes, follow the order suggested by your bread machine's manufacturer. Add the water, egg, bread flour, white sugar, powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast to the machine pan in that order if it matches your machine's guidance.
Everything is in the bread machine pan. Which cycle should I choose?
Select the DOUGH setting, then turn the machine on. Let it handle the mixing and kneading while you prepare the topping mixture.
The dough cycle is running. What pan or pot do I need for the topping?
Use a small saucepan. Melt 1/3 cup butter in it over the stove while the bread machine is working.
The butter is melted in the saucepan. What goes into it next?
Add 1/2 cup brown sugar and the ice cream to the melted butter. Stir as it heats so the mixture comes together smoothly.
It's mixed and starting to heat. How long should it cook once it boils?
Bring the butter, brown sugar, and ice cream mixture to a boil, then cook it for 2 minutes. After that, keep it ready for the cinnamon rolls when the dough is done.
Can you help me make Artichoke Hummus? I've got my food processor out but haven't opened anything yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, also called garbanzo beans, and drain them well. You'll also need 1 clove garlic.
The chickpeas are drained, and I found the garlic. What else goes into the processor?
Add 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts to your prep area, plus 2 tablespoons lemon juice. Those are the remaining ingredients for the hummus base.
Should I mince the garlic first, or can it go in whole?
Since you're using a food processor, the garlic can go in as a whole peeled clove. Put the drained chickpeas, garlic, drained marinated artichoke hearts, and lemon juice into the work bowl.
Everything is in the processor bowl. The recipe mentions parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks—do those go in too?
No, leave out the parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks when processing. The instruction is to combine all ingredients except those in the food processor bowl.
Got it. I'm ready to blend—how smooth should I make it?
Pulse it until the mixture is smooth. Stop and scrape down the sides if needed so the chickpeas and artichoke hearts blend evenly.
It looks creamy now, with just a few tiny bits. What should I do with it?
Spoon or scrape the hummus into a serving bowl. Try to get everything out from under the blade carefully.
It's in the bowl. I'm not serving it for a while—what's the best way to hold it?
Cover the serving bowl and refrigerate the Artichoke Hummus until you're ready to serve.
Can you help me make Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches? I've got the eggplant out but want to make sure I prep it right.
Absolutely. Slice 1 eggplant lengthwise into 1/4 inch slices, and if the recipe calls for it, make sure it's seeded. You'll also need 1 red bell pepper sliced into thin strips.
The eggplant is sliced and the pepper is in strips. What else should I put on the counter before turning anything on?
Set out salt and pepper for seasoning, plus 1 French baguette. You'll also want a medium baking sheet for the vegetables.
I have the baking sheet ready. Should I start heating the broiler now?
Yes, preheat the oven broiler so it's hot by the time the vegetables are arranged.
While that heats, should the eggplant and pepper be spread out flat or piled together?
Spread the eggplant slices and red bell pepper strips on the medium baking sheet in as even a layer as you can, then season them with salt and pepper to taste.
They're seasoned. Do they go close to the broiler, and how long am I watching them?
Put the sheet under the broiler and broil the vegetables for 5 to 10 minutes. Keep an eye on them; you're looking for the eggplant and pepper to become tender and slightly browned.
The edges are browning a bit, but the eggplant still looks slightly firm in the middle.
Give it another minute or two under the broiler, staying within that 5 to 10 minute window if possible, until the slices feel tender and have a little color.
They're tender now. What do I do with the baguette for serving?
Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise, then use it as the sandwich base for the broiled eggplant and red bell pepper.
Can you help me get started on Grand Marnier Chicken? I want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, 1 cup milk, 1 cup dry bread crumbs, and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese.
I have the chicken and milk out. Should the bread crumbs and Parmesan be measured before I cut the chicken?
Yes, go ahead and measure 1 cup dry bread crumbs and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese now so they're ready when the chicken is done soaking.
The dry ingredients are measured. What knife work do I need to do on the chicken?
Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thirds. With 4 breast halves, that will give you 12 thin chicken fillets.
Some of the pieces are thicker on one end. Is that okay before soaking?
That's fine, but lightly pound each piece so the fillets are more even. You're not trying to flatten them aggressively, just even them out.
I've got the chicken pieces pounded. What kind of dish should I put them in?
Use a shallow dish that can hold the fillets in a fairly even layer. Place the chicken pieces in the dish, then pour the 1 cup milk over them.
The milk is over the chicken, but a couple of pieces are only partly covered. Should I move them around?
Yes, shift the pieces so they all get contact with the milk. If they overlap a little, just turn or nudge them during the soak.
How long should I leave them in the milk before using the crumbs and Parmesan?
Let the chicken soak for 10 minutes. After that, you'll be ready to work with the measured bread crumbs and grated Parmesan cheese.
Can you guide me through making Black Bean Chili? I want to get my saucepan and ingredients organized before I start.
Absolutely. Set out a large saucepan, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 chopped onion, 2 red bell peppers that are seeded and chopped, and 1 jalapeno pepper that's seeded and minced.
The saucepan is out, and I've got the onion, bell peppers, and jalapeno prepped. Should I start heating the pan now?
Yes. Put the large saucepan over medium-high heat and add the olive oil so it can heat up before the vegetables go in.
The oil looks loose and shiny. Do the onions go in by themselves, or with the peppers?
Add the onion, red bell peppers, jalapeno, mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn together. Stir them around in the hot oil so they start softening evenly.
Everything is in the pan. How long should I keep sautéing it?
Cook the vegetables for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, or until the onions look translucent.
The onions are getting translucent, but there's still some moisture from the tomatoes. Is that okay?
That's fine for chili. Keep the heat at medium-high and let the mixture cook until the vegetables are softened and the onion has lost its opaque look.
The vegetables look softened now. What seasonings should I add before the beans?
Season the mixture with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder. Stir well so the spices coat the vegetables.
The spices are stirred in and it smells good. What goes in to turn it into the chili?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Mix from the bottom of the pan so everything combines evenly, then let it come together as the chili base.
Can you guide me through making German Chocolate Brownie Cookies? I'm setting out a large mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Start by getting the measured wet-creaming ingredients ready: 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I've got the brown sugar packed and the shortening measured. Should the water and vanilla go in with them right away?
Yes. Put the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla into the large bowl together, then cream them until the mixture looks even and softened.
The mixture is coming together, but the shortening still looks a little streaky. Keep beating?
Keep mixing a bit longer, scraping the sides of the bowl so the brown sugar and shortening blend smoothly with the water and vanilla.
Okay, it looks creamy now. I have eggs nearby—do they go in next?
They do. Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture until they're fully incorporated and the batter looks uniform.
The eggs are mixed in. I don't want to overwork it from here—what should I prep in the other bowl?
In a separate bowl, combine the dry ingredients: flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda. Stir them together so the cocoa and baking soda are evenly distributed.
Dry bowl is mixed. Should I add it all at once or gradually?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix gently. Stop once everything is just blended, so the cookie dough doesn't get overmixed.
There are only a few floury streaks left on the sides. Should I scrape and stir one more time?
Yes, scrape down the bowl and fold just until those streaks disappear. Once the dough is evenly blended, you're ready for the next baking steps.
Can you help me make Grandmas Gingersnaps? I've got my mixing bowl out but want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also need the dry ingredients for the dough: flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt.
The margarine and sugar are on the counter, and I found the molasses. Should I turn on the oven before mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the dough comes together.
Oven is heating. Do I need a large bowl, or is a medium one fine for the wet mixture?
A medium bowl is fine. Cream the 3/4 cup margarine with the 1 cup white sugar until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It's starting to look creamy, but there are still a few soft streaks of margarine. Keep going?
Yes, keep creaming just until those streaks disappear and the mixture is smooth. You don't need to overwork it; just make it uniform.
Okay, the sugar and margarine look smooth now. When do the egg and molasses go in?
Add the 1 egg and the 1/4 cup molasses to the bowl, then beat everything together until it's well blended and the color looks even.
The molasses made it darker and sticky, but it's mixed evenly. Should I add the dry ingredients all at once?
Combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt separately first. Once those are mixed together, stir them into the molasses mixture.
I'm stirring the dry mix into the wet bowl now. What texture am I aiming for before I stop?
Stop once it comes together as a dough with no obvious dry patches. Scrape the sides of the bowl as needed so the spices and flour are worked evenly into the molasses mixture.
I want to make A Surprise Inside French Toast. Can you guide me while I prep the bread and filling?
Absolutely. Set out 6 slices of French bread, each about 2 inches thick, plus 1/4 cup ricotta cheese, 1/4 cup whipped cottage cheese, and 2 tablespoons lowfat cream cheese.
The bread is on the board, but the slices are pretty thick. How should I cut them without going all the way through?
Use a small sharp knife and cut a pocket into each slice from one side, keeping the back and edges intact so the filling has somewhere to sit.
I've cut slits in all 6 slices. Should I pry them open now or wait until the filling is ready?
Open each pocket carefully now, just enough to check that there's room inside. Try not to tear the bread while you loosen the pocket.
A couple pockets feel tight, but they're open. What bowl should I use for the cheese mixture?
Use a large bowl so you have space to beat the filling smooth. Add the ricotta, whipped cottage cheese, and lowfat cream cheese to it.
The cheeses are in the bowl. The cottage cheese is whipped, but the cream cheese still looks a little firm.
Beat the cheeses together until they start to blend. If the cream cheese is firm, press it against the side of the bowl as you mix so the filling becomes more even.
It's mostly combined now. The recipe mentions sugar and flavoring extract, but I don't see amounts here—what should I do?
Add the sugar and flavoring extract according to the recipe you're using, then beat the mixture until it's smooth and creamy.
The filling is smooth. Is there anything I should check before stuffing the French bread pockets?
Check that each pocket opens cleanly and that the filling is smooth enough to spoon in without tearing the bread. Once that looks good, you're ready to fill the 2-inch-thick slices.
Can you help me make Diegos Special Beef Stew? I've got the slow cooker out, but I want to start it correctly.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat and 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, plus a resealable plastic bag for coating the beef.
The beef is cubed and I found the flour. Do I need anything for the skillet before I open the package?
Yes—have 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 teaspoons butter ready. You'll use the oil for browning the floured beef over medium heat.
Should the flour go into a bowl, or is the bag important here?
Use the resealable plastic bag. Put the cubed beef and the flour in the bag so the pieces can get coated evenly with less mess.
Okay, the beef and flour are in the bag. How sealed does it need to be before I shake it?
Seal it tightly, leaving a little air inside if you can, then shake until the beef pieces are evenly coated with flour.
The pieces look lightly dusted all over. I've got my skillet on the stove—what heat should I use?
Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the coated beef in a single layer if possible.
Some pieces are touching because my skillet is small. What am I looking for while they cook?
Brown the beef on all sides, turning the pieces so the outside gets color. If the pan feels crowded, work in batches rather than steaming the meat.
The beef is browned and I don't want to lose those juices. Where does it go now?
Transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker, scraping in any flavorful bits from the skillet that come along easily.
Can you help me get Dads BBQ Roast started? I've got the roast out on the counter but want to make sure I don't miss anything.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup white sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also need your mixing bowl, beaters or a sturdy spoon, and the baking pan you plan to use.
The butter is soft, and I have both sugars measured. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the batter is mixed.
Oven is heating. The brown sugar is packed into the measuring cup—does it go in with the butter right away?
It does. Put the softened butter in the bowl with the white sugar and the packed brown sugar, then beat them together until the mixture looks lighter and fluffy rather than dense or sandy.
It's starting to look creamy, but I still see a few darker streaks of brown sugar.
Keep beating a little longer and scrape the sides of the bowl so the butter and both sugars blend evenly. You're looking for a smooth, fluffy base before adding the eggs.
That texture looks better now. Do I add the 2 eggs one at a time or both together?
Add the eggs and blend them in well. If it's easier for your bowl, you can add them one at a time, mixing after each, but the key is that the egg mixture becomes evenly combined.
The eggs are mixed in, and the batter looks glossy. What dry ingredients come next?
Mix the flour, baking soda, and salt into the egg mixture. Add them gradually if you want less mess, and stir just until the dry streaks disappear.
I've got a little flour on the sides of the bowl. Should I keep beating hard?
Scrape down the sides and fold or mix gently until everything is incorporated. Once the flour, baking soda, and salt are mixed in, the batter for the Candy Bar Squares is ready for the pan.
I'm making Eclairs II and want to get the pan and ingredients set up before I start heating anything.
Great. For this recipe, put out 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a medium saucepan and a cookie sheet.
I've got the saucepan out. Should I prep the oven or the cookie sheet first?
Start by preheating the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C), then grease the cookie sheet so it's ready when the dough is prepared.
The oven is set to 450 and the cookie sheet is greased. Do I cut up the butter or just put it in whole?
Either is fine, but smaller pieces will melt more evenly. Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to the medium saucepan.
The butter and water are in the pan. What heat should I use?
Use enough heat to bring the mixture to a boil, and stir as it heats so the butter melts completely into the water.
It's starting to steam, but I can still see butter pieces floating. Keep stirring?
Yes, keep stirring until the butter is fully melted. You're looking for the mixture to reach a boil with no solid butter pieces left.
The butter has melted now, and the liquid is bubbling. Where do the flour and salt fit in?
Have the 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt measured and ready beside the stove. The steps you're on have brought the butter and water to a boil, so you're set up for the next part.
Before I move on, can you confirm I didn't miss anything from the prep?

You're on track: the oven is preheated to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C), the cookie sheet is greased, and the saucepan has 1/2 cup butter with 1 cup water brought to a boil while stirring until the butter melted completely.

I'm cooking Blackened Tuna today. Can you help me get the tuna and seasonings organized before the pan gets hot?
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 pounds of fresh tuna steaks, about 1 inch thick, and 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning. Pat the tuna dry if it looks damp so the seasoning clings well.
The tuna steaks are dry and on a plate. How heavy should I go with the Cajun seasoning?
Coat them generously on the surfaces you're cooking, using the 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning across the steaks. Press it on lightly so it forms an even layer instead of falling off in the skillet.
They're coated. What fat should I use in the skillet?
Use 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet. Put the skillet over high heat so the fat gets very hot for the blackened crust.
The butter is melting into the oil. Should I wait for a certain look before adding the tuna?
Yes. Wait until the oil and butter are nearly smoking; that high heat is what helps the Cajun coating blacken quickly.
It's just starting to smoke. How do I place the steaks without crowding them?
Lay the tuna steaks into the pan in a single layer, leaving space between them if you can. If the skillet is too small, cook them in batches rather than squeezing them together.
They're in the pan and sizzling hard. Do I flip them right away or leave them alone?
Leave them undisturbed on that side so the crust can form. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, or until that side is blackened.
The underside looks dark and crusty around the edges. Is that the stopping point for this recipe?

Yes, for this recipe the cooking instruction is to cook one side for 3 to 4 minutes, or until blackened. Once that side has the dark crust you want, take the steaks out of the hot skillet and serve right away.
I'm baking Fresh Apple Walnut Cake today. Can you help me set up the dry ingredients and pan in the right order?
Absolutely. Put the oven rack in a comfortable middle position and start by preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. I have a 9x13 inch pan out—should I prep that before mixing?
Yes. Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour so the cake will release cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. For the dry bowl, I'm seeing flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt—what amounts do I measure?
Measure 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Those are measured. Do I just whisk them, or does this recipe need sifting?
This one calls for sifting them together, so sift the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt into a bowl until they're evenly combined.
The sifted mixture looks even and a little lighter. What should I do with the apples?
Combine the apples with the white sugar in a separate bowl, then set that mixture aside.
Should the apple and sugar bowl sit while I clean up the flour on the counter?
That's fine. Let the apples and white sugar sit aside while you wipe down the counter and keep the sifted dry ingredients ready.
So at this point I should have the oven hot, the pan ready, dry ingredients sifted, and apples with sugar set aside?

Correct. You're set up with the oven at 350 degrees F or 175 degrees C, a greased and floured 9x13 inch pan, the 3 cups flour mixture sifted with baking soda, cinnamon, and salt, and the apples combined with white sugar and resting aside.
I want to make Artichoke Hummus. Can you help me get the ingredients and food processor set up?
Absolutely. Put the food processor bowl and blade in place, then grab 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, also called garbanzo beans, and drain them well.
The chickpeas are drained and the processor is ready. What else goes in?
You'll also need 1 clove of garlic, 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts, and 2 tablespoons lemon juice.
I have the garlic, artichoke hearts, and lemon juice measured. Do I add everything at once?

Yes. Add the chickpeas, garlic, drained marinated artichoke hearts, and lemon juice to the work bowl of the food processor. The recipe notes to combine all ingredients except parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks at this point.
Everything is in the processor bowl. Should I scrape down the sides before blending?
You can if anything is stuck high on the bowl, then secure the lid and pulse the mixture until it becomes smooth.
It's getting creamy but there are still a few small artichoke pieces. Keep pulsing?
Yes, pulse a little longer, stopping to scrape the sides as needed, until the hummus looks smooth and evenly blended.
The texture looks smooth now. What serving dish should I use?
Spoon the artichoke hummus into a serving bowl and smooth the top so it's ready for the table or for chilling.
It's in the bowl, but I'm not serving it right away. How should I store it?
Cover the serving bowl and refrigerate the hummus until you're ready to serve it.
I'm baking Grandmas Gingersnaps and want to get the dough started. Can you walk me through what to pull out?
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup margarine, 1 cup white sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses. You'll also need flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt for the dry mixture.
The margarine is softened and I've measured the sugar and molasses. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the dough comes together.
Oven is heating. I have a medium bowl out—does the margarine go in there with the sugar?
That's right. Put the margarine and the 1 cup white sugar in the medium bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's lighter and pretty smooth now. I'm not sure whether the egg or molasses goes in next.
Add the 1 egg and the 1/4 cup molasses to that bowl, then beat until everything is well blended and the color is even.
The mixture looks glossy and brown. Do I combine the spices with the flour separately?
Yes. In another bowl, combine the flour, ginger, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt so the leavening and spices are evenly distributed.
The dry ingredients are mixed. Should I dump them in all at once or stir gradually?
Stir the dry mixture into the molasses mixture to form a dough. Add it in a few portions if that feels easier to manage, scraping the bowl as needed.
It's turning into a thick dough and there are only a few dry streaks left. How should it look before I stop?
Stop once the flour mixture is fully incorporated and the dough looks cohesive, with no loose dry patches. At that point the gingersnap dough is ready for the next shaping or baking steps.
I'm making Butterscotch Brownies in a Jar. Before I get the oven going, can you help me make sure I have the mix and add-ins straight?
Absolutely. For the jar mix, you'll want 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 tablespoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup flaked coconut ready to go.
I see the flour and coconut, and I'm checking the small amounts now. Anything cold from the fridge?
Yes—set out 3/4 cup butter so it can soften. You'll also need 2 eggs beaten and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract when you mix the batter.
The butter is softening, and I have a 9x13 inch pan. Should I heat the oven while I finish measuring?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. That gives it time to come up to temperature while you prep the pan and batter.
Oven is heating. Do I need parchment, or is greasing the pan enough for this?
The recipe calls for greasing the 9x13 inch baking pan. Coat the bottom and corners well so the brownies release cleanly.
Pan is greased. The jar mix looks a little clumped from sitting on the shelf.
Empty the jar of brownie mix into a large mixing bowl, then stir through it to break up those lumps before adding the wet ingredients.
The dry mix is loosened up. Should the eggs, butter, and vanilla go in separately or together?
Add the 3/4 cup softened butter, the 2 beaten eggs, and the 2 teaspoons vanilla extract to the bowl, then mix until everything is well blended.
It's coming together into a thick batter. Any texture cue before I spread it in the pan?
You're looking for a uniformly blended batter with no dry pockets or big lumps of mix. Once it looks even, spread it into the greased 9x13 inch pan and keep the oven at 375 degrees F.
I'm planning to make Alaskan Halibut Lasagna. Can you walk me through the halibut part so I don't overcook it?

Absolutely. Have 6 tablespoons butter or margarine available, but keep it divided because you'll only use 2 tablespoons to start. You'll also need 1 1/2 pounds halibut steaks with the bones removed, cut into 1 inch cubes.
The halibut is cubed, and I've got the butter measured. What seasonings should be ready by the stove?
Set out 2 minced garlic cloves and 3/4 teaspoon dried thyme. Keep them close, since they go into the skillet with the fish.
I have a large skillet on the burner. What heat should I use for the butter?
Put the skillet over medium heat and melt 2 tablespoons of the butter. Let it coat the bottom of the pan, but don't let it brown.
The butter is melted and foamy around the edges. Should the garlic go in before the fish?
Add the halibut cubes, minced garlic, and dried thyme together. Stir gently so the fish gets coated without breaking up too much.
The fish is in the pan now. How often should I move it around?
Give it a gentle turn now and then, just enough for the pieces to cook evenly. Keep the heat at medium and cook until the fish flakes easily with a fork, about 10 minutes.
It's been close to 10 minutes. What exactly should the texture look like?
Press a piece lightly with a fork. If it separates into flakes easily and looks opaque through the center, it's ready. Try not to keep cooking past that point.
The halibut flakes cleanly. Do I leave it in the skillet while I prep the next part?
No, remove the halibut mixture from the skillet and set it aside. That keeps it from continuing to cook while you move on with the lasagna.

I'm making Fresh Apple Cake and want to get organized before I start mixing. What should I pull out first?
Set out 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil and 2 cups white sugar, since those will go into the batter together.
Oil and sugar are measured. I've got a mixing bowl ready—what else belongs with them?
Add 3 beaten eggs and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract to your setup. Those get beaten together with the oil and sugar.
Before I combine anything, should the oven be on?

The oven is heating. I'm using a tube pan—do I need to prep it now?
Go ahead and grease one 10 inch tube pan well, including the center tube and the edges, so the cake releases cleanly.

Make sure the oven is still at 325 degrees F, the 10 inch tube pan is fully greased, and the wet mixture is ready to receive the sifted dry ingredients.
I'm making Crustless Spinach Quiche 2 and want to get everything set up before I start mixing.
Great. Put a small mixing bowl and a quiche pan on the counter, and coat the quiche pan with nonstick cooking spray so it's ready for the filling later.
