messages.content: I'm making Anzac Biscuits I and want to get the counter set up before I start mixing. Can you walk me through it?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup quick cooking oats, 3/4 cup flaked coconut, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need sugar, syrup, butter, and boiling water for the mixture.
The oats, coconut, flour, and baking soda are out. Should I start with a bowl or the saucepan?
Start with a mixing bowl for the dry ingredients. Add the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut, then stir them together so the coconut and oats are evenly spread through the flour.
The dry mix looks even. What size pan should I use for the butter and syrup?
Use a small saucepan. Keep it over low heat and melt the syrup and butter together gently, stirring so the mixture warms evenly without scorching.
The butter has melted into the syrup and it's smooth. Do I add the baking soda straight to that?
Not straight in by itself. Mix the baking soda with the boiling water first, then add that to the melted butter and syrup mixture.
It foamed a little when I added the soda water. Is that okay?
Yes, that reaction is expected. Give it a careful stir so the soda mixture is fully combined with the butter and syrup.
The saucepan mixture is blended. How do I combine it with the oats and coconut without making a mess?
Pour the warm butter mixture over the dry ingredients in the bowl. Stir from the bottom up, folding until the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut are evenly moistened.
The mixture is coming together and looks sticky in spots. Should I keep stirring?

Yes, keep stirring just until there are no dry patches left. Once the butter mixture is evenly worked through the dry ingredients, you're ready for the next shaping or baking step your recipe calls for.
I'm making Chocolate Covered Banana Pie and have a 9 x 13 inch pan ready. Can you help me pace the crust part?
Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you gather everything.
Oven is heating. For the crumb mixture, what should I measure out?
Measure 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, and 2/3 cup melted butter. You'll also need 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips for the recipe.
The wafers are crushed and the pecans are chopped. Should the butter go in while it's still melted?
Yes, pour in the melted butter while it's fluid, then stir it with the crushed cookie crumbs and pecans until the crumbs look evenly moistened.
Some crumbs look drier near the edge of the bowl. Do I keep mixing or add anything?
Keep folding and scraping the bowl so the butter distributes through the crumbs and pecans. Don't add extra ingredients; the mixture just needs to come together enough to press.
It's holding when I squeeze a bit. How firmly should I pack it into the pan?
Press the crumb mixture evenly into the 9 x 13 inch pan, using the bottom of a measuring cup or your fingers to make a compact, level layer.
The crust is spread out. Do I need to do anything with the sides, or just the bottom?
For this pan, focus on an even layer across the bottom. Once it's pressed in, put it in the 375 degrees F oven.
Timer question: how long should it bake, and what should I look for when it comes out?
Bake it for 5 minutes at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C. After that, take it out and let it cool before continuing with the rest of the pie.
I'm making Broccoli Cheese Crepes and want someone to keep me on track. What should I set out for the crepe batter?
For the batter, put out 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a blender ready.
Blender is on the counter. Should the eggs and water go in before the flour?
Yes, add the eggs and water to the blender, then add the flour and salt. That helps everything blend smoothly.
All four batter ingredients are in. How long should I blend it?
Cover the blender and process the mixture until the batter looks smooth with no visible flour pockets.
It looks smooth now, a little thin like crepe batter. Do I use it right away?
Let it stand for 15 minutes before cooking. That rest gives the flour time to hydrate and helps the crepes cook more evenly.
While it rests, can I start the saucepan part?
Yes. In a small saucepan, saute the onion in butter until the onion is tender. Keep the heat moderate so the butter doesn't brown too much.
The onion is soft and smells good. What texture am I looking for before adding anything else?
Tender is the key point: the onion should look softened and a bit translucent, not crisp or browned hard.
Okay, it's there. What do I stir in next?
Stir in the flour until it's blended with the buttery onion mixture. Keep stirring so it turns into an even paste without dry streaks.
I'm making Fresh Apple Cake today. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put a 10 inch tube pan on the counter, and gather 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil, 2 cups white sugar, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract.
The pan is out, and I've measured the oil and sugar. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, turn the oven to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C, so it can heat while you prep the batter.
Oven is on. For the pan, do I just coat the inside lightly?
Grease the inside of the 10 inch tube pan well, making sure you get around the center tube and the bottom edge so the cake releases cleanly.
Done. I have the eggs beaten in a small bowl. What goes into the mixing bowl first?
Add the vegetable oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar to the mixing bowl, then beat them together until the mixture looks even and glossy.
It's mixed, but the sugar still makes it look a little grainy. Is that okay?
That's okay for this stage. Keep it evenly combined, but it doesn't need to become perfectly smooth before you handle the dry ingredients.
What dry ingredients should I prepare next?
Sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a separate bowl so they're evenly distributed before they go into the batter.
The sifted mixture is ready. Should I clean anything up before continuing?
You can clear away the measuring cups for the oil, sugar, and vanilla, but keep the wet bowl, the sifted dry ingredients, and the greased tube pan nearby for the next part of the cake.

Place the squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.

Yes, for this lunch, keep any extra liquid separate and add it only after you open the thermos so the noodles, pasta, rice, or grains stay in better shape.
I'm making Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs. Can you help me get the ingredients and timing straight before I start?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms, 2 chopped green onions, and 1 clove of garlic, crushed. You'll also need cayenne pepper for the mushroom mixture.
The mushrooms are chopped and the green onions are ready. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's hot when the filling is ready.
Oven is on. I've got a medium saucepan out—does the oil go in cold or should I warm the pan first?
Add the 2 tablespoons olive oil to the medium saucepan and heat it over medium heat. Give it a moment until the oil looks loose and glossy.
The oil is warmed. Do I add everything at once, or should the garlic go in separately?
For this recipe, stir in the 3 cups chopped mushrooms, the 2 chopped green onions, the crushed garlic clove, and the cayenne pepper together.
They're in the pan now. How often should I stir so the garlic doesn't catch?
Stir every minute or so and keep the heat at medium. The mushrooms should start releasing moisture, which helps protect the garlic.
There's liquid in the pan and the mushrooms are shrinking. How long am I cooking this mixture?
Cook it for 10 minutes total, or until the mushrooms and onions are tender. If the pan starts looking dry before then, keep stirring and watch the heat.
At 10 minutes, what texture am I looking for before I stop?
Stop when the mushrooms are tender and the green onions have softened into the mixture. The filling should look cooked down and fragrant, with no raw garlic bite.

Measure 1/2 cup mayonnaise into the jar, then add 3 teaspoons milk.

Yes. Add 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1 pinch ground black pepper right into the jar with the mayonnaise and milk.

Use a tight-fitting lid, because you'll be shaking the jar vigorously and you don't want any dressing leaking out.

Really shake it vigorously until the mayonnaise, milk, salt, and pepper come together into a smooth dressing.

If you're keeping it make-ahead, keep the medium-cut raw vegetables in their separate layer until you're ready to serve.

Pour the shaken dressing over your salad when you're ready to serve.
Anything else to do with the jar before I put things away?
Wipe the rim if needed, close the lid tightly, and keep the dressing ready for your salad alongside the separate vegetable layer.
I'm making Cabbage Kielbasa Supper in the slow cooker. Can you help me get it set up without missing anything?
Absolutely. Use a 5-qt. slow cooker for this one. Have 8 cups shredded cabbage ready, along with 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2 inch cubes.
The cabbage is shredded, and I'm cutting the potatoes now. Do they need to be exact cubes?
They don't have to be perfect, but keep them close to 1/2 inch so they cook evenly and get tender during the long slow-cooker time.
Potatoes are cut. I also have an onion on the counter—how should I prep it?
Chop 1 medium onion, then add it to the slow cooker with the cabbage and potatoes. Sprinkle in 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, plus pepper.
The slow cooker is already looking pretty full with the cabbage and potatoes. Is that okay?
Yes, that's expected. The cabbage will cook down quite a bit, so it's fine if the slow cooker looks full at this stage.
I've mixed the cabbage, potatoes, onion, salt, and pepper in the crock. What liquid goes in?
Pour the broth over everything in the slow cooker, letting it run down through the cabbage and potatoes.
Broth is in. Where does the kielbasa go—mixed in or left on top?
Place the sausage on top rather than stirring it through. It will heat through while the vegetables cook underneath.
Lid is on. What setting and how long should I plan for before serving?
Cook it covered on low for 8-9 hours, until the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.

Put 2 cups all-purpose flour and 1 cup white sugar on the counter first, along with a large mixing bowl.

Yes. Measure out 2 teaspoons baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda.

Go ahead and beat the mixture for 3 minutes, keeping the bowl steady so everything blends evenly.

Scrape down the sides of the bowl and keep the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan nearby so the batter can go in cleanly.
And for the finished platter, I should still keep those decorative touches small, right?

I'm making Eclairs II and want someone to talk me through the early steps. What should I set out?
Set out 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water, plus a medium saucepan for heating them together.
Butter and water are ready. Are there any dry ingredients I should measure before I turn on the stove?
Yes—measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt so they're ready when you need them.
Got it. Should I prepare the oven before I start the saucepan?
Yes, preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) so it can come up to temperature while you work.
The oven is heating. What should I do about the pan for baking?
Grease a cookie sheet now, before the dough work begins, so it's ready when you need to use it.
Cookie sheet is greased. I have the saucepan on the counter—what goes in?
Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to the medium saucepan.
They're in the pan. What heat cue am I watching for?
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring as it heats so the butter melts completely.
So I should keep stirring until the butter is fully melted and the water-butter mixture is boiling?
Exactly. Once it reaches a boil and the butter has melted completely, you've completed the listed cooking step for this part of Eclairs II.
I'm making Famous Caramel Cookie Bars and want to set up before the caramel gets sticky. What should be on the counter?

Set out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 unwrapped caramels, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a baking sheet or tray, a small saucepan, a spoon, and a clear spot in the refrigerator for the tray.
The cookies are still in neat rows in the package. Should I line the tray or just put them straight on it?

Either is fine, but lining the tray can make cleanup easier. Arrange the shortbread cookies in a single layer on the baking sheet or tray, with a little space between them so you can spoon caramel over each one cleanly.
All 40 cookies are laid out. I've unwrapped the caramels too—what heat should I use for the saucepan?
Put the 35 unwrapped caramels in a small saucepan with the 1/4 cup water. Use medium-low heat so they melt gently rather than scorch.
The caramels are starting to soften around the edges. How often should I stir?
Stir frequently, scraping the bottom and sides of the pan as they melt. Keep the heat at medium-low until the mixture turns smooth and pourable.
It's smooth now, but it thickens quickly when I lift the spoon. Is that okay?
Yes, that's normal for melted caramel. Work steadily and spoon a thin line of caramel over each shortbread cookie rather than trying to cover the whole surface.
I'm getting little strings of caramel between cookies. Any way to keep the lines tidier?

Let the extra caramel drip back into the saucepan for a second before moving to the next cookie, and keep each spoonful small. If the caramel gets too stiff, warm it briefly over medium-low heat while stirring.
The caramel lines are on all the cookies. Do they sit out, or should I chill them right away?
Move the tray to the refrigerator and leave the cookies there until the caramel is set. Once the caramel feels firm instead of tacky, they're ready to serve or store.
I'm making Fried Chicken Tenders and want to get the breading station set up before I touch the chicken. What should I put out?

Set out 1 cup all-purpose flour, 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs, 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper. You'll also need shallow bowls for the flour and breadcrumbs, plus a small bowl for eggs and water.
I've got the flour and breadcrumbs on the counter. Should they go in the same dish or separate ones?
Keep them separate. Put the flour by itself in one shallow bowl so each chicken piece can get a dry coating before it goes into the egg mixture.
The flour bowl is ready. How do I season the breadcrumb bowl?
Pour the Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs into a second shallow bowl, then mix in the ground black pepper and cayenne pepper so the spice is evenly distributed through the crumbs.
I mixed the crumbs with the pepper and cayenne. What should I do with the eggs?
Crack the eggs into a small bowl and add the water, then beat them together until the mixture looks smooth enough for dipping.
Okay, I have three bowls now: flour, egg mixture, and seasoned crumbs. What order should the chicken go through?
Work with one piece at a time. Coat the chicken in the flour first, dip it into the eggs and water, then press it into the seasoned bread crumbs.
Should I shake off extra flour before the egg bowl, or leave it thick?
Give each piece a light shake after the flour so it's coated but not clumpy. That helps the egg layer stick, and then the bread crumbs can cling more evenly.
The first few tenders are breaded. Where should I put them while I finish the rest?
Set the coated chicken pieces aside in a single layer as you finish breading the remaining tenders, keeping the flour-to-egg-to-breadcrumb order for each piece.

Get 12 ounces dry fettuccine pasta, 1 pound lean ground beef if you're using it, 1 cup chopped onion, and 1 cup chopped red bell pepper.
I've got the fettuccine out and the beef is thawed. Do I need a pot and a skillet right away?

The water is heating, and I'm chopping the onion and red bell pepper. Should those be measured exactly?
Aim for 1 cup chopped onion and 1 cup chopped red bell pepper so the balance stays right for the Baked Fettuccine Lasagna.
The pot is boiling now. How long should the fettuccine cook?
Add the dry fettuccine to the boiling water and cook it for 8 to 10 minutes, just until al dente, then drain it.
Pasta is in. While the timer runs, should I start the meat?
Yes, start browning the 1 pound lean ground beef in the large skillet over medium heat.
The beef is browning, and there's some fat collecting in the pan. What should I do when it's cooked through?
Drain the fat from the pan, then transfer the browned meat to a bowl.
The pasta is drained and the meat is in a bowl. For packing, when does the crunchy topping come back in?

I'm making Almond Buttercrunch and want to keep the candy part under control. What should I set out before I turn on the stove?

Set out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a saucepan, a spoon or heatproof spatula, a candy thermometer if you have one, and a large buttered cookie sheet ready before the mixture gets hot.
The cookie sheet is buttered and the saucepan is on the stove. Do the butter, sugar, and almonds all go in together?
Yes. Put the butter, white sugar, and 1 cup chopped almonds into the saucepan over low heat. Keep the heat gentle so the butter can melt and the sugar can start dissolving without scorching.
It's starting to look glossy around the edges. Should I keep stirring while it warms up?
Keep stirring constantly until the mixture reaches a boil. Scrape the bottom and corners of the pan as you go so the sugar mixture heats evenly.
It has begun bubbling steadily. Do I keep moving it with the spoon?
Once it boils, stop stirring, and don't shake the pan. Let it cook undisturbed from here so the candy can set up properly.
I have a thermometer clipped on. What temperature am I aiming for?
Heat it to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. Watch closely as it nears that range, because candy can move quickly at the end.
If the thermometer seems slow, is there another way to tell it's ready?
Yes. Drop a small amount of the syrup into cold water. It should form hard, brittle threads; that means it has reached the right stage for the buttercrunch.
It hit the range and the cold-water bit snapped. How do I get it out of the pan?
Carefully pour the hot mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet right away. Tilt or gently spread it as needed, but work cautiously because the candy will be extremely hot.

memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For tonight's Candy Bar Squares, I'm serving them from a casserole-style pan with a finishing drizzle or topping. What's the best way to use the sauce?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Mix a small amount of sauce into the center and leave the edges mostly plain.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Candy Bar Squares as a skillet or casserole serving with a sauce, dressing, glaze, drizzle, topping, or finishing condiment. How should I handle the sauce?

messages.content: For tonight's Candy Bar Squares, I'm serving them from a casserole-style pan with a finishing drizzle or topping. What's the best way to use the sauce?
Spoon a small amount through the middle portion and keep the outer edges mostly plain.
Perfect—that center-drizzled version is what I want just for this batch. Before I dirty any bowls, what should I set out?
Start with 1 cup butter, softened, and 1 cup white sugar near your mixing bowl.
I have a large bowl and the mixer ready. Are there more ingredients to pull before creaming?
Yes. Set out 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 2 eggs. You'll also use flour, baking soda, and salt when the batter comes together.
Since this is going into a casserole pan, should the oven be warming while I measure?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready when the batter is mixed.
The butter is soft and both sugars are measured. What texture should I look for once I start mixing?
Beat the butter or margarine with the white and brown sugars until the mixture turns light and fluffy; scrape the bowl if the sides need it.
It looks paler and fluffy now. Do the eggs go in at this point?
Blend in the 2 eggs, mixing well until they are evenly worked into the sugar-butter mixture.
The batter looks smooth and a little glossy. What happens with the dry ingredients?
Mix the flour, baking soda and salt into the egg mixture just until combined.
When I serve it with the topping, I want the edges easier to cut and lift from the pan. Any final serving cue?
For this pan, keep the drizzle concentrated toward the center and leave the edges mostly plain when you finish and serve it.
I'm making churros today and have a small saucepan ready. What should I put on the counter before I start?
Set out 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also need flour for the dough and oil for frying later.
I've got the water, sugar, salt, vegetable oil, and flour nearby. Do I start in the saucepan?
Yes. Put the saucepan over medium heat and combine the 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil in it.
The mixture is in the pan. Should I stir it while it heats?
Give it a light stir so the sugar and salt dissolve evenly, then let it come up to a boil over medium heat.
It's bubbling now. Do I leave it on the heat?
Once it reaches a boil, remove the saucepan from the heat right away.
The pan is off the burner. How do I add the flour without making a mess?
Add the flour to the hot liquid and stir steadily. Keep mixing until the dough pulls together and forms a ball.
It's thickening and clumping together. Is that the texture I want?
Yes, that's the right direction. Keep stirring just until it's one cohesive ball rather than loose paste.
The dough is together. What should I do for the frying setup?
Heat oil for frying in a deep-fryer or a deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. Once the oil is at that temperature, you'll be ready to fry the churros.
I'm making Cornbread Dressing I and want to get the biscuit and cornbread base right. Can you walk me through it?

Absolutely. Set out 1 (12 ounce) package of refrigerated biscuit dough and 1 (8 ounce) package of corn bread mix. You'll use the biscuit dough to make enough baked biscuits for 4 cups once crumbled, and the cornbread should bake in an 8x8 inch pan according to its package directions.
Got it. I also have onion and celery on the counter—how much should I dice?
Dice 1 cup of onion and 1 cup of celery. Keep them separate or together in a small bowl; they'll go into a pot later with margarine and chicken broth.
Before I start baking, should I grease the cornbread pan or just follow the box?
Follow the corn bread mix package directions for pan prep and baking. The recipe's key point is that you end up with one 8x8 inch pan of cornbread, plus enough biscuits to crumble into 4 cups.
The biscuits are in, and the cornbread pan is ready. Do I crumble them hot or wait?
Let both the biscuits and cornbread cool first so they're easier to handle and crumble. Once cooled, break them into crumbles; measure the biscuit crumbles so you have 4 cups.
The cornbread is cooling now. Should I turn the oven back on for the dressing?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready for the dressing after the crumbled breads and vegetable mixture come together.
My onion and celery are diced. What pot should I use for that part?
Use a small pot. Combine the 1 cup diced onion and 1 cup diced celery with margarine and chicken broth in that pot.
Do I need to add the crumbled biscuit and cornbread into the pot too?

Not for this step. The recipe has you combine the onion, celery, margarine, and chicken broth in the small pot; keep the cooled, crumbled biscuits and cornbread nearby so they're ready for the next mixing stage.
I'm making Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake and want to get everything arranged before the ice cream gets too soft. What should I put out?

Set out 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies, 1/4 cup melted margarine, 1 cup hot fudge topping, and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream. You'll also want a 9-inch springform pan or a pie plate ready.
I've got the pan and ingredients out. Do I use all the cookies for the crust?
Use only half of the cookies for the crust—about 20 cookies. Crush those into crumbs and keep the remaining cookies whole for lining the edge of the pan.
The crumbs are a little uneven. Is that okay for pressing into the bottom?
A few small uneven bits are fine, but aim for mostly crumbs so the crust holds together. Mix the crushed cookies with the melted 1/4 cup margarine until the crumbs look evenly moistened.
The crumb mixture is damp and clumping lightly. How do I shape it in the pan?
Press it firmly and evenly across the bottom of the 9-inch springform pan or pie plate. Use the bottom of a measuring cup or your fingers to compact it into a solid crust.
Crust is packed in. What do I do with the whole cookies I saved?
Stand the remaining whole cookies upright around the edge of the pan, with their flat sides against the side if that helps them stay in place.
They're standing around the rim, but a couple lean inward. Should I fix that before adding fudge?
Yes, straighten them as much as you can so they make a neat border. Then spread 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the cookie crust.
I have 1 cup of fudge topping total. Should I use all of it on the crust?
For this step, use 3/4 cup over the crust and keep the remaining fudge topping aside. Spread it gently so you don't disturb the cookie border.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake

messages.content: I'm making Barbecued Shredded Beef and have a large roasting pan out. What should I set up before the beef goes in?
Set the oven to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C. While it heats, put your 3 pounds beef roast on the counter, chop 2 onions, and keep the roasting pan nearby.
The oven is heating and the onions are chopped. Should the roast go in plain, or do I season the pan first?
Put the roast directly into the large roasting pan, then scatter the chopped onions over the top and around it so they can cook down with the beef.
Roast and onions are in the pan. I have the beer and Worcestershire sauce out—how much of each am I using?
Use 2 cans or bottles of beer, 12 fluid ounces each, and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce. You'll mix the sauce ingredients separately before pouring them over the roast.
What goes in that mixing bowl besides the Worcestershire?
In a large bowl, combine the Worcestershire sauce with liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir those together so the seasonings are evenly distributed.
That mixture is combined. Do I pour the beer into the pan or into the bowl?
Pour the beer into the bowl with the Worcestershire mixture, stir it together, then add the whole mixture to the roasting pan over and around the beef and onions.
The liquid is in the roasting pan now. Should the onions be submerged or sitting on top?
It's fine if some onions sit on top of the roast and some settle into the beer mixture. Just make sure the liquid is in the pan and the onions are spread over the beef rather than piled in one spot.
Before I put it in the oven, can you recap the setup so I know I didn't miss anything?

You should have the oven at 275 degrees F, or 135 degrees C; a 3 pound beef roast in a large roasting pan; 2 chopped onions scattered over it; and a stirred mixture of 2 12-fluid-ounce beers, 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper added to the pan.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip and have the casserole dish out. What should I set on the counter?

Set out 1 cup mayonnaise, 8 ounces sour cream, 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, and 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts. You'll also need the cheese and crab meat called for in the mixing step, plus a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish.
The artichoke can is open. Do I need to do anything to them before mixing?
Yes—drain the artichoke hearts well, then chop them so they'll spread evenly through the dip instead of staying in large pieces.
I'm ready to start heating the oven. What temperature should I use?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. While it heats, you can assemble everything directly in the casserole dish.
I've got the 1-1/2 quart dish in front of me. What goes in together?

Add the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, drained chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat to the casserole dish. Stir until the creamy base and soup mix are evenly worked through the crab and artichokes.
The mixture looks pretty thick and creamy. Should I cover the dish before it bakes?
Leave it uncovered. Put the casserole dish in the preheated oven and bake it for 30 minutes.
While it bakes, what texture am I looking for at the end?
After 30 minutes, it should be hot all the way through and ready to serve right away. If the top looks warmed and the dip is bubbling at the edges, you're in good shape.
It just came out of the oven and smells garlicky. How should I serve it?
Serve it immediately while it's hot and creamy. Put the casserole dish on a heat-safe surface and offer sturdy dippers like crackers, bread pieces, or vegetables.
I'm making Broccoli Chicken Roli and have a bowl, a cookie sheet, and foil out. What should I put on the counter first?
Start with the main filling ingredients: 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat and 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli. Put them near your large mixing bowl so they're ready to combine.
Chicken and broccoli are ready. I'm chopping the vegetables now—how much onion and bell pepper do I need?
Use 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper. Try to chop them fairly small so they mix evenly through the filling.
The onion and green pepper are measured. Does everything go into the bowl at once?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the chicken, broccoli, onions, bell pepper, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic.
I added those. The mixture looks a little separated with the mayonnaise and mustard in spots.
Keep folding and stirring until it's all mixed together. You want the chicken, broccoli, vegetables, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic evenly distributed.
It's mixed now and looks more even. Should I deal with the oven before shaping or baking anything?
Yes, turn the oven on to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C. Let it preheat while you get the pan ready.
The oven is set to 400. What should I do with the cookie sheet?
Cover the cookie sheet with aluminum foil, pressing it flat so it sits smoothly on the pan.
Foil is on the sheet. Is there anything else from the prep list I should double-check before moving on?

Check that the bowl has the cooked chicken, fresh broccoli, onion, green bell pepper, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic all mixed together, and that the foil-lined cookie sheet is ready for the next part of the recipe.
I'm making Black Bean Chili and have a large saucepan ready. Can you help me pace the prep and cooking?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 chopped onion, 2 red bell peppers that are seeded and chopped, and 1 jalapeno pepper that's seeded and minced.
The onion and peppers are chopped. Should I keep the jalapeno separate or can it go in with the other vegetables?
It can stay with the onion and red bell peppers since they'll all go into the pan together once the oil is hot.
The saucepan is on the stove. What heat should I use for the oil?
Pour in the olive oil and heat it in the large saucepan over medium-high heat until it looks loose and shiny.
The oil is moving easily in the pan. Do the vegetables go in now?
Yes. Add the onion, red bell peppers, jalapeno, mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn. Sautee them for 10 minutes, or until the onions turn translucent.
I'm stirring, and the pan is pretty full. Should I be looking for browning or mostly softening?
Mostly softening. Keep everything moving so it cooks evenly, and use the onions as your cue: translucent is the target rather than deep browning.
The onions look translucent and the peppers have softened. What seasonings go in?
Season the vegetables with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder, stirring so the spices coat the mixture evenly.
The spices are mixed in and it smells good. What should I add to turn it into the chili?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Mix well so the beans and broth combine with the seasoned vegetables.
I'm making Chicken Marsala with Portobello Mushrooms. Can you help me get the prep lined up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. Put the oven on to preheat at 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it's ready when you need it.
Oven is heating. What ingredients should I pull onto the counter?
You'll need 3/4 cup butter, divided; 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided; 4 portobello mushroom caps, sliced; and 1 clove garlic, chopped.
The mushrooms are sliced, and I've got the garlic chopped. How much butter and oil go into the skillet right now?
Use 1/2 cup of the butter and 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Let the butter melt into the oil before adding the mushrooms.
The butter has melted and the skillet looks evenly coated. Do the portobellos go in by themselves?
Yes, add the sliced portobello mushroom caps to the skillet and cook them over medium heat, stirring as they soften.
How tender should they be before I stop cooking them?
Cook and stir until the mushroom slices are tender throughout and have released some moisture, but don't let them scorch.
They're soft now and there's a little liquid in the pan. Should I add anything else at this point?
For this part of the recipe, don't add more. Take the skillet off the heat once the mushrooms are tender.
Skillet is off the burner. What should I do with the mushrooms while I keep working?
Cover the mushrooms to keep them warm, then set them aside until you're ready to use them in the Chicken Marsala.
I'd like to put together the Double Fudge Brownie Mix as a jar gift. What should I set out?
Set out a clean 1 quart or 1 liter jar, plus the dry ingredients: 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
I have the jar washed and dried. Does the order matter when I layer everything?
Yes, use the listed order so the jar looks neat: white sugar first, then unsweetened cocoa powder, then all-purpose flour, and chopped pecans on top.
The sugar is in. The cocoa is a little dusty—should I press it down?
You can gently tap the jar on the counter or level the cocoa with a spoon, but don't pack it hard. That keeps the layers distinct while still leaving room for the flour and pecans.
Cocoa and flour are layered now. The flour left some powder on the inside glass.
Wipe the inside rim carefully with a dry paper towel before adding the pecans. Try not to disturb the layers below.
The pecans are on top and the jar is full. What needs to go on the tag?
Attach a tag with the baking instruction from the recipe: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
Should I add anything else to the tag about mixing or baking time?
This recipe only gives that preheat instruction for the tag, so keep the required wording to the oven temperature and avoid inventing extra directions.
Okay, the tag is tied on. Any final check before I give it away?
Make sure the lid is secure, the layers are visible, and the tag is firmly attached. The Double Fudge Brownie Mix is ready to gift.
I'm making Chicken Vegetable Stew today and have a large pot ready. Can you help me organize the prep?
Absolutely. Cut 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces, chop 1 onion, and set out 1/2 pound baby carrots plus 4 potatoes.
The chicken is cut up, the onion is chopped, and the carrots are still whole. Should I peel or cut the potatoes before they go in?
Use the potatoes in stew-friendly pieces so they cook evenly with the chicken and carrots. Once they're prepped, keep the chicken, onion, baby carrots, and potatoes close to the pot.
Everything is prepped on the counter. Does the onion need to be softened separately first?
For this stew, you can load it straight into the large pot: add the chopped onion, chicken breast meat, baby carrots, and potatoes together.
They're all in the pot now. What seasoning goes in at this stage?
Add the salt and turmeric over the ingredients, then give the pot a gentle stir so the seasoning starts to distribute.
I added salt and turmeric. I also have tomato paste open—how do I add it without clumps?
Dissolve the tomato paste in water first, stirring until it loosens into a smooth mixture, then pour that into the pot.
The tomato paste mixture is in. Should I season more before it cooks down?
If you'd like, add garlic powder and ground black pepper now. They're optional, so use them just to season to your taste.
I added a little garlic powder and black pepper. Anything I should check before leaving it to simmer?

Make sure the chicken, potatoes, carrots, and onion are settled in the liquid and the tomato paste is mixed through. From here, cook until the chicken is done and the vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally so nothing sticks.
I'm making Escargots Vol au Vent and have the snails out. Can you keep me on track from prep through the butter mixture?
Absolutely. Set out 12 helix snails without shells and 1/2 cup softened butter so both are ready to use.
The butter is softening on the counter. What aromatics should I chop before I touch the snails?
Finely chop 2 cloves of garlic and 1 green onion. Keep them close to your mixing bowl, since they'll go straight into the butter.
Garlic and green onion are chopped. Should I start heating the oven yet?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's ready when the escargots are assembled.
Oven is heating. The snails are in a small container with liquid—what do I do with them?
Drain the escargots, rinse them under cold water, then drain them again well so extra liquid doesn't water down the butter mixture.
They're rinsed and sitting in the strainer. Should I pat them dry or move on to the bowl?
Let them drain thoroughly; a light pat is fine if they still look wet. While they finish draining, use the mixing bowl for the seasoned butter.
I've got the bowl ready with the softened butter. What goes in with it?
Add the finely chopped garlic and green onion to the butter, along with parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine.
Everything is added, but the butter is a little uneven. What texture am I looking for before using it?
Mix thoroughly until the butter is evenly combined with the garlic, green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine, with no plain butter streaks left.
I'm making Apple Cranberry Crisp 2 and have an 8 inch square dish ready. Can you help me pace the prep?
Absolutely. Start by getting the fruit ready: you'll need 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced, plus 3/4 cup cranberries.
The apples are sliced and the cranberries are measured. What should I set out for seasoning?
Measure 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. The fruit mixture also gets nutmeg, so keep that nearby too.
Before I mix anything, should I deal with the oven and baking dish?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, and butter the 8 inch square baking dish so the crisp won't stick.
The oven is heating and the dish is buttered. I've got a large mixing bowl out.
Use that bowl for the filling: combine the sliced apples, cranberries, white sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Toss until the fruit is evenly coated.
Some apple slices are clumping together with the sugar. Should I keep tossing?
Yes, gently separate the slices as you toss so the cranberries and spices spread through the fruit instead of sitting in pockets.
The fruit looks evenly coated now. Does it go straight into the baking dish?
It does. Transfer the apple-cranberry mixture into the buttered dish and spread it evenly from corner to corner.
The bowl still has a little cinnamon-sugar residue. Is that okay for the topping?
That's fine. In the same bowl, combine the oats, flour, and brown sugar, scraping in any remaining spice mixture so nothing gets wasted.
Can you help me make Broccoli Coleslaw? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to make sure I start with the dressing correctly.

Absolutely. For the dressing, set out 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1 chicken-flavored ramen packet from a 3 ounce package. Keep the noodles separate for later, but save the seasoning packet for the dressing.
The ramen is crushed already. Do I add the noodles to the dressing too, or just the seasoning?
Just the seasoning packet goes into the small bowl with the olive oil, vinegar, and sugar. Whisk or stir it until the sugar starts dissolving and the seasoning is evenly mixed in.
It looks a little grainy from the sugar. Is that okay before it chills?
That's fine. Mix it well, then refrigerate the dressing for at least 1 hour before serving, or let it sit overnight if you have the time. The chill helps the flavors come together.
While that's in the fridge, should I prep the vegetables in the big bowl?
Yes. In a large bowl, combine the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds. Toss them a bit so the add-ins are spread through the broccoli mixture instead of sitting in one spot.
Should the ramen go in with the vegetables now or right before serving?
Stir the crushed ramen noodles into the large bowl when you're ready to assemble. If you want them crunchier, wait until close to serving before mixing them in.
The dressing has chilled for 1 hour. Do I pour all of it over the broccoli mix?

Pour it over gradually and toss as you go so everything gets coated. The recipe's dressing amount is made from the full 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup vinegar, 1/2 cup sugar, and reserved seasoning packet, so use it to dress the full bowl to your liking.
Any final serving tip before I bring it to the table?

Give the coleslaw one last toss, making sure the crushed ramen is stirred in evenly with the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds. Serve it chilled, and keep any leftovers refrigerated.
Can you help me make Best Macaroni Salad? I've got a big pot and a mixing bowl ready.

Absolutely. Set out 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup peeled, seeded, chopped cucumber, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. You'll also want ham and cheese ready for stirring in later.
The macaroni and mayo are on the counter. For the cucumber, should it be prepped before I start boiling water?
Yes, that's a good time to do it. Peel the cucumber, scoop out the seeds, and chop enough for 1 cup while your pot of salted water comes to a boil.
Water is boiling now. Do I add the whole 16 ounce package of macaroni?
Add the full package to the salted boiling water and cook it until al dente, so it's tender but still has a little firmness.
The pasta tastes al dente. Should I drain it hot or cool it down first?
Drain it, then rinse it under cold water to stop the cooking and cool it for the salad. Let it drain well so the dressing doesn't get watery.
It's rinsed and draining in the colander. What goes into the large bowl first?
Put the cooled macaroni in the large bowl, add the 1/2 cup mayonnaise, and mix until the pasta is evenly coated.
The mayo is mixed in. I have the chopped cucumber and dried minced onion measured out.
Stir in the 1 cup chopped cucumber and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion, then add the ham and cheese and fold everything together.
Everything is in the bowl, but some pieces of cucumber are sitting on top. Is there anything else before serving?
Give it one more thorough mix so the cucumber, onion, ham, cheese, and dressed macaroni are evenly distributed. Once it looks well combined, it's ready to serve or chill.
Can you help me make Cabbage Kielbasa Supper in the slow cooker? I want to make sure I load it in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out a 5-qt. slow cooker, then prep 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2 inch cubes, and 1 medium chopped onion.
The cabbage is shredded and the potatoes are cubed. Should the onion go in with them right away?
Yes. Add the cabbage, potatoes, and chopped onion directly to the slow cooker. Sprinkle in 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, plus pepper if you're using it.
It looks really full already. Is that okay before I add liquid?
That's expected for this recipe. The cabbage takes up a lot of space at the start, but it will cook down as the slow cooker runs.
Good to know. Where does the broth come in?
Pour the broth evenly over everything in the slow cooker so the vegetables are moistened throughout.
The broth is in. Do I stir it, or leave the layers alone?
A light settling stir is fine if you need room, but don't worry about mixing it perfectly. Keep the vegetables underneath because the sausage goes on top.
I'm ready for the kielbasa. Should I tuck it down into the cabbage?
Place the sausage on top rather than burying it. The slow cooker may be full, but as the cabbage softens, everything will settle.
Once the lid is on, how long should I cook it, and what am I checking for at the end?
Cover it and cook on low for 8-9 hours. It's done when the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.
I want to make Beet and Pear Puree today. Can you guide me without rushing through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 8 medium beets, 1 pound unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, and 4 Bosc pears that are peeled, cored, and minced.
I have the beets and butter out, and I'm mincing the onions now. Should I start heating anything?
Yes—preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's ready for roasting the beets.
The oven is heating. Do the beets need trimming or peeling before they go in?
For this recipe step, wash the beets well and place them in a roasting pan. You can handle any peeling after they roast and cool if needed.
They're washed and in the pan. How long should I expect them to take?
Bake them for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until they're tender when pierced. Once they're done, set them aside to cool before handling.
While the beets roast, I've got the pears peeled, cored, and minced. Anything else I should prep?
That's the main prep covered: the Vidalia onions should be minced, and the Bosc pears should stay peeled, cored, and minced until you're ready for the skillet stage.
The beets are tender now, and I've moved them aside to cool. What pan should I use next?
Use a large skillet and place it over medium heat. Add the unsalted butter and let it melt evenly.
The butter is melting in the skillet. Should I keep the heat at medium while I get the onions and pears nearby?
Yes, keep it at medium heat and have the minced Vidalia onions and minced Bosc pears ready to add once the butter is fully melted.
I want to make French Apple Cream Pie. Can you guide me while I get everything set up?
Absolutely. Set out 1 recipe pastry for a 9 inch double crust pie and 1 (21 ounce) can apple pie filling. You'll also need the spices in a moment.
The pastry and the can of filling are on the counter. Which spices should I measure?
Measure 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg. If your lemon rind is ready, keep it nearby too, since it gets mixed with the filling.
I've got the cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon rind. Should I heat the oven before rolling the dough?
Yes, preheat the oven to 425 degrees F, which is 220 degrees C, so it can come up to temperature while you work on the pastry.
Oven is heating. My pastry is still chilled—do I roll both crusts right away?
Roll out the pastry shell, then let it rest in the refrigerator. Keeping it cool helps it stay easier to handle before it goes into the pan.
The rolled pastry has rested. I have a 9 inch pie pan ready—how should I place it?
Line the 9 inch pie pan with one rolled out pastry crust, easing it into the bottom and sides rather than stretching it.
The bottom crust is in the pan. Should the filling go straight in from the can?
Put the apple pie filling in a medium mixing bowl first, then combine it with the cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon rind so the spices are evenly distributed.
It smells good and the filling looks evenly mixed. Is that the point where I add it to the crust?
Yes, spoon the mixed apple filling into the lined pie pan and spread it gently so it sits evenly in the crust.
Can you help me make A Very Intense Fruit Smoothie? I've got my blender out but haven't started measuring anything yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 (10 ounce) package of frozen mixed berries, 1 (15 ounce) can of sliced peaches that you'll drain, and 2 tablespoons of honey.
The berries are still frozen solid. Should I thaw them before they go in?
No need to thaw them for this recipe. Use the frozen mixed berries as they are; they'll help make the smoothie thick and cold.
Okay. I opened the peaches—do I pour off all the liquid from the 15 ounce can?
Yes, drain the sliced peaches before adding them. Once drained, add the peaches to the blender with the frozen berries.

Add the 2 tablespoons of honey right on top of the fruit. That gives you all the ingredients in the blender: frozen mixed berries, drained canned peaches, and honey.

You can start blending right away. If the frozen berries catch under the blades, stop the blender and gently shake or stir the mixture, then continue blending.

Pause and scrape down the sides if needed, then blend again until the smoothie looks completely smooth.

That's it for the recipe. Pour the smoothie into glasses and serve it right away while it's cold and freshly blended.
I'm making Frosted Shortbread today. Can you guide me without rushing me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butter, softened, and make sure it's real butter with no substitutes. You'll also need 1 cup packed brown sugar.
The butter is soft and I packed the brown sugar into the measuring cup. What else should be on the counter?
Add 1 egg yolk and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to your setup. You'll also need flour and salt for the dry mixture, plus a greased 15-in pan.
I have a mixing bowl ready. Should I start with the butter?
Yes. Put the softened butter and packed brown sugar in the mixing bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks blended and smooth.
It's combined and looks creamy. Do I add the yolk straight in?
Go ahead and add the egg yolk, then pour in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Mix well so the yolk and vanilla are evenly worked into the creamed mixture.
That's mixed in. The bowl looks a little loose but uniform.
That's fine. In a separate bowl, combine the flour and salt, then add that dry mixture to the creamed mixture.
Should I dump all the flour and salt in at once, or add it gradually?
Add it in gradually if that feels easier to control. Keep mixing just until the dry ingredients are incorporated into the butter-sugar mixture.
The dough is together now. I've greased the pan—how do I shape it?
Press the dough evenly into the greased 15-in pan, working it out toward the edges so the shortbread layer is level before you move on.
Can you help me put together Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies? I'm setting this up as a jar mix rather than baking them right away.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also want a clean wide-mouth glass jar that holds 1 liter.
I've got the jar washed and dry. Should I mix anything before it goes in?

Yes. In a bowl, combine the 4 cups all-purpose flour with the 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. The recipe also says to combine the flour with salt and nutmeg, so add those with the dry mixture if you're including them.
The dry mixture is blended. Do I put the flour in the jar first or the sugar?
Layer the 1 1/2 cups white sugar into the bottom of the clean 1 liter wide-mouth jar first. Try to make the layer even so the finished jar looks neat.
Sugar layer is in. The flour mixture looks like a lot—any trick for adding it cleanly?
Spoon or funnel the flour mixture in slowly on top of the sugar. Tap the jar gently as you go so it settles without making a mess, but keep the layers as distinct as you can.
It's filled almost to the top. Should I pack it down?
Press the contents firmly in place, just enough to compact the layers so they fit securely. Then seal the jar tightly.
Jar is sealed. I want to include baking directions for the person receiving it—what should the card say?
Write a card that starts with: "In a large bowl, beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy." Attach that card to the jar.
Should I mention that this is a sugar cookie mix on the tag too?
Yes, label it "Cookie Jar Sugar Cookies" and tie the instruction card to the jar. That way the recipient knows it's a sugar cookie mix and has the first mixing direction ready to follow.
I want to make Cheddar Artichoke Quiche Cups. Can you guide me while I prep everything?

Absolutely. Start by pulling out a 1 (7.5 ounce) jar of marinated artichoke hearts, 1 small finely chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 4 beaten eggs. You'll also need bread crumbs, mustard, oregano, pepper, and hot pepper sauce for the egg mixture.

Drain the artichoke hearts, but don't discard all the liquid. Reserve half of the marinade because you'll use it to cook the onion and garlic.

Chop the artichoke hearts into small pieces, then set them aside while you work on the aromatics.

Use the reserved marinade in the skillet. Add the finely chopped onion and minced garlic, then sauté them in that marinade until they're tender.
The onion is soft and the garlic smells cooked. Do I leave that mixture in the pan?
Take it off the heat and set the onion-garlic mixture aside so it can stop cooking while you mix the bowl ingredients.
My eggs are already beaten in a large bowl. What should I add to them?
Into the beaten eggs, combine the bread crumbs, mustard, oregano, pepper, and hot pepper sauce. Stir until the mixture looks evenly blended.
Should the chopped artichokes and sautéed onion mixture be folded in after that?

Yes, that's the right point to bring those prepared parts together: add the chopped artichokes and the sautéed onion and garlic to the seasoned egg mixture, then stir gently so the quiche cup filling is evenly distributed.
Can you help me make Asparagus Sandwiches? I've got a 10 ounce can of asparagus tips drained already.
Absolutely. Lay the drained asparagus tips on paper towels so the extra liquid can wick away while you get the spread ready.
They're on towels. For the spread, am I using mayonnaise with the onion?
Yes. In a small bowl, stir together 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons finely chopped onion, and 1 pinch seasoning salt until the onion is evenly mixed through.
The mixture looks smooth with little onion bits in it. Should the asparagus be completely dry before I roll these?
It doesn't need to be bone dry, but blot off any obvious moisture. Too much liquid can make the bread soft before you serve it.
I'm ready with the bread. Do I cut the crusts off before spreading?
Yes, remove the crusts from the bread slices first. Then spread a thin layer of the mayonnaise mixture over each slice, all the way close to the edges.
Thin layer makes sense. How much asparagus goes on each slice?
Place one asparagus spear on a prepared slice of bread. Set it near one edge so it's easy to roll up neatly.
When I roll them, should I press hard to seal them?
Roll gently but snugly around the spear. A light press at the seam is enough; pressing too hard can squeeze out the filling.
I've got several rolled up now. Any quick serving tip so they stay tidy on the plate?
Arrange them seam-side down on the serving plate. If they feel damp, give them a minute on a clean paper towel before plating.
Can you help me make churros today? I'm setting up my saucepan and frying pan now.

I've got the water, sugar, salt, and oil measured. Should they all go into the saucepan together?

They're in the pan. Do I stir while it heats, or just let it come up?
Give it a gentle stir so the sugar and salt dissolve evenly, then let the mixture come to a boil over medium heat.
It's boiling now and the sugar looks dissolved. What should I do before it cooks down too much?
Take the saucepan off the heat as soon as it reaches that boil.
Pan is off the burner. I have flour nearby, but the dough texture is what I'm unsure about.
Stir in the flour while the mixture is still hot. Keep mixing until it pulls together and forms a ball.
It's thickening and clumping around the spoon. Should it be one smooth mass?
That's what you want: a single dough ball that has come together rather than a loose batter.
Great, the dough is together. I'm ready to heat oil for frying—what temperature am I aiming for?
Heat the frying oil in a deep-fryer or deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, before frying the churros.
Can you help me make Gelatin Fruit Salad? I've got a saucepan out, but I want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple left undrained.
The applesauce and gelatin are on the counter. Should the pineapple juice go in too, or do I drain it?
Keep the pineapple undrained, so the juice goes in with the crushed pineapple later. For now, pour the 1 cup applesauce into the saucepan.
Applesauce is in the pan. Am I just warming it or bringing it all the way up?
Bring the applesauce to a boil, stirring occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't scorch on the bottom.
It's bubbling now. Do I keep it on the burner while adding the cherry gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat, then stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is fully dissolved.
The gelatin looks dissolved and smooth. I'm a little worried the soda will foam when I pour it in.
That can happen, so add the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda slowly while stirring gently.
The soda is mixed in without too much fizz. When do I add the pineapple?
Stir in the 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple, including its juice, until it's evenly distributed through the gelatin mixture.
It's all mixed. Should I pour it into a serving bowl before chilling?
Yes, transfer it to your serving bowl or mold, then refrigerate it until firm. Once it's set, it's ready to serve chilled.
Can you guide me through making Atomic Canuck Chili? I'm starting by clearing space near the stove and slow cooker.
Absolutely. Set out a large skillet and your slow cooker. For the base, you'll need 2 pounds lean ground beef and 1/2 large onion, diced.
The beef is thawed and the onion is diced. Which seasonings should I put beside the skillet?
Keep 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper and 3 tablespoons garlic powder nearby. The recipe also has you brown everything with seasoned pepper, so have that within reach too.

Put the ground beef, diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper into the large skillet together. Cook over medium heat, breaking up the beef as it browns.

Drain off the fat carefully, then transfer the browned beef and onion mixture into the slow cooker.
The meat mixture is in the slow cooker. What should I stir in from the pantry and fridge?
Stir in the mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce until everything is well combined.

Season it now with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper, then stir again so the heat is distributed through the chili.

Wipe the skillet once it's cooled enough to handle and rinse any sticky tomato paste or barbeque sauce utensils before they dry. When you serve, give the chili a good stir so the beef, beans, vegetables, and sauce are evenly portioned.

messages.content: For Easy Punch, can we do my center-and-crescent garnish on the bowl instead of a full scatter?

Yes. Once the punch is mixed, keep the softer garnish gathered in the middle and place the crisp garnish in a little crescent off to one side, so the surface stays intentional rather than evenly covered.
Great. Before I pour anything, what size bowl and ingredients should I put on the counter?
Use a large punch bowl. Set out 4 packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder, each 0.13 ounce, plus 2 cans of pineapple juice, each 46 fluid ounces.
The bowl is out, and I have the drink mix and pineapple juice. What else goes into the base?
Add 3 cups white sugar to your prep area, and measure 4 quarts water. Those combine with the drink mix and pineapple juice in the punch bowl.
That layout sounds right—the garnish should stay composed, not dusted all over the top. Should I add the powders first or the liquids first?
You can add them to the large punch bowl together: strawberry drink mix powder, pineapple juice, white sugar, and water. Pour slowly so the powder does not puff up, then give yourself room to stir.
The mix, juice, sugar, and water are in. It looks cloudy and a little grainy; how long should I stir?
Stir until the sugar and drink mix are dissolved. Scrape around the bottom and sides of the bowl as you go, because the sugar can settle there.

Yes, keep stirring until that gritty feel is gone. The punch should look evenly colored and the spoon should move without dragging through sugar crystals.

Stir in the ginger ale gently at the end, using the amount your recipe source calls for if you have it. Add it slowly to preserve the bubbles and avoid splashing.

Give the punch one gentle final stir, then add your center-and-crescent garnish: softer pieces gathered in the middle, crisp pieces curved along one side. Serve from the large bowl while it is cold and fizzy.
Can you guide me through making Frosted Shortbread? I've got my mixer out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butter, softened, with no substitutes, and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Those two get creamed together, so it helps if the butter is soft but not melted.
The butter is soft and the brown sugar is packed. Do I need the egg now too?
Yes. Have 1 egg yolk ready, along with 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll add both after the butter and brown sugar are creamed.
What pan should I prep before I get my hands messy?
Grease a 15-in pan so it's ready when the dough is mixed. You'll press the shortbread mixture into it rather than scoop or roll it.
Pan is greased. How should the butter and sugar look once I mix them?
Put the softened butter and packed brown sugar in a mixing bowl and cream them together until they look well blended and a bit lighter, with no big streaks of butter showing.
That's mixed and smooth. Should I add the yolk and vanilla straight in?
Yes, add the egg yolk and the vanilla extract to the creamed mixture, then mix well so the yolk is fully incorporated.
It looks evenly mixed. The recipe mentions dry ingredients—how do I handle those?
Combine the flour and salt separately, then add that mixture to the creamed mixture. Mix just until it comes together into a shortbread dough.
The dough is ready and a little crumbly but holds when pressed. What's the best way to get it into the pan?
Transfer it to the greased 15-in pan and press it evenly across the bottom, especially into the corners and edges, so the shortbread bakes in an even layer.
Can you help me make Chocolate Covered Banana Pie? I'm starting with the crust and want to keep the steps straight.
Absolutely. Set out 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, 2/3 cup melted butter, and 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips so everything is measured before you start.
The wafers are crushed and the pecans are chopped. Should the butter be fully melted before I mix?
Yes, melt the 2/3 cup butter completely so it coats the crumbs evenly. Stir the crushed vanilla wafers, chopped pecans, and melted butter together until the mixture looks evenly moistened.
It's mixed, but it still looks crumbly rather than like dough. Is that okay?
That's fine for a crumb crust. It should clump a bit when pressed, but it doesn't need to become a smooth dough.
What pan should I use for pressing it in?
Use a 9 x 13 inch pan. Scatter the crumb mixture across the bottom first, then press it down firmly and evenly into the pan.
I've pressed it in. Do I need to chill it or bake it right away?
Bake it right away at 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, for 5 minutes.
It's in the oven now. Should I be watching for browning, or just go by the time?
Go by the 5 minutes; this is a short bake to set the crust. If the edges look slightly firmer, that's enough.
The timer is done and the pan is out. What should I do before adding anything else?
Let the crust cool completely in the pan. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips ready for the chocolate-covered part once the cooled base is ready.

Yes—preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready if you need it while the chicken cooks.

Add the 1/2 teaspoon onion powder when the chicken goes into the skillet so it seasons the surface as the chicken starts cooking.

Cook it for about 15 minutes, turning as needed, until the chicken is browned and just about done.

Sprinkle on the 1 pinch salt, then add pepper to taste. Give the chicken a brief turn in the skillet so the seasoning hits both sides, then it's ready to serve.

Chop 1 large yellow onion and slice 1 cup celery. Keep them nearby, since the onion goes in soon after the chicken is browned, and the celery will simmer later with the stew.

Yes. Add the chopped onion to the pot and sauté it in those browned bits until it softens, about 5 minutes. Stir now and then so it doesn't stick.

Add the broth, beans, tomatoes, sliced celery, carrots, wine, bay leaf, and herbs, then return all the chicken to the pot. Stir everything together so the chicken is tucked into the liquid.

Cover the pot and let the stew simmer for 40 minutes. Keep it at a gentle simmer rather than a hard boil, and check near the end that the chicken is tender and the vegetables have softened.

Measure 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
I've got the flour and cocoa measured, and the baking powder and salt are ready too. Should the pan be prepared before I mix?
Yes, butter one Madeleine pan now. Make sure the shell-shaped wells get a light, even coating so the cakes release cleanly.
Pan is buttered. Do I sift everything together directly into a bowl?
Yes. Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together into a mixing bowl so the cocoa breaks up and the leavening is evenly distributed.
The dry mix looks smooth and evenly colored. What happens with the butter mixture?
In a separate bowl, cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar. Work it until the mixture looks blended and a bit lighter.
Should I add the dry ingredients into that after creaming, or is there another prep detail from the recipe first?
From the steps you're following, the required prep is covered: oven preheated, pan buttered, dry ingredients sifted, and butter creamed with vanilla and sugar.
Good. Before I continue, can you recap the exact dry ingredient amounts so I don't misread them?
For the dry mixture, use 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
Can you guide me through making Grandmas Wheat Germ Cookies? I'm setting up my mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl in your workspace and start by measuring 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour and 1 1/2 cups toasted wheat germ.
Flour and wheat germ are measured. Are oats part of the dry mix too?
Yes. Add 1 cup quick-cooking oats, then measure in 1 cup packed brown sugar with the dry ingredients.
The brown sugar is a little clumpy. Should I break it up before mixing?
Break up the larger clumps with your fingers or a spoon so it blends evenly with the flour, wheat germ, and oats.
Dry ingredients are combined in the big bowl. What should I use for the wet mixture?
In a separate bowl, combine the applesauce, oil, and eggs. Whisk or stir them until the eggs are fully blended into the mixture.
The applesauce mixture looks smooth. Do I pour it all into the dry bowl at once?
Yes, add the applesauce, oil, and egg mixture to the flour mixture, then stir until everything is mixed well.
It's coming together and looks thick. Should I keep stirring until it's completely uniform?
Stir just until the dry pockets are gone and the dough looks evenly moistened; there's no need to overwork it.
I still need to add the mix-ins. What goes in at the end?
Stir in the chocolate chip and walnuts, folding them through the dough so they're evenly distributed.
Can you help me make Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon? I've got the figs out but haven't started cutting yet.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 figs, halved, so start by slicing each fig lengthwise and setting the halves cut-side up.
The figs are halved and on a small tray. How much cheese should I use?
Use 6 ounces goat cheese total. Spoon or press a little into the center of each fig half so the cheese sits snugly without overflowing too much.
Cheese is in. I also have pecans and bacon nearby; what should I prep with those?
Measure 1/2 cup toasted, chopped pecans, and make sure your 3 slices bacon are cut in half. Keep toothpicks close for securing the wrapped figs.
The bacon is halved and the pecans are chopped. Should I turn on the oven now?
Yes, preheat the broiler now so it's hot by the time the figs are assembled.
Broiler is heating. Do the pecans go on before or after the bacon?
Press the toasted, chopped pecans directly into the goat cheese before wrapping. That helps them stick instead of falling off.
The pecans are pressed into the cheese. The figs feel a little delicate—how tightly should I wrap them?
Wrap each stuffed fig half with half a slice of bacon, just snug enough to hold everything together without crushing the fig.
They're wrapped, but a few pieces of bacon want to spring loose. What's the best way to secure them?
Push a toothpick through each wrapped fig half to hold the bacon in place. Once they're all secured, they're assembled and ready for the broiler.

source_seed.recipe_title: Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon

messages.content: Can you guide me through making Cinnamon Crackle Cookies? I've got a large mixing bowl and baking sheets ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're easy to blend.
Both are softened and in reach. Which sugars do I need before I start mixing?
Measure 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep a little extra sugar nearby for rolling the dough balls later.
The sugars are measured. Should the butter and shortening go in the bowl together?
Yes. Add the butter, shortening, sugar, and packed brown sugar to the mixing bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and well combined.
It's lighter and creamy now. I see the recipe mentions egg and extracts—do those go in next?
They do. Add the egg and extracts to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly blended.
That's mixed in. I don't want floury pockets—how should I handle the dry ingredients?
Combine the next eight ingredients in a separate bowl, then add them gradually to the creamed mixture. Mix as you go so the dough comes together evenly.
The dough looks consistent. Should I chill it or start shaping right away?
Follow the recipe from here and shape the dough into 1-in balls. Roll each ball in sugar before placing it on the baking sheets.
I'm using ungreased baking sheets. How should I arrange the sugared balls?
Place the sugar-rolled 1-in balls apart on the ungreased baking sheets so they have room as they bake.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Go for lots of small browned spots scattered over the vegetables and chicken pieces, not a single deeply dark surface.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: I'm turning Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme into a sheet-pan vegetable dinner tonight; for the browning, what should I be looking for on the pan?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Aim for smaller browned freckles across many pieces rather than one dark side.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme as a sheet-pan vegetable dish. How should I manage the browning?

messages.content: I'm turning Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme into a sheet-pan vegetable dinner tonight; for the browning, what should I be looking for on the pan?
Go for lots of small browned spots scattered over the vegetables and chicken pieces, not a single deeply dark surface.
Great, I've got the sheet pan out and a large bowl ready. What should I pull from the fridge first?
Start with the creamy marinade base: measure 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream into the bowl, then add 1/4 cup lemon juice.
The yogurt and lemon juice are in. I'm checking the small bottles now—what gets added?
Add 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed.
All right, those are measured. Do I whisk this before the chicken goes in?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine those with the remaining marinade ingredients until the mixture is even and the celery seed is distributed.
The marinade looks smooth. I have the chicken beside the bowl—how should I coat it without making a mess?
Place the chicken into the mixture and turn each piece so the marinade covers all sides. Use tongs if you want to keep your hands cleaner.
It's coated. Since I'm cooking tomorrow, how should I store it tonight?
Cover the bowl well and marinate the chicken overnight in the refrigerator.
Tomorrow, when I take it out, do I scrape off the marinade or keep it thick?
Lift the chicken from the marinade and let the excess drip off, then coat each piece with crumbs so the surface is ready to brown.
When it goes onto the vegetable pan, any last texture cue so I don't overdo the color?
Spread the pieces so they have room, then watch for light, speckled browning across the pan while the crumb coating sets rather than pushing for one dark crust.
Can you help me make Festive Shortbread Logs? I've got a bowl and mixer ready, but I want to keep the ingredients straight.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar to start. Those two get creamed together in the mixing bowl.
The butter is soft and the sugar is measured. Are there any other ingredients before I turn on the mixer?
Yes—have 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and 2 cups all-purpose flour nearby. That's the full ingredient list for these shortbread logs.
Okay, I'm starting with the butter and sugar. How long should I mix them?
Cream the softened butter with the confectioners' sugar until the mixture looks smooth and lighter, scraping the bowl if butter sticks to the sides.
It's looking creamy now, and the sides are scraped down. Does the vanilla go in by itself?
Yes, add the vanilla extract to the creamed mixture and mix just until it's evenly worked in.
Vanilla is mixed in. I'm worried about dumping in all the flour at once because the bowl is a little shallow.
Add the flour gradually instead. Mix after each addition so it incorporates cleanly, then continue until the dough is well combined.
The dough is together, but it's soft and a little tacky. Should I flour the counter or my hands?
Lightly flour your hands. Take tablespoonfuls of the dough and shape each portion into a cookie, using the flour just to keep it from sticking.
I'm portioning tablespoonfuls now. Should they be shaped like little logs rather than round cookies?
Yes, for Festive Shortbread Logs, gently roll each tablespoonful into a small log shape. Keep them even so they look consistent and handle them lightly so the dough stays tender.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Dice the cheese into small pieces, then fold it in after you take the hot mixture off the heat so it softens gently.
