original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut the cheese into small cubes and fold them in off heat.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chocolate Cream Dessert as a hot egg or pasta dish with cheese added near serving. How should I handle the cheese?

messages.content: I'm making Chocolate Cream Dessert today, but I'm treating this batch like a hot egg-or-pasta dish where cheese gets added right near serving. For this one, how should I handle the cheese?
Dice the cheese into small pieces, then fold it in after you take the hot mixture off the heat so it softens gently.
Perfect, that's only for this batch. Before I get to that part, what should I pull from the fridge and pantry?
For the crust, start with 1/4 cup cold margarine and 1 cup all-purpose flour. Keep the margarine cold until you're ready to work it into the flour.
I've got those measured. Do I need the cream cheese and sweetener out now too?
Yes. Set out 1 (8 ounce) package light cream cheese so it can be softened, along with 2 tablespoons heat-stable granular sugar substitute.
The margarine is still cold, and I have a bowl ready. What texture am I looking for when I mix it with the flour?
Cut the cold margarine into the flour in the bowl until the mixture looks crumbly, with small bits of margarine distributed through the flour.
It looks like coarse crumbs. What dish should I use, and do I need to grease it?
Use an 11-in baking dish coated with nonstick cooking spray, then press the crumbly mixture evenly into the bottom.
The crust is pressed in. Should it be packed down firmly or just lightly leveled?
Press it firmly enough to hold together and make an even layer, but don't mash it so hard that it becomes dense.
It's ready for the oven. What temperature and timing should I use?
Bake it at 350 degrees F for 15-18 minutes, watching for the crust to become lightly browned.
It's lightly browned at the edges. Do I move on right away or let it sit?
Let it cool completely before adding anything on top or continuing with the dessert.
Can you guide me through Apple Cranberry Crisp 2? I've got an 8 inch square baking dish ready, but I want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples peeled, cored, and thinly sliced, plus 3/4 cup cranberries. Those will be the fruit base for the crisp.
The apples are sliced and the cranberries are measured. What should I pull out for the seasoning?
Measure 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. The recipe also has you mix nutmeg in with the fruit, so keep that nearby if you're using it.
Before I mix the fruit, should the oven and pan be ready?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, and butter the 8 inch square baking dish so the crisp is easy to serve later.
The oven is heating and the dish is buttered. Do I combine the apples and cranberries directly in the baking dish?
Use a large bowl first. Add the sliced apples, cranberries, white sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg, then toss until the fruit is evenly coated.
I'm tossing it now. Should the sugar and cinnamon look evenly distributed before I transfer it?
Yes, aim for the apple slices and cranberries to look lightly and evenly coated, without dry piles of cinnamon or sugar sitting at the bottom of the bowl.
That looks even. How should I arrange it in the pan?
Spoon the fruit mixture into the buttered 8 inch square baking dish and spread it into an even layer so it bakes consistently.
The fruit is in the dish. What do I do with the bowl now?
Use that same bowl to combine the topping ingredients: oats, flour, and brown sugar. Mix them together there so you don't need an extra bowl.
Can you help me get Dad's BBQ Roast started? I have a beef rump roast out, but I want to be sure I'm using the right amounts for the coating.
Absolutely. For the coating, measure 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard and use 2 envelopes of dry onion soup mix, each 1 ounce.
Got it. The roast is about 5 pounds—does that match the recipe?
Yes, that's exactly right: 1 beef rump roast, 5 pounds. You'll also want a small bowl for mixing and aluminum foil for wrapping or lining the roast area.
I've got the bowl and foil ready. Should the mustard and soup mix just be stirred together as-is?
Yes. Add the yellow mustard to the small bowl, sprinkle in both envelopes of dry onion soup mix, and stir until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The mixture is thick and speckled from the soup mix. How should I set up the foil?
Lay out 2 long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise, making a plus shape. That gives you enough overlap to hold the roast in the center.
The foil is crossed on the counter. Do I need to trim or season the roast before it goes on?
The recipe just has you pat the roast dry. Use paper towels to remove surface moisture, then place the roast right in the center of the crossed foil.
It's patted dry and sitting on the foil. Should the mustard mixture go on every side?
Coat it generously with the mustard and onion soup mixture. Spread it over the top and sides so the roast is well covered.
Some of the coating is sliding down onto the foil. Is that okay?
That's fine. Just scoop or smear any fallen mixture back onto the beef as much as you can, keeping the 5 pound roast generously coated before you continue with the rest of your cooking plan.

messages.content: Tonight I'm turning Baked Halibut Steaks into a quick broth-or-noodle bowl, so for this one I want the onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot handled differently. What should I do with the allium?
For this bowl, prep the allium two ways—one finer cut and one larger, fresher cut—and stir both in right at the end.
Perfect, that's the one-night version I'm after. I've got the fish out; what should I gather first?
Set out 1 teaspoon olive oil and 1 cup diced zucchini to build the vegetable base.
Zucchini is diced. I'm using onion and garlic for the allium—how much do I need nearby?
Have 1/2 cup minced onion and 1 clove garlic, peeled and minced. Since you're doing the bowl version, divide those cuts so some can stay more delicate for the end.
Got it. I'm clearing space for the baking dish too—what oven setup do I need?
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C, and lightly grease a shallow baking dish.
The oven is heating and the dish is greased. Should I start the saucepan now?

Yes. Warm the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat, then add the zucchini. If you want a little cooked allium flavor, add only the portion you don't mind softening; save the brighter cuts for the very end.
The zucchini is in the pan. How long am I cooking it, and what texture am I watching for?
Cook and stir for about 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender rather than browned.
Tender now. I've got tomatoes, basil, salt, and pepper waiting by the stove.
Take the saucepan off the heat, then mix in the tomatoes, basil, salt, and pepper. Fold in the reserved allium cuts last so they keep that fresh broth-bowl edge.
The mixture smells good. How should the halibut go into the dish before I add anything around it?
Arrange the halibut steaks in a single layer in the prepared baking dish so they sit evenly and have room for the vegetable mixture around them.
Can you guide me through making Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts? I'm setting up the saucepan and baking sheets now.
Absolutely. For the syrup, set out 1 cup white sugar, 1 cup water, 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons orange flower water.
I've got the sugar, measured water, lemon juice, and orange flower water ready. Do I start with the almonds or the syrup?
Start with the almonds. Bring 6 cups of water to a boil in a pot large enough to hold them comfortably.
The pot is coming up to a boil. Should the almonds go in while it's still on the burner?
Once the water reaches a boil, remove the pot from the heat, then add the almonds to the hot water.
They're in the hot water off the heat. How long should they sit?
Let the almonds soak for about 5 minutes. After that, drain them and peel off the skins while they're still warm enough to slip easily.
Some of the skins are sliding off, but a few are stubborn. Is that okay?
Yes, just keep peeling until they're clean. If a skin resists, pinch the almond gently from one end and it should pop free.
The peeled almonds are drained. Should I dry them with a towel before baking?
A quick pat dry is helpful, then spread the almonds in a single layer on baking sheets so moisture can evaporate evenly.
They're spread out. What oven setting and texture am I aiming for?
Bake them at 200 degrees F, which is 95 degrees C, until they're completely dry and lightly toasted. Let them cool before you continue using them for the tarts.
Can you guide me through making Corn Bread Sloppy Joes? I'm setting up the counter now.
Absolutely. Put out 1 (8.5 ounce) package corn bread/muffin mix, 1 egg, and 1/3 cup milk for the corn bread portion.
I've got the mix, egg, and milk measured. Do I need to start the oven or the skillet first?
Start with the corn bread. Prepare the corn bread or muffin mix according to the package directions, using the egg and milk, then bake it as the package directs.
The corn bread is in the oven. What should I prep while it bakes?
Get a large skillet ready for the filling and have 2 pounds ground beef available. You'll also need onion for the skillet step.
Skillet is heating on medium, and the beef and onion are ready. Should they go in together?
Yes. Cook the ground beef and onion together in the large skillet over medium heat until the meat is no longer pink.
The beef has browned and there's liquid in the pan. Do I leave that in for the sauce?
Drain the beef mixture before adding the sauce ingredients so the sloppy joe filling doesn't turn greasy or watery.
Drained. I have spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix nearby. Do they all go in now?
They do. Stir the spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix into the cooked beef and onion until everything is evenly combined.
It's mixed and looks saucy. How do I know when the filling is ready?
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring as needed. Once it reaches that bubbling boil, you're at the finishing point for the sloppy joe topping.
I'm making Corn Bread Sloppy Joes and have a baking dish and skillet ready. Can you guide me through it?

Absolutely. Set out the corn bread part first: 1 (8.5 ounce) package corn bread/muffin mix, 1 egg, and 1/3 cup milk. You'll prepare and bake the corn bread according to the package directions using the egg and milk.
The corn bread mix, egg, and milk are out. Should I get the meat started while that bakes?
Yes. While the corn bread bakes, use a large skillet for the filling. Add 2 pounds ground beef and onion, and cook over medium heat until the beef is no longer pink.
Do I need to break the beef up pretty small in the pan?
Break it up as it cooks so the filling has an even sloppy joe texture. Keep it over medium heat until there's no pink left, then drain off the excess fat.
The beef is browned and drained. The corn bread is still in the oven.
Good timing. With the beef drained, stir in the spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix right in the skillet.
Should the sauce just coat the meat, or am I heating it longer?
Heat it until the mixture comes to a boil. Stir occasionally so the sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix distribute evenly through the beef.
The filling is bubbling now, and the corn bread looks baked through.
Great. Once the filling has reached a boil and the corn bread is baked according to the package directions, you can use the corn bread as the base for serving the sloppy joe mixture.
Should I let the corn bread sit before spooning the beef mixture over it?
Let it rest just briefly so it's easier to portion, then spoon the hot sloppy joe mixture over the corn bread and serve while the filling is still warm.
Can you guide me through making Fancy Brussels Sprouts? I've got a saucepan ready.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup water, 1/4 cup minced fresh parsley, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need the brussels sprouts for the simmering step, plus water chestnuts and butter to heat through at the end.
The water, parsley, sugar, and salt are measured. Should I combine them before heating?
Yes. Put the water, parsley, sugar, and salt into the saucepan, then place it over medium heat.
It's on the stove now. Am I waiting for a full boil or just bubbles around the edges?
Bring that mixture to a boil over medium heat, so look for steady bubbling across the liquid rather than just a few bubbles at the edge.
It's boiling. Do the brussels sprouts go in whole at this point?
Add the brussels sprouts now. Once they're in, make sure they're sitting in the seasoned liquid so they can cook evenly.
They're in the pan. Should I leave it uncovered while they cook?
Cover the saucepan and let the brussels sprouts simmer for 6-8 minutes, or until they're tender.
I'm at about 6 minutes. How tender should they feel before I drain them?
They should be tender when pierced, but not falling apart. If they still feel firm in the center, give them another minute or two, staying within that 6-8 minute range, then drain them.
They're tender and drained. What's the last thing to do before serving?
Add the water chestnuts and butter to the drained brussels sprouts, then heat everything through so the butter coats the vegetables and the water chestnuts warm up.
Can you guide me through making Carrot Pineapple Cake I? I'm getting my baking area set up.
Absolutely. Start by pulling out the dry ingredients listed for the cake: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt.
I have the flour and baking soda measured. Should the baking powder and salt go in the same bowl?
Yes, they can go into the same mixing bowl with the flour and baking soda. Add the 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1 teaspoon salt there too.
Great. I've got a 9x13 inch pan nearby. Should I prep the oven before mixing?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it is ready when the batter is mixed.
The oven is heating. What should I do with the pan so the cake releases cleanly?
Grease and flour the 9x13 inch pan, making sure the corners and sides are coated so the cake does not stick.
Pan is greased and floured. I'm back at the bowl with the dry ingredients.
Mix the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon together until the dry ingredients look evenly combined.
I don't see any streaks of flour or leavening clumps now. What's next in the bowl?
Make a well in the center of the dry mixture. Into that well, add the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
So the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla all go into the center before I start combining everything?
That's right. Keep them in the well at first, then you can begin bringing the dry mixture in from the sides to form the cake batter.
Can you help me make Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon? I'm putting the ingredients out now.
Absolutely. Set out 6 figs and halve them so you have the bases ready, then keep 6 ounces of goat cheese nearby for stuffing.
The figs are halved, and the goat cheese is on the board. What else should I prep before turning on the heat?
You'll also need 1/2 cup toasted, chopped pecans and 3 slices of bacon cut in half. Have toothpicks ready too, since they'll hold the wrapped figs together.
I've got the pecans chopped and the bacon sliced into halves. Should I start the oven setup now?
Yes, preheat the broiler so it's hot by the time the figs are assembled.
Broiler is heating. For the figs, should the cheese go right into the cut side?
Yes. Spoon or press the goat cheese into each fig half, using the cut side as the little pocket.
Some of the goat cheese is soft and spreading a bit. Is that okay before I add the nuts?
That's fine. Once the cheese is in place, press the toasted, chopped pecans into the goat cheese so they stick.
The pecans are pressed in. I'm worried the bacon might slide off the figs.
Wrap each stuffed fig half with half a slice of bacon, then secure it with a toothpick to keep everything tucked together.
All of them are wrapped and pinned. Anything I should check before they go under the broiler?
Make sure each fig half has goat cheese, pecans pressed into the cheese, and a half slice of bacon held with a toothpick. Once the broiler is preheated, they're assembled according to the recipe.

source_seed.recipe_title: Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon

messages.content: I'm making Baked Fish and Rice 2 and have an 11-in. baking dish out. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. Grease that 11-in. baking dish, and set your oven to 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you assemble the rice base.
The dish is greased. Which ingredients go in before it bakes?
Combine 1 1/2 cups boiling chicken broth with 1/2 cup uncooked long grain rice right in the baking dish. Stir in 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder.
The broth is hot and everything is mixed in the dish. Should it be covered tightly?
Yes, cover the dish before it goes in the oven. Bake it at 375 degrees F, 190 degrees C, for 10 minutes so the rice can start absorbing the broth.
It has baked for 10 minutes. The rice has started soaking things up but there's still moisture.
That's expected at this point. Take the dish out carefully, uncover it, and add the broccoli, Parmesan cheese, and half of the onions over the rice mixture.
I'm adding those now. Should I mix the broccoli, Parmesan, and onions into the rice or leave them on top?
Gently spread them into the rice mixture so they're evenly distributed, but don't worry about making it perfectly uniform.
The vegetables and cheese are in. I have the fish fillets ready on a plate.
Lay the fish fillets over the rice mixture in an even layer, then sprinkle the tops with paprika.
The fish is on top with paprika. Anything I should check before putting it back in?
Make sure the fillets are sitting flat over the rice and the toppings are tucked in the dish rather than piled on the edges. Then it's ready to continue baking according to the recipe.
Can you guide me through making Cinnamon Bread I? I've cleared some counter space and want to set up before I start mixing.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready.
I have the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda out. Should I get the pan and oven ready before measuring everything?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's hot by the time the batter is ready.
The oven is heating. What pan size am I using for this loaf?
Use one 9x5 inch loaf pan, and grease it well so the cinnamon bread releases cleanly after baking.
The 9x5 pan is greased. I've got a big bowl out—what goes in there?
Measure the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla into the large mixing bowl.
I'm adding everything to the bowl now. Does the cinnamon go in with the dry ingredients or just all together?
For this recipe, it all goes into the same large mixing bowl together, including the 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon.
Everything is in the bowl, and I don't see dry pockets yet. How long should I mix it?
Beat the mixture for 3 minutes. Keep the bowl steady and scrape the sides if needed so the batter comes together evenly.
After 3 minutes, should it be perfectly smooth, or is a little texture okay?
A little texture is fine for a quick bread batter. Once it has been beaten for the full 3 minutes and looks evenly combined, you're ready to pour it into the greased loaf pan.
Can you guide me through making Basic Chicken Stock? I've got a large pot ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound chicken parts, 1 large onion, 3 stalks celery with some leaves, and 1 large carrot.
The chicken is thawed, and the vegetables are on the cutting board. Should I peel the onion or just cut it?
Peel off the papery outer skin, then quarter the onion so the pieces can flavor the stock easily.
Onion is quartered. The celery has leaves still attached; do I use those too?
Yes, include some of the celery leaves. Scrub the celery and carrot, then chop both into 1 inch chunks.
The carrot and celery are chopped. Do the chicken pieces need browning first?
For this basic stock, don't brown them. Put the chicken pieces straight into the large soup pot or Dutch oven.
Chicken is in the pot. Should the vegetables go in together or in layers?
They can all go in together. Add the quartered onion, chopped celery, and chopped carrot to the pot with the chicken.
Vegetables are in. I see salt and cloves mentioned—do those go in now?
Yes, add the salt and cloves now, right on top of the chicken and vegetables.
Everything is in the Dutch oven. How much water should I add before I put it on the stove?
Pour in 6 cups water. The pot is set up for the stock from there.
I'm making Carrots and Onions Au Gratin and have a baking dish ready. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Slice 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots and 2 medium onions, and keep them close to the stove.
The carrots and onions are sliced. Do I need to pull anything from the fridge before I turn on the oven?
Yes—set out 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter so everything is ready when you assemble the dish.
Cheddar and butter are out. What temperature should the oven be?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. Should I start the vegetables on the stove now?
Yes. Put the sliced carrots and onions in a pot, add enough lightly salted water to cover them, and bring it to a boil.
They're in salted water and it's starting to boil. How long should I cook them?
Cook them for 5 minutes, just until they're tender but still firm.
After 5 minutes they're not mushy, just a little firm in the center. What should I do with the water?
Drain the carrots and onions well so the baking dish doesn't end up watery.
They're drained. How do I start layering them in the baking dish?
Spread 1/2 of the drained carrots and onions evenly in the baking dish, then keep the remaining vegetables, Cheddar, and butter nearby for the next assembly step.
I want to make Cookie Jar Gingersnaps, and I've got a large mixing bowl out. Can you help me set up without getting ahead of myself?
Absolutely. Start by putting the measured wet-base ingredients within reach: 3/4 cup shortening, 1 cup sugar, 1 egg, and 1/4 cup molasses.
Shortening and sugar are measured. Should I add the egg and molasses right away too?
Hold them for a moment. Cream the shortening and sugar together in the large bowl until they look well blended and a little lighter in texture.
The mixture is smooth and pale. I'm scraping down the sides of the bowl now.
Good. Beat in the egg next, then add the molasses and mix until the dough base is evenly combined.
It's sticky and dark from the molasses. What dry ingredients need to go in?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt so the spices and leavening are evenly distributed.
Dry bowl is mixed. Do I dump it all into the creamed mixture?
Add it gradually to the creamed mixture, mixing between additions. That helps keep the dough even and makes it easier to manage.
The dough has come together and is pretty soft. Should I be shaping it now?
Yes. Scoop teaspoonfuls of dough and roll each portion into a ball, keeping the sizes fairly consistent.
I'm rolling them now. Any quick cleanup or handling tip while I finish the tray?
If the dough sticks to your hands, pause to scrape your fingers or lightly clean them before continuing. Keep rolling teaspoonfuls into balls until the dough is portioned.
I want to make Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip. I've got a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish out—can you talk me through it?
Absolutely. Heat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the dip is mixed.
Oven is heating. What should I measure into the dish first?
Add 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream directly to the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish.
Those are in. I have the soup mix packet and the artichokes next to me.
Stir in 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, then add 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts that have been drained and chopped.
The artichokes are chopped and mixed in. The instructions mention cheese and crab meat too—do they go in now?
Yes, combine the cheese and crab meat into the same mixture now, along with the mayonnaise, sour cream, soup mix, and artichoke hearts. Mix until everything is evenly distributed.
It's all combined in the casserole dish. Should I cover it before it goes in?
Bake it uncovered. Put the casserole dish in the 350 degree F oven and bake for 30 minutes.
While it bakes, what should I be looking for so I know it's ready?
After the 30 minutes, it should be hot throughout and look like a creamy baked dip. Since this recipe's timing is 30 minutes uncovered, use that as your main guide.
Timer is about to go off. How do I serve it?
Take it out carefully and serve the Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip immediately while it's hot.
I want to make Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches. Can you talk me through the setup before I turn anything on?

Absolutely. Get 1 small onion finely chopped, 1 medium tomato diced, 1 stalk celery chopped, and 1 green bell pepper finely chopped. You'll also need cheese, chili powder, salt, and slices of bread for broiling.
The vegetables are prepped, but my baking sheet is still in the cupboard. Do I need that right away?
Yes, pull out a baking sheet or a broiling pan now so it's ready. Once your oven's broiler is preheated, the sandwiches can go together quickly.
Broiler is on. Should I mix the topping while it heats?
That's the right time. In a medium bowl, stir together the onion, tomato, celery, green bell pepper, cheese, chili powder, and salt until the vegetables and cheese are evenly distributed.
The mixture looks colorful and a little chunky. Is that okay, or should it be smoother?
Chunky is fine for these sandwiches. Just make sure the pieces are well mixed so each slice gets some onion, tomato, celery, bell pepper, cheese, seasoning, and salt.
I'm laying out the bread now. Should the slices touch on the pan?
Arrange the slices of bread on the baking sheet or broiling pan with a little space between them if you can. That helps the broiler reach the edges more evenly.
How much of the vegetable-cheese mixture goes on each slice?
Top each slice with 1/4 of the mixture, spreading it all the way out to the edges so the bread is covered evenly.
The topping is spread to the edges. Anything to check before I slide the pan under the broiler?

Check that the broiler is fully preheated, the bread is in a single layer, and the topping is evenly divided. Then place the pan under the broiler and keep an eye on it, since broilers can brown sandwiches quickly.
I want to make BBQ Chuck Roast today. Can you talk me through the setup before I start mixing anything?

Absolutely. Have a 1 (5 pound) chuck roast ready, plus 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer. You'll also need a large bowl for the marinade, something to cover it for the refrigerator, an outdoor grill set up for indirect heat later, and a saucepan for the marinade after the roast comes out.
The roast is still wrapped, and I've got the sauces and beer out. Should the marinade go together before I unwrap the meat?
Yes, mix the marinade first so the roast can go straight in. In the large bowl, combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt.
I've got that stirred together. It smells pretty strong from the teriyaki and beer—do I just set the roast in it now?
Set the chuck roast into the marinade and turn it so the surface gets coated. Cover the bowl well, then put it in the refrigerator for six hours.
Six hours is fine. When you say turn it often, how often should I be opening the bowl?
A few turns during the six-hour chill is enough—just rotate the roast so different sides spend time in the marinade. Keep it covered and refrigerated between turns.
The marinating time is almost done, and I'm getting the grill ready. What setup am I aiming for?
Preheat the outdoor grill for indirect heat. That means the roast should cook away from the direct flame or hottest coals, so arrange the heat to one side or around the edges depending on your grill.
The grill is heating indirectly. What do I do with the bowl of marinade when I take the roast out?
Remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan. Keep the roast separate from the liquid once it comes out of the bowl.
Should I discard anything at this point, or is the saucepan step part of the cooking plan?

Use the saucepan step as part of the plan: the recipe has you pour the marinade into a saucepan after removing the roast. From here, you're set up with the roast ready for the indirect grill and the marinade collected separately.
I want to make Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts today. Can you talk me through the setup before I start heating anything?

Absolutely. For the syrup flavoring, set out 1 cup white sugar, 1 cup water, 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons orange flower water. You'll also need a pot for blanching the almonds, a strainer, baking sheets, and your oven set low later.
The sugar, water, lemon juice, and orange flower water are measured. Should I start with the syrup or the almonds?
Start with the almonds. Bring 6 cups of water to a boil in a pot so you can loosen their skins.
The water is boiling. Do I keep it on the burner when the almonds go in?
No—take the pot off the heat, then add the almonds to the hot water. That gentle soak is enough to loosen the skins without cooking them too aggressively.
They're in the hot water now. How long should I leave them there?
Let them soak for about 5 minutes. After that, drain them, then peel off the skins while they're still easy to handle.
I've drained them, and the skins are slipping off pretty well. Should the peeled almonds be wet when they go on the trays?
They can be a little damp from peeling, but spread them out on baking sheets in a single layer so moisture can evaporate evenly.
What oven temperature should I use for drying them?
Bake them at 200 degrees F, which is 95 degrees C, until they're completely dry and toasted. Keep the heat low so they dry through without scorching.
How will I know they're ready to come out?
They should feel dry rather than tacky, look lightly toasted, and smell nutty. Once they reach that point, let them cool on the baking sheets before moving on with the tart preparation.
Can you stay with me while I make Curried Winter Squash? I already have cooked squash ready to mash.
Absolutely. Measure out 3 cups of cooked, mashed winter squash and put it in a medium microwave-safe bowl if you have one.
The squash is mashed and in the bowl. How much curry powder goes in?
Add 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder to the squash, then give it a quick stir so the spice starts spreading through the mash.
It smells good already. I'm checking the fridge—should I use butter or margarine here?
Either works for this recipe: use 2 tablespoons butter or 2 tablespoons trans fat-free margarine. Add it to the bowl with the squash and curry.
Butter is in. I also see maple syrup on the counter—does that go in now?
Yes, add 2 tablespoons maple syrup. Once it's in, stir everything together in the medium bowl until the curry, fat, and syrup are evenly mixed into the squash.
The mixture is combined. Should the butter be fully melted before I microwave it?
It doesn't have to be melted beforehand. Microwave the bowl on high until the squash is heated through, about 5 minutes; the butter will melt as it warms.
I'm halfway through heating and there are a few cooler spots. Should I stir it?
Yes, pause and stir if your microwave heats unevenly, then continue until the whole bowl is hot and smooth.
It's heated through now. The recipe mentions coconut—how should I handle that?
Sprinkle coconut on top if desired, then serve the curried winter squash warm.
I want to make Aunt Mamies, and I'm starting by clearing space for the dough. Can you talk me through what to set out?
Set out 1 (8 ounce) package of softened cream cheese and 1/2 cup softened butter. You'll also need 2 cups all-purpose flour and 1 cup white sugar.
The cream cheese and butter are soft, but not melted. Should I use a bowl or a saucepan yet?
Start with a mixing bowl for the softened cream cheese and butter. Beat them together until they look smooth and well blended before you bring in the flour.
I'm using a hand mixer. The mixture is creamy with a few tiny streaks left.
Give it another short mix until those streaks mostly disappear. It doesn't need to be whipped, just evenly combined.
That looks blended now. Do I add all the flour at once?
Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour and mix well. If it starts to look heavy, slow the mixer down or finish by hand so the dough comes together without flour flying out.
The dough is thick and a little soft. Is that right before chilling?
Yes, that fits. Shape it into a ball, cover it, and chill it for 2 hours so it firms up.
I've wrapped the dough ball and put it in the refrigerator. What should I prep while it chills?
Keep the sugar ready for the stovetop part. When you're ready, you'll use a saucepan over medium heat to cook the sugar with milk, stirring occasionally.
The 2 hours are nearly up. How do I know the saucepan mixture is done?

Cook the 1 cup white sugar with the milk over medium heat, stirring now and then, until the milk boils and the sugar is dissolved. Once it reaches that point, take it off the heat and continue with the chilled dough as your recipe directs.
Can you walk me through Curried Winter Squash? I've already got a microwave-safe bowl nearby.
Absolutely. For the base, you'll need 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash and 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder.
The squash is mashed, and I measured the curry powder. What else should I pull out?
Add 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, plus 2 tablespoons maple syrup. Those will help make the squash rich and a little sweet.
I have butter and maple syrup ready. Should the bowl be medium-sized?
Yes, use a medium bowl. Put the mashed squash, curry powder, butter or margarine, and maple syrup into it.
The butter is still cold. Is that okay before microwaving?
That's fine. Stir everything together as well as you can; the butter will soften and melt as it heats.
It's mixed, though a little streaky from the curry. How long should I microwave it?
Microwave it on high until it's heated through, about 5 minutes. You can pause and stir partway through if you want the curry and butter evenly blended.
After 5 minutes it's hot and smoother. The recipe mentions coconut—when does that go on?
Sprinkle coconut over the top now, if you'd like to use it. It's optional, so you can leave it plain too.
I'll add a small sprinkle for texture. How should I serve it?
Give it one final stir or smooth the top, then serve the Curried Winter Squash warm.
I'm making Dads Best Burgers and have a bowl and grill ready. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 softened 3 ounce package of cream cheese and 1 egg, since those go into the bowl for the base mixture.
The cream cheese is soft and the egg is out. Which add-ins should I chop or measure before mixing?
Finely chop 1 medium onion and measure 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs. Keep them close to the bowl so everything can be combined evenly.
Onion is chopped and the bread crumbs are measured. Do I just stir those with the cream cheese and egg?
Yes. In the bowl, combine the first seven ingredients until the cream cheese, egg, onion, and bread crumbs are worked together into a fairly even mixture.
It's coming together, but the cream cheese is making a few soft pockets. Is that okay?
A few small soft pockets are fine, but give it another stir so the mixture is mostly uniform before adding the meats.
Good, the base looks more even now. How do I add the beef and sausage without overworking it?
Crumble the beef and sausage over the mixture, then mix well but gently—use your hands or a fork just until the meat is distributed throughout.
The meat mixture is combined. How many patties should I make, and should they be thick?
Shape the mixture into eight patties. Try to keep them similar in thickness so they grill at the same pace.
The patties are shaped and the grill is heating. What timing should I use?
Grill them uncovered over medium-hot heat for 4-6 minutes on each side, or until the burgers are no longer pink in the center.
Can you help me make Baked Aloha Chicken? I've got chicken legs out and want to set up the sauce correctly.
Absolutely. Start by heating the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), so it's ready when the chicken is assembled.
Oven is heating. For the sauce, I see lemon juice and corn syrup on the counter—how much of each goes in?
Measure 1/4 cup lemon juice and 1/4 cup light corn syrup into a mixing bowl.
Both are in the bowl. What should I add before I stir?
Add 2 tablespoons soy sauce and 1 teaspoon salt. The recipe also has you stir in ginger and corn oil with those sauce ingredients until the mixture looks smooth.
I'm whisking it now. Should it be completely blended before the pineapple goes in?
Yes, get the lemon juice, corn syrup, soy sauce, salt, ginger, and corn oil smooth first so the pineapple mixes evenly afterward.
The sauce looks smooth. I have crushed pineapple—do I drain it or use the juice?
Use the crushed pineapple with its liquid. Stir it right into the sauce so the whole mixture stays loose and fruity.
Pineapple is mixed in. What dish should I use for the chicken legs?
Use an ovenproof glass baking dish. Arrange the chicken legs in it with enough room for the sauce to cover them well.
The chicken legs are in the glass dish. Do I pour all of the sauce over them now?
Yes, pour the sauce over the top of the chicken legs, making sure the pineapple mixture is spread across the pieces before the dish goes into the 350 degree F oven.
Can you help me make Chicken with Vegetables in the slow cooker today? I've got the crock ready.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms, 4 chicken drumsticks with the skin removed, 4 chicken thighs with the skin removed, and 4 sliced celery ribs.
The mushrooms are sliced, and the chicken pieces are already skinned. Should the celery go in right away?
Put the mushrooms and all the chicken into the slow cooker first so they form the base.
Okay, the chicken is in with the mushrooms. The celery is sliced on the board.
Add the sliced celery next, along with the zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper.
I'm pouring everything in now. Do I need to stir it around the chicken?
A gentle stir is fine to distribute the vegetables and seasonings, but keep the chicken settled in the slow cooker rather than breaking it up.
It's mixed and the lid is on. What setting and timing should I use?
Cook it covered on low for 5 hours, or until the meat juices run clear.
If I check near the end, what should I look for besides the juices running clear?
The chicken should be tender, and the vegetables should be cooked through without needing to be mashed or broken apart.
Once it's done, how do I hold it while I get the table ready?
Remove the chicken and vegetables from the slow cooker and keep them warm until you're ready to serve.
I want to make Carrots and Onions Au Gratin. Can you help me get set up before I start slicing?
Absolutely. For this recipe, have 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots sliced and 2 medium onions sliced. You'll also need 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter nearby.
The carrots are baby carrots, but some are thick. Should I cut them smaller?
Yes, slice any thicker baby carrots so the pieces are fairly even. That will help them cook in the same 5-minute window and stay tender but firm.
I've got the onions sliced too. What dish and oven setting should I use?
Use a baking dish that can hold the vegetables in layers, and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
Oven is heating. Do the carrots and onions go straight into the baking dish?
Not yet. Put the sliced carrots and onions into a pot, add enough lightly salted water to cover them, and bring the pot to a boil.
How salty should the water be, and do I cover the pot?
Keep the water lightly salted, just enough to season the vegetables. You can leave the pot uncovered while bringing it to a boil so you can watch it easily.
It's boiling now. What texture am I looking for before draining?
Cook them for 5 minutes, or until the carrots and onions are tender but still firm. They should give slightly when pierced, not turn soft or mushy.
They're tender but still holding shape. How do I move them into the baking dish?
Drain the carrots and onions well, then spread 1/2 of the drained mixture evenly in the baking dish. Keep the Cheddar cheese and butter ready for the gratin assembly.
I want to make Eggnog II. Can you help me get set up before I put anything on the stove?
Absolutely. Set out a large saucepan and gather 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I've got the saucepan, eggs, milk, sugar, and vanilla. Do I add the vanilla right away too?
For the cooking part, combine the beaten eggs, the 2 1/4 cups milk, and the 1/3 cup white sugar in the large saucepan. Keep the vanilla ready, but don't add it in this step.
The eggs, milk, and sugar are in the pan. Should the heat be low or medium?
Use medium heat. Stir the mixture as it cooks so the eggs heat gently and evenly instead of settling on the bottom.
I'm stirring now. What should I watch for so I know it's cooked enough?
Cook and stir until the mixture coats a metal spoon. Dip the spoon in, lift it out, and look for a thin coating that clings to the spoon rather than running off immediately.
It's starting to look thicker, and it coats the spoon lightly. Is that the point where I stop heating it?
Yes. Once it coats the metal spoon, remove the saucepan from the heat.
Pan is off the burner. I'm worried it'll keep cooking from the heat of the pan—what do I do next?
Cool it quickly: place the pan in a sink or bowl of ice water and stir the eggnog for 1 to 2 minutes.
It's sitting in ice water and I've stirred it for about 1 minute. Anything else from the recipe before serving or chilling?
After that quick cooling, stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. The recipe's cooked-and-cooled base is done, so you can continue cooling it as needed before serving.
Can you help me make Glazed Ham? I'm starting with an 8 pound bone-in shank ham and want to get set up correctly.

Absolutely. Put the ham, a roasting pan with a tight fitting lid, water, honey, and brown sugar within reach. For the ingredients, you'll need 1 (8 pound) bone-in shank ham, 4 cups water or as needed, 1/2 cup honey, and 1/2 cup brown sugar.
I have the ham and a roasting pan. Should I heat the oven before I unwrap everything?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the ham is in the pan.
The oven is heating. Do I need to mix the 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar right now?
Measure them so they're ready, but for the steps you're doing right now, focus on getting the ham into the roasting pan and adding the water.
Okay, the ham is unwrapped. Which side should go into the pan?
Set the bone-in shank ham in the roasting pan in a stable position, with the cut side arranged so it sits securely and won't tip when you add water.
It fits snugly. How much water should I pour around it?
Pour water into the roasting pan until it reaches a 2 inch depth. The recipe lists 4 cups water, or as needed, so use enough to reach that depth without splashing over the sides.
I'm at about 2 inches of water now. Should the lid go on tightly or leave a little vent?
Cover the roasting pan with a tight fitting lid. Don't vent it; the covered pan helps keep moisture around the ham.
The lid is on and the oven is at 275. Is there anything else before it goes in?
Check that the pan is steady, the water is still at about a 2 inch depth, and the lid is seated tightly. Then place the covered roasting pan in the 275 degrees F oven.
Can you help me make Eggplant Mixed Grill? I've got a resealable plastic bag and the vegetables ready to prep.

Absolutely. Start by setting up the marinade ingredients: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil. You'll also need vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic for the bag.
The herbs are chopped and measured. Should the oil and seasonings go straight into the bag?

Yes. In the large resealable plastic bag, combine the olive oil, parsley, oregano, basil, vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic. Press the bag gently from the outside to help the herbs and seasoning mix through the oil and vinegar.
The marinade is mixed. I have onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and both bell peppers on the board.
Add the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper into the bag with the marinade. Try to spread them out a bit so the marinade can reach all the pieces.
They're in the bag, but it's pretty full. How do I coat everything without making a mess?
Seal the bag firmly, leaving just enough space to move the vegetables around, then turn and gently massage the bag so the marinade coats the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and peppers.
Everything looks coated. How long does it need to sit before grilling?
Put the sealed bag in the refrigerator and marinate for 2 hours. Turn it occasionally during that time so the vegetables keep getting evenly coated.
The vegetables have been marinating, and I'm about ready to cook. What should I do with the grill?
Preheat the grill for high heat. While it heats, keep the vegetables chilled until you're ready to take them out of the bag.
The grill is hot. Anything I should do before putting the vegetables on?
Lightly oil the grill grate so the marinated vegetables are less likely to stick, then you're ready to place them on the hot grill.
Can you help me cook Adriennes Tom Ka Gai and keep me on track while I prep?
Absolutely. Set a large saucepan on the stove, and gather 2 teaspoons peanut oil plus 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced. You'll also want your aromatics ready before the pan heats up.
The saucepan is out, and I sliced the garlic. I'm checking the ginger and lemongrass amounts now.
Measure 2 tablespoons grated fresh ginger root and 1/4 cup chopped lemon grass. Keep them close to the garlic so they can all go into the hot oil together.
I've got those measured. Should I heat the oil before adding anything?
Yes. Pour the peanut oil into the large saucepan and warm it over medium heat until it shimmers lightly, but don't let it smoke.
The oil looks ready. I also have red pepper, coriander, and cumin beside the stove.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin. Cook them while stirring until they smell fragrant, about 2 minutes.
It smells really good now, and the garlic is just starting to soften. What should happen with the chicken?
Add the chicken and onion to the saucepan. Keep stirring as they cook until the chicken turns white and the onion looks translucent, about 5 minutes.
The chicken is white and the onion has softened. I have the bok choy washed and chopped.
Stir in the bok choy and let it cook until it begins to wilt. That can take 5 to 10 minutes depending on the size of the pieces and how full the pan is.
The bok choy is wilting but still a little crisp. Is that okay for serving?
Yes, that's right for this stage. Once it has wilted to your liking within that 5 to 10 minute window, give everything a final stir and serve the Tom Ka Gai hot.
I want to make Fire Side Coffee mix for a jar. Can you help me get the dry ingredients straight before I start?

Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl, a sifter, and a clean jar with a tight lid. For the mix, you'll need 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I've got the creamer and hot chocolate measured. Should the coffee granules go in whole or be crushed first?
Use the instant coffee granules as they are. Measure 1 1/2 cups, then add them with the creamer, hot chocolate mix, and the 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon so everything can be sifted together.
The instructions I'm looking at mention nutmeg too, but I don't see an amount in the ingredient list. What should I do?

Good catch. The listed measured spice is 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, while the instruction says to sift in cinnamon and nutmeg. Since no nutmeg amount is provided, don't guess a required quantity; sift the measured ingredients together, and only include nutmeg if you already have a separate amount you intend to use.
Okay, I'm ready to sift. Is the goal just to combine it, or should it look really fine?
Sift it until the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, and cinnamon are evenly blended and any clumps are broken up. It should look like a uniform dry drink mix.
It's mixed and fluffy now. My jar opening is narrow—any trick for transferring without making a mess?
Use a funnel or spoon it in slowly, tapping the jar lightly as you go. Once all the mix is in, seal the jar with its lid so the powder stays dry.
Jar is sealed. How much do I use for one mug?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Stir well so the coffee granules and cocoa mix dissolve fully.
If it tastes a little weak after stirring, is it okay to change the amount?

Yes. The recipe's final direction is to adjust to taste, so after starting with 3 teaspoons in 1 cup of hot water, add a little more mix if you want it stronger or dilute with more hot water if you want it lighter.
Can you walk me through making Corned Beef Hash? I've got a large skillet ready.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 large potatoes, peeled and diced; 1 (12 ounce) can corned beef, cut into chunks; 1 medium onion, chopped; and 1 cup beef broth.
The potatoes are diced and the onion is chopped. Should the skillet be heated before everything goes in?
Set the large deep skillet over medium heat, then add the potatoes, corned beef chunks, chopped onion, and beef broth all together.
Everything is in the pan. It looks like the broth is sitting mostly at the bottom—do I stir it right away?
Yes, give it a gentle stir so the onion and corned beef are distributed among the potatoes, but don't worry if the broth doesn't cover everything.
Okay, it's mixed. Do I leave it uncovered or put the lid on?
Cover the skillet and let it simmer over medium heat. You're cooking it until the potatoes are soft enough to mash and the liquid is almost gone.
How should I check the potatoes without breaking everything up too soon?
Lift the lid carefully and press a potato cube with a spoon or fork. If it gives easily and can be mashed, you're close. If it still feels firm, cover it again and keep simmering.
The potatoes are tender now, but there's still a little broth around the edges.
Let it simmer a bit longer with the lid on or slightly ajar until that liquid is nearly gone. The hash should look moist, not soupy.
The liquid is almost gone and the potatoes are mashable. What's the best way to serve it?
Mix everything well in the skillet so the softened potatoes, corned beef, and onion come together, then serve the Corned Beef Hash hot.
Can you help me make Carrot Pineapple Cake I? I'm getting my baking area set up now.
Absolutely. Start by pulling out the dry ingredients you'll measure: 2 cups all-purpose flour and 2 teaspoons baking soda.
Those are on the counter. I also have measuring spoons out—what else goes with the dry mix?
Add 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1 teaspoon salt to your setup. You'll also be mixing in cinnamon with those dry ingredients.
Before I start mixing, should the oven be heating already?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can preheat while you prep the pan and batter.
Oven is on. I've got a 9x13 inch pan—what should I do to it?
Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour so the cake releases more easily after baking.
Pan is ready. For the bowl, do I whisk all the dry ingredients together now?
Yes. In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon until they're evenly distributed.
The dry mixture looks even. The recipe mentions making a well—how deep does that need to be?
Just make a broad indentation in the center of the dry ingredients, deep enough to hold the wet additions without spilling over right away.
Okay, I've made the well. What goes into it?
Pour the sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla into the well in the center, then you'll be ready to bring the batter together from there.
Can you help me make Chicken Pot Pie II 2? I'm setting up the counter now and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Pull out 3 bone-in chicken breast halves, skinless, and a 1 (14.5 ounce) can of chicken broth. You'll also want a pot large enough for the chicken to sit in a single layer or close to it.
The chicken and the 14.5 ounce broth can are out. What vegetables should I grab before I start washing anything?
Grab 3 potatoes and 1 yellow onion. Keep them nearby while you start the chicken so you're not searching for ingredients with wet hands.
Got the potatoes and onion. For the chicken, should I rinse it right in the sink and then move it to the pot?
Yes. Wash the chicken breasts in water, then place them in the pot. Add enough water to just cover the chicken—no need to fill the pot higher than that.
The chicken is in the pot and the water barely covers it. Do I season the water now?
Add some salt, pepper, and garlic powder to the pot now. Stir the water lightly so the seasoning spreads around the chicken.
Seasoning is in. Should the chicken broth go in at this point too, or just stay ready for later?

The well is made. I've got the egg in a small bowl; how far should I beat it?
Beat the egg until it looks frothy, with small bubbles across the surface rather than just streaky yolk and white.
The egg is foamy now. I have cooking oil, milk, and bananas next to it—do those go into the egg bowl?
Yes. Mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the beaten egg until the wet mixture looks mostly combined.
Wet mixture is together. How do I bring it into the dry ingredients without making the muffins tough?
Pour the wet mixture into the well and stir gently, just until the dry ingredients are moistened and the chocolate chips are distributed. Stop before the batter gets overly smooth.
I want to make Empanadas, but I'm starting with the dough today. Can you guide me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 package of cream cheese, the 3 ounce size, so they're easy to blend smoothly.
Butter and cream cheese are on the counter. Do I need the filling ingredients out now too?
You can have 1 cup fruit preserves ready, but the dough comes first. Also measure 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour so it's ready to beat in.
I've sifted the flour. Should I use a bowl and mixer for the butter and cream cheese?
Yes, use a mixing bowl and cream the softened butter with the cream cheese until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.

Beat in the 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour until it's incorporated into the butter-cream cheese mixture and forms a soft dough.

That's fine for this dough. Shape it into a smooth ball as best you can; chilling will firm it up.

Either works. Wrap the smooth dough ball in foil or cling wrap, making sure it's covered well so it doesn't dry out in the refrigerator.
Wrapped and ready. How long should it chill before I bake with it?
Refrigerate it overnight, or keep it chilled for up to a week. When it's baking time, take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it.
I want to make Cindis Egg Rolls, but I'd like you to guide me while I prep. What should I pull out first?
Get a large wok ready, plus a big mixing bowl and a small bowl. For the filling, start with 1 pound ground pork and 4 cups shredded cabbage.
The pork and cabbage are on the counter. What vegetables should I prep before I turn on the stove?
Shred 1 large carrot, then cut 1/2 green bell pepper into thin strips. You'll also want onion, garlic, and ginger ready to mix with the vegetables.
Should the carrot and bell pepper go straight into the wok with the pork?
Not yet. Cook the ground pork by itself in the large wok over medium-high heat so it browns evenly without the vegetables steaming it.

Drain the pork, then set it aside. That keeps the egg roll filling from turning wet.

Put the cabbage, shredded carrot, green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger into the large bowl, then toss them together so everything is evenly mixed.

The sauce looks glossy but I see a few tiny cornstarch clumps. Should I worry?
Whisk or stir a little longer, pressing any clumps against the side of the bowl, until it's smooth before combining it with the filling components.

Yes. Keep the citrus guacamole base intact, and finely chop a small amount of pickle, capers, olive, or pepperoncini so it disappears into the mashed avocado mixture and gives little bright bites throughout.
Perfect. I've got a bowl and a cutting board out. What ingredients should I put on the counter before I cut anything?

Set out 2 avocados, plus 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice. You'll also want cumin, cilantro, salt, and hot pepper sauce if you plan to use it.
The avocados are ripe. Should I mash them before adding the juices, or stir everything together at once?
Peel and pit the 2 avocados, then mash them in a large bowl first. Once they're creamy but still a little textured, stir in the lime juice, orange juice, and pineapple juice.
And just to be clear, the briny thing should be folded into the guacamole like I normally like it, not sprinkled over the top.
Right—fold the finely minced pickle, capers, olive, or pepperoncini directly into the creamy avocado mixture after the juices go in, so it's evenly scattered without turning into a topping.
I've mashed the avocados and added all three juices. How much seasoning should I focus on next?
Stir in the cumin, chopped cilantro, and salt next. The recipe doesn't give amounts for those, so add them gradually and taste as you go so the citrus still stays noticeable.
The texture is soft but not runny. Should the hot pepper sauce go in now?
Yes, if you're using hot pepper sauce, mix it in now. Add a little at a time, stir well, and taste before adding more so it doesn't overpower the lime, orange, and pineapple.
I still have the avocado pits on the board. Is there any reason to keep one?
Place one of the avocado pits into the bowl with the guacamole to help keep it fresh, especially if it will sit for a bit before serving.
We're eating soon, but I may need ten minutes to clear the counter. What's the best way to hold it?
You can serve it immediately, or refrigerate it until serving. Since it's only a short wait, smooth the surface, keep the pit in the bowl, cover it, and give it a quick stir before bringing it out.
Can you help me get started on Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake? I want to make sure I have the ingredients measured before I turn on the oven.
Absolutely. For this cake, measure out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour and 2 teaspoons baking soda first. Keep them nearby, since they'll be sifted with the other dry ingredients.
The flour and baking soda are on the counter. What else should I set out before I grab the pans?
You'll also need 1/2 teaspoon salt and 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate, chopped. Once those are ready, you'll have the listed ingredients gathered.
I've got the salt, and I'm chopping the chocolate now. Should I preheat while I finish that?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) while you finish chopping the unsweetened chocolate.
The oven is heating. I have two round pans out—what size should they be?
Use 2 (9 inch) pans. Grease them well, then dust them with flour so the cake layers will release cleanly.
I greased the pans, but I'm not sure how much flour to leave in them after dusting.
After flouring each pan, tap and rotate it so the inside is lightly coated, then shake out any loose excess. You just want a thin flour layer over the greased surface.
Pans are ready and the oven is almost at temperature. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
Sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt. That keeps the dry mixture even and helps break up any clumps.
The dry ingredients are sifted into a bowl. Do I combine them with the chocolate yet?
Not yet based on the steps we have here. Set the sifted flour, baking soda, and salt mixture aside for now, with the chopped unsweetened chocolate ready for the next stage.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip for people arriving soon. Can you guide me through it without rushing? I've got a casserole dish out.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you mix the dip.
Oven is heating. For the creamy base, what amounts should I measure?
Measure 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream. Add both directly to a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish if you want to mix and bake in the same dish.
They're in the dish. I also have the soup mix packet and canned artichokes—how do those go in?
Stir in 1 package of garlic and mushroom soup mix, the 1 ounce size. Then add 1 can of artichoke hearts, 14 ounces, drained and chopped.
The artichokes are chopped and mixed in. The instruction I have mentions cheese and crab meat too—should I add those before baking?
Yes, add the cheese and crab meat to the same casserole dish now, then fold everything together until the sour cream, mayonnaise, soup mix, artichokes, cheese, and crab are evenly combined.
It's mixed, but the top looks a little uneven. Should I smooth it out or cover it?
Smooth the top lightly so it bakes evenly, but leave it uncovered. That helps the dip heat through and lets the surface set a bit.
Okay, it's uncovered and ready. How long should it bake?
Bake it uncovered for 30 minutes at 350 degrees F.
Timer's done. It's hot and bubbly around the edges—what's the best way to serve it?
Serve it immediately while it's hot and creamy. Bring it to the table carefully in the casserole dish, with crackers, bread, or vegetables for dipping.
Can you help me make Dad's Flat Bread? I've got a large mixing bowl out, but I want to make sure I start with the yeast correctly.

Absolutely. For the yeast, measure 1/2 cup of the warm water into the bowl and dissolve 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast in it. The water should be warm, about 110 degrees to 115 degrees, not hot.
The yeast is in the bowl with the warm water. Before I add anything else, how much water should I still have left?
You started with 2 cups warm water total, divided. Since 1/2 cup went in with the yeast, you should have 1 1/2 cups remaining to add with the next ingredients.
Got it. I have sugar and oil nearby. What goes into the bowl with the yeast mixture?
Add 1/3 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining water. Beat the mixture until it looks smooth.
I'm beating it now. It's smoother, but still more like a thick batter than dough. Is that okay at this point?
Yes, that's fine. After it's smooth, begin adding the remaining all-purpose flour gradually, just enough to turn it into a soft dough rather than a pourable batter.
When you say soft dough, should it still stick to my fingers a little, or should I keep adding flour until it's dry?
Keep it soft. A little tackiness is okay, but it should hold together and be workable. Avoid making it dry or stiff with too much extra flour.
The dough is holding together now. Should I flour the counter before I take it out of the bowl?
Yes. Lightly flour your work surface, turn the dough out onto it, and dust your hands if needed so it doesn't cling too much while you knead.
It's on the floured surface. How long should I knead, and what am I looking for?
Knead the dough until it becomes smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. It should feel springy and more cohesive by the end.
Can you help me make Coconut Ambrosia Salad for serving later today?
Absolutely. Start by setting out a large mixing bowl and make sure the fruit is well drained: 1 (11 ounce) can mandarin oranges and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple.
The oranges and pineapple are drained. Should I add the creamy part next?
Yes. Add 3 1/2 cups thawed frozen whipped topping to the bowl, then add 2 cups shredded coconut.
I'm worried about breaking up the mandarin oranges. How gently should I mix this?

Use a wide spatula and fold slowly from the bottom of the bowl, turning the mixture over rather than stirring hard. You want the whipped topping to coat the fruit and coconut without crushing the oranges.
The recipe also mentions marshmallows and milk in the bowl. Do those go in with everything else?
Yes, combine the oranges, pineapple, whipped topping, coconut, marshmallows, and milk together in the large bowl, then mix until everything is evenly distributed.
It looks combined now. How long does it need to chill?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate it for 1 hour before serving so the salad firms up and the flavors settle together.
While it chills, should I do anything for serving?
You can tidy the rim of the bowl, keep it covered in the refrigerator, and have serving spoons ready. If you're transferring it to a serving dish, wait until after the chill time so it stays fluffy.
The hour is up. What's the final touch?
Give it one gentle fold, spoon it into the serving bowl if needed, and garnish with cherries right before serving.
Can you help me make Broccoli Chicken Roli? I already have some cooked chicken ready and want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat and 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli. Use a large mixing bowl so there's enough room to combine everything without spilling.
Chicken and broccoli are in a big bowl. I'm chopping the vegetables now—how much onion and green pepper should go in?
Add 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper to the bowl with the chicken and broccoli.
Those are added. The bowl looks pretty full; what else gets mixed in before it goes near the oven?
Add the cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic to that same bowl. Keep everything together there so the filling comes together evenly.
I've added those. Should I fold it gently or really stir it?
Mix it all together until the chicken, broccoli, onion, bell pepper, and seasonings are evenly coated. A sturdy spoon or spatula works well; stir enough to combine, but you don't need to mash it.
The mixture is combined and looks creamy. Should I start heating the oven yet?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
Oven is preheating. What pan setup do I need so cleanup is easy?
Cover a cookie sheet with aluminum foil. Smooth it down so the surface is even and ready for the mixture when you're ready to assemble or bake.
The foil is on the cookie sheet. Anything I should check before I move the bowl over?

Give the mixture one last stir to make sure the chicken, broccoli, onion, green bell pepper, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic are evenly distributed, then keep the foil-lined cookie sheet ready by the preheated oven.

Set out 1 tablespoon butter, softened; 1 egg white; 1/4 cup white sugar; and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also want cookie sheets, a small saucepan, and a medium-sized bowl.

Can you guide me through making Curried Winter Squash? I've got the cooked squash ready but want to make sure I season it right.
Absolutely. Measure out 3 cups of cooked, mashed winter squash into a medium microwave-safe bowl. You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder for the seasoning.
The squash is in the bowl, and I measured the curry powder. What should I add with it?
Add 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, plus 2 tablespoons maple syrup. Those will melt in and balance the curry.

Stir it together before heating so the curry powder, butter or margarine, maple syrup, and mashed squash are evenly combined in the medium bowl.
It's mixed, but the butter is still in a few soft pieces. Is that okay for the microwave?
Yes, that's fine. Microwave it on high until it's heated through, about 5 minutes. The butter or margarine should finish melting as it warms.
Should I stop and stir during those 5 minutes?
You can pause once partway through and stir for a smoother texture, then continue microwaving until the squash is hot all the way through.
It's hot now and looks creamy. The recipe mentions coconut—when does that go on?
Sprinkle coconut over the top after heating, if you'd like to use it. It's optional, so you can add just enough for a light topping or skip it.
I'll add a small sprinkle. Any final serving tip?
Once the coconut is on, serve the Curried Winter Squash warm straight from the bowl or transfer it to a serving dish.
I want to make Cinnamon Chocolate Cake 2, but I'd like you to guide me while I set up. What should I pull out first?
Start with the dry ingredients you'll measure into a mixing bowl: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.

Yes, add the cinnamon and salt to the same mixing bowl with the flour and sugar, then stir them together so the first four ingredients are evenly combined.

Use a saucepan. Add the water, oil, butter, and cocoa to it, then set it over medium heat.

Bring the saucepan mixture to a boil over medium heat. Keep an eye on it and stir as needed so the cocoa and butter blend smoothly.

The recipe has you pour it over the dry ingredients at this point. Pour carefully into the mixing bowl, then mix well until the dry ingredients are fully moistened.

Yes. Add the eggs, buttermilk, vanilla, and baking soda to the bowl, then mix well again until the batter looks smooth and evenly blended.
Any texture check before I move on with the cake batter?
Look for a uniform batter with no dry streaks from the flour mixture and no visible pockets of baking soda. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl once, then give it a final mix.

Can you help me make Fire Side Coffee? I'm setting up a jar for the mix and want to do it in the right order.

Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, and a clean jar with a tight lid. You'll need 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I've got the creamer and hot chocolate mix measured. Should the coffee granules go in whole, or do they need crushing?
The instant coffee granules can go in as they are. Measure 1 1/2 cups of them, then add them with the creamer and hot chocolate mix so everything can be sifted together evenly.
The cinnamon is ready too. I noticed the directions mention nutmeg—how should I handle that?

Add the 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and if you're following the instruction that includes nutmeg, sift it in with the dry ingredients as well. Since there isn't a listed amount for nutmeg, use only what your recipe notes or keep it very light.
Everything is in the sifter now, but the hot chocolate mix is a little clumpy.

That's fine—sift the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and nutmeg together into the bowl. Break up any clumps as they hit the mesh so the finished drink mix is smooth and evenly blended.
The powder looks uniform now. Do I pack it into the jar or just pour it in loosely?
Pour the mixture into the jar loosely rather than packing it down. Tap the jar gently to settle the powder, then seal it with the lid so it stays dry.
I want to make a cup right away. What ratio should I use?
For 1 serving, stir 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture into 1 cup of hot water. Mix until the powder dissolves and the drink looks smooth.
If it tastes a little weak or too sweet, what's the best adjustment?
Adjust to taste: add a bit more mix if you want it stronger or richer, or add more hot water if it's too intense or sweet. Give it a final stir before serving.
Can you help me make Butterscotch Basketball Cookies? I've got a microwave and a mixing bowl ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup butter, softened. The butter should be real butter, with no substitutes.

Yes—measure 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Pack the brown sugar firmly so the amount is accurate.

Yes. Put the butterscotch chips in a microwave-safe bowl and melt them carefully, stirring as needed. Once melted, let them cool for 10 minutes.
They're melted and cooling. While I wait, can I work on the butter mixture?
Go ahead. In your mixing bowl, cream the softened butter with the sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks blended and smooth.

When you're ready, add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
The egg, milk, and vanilla are mixed in. The bowl looks lighter and looser now.
That sounds right. Scrape down the sides of the bowl so the butter-sugar mixture and the added liquids are fully incorporated.
The melted butterscotch has cooled for 10 minutes. Do I pour it all in at once?
Yes, add the melted butterscotch chips to the bowl and beat them in until the dough is evenly butterscotch-colored.

Absolutely. Start by putting a large mixing bowl on the counter and measuring the dry ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 3 teaspoons baking powder.

Pack the brown sugar into the 1/2 cup measure so it holds its shape when tipped out. Add it to the bowl with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.

Just combine the dry mixture evenly. A quick whisk or stir is enough to distribute the flour, sugars, baking powder, and salt.

Set aside 1 tablespoon baby food for the glaze before you mix the rest into the batter.

Use a second bowl. In it, beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food until the mixture looks fairly smooth.

Use the frozen pie crust as directed here and get the oven heating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.

The recipe just has you bake the pie crust on its own for about 10 minutes, until it's only starting to brown.

Check for light browning at the edges or surface rather than a fully dark crust. Once it's just starting to brown, take it out.

Yes. In the large bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, salt, pepper, and hot sauce until the mixture looks evenly combined.

Whisk until the eggs are fully broken up and the cream is blended in, with no obvious streaks. Once the crust has cooled, the filling is ready for the next part of the quiche.

It's the next day and everything is chilled. What's the last meat-prep step before I portion it?
Lift out the beef shank, trim away the gristle, cut the meat into medium sized pieces, and set it aside.
I want to make Chocolate Covered Banana Pie. Before I get my hands buttery, what should I set out? I've got a 9 x 13 inch pan ready.

Set out 3 cups crushed vanilla wafers, 1/2 cup chopped pecans, 2/3 cup melted butter, and 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips. You'll also want a mixing bowl and something flat, like the bottom of a measuring cup, to press the crust evenly into that pan.
The wafers are crushed and the pecans are chopped. Should I turn on the oven now or wait?
Go ahead and heat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it warms, you can mix the crust so it's ready to bake as soon as the oven is hot.
My butter is melted. Do the chocolate chips go into the crust mixture too?

For the crust step, combine only the crushed cookie crumbs, chopped pecans, and melted butter or margarine. Stir until the crumbs look evenly moistened and hold together a bit when pressed. Keep the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips aside for the chocolate-covered part.
The mixture looks sandy but damp. How firmly should I pack it into the pan?
Press it into the 9 x 13 inch pan in an even layer, using steady pressure so the bottom is compact without being rock-hard. Pay attention to the corners so they aren't thinner than the center.
It's spread out, but a little crumbly along one edge. Is that okay before baking?
That's fine. Just press that edge once more with the flat bottom of a cup or your fingers. The butter will help it set during the short bake.
The oven is at temperature. How long does the crust need?
Bake the crust at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C, for 5 minutes. Since it's brief, stay nearby; you're looking for it to set lightly, not brown deeply.
The timer went off after 5 minutes. It smells toasty—what should I do with the pan now?
Take the pan out carefully and let the crust cool. Once it's cooled, it will be ready for the remaining pie assembly with the semisweet chocolate chips.

The flour and white sugar are measured. Should I pack the brown sugar firmly now?

Use another bowl and beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food until the mixture looks fairly smooth.

Great. Before my hands get messy, what should I set out on the counter?

Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil or a little more to taste, 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt, pepper, and your tender herb stems. You'll also want a mixing bowl, a plate or tray for the patties, and grill tongs.
