Start it now: preheat the outdoor grill for high heat. While it heats, you can mince the tender stems and mix the burger mixture.
Perfect, using those tender stems is my usual way to get more flavor from the herbs.
Then keep that going here: trim off any tough or woody pieces, mince the tender stems finely, and add just enough that they blend into the meat instead of making the patties loose.
The grill is heating, and the stems are minced. How do I combine everything without overworking the beef?

Put the ground beef in the bowl, then add the 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, the 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil, the 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt, pepper, and the minced tender stems. Mix gently with your fingers or a fork just until the seasonings look evenly spread.
The mixture looks combined and still a little loose, not mashed. How many burgers should I make?
Shape it into 4 burger patties. Press them together firmly enough to hold, and make a shallow dimple in the center of each so they cook more evenly on the hot grill.
They're shaped. Do I oil the patties or the grill grate?
Lightly oil the grill grate, not the patties. Once the grate is ready, place the patties on the high-heat grill with a little space between them.
They're on the grill. What timing and temperature am I aiming for before serving?

Cook the burgers about 6 minutes total, turning once, until they reach an internal temperature of 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), or to your desired doneness. Let them come off the grill once the texture feels set and the juices are running clearly enough for your preference.
Can you guide me through making Cookie Jar Gingersnaps? I've got a mixing bowl and measuring cups out.
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup shortening and 1 cup sugar to begin. Those two get creamed together in a large mixing bowl, so make sure the shortening is soft enough to blend smoothly.
The shortening and sugar are measured. Should I get the wet ingredients ready too?
Yes. You'll need 1 egg and 1/4 cup molasses. Keep them nearby so you can beat them in right after the shortening and sugar are creamed.
I'm creaming the shortening and sugar now. What texture am I looking for?
Mix until the sugar is worked evenly through the shortening and the mixture looks smooth and creamy rather than streaky or clumpy.
That looks creamy. I don't want molasses splashing everywhere—how should I add it?
Crack in the egg first, then pour in the 1/4 cup molasses. Beat them into the creamed mixture at a moderate speed or by hand with steady strokes until everything is evenly combined.
The bowl is sticky but mixed. What dry ingredients go in next?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. Once those are mixed together, add them gradually to the creamed mixture so the dough comes together evenly.
When I add the dry mix gradually, should I stop as soon as I don't see flour?
Yes, mix just until the dry ingredients are incorporated and the dough looks consistent. Scrape the sides of the bowl if needed so no pockets of flour or spice remain.
The dough is ready. How do I shape the cookies for the jar?
Scoop teaspoonfuls of dough and roll each one into a ball. Try to keep them similar in size so the gingersnaps bake evenly.

messages.content: For Blackened Tuna, can we plate it with my usual pair of narrow sauce streaks instead of coating the fish?
Yes. We'll cook the Blackened Tuna as written, then plate the tuna over 2 slim sauce streaks and leave any extra sauce on the side so the blackened crust stays uncovered.

Set out 1 1/2 pounds fresh tuna steaks, about 1 inch thick, along with 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning. Pat the tuna dry if it feels damp so the seasoning grabs well.

Yes—measure 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter. Keep them close to the skillet because the pan will be over high heat.

Coat the tuna generously with the Cajun seasoning on the surface you're cooking, pressing it in lightly so it forms a good blackened layer.
Seasoning is on. Should I add the oil and butter together, or one before the other?
Add the olive oil and butter to the large skillet together, then heat them over high heat. Watch closely as the butter melts and the oil gets very hot.

Wait until the oil is nearly smoking. At that point, carefully lay the tuna steaks into the pan without crowding them.

Let the tuna cook on that side for 3 to 4 minutes, or until the surface is blackened. Avoid moving the steaks while the crust forms.

Lift the tuna out carefully, keep the blackened side visible, and plate it across the 2 narrow sauce streaks. Put any remaining sauce nearby rather than over the fish.
Can you guide me through Country Fried Chicken while I set up the coating station?
Absolutely. Put a large resealable plastic bag on the counter for the dry coating, and have a shallow bowl ready for the egg and milk mixture.
I've got the bag and bowl out. Which dry ingredients should go in the bag?
Measure 1/3 cup all-purpose flour into the bag, then add 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika.
The flour, garlic salt, pepper, and paprika are in the bag. Should I mix them before adding chicken?
Yes. Seal the bag and give it a good shake so the seasonings are evenly combined throughout the flour mixture.
Done. For the shallow bowl, am I just cracking in the egg with the milk?
Right. Beat the egg and milk together in the shallow bowl until they look smooth and blended.
The egg mixture is ready. How many pieces of chicken should I coat at once?
Add the chicken to the bag a few pieces at a time so each piece has room to move around. Seal the bag and shake until the chicken is coated.
Some pieces are flour-coated now. Do they go straight back into the bag or into the egg bowl first?
Dip each coated piece into the egg and milk mixture first, turning it so it's covered, then let any excess drip off briefly.
They're dipped. How do I get that thicker country-fried coating?
Return the dipped chicken to the flour mixture and shake again. That second coating helps build the classic country fried crust.
Can you guide me through making Cookie Bowl? I want to get the ingredients and pan setup right before I mix anything.

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds. For the shaping setup, you'll also need a 9x5 inch loaf pan or a metal bowl, foil, and a cookie sheet.
I've got the dry ingredients measured. Should I start the oven before wrapping the pan?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the bowl form is prepared.
The oven is on. I'm using a 9x5 inch loaf pan; how exactly should the foil go on it?
Turn the loaf pan upside down, then cover the outside of it with foil. Smooth the foil over the bottom and sides so it creates a clean surface for shaping the cookie bowl.
The foil is wrapped around the outside. Do I put the pan straight in the oven like that?
Place the upside-down, foil-covered pan onto a cookie sheet. That gives it support and makes it easier to move in and out of the oven later.
Cookie sheet is ready. For the dry mix, do the almonds go in with the flour or later?
Add them now. Stir together the flour, cocoa powder, salt, and sliced almonds until the cocoa is evenly distributed and the almonds are mixed through.
The cocoa is leaving a few darker streaks in the bowl. Is that okay, or should I keep stirring?
Keep stirring until the mixture looks fairly even in color. Since this step is just combining the flour, cocoa, salt, and almonds, there shouldn't be any pockets of cocoa or salt left.
The dry mixture looks uniform now, and the foil-covered pan is sitting on the cookie sheet. Anything else before I move on?

That completes the listed prep: the oven is at 350 degrees F/175 degrees C, the upside-down 9x5 inch loaf pan is covered with foil and set on a cookie sheet, and the flour, cocoa, salt, and almonds are stirred together. Set the dry mixture aside until the next part of the recipe.
I'm making Cookie Bowl and want to get set up before I touch the oven. What ingredients should I put on the counter?
Set out 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds. Those are the dry ingredients you'll be using.
Got them. Should I measure the cocoa and flour into the same area, or keep anything separate?
You can measure them separately for accuracy, but they'll all be stirred together soon: flour, cocoa powder, salt, and sliced almonds.
Before mixing, what equipment do I need for shaping the bowl?
You'll need either a 9x5 inch loaf pan or a metal bowl, foil to cover the outside, and a cookie sheet to hold it while it bakes.
I have a metal bowl and foil ready. Should the oven be on now?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. How exactly do I wrap the bowl?
Turn the metal bowl upside down, then cover the outside with foil so the exterior surface is protected and ready for the cookie bowl shape.
The foil is on the upside-down bowl. Where does it go?
Place the foil-covered upside-down bowl onto a cookie sheet so it's stable and easy to move in and out of the oven.
That's set. What should the dry mix look like before I set it aside?
Stir together the 1 1/4 cups flour, 1/2 cup cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds until the cocoa and salt are evenly distributed, then set the mixture aside.
Can you guide me through making Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches? I've got the eggplant on the cutting board.
Absolutely. Seed the eggplant if it isn't already, then slice it lengthwise into 1/4 inch slices. You'll also need 1 red bell pepper sliced into thin strips.
The eggplant is sliced and the pepper strips are ready. What should I set out besides those?
Set out salt and pepper for seasoning, plus 1 French baguette. You'll also want a medium baking sheet for the vegetables.
Baking sheet is out. Do I need to heat anything before the vegetables go on it?
Yes, preheat the oven broiler so it's hot by the time the eggplant and pepper are arranged.
The broiler is heating. Should I oil the pan, or just put the vegetables straight on?
For this recipe, just place the eggplant slices and red bell pepper strips on the medium baking sheet, then season them with salt and pepper to taste.
They're spread out and seasoned. How close should I watch them under the broiler?
Keep a close eye on them and broil for 5 to 10 minutes, until the eggplant and pepper are tender and slightly browned.
They're starting to brown at the edges but the eggplant still looks a little firm in the middle.
Give them a bit more time within that 5 to 10 minute window, checking often. Pull them once the eggplant has softened and the vegetables are slightly browned.
The vegetables are tender now. How do I prep the bread for serving?
Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise, then use it as the base for the broiled eggplant and red pepper sandwiches.
Can you guide me through making Cabbage Rolls II? I've got the cabbage out but haven't started anything yet.
Absolutely. Set up 12 cabbage leaves, 1 cup cooked white rice, 1 beaten egg, and 1/4 cup milk. You'll also need onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper for the filling.
The rice is already cooked, and I have the egg and milk measured. Should I start with the cabbage leaves?
Yes. Put a large pot of water on the stove and bring it to a boil so the leaves can soften enough to roll.
The pot is coming up to a boil. Do I need a bowl or colander ready?
Have a colander or clean draining area ready. Once the water boils, add the cabbage leaves and boil them for 2 minutes, then drain them well.
The leaves are drained. They're soft but still holding together.
That's what you want. Lay them out so they can cool slightly while you make the filling in a large bowl.
I've got a large bowl ready. What goes into the filling exactly?
Combine the 1 cup cooked white rice, beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper in the bowl.
Should I mix it until it's completely smooth, or just combined?
Mix until everything is evenly combined, but don't overwork the ground beef. You just want the rice, egg, milk, onion, salt, and pepper distributed through the meat.
The filling is mixed. How much should I put on each leaf so they roll neatly?
Place about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture in the center of each cabbage leaf. Fold the sides in, roll it up, and tuck in the ends so each cabbage roll holds its shape.
Can you guide me through Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme? I'm setting up the counter now.
Absolutely. Set out a large bowl and measure 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream, plus 1/4 cup lemon juice. Those will start the marinade.
I've got sour cream and the lemon juice measured. Are there any small seasonings I should grab before the chicken comes out?
Yes. Measure 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed. Keep them close to the bowl with the sour cream and lemon juice.
The bowl is ready. Should I whisk those together or just stir them in?
Stir them together well in the large bowl. The recipe says to combine the first eight ingredients, so make sure the marinade ingredients are evenly mixed before adding the chicken.
The mixture looks smooth. Do I add all the chicken pieces at once?
Add the chicken to the mixture, then turn each piece so it gets coated on all sides. Use tongs if you want to keep your hands cleaner.
Everything is coated. It's in a covered dish now—how long does it need to sit?
Cover it and marinate it overnight in the refrigerator. That gives the chicken time to absorb the flavor and stay moist.
Tomorrow when I take it out, do I use the marinade for anything else?
No, just remove the chicken from the marinade. Let the excess drip off, then discard the used marinade.
What's the last prep before it goes toward baking?
Coat each chicken piece with crumbs after it comes out of the marinade. Press the crumbs on gently so they stick evenly.
Can you guide me through making Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms? I've got the mushrooms out and want to set up before I turn on the oven.

Absolutely. Set the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), and have a large baking sheet ready. You'll need 1 pound fresh mushrooms with the stems removed, plus 3/4 cup melted butter divided for the pan and filling.
The mushrooms are stemmed. For the filling, what should I put beside the butter?
Measure out 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons and 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese. You'll also be mixing in crabmeat, lobster, and garlic with the remaining butter.
I have a big sheet pan. How much butter goes on it, and should I use parchment?
Use about 1/4 cup of the melted butter to brush the large baking sheet. The recipe has the mushrooms go directly onto the buttered sheet, so parchment isn't necessary.
The sheet is buttered. Should the caps be close together or spaced out?
Arrange the mushroom caps in a single layer over the baking sheet. They can sit fairly close, but keep them from overlapping so each cap is easy to stuff.
The caps are lined up. I'm ready to make the seafood mixture—what bowl size and order should I use?
Use a medium bowl. Add the crushed seasoned croutons, the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, shredded mozzarella cheese, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic, then mix until the filling is evenly combined.
The croutons are soaking up the butter pretty quickly. Is the texture supposed to be loose or packed?
It should look moist and scoopable rather than soupy. The croutons will absorb the butter, while the mozzarella helps the crabmeat and lobster mixture hold together for stuffing.
Once the filling is mixed, should I mound it high in each mushroom or keep it level?

Spoon the filling into the mushroom caps and gently mound it so each one gets a generous portion without spilling all over the pan. Keep the oven at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) while you finish loading the tray.
Can you guide me through making Caramelized Apple Bites? I've got a microwave and a medium bowl ready.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrapped and chopped, plus 2 tablespoons of light corn syrup to make the coating.
The caramels are unwrapped and chopped, and I measured the corn syrup. Do the apples need any prep before we heat the caramel?
Yes—prep 2 apples by peeling, coring, and dicing them. Keep the pieces bite-sized so they'll coat easily.
The apples are diced. Should they go into the bowl with the caramels right away?
Not yet. Put only the chopped caramels and the light corn syrup into the medium microwave-safe bowl.
They're in the bowl together. How long should I microwave them?
Microwave the bowl on high for approximately 30 seconds, just until the caramels are melted.
After 30 seconds, the caramel looks melted but a little thick. Is that okay?
That's fine for this recipe as long as it's melted enough to coat. Give the caramel and corn syrup mixture a quick stir to bring it together.
It's smooth now. Do I add all the diced apples at once?
Yes, place the diced apples into the bowl and toss them until they're coated with the caramel and light corn syrup mixture.
The apple pieces are coated. Can I serve them right away, or should they sit for a bit?
Let the Caramelized Apple Bites cool before serving so the coating can settle and they're comfortable to eat.
Can you guide me through making a Cosmopolitan? I've got a shaker and cocktail glass ready.
Absolutely. Set out vodka, cointreau, fresh lime juice, cranberry juice, plenty of ice, and a lime for the twist garnish.
For the liquor, how much vodka and cointreau should I measure?
Measure 1 jigger of vodka, which is 1.5 fluid ounces, and add 1/2 fluid ounce cointreau.
Those are measured. What about the lime and cranberry juice?
You'll need 1 teaspoon fresh lime juice and 1 1/2 fluid ounces cranberry juice.
I squeezed the lime and measured the cranberry. Does everything go straight into the shaker?
Yes. Fill the shaker with lots of ice, then pour in the vodka, cointreau, fresh lime juice, and cranberry juice.
The shaker feels pretty full with ice. How long should I shake it?
Shake it vigorously for several seconds, enough to chill the drink well and blend everything together.
It's cold now. Should I pour it over ice or strain it?
Strain it into a cocktail glass rather than serving it over the shaker ice.
I've strained it into the glass. What's the garnish supposed to be?
Garnish the Cosmopolitan with a lime twist, then serve it right away while it's chilled.
Can you help me make Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men? I'm setting up the mixing bowl and want to get the early ingredients right.
Absolutely. Put a large bowl on your counter and measure out 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar. Those two will be creamed together until the mixture looks smooth.
I've got the margarine softening and the sugar measured. Do I need anything wet before I start mixing?
Yes—keep 1/2 cup molasses and 1 egg yolk nearby. You'll add them after the margarine and sugar are smooth.
The bowl is ready. How smooth should the margarine and sugar look?
Cream them until you don't see separate streaks of margarine and the sugar is evenly worked in. It should look cohesive and soft rather than chunky.
That looks smooth now. Should I pour in the molasses all at once?
Go ahead and stir in the molasses, then add the egg yolk. Mix until both are fully blended into the creamed margarine and sugar.
The molasses mixture is dark and even. What dry ingredients am I combining separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg. Once they're mixed together, blend them into the molasses mixture.
Should I add the dry mixture gradually, or dump it in?
Add it in portions if that's easier to control, scraping the bowl as needed. Keep blending until the dough looks smooth with no dry patches.
The dough is together and smooth. What should I do with it before shaping cookies?
Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. That rest will firm it up so it's easier to handle for the gingerbread men.
Can you guide me through making Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers? I want to get the prep organized before I touch the meat.
Absolutely. Set up a large mixing bowl and have these ready: 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg.
Cheddar, Parmesan, onion, and the egg are on the counter. Do I need the grill going before I mix the patties?
Yes, get the grill preheating to high heat so it is ready by the time the patties are shaped.
The grill is heating. What should go into the bowl before the beef?
Add the Cheddar cheese, Parmesan cheese, chopped onion, egg, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper to the large bowl, then mix those together.
Should that mixture look smooth, or is it okay if the onion and cheese are still chunky?
Chunky is fine. You just want the egg and seasonings distributed through the cheese and onion so the beef can mix in evenly.
Okay, the bowl mixture is combined. How do I add the beef without overworking it?
Crumble the ground beef into the bowl in loose pieces, then mix it together by hand just until everything is evenly combined.
The beef mixture is ready. How many burgers am I shaping from this?
Shape the mixture into 6 patties. Try to keep them even in size so they cook at the same pace on the hot grill.
I have 6 patties formed. Where does the bacon come in?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty, tucking or securing the ends as needed, then they will be ready to go onto the preheated high-heat grill.

Chop just the very tender stems finely into the dressing, and hold the leaves aside so they stay fresh and separate.
Perfect, that's the special version I'm doing this time. I've cleared the counter—what do I need first?
Pull out 6 russet potatoes and 1 cup all-purpose flour. Keep the potatoes whole for the boil, and have the flour ready for later.
The potatoes and flour are out. Are there any smaller items I should set beside them?
Yes: set out 1 egg, lightly beaten, plus 1 tablespoon olive oil. That gives you all the listed ingredients for Grandmas Gnocchi.

Fill the large pot, salt the water well, and bring it to a boil before adding the potatoes.

Leave them unpeeled for now. Once the water is boiling, drop in the potatoes and cook them until they're tender but still firm, about 15 minutes.
How do I check that tender-but-firm point without overdoing them?
Pierce one with a fork or small knife; it should go in without much force, but the potato shouldn't be falling apart.

Let them cool slightly, just until you can handle them safely, then peel off the skins.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this batch only, cover the surface with a light, thin glaze, but keep one corner unglazed.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm putting Chicken Tortilla Soup IV into a one-off gift spread alongside fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and desserts, so I want the presentation to fit that box. What should the top look like?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a thin full-surface glaze and leave one corner plain.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chicken Tortilla Soup IV for a gift box or dessert platter with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, or desserts. How should I finish the top?

messages.content: I'm putting Chicken Tortilla Soup IV into a one-off gift spread alongside fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and desserts, so I want the presentation to fit that box. What should the top look like?
For this batch only, cover the surface with a light, thin glaze, but keep one corner unglazed.
Perfect, that's the special finish I want just for this one. I've got a large pot and paper towels ready—what ingredients should I line up first?
Start with 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil and 6 corn tortillas, each 6 inches, cut into 1/2 inch strips.
The tortilla strips are cut. Should I measure the soup seasonings now too?
Yes. Put 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin on the counter so everything is ready.
Oil is measured, and the pot is on the stove. How much goes in for the first batch?
Pour 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat.
The oil looks warm and shimmery. Do all the tortilla strips go in at once?
Add only half of the tortilla strips. Stir them often while they cook, and keep going until they turn crisp.
They're crisping up, but a few pieces are browning faster than the rest. Should I keep stirring?
Yes, keep them moving so they crisp evenly, then lift that batch out as soon as the strips are crisp.
First batch is out of the pot. Where should I put them so they don't get greasy?
Spread them on paper towels and let them drain.
The paper towels are catching the oil. How do I handle the remaining strips?
Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of oil to the pot, crisp the remaining tortilla strips the same way, then set all the strips aside.
Can you guide me through Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style? I've got the squash on the counter but haven't heated the oven yet.
Absolutely. Set the oven to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C, so it can heat while you get organized.
Oven is set. For the squash, I need it cut lengthwise and seeded, right?
Yes. Use 1 spaghetti squash, halve it lengthwise, and scoop out the seeds. Keep the halves intact for baking.
The halves are ready. What ingredients should I have nearby besides the squash?
Have 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 cans of stewed tomatoes ready; each can should be 14 ounces.
I found the onion, garlic, and tomatoes. Do I need a baking dish or a sheet pan for this part?
Use a baking sheet. Give it a thin, even layer of cooking spray so the squash doesn't stick.
The sheet pan is sprayed. Which way should the squash face?
Place the squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
They're on the pan cut side down. How long should they bake?
Bake them in the preheated oven for 35 minutes.
When the timer goes off, what texture am I looking for before moving on?
Check by sliding in a knife; the squash is ready when a knife can be easily inserted. If it still feels firm, give it a little more time and check again.
Can you guide me through Babis Bean Salad? My black-eyed peas have been soaking overnight.

Absolutely. Drain the soaked black-eyed peas if they're still in soaking water, then measure out 1 1/2 cups for the salad. You'll also want 1/3 cup chopped celery with the leaves included, 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot, and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley ready nearby.
I've got the peas drained and the vegetables on the counter. What size pot should I use for the beans?
Use a saucepan that gives the beans a little room to move around. Add the soaked black-eyed peas, then pour in enough water to cover them by 1 inch.
The beans are covered by about an inch of water. Should I turn the heat up high?
Bring them up gently until the water reaches a slow boil. You're looking for steady, mild bubbling rather than a hard rolling boil.
It's starting to bubble slowly now. Do I leave it there?
Once you have that slow boil, reduce the heat to low. Let the beans simmer until they're tender but not mushy, which should take about 35 minutes.
How can I tell the texture is right without overcooking them?
Taste a bean near the end of the 35 minutes. It should be soft enough to bite through easily but still hold its shape, not collapsing or turning pasty.
While they simmer, should I chop the celery leaves in with the celery?
Yes. Chop the celery and its leaves together until you have 1/3 cup. Keep the 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley separate and ready for when the beans have cooled.
The beans are tender now and still intact. What should I do before mixing in the vegetables?
Take the saucepan off the heat and set the beans aside to cool. Once they've cooled, they'll be ready to combine with the celery, shredded carrot, and parsley for the salad.
I want to make Dads Flat Bread. Can you guide me without rushing? I'm setting out a big mixing bowl now.

Absolutely. Start by checking the basics: you'll need 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast and 2 cups warm water total, divided. The water should be between 110 degrees and 115 degrees so the yeast wakes up without getting overheated.
I've got the yeast and a thermometer. Should I measure all the water at once or split it now?
Measure the 2 cups, then pour off 1/2 cup for dissolving the yeast in the large mixing bowl. Keep the remaining water nearby for the next mix-in.
The 1/2 cup is in the bowl with the yeast. What should I have ready before stirring in more?
Set out 1/3 cup sugar and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also need salt, rye or whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, and that remaining warm water close by.
Okay, the sugar and oil are measured, and I have the flours on the counter. How do I combine this without making it lumpy?

Add the sugar, oil, salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining warm water to the yeast mixture. Beat it until the mixture looks smooth, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed.
It's smoothing out, but it still looks more like thick batter than dough. Is that expected?
Yes, that's fine at this point. Begin adding more all-purpose flour gradually, just enough so it turns into a soft dough rather than a sticky batter.
How soft should the dough feel before I take it out of the bowl?

It should hold together and pull away enough to handle, but it does not need to be stiff. If it clings heavily to your fingers, add a little more all-purpose flour; if it feels tender and workable, you're ready to knead.
I've floured the counter. How long do I knead it, and what am I looking for?
Turn the dough onto the floured surface and knead until it becomes smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. Add only light dustings of flour as needed so the dough stays soft.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this chilled dessert version, add just the smallest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: Tonight I'm turning Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea into a cold fruit-dessert drink, and I was considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. Which of those warm spices should go in this batch?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: Tonight I'm turning Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea into a cold fruit-dessert drink, and I was considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. Which of those warm spices should go in this batch?
For this chilled dessert version, add just the smallest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Perfect, that's the one I want tonight. I've got a large pot out—what should I measure into it first?
Put 1 pound fresh or frozen cranberries in the pot, then pour in 3 quarts cold water.
The cranberries and water are in. Should I bring it up gently or go straight to boiling?
Bring the pot to a boil, then cook only until the berries pop, which should take about 5 minutes.
They're starting to split open and the liquid is bright red. Do I keep simmering for more flavor?
No, stop once the berries have popped. Take the pot off the heat so the cranberries don't overcook.
Pot is off the burner. Since I'm serving it cold, how long should it sit before I strain it?
Let it stand at room temperature until the liquid is cold; that will take several hours.
While it cools, I want to set up the juices. What amounts do I need ready?
Measure 2 cups orange juice and 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice, and keep the lemon juice and sugar ready for stirring in later.
It's cooled now. Do I press the cranberries through the strainer or just separate them out?
Strain out the cranberries from the liquid; don't worry about forcing them through unless you want a thicker texture.
The liquid is strained and back in the pitcher. How do I finish it before chilling and serving?
Stir the orange juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice, sugar, and that tiny pinch of ginger into the cranberry liquid, then chill it well before serving.
Can you help me make Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon? I've got the salmon, but I want to make sure I'm not missing any prep.

Absolutely. For this recipe, you'll need a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank and 6 salmon fillets, each about 4 ounces. The key early prep is getting that plank soaked well before it goes near the grill.
I have the untreated cedar plank. Does it need a quick rinse, or should it go straight into water?
Submerge the untreated cedar plank fully in water. If it floats, weigh it down with a bowl, can, or heavy plate so the whole plank stays underwater.
Got it weighted down in a container. How long should I leave it there?
Let it soak approximately 12 hours, or overnight. That long soak helps the cedar plank handle the high grill heat without burning too quickly.
While that soaks, what other ingredients should I set aside for the salmon?
Have 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil ready, along with 1 large red onion, chopped. Keep the salmon chilled until you're closer to grilling.
The plank soaked overnight, and I've chopped the red onion. What should I do with the grill?
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat. Give it time to get properly hot before adding the cedar plank.
The grill is heating. Should the plank be dried off first or go on wet?
Let the excess water drip off, but don't dry it completely. Put the prepared plank on the hot grill while it's still damp from soaking.
The plank is on the grill now. Anything I should add before the salmon goes down?
Sprinkle the prepared plank with coarse salt. Once that's on, you're set up for the salmon to pick up the cedar aroma as it cooks.
Can you guide me through making Chocolate Hazelnut Fruit Crepes? I've got a skillet out but haven't started assembling anything.
Absolutely. Set out 4 crepes, 1 cup chocolate hazelnut spread, 4 sliced bananas, and a 1 (7 ounce) can of pressurized whipped cream for serving.
The crepes are on a plate and the bananas are sliced. How much spread goes on each crepe?
Use 1/4 cup of chocolate hazelnut spread on each crepe. Spread it over the surface while leaving just a little room at the edges so it doesn't squeeze out too much when rolled.
Should the banana slices go all over the crepe or in one area?
Arrange 1 sliced banana down the center of each crepe, right over the chocolate hazelnut spread. Keeping the fruit in the middle will make them easier to roll.
They're filled now. Do I fold the sides in or just roll them?
Roll each crepe up around the banana filling. Try to keep the seam tucked underneath so the crepes stay closed when they go into the skillet.
The skillet is on the stove. What heat should I use before I put them in?
Warm the skillet over medium heat, then place the rolled crepes in gently, seam side down if you can.
Do they need to brown, or am I just heating the filling?
You're mainly warming them through. Let the crepes warm in the skillet for about 90 seconds; the spread should soften and the banana should lose the chill without needing a long cook.
They're warm and soft. How should I serve them with the whipped cream?
Move the crepes to plates while they're still warm, then top or serve alongside the pressurized whipped cream. They're ready to eat right away.
I want to make Best Chocolate Chippers, but I'd like you to guide me while I set up. What should be ready on the counter?
Set out 1 cup butter, 1 cup vegetable oil, 1 cup white sugar, and 1 cup packed brown sugar. You'll also need a large mixing bowl and whatever you use for creaming, like a hand mixer or sturdy spoon.
Butter, oil, and both sugars are measured. Should I get the oven going before I mix?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the dough is ready.
The oven is heating, and I've got the large bowl out. Do the butter and oil go in together?
They do. Add the butter, vegetable oil, packed brown sugar, and white sugar to the large bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's starting to come together, but I still see a few buttery streaks. Keep mixing?
Keep going a little longer. You're looking for the fats and sugars to look evenly blended and smooth, with no obvious streaks of butter or dry sugar pockets.
Okay, the mixture looks smooth now. What gets added after the creaming part?
Beat in the eggs and vanilla until they're worked through the creamed mixture.
Eggs and vanilla are mixed in. I'm clearing space for the dry ingredients—what should I combine separately?
Combine the flour, baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt together before adding them to the bowl. That helps the leavening and salt spread evenly through the dough.
The dry mixture is ready. How should I add it without overworking the dough?

Stir the combined flour mixture into the creamed mixture just until it's incorporated. Stop once you don't see dry streaks, and the dough for the Best Chocolate Chippers is ready for the next baking step.
Can you walk me through Cabbage Rolls II? I've got cabbage leaves and cooked rice ready.
Absolutely. You'll need 12 cabbage leaves and 1 cup cooked white rice for the rolls. Keep the rice nearby for the filling.
What should I set out with the rice before I start heating anything?
Set out 1 egg, beaten, and 1/4 cup milk. The filling also gets onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper mixed in with the rice.
Got it. Do I need a big pot for the cabbage leaves?
Yes, use a large pot and bring the water to a boil so the leaves have enough room to soften without crowding.
The leaves are separated. How long do they go in the boiling water?
Boil the cabbage leaves for 2 minutes, then drain them well. They should be flexible enough to roll without tearing.
They're drained and cooling a little on a towel. Should I mix the filling now?
Yes. In a large bowl, combine the 1 cup cooked rice, beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper.
Should the filling be packed tightly into the leaves or kept loose?
Keep it compact enough to hold together, but don't overpack. Spoon about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture into the center of each cabbage leaf.
Once the filling is in the middle, how do I shape the rolls neatly?
Fold the sides in as you roll each cabbage leaf around the filling, tucking in the ends so the rolls stay closed.
Can you guide me through making Cookie Jar Gingersnaps? I've got a large mixing bowl and measuring cups out.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 3/4 cup shortening and 1 cup sugar, since those get creamed together in the bowl.
Shortening and sugar are measured. Do I need the wet ingredients ready before mixing?
Yes, have 1 egg and 1/4 cup molasses nearby so they can go in right after the shortening and sugar are creamed.
All right, the egg and molasses are on the counter. What texture am I looking for when I cream the first two ingredients?
Beat the shortening and sugar in the large mixing bowl until they look well blended and creamy, with the sugar worked evenly through the shortening.
That's looking smooth and lighter now. Should I add the egg by itself or with the molasses?
Add the egg and the molasses, then beat them into the creamed mixture until everything is evenly combined.
The mixture is darker and sticky now. What dry ingredients need to be combined separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt before adding them to the creamed mixture.
I've mixed the dry bowl. Should I dump it in all at once?
Add the dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture, mixing as you go so the dough comes together evenly.
The dough is together and a bit thick. How should I shape the cookies?
Scoop teaspoonfuls of dough and roll each portion into a ball. Once they're all shaped, you'll be ready for the next baking step.
Can you guide me through making Butterscotch Brownies in a Jar? I'm setting up my counter and want to know what to measure out.
Absolutely. For the dry mix, have 2 cups all-purpose flour ready, along with 1 1/2 tablespoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup flaked coconut.
I've got the flour, baking powder, salt, and coconut out. Should I heat the oven before I open the jar mix?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the batter is mixed.
The oven is warming. What pan should I use, and does it need anything before the batter goes in?
Use a 9x13 inch baking pan and grease it well so the brownies release cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. I'm opening the jar now—do I just dump everything into the bowl?
Empty the jar of brownie mix into a large mixing bowl, then stir the dry mix a bit to break up any lumps before adding the wet ingredients.
There are a few clumps in the bowl. I'm breaking them up with a spoon; what should I add next?
Add 3/4 cup softened butter, 2 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract to the bowl.
The butter is soft and the eggs are beaten. How much mixing am I aiming for?
Mix until everything is well blended, scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl so no dry pockets of mix remain.
The batter looks even now. Should I spread it into the prepared pan right away?
Yes, spread the well-blended batter evenly in the greased 9x13 inch pan, then it's ready for the oven once your preheat is complete.
Can you guide me through making Chunky Pizza Dip? I've got a large saucepan out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 minced garlic cloves first. You'll heat those together in the saucepan or a Dutch oven, so keep the tomatoes nearby too.
The garlic is minced and the oil is measured. For the tomato part, what exactly should I open?
Open 2 cans of petite diced tomatoes, 14.5 ounces each, and measure 1/4 cup tomato paste. The tomatoes and paste will go in after the garlic starts sizzling and turning golden.
Should I put the garlic into hot oil, or warm them up together?
Warm them together. Add the olive oil and minced garlic to the pan, then heat until the garlic starts to sizzle and just turns golden. Don't let it brown too deeply.
It's sizzling now and the garlic is lightly golden around the edges. Do the tomatoes go in all at once?
Yes, add the petite diced tomatoes and the tomato paste now. Stir in the basil and oregano as well, then bring the mixture up to a simmer.
It looks a little loose after stirring. Is that okay before it simmers down?
That's fine. Once it reaches a steady simmer, leave it uncovered so moisture can cook off and the sauce can thicken into a dip texture.
How long should I let it go, and what texture am I watching for?
Simmer it uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes. Stir now and then, and look for it to become thick enough that it will cling to a chip, breadstick, or spoon instead of running right off.
It's thickened after about 20 minutes. I'm not serving it immediately—what should I do with it?
Take it off the heat, let it cool, and then refrigerate it. When you're ready to serve, you can rewarm it gently if you want it hot for dipping.
Can you guide me through making Campagnard Sauce? I've got a mixing bowl out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cloves of minced garlic, 1/2 cup goat cheese, 1 minced celery stalk, 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, olive oil, plus salt and pepper for seasoning.
The garlic is minced, and the goat cheese is measured. Should the celery be really fine for this sauce?
Yes, mince the celery fairly fine so it blends smoothly into the sauce instead of leaving large crunchy pieces.
Celery is minced now. Do I add everything to the bowl at once or hold anything back?
Add the garlic, goat cheese, minced celery, balsamic vinegar, and olive oil to the bowl together. Keep the salt and pepper aside for tasting after it's mixed.
The goat cheese is a little firm. Should I mash it before stirring?
That will help. Press it against the side of the bowl with a spoon or spatula, then stir it through the garlic, celery, vinegar, and olive oil until the mixture starts coming together.
It's mixed but still looks a bit chunky from the cheese and celery. Is that okay before seasoning?
That's fine at this point. Season it to taste with salt and pepper, starting lightly, then mix again and adjust if it needs more brightness or savory depth.
I added a small pinch of salt and pepper. How smooth should I make it?
Blend it well until the sauce is smooth. You can use a blender, food processor, or an immersion blender if you want a more even texture.
The sauce is smooth now. I'm not serving it right away—what's the best way to store it?
Cover the sauce and refrigerate it until you're ready to serve. Give it a quick stir after chilling in case it firms up or separates slightly.
Can you guide me through making Anzac Biscuits I? I'm setting out my mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup quick cooking oats, 3/4 cup flaked coconut, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need a small saucepan for melting the syrup and butter.
I've got the oats, coconut, flour, and baking soda on the counter. Should I combine the dry ingredients in the bowl?
Yes. Add the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut to the mixing bowl, then stir them together so the coconut and oats are evenly distributed.
The dry mix looks even. I have the small saucepan ready—what goes in there?
Set the saucepan over low heat and melt the syrup and butter together gently, stirring as they loosen and combine.
The butter has melted into the syrup. The mixture is smooth and warm.
Great. In a separate cup or small bowl, mix the baking soda with boiling water, then pour that into the melted butter and syrup.
It foamed a little when I added the soda mixture. Is that okay?
Yes, that's expected. Give it a quick stir so the soda mixture is blended through the butter and syrup.
All mixed. Should I pour it straight into the oats and flour mixture?
Yes, add the warm butter mixture to the dry ingredients. Stir until everything is moistened and the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut are evenly coated.
The mixture is combined and smells good. Anything else before I portion them?
That completes the recipe steps you've listed: the butter mixture is incorporated into the dry ingredients, so you're ready to shape or portion the biscuit mixture as your baking setup calls for.
Can you guide me through making Fig Bars II? I'm setting things out now and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Start by getting the main measured ingredients ready: 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder.
I've got the sugar and eggs on the counter. Should I start heating the oven before I measure the flour?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is mixed.
Oven is heating. What pan should I use for these bars?
Use a 9x13 inch baking pan. Grease it well, then dust it with flour so the bars release more easily after baking.
The pan is greased and floured. For the batter, do the eggs and sugar go together first?
They do. Put the 3 eggs and 1 cup white sugar in a large bowl and beat them until the mixture looks thick and pale.
It's lighter now, but I'm not sure if it's thick enough. What should I be looking for?
Look for a noticeably paler color and a little more body than plain beaten eggs. It should fall from the beaters in a soft ribbon rather than looking thin and watery.
That makes sense. I measured the 7/8 cup flour and the baking powder. Do they go straight in?
Sift the flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder together first. The recipe also calls for salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice to be sifted with them before adding the dry mixture.
Okay, the dry ingredients are sifted. How do I combine everything without knocking it down too much?

Blend the sifted dry ingredients into the egg-sugar mixture gently, just until they're incorporated, and add the vanilla along with them. Once the batter is even, it's ready for the prepared 9x13 inch pan.
Can you guide me through Crawfish Etouffee III? I'm setting a large saucepan on the stove now.
Absolutely. For the base, have 1 chopped onion ready, plus 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed tomato soup and 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup.
I've got the onion and both 10.75 ounce soup cans. Is there another can I should open before the pan gets hot?
Yes—open 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers. Once that's ready, warm the large saucepan over medium heat.
The pan is on medium and the onion is chopped. Do I add oil or just start with the onion?
The recipe just says to sauté the chopped onion in the large saucepan over medium heat until it turns clear, so add the onion and cook it gently, stirring as it softens.
The onion is looking translucent now, and the pan smells sweet. Should I pour in everything canned at once?
Go ahead and add the condensed tomato soup, the condensed cream of mushroom soup, and the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers. Stir until the soups loosen and the mixture looks evenly combined.
It's all mixed together, but it's pretty thick. How long should this part bubble before the crawfish goes in?
Let that sauce simmer for 15 minutes. Keep the heat steady enough for gentle bubbling, and stir now and then so the thick soup base doesn't stick.
I'm about 10 minutes into that simmer and it's starting to look smoother. Should the lid be on?
You can leave it uncovered and keep stirring occasionally. The main goal is simply to give the tomato soup, mushroom soup, tomatoes, chiles, and onion time to meld during the 15 minutes.
The 15 minutes are up. I have the crawfish ready next to the stove—what's the final timing?
Place the crawfish into the pan, stir it through the sauce, and let everything simmer for 25 minutes. Keep it at a gentle simmer so the crawfish heats through without the sauce scorching.
Can you walk me through Baked Fettuccine Lasagna? I've got a big pot and skillet ready, but I want to make sure I prep the ingredients in the right order.

Absolutely. Set out 12 ounces dry fettuccine pasta, 1 pound lean ground beef if you're using it, 1 cup chopped onion, and 1 cup chopped red bell pepper. You'll also want a colander nearby for draining the pasta.
The fettuccine is measured, and I'm using the beef. Should I chop the onion and red bell pepper before starting the water?
Yes, go ahead and chop the onion and red bell pepper now so each is ready at 1 cup. Once they're prepped, fill the large pot, lightly salt the water, and bring it to a boil.
The onion and pepper are chopped, and the salted water is heating. How do I handle the pasta once it boils?
When the water reaches a steady boil, add the fettuccine and cook it for 8 to 10 minutes, checking near the end so it's al dente rather than soft. Drain it well in the colander.
I put the pasta in. While it cooks, can I start the beef, or should I wait until the noodles are drained?
You can start the beef while the pasta cooks if you're comfortable watching both. Put the large skillet over medium heat and brown the 1 pound lean ground beef, breaking it up as it cooks.
The beef is in the skillet, and the pasta has about a minute left. What texture should I look for before draining the noodles?
Taste a strand: it should be tender but still have a slight bite in the center. If it's there, drain the fettuccine right away so it doesn't keep softening in the hot water.
The fettuccine is drained, and the beef is browned. There's some fat in the pan—what should I do with it?
Carefully drain the fat from the skillet. Once the fat is removed, transfer the browned meat to a bowl so it's ready for the next part of the lasagna assembly.
The meat is in a bowl now. Should the chopped onion and red bell pepper stay separate for the moment?

Yes, keep the 1 cup chopped onion and 1 cup chopped red bell pepper ready on the side. At this point you've completed the listed prep: pasta boiled and drained, beef browned over medium heat, fat drained, and meat transferred to a bowl.
Can you help me make Festive Shortbread Logs? I've got a mixing bowl out but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar first; those will get creamed together in the bowl.
The butter is soft and the sugar is measured. Are there any other ingredients I should put on the counter before mixing?
Yes—have 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and 2 cups all-purpose flour ready so you can add them smoothly once the butter and sugar are combined.
I'm using a hand mixer. How should the butter and confectioners' sugar look when they're creamed?
Beat them in the mixing bowl until the mixture looks smooth and lighter, with the sugar worked evenly into the softened butter.
That's looking pale and creamy. Do I pour in the vanilla all at once?
Yes, add the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract all at once, then mix just until it's blended through the butter-sugar mixture.
Vanilla is mixed in. The flour is measured, but I don't want a mess—how do I add it?
Add the 2 cups all-purpose flour gradually, mixing as you go. Keep the speed low at first, then mix well once the flour starts to disappear into the dough.
The dough is coming together and feels soft. Should I flour the counter or my hands for shaping?
Lightly flour your hands rather than heavily flouring the dough. Scoop tablespoonfuls of batter and shape them into cookie logs or cookies with your hands.
I've shaped a few tablespoon-sized pieces. Should they all be about the same size?
Yes, keeping each portion close to a tablespoonful will help them look even and bake more consistently. Once they're shaped, place them on your baking surface with a little space between each one.
I want to make Banana Chip Muffins I, but I'd like to get the dry ingredients organized before I start. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and measure in 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour and 1/2 cup white sugar.
Flour and sugar are in the bowl. Which small amounts should I measure next?
Add 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt to that same large bowl.
Those are measured. I noticed the directions mention chocolate chips too—do they go in with the dry mix?
Yes. Measure the chocolate chips into the large bowl along with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Everything dry is in the big bowl. Should I stir it a lot or just lightly combine it?
Mix it thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly distributed, then make a well in the center of the dry ingredients.
The well is made. What tool should I use for the egg?
Use a small bowl for the egg, and beat it until it looks frothy.
The egg is foamy now. I have the bananas, milk, and cooking oil ready beside it.
Good. Mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the beaten egg mixture.
The wet mixture is together. Should I pour it into the well I made in the dry bowl?
Yes, that well is ready for the wet mixture. Pour it in when you're ready to combine the muffin batter.
Can you guide me through making Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts? I want to get the ingredients organized before I start.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup water for the syrup components.
Sugar and water are on the counter. Are there any flavorings I should measure now?
Yes—measure 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice and 2 tablespoons orange flower water so they're ready when you need them.
Got it. For the almond prep, what size pot should I use?
Use a pot roomy enough for 6 cups of water, then bring those 6 cups of water to a boil.
The water is boiling. Do I keep it on the heat when the almonds go in?
Take the pot off the heat first, then add the almonds to the hot water.
They're in the pot. How long should they sit before I handle them?
Let the almonds soak in the water for about 5 minutes; after that, drain them and peel off the skins.
I've peeled them. Should I dry them with a towel or use the oven?
Spread the almonds out on baking sheets and use the oven to dry them. Bake at 200 degrees F, or 95 degrees C, until they're completely dry and toasted.
How will I know they're ready to come out?
They should look dry all the way through and lightly toasted, with no dampness left on the baking sheets. Let them cool before moving on with the tart preparation.
Can you guide me through the Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart? I'm starting with the crust ingredients and want to get the dry mix right.
Absolutely. Set out a bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, and measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour with 1 tablespoon light brown sugar.
I've got the flour and brown sugar measured. What smaller seasonings go in with them?
Add 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/8 teaspoon salt to the same bowl so all the dry ingredients are together.
Should I just stir those, or is sifting important here?
Sift them together in the bowl: the flour, light brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt. That helps break up the sugar and spreads the cinnamon evenly.
The dry ingredients look even now. I have cold butter nearby—what texture am I aiming for?
Cut in the butter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. Use a pastry cutter, two knives, or your fingertips, and stop before it turns into a paste.
Some bits are pea-sized and some are sandy. Is that okay before I add water?
Yes, that's the right range for coarse crumbs. Keep the butter pieces visible enough to make the crust tender.
I'm ready for the ice water. How should I add it so I don't make the dough gummy?
Sprinkle the ice water over the crumbly mixture, then toss it with a fork until it's evenly moistened. Use a light hand rather than stirring hard.
It's starting to clump when I press it, but it's not a smooth dough. What do I do before chilling or filling?
That's fine. Pat the mixture into a round, then wrap it in plastic so it holds together and doesn't dry out.
Can you guide me through Country Fried Chicken? I'm setting up my counter and want to measure the dry coating correctly.
Absolutely. For the coating, measure 1/3 cup all-purpose flour into a large resealable plastic bag.
The flour is in the bag. Which seasonings go in with it?
Add 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika to the bag with the flour.
Those are measured. Should I mix the bag now or prep the wet bowl first?
Go ahead and seal the bag and shake it lightly so the flour, garlic salt, pepper, and paprika are evenly combined.
The coating looks evenly speckled. I have a shallow bowl ready—what goes there?
Beat the egg and milk together in that shallow bowl until the mixture looks smooth and blended.
The egg and milk are mixed. How many pieces of chicken should I coat at once?
Add the chicken to the seasoned flour bag a few pieces at a time, then seal and shake until each piece is coated.
I've got the first batch coated in flour. Does it go straight back in the bag or into the egg mixture next?
Dip each floured piece into the egg-and-milk mixture so it's moistened on all sides.
They're dipped and a little wet. How do I get the final coating on without making a mess?
Return the dipped chicken pieces to the flour mixture in the bag and shake again to build the second coating before cooking.
Can you guide me through making churros? I've got a small saucepan out but want to measure everything before heating.

Absolutely. Measure 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. Keep the flour nearby too, since you'll stir it in once the hot mixture comes off the heat.
The water, sugar, salt, and oil are measured. Should they all go into the saucepan together?
Yes. Put the 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil into the small saucepan, then set it over medium heat.
They're in the pan over medium heat. Am I just warming it or looking for a full boil?
Bring it to a boil. Once it reaches a boil, take the saucepan off the heat right away.
It boiled and I moved it off the burner. The surface has settled down—when does the flour go in?
Stir in the flour now while the mixture is still hot. Mix until it comes together and forms a ball.
It's thickening, but some floury streaks are still showing. Should I keep stirring?
Keep stirring until the dough looks unified and pulls together into one ball. You don't need to cook it further on the burner for this step.
The dough is in a ball. I'm setting up to fry—what temperature should the oil be?
Heat the frying oil in a deep-fryer or deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
I'm using a deep skillet. Any quick check before I start frying the churros?
Make sure the oil is steady at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), the skillet has enough depth for frying, and the dough is ready to shape before you begin.
Can you help me make Almond Buttercrunch? I want to get my ingredients and pan set up before I turn on the stove.

Absolutely. Set out 3/4 cup butter, 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup chopped almonds, and 2 cups milk chocolate chips. You'll also want a saucepan and a large cookie sheet that's been buttered before the hot candy is ready.
I've got the butter, sugar, almonds, and chocolate chips measured. Should the cookie sheet be buttered now or later?
Butter the large cookie sheet now. Once the buttercrunch reaches temperature, you'll need to pour it out right away, so it's best to have the sheet ready beside the stove.
Cookie sheet is ready. What goes into the saucepan?
Put the butter, the 2 cups white sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds into the saucepan. Keep the heat low while they combine.
The butter is starting to melt into the sugar and almonds. Do I keep stirring?
Yes, stir constantly while the mixture comes up to a boil. Keep it moving until it boils, but once it reaches a boil, stop stirring and don't shake the pan.
It's boiling now, and I've stopped stirring. What should I watch for from here?

Let it continue heating without stirring until it reaches 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. If you're checking without relying only on a thermometer, a little syrup dropped into cold water should form hard, brittle threads.
I have cold water ready and the thermometer is climbing. Is the hard-thread check supposed to be crisp right away?
Yes. When a small amount hits the cold water, it should set into hard, brittle threads rather than staying soft or bendy. That matches the 300 to 310 degrees F range.
It's at temperature and the cold-water bit turned brittle. How do I get it onto the sheet safely?

Carefully pour the hot mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet right away. Keep your hands clear of the syrup, tilt the saucepan steadily, and let the buttercrunch spread out on the prepared sheet.
Can you help me make Apple Butter V? I've got a big pile of tart apples and want to do it right.
Absolutely. For this recipe you'll need 6 pounds tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups apple cider. Have a Dutch oven ready too, since the apples start there.
The apples are cored and sliced, and I have the cider. What should I measure out before I start cooking?
Measure 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon. Keep them nearby; the first cooking stage is focused on softening the apples with the cider.
Okay, the Dutch oven is on the counter. Do the apples go in dry, or should I add liquid first?
Put the sliced apples into the Dutch oven first. Once they're in, pour in the 6 cups apple cider so the fruit can cook down evenly.
They're in the pot with the cider. Should I stir them before turning on the heat?
A quick stir is fine to settle everything, then bring the mixture to a boil. After it reaches a boil, cook it over medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
When you say soft, am I looking for them to fall apart or just be tender?
They should be soft enough to mash or press easily. If the slices still feel firm after 30 minutes, keep them on medium heat a little longer until they give way.
The apples are really tender now and the pot smells like cider. What tool do I need next?
Set up a food mill. Carefully ladle or transfer the softened apple-and-cider mixture into it, working in batches if that's easier.
Got it. Should I include all the cooked liquid when I run it through the food mill?
Yes, press the softened mixture through the food mill so the cooked apples and cider become smooth. Then you'll be ready to continue with the sugar and cinnamon you measured earlier.
Can you help me cook Blackened Tuna tonight? I've got tuna steaks but want to make sure I handle the timing right.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 pounds fresh tuna steaks, about 1 inch thick, plus 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 tablespoons butter.
The tuna steaks are about 1 inch thick, and I found the Cajun seasoning. Should I season them before the pan is hot?
Yes. Generously coat the tuna all over with the Cajun seasoning so the surface is well covered before it goes into the skillet.
They're coated. What pan setup should I use?
Use a large skillet and put in the 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter. Heat them together over high heat.
The butter is melting fast. Am I waiting for bubbling or smoke?
Keep it on high heat until the oil is nearly smoking. That very hot pan is what helps blacken the outside.
It's just starting to smoke. Do I lay the steaks in carefully one at a time?
Yes, place the tuna steaks in the pan carefully in a single layer. Try not to move them once they hit the skillet.
They're sizzling hard. How long do I leave the first side?
Cook on one side for 3 to 4 minutes, or until that side is blackened.
The surface looks dark and crusted after about 4 minutes. Should I keep cooking this side longer?
No, if it's blackened, that side has done its job. Take it off that side rather than continuing to cook it there, and serve while it's hot.
Can you help me make Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.

Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup margarine, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup molasses, and 1 egg yolk. You'll also need the dry ingredients from the recipe ready nearby: flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg.
The margarine is a little soft already, and I measured the sugar. Should those go in the large bowl together?
Yes. Put the margarine and sugar into the large bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth, with no obvious streaks of margarine.
It's smoothing out but still looks a bit grainy from the sugar. Is that okay for this stage?
That's fine as long as the margarine and sugar are evenly combined. Scrape the sides of the bowl once, then mix just until it looks cohesive and creamy.
Okay, the bowl is scraped and the mixture looks even. I have the molasses measured and the egg separated.
Pour in the 1/2 cup molasses and add the 1 egg yolk. Stir them into the creamed mixture until the color is even and the yolk is fully blended in.
The molasses mixture is smooth now. For the dry ingredients, should I mix the spices with the flour before adding them?
Yes, combine the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg together first so the leavening and spices are distributed evenly.
I've whisked the dry ingredients together. Do I dump them all in, or add them gradually?
Add the dry mixture into the molasses mixture and blend until the dough is smooth. If it feels easier to control, add it in portions, but keep mixing only until everything is incorporated.
The dough has come together and looks smooth. It's a little soft and sticky—what should I do before cutting shapes?
Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. That rest will firm it up so it's easier to roll and cut into gingerbread men.
I want to make Easy Pot Roast today. Can you guide me without getting too far ahead?

Absolutely. Set out a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast, 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. You'll also want a medium sized oven bag.
The roast is out, and I found the oven bag. Should I heat the oven before prepping the meat?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the roast is bagged.
Oven is heating. The top of the roast has a fat cap—do I just leave it and score through it?
Score the roast on the top and sides with shallow cuts. You don't need to remove the fat cap; just make cuts across the surface so the seasoning liquid can reach the meat better.
Done. Should the roast go straight into the bag now, or do I mix the liquid first?
Place the scored roast in the medium sized oven bag first, then mix the sauce separately so it pours evenly.
I've got a bowl ready. What exactly goes into the sauce?
Combine the 2 cups water, the 1 ounce package of dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. Stir until the soup mix is mostly dispersed.
The mixture looks a little cloudy and speckled from the soup mix. Is that okay?
That's fine. Pour the mixture over the roast in the oven bag, aiming to coat the top and let the liquid collect around the meat.
I also have vegetables for the pan. Where should they go so they cook with the roast?

Arrange the vegetables around the meat in the oven bag, keeping the roast centered. Once everything is in place, close the bag according to its directions and set it in the oven-safe dish for roasting.
I want to make Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken today. Can you guide me without rushing? I'm starting by clearing the counter.
Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl, a spoon or whisk, a brush, and a lightly oiled 9x13 inch baking dish. For the glaze, you'll need 1/2 cup ketchup and 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice.
I've got the bowl and baking dish ready, and the ketchup and pineapple juice are measured. What else goes into the glaze?
Measure 4 tablespoons molasses and 2 tablespoons dark rum. Keep mustard and garlic nearby too, since they get mixed into the glaze even though the amounts aren't listed here.
The molasses is thick, but it's measured. Should I combine everything in the bowl now?
Yes. Add the ketchup, unsweetened pineapple juice, molasses, dark rum, mustard, and garlic to the medium bowl. Stir slowly at first so the molasses loosens into the thinner ingredients.
It's looking glossy but a little streaky. Is that okay, or should it be completely smooth?
Keep mixing until the color looks even and the molasses is fully blended. Then season the glaze with salt and pepper to taste.
I added salt and pepper. The chicken pieces are still on a plate—should I prep the dish before moving them?
Yes, make sure the 9x13 inch baking dish is lightly oiled, then place the chicken pieces in it in a single layer if you can.
They fit in the dish. Do I pour the glaze over them or brush it on?
Brush both sides of the chicken pieces with the prepared glaze, using about 1/2 of the glaze for this marinating stage. Save the remaining glaze separately.
Both sides are coated, and I saved the rest of the glaze. How long does this need to sit before cooking later?
Cover the baking dish and refrigerate the chicken to marinate for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if you want a deeper flavor.
Can you help me make Beet and Pear Puree? I'm setting up my counter now and want to be sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Pull together 8 medium beets, 1 pound unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, and 4 Bosc pears that are peeled, cored, and minced.
I have the beets and butter out. Should I prep the pears and onions before the oven goes on?
Yes, that's a good use of time. Mince the Vidalia onions, then peel, core, and mince the Bosc pears. While you're doing that, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
The oven is heating, and the pears are already browning a little where I cut them. Is that a problem for the puree?
A little browning is fine here since they'll be cooked into the puree. Keep them together in a bowl while you get the beets ready.
For the beets, do I peel them before roasting or just wash them?
For this recipe, wash the beets well and place them in a roasting pan. You don't need to peel them before they go into the oven.
They're in the roasting pan. How long should I plan for, and how do I know when they're done?
Bake the beets for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until they're tender. Check by piercing one with a knife; it should slide in without much resistance.
The knife goes in easily now. They're hot, though—do I keep going right away?
Set the roasted beets aside to cool before handling them further. That makes the next prep safer and less messy.
While the beets cool, should I start the skillet with the butter?
Yes. Melt the 1 pound unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat, then you'll be ready for the minced Vidalia onions and pears when the recipe continues.
Can you guide me through Crawfish Etouffee III? I'm setting out the cans and a large saucepan now.

Absolutely. Have the chopped onion ready, plus 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed tomato soup, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup, and 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers.
The onion is chopped, and I found both 10.75 ounce soup cans. Should the pan be heating yet?
Yes, put the large saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté it until it turns clear.
The onion is in the pan. About how clear should it look before I add anything else?
It should look softened and translucent rather than browned. Once it reaches that point, you're ready to add the canned ingredients.
Okay, the onion looks translucent. I've got the tomato soup, mushroom soup, and the tomatoes with green chile peppers open.

Pour in the condensed tomato soup, the condensed cream of mushroom soup, and the 10 ounce can of diced tomatoes with green chile peppers. Stir everything together so the onion is evenly mixed through the sauce.
It's all combined, but the soups are pretty thick. Should I keep stirring while it heats?
Give it a good stir as it warms, then let the mixture simmer gently for 15 minutes. Keep the heat moderate so it bubbles lightly instead of boiling hard.
The sauce has been simmering for 15 minutes and smells good. When do the crawfish go in?
Add the crawfish to the pan now, stirring gently so they're coated in the sauce.
The crawfish are mixed in. How long should I let everything cook together?
Let the crawfish simmer in the sauce for 25 minutes. Stir occasionally, then serve the etouffee hot once that simmer is done.
I want to make Empanadas, but I'm starting with the dough today. Can you guide me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 package of cream cheese, the 3 ounce size. Those two need to be soft enough to cream together smoothly.
The butter is softened and the cream cheese is on the counter. What else belongs on the counter?
You'll also need 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour and 1 cup fruit preserves. The preserves can wait until you're ready to use the dough, but it's good to confirm you have them.
I've got the flour sifted. Should I use a bowl and mixer for the butter and cream cheese?
Yes, use a mixing bowl and a hand mixer or sturdy spoon. Cream the softened butter and cream cheese together until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It's smooth now, with no obvious streaks. Do I add the flour all at once?
Beat in the 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour. Add it steadily and mix just until it's incorporated into a dough.
The dough has come together, but it's soft. Is that okay before chilling?
That's fine. Shape the dough into a smooth ball, then wrap it well in foil or cling wrap so it doesn't dry out in the refrigerator.
Wrapped and ready. How long does it need to chill before I bake with it?
Refrigerate the wrapped dough overnight. If needed, you can keep it chilled for up to a week before using it.
When I'm ready to bake, should I work with it straight from the fridge or let it sit?
Take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it. That gives it time to soften enough to handle while still staying chilled.
Can you help me make Fresh Apple Cake? I've got my mixing bowl out and want to be sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups vegetable oil and 2 cups white sugar first; those will get beaten into the wet mixture.
Oil and sugar are measured. Do the eggs go in whole, or should I prep them somehow before mixing?
Beat 3 eggs before adding them. Also measure 2 teaspoons vanilla extract so it's ready to go in with the oil, eggs, and sugar.
The eggs are beaten and the vanilla is measured. What should I do with the oven while I'm setting up the pan?
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C, so it's hot when the batter is ready.
Oven is heating. I have a few pans here—what pan does this cake need?
Use 1 10 inch tube pan, and grease it well so the apple cake releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. Should I combine the wet ingredients by hand, or is a mixer better?
Either works, but beat together the vegetable oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar until the mixture looks evenly blended.
That mixture looks smooth and glossy. What dry ingredients should I get ready next?
Sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a separate bowl to break up lumps and distribute the spices evenly.
I've sifted the dry bowl. Anything I should check before I move on with the batter?

Make sure the oven is still at 325 degrees F and the 10 inch tube pan is greased. You should have the wet mixture beaten and the sifted flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg ready to combine next.

I want to make Brandy Flamed Peppercorn Steak tonight. Can you guide me without rushing it?

Absolutely. Set out 3 tablespoons crushed black peppercorns, 2 beef top sirloin steaks that are 8 ounces each, 1 tablespoon lemon pepper, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a large skillet for the stovetop.
The steaks are on a board and I've got the peppercorns crushed. Should I season them right away?
Yes. Press the crushed black peppercorns firmly into both sides of each steak so they cling to the surface instead of just sitting loosely on top.
Some pepper is falling off when I lift the steaks. Is that okay?
A little fallout is fine. Just press again with the flat of your hand and aim for an even pepper crust on both sides before adding the next seasonings.
Okay, the pepper crust looks fairly even. Where do the lemon pepper and salt go?
Sprinkle the steaks with the 1 tablespoon lemon pepper and the 1 teaspoon salt, coating both sides as evenly as you can.
Seasoning is done. I have the large skillet ready—what heat should I use?

Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour. That rest will firm it up and make it easier to handle when you're ready for the next stage.

Spoon the white sugar into the clean jar first. Try to level it out so the layer looks even through the glass.

Press the layers firmly in place. You want the contents compact enough that they won't shift much when the jar is moved.

Write: "In a large bowl, beat 1 egg with 1 cup softened butter or margarine until light and fluffy." Attach that card securely to the jar so the baker has the next step with the mix.

Use a large mixing bowl. Empty the jar of brownie mix into it, then stir through the dry mixture to break up any lumps before adding the wet ingredients.
