Stir just until the dry mix is loosened and the lumps are broken apart. The coconut can still be visible; you mainly want the flour mixture evenly loosened.

Yes. Add the 3/4 cup softened butter, the 2 beaten eggs, and the 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract to the bowl, then mix until everything is well blended.

A thick brownie batter is fine. Once it's well blended with no dry pockets, spread it into the greased 9x13 inch pan and keep the oven at 375 degrees F, or 190 degrees C.

Yes. Add the milk and egg to the bowl, then beat on low speed until the mixture looks smooth. Keep the speed low so the flour stays in the bowl and the dough base comes together evenly.

That's the point where you start stirring in the remaining flour gradually. Add enough of it to form a soft dough rather than dumping in all the flour automatically.

It should pull together into a dough that's soft and workable, not dry or stiff. If it's still very sticky, add a little more of the reserved flour; if it holds its shape, stop there.
The dough is holding together now. What do I do on the counter?
Lightly flour the surface, turn the dough out onto it, and knead until it becomes smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. Use small dustings of flour only as needed to keep it from sticking.

Season them with salt, then mash the potatoes with a fork until they're broken down and fairly even. Keep the flour, beaten egg, and olive oil nearby for the next stage, and when you plate later, use your usual centered soft garnish with the crisp crescent.

Before I open anything, what should be on the counter for the roast itself?

Set out the 4 pounds boneless chuck roast, 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. You'll also want a medium sized oven bag and the vegetables you plan to arrange around the meat.
I have the chuck roast and the oven bag out. Should I warm the oven now or wait until the sauce is mixed?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, while you prep the roast and liquid mixture.
Perfect—that shaped topping is the look I want for this kind of dish; the top shouldn't look like it was dusted evenly everywhere.
Understood. Keep that final garnish concentrated and intentional. For the next prep move, score the roast across the top and sides, then place it into the medium sized oven bag.
When you say score it, am I cutting deep slits or just marking the surface?
Make shallow cuts on the top and sides—enough to open the surface a bit, not deep pockets. Once it's scored, settle the roast inside the oven bag without tearing the bag.
The roast is in the bag. How do I make the liquid so the soup mix doesn't clump?

Combine the 2 cups water with the dry onion and mushroom soup mix, then stir in the 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. Whisk or stir until the mix is mostly dispersed, then pour that mixture over the roast in the bag.
The liquid is poured over it. I have carrots and potatoes ready—where should they go?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag, keeping them tucked along the sides rather than piled on top so the roast stays exposed to the seasoned liquid.
So after the vegetables are around it, I'm basically ready to close things up and cook?

Yes. With the vegetables arranged around the meat and the liquid in the bag, close the oven bag according to its directions and get it into the 350 degrees F oven. When you serve, bring back that centered soft garnish with the crisp crescent so the finish matches the style you wanted.
I'm making Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf and have a skillet and loaf pan ready. Can you guide me through the prep?
Absolutely. Start by getting the main ingredients set out: 12 ounces chopped raw bacon, 1 small white onion chopped, 5 button mushrooms chopped, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef.
The bacon is chopped, but I'm still cutting the onion and mushrooms. Should I heat the oven while I do that?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, while you finish chopping.
Oven is heating. For the bacon, should I use the skillet now or wait until the vegetables are ready?
Use the skillet now. Put the chopped raw bacon in the skillet and cook it over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the pieces are browned.
The bacon is sizzling and there's a lot of grease. What texture am I looking for before I pull it?
Look for browned pieces with some crisp edges, not pale or rubbery. Once it reaches that point, lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon.
I have a plate out. Should I drain it there or put something under it?
Line the plate with paper towels, then transfer the bacon onto the paper towels so the extra grease can drain off.
Bacon is draining. The skillet still has quite a bit of bacon grease in it—how much stays?
Carefully discard the excess grease and leave only 1 tablespoon of bacon grease in the skillet.
Got it down to about 1 tablespoon. Do I add the onion, mushrooms, and beef yet?

You've completed the listed setup steps: oven preheated, bacon browned and drained, and the skillet reserved with 1 tablespoon of bacon grease. Keep the chopped onion, chopped mushrooms, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef ready for the next meatloaf steps.

I'm making Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version tonight. Can you help me get set up before I touch the pork?
Absolutely. Put out 6 center cut pork chops trimmed of any visible fat, plus 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt.
The chops are trimmed, and I have the garlic powder and seasoning salt. Do I need anything for coating them?

Rinse the pork chops, then pat them dry really well with paper towels. Once they're dry, season them with the garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste.

Work one chop at a time: dredge it lightly in flour, dip it into the beaten egg mixture, then coat it liberally with bread crumbs.

Yes, shake off loose flour so the egg mixture clings instead of turning pasty. Then press the bread crumbs on generously so the coating covers the pork well.
All 6 chops are breaded. Anything I should check before they go toward the oven?
Make sure each chop has an even bread-crumb coating and the oven has reached 350 degrees F. Then you're ready to continue baking them according to the recipe.

I'm making Garlic Chicken Stir Fry and I've got a wok out. Can you talk me through the prep before I turn on the heat?

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep the chicken nearby too, since it goes in once the aromatics have cooked.
I minced all 6 cloves, but the cooking step only mentions 2 cloves going into the hot oil. Should I start with just those?

Yes, use 2 cloves of the minced garlic when the oil starts to smoke, along with the grated ginger, chopped green onions, and salt. Keep the rest of the minced garlic aside so you don't overcrowd that quick aromatic step.
Got it. The green onions are chopped and the ginger is grated. How hot should the wok be before the oil goes in?
Put the wok or large skillet over high heat, then add the 2 tablespoons peanut oil and let it heat until it just begins to smoke. That's your cue to move quickly.
The oil is shimmering and I'm seeing the first little wisps of smoke.
Stir in the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped bunch of green onions, and salt right away. Keep everything moving so the garlic perfumes the oil without burning.

Stir-fry them until the onion pieces look translucent, about 2 minutes. They should soften and turn glossy, but you don't want the garlic to get dark.
The onions are glossy now and it's been about 2 minutes. The chicken is ready beside the stove.
Add the chicken to the wok and stir constantly so it gets coated in the garlic, ginger, green onion mixture. Cook until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes.
The chicken pieces are no longer pink on the outside after about 3 minutes. Is that the stopping point for this recipe?
For the listed steps, yes: once the chicken is opaque, the Garlic Chicken Stir Fry is done. Give it one final toss in the wok, then serve it hot while the aromatics are still bright.

I want to make Fruited Ice Cream today. Can you help me get set up with the ingredients and ice cream maker?
Absolutely. Set out your ice cream maker's freezer canister, then measure 2 (14 ounce) cans sweetened condensed milk and 5 cups milk.
The canister is ready, and I have the condensed milk and milk measured. What else should be on the counter?
Add 2 cups heavy cream and 2 tablespoons vanilla extract to the lineup. You'll also need the salt and fruit called for in the recipe, though the amounts aren't specified here.
I have the cream and vanilla. Should I mix this in a bowl first or put everything straight into the freezer canister?
Put everything straight into the freezer canister: the condensed milk, milk, cream, vanilla, salt, and fruit. Stir gently so the milks and cream are evenly combined.

It should look creamy and well blended, with the fruit distributed throughout. If any condensed milk is sitting on the bottom, scrape and stir until it's incorporated.

Yes. Lock in the canister and freeze the ice cream according to your ice cream maker manufacturer's directions.

Serve it right away for a soft-serve texture, or transfer it to a freezer-safe container and freeze until firmer. Scrape the canister clean before the ice cream hardens onto the sides.

Have 3 1/2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, and 2 cups shredded coconut ready. The draining you already did is the big thing for keeping the texture creamy instead of loose.
I've got a big bowl out. Do the oranges and pineapple go in before the whipped topping?
Yes. Add the drained mandarin oranges and drained crushed pineapple to the large bowl, then spoon in the thawed whipped topping.
The whipped topping is soft enough to scoop. Should I stir hard or fold it?
Fold gently so the oranges stay mostly intact and the whipped topping stays fluffy. Once the fruit is coated, add the shredded coconut.
The coconut is in. The recipe also mentions marshmallows and milk—when do those join the bowl?
Add the marshmallows and milk with the fruit, whipped topping, and coconut in that same large bowl, then mix everything together well until it looks evenly combined.
It's mixed and looks creamy with the coconut spread through it. How long should it sit before I serve it?
Cover the bowl and chill it for 1 hour before serving. That short rest helps the flavors come together and firms the salad up a bit.
After the 1 hour chill, should I stir it again or just scoop it into a serving dish?
Give it a gentle stir, transfer it to your serving bowl if you like, and garnish with cherries right before serving.
I'm making Eclairs II and want to set up before I turn on the stove. What should I pull out?
Get 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a medium saucepan, a cookie sheet, and something to grease it with.
The ingredients are on the counter. Does the oven need to start heating before I work on the pan?
Yes, set the oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C, so it can preheat while you handle the cookie sheet and saucepan.
Oven is set. For the cookie sheet, do I just lightly grease the surface?
That's right. Grease the cookie sheet so the eclair dough won't stick when it bakes.
Cookie sheet is ready. I've got the medium saucepan on the burner but it's still off.
Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to the medium saucepan before turning up the heat.
Butter and water are in the pan. Should I add the flour and salt yet?
Hold the 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt for later. For now, focus on heating the butter and water together.
The butter is starting to soften around the edges. How active should the boil be?
Bring the butter and water mixture to a boil, stirring as it heats so the butter melts completely into the water.
It's bubbling now and I'm stirring. I still see a small piece of butter.
Keep stirring until that last bit of butter disappears completely, then you'll be ready for the next part of the recipe.

Perfect, that's exactly how I want to handle this one. I've got the container plan set—what food prep should I tackle first?
Get the fruit ready first: peel, core, and thinly slice 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples, then measure out 3/4 cup cranberries.
The apples are sliced and the cranberries are measured. Which small ingredients should I pull over next?
Bring over 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. You'll be mixing those with the fruit shortly.
Those are on the counter. Should I prep the pan and oven before mixing the filling?
Yes—heat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, and butter an 8 inch square baking dish.
The dish is buttered and the oven is warming. Do I combine everything in the baking dish or use a bowl?
Use a large bowl first. Mix together the sliced apples, cranberries, white sugar, cinnamon, and the nutmeg called for in the directions.
The fruit mixture smells great. How should it look before it goes into the pan?
Aim for the apple slices and cranberries to be evenly coated with the sugar and spices, with no dry clumps sitting at the bottom of the bowl.
It's evenly coated now. How do I transfer it without making one side too packed?
Tip the mixture into the buttered 8 inch square baking dish and spread it into an even layer, nudging the fruit into the corners.
Fruit layer is even. What do I do with the bowl before I clean up?
Use that same bowl to combine the oats, flour, and brown sugar, just as the recipe directs.
I'm making Atomic Canuck Chili and I've got the slow cooker out. Can you help me stage the ingredients before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 pounds lean ground beef and 1/2 large onion, diced. You'll brown those together in a large skillet before they go into the slow cooker.
The beef and diced onion are ready. What seasonings should I have beside the skillet?
Keep 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper and 3 tablespoons garlic powder within reach, plus seasoned pepper for the browning step.
Skillet is on the burner. What heat should I use, and do the spices go in right away?
Use medium heat. Add the ground beef, diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper to the large skillet, then cook until the beef is browned.
The beef is browned and the onions look softened. There's some fat in the pan—should I leave it for the chili?
Drain off the fat, then transfer the browned beef and onion mixture into the slow cooker.
It's in the slow cooker now. I'm lining up the add-ins; what goes in with the meat mixture?
Stir in the mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce.
Do I need to drain the kidney beans, or should that liquid help the chili?
Keep the kidney bean liquid in there—the recipe calls for kidney beans with liquid, so it becomes part of the chili base.
Everything is stirred together. How do I adjust the heat level at the end?
Season the slow cooker mixture with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper, tasting as you go so the Atomic Canuck Chili lands where you want it.
I want to make Cinnamon Crackle Cookies. Can you keep me on track while I set up the mixing bowl?
Absolutely. Put a mixing bowl on the counter and measure out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're ready to cream together.
The butter is soft and both fats are in reach. Which sugars should I measure before the mixer starts?
Measure 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Add them with the butter and shortening in the bowl.
Everything is in the bowl. What texture am I looking for when I cream it?
Beat the butter, shortening, and both sugars until the mixture looks blended and creamy, with no obvious streaks of butter or shortening.
It looks smooth and a little fluffy. I've got the egg and extracts beside me.
Add the egg and extracts to the creamed mixture, then mix well so they're fully incorporated.
The wet mixture is combined. Should I dump in the dry ingredients all at once?
Combine the next eight ingredients in a separate bowl first, then add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture so the dough comes together evenly.
I'm adding the dry mix in portions. How thick should the dough be before shaping?
It should hold together well enough to shape. Once the dry ingredients are mixed in and no loose floury patches remain, you can start forming the cookies.
The dough is ready, and I have sugar and ungreased baking sheets out. How do I portion them?
Shape the dough into 1-in balls, roll each ball in sugar, and place them on ungreased baking sheets.
I want to make Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup. Can you help me set up so I'm not hunting for things mid-cook?
Absolutely. Put a large pot on the stove and gather 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 medium onion chopped, 1 green bell pepper chopped, and 1 large carrot peeled and thinly sliced.
I've got the pot out, and the onion, pepper, and carrot are prepped. Do I need the blender right away?
Not right away, but keep it nearby for later. You'll start on the stove first with the oil and vegetables.
Okay, the pot is on the burner. How hot should it be before the vegetables go in?
Heat the 2 tablespoons vegetable oil in the large pot over medium heat. Once the oil looks loose and shimmery, you can add the vegetables.
The oil is shimmering. I'm adding the onion, bell pepper, and carrot now—anything else in that batch?
Yes, stir in the garlic with the onion, bell pepper, and carrot. Cook everything for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are tender.
It's been about 5 minutes and the carrot slices are softening. The pot smells good. What goes in next?
Mix in 1 can black beans along with the chicken broth, stirring so the softened vegetables and beans are evenly combined.
The beans and broth are in. Should I blend the whole soup or just part of it?
Just blend the remaining can of beans separately. Put that can of beans in a blender and puree until smooth.
The puree is smooth now. Is that meant to thicken the soup when I add it back?
Exactly. The pureed beans will give the soup body while the 1 can of whole black beans keeps some texture.

Measure 1/3 cup white sugar and keep 1 teaspoon vanilla extract nearby.

Use medium heat and stir steadily, scraping the bottom and sides as it warms.

I'm making Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms and want to set up the pan and filling without missing anything.
Great—start by getting out 3/4 cup melted butter, divided, plus 1 pound fresh mushrooms with the stems removed. You'll also need a large baking sheet and a medium mixing bowl.
The mushrooms are cleaned and stemmed. What should I pull together for the stuffing?
Have 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons and 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese ready, along with the crabmeat, lobster, and garlic for the filling.
Before I mix anything, should I heat the oven or prep the baking sheet?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it heats, keep the melted butter nearby because you'll use it in two places.
Oven is heating. The baking sheet is clean—how much butter goes on it?
Brush the large baking sheet with about 1/4 cup of the melted butter, coating the area where the mushroom caps will sit.
The pan is buttered. Do the caps go open-side up or down?
Arrange the mushroom caps in a single layer on the buttered baking sheet, with the hollowed side facing up so they're ready to hold the stuffing.
They're lined up and there's still melted butter left. What goes into the bowl?
In the medium bowl, combine the crushed seasoned croutons, the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, shredded mozzarella cheese, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic.
Should the filling be loose or packed together before I spoon it into the mushrooms?

Mix it until the croutons are moistened by the butter and the cheese, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic are evenly distributed. It should hold together lightly enough to spoon into the mushroom caps without being compressed too firmly.
I want to make Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers today. Can you help me set up before I touch the meat?

Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and gather 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg. You'll also need the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, ground beef, and bacon for the next steps.
The cheeses, onion, and egg are out. Should I get the grill going now or wait until the patties are shaped?
Go ahead and preheat the grill for high heat now so it's ready when the burgers are formed.
The grill is heating. What goes into the bowl before the beef?

Add the Cheddar, Parmesan, chopped onion, egg, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper to the large bowl. Stir those together until the egg and sauces are worked through the cheeses and onion.
That mixture looks loose and a little chunky from the onion. Is that okay?
Yes, that's right for this stage. The ground beef will bind with it next, so don't worry if the onion pieces are visible.
I'm ready for the beef, but I don't want to overwork it. How should I add it?
Crumble the ground beef into the bowl in pieces, then mix everything together by hand just until the seasonings and cheese mixture are evenly distributed.
The beef mixture is combined. How many burgers am I shaping?
Shape the mixture into 6 patties. Try to keep them even so they cook at the same pace on the hot grill.
The patties are formed. Where does the bacon come in?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty, securing it snugly against the edge before they go to the grill.
I'm making Barbecued Shredded Beef today. Can you talk me through what to set out before I turn on the oven?
Absolutely. Put a 3 pounds beef roast on the counter, chop 2 onions, and have a large roasting pan ready so the beef and onions can go straight in.
The roasting pan is out, and the onions are chopped. What liquids and seasonings should I have nearby?
You'll need 2 12 fluid ounce cans or bottles of beer and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce. Also have liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper ready for the seasoning mixture.
Should I start heating the oven while I mix that?
Yes, preheat the oven to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C, so it's ready once the roast is assembled.
The oven is heating. Does the roast go into the pan by itself or with the onions?
Set the beef roast in the large roasting pan, then scatter the chopped onions evenly over the top and around it.
The beef and onions are in the pan. How should I build the sauce so it's not uneven?
Use a large bowl and combine the Worcestershire sauce with the liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir those together before adding the beer.
Okay, the seasonings are mixed. Do I pour the beer into the bowl or straight over the meat?
Pour the beer into the bowl with the Worcestershire mixture, stir it well, then add that mixture to the roasting pan over the beef and onions.
The liquid is in the pan. Anything to check before I put it in the oven?
Make sure the roast is settled in the pan, the onions are distributed around it, and the beer mixture is in the bottom of the roasting pan. Once the oven is at 275 degrees F, it's ready to go in.
I'm putting together Double Fudge Brownie Mix as a jar gift. Can you help me set it up neatly?
Absolutely. Set out a clean 1 quart or 1 liter jar, plus the dry ingredients: 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
I have the jar washed and dried. Should I measure everything before layering?
Yes, measure each ingredient first so the layers stay tidy. Keep them separate for the moment: sugar in one bowl, cocoa in another, flour in another, and the chopped pecans ready to go on top.
The sugar and cocoa are measured. Which one goes into the jar first?
Add the 2 cups white sugar first, smoothing it into an even layer at the bottom of the jar. After that, spoon in the 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder gently so it forms a clear second layer.
The cocoa layer looks a little dusty on the glass. Is that okay?
That's fine. If you want a cleaner look, lightly tap the jar on the counter to settle the cocoa, and wipe the inside rim above the layer with a dry paper towel before adding the next ingredient.
Okay, the cocoa is settled. What goes in after that?
Add the 1 cup all-purpose flour over the cocoa. Spoon it in slowly and level it gently, trying not to dig into the cocoa layer underneath.
The flour is in. I still have the pecans measured out.
Top the jar with the 1 cup chopped pecans. Once they're in, close the lid securely so the layers don't shift too much when the jar is moved.
I'm making the tag now. What exactly should it say?
Write the baking note for the recipient: "Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C)." Attach that tag to the jar, and the Double Fudge Brownie Mix is ready to give or store.

messages.content: Tonight I'm plating Coconut Ambrosia Salad for dinner, and I only want a small decorative finish or topping. What would look best?
Choose a single garnish and set it a little off-center.
Great, that's the look for tonight. I have a large mixing bowl out—what fruit should I open and drain?
Drain 1 (11 ounce) can of mandarin oranges and 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple. Let them sit in the strainer for a minute so the salad doesn't get watery.
The oranges and pineapple are drained. What cold ingredients should come out of the fridge or freezer?
Set out 3 1/2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, and measure 2 cups shredded coconut.

Yes. In the large bowl, combine the mandarin oranges, crushed pineapple, thawed whipped topping, shredded coconut, marshmallows, and milk.

Fold gently with a spatula, turning from the bottom of the bowl until the whipped topping coats the fruit, coconut, marshmallows, and milk evenly.
It looks combined but still fluffy. How long does it need to chill before dinner?
Cover the bowl and chill it for 1 hour before serving so the texture sets and the flavors come together.
After chilling, should I spoon it into individual plates or keep it in the bowl?
For your plated dinner, spoon neat portions onto the plates after the 1 hour chill, keeping the edges clean.
I'm ready to send the plates out. What exactly goes on top?
Add cherries as the garnish, keeping to that single off-center finishing touch on each serving.
I'm making Chicken Tortilla Soup IV and want to get set up before I turn on the stove.
Great. Put a large pot on the stove and gather 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin.
The tortillas are still whole. How should I cut them for this recipe?
Cut the corn tortillas into strips about 1/2 inch wide. Keep the strips in two roughly equal piles because you'll crisp them in batches.
I've got the strips divided. How much oil goes into the pot first?
Add 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil to the large pot and warm it over medium heat.
The oil looks warm and a little shimmery. Do I add all the tortilla strips?
Add only half of the tortilla strips for this batch. Stir them often so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in one spot.
They're turning crisp now. Where should I put them when they're done?
Lift them out and drain them on paper towels so the extra oil comes off.
The first batch is draining. There's not much oil left in the pot.
Pour in the remaining 1/2 teaspoon vegetable oil, then add the remaining tortilla strips and crisp them the same way, stirring often.
The second batch is crisp too. Should I mix these into the soup yet?
Drain the second batch on paper towels as well, then set all the crisp tortilla strips aside. Keep the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the soup.
I'm making Aaahh Potato Soup and want to get everything set up before the pot goes on. What should I pull out?
Grab 2 Yukon Gold potatoes and cube them, plus 1 (5.5 ounce) package of au gratin instant potato mix. You'll also need a large saucepan or pot for cooking.
The potatoes are cubed and the boxed mix is open. What liquids am I using?
Measure out 1 (10.5 ounce) can of condensed chicken broth and 1 1/2 cups water. Keep a little extra water nearby in case the potatoes aren't fully covered once everything is in the pot.
Do I add the potato mix dry, or prepare it separately first?
Add the au gratin potato mix straight into the pot dry with the cubed potatoes, condensed chicken broth, and measured water. Stir it together so the mix starts dispersing into the liquid.
It looks a bit thick already and a few potato pieces are sticking up. Is that okay?
Add just enough extra water to cover the potatoes if needed. They don't need to be swimming, but the pieces should be mostly submerged so they can cook evenly.
What heat should I use once everything is covered?
Set the pot over medium heat. Let it cook there, stirring occasionally, until the Yukon Gold potato cubes are tender, which should take about 40 minutes.
How often should I stir so the mix doesn't catch on the bottom?
Give it a good stir every so often, scraping the bottom of the pot as you go. The instant au gratin mix can thicken the soup, so occasional stirring helps keep it smooth while the potatoes soften.
The potatoes are tender now. How do I finish the soup without overcooking it?
Stir in the cream at the end and heat it through gently. Once the soup is hot and creamy, take it off the heat and serve.

Open the 4 (0.13 ounce) packages unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder and the 2 (46 fluid ounce) cans pineapple juice first; those give you the color and base.

Pour the pineapple juice into the large punch bowl, sprinkle in the strawberry drink mix, add the white sugar, and then add the water. Stir from the bottom and around the sides so no powder sits in pockets.

Add the ginger ale after the mixture is dissolved. Stir it in gently so you keep some fizz instead of flattening it.

Use the butter and heavy cream to make the hot spuds creamy, then fold in the diced cheese off heat near serving so you get soft cheesy pockets rather than a stringy or oily mix.
I want to make Fire Side Coffee and store it in a jar. Can you help me set up the dry mix?

Absolutely. Put out a mixing bowl, a sifter or fine mesh strainer, and a clean jar with a tight lid. Measure 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I've got the bowl and jar ready. Should I measure everything straight into the sifter?

Yes, that works well. Add the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee granules, and cinnamon to the sifter over the bowl. The recipe directions also mention nutmeg, so if you're using it, sift it in with the other dry ingredients.
The instant coffee granules look a little chunky. Is that okay?
That's fine. Sifting will break up some clumps and help the mix blend more evenly. If any large bits stay behind, press them gently through the strainer or crush them lightly before adding them back.
Everything has been sifted into the bowl. Do I need to stir it too?
Give it a quick stir with a dry spoon or whisk so the creamer, chocolate, coffee, cinnamon, and nutmeg are evenly distributed throughout the mix.
It looks uniform now. How should I get it into the jar without making a mess?
Use a funnel if you have one, or spoon the mix in carefully. Pour it into the jar, tap the jar gently to settle the powder, then seal it with the lid.
The jar is sealed. How do I make one cup to try it?
For one serving, stir 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture into 1 cup of hot water until dissolved.
If it tastes too strong or too mild, what's the easiest fix?
Adjust it to taste: add a little more mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or add more hot water to mellow it out.
I'm making German Sweet Chocolate Pie and I've got a microwave-safe bowl out. Can you help me get started?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (4 ounce) bar of German sweet chocolate, chopped, plus 1/3 cup milk. You'll use the milk in two parts, so keep a tablespoon measure handy.
The chocolate is chopped. Do I put all the milk in with it?

Use only 2 tablespoons of the milk with the chopped chocolate in the large microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stopping to stir halfway through. You're looking for the chocolate to be almost melted.
It's been stirred halfway, and it looks mostly melted but still a little soft and lumpy.
That's fine. Stir it well after heating; the remaining warmth should smooth out the almost-melted chocolate without needing to overheat it.
What should I have ready before mixing the creamy part?
Have 4 ounces softened cream cheese, 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk ready. A wire whisk is the right tool here.
The cream cheese is soft. Should I add everything into the chocolate bowl?
Yes. Beat the softened cream cheese, the white sugar, and the remaining milk into the chocolate with the wire whisk until the mixture is blended.
It's smooth now. Does it need to chill before the topping goes in?
Yes, refrigerate the mixture for 10 minutes so it firms slightly before folding in the topping.
The bowl has chilled. How careful do I need to be with the whipped topping?
Gently fold in 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping until no streaks remain. Use broad, slow turns with a spatula so the mixture stays light.
I want to make Eggplant and Pepper Parmesan Sandwiches. Can you help me set up without missing anything?
Absolutely. Have ready 1 eggplant, seeded and sliced lengthwise into 1/4 inch slices, plus 1 red bell pepper sliced into thin strips. You'll also need salt and pepper to taste and 1 French baguette.
The eggplant is sliced and the pepper is in strips. Should I turn on the oven now?
Yes, preheat the oven broiler so it's hot by the time the vegetables are arranged.
I've got a medium baking sheet out. Do the vegetables need oil, or just seasoning?
For this recipe, place the eggplant slices and red bell pepper strips on the medium baking sheet and season them with salt and pepper.
Should the eggplant slices be flat on the sheet, or is it okay if they overlap a bit?
Lay them as flat as you can so the broiler can brown them evenly. A little touching is fine, but avoid piling the pepper strips or eggplant slices.
They're seasoned and spread out. How long should they go under the broiler?
Broil them for 5 to 10 minutes, watching for the vegetables to become tender and slightly browned.
I'm at about 6 minutes and the peppers are browning, but the eggplant still looks a little firm.
Give it a few more minutes, staying within that 5 to 10 minute range. Pull the sheet when the eggplant is tender and the vegetables are lightly browned, not charred.
The vegetables are tender now. What should I do with the baguette?
Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise, then use it as the base for the broiled eggplant and red bell pepper.
I'm making Baked Salmon with Herbs. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I touch the fish?

Absolutely. Put the salmon aside for a moment and gather the topping ingredients you have quantities for: 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs, 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese, and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes.
Those are on the counter. The crumb mixture mentions more herbs too—what should I have ready?
Have thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper within reach as well. The recipe uses them in the bread crumb bowl, though it doesn't give amounts here.
Got it. What pan should I use, and do I need to oil it?
Use a 15-in baking pan. Line it with foil, then coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray so the salmon won't stick.
The foil is sprayed. Should I mix the dry topping right in a small bowl?
Use a bowl with enough room to toss everything. Combine the soft bread crumbs, minced garlic, Parmesan, dried parsley flakes, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
The bowl smells garlicky already. Do I add the butter before or after stirring the herbs through?
Stir the dry ingredients together first so the seasonings are distributed, then add the butter and toss until the crumbs are evenly coated.
The crumbs look moistened and a little clumpy. Is that the texture I want?
Yes, that sounds right. You want the butter coating the crumb mixture evenly rather than leaving dry patches at the bottom of the bowl.
My pan is ready and the topping is mixed. Where does the salmon go?
Place the salmon on the prepared foil-lined pan. Keep the crumb mixture nearby so it's ready for the next topping step if your full recipe continues from there.

messages.content: For this Deep Fried Turkey, I'm serving it family-style on a big platter tonight, and I want a dressed-up finish with optional garnishes or little decorative touches. What would you do at the end?
For this platter, finish with 3 small garnish groupings placed around the turkey so it looks intentional but still easy for people to serve themselves.
Perfect, that's the look I want just for tonight. Before the oil comes out, what ingredients should I gather first?
Set up the big items first: 3 gallons peanut oil for frying, or as much as your fryer needs, plus 1 whole 12 pound turkey with the neck and giblets removed.
The fryer area is clear, and the turkey is still wrapped. What else belongs on the counter?
Add 1/4 cup Creole seasoning and 1 white onion to your prep area. Keep plenty of paper towels nearby too, since the turkey needs to be thoroughly dried.
Got it. For equipment, am I using the stockpot or the turkey fryer right away?
Yes. In a large stockpot or turkey fryer, start heating the peanut oil to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
I'm watching the oil level because I don't want a mess. How much space should I leave?
Leave enough room for the whole turkey to go in without pushing the oil over the top; if the pot is too full, the oil will spill over.
While the oil heats, I want the serving setup ready. What should I line the platter with?
Layer a large platter with food-safe paper bags so it's ready to catch the turkey once it comes out of the fryer.
The platter is lined. Before seasoning, what should I do with the bird itself?
Rinse the turkey, then pat it very thoroughly dry with paper towels. Take your time here, because excess moisture and hot oil do not mix well.
Once it's dry and cooked, how should I connect that platter setup with the finishing idea?
Transfer the turkey to the lined platter, let it sit neatly as the centerpiece, then add those 3 small garnish clusters around the edges so the finish stays decorative without covering the turkey.
I want to make Dutch Cream Waffles. What should I pull out before I start mixing?
Set out 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 3 separated eggs so you have the 3 egg yolks and 3 egg whites ready in separate bowls.
I've got the flour, salt, and the separated eggs. Which bowl should I use for the dry ingredients?
Use a large mixing bowl for the dry ingredients. Add the flour and salt to it, then give them a quick stir so the salt is evenly mixed through the flour.
The flour and salt are combined. For the yolks, should I use the mixer right away?
Yes. Put the egg yolks in a small mixing bowl and beat them on low speed while adding the cream.
The yolk mixture is starting to come together. How long do I keep beating it?
Keep beating it for 1 minute. Stay on low unless your mixture needs a little help smoothing out.
One minute is done. It looks fairly smooth, with a few streaks around the edge of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides if needed, then pour the yolk-and-cream mixture into the large bowl with the flour and salt.
It's in the flour bowl now. Do I mix gently or use the mixer again?
Use the mixer again: combine everything on low speed at first so the flour doesn't puff out of the bowl.
The dry flour is mostly incorporated. What texture am I aiming for before I cook the waffles?
Increase to medium-high and beat until the batter is smooth. Once it looks even and lump-free, you're ready to move on with the waffles.
I'm making Fresh Apple Walnut Cake. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt within reach. You'll also need the apples and white sugar ready for a later step.
The dry ingredients are on the counter. Should I do anything with the oven right away?
Yes, get the oven heating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is prepared.
Oven is heating. I have a 9x13 inch pan—how should I prep it?
Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour so the cake releases more easily after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. Do the dry ingredients just get stirred together?
For this recipe, sift the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together. That helps distribute the baking soda and cinnamon evenly through the flour.
I'm sifting them into a big bowl now. Should it look completely uniform?
Yes, it should look evenly blended, with no obvious streaks of cinnamon or little clumps of baking soda left behind.
That looks even. What should I do with the apples before they go into the cake?
Combine the apples with the white sugar in a separate bowl, then set that mixture aside as the recipe directs.
So at this point the oven is heating, the pan is ready, the dry mix is sifted, and the apples with sugar are set aside—is that right?
That's right. You've completed the setup steps for Fresh Apple Walnut Cake: 350 degrees F oven, prepared 9x13 inch pan, sifted dry ingredients, and apples combined with white sugar and set aside.
I'm making Crab Cake Sauce for dinner. Can you help me get it started?
Absolutely. Set out a blender and the main ingredients: 1 cup sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup cottage cheese, and 1/3 cup hot salsa.
I've got the blender out, and the sour cream and mayo are measured. Does the cottage cheese go in as-is?
Yes, add the 1/2 cup cottage cheese as-is. The blender will smooth it out with the sour cream and mayonnaise.
Okay, the cottage cheese is in. I'm opening the hot salsa now—should I drain it?
No need to drain it. Add the 1/3 cup hot salsa straight in so the sauce gets both the heat and the liquid for blending.
The salsa is in the blender. The recipe also mentions cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt—do those blend in too?
Yes. Add the cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt to the blender with the sour cream, mayonnaise, cottage cheese, and salsa.
Everything is in. What texture am I looking for before I stop blending?
Puree it until the sauce looks smooth and creamy, with no obvious cottage cheese curds remaining. Scrape down the sides if anything is sticking.
It's mostly smooth, but I see a few tiny flecks from the salsa.
That's fine—the salsa may leave small flecks. As long as the base is smooth and blended, you're good.
Should I serve it right away with the crab cakes, or does it need time?
Chill it before serving. Transfer it to a covered bowl or container and refrigerate it until it's cold, then spoon it alongside the crab cakes.
I'm making Garlic Chicken Stir Fry. Can you help me get set up before I turn on the wok?
Absolutely. Have 2 tablespoons peanut oil ready, plus 6 cloves garlic minced. You'll also want 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger and 1 bunch green onions chopped.
I've got the oil measured and the garlic minced. Do I use all the garlic right away?

For the hot-oil step, use 2 cloves of the minced garlic with the ginger, green onions, and salt. Keep the rest of the minced garlic nearby so it's ready if you're adding it with the chicken or adjusting the flavor as you cook.
My wok is on the stove. Should I add the peanut oil while it's heating?
Yes. Pour the 2 tablespoons peanut oil into the wok or a large skillet and heat it until the oil begins to smoke slightly.
The oil is shimmering and just starting to smoke. What goes in now?
Quickly stir in the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving so the garlic doesn't scorch.
The onions are softening. What texture am I looking for before adding the chicken?
Stir-fry until the green onion looks translucent, about 2 minutes. It should smell garlicky and gingery, with the onions softened but not browned.
It's been about 2 minutes and the onion looks translucent. I have the chicken ready.
Add the chicken to the wok and stir it through the garlic, ginger, and green onions so the pieces make contact with the hot pan.
How do I know when the chicken is done enough for this step?
Keep stirring until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes. Once there's no raw-looking surface, you're at the end of this recipe's cooking steps.
I want to make Classic Peanut Butter Cookies. Can you talk me through getting started?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup unsalted butter and 1 cup crunchy peanut butter so they're ready to cream together.
Butter and crunchy peanut butter are out. What sugars should I measure before I start mixing?
Measure 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Those will go into the bowl with the butter and peanut butter.
I've got both sugars measured. Should I use a mixer for this part?
Yes, a mixer will make it easier. Cream the butter, crunchy peanut butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar together until the mixture looks blended and smooth enough to continue.
The mixture looks creamy and even. What goes in next?
Beat in the eggs until they're fully incorporated into the creamed mixture.
The eggs are mixed in. I have another bowl clean—what should I do with it?
Use that separate bowl to sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
The dry ingredients are sifted together. Do I add them all at once?
Add the sifted dry mixture into the batter and stir until it's combined. Scrape the sides of the bowl as needed so there aren't dry pockets.
The dough has come together. Anything I should check before I move on to shaping or baking?
Check that the dough is evenly mixed, with the flour mixture fully stirred into the peanut butter batter. Once it looks consistent, you're ready to portion it for the next stage.
I want to make Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies. Can you talk me through the prep while I get the mixer ready?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening so they're ready to cream smoothly.
Both fats are softened and in reach. Which sugars should I measure before I start mixing?
Measure 1 cup packed light brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. Keep them near the large bowl with the butter and shortening.
The sugars are measured. Should I heat the oven before combining anything?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the dough is mixed.
Oven is heating. I've got the large bowl on the counter—what goes in for the creaming stage?
Add the butter, butter flavored shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla to the large bowl, then cream them together until the mixture looks smooth.
It's getting pale and smooth. I'm setting up a separate bowl for the dry ingredients—what should I combine?
In that bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Give them a quick mix so the spices and leavening are evenly distributed.
The dry mixture smells spicy and looks even. Do I dump it all in or add it gradually?
Stir the dry mixture into the sugar mixture. Add it steadily and mix just until it comes together so the dough stays tender.
The dough is mixed and there are no dry streaks. What's the last addition before scooping?
Stir in the oats and raisins until they're evenly spread through the dough, then you'll be ready to portion the cookies for baking.
I want to make Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread in my bread machine. Can you talk me through what to set out first?

Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, and 1 1/2 cups bread flour. You'll also need the sunflower seeds nearby, but don't add them at the beginning.
The water, butter, honey, and bread flour are ready. Should I put them straight into the machine pan?
Yes. Add those ingredients to the bread machine pan in the order your bread machine manufacturer recommends. Keep the sunflower seeds out for now.
My machine usually wants liquids before flour, so the water is going in first. Does softened butter matter here?
Softened butter is best because it blends more easily during kneading. After the water, add the softened butter and honey, then add the bread flour according to your machine's order.
Everything except the sunflower seeds is in the pan. Which setting should I choose?
Select the basic white cycle on the bread machine, then press start.
It's running now. I'm keeping the seeds beside the machine so I don't forget them.
Good plan. Wait for the machine's alert during the knead cycle, then add the sunflower seeds at that point.
The alert just sounded while it's kneading. Do I just scatter the seeds in?
Yes, add the sunflower seeds now while the knead cycle is active so the machine can work them into the dough.
Seeds are in and the lid is closed again. Anything else I should do before it bakes?
No extra recipe step is needed. Let the bread machine continue through the basic white cycle, and avoid opening the lid unless your machine instructions specifically call for it.

messages.content: Tonight I'm turning Classic Peanut Butter Cookies into a warm skillet-style dessert and I want a little pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini edge. What's the best way to work in that briny note?
For this skillet version, warm the pan with just a spoonful of the brine for flavor, but keep the pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces out of the cookie itself.
Perfect, that's exactly the twist I'm doing for this batch. I've got the skillet out—what should I measure first?
Measure 1 cup unsalted butter and 1 cup crunchy peanut butter so they're ready to cream together.
Both are on the counter. I want the sugars ready before I start mixing; what amounts do I need?
Set out 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar.
The butter is soft and the sugars are measured. Should I combine all four of those now?
Yes. Cream together the butter, crunchy peanut butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks blended and smooth enough to continue.
It's creamy now, and I'm using a sturdy spoon because of the skillet plan. What goes in after that?
Beat in the eggs next, mixing until they disappear into the peanut butter-sugar mixture.
Eggs are mixed in. I've got a separate bowl nearby for the dry ingredients—what should go there?
In that separate bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
The dry bowl is sifted. Before I bring it together, do I add any of the briny solids now?
No solids here. Keep the briny pieces out, and rely on that spoonful of brine in the warm pan for this batch's savory edge.
Got it. The wet mixture is waiting and the pan is warm with the brine aroma. How do I finish the batter?
Stir the sifted dry ingredients into the batter until combined, then it's ready for your warm skillet treatment.

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.

messages.content: For this batch of Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread, I'm treating it more like a chilled fruit dessert, and I have cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and nutmeg nearby. Which warm spice direction makes sense here?
For this batch, keep it very restrained: use just a tiny pinch of ginger, and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Perfect, that's the direction I wanted for this loaf. I've got the bread machine pan out—what should go in first?
Start with the liquids and soft ingredients your machine calls for in its order: measure 1 1/3 cups water, then have 2 tablespoons softened butter ready to add to the pan.
The water is measured and the butter is soft. I'm trying not to crowd the counter—what else do I need before I load it?
Set out 3 tablespoons honey and 1 1/2 cups bread flour. Keep the sunflower seeds aside for later; they don't go in with the first load.
Honey and flour are measured. Should the ginger go in with those, or wait for the seed beep?
Add that tiny pinch of ginger with the main ingredients in the bread machine pan. The sunflower seeds should still wait until the machine alerts you during kneading.
I'm at the pan now. Do I just layer everything in, or does the order matter?
Use the order recommended by your bread machine's manufacturer. Place all the ingredients in the pan except the sunflower seeds, following that order.
The pan is loaded and the seeds are still in a small bowl. Which setting am I choosing?
Select the basic white cycle, then press start.
It's running now. I'm listening for the alert—what exactly happens when it sounds?
When the alert sounds during the knead cycle, add the sunflower seeds to the pan.
Seeds are in. Since I'm serving this chilled with fruit, anything special after the machine finishes?
Let the bread finish its cycle, then cool it completely before chilling or slicing for fruit. That keeps the texture cleaner for a dessert-style serving.
I'm making Cinnamon Bread I. Can you help me set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda within reach.
I've got the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda out. Is the pan a standard loaf pan?
Yes, use one 9x5 inch loaf pan. Grease it well so the bread releases cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased. Should I turn the oven on before I measure the batter ingredients?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. I'm using a large mixing bowl—what goes into it?
Measure the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla into the large mixing bowl.
Just checking: the cinnamon amount is 1 1/2 teaspoons, right?
That's right: 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon goes in with the rest of the measured ingredients.
Everything is measured into the bowl. Do I stir gently or use a mixer?
Beat the mixture for 3 minutes, scraping the bowl as needed so the flour and liquids combine evenly.
The batter looks smooth after beating. Anything else before it goes into the pan?
Give the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan a quick check for full coverage, then pour in the batter and keep the oven at 350 degrees F.
I'm making Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken and want to get the glaze organized before I touch the chicken. What should I measure out?
Set out 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum. You'll also need mustard, garlic, salt, and pepper for the glaze.
I've got the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and rum measured. What bowl should I use for mixing?
Use a medium bowl so you have room to stir without splashing. Add the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, dark rum, mustard, and garlic to it.
The glaze ingredients are in the bowl, but the molasses is sitting at the bottom. Is that okay?
Yes, that's normal. Stir it well until the molasses loosens and the mixture looks smooth and glossy, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
The glaze is smooth now. Should I oil the pan before adding the chicken?
Yes. Lightly oil a 9x13 inch baking dish, then place the chicken pieces in the dish in a single layer if you can.
The chicken is in the dish. Do I pour all the glaze over it?
Use about 1/2 of the prepared glaze for this part. Brush both sides of the chicken pieces so they're coated, and save the remaining glaze.
I brushed both sides and still have glaze left. How long does it need to sit?
Cover the dish and refrigerate it to marinate for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if you have the time.
If I'm marinating overnight, should I do anything to keep the fridge clean?

Keep the baking dish covered tightly and place it on a rimmed tray or lower fridge shelf in case of drips. When you're ready to continue, keep the reserved glaze separate from anything that touched raw chicken.
I want to make the Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart, but I'm starting with the crust ingredients. Can you help me keep the prep organized?

Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a mixing bowl, a sifter, a fork, plastic wrap, butter, and ice water for the dough steps.
I've got the flour, sugar, cinnamon, and salt measured. Should they all go through the sifter together?
Yes. Sift the flour, light brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt together into the bowl so the dry mixture is evenly blended and light.
The dry ingredients are sifted. The brown sugar left a couple tiny bits behind—should I press them through?
If they're small and soft, press them through gently with the back of a spoon. If any bits are hard, leave them out so the crust texture stays even.
Okay, the bowl looks uniform now. I'm ready for the butter part—what texture am I aiming for?
Cut in the butter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. Use a pastry cutter, two knives, or your fingertips, and stop before it turns into a smooth paste.
It's crumbly with some pea-sized pieces. Do I add the ice water all at once?
Sprinkle the ice water over the crumbs rather than dumping it in one spot. Toss with a fork as you go until the mixture is evenly moistened.
The dough is moist in patches but not sticky. How do I know when to stop tossing?
Stop once the crumbs hold together when gently pressed. It should look hydrated enough to gather, but still a bit shaggy rather than wet.
It holds together now. What should I do before chilling or setting it aside?
Pat the dough into a round, wrap it well in plastic, and keep it compact so it's easier to roll later for the tart.
I want to make Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake. Can you help me set up without missing anything?
Absolutely. Put out 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies, 1/4 cup melted margarine, 1 cup hot fudge topping, and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream.
I have the cookies and margarine ready. Should the ice cream stay in the freezer for now?
Yes, keep the 2 quarts of vanilla ice cream frozen while you build the cookie crust and fudge layer. You'll also want a 9-inch springform pan or a pie plate nearby.
The pan is out. How many cookies am I crushing for the crust?
Crush half the package of small chocolate chip cookies, about 20 cookies, until they're crumbly enough to form the base.
They're mostly crumbs with a few small pieces. Is that okay?
That's fine for this cake. Stir those crumbs together with the 1/4 cup melted margarine so the mixture is evenly moistened.
The crumbs look damp and sandy now. Where do they go?
Press the crumb mixture firmly into the bottom of the 9-inch springform pan or pie plate, making an even crust.
Crust is pressed in. What do I do with the cookies I didn't crush?
Stand the remaining whole cookies upright around the edge of the pan, pressing them gently into place against the crust.
The cookie border is set. How much fudge goes on before the ice cream?
Spread 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the crust in an even layer, staying inside the cookie border.
