messages.content: I'd like to make Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth. Can you help me set up before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Put a large pot on the stove and gather 2 quarts water and 12 ounces beef shank to start.
The pot is out, and I have the water and beef shank. Are there vegetables for this version too?
Yes. Have 2 large onions chopped and 2 large carrots sliced, so they're ready when you need them.
Onions are chopped and carrots are sliced. Do I add everything to the pot right away?
Begin with just the water: pour the 2 quarts into the large pot and bring it to a boil.
The water is heating now. How strong should the boil be before the beef goes in?
Wait until it reaches a steady boil, then lower the beef shank into the pot carefully.
The beef is in. Should I keep it boiling hard or turn it down?
Turn it down to a simmer and let the beef shank cook gently for 1 1/2 hours.
It has simmered for the full time. The broth is hot and the meat looks cooked through.
Take the pot off the heat and let it cool overnight before you handle the meat.
It cooled overnight in the pot. What should I do with the beef now?
Lift the meat out, trim off any gristle, cut the meat into medium sized pieces, and set it aside.
I'm making Diegos Special Beef Stew. Can you help me get started and keep the steps manageable?

Absolutely. Set out 1 pound cubed beef stew meat, 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 teaspoons butter. You'll also want a resealable plastic bag, a skillet, and a slow cooker nearby.
I've got the beef, flour, olive oil, and butter out. Should the beef go straight into the skillet?
Not yet. Put the cubed beef into the resealable plastic bag with the flour so the pieces can be coated before browning.
The beef and flour are in the bag, but some flour is sitting in the corners. Is that okay?
Yes. Seal the bag well, then shake and turn it until the beef is evenly coated with the flour. If flour gathers in a corner, massage the bag lightly to work it over the meat.
The beef looks lightly coated now. What pan setup should I use?
Place your skillet over medium heat and add the 2 tablespoons olive oil. Let the oil warm before adding the beef so it can brown instead of just steaming.
Do I add the 2 teaspoons butter with the oil, or save it?

Have the butter ready, but for the listed cooking step, heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat and brown the beef on all sides. If you add the butter, keep the heat at medium so it doesn't scorch.
The beef is in the skillet. How dark should I let the sides get?
Aim for browned surfaces on all sides, not fully cooked-through meat. Turn the cubes as needed so each side picks up color.
The beef is browned and there are browned bits in the skillet. What happens next?
Transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker. Scrape up any loose browned bits that come along easily, since they'll add flavor to the stew base.
I'm making German Chocolate Brownie Cookies and want to get the bowl set up correctly. What should I pull out first?
Start with the creaming ingredients: 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Set out a large mixing bowl too.
I've got the brown sugar packed and the shortening measured. Do those go in together with the water and vanilla?
Yes. Put the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla into the large bowl, then mix until the ingredients come together into a creamed mixture.
The mixture looks soft and combined. I noticed the next part mentions eggs—should I add them straight into this bowl?
Add the eggs directly to the creamed mixture and beat them in until everything looks evenly blended.
Eggs are mixed in. I'd like to keep the dry ingredients from clumping—what bowl should I use?
Use a separate bowl for the dry ingredients. Combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda there so they're evenly distributed before they go into the wet mixture.
The flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda are combined. Should I dump it all in at once or add it slowly?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix gently. Stop once it is just blended so the cookie dough doesn't get overworked.
The dough is mostly uniform, with no dry streaks left. Is that the texture I'm aiming for?
That sounds right. Since the instruction is to mix until just blended, a cohesive dough with the dry ingredients incorporated is the point to stop.
Before I clean up, can you recap the order so I know I didn't miss anything?

You combined 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract in a large bowl; beat in the eggs; mixed flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda in another bowl; then stirred the dry mixture into the creamed mixture until just blended.
I'm making Apple Butter V and have a Dutch oven ready. Can you help me organize the ingredients before I start cooking?
Absolutely. For this batch, you'll want 6 pounds tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups apple cider. Keep the Dutch oven close because the apples go straight into it.
The apples are sliced and the cider is measured. Are there any sweeteners or spices I should pull out now?
Yes—set out 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon. The cooking starts with the apples and cider, but having the sugar and cinnamon measured will keep things smooth.
Got it. The apples are in a big bowl right now; should I transfer them to the pot all at once?
Yes, place the sliced, cored apples in the Dutch oven. It's fine if they mound up a bit as long as the pot has room for the cider and simmering.
They're in the Dutch oven. I don't want them sticking—does the cider go in before the heat?
Pour in the 6 cups apple cider before turning up the heat. That liquid will help the apples soften evenly as the mixture comes up to a boil.
The cider is in, and the pot is on the stove. How hot should I run it?
Bring the apple-and-cider mixture to a boil, then cook it on medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
After about 30 minutes, what texture am I looking for before I stop cooking?
The apples should be very soft and collapsing easily when pressed with a spoon. If a few slices still feel firm, keep them on medium heat a little longer until the whole mixture is softened.
The apples are soft now. I have a food mill set over a bowl—what do I do with the hot mixture?
Carefully ladle the softened apple mixture into the food mill and press it through. Work in batches if needed, and scrape the underside of the mill so you keep all the smooth apple pulp.
Can you help me make Crawfish Chowder? I've got a large skillet out but want to be sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1/4 cup butter and 1/2 bunch green onions, chopped. Keep the skillet ready for medium heat.
The green onions are chopped. I also see another stick of butter and the crawfish in the freezer—do those come in later?
Yes. You'll also need 1/2 cup butter and 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned. Have the crawfish ready to go before the skillet gets too hot.
Should I thaw the crawfish first, or can I add them frozen when it's time?
Use the 2 pounds frozen crawfish as listed, cleaned and ready. If there's excess ice or liquid on them, drain it off so they sauté instead of steaming too much.
Okay, the skillet is on medium heat. Which butter amount goes in first?
Melt the 1/4 cup butter in the large skillet over medium heat. Let it fully melt and coat the pan, but don't let it brown.
It's melted and bubbling lightly. Do the green onions go straight in?
Yes, add the chopped 1/2 bunch green onions and sauté them in the butter until they're tender.
They've softened and smell good. Do I leave them in there while the crawfish cooks?
Take the green onions out of the pan and set them aside. You'll use the same skillet for the crawfish.
The pan is empty now. How do I handle the crawfish part without overcooking them?
Melt the 1/2 cup butter in that same skillet, then add the 2 pounds cleaned crawfish and sauté them for 5 minutes. After that, set the crawfish aside.
Can you help me make Chipotle Mayo Relish? I've got a food processor out but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Measure 1 cup light mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce that have been seeded and minced, 1/4 cup chopped green onion, and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish.
The mayo is measured. For the chipotle peppers, should I include the adobo sauce with them?
Use the minced chipotle peppers with the adobo that clings to them, then keep the can nearby. After blending, you can add a little more adobo sauce if you want extra smoky heat.
Okay, I have the peppers seeded and minced. What goes into the processor right now?
Add the 1 cup light mayonnaise and the 2 tablespoons minced chipotle peppers to the food processor. Process until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It's blended and pale orange. It tastes good but maybe a little mild.
Blend in a little more adobo sauce if you'd like. About 1/2 teaspoon is a good amount to boost the flavor without overwhelming the relish.
I added the 1/2 teaspoon and pulsed it. Should the green onion go in the processor too?
No need to process the green onion. Transfer the chipotle mayo mixture to a serving bowl so you can stir in the remaining ingredients by hand.
It's in a bowl. I've got the chopped green onion and sweet pickle relish ready.
Stir in the 1/4 cup chopped green onion and the 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish until they're evenly distributed through the mayo.
Looks mixed. I'm serving it with sandwiches later—does it need fridge time?
Yes, chill it until serving. Cover the bowl and refrigerate it so the texture firms up a bit and the chipotle, onion, and relish flavors come together.
Can you guide me through Adriennes Tom Ka Gai? I've got a large saucepan out and want to prep as I go.

Absolutely. Set out 2 teaspoons peanut oil, 2 cloves garlic thinly sliced, 2 tablespoons grated fresh ginger root, and 1/4 cup chopped lemon grass. Keep the red pepper, coriander, and cumin nearby too, since they go into the pan with the aromatics.
The garlic is sliced and the ginger is grated. Should the lemon grass be chopped pretty small?
Yes, chop the lemon grass finely enough that it can soften and release its aroma quickly. Once that's ready, place the large saucepan over medium heat and warm the peanut oil.
The oil is shimmering a little, not smoking. Is that right for adding the aromatics?
That's right. Stir in the garlic, ginger, lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin. Keep them moving in the oil and cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
It smells strong and the garlic is just starting to color. I have the chicken and onion ready.
Add the chicken and onion to the saucepan. Stir frequently so the spices coat everything, and cook until the chicken turns white and the onion looks translucent, about 5 minutes.
The chicken pieces are white on the outside and the onion has softened. Should I lower the heat?
Medium heat is fine unless anything is sticking or browning too fast. Scrape the bottom as you stir, then get the bok choy ready to add.
The bok choy is washed and chopped. Do the stems and leaves go in together?
For this recipe, stir in the bok choy together and cook until it begins to wilt. That should take 5 to 10 minutes, depending on how thick the pieces are.
The leaves are wilting but the stems still have some crunch. Is that the texture I want?
Yes, that's a good stopping point if the bok choy has begun to wilt and the stems are tender-crisp. Give the pot one final stir so the chicken, onion, and greens are evenly mixed, then serve it hot.
I'm making Broccoli Coleslaw today. Can you guide me through it without rushing?

Absolutely. Start by setting out the dressing ingredients: 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, and 1/2 cup white sugar. You'll also need 1 (3 ounce) package of chicken flavored ramen noodles; keep the seasoning packet because it goes into the dressing.
I've got the oil, vinegar, sugar, and ramen. Should I crush the noodles right away or wait?
You can crush the ramen noodles now and set them aside, but don't mix them into the salad yet. Open the seasoning packet and add that packet to a small bowl with the olive oil, vinegar, and sugar.
The dressing ingredients are in the small bowl. How well should I mix it?
Whisk or stir until the sugar starts dissolving and the seasoning is evenly blended through the oil and vinegar. It does not have to look creamy, just well combined.
Okay, the dressing is mixed. Does it need to chill before I add it to the vegetables?
Yes. Refrigerate the dressing for at least one hour before serving, or let it sit overnight if you're preparing ahead. That gives the flavors time to come together.
While that chills, what bowl should I use for the slaw mix?
Use a large bowl so you have room to toss everything. Add the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds to that bowl.
The vegetables and sunflower seeds are in. Should the ramen go in before or after the dressing?
Stir in the crushed ramen noodles with the broccoli mixture. If you want them crunchier, add them closer to serving time; the recipe's basic direction is to crush them and stir them in.
The dressing has chilled for about 1 hour. How should I bring it all together for serving?

Give the chilled dressing another quick stir, pour it over the broccoli mixture, and toss until everything is coated. Serve it right away for the most crunch, or keep it refrigerated if you made it ahead overnight.
Can you guide me through making churros? I've got a saucepan and a deep skillet ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also need flour for the dough and enough oil in the deep skillet for frying.
The water, sugar, salt, vegetable oil, and flour are on the counter. Should I start on the stove?
Yes. Put the small saucepan over medium heat, then add the 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil.
They're in the pan. Do I stir it while it heats?
Give it a gentle stir so the sugar and salt dissolve evenly, then let the mixture come up to a boil.
It's boiling now and the sugar looks dissolved. Do I keep it on the burner?
Take the saucepan off the heat as soon as it reaches that boil.
Off the heat. I'm ready to add the flour, but what texture am I looking for?
Stir in the flour firmly until the mixture comes together and forms a ball. It should pull away from the sides of the pan rather than stay loose.
The dough has formed a ball. Should I heat the frying oil now?
Yes. Heat oil in your deep-fryer or deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
The oil is heating toward 375. Anything I should watch before frying?
Keep the oil steady at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) before adding the churro dough, and work carefully since the oil will be very hot.
Can you help me make Fig Bars II? I've got my mixer out, but I want to make sure I'm not missing anything before I start.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup white sugar and 3 eggs, since those get beaten together for the base of the batter.
Sugar and eggs are on the counter. What dry ingredients should I measure before the bowl gets messy?
Measure 7/8 cup all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder. The recipe also has you sift in salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice with those dry ingredients.
I'll get those spices ready too. What pan and oven setup do I need?
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C, and prepare a 9x13 inch baking pan by greasing it and dusting it with flour.
The oven is heating, and I'm greasing the pan now. Should I flour it heavily or just coat it?
Just a light, even coating is enough. Tap the pan around so the flour clings to the greased surface, then shake out any loose excess.
Pan is ready. I'm about to start mixing—what texture am I aiming for with the eggs and sugar?
Beat the eggs and sugar in a large bowl until the mixture looks thick and pale. It should lighten in color and feel a bit fuller before you add the dry ingredients.
It's paler and thicker now. Do I dump the flour mixture straight in?
Sift the flour, baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice together first, then blend that into the egg mixture. Add the vanilla along with it as the recipe directs.
Okay, I'm folding that in. Any advice so I don't overwork it?
Mix only until the sifted dry ingredients and vanilla are incorporated into the egg mixture. Scrape the sides of the bowl once or twice, then stop when you no longer see dry streaks.
Can you help me make Almond Apricot Bread? I'm setting out bowls and measuring cups now.
Absolutely. For the dry ingredients, measure 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour into a large bowl, then add 1/2 cup sugar.
Flour and sugar are in the big bowl. Should the brown sugar go in with those?
Yes. Add 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to that same bowl, along with 3 teaspoons baking powder and the salt from the recipe.
The brown sugar is a little clumpy. Do I need to break it up before mixing?
Break up the larger clumps with a spoon or your fingers, then stir the flour, both sugars, baking powder, and salt together so they're evenly combined.
Dry bowl is mixed. I've got the baby food open—what should I do with it before I start the wet bowl?
Spoon out 1 tablespoon of the baby food and set it aside for the glaze. Keep the remaining baby food for the batter.
Done. For the other bowl, what goes in with the remaining baby food?
In another bowl, beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food until the mixture looks fairly smooth.
It's mixed, but I don't want the bread to turn tough. How should I combine the bowls?
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir gently, just until the dry ingredients are moistened. Stop when you no longer see big dry patches.
There are a few tiny streaks of flour near the side of the bowl. Should I keep stirring?
Scrape the sides once or twice and fold those streaks in, but don't beat the batter. A slightly lumpy batter is fine for Almond Apricot Bread.
Can you guide me through making Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad? I've got the chicken out but haven't started heating anything yet.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided, and 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, about 6 ounces each. You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning and 2 cloves garlic, crushed.
I have the 2 chicken breasts, Cajun seasoning, garlic, and olive oil. What pan should I use?
Use a large skillet so the chicken has room to sear instead of crowding. Add 1 tablespoon of the olive oil to the skillet and warm it over medium heat.
The skillet is on medium with the oil. Should I season the chicken before it goes in?
Yes. Coat both sides of the chicken breast halves with the Cajun seasoning, using the 1 1/2 tablespoons total.
Both sides are seasoned. The oil looks hot but not smoking.
Good. Lay the chicken into the hot oil carefully, leaving space between the pieces so they blacken well.
The chicken is in the pan. When does the crushed garlic go in?
Stir in the 2 cloves of crushed garlic now, moving it around the skillet so it flavors the oil without sitting in one spot.
It smells great. How long should I cook the first side?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on that side, keeping the heat at medium so the seasoning darkens without burning.
I flipped both pieces after 5 minutes. What am I looking for before serving?
Cook the second side for another 5 minutes, or until the juices run clear. Once done, let the chicken rest briefly, then slice it for the salad.
Can you help me make Baked Fake Steak with Gravy? I've got the ground beef out, but I want to make sure I set everything up right.

Absolutely. For the beef mixture, you'll need 3 pounds ground beef, 17 saltine crackers finely crushed, 1/2 cup milk, and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder. You'll also season it with onion powder, salt, and pepper.
The crackers are still whole. Should I crush them before they go in with the meat?
Yes, crush the 17 saltine crackers finely first so they blend evenly into the beef. A rolling pin or the bottom of a measuring cup works well if they're in a bag.
Okay, crumbs are ready. What bowl should I use for mixing 3 pounds of beef?
Use a large bowl with plenty of room so you can combine everything without packing it too tightly at the start. Add the ground beef, the crushed saltines, and the 1/2 cup milk.
I added those. The mixture looks a little loose from the milk—do I keep mixing?
Keep mixing just until the cracker crumbs and milk are worked through the beef. It should start holding together, but try not to overwork it more than needed.
Ready for seasoning. Does the garlic powder go in now?
Yes. Sprinkle in the 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, along with onion powder, salt, and pepper, then mix until the seasoning is well blended throughout.
The meat mixture is seasoned. I have a jellyroll pan—what size am I supposed to use?
Use a 10x15 inch jellyroll pan. Line it with waxed paper before adding the beef mixture.
The pan is lined. Do I spread the beef gently or pack it down?
Press the beef mixture firmly into the lined 10x15 inch pan, spreading it evenly into the corners so it forms a compact, level layer.
Can you help me make Famous Caramel Cookie Bars? I've got a tray out but want to make sure I'm setting everything up right.
Absolutely. Set out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels with the wrappers removed, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips.
The caramels are unwrapped and the cookies are still in neat rows. Should I line the tray or just use it bare?
Use a baking sheet or tray, and arrange the shortbread cookies on it in a single layer so each one is easy to reach when you add the caramel.
They fit on one sheet with a little space between them. What pan should I use for the caramel?
Choose a small saucepan. Add the 35 unwrapped caramels and the 1/4 cup water, then warm them over medium-low heat.
The caramel is starting to soften around the edges. How much should I stir it?
Stir frequently as it melts so the caramel and water come together smoothly and the mixture doesn't scorch on the bottom.
It's glossy now, but still a little thick. Is that okay for putting on the cookies?
Yes, as long as it's melted enough to spoon. Use a spoon to drizzle a thin line of caramel over each shortbread cookie.
I'm getting strings of caramel between cookies. Any trick to keeping the lines tidy?

Work close to the cookie surface and lift the spoon straight up at the end of each line. If the caramel thickens too much while you work, keep it gently warm over low heat just until it loosens again.
All the cookies have caramel lines now. Do they need to sit out, or should I chill them?
Place the cookies in the refrigerator until the caramel is set. Once the caramel feels firm, they're ready to serve or store.
Can you guide me through making Fig Bars II? I'm setting out the bowl and pan now.

Absolutely. Pull together 1 cup white sugar, 3 eggs, 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking powder. You'll also want the seasonings and vanilla ready for the flour mixture: salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice.
I've got the eggs and sugar on the counter. Should the oven be heating while I measure the dry ingredients?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C. While it heats, measure the flour and baking powder so they're ready to sift.
The oven is on. I'm using a 9x13 inch pan—how should I prep it?
Grease the 9x13 inch baking pan well, then dust it with flour. Tap out any excess so the bars release cleanly after baking.
Pan is greased and floured. For the batter, do I combine the eggs with the sugar right away?
Yes. In a large bowl, beat the 3 eggs with the 1 cup white sugar until the mixture looks thick and pale. That texture matters, so give it enough time to lighten.
It's getting lighter but still a little loose. What should it look like before I stop beating?
Look for a noticeably paler color and a thicker consistency that falls from the beaters in soft ribbons. Once it reaches that point, you're ready to add the dry mixture.
Okay, the egg mixture is thick and pale. How do I handle the flour and spices?
Sift together the 7/8 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice. Sifting helps spread the baking powder and spices evenly.
The dry ingredients are sifted. Do I stir them in all at once, and where does the vanilla go?
Blend the sifted dry ingredients into the egg mixture along with the vanilla. Stir just until everything is incorporated, then spread the batter into your prepared pan.
I'm making Chicken Vegetable Stew and I've got a large pot out. Can you guide me through it while I prep?
Absolutely. Start by getting the main ingredients ready: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into bite-size pieces, 1 chopped onion, 1/2 pound baby carrots, and 4 potatoes.
The chicken is cut up and the onion is chopped. Should I peel or chop the potatoes before they go in?

Cut the potatoes into stew-friendly chunks so they cook evenly with the chicken and carrots. Once they're ready, put the chopped onion, chicken breast pieces, baby carrots, and potatoes into the large pot.
Everything is in the pot now, but it looks pretty full. Is that okay before I add seasoning?
That's fine for a stew as long as there's room to stir. Sprinkle in the salt and turmeric, then gently turn the ingredients so the seasoning reaches the chicken and vegetables.
I've added the salt and turmeric. I also have tomato paste—do I just spoon it straight into the pot?
Dissolve the tomato paste in water first so it blends smoothly instead of staying in clumps. Pour that tomato mixture into the pot once it's loosened.
The tomato paste is mixed with water and added. Should the liquid cover the vegetables completely?

The recipe only says to dissolve the tomato paste in water and add it, so don't worry about forcing a specific level. Give the pot a careful stir so the tomato mixture, turmeric, chicken, carrots, onion, and potatoes are distributed.
It smells good already. I found garlic powder and ground black pepper in the cabinet—do they belong in this?
Yes, those are optional seasonings here. If you want a little more flavor, add garlic powder and ground black pepper to taste, then stir again.
I added a light shake of both. Anything I should check before I let it cook down?

Make sure the chicken pieces are separated rather than stuck together, the potatoes are tucked into the liquid as much as possible, and the seasonings are mixed through. After that, let it cook until the chicken is done and the potatoes and carrots are tender.
Can you help me make Basic Chicken Stock? I've got a large pot out but haven't prepped anything yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound chicken parts, 1 large onion, 3 stalks celery with some leaves, and 1 large carrot. You'll also need salt and cloves when everything goes into the pot.
The chicken is ready, and I found a big yellow onion. Should I peel and dice it?
Peel it if the outer skin is papery, then quarter the onion. No need to dice it finely for stock.
Onion is quartered. My celery has leaves on the inside stalks—do those go in too?
Yes, include some of those leaves. Scrub the celery and the carrot, then chop both into 1 inch chunks.
I'm cutting the carrot now. Is it okay if the pieces are a little uneven?
That's fine for stock. Aim for roughly 1 inch chunks so they release flavor well without needing careful presentation.
Vegetables are chopped. Do I brown the chicken first or just add everything?
For this basic stock, just place the chicken pieces, quartered onion, chopped celery, chopped carrot, salt, and cloves into your large soup pot or Dutch oven.
Everything is in the Dutch oven. How much water should I add?
Pour in 6 cups water, making sure the chicken and vegetables are sitting in the water.
Done. The pot looks full but not crowded. Anything to check before I turn on the stove?
Give it a quick look to confirm the chicken parts, onion, celery, carrot, salt, cloves, and 6 cups water are all in the pot. Then you're ready to start cooking the stock.
I want to make Feta Chicken Salad for lunch. Can you guide me while I prep everything?

Absolutely. Set out a serving bowl and a smaller mixing bowl. For the salad base, you'll need 3 cups diced cooked chicken, 2 large stalks celery diced, 1 red bell pepper seeded and diced, and 1/2 red onion diced.
The chicken is already diced, and I've got the celery on the board. Should the bell pepper and onion be chopped about the same size?

Yes, aim for small, even dice so everything mixes well and you get a bit of crunch in each bite. Seed the red bell pepper before dicing it, and dice the 1/2 red onion fairly finely if you want it to blend in more gently.
Done. I have the serving bowl ready—what should go into it first?
Add the diced cooked chicken, diced celery, and diced red onion to the serving bowl, then give them a quick toss so they're evenly distributed.
Do I add the red bell pepper to that bowl too, or hold it back?
Add the diced red bell pepper in with the chicken mixture as well. Stir it through gently so the vegetables are spread evenly without mashing anything.
The salad base looks mixed. I've got a smaller bowl for the creamy part—what goes in there?
In the separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the dressing looks creamy with the feta distributed throughout.
The feta is a little chunky. Should I smooth it out completely?
It doesn't need to be perfectly smooth. Small feta pieces are good here; just stir enough that the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill are combined into a dressing.
Okay, dressing is mixed. How do I combine it without making the chicken salad mushy?
Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and fold everything together with a spoon or spatula until coated. Taste it, then season with salt and pepper as needed before serving.
I'm making Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon. Can you help me get set up before I start soaking anything?
Absolutely. You'll need a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank, 6 salmon fillets that are 4 ounces each, 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, and 1 large red onion, chopped.
I have the salmon and onion ready. For the plank, does it need any prep before it goes near the grill?
Yes. Submerge the untreated cedar plank completely in water so it can soak through instead of scorching right away on the grill.
How long should I leave it underwater? I'm trying to plan the timing.
Let it soak approximately 12 hours, or overnight. If you can weigh it down with a bowl or pot so it stays fully submerged, that helps.
The plank has soaked overnight, and the salmon fillets are still chilled. What should I do with the grill?
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat. Give it time to get properly hot before you add the plank.
Should the onion and olive oil be ready by the grill, or can they wait?
Have them ready nearby: the chopped large red onion and the 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil are part of the salmon setup, so it's easier if they're prepped before the plank goes on.
The grill is hot now. Do I put the wet plank directly on the grate?
Yes, place the prepared soaked plank on the grill. Once it's positioned, sprinkle it with coarse salt.
Any quick check before I start arranging the 6 fillets?
Make sure the plank is untreated, well soaked, and sitting securely on the high-heat grill with the coarse salt added. Then you're ready to work with the 6 salmon fillets.

Set out 1 whole chicken, about 2 to 3 pounds, cut into pieces, plus 1 tablespoon olive oil for the skillet. You'll also want a large skillet ready for medium high heat.

messages.content: For the Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake, can we keep the garnish pared down to my usual two-part finish?
Yes. We'll keep the top simple: use one finishing touch for flavor and one for crunch, and leave off any extra decorative bits.
Perfect. Before I start crushing anything, what should be on the counter?
Set out 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies and 1/4 cup melted margarine. You'll also want a 9-inch springform pan or pie plate ready.
I've got the pan and the margarine melted. Should the ice cream come out now too?
Yes, bring out the 2 quarts vanilla ice cream so it can soften a bit while you build the crust. Keep 1 cup hot fudge topping nearby as well.
And that simple ending is exactly the way I like doing this kind of cake. How do I start the base?
Crush about half of the cookies, roughly 20 small cookies, until they're crumbs. A bag and rolling pin works well if you want less cleanup.
The crumbs are done, but they're a little uneven. Is that okay?
A few tiny chunks are fine. Stir the crumbs together with the melted margarine until they look evenly moistened.
They're mixed. Do I press them into just the center or all the way out?
Press the crumb mixture firmly across the bottom of the 9-inch springform pan or pie plate, going all the way to the edges so the crust holds together.
The crust is packed in. What happens with the cookies I didn't crush?
Stand the remaining cookies upright around the edge of the pan. Nestle them close together so they make a cookie wall.
The cookie border is in place, and the fudge is warm enough to spread. How should I finish this layer?
Spread 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the crust in an even layer. After that, you'll be set up for the softened vanilla ice cream and the restrained two-part garnish.

messages.content: Can you help me make Caramel Chocolate Corn? I've got a big bowl ready, but I want to make sure I set everything up in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by measuring out 16 cups of popped popcorn and 1 cup of roasted peanuts. Keep them nearby, since they'll get combined before the coating is mixed.
The popcorn is popped and measured, and I have the peanuts too. What should I pull out for the caramel part?
You'll need 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter for the caramel mixture. The recipe also has you combine those with corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in a microwave-safe bowl.
Got it. Before I start heating anything, what pan or tray prep should I do?

Should I put the loaf pans on a sheet pan right away, and what temperature should the oven be?

Set the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. Then grease and flour two 9 x 5 inch loaf pans; you can place them on a sheet pan once they're filled to make moving them easier and catch any overflow.
I'm clearing counter space. Which measured ingredients should be closest to the mixing bowl?
Keep these within reach: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 3 eggs, 2 cups white sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil. You'll also need the applesauce, then sour cream or buttermilk for the blending stage.
I'd like to keep cleanup simple. Do I start with the wet ingredients in one big bowl?
Yes, use a large bowl for the eggs, sugar, and oil. Beat those together until they look smooth and evenly combined, then keep the measured flour nearby without crowding your workspace.
That route is the one I usually like for this kind of loaf.
It suits this bread well: the sheet pan makes the loaf pans easier to handle, and the brief uncovered rest helps the crust and surface settle before slicing.
The eggs, sugar, and oil are mixed and glossy. What goes in next?
Blend in the applesauce now. Once that's worked through the mixture, add the sour cream or buttermilk and mix until the batter looks consistent.
The pans are greased and floured. Should I divide everything between both pans?
Yes, portion the batter evenly into the two prepared 9 x 5 inch loaf pans. Set them on the sheet pan carefully so both pans stay level going into the oven.
When the loaves come out, how should I handle them before serving?
Set the loaves where air can circulate and leave them uncovered briefly before serving. Check that the texture has settled, then slice once they're sturdy enough to handle cleanly.
Can you guide me through making Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches? I'm starting with the vegetables and want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Get the vegetables ready first: finely chop 1 small onion, dice 1 medium tomato, chop 1 stalk of celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper.
The onion and tomato are done. Should the celery and bell pepper be small pieces too?
Yes, keep them fairly small so the topping spreads evenly and cooks quickly under the broiler. Once they're chopped, put all the vegetables into a medium bowl.
They're in the bowl. What else goes into the mixture?
Stir in the cheese, chili powder, and salt with the onion, tomato, celery, and bell pepper until everything is evenly combined.
Before I mix too much, should I turn the oven on?
Yes, preheat your oven's broiler now so it's hot by the time the sandwiches are assembled.
Broiler is heating. What pan should I use for the bread?
Lay the bread slices on a baking sheet or a broiling pan in a single layer, leaving a little space between them if you can.
The bread is on the pan. How much topping goes on each slice?
Spoon 1/4 of the vegetable-cheese mixture onto each slice, then spread it all the way out to the edges so every bite gets topping.
Should the edges be covered even if the mixture is chunky?
Yes. Press and spread the chunky bits gently so the topping is even across the bread, then the sandwiches are ready to go under the broiler.
Can you guide me through Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style? I already put a spaghetti squash on the counter.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded, plus 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 cans of stewed tomatoes, 14 ounces each.
I've got the onion, garlic, and tomatoes. Should I get the oven going before I cut the squash?
Yes, preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C. While it heats, halve the squash lengthwise and scoop out the seeds.
The squash is cut and seeded. What pan setup do you want?
Use a baking sheet and coat it with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash doesn't stick while it bakes.

Place the squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
They're on the sheet now. How long should I bake them?
Bake the squash in the preheated oven for 35 minutes, or until a knife can be inserted easily into the flesh.
While it bakes, should I chop the onion pretty fine?
A regular chopped onion texture is fine here. Keep the chopped onion, minced garlic, and stewed tomatoes ready for the lasagna-style part after the squash softens.

Use the knife check rather than only the timer: after 35 minutes, the squash should be tender enough that a knife slides in easily.
Can you walk me through making Chocolate Covered Pretzels? I've got a counter cleared and want to set things up right.

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler, something for stirring, and wax paper for the coated pretzels to cool on.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips out. Does the cream go in with the chocolate right away?
Yes. Put the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream together in the top of the double boiler. Keep the heat low so the chocolate melts gently instead of scorching.
The water is simmering under the bowl. How much should I stir while it melts?
Stir constantly while the chocolate and cream melt. You're looking for a smooth, glossy mixture that stays very warm for dipping.
It's smooth now. Should I dump in a handful of pretzels or do them separately?
Dip the pretzels 1 at a time. Work quickly so each pretzel gets coated while the chocolate mixture is still very warm.
They're a little drippy when I lift them out. Is that okay?
That's fine. Let the extra chocolate drip back into the double boiler for a moment, then transfer each coated pretzel to the wax paper.
I've got wax paper laid out. Do they need spacing?
Give them a little space so they don't stick together as they set. Place each dipped pretzel on the wax paper and leave them there to cool.
Once they're all on the wax paper, is there anything else I should do before serving?
Just let them set and cool fully on the wax paper. Once the chocolate is firm, they're ready to serve or pack up.

Absolutely. Have 16 cups popped popcorn ready, plus 1 cup roasted peanuts. You'll also need 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter for the caramel mixture.

Yes—grease your cookie sheets before you start coating the popcorn. That way the caramel corn has somewhere ready to go once it's mixed.
Cookie sheets are greased. Do I keep the popcorn in the bowl or move it somewhere else?
Move the popcorn and the roasted peanuts into a paper bag. The bag gives you room to shake everything together later.
All 16 cups of popcorn and the 1 cup of peanuts are in the paper bag. Do I close it up now?
You can fold the top loosely for now, but mainly just set the bag aside while you make the caramel mixture.
I'm at the microwave. What bowl should I use for the sugar and butter?
Use a microwave-safe bowl, with enough space for stirring. Add the 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter to it.
The brown sugar and butter are in the bowl. The recipe also mentions corn syrup, vanilla, and salt—do those go in now too?
Yes, combine the corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in that same microwave-safe bowl with the sugar and butter.
Everything for the caramel base is in the bowl. Before I microwave it, should the popcorn bag just stay off to the side?
Exactly. Keep the popcorn and peanuts set aside in the paper bag while the caramel mixture is prepared, and keep the greased cookie sheets nearby for when you're ready to spread it out.
I want to make Churros today. Can you guide me through the setup before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Put a small saucepan on the counter and measure out 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil.
I've got the water, sugar, salt, and oil measured. Should the saucepan be heated before everything goes in?
Set the saucepan over medium heat, then add the water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, the salt, and the 2 tablespoons vegetable oil together.
Everything is in the pan over medium heat. Am I waiting for a simmer or a full boil?
Let it come all the way to a boil. As soon as it reaches that point, remove the saucepan from the heat.
It boiled and I moved it off the burner. What texture should I look for when adding the flour?
Stir in the flour while the mixture is off the heat, mixing until it comes together and forms a ball.
The dough is clumping together into one ball now. Should I start heating the frying oil?
Yes. Heat oil for frying in a deep-fryer or a deep skillet until it reaches 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
I'm using a deep skillet. Any practical check before I fry, since the oil is getting hot?
Keep the skillet steady and use a thermometer if you have one, aiming to hold the oil at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) before adding the dough.

Combine 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat; bring it to a boil and remove it from heat; stir in flour until the mixture forms a ball; then heat frying oil in a deep-fryer or deep skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Cut the French baguette in half lengthwise, then you'll be ready to build the sandwiches with the broiled eggplant and red pepper.

Start with the dry ingredients you'll measure: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt.

Absolutely. Put out three shallow bowls if you have them. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour into one bowl, and keep 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs ready for a second bowl.

Stir 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper into the Italian-style bread crumbs so the seasoning is evenly mixed through.

Keep them separate. Put the eggs and water together in a small bowl, then beat them lightly so the mixture can coat the chicken smoothly.

Work with one piece of chicken at a time: coat it in the flour first, dip it into the eggs and water, then cover it with the seasoned bread crumbs.

Roll each tender through the crumbs, then gently press so the coating sticks. Try to cover the whole surface before moving the piece aside.

Set each breaded tender aside on a plate or tray as you finish it, keeping the pieces in a single layer so the coating doesn't rub off.
A little flour is clumping in the egg bowl. Is that a problem?
A few clumps are fine. Just keep going one piece at a time, using the flour, then the eggs and water, then the bread crumbs, and set the coated chicken aside when each piece is done.

The oats, coconut, flour, and baking soda are measured. Should I combine anything before using the saucepan?
Yes. In a mixing bowl, stir together the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut until the coconut and oats look evenly distributed.
The dry bowl is mixed. What kind of pan should I use for the syrup and butter?
Use a small saucepan and keep the heat low. Add the syrup and butter, then let them melt together gently so the mixture becomes smooth rather than browned.
The butter is almost melted into the syrup. Do I stir it constantly?
Give it a few slow stirs as it melts, just enough to help the butter blend into the syrup. Keep the heat low the whole time.
It's melted and smooth now. What do I do with the baking soda?
Mix the baking soda with the boiling water, then add that mixture to the melted butter and syrup in the saucepan.
It foamed a bit when I added the soda water. Is that okay?
Yes, that reaction is expected. Once it's combined, pour the butter mixture into the bowl of dry ingredients.
The wet mixture is in the bowl with the oats and coconut. How much mixing should I do?
Stir until the dry ingredients are evenly moistened and you don't see loose flour. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl so the butter mixture is worked through everything.
I want to make Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf. Can you guide me from the prep stage?

Absolutely. Start by getting the oven ready and setting out the ingredients you'll need: 12 ounces chopped raw bacon, 1 small white onion chopped, 5 button mushrooms chopped, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef.
I've got the beef in the fridge and the bacon open. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the meatloaf mixture is ready later.
While it heats, I'm chopping the onion and mushrooms. How small should they be?
Chop the small white onion and the 5 button mushrooms into fairly small pieces so they'll mix evenly with the beef and bacon later.

Put the 12 ounces of chopped raw bacon into the skillet and cook it over medium heat. Stir it around as it cooks so the pieces brown evenly.
The bacon is sizzling and giving off a lot of fat. Am I waiting for crisp pieces or just browned?
Cook it until the bacon pieces are browned. They don't need to be dried out completely, but they should have good color before you take them out.
The pieces look browned now. What's the cleanest way to pull them from the pan?
Use a slotted spoon to lift the bacon out of the skillet, letting extra grease drain back into the pan, then transfer the bacon to paper towels.
The bacon is draining on paper towels, and there's still grease in the skillet. How much should I keep?
Discard the excess bacon grease, leaving just 1 tablespoon in the skillet. That keeps the bacon flavor without making the mixture overly greasy.
Can you help me make Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men? I'm setting up my mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Put out a large bowl and gather 1/2 cup margarine and 1/2 cup sugar to start the dough base.
The bowl is ready, and I've measured the margarine and sugar. Should they go in together?
Yes. Add both to the large bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks smooth rather than streaky.
It's looking smooth. I also have molasses nearby—how much goes in?

Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. That will firm it up so it's easier to handle for gingerbread men.

Use a large stockpot or turkey fryer, and make sure it's positioned safely before adding heat. Also get a large platter ready and line it with food-safe paper bags for later.
I've got the fryer and platter ready. How much space do I need to leave for the turkey in the oil?
Leave plenty of room in the pot or fryer for the turkey to displace the oil. If it's filled too high, the oil can spill over when the turkey goes in.

Use the 1/4 cup Creole seasoning to season the turkey once it's dry. Keep the 1 white onion with your prepared ingredients so it's ready for the recipe.

Check that the oil is at 400 degrees F, the fryer still has room for the turkey without spilling over, and the turkey is thoroughly patted dry. Keep that lined platter nearby for when you need a place to set the cooked turkey.

Seal it fully so flour doesn't escape, then shake the bag until the beef pieces are evenly coated with flour.

Heat the olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Once it's hot, add the coated beef and brown it on all sides.

Let the pieces sit long enough to brown, then turn them so each side gets color. Try not to crowd the skillet too much while browning.

Transfer the browned beef from the skillet into the slow cooker. That completes the recipe's listed prep before the slow-cooker stage.

Leave the tender herbs as bigger leaves rather than chopping them finely, and set them together in a little cluster off to one side of the bowl.
That's the version I'm going with. I've got a big salad bowl and serving bowls out—what should I put on the counter before I start assembling?
Set out 1 pound of bocconcini, the bite-size mozzarella balls, plus 8 cherry tomatoes cut in half. Since you're building bowls, also have your rice or noodles ready to use as the base.

Whisk the lemon juice and olive oil together first, then pour that over the salad. Season it to taste with salt and pepper after the dressing goes on.

Toss gently but thoroughly, lifting from the bottom and turning the ingredients until everything is coated with the lemon-olive oil dressing.
It's coated now. Since this is going over rice or noodles, should I add the basil before or after it goes into the serving bowls?
Portion the rice or noodles into the bowls, spoon the dressed salad over the top, then sprinkle the basil over the salad right before serving.

Place that small pile of larger soft-herb leaves at one edge of each bowl, separate from the basil sprinkle, and serve immediately.

Cover it and process until the batter looks smooth, with no dry flour streaks left.

I want to make Crab Quiche today. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Put a 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust on the counter, and have 4 eggs ready nearby.
The crust and eggs are out. What should I grab from the fridge or pantry?
You'll need 1 cup heavy cream and 1/2 teaspoon salt. The filling step also uses pepper and hot sauce, so keep those within reach too.

Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready for the crust.
The oven is warming. Do I bake the frozen crust as-is?
Bake the pie crust for about 10 minutes, just until it's starting to brown.
It's been about 10 minutes and the edges are lightly browned. Do I leave it in?
Take it out of the oven now and let it cool before you add the filling.
The crust is cooling on the counter. What bowl size should I use for the filling?
Use a large bowl so you have room to whisk the 4 eggs smoothly with the cream and seasonings.
I've got the large bowl ready. What exactly goes in?
Whisk together the eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, pepper, and hot sauce until the mixture is even and well combined.
I want to make Dads Flat Bread this afternoon. Can you guide me from the counter setup onward?

Absolutely. Set out 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast, 2 cups warm water at 110 degrees to 115 degrees, 1/3 cup sugar, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. Keep the water divided, because only part of it goes in at the beginning.
I've got the yeast packet and the warm water measured. How much water goes into the bowl with the yeast?
Use a large mixing bowl and stir the yeast into 1/2 cup of the warm water until it dissolves. Save the rest of the water for the next mixing stage.
The yeast is dissolved in the bowl. Should I add the sugar and oil right away?

Yes. Add the 1/3 cup sugar and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, then add the salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining warm water. Beat the mixture until it looks smooth.
I'm beating it now. If it's smooth but still pretty loose, is that expected before adding more flour?
That's fine at this point. Once the mixture is smooth, start adding enough of the remaining all-purpose flour to bring it together into a soft dough rather than a batter.
How should the dough feel when I stop adding flour?
Stop when it holds together as a soft dough and is manageable enough to turn out, but don't make it stiff or dry. A little tackiness is okay before kneading.
My counter is floured and the dough is out of the bowl. What's the kneading goal?
Knead it on the floured surface until it becomes smooth and elastic. Plan on about 6-8 minutes, adding only enough flour to keep it workable.
After a few minutes it's starting to stretch better. Should I keep going until the full time is up?
Keep kneading until it feels springy and smooth; if that happens near the 8-minute mark, you're right on track. Once it's elastic, you've completed this mixing and kneading stage for Dads Flat Bread.
I want to make Famous Caramel Cookie Bars. Can you guide me through the prep so I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Set out 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels with the wrappers removed, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips.
I've got the cookies and caramels ready, and the wrappers are off. What should I do with the cookies?
Lay the shortbread cookies in a single layer on a baking sheet or tray so each one is easy to reach when the caramel is ready.
They're lined up on the tray. Should the caramel go in a pot with the water now?
Yes. Put the unwrapped caramels and the 1/4 cup water into a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir frequently so the caramels melt evenly and don't catch on the bottom.
The caramel is starting to loosen but there are still a few lumps. Should I turn the heat up?
Keep it at medium-low and keep stirring. Once the caramel is smooth enough to spoon, take your time working with it while it's still pourable.
It's smooth now. How much caramel goes on each shortbread cookie?
Spoon a thin line of caramel over each cookie. Aim for a narrow strip rather than covering the whole cookie, so the caramel sets neatly.
Some lines are thicker than others. Is that a problem before chilling?
That's fine. If any spots are very heavy, you can gently nudge the caramel with the spoon, then transfer the tray to the refrigerator.
How long do they stay in the fridge, and what am I looking for?
Refrigerate the cookies until the caramel is set. They're ready for the next handling or serving once the caramel feels firm enough that it doesn't smear when touched lightly.
I want to make Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing for lunch. Can you guide me through the prep?

Absolutely. Since this is a quick assembly salad, set out a medium bowl for the chicken mixture and a small bowl for the dressing. You'll need 4 cups rotisserie chicken, skinned and boned, with the meat shredded into bite-sized pieces.
The chicken is shredded. What vegetables should I prep before mixing?
Dice 2 medium celery ribs into small pieces, then thinly slice 2 medium green onions. Keep them close to the chicken bowl so everything can go in together.
Celery and green onions are ready. Do the peanuts go in now or later?
Add them now with the chicken, celery, and green onions. Use 1/4 cup chopped honey-roasted peanuts, then give the mixture a light toss so the pieces are evenly distributed.
That bowl is mixed. I have a small bowl ready for the dressing—what goes into it?
Whisk together the lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, and mint in the small bowl. Add 2 Tbs. water as you whisk to loosen the dressing.
Should the dressing be smooth, or is it okay if the herbs stay visible?
The herbs will stay visible, and that's fine. You're looking for the sugar to dissolve and the fish sauce, lime juice, ginger, red pepper, cilantro, mint, and water to blend into a pourable dressing.
It smells balanced now. Do I pour all of it over the chicken mixture?
Yes, toss the dressing with the chicken mixture. Fold gently so the shredded rotisserie chicken stays in bite-sized pieces while the celery, green onions, and peanuts get coated.
I'm serving it right away. How should I plate it?

Arrange a bed of Boston lettuce on the serving plate or bowl, then spoon the dressed chicken salad over it. Add any suggested accompaniments alongside, and serve while the celery and peanuts still have their crunch.

Perfect, that's the one I want just for tonight. Before anything heats, what should I measure out?
For the dredge, measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour and 2 teaspoons salt into a shallow bowl so the chops can be coated easily.
The shallow bowl is out. Are there any seasonings I should add before the pork touches it?
Yes—add 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder to that same bowl, then stir the flour mixture until it looks evenly speckled.
I've got the dry mix combined. Should I coat the chops right away or set up the skillet first?
Set the skillet with oil first so it's ready for browning, then dredge each pork chop in the flour, salt, mustard, and garlic powder mixture.

Brown the chops on both sides in the skillet; you're looking for color on the coating, not cooking them all the way through there.
They have color on each side now. Since we're using trays tonight, where do they go?
Move the browned chops onto the 2 trays in a single layer, giving them a little space so the oven heat can reach the coating.
They're spread out. What happens with the soup and water?
Combine the soup and water until smooth, then pour that mixture over the chops so each tray gets some of the sauce.
Both trays are sauced. Any last handling note before they go in?
Slide in both trays, rotate them once during cooking, and when they're done, bring them straight out for serving rather than holding them for a final rest.
I'm making Crawfish Chowder and want to get the skillet work right. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup butter, 1/2 bunch green onions chopped, another 1/2 cup butter, and 2 pounds frozen cleaned crawfish.
The crawfish are frozen but cleaned. Should I start with the onions or the crawfish?
Start with the onions. Put a large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter in it.
The butter is mostly melted and foaming a bit. Do the green onions go in now?
Yes, add the chopped 1/2 bunch green onions to that butter and sauté them until they're tender.
They're softening and smell good. Should I brown them or keep them gentle?
Keep it gentle; the recipe only calls for them to become tender, not browned.

Take the green onions out of the pan and set them aside so you can use the same skillet for the crawfish.
The skillet has a little butter left in it. Do I wipe it out before adding more?
No need to wipe it. In that same skillet, melt the 1/2 cup butter.
The 1/2 cup butter is melted. How long should the crawfish cook?
Add the 2 pounds frozen cleaned crawfish and sauté them in the butter for 5 minutes, then set them aside.
I want to make Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style. Can you help me get set up before I start cutting anything?
Absolutely. Put out 1 spaghetti squash, then halve it lengthwise and scoop out the seeds if you haven't already. You'll also want 1 chopped onion ready for the lasagna-style mixture.
The squash is halved and seeded, and the onion is chopped. What other ingredients should be on the counter?
Have 2 tablespoons minced garlic nearby, plus 2 cans of stewed tomatoes, 14 ounces each. For the baking part, you'll also need a baking sheet and a little cooking spray.
Got it. Should I heat the oven now, and to what temperature?
Yes, start preheating the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
The oven is warming up. How should I prep the baking sheet so the squash doesn't stick?
Give the baking sheet a thin, even coating of cooking spray. It only needs a light layer.
The sheet is sprayed. Do the squash halves go skin side down or cut side down?
Place the squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet. That helps the flesh steam and soften as it bakes.
They're on the sheet cut side down. How long should I bake them?
Bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated oven.
When the timer goes off, how do I know if it needs more time?
Check it with a knife: the squash is ready when a knife can be easily inserted into the flesh. If it still feels firm, give it a little more time and check again.
I want to make Eggnog Blend today. Can you guide me through what to set out before I start heating anything?

Absolutely. Put out 4 cups half-and-half, 1 cup white sugar, 11 beaten egg yolks, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also need a saucepan, a whisk, and room in the refrigerator for chilling the mixture overnight.
The half-and-half and sugar are measured. Should those go straight into the saucepan together?
Yes. Set the saucepan over low heat, add the half-and-half and white sugar, and stir gently so the sugar dissolves without the dairy getting too hot.
The sugar is dissolving slowly. When do the beaten yolks go in?
Whisk the beaten egg yolks in gradually while the pan stays on low heat. Keep the whisk moving so the yolks blend smoothly into the warm half-and-half.
I'm worried about scrambling the eggs. What should the mixture look like as it cooks?

You're aiming for a light custard. It should thicken gently, but do not let it boil. If you see bubbling or it starts heating too fast, lower the heat or briefly lift the pan off the burner while whisking.
It's starting to coat the whisk a little and there's no boiling. Is that enough?
That sounds right for a light custard. Take it off the heat, let it cool, then transfer it to the refrigerator to chill overnight.
Should I cover it before refrigerating, or leave it open while it chills?
Let it cool first, then cover it before refrigerating so it stays clean and doesn't pick up other fridge flavors during the overnight chill.
It's the next day and the mixture is cold. How do I complete the eggnog?
Stir the vanilla into the chilled mixture, then stir in the cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream until the Eggnog Blend is smooth and ready to serve.
