Set the sifted flour, baking soda, and salt mixture aside.
I'm making the Awesome Turkey Sandwich for lunch. Can you guide me through it while I get the counter set up?

Absolutely. Put out 2 slices of whole wheat bread; you can toast them if you want a firmer sandwich. You'll also need 1 tablespoon mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard, and 3 slices smoked turkey breast.
The bread is toasted and cooling on a plate. Should the spreads go on while it's still a little warm?
Yes, slightly warm toast is fine. Spread the mayonnaise on one slice, then spread the Dijon mustard on the other slice so each piece of bread has its own layer.
I measured the mayo and mustard. Do I spread them all the way to the crust?
Spread them close to the edges so the flavor is even, but don't overload the corners. The 1 tablespoon mayonnaise and 2 teaspoons Dijon should make a thin, steady coating.
Both slices are spread. I have the smoked turkey opened—how should I place it?
Lay the 3 slices of smoked turkey breast on one side of the sandwich, overlapping them a bit so the turkey covers the bread evenly.
Turkey is on the mayo side. The recipe mentions guacamole next; how thick should that be?
Spread the guacamole right over the turkey in an even layer. Keep it thick enough to taste, but not so much that it squeezes out when you close the sandwich.
Guacamole is on. I've got salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese ready beside the plate.
Pile those on over the guacamole: add the salad greens, then bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese. Try to keep the taller ingredients centered so the sandwich closes neatly.
It's stacked pretty high. Any trick for serving it without everything sliding out?
Place the mustard-coated slice on top, press gently with your palm, and cut the sandwich in half with a sharp knife. If it feels loose, hold each half with a toothpick while serving.
I want to make Chili For Two. Can you guide me from prep through serving?
Absolutely. Set out a saucepan and gather 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 garlic clove minced, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can chili beans. Keep the beans undrained.
The beef and onion are ready, but I still need to mince the garlic. Should the beans be opened now too?
Yes, go ahead and open the chili beans so they're ready to pour in later, liquid and all. Mince the garlic before you start heating the pan so the first cooking part moves smoothly.
Garlic is minced and the saucepan is on the stove. What heat should I use for the beef mixture?
Use medium heat. Add the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic to the saucepan, then cook while breaking up the beef until the meat is no longer pink.
The beef has browned and I can see some fat in the pan. Do I drain it before adding beans?
Yes. Carefully drain off the excess fat after the beef is no longer pink, then return the saucepan to the burner.
Drained and back on the stove. The pan looks a little dry—do the chili beans go in with their liquid?
They do. Stir in the 15.5 ounce can of chili beans undrained, mixing them through the beef, onion, and garlic.
Everything is stirred together. Should I bring it up slowly or turn the heat higher?
Bring it to a boil from here. You can raise the heat a bit if needed, but stir occasionally so the chili doesn't catch on the bottom.
It just started bubbling around the edges and then more in the center. How long should it simmer?
Reduce the heat, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer for 10-15 minutes, until the chili is heated through. Give it an occasional stir, then serve it hot.
I'd like to make Escargots Vol au Vent—can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Put your oven on to preheat at 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's ready when you need it.
Oven is heating. For the snails, I have 12 helix snails without shells—do they need any prep before mixing?
Yes. Drain the escargots, rinse them under cold water, then drain them again well so they don't water down the butter mixture.
They're rinsed and sitting in the strainer. What should I do with the butter?
Use 1/2 cup softened butter and place it in a mixing bowl. Softened is best because it will blend smoothly with the seasonings.
The butter is in the bowl. I've got garlic and green onion on the board—how much goes in?
Finely chop 2 cloves garlic and 1 green onion, then add both to the bowl with the softened butter.
Garlic and green onion are added. The recipe also mentions parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine—do those go in now too?
They do. Add the parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine to the same mixing bowl with the butter, garlic, and green onion.
Everything for the butter mixture is in the bowl. Should I stir gently or really work it together?
Mix it thoroughly so the garlic, green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine are evenly distributed through the butter.
The mixture looks even now. Is there anything else I should check before using it with the escargots?
Just make sure the escargots are well drained and the butter mixture is cohesive. You're set to continue assembling the Escargots Vol au Vent from there.
I'm making Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks today. Can you help me set up the marinade without getting ahead of myself?
Absolutely. Put a medium bowl on the counter, along with a whisk and a large resealable bag. For the marinade, measure 3 tablespoons soy sauce and 1/2 cup vegetable oil into the bowl.
The soy sauce and oil are in. I also see sherry and fresh ginger here—how much of each goes in?
Add 2 tablespoons sherry, then grate in 1 teaspoon fresh ginger root. The recipe also calls for garlic in the whisked mixture, so add that with the marinade ingredients if you have it ready.
Everything is in the bowl. Should I whisk it a lot or just stir it together?
Whisk until the soy sauce, oil, sherry, ginger, and garlic look evenly combined. The oil may still separate a bit, but the mixture should look well blended before it goes into the bag.
The marinade looks combined. Is the bag the next thing, and should I set it in anything?
Yes. Open the large resealable bag and set it upright in a bowl or dish so it is easier to fill. Pour the marinade into the bag carefully.
The marinade is in the bag. I have the swordfish steaks ready—do I put them straight in?
Place the swordfish steaks into the bag with the marinade. Seal it most of the way, press out extra air, close it fully, then gently shake and turn the bag so the steaks are coated all over.
They're coated. I'm worried about leaks in the fridge—what's the safest way to store it?
Lay the sealed bag in a shallow dish or on a rimmed plate before refrigerating. That keeps the marinade contained if the bag drips.
How long should I leave the swordfish in the refrigerator before cooking?
Refrigerate the bag and let the swordfish steaks marinate at least 4 hours. Turn the bag once or twice during that time if you can, so the marinade stays evenly distributed.
I'm making Adobo Chicken with Ginger. Can you help me get set up before I start cooking?

Absolutely. Put a Dutch oven on the stove and gather 1 (3 pound) whole chicken cut into 8 pieces, 1/2 cup soy sauce, 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar, and 1 bulb garlic, peeled and crushed. You'll also need the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns for the braise.
The chicken is already cut up. Should I mix anything separately, or does it all go straight into the pot?
It can go straight into the Dutch oven. Add the chicken pieces, soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns together in the pot.
Do I need to brown the chicken first for this version?
Not for these directions. This version starts by simmering the chicken directly in the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Okay, everything is in the Dutch oven. What heat should I use?
Set it over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Keep an eye on it so the liquid comes up steadily without boiling over.
It's starting to bubble around the edges but isn't fully boiling yet.
Let it keep heating until the liquid reaches a real boil across the pot. Once it does, turn the heat down so it settles into a simmer.
It's boiling now, and I've lowered the heat. Should the lid go on right away?
Yes, cover the pot once it's at a simmer. Let the chicken cook covered for 30 minutes.
During that 30 minutes, do I just leave it alone?
Mostly let it simmer, but baste the chicken occasionally with the cooking liquid so the pieces stay coated as they cook.
I'm making Garden Party Salad today. Can you help me get the dressing started before I prep the salad bowl?
Absolutely. For the dressing ingredients you have listed, set out 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup orange marmalade, 3 tablespoons cider vinegar, and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise.
I've got the oil and marmalade measured. Should the marmalade go straight into a small bowl?
Yes, add the marmalade to a small bowl, then pour in the vegetable oil. The small bowl will make it easier to whisk the dressing smooth.
The oil and marmalade are in. I still need the vinegar and mayo, right?
Right. Add the cider vinegar and mayonnaise to that same bowl, then whisk everything together until the dressing looks smooth and combined.
It's coming together, but there are a few little marmalade streaks. Keep whisking?
Keep whisking briefly until those streaks mostly disappear. Once it's smooth, cover the bowl and chill the dressing.
The dressing is chilling. What should I set up for the salad part?
Use a large bowl for the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley. Since the recipe says to combine them just before serving, wait until you're close to eating before tossing them with the dressing.
We're about ready to serve. I have the chicken in the large bowl with the raisins, almonds, and parsley.
Great. Take the chilled dressing out, give it a quick whisk if it separated, then pour it over the chicken mixture.
Dressing is on. How much should I toss it?
Toss gently until the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley are evenly coated. Once everything is dressed, serve the Garden Party Salad right away.
I want to make Cabin Hash for dinner. Can you help me get set up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. Have 12 medium potatoes peeled, already cooked, and cubed, plus 3 cups of cubed fully cooked ham ready to go.
The potatoes and ham are ready. What else should I put by the stove?

Set out 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup butter or margarine. You'll also want a large skillet, a spoon or spatula for frequent stirring, salt, pepper, broccoli, and sour cream if you want it for serving.
Should the skillet be large enough for everything at once?
Yes, use a large skillet so the potatoes, ham, and onion can spread out and brown instead of just steaming.
I've got the skillet out. Do I melt the butter before adding the hash ingredients?
Melt the butter or margarine in the skillet, then add the cooked cubed potatoes, cubed ham, and chopped onion.
Everything is in the pan now. How active should I be with stirring?
Stir frequently as it cooks. Keep it moving enough to prevent sticking, but still give the potatoes contact with the skillet so they can become lightly browned.
The potatoes are starting to brown on the edges. Where does the broccoli come in?
Add the broccoli once the potatoes are lightly browned, then keep cooking just until the broccoli is heated through.
The broccoli is hot now, and the pan looks done. How should I season and serve it?
Season the Cabin Hash with salt and pepper to taste, then serve it hot. Add sour cream on the side or on top if you'd like.
I want to make Easy Punch for a group. Can you guide me through it while I set up the bowl?
Absolutely. Set out a large punch bowl and gather 4 packages of unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder, 0.13 ounce each, plus 2 cans of pineapple juice, 46 fluid ounces each.
The bowl is ready, and I found the drink mix and pineapple juice. What else should be on the counter?
You'll also need 3 cups white sugar and 4 quarts water. Keep a long spoon or ladle nearby so you can stir everything well.
I have the sugar, water, and a big spoon. Should I pour the powders in before the liquids?
Yes, that's fine. Add the strawberry drink mix powder to the punch bowl, then pour in the pineapple juice, add the 3 cups sugar, and pour in the 4 quarts water.
Everything is in the punch bowl. The powder and sugar are floating a bit on top.
Stir steadily, scraping through the bottom and around the sides of the bowl, until the drink mix and sugar are fully dissolved.
How can I tell it's dissolved enough?
The punch should look evenly colored, and you shouldn't feel gritty sugar at the bottom when you drag the spoon through it.
It looks smooth now. The last line mentions ginger ale, but I don't see an amount listed.
Right, the recipe says to stir in the ginger ale but doesn't give a quantity. Add the ginger ale you have gradually, stirring gently so you keep some fizz.
The ginger ale is mixed in. Should I serve it right away or do anything else?
You can serve it right away from the punch bowl. Give it one gentle stir before ladling, and keep it chilled if it will sit out for a while.
I'm making Gingery Fish Kabobs and want to get the sauce started. What should I set out?

Set out 2 cups pineapple juice, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, 2 tablespoons light soy sauce (50% less sodium), and 1 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar. You'll also need garlic and ginger, plus a small saucepan and a spoon or whisk.
I've got the small saucepan out. Should the cornstarch go in dry or with the juice?
Add the pineapple juice to the small saucepan, then whisk in the cornstarch until it dissolves and you don't see dry clumps.
The mixture looks smooth, but it's still cold. Do I add the other liquids before heating?
Yes. Stir in the light soy sauce and white vinegar now, then add the garlic and ginger so everything heats together.
The soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and ginger are in. Should I bring it to a boil?
Bring it up gently over heat, then keep it at a simmer rather than a hard boil. Stir now and then so the cornstarch thickens evenly.
How long should I plan to simmer it?
Simmer it until it's slightly thickened, about 7 minutes. It should look a little glossier and coat the spoon lightly.
It's starting to thicken around the edges. Should I keep stirring the whole time?
Give it regular stirs, especially around the edges and bottom of the saucepan, so it stays smooth while it finishes thickening.
It coats the spoon now and smells gingery. What do I do before using it on the kabobs?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the sauce cool. Once it has cooled down, it's ready to use with the Gingery Fish Kabobs.
I want to make Cinnamon Rolls I with the bread machine. Can you guide me while I set up?

Absolutely. Start by checking the dough ingredients you'll load into the machine: 1 cup warm water at 110 degrees F, 1 egg, 3 cups bread flour, and 1/4 cup white sugar. You'll also need powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast for the same bread-machine step.
The water is warm and I have the egg out. Should the flour and sugar go right by the machine too?
Yes, keep the 3 cups bread flour and 1/4 cup white sugar next to the bread machine so you can add everything in the manufacturer's recommended order.
I also see powdered milk, salt, butter, and yeast in the recipe instructions. Are those part of the dough load?
They are. Add the water, egg, bread flour, white sugar, powdered milk, salt, 5 tablespoons butter, and yeast to the bread machine in the order your machine's manual suggests.
Everything is in the bread machine. Which setting am I using?
Choose the DOUGH setting, then turn the machine on. Let it handle the mixing and rising while you work on the saucepan mixture.
While the dough cycle starts, what should I put in the saucepan?
Use a small saucepan and melt 1/3 cup butter over the heat. Keep it moving just enough so it melts evenly.
The butter has melted. What gets added to it?
Stir in 1/2 cup brown sugar and the ice cream. Once they're combined, bring the mixture to a boil.
It's starting to bubble. How long should I let that cook?
Once it reaches a boil, cook it for 2 minutes. After that, take it off the heat and keep it ready for the next part of the cinnamon rolls.
I want to make Chocolate Covered Pretzels. Can you help me set up so the coating goes smoothly?

Absolutely. Put out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler, a spoon or spatula for constant stirring, and wax paper ready for the coated pretzels.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips measured. Should the wax paper be laid out before I melt anything?
Yes, lay the wax paper out now. Once the chocolate mixture is very warm and smooth, you'll want to dip the pretzels quickly and set them down right away to cool.
The double boiler is ready. Do the chocolate chips and cream go in together?
They do. Add the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream to the double boiler, keep the heat low, and stir constantly as they melt together.
The chocolate is starting to soften but there are still a few chips holding their shape.
Keep stirring over low heat until the mixture looks melted and smooth. Don't rush it with higher heat; the recipe relies on gentle melting in the double boiler.
It's smooth now and still very warm. What's the best way to coat the pretzels?
Dip the pretzels one at a time, working quickly so the warm chocolate mixture coats them well. Let the excess drip off briefly before placing each pretzel on the wax paper.
I'm getting a little chocolate pooling under some of them on the paper.
That's okay. Pause each pretzel over the bowl for a moment after dipping, then set it on the wax paper. Since you're coating them while the mixture is still very warm, a little pooling can happen.
They're all dipped and spread out on the wax paper. What should I do while they sit?
Leave them on the wax paper to set and cool. Once the chocolate coating has firmed up, they're ready to serve or store.
I want to make Best Chocolate Chippers. Can you guide me while I get the ingredients set out?
Absolutely. Put 1 cup butter and 1 cup vegetable oil on the counter, and grab a large mixing bowl so you're ready to start combining everything.
The butter and oil are ready. Which sugars should I measure before turning on the oven?
Measure 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Keep them nearby with the butter and oil since they'll all be creamed together.
Both sugars are measured. Should I preheat now or mix first?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can come up to temperature while you mix the dough.
The oven is heating. I've got the large bowl ready—what goes in it?
Add the butter, vegetable oil, brown sugar, and white sugar to the large bowl. Cream them together until the mixture looks smooth and well blended.
It's smoothing out, but the oil took a minute to blend in. Is that okay?
Yes, that's fine. Keep mixing until there aren't streaks of oil and the sugars are evenly worked into the butter mixture.
That looks even now. What should I add next?
Beat in the eggs and vanilla, mixing until they're fully incorporated into the creamed mixture.
The eggs and vanilla are mixed in. What do I do with the dry ingredients?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt. Stir that dry mixture into the creamed mixture until the dough comes together.
I want to make Biriyani today, but I'd like to take it one stage at a time. What should I set out first?
Set out 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, and keep a large skillet ready for the stovetop.
The skillet is clean and those two ingredients are measured. What else needs to be prepped before heat goes on?
Measure 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar, then slice 1 medium onion so it's ready to go into the skillet.
The onion is sliced. Should I start with the oil by itself?
Yes. Pour the olive oil into the large skillet and heat it over medium heat.
The oil is warming in the pan. Do the yogurt and vinegar go in together?
They do. Mix the plain yogurt and distilled white vinegar into the skillet, stirring so they combine with the oil.
It's mixed together now. Where does the sliced onion come in?
Add the sliced onion to the skillet and cook it in the mixture until it turns tender.
The onion has softened. I still have garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes waiting.
Stir in the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes, making sure they're mixed evenly through the onion and yogurt mixture.
Once those are in, should I just keep it moving so nothing catches on the bottom?
Yes, give it steady stirs as everything comes together in the skillet, especially around the edges and bottom, so the mixture stays even and doesn't stick.
I want to make Crawfish Chowder. Can you talk me through the stovetop part as I go?
Absolutely. Set out a large skillet, 1/4 cup butter, 1/2 bunch chopped green onions, 1/2 cup butter, and 2 pounds frozen cleaned crawfish.
The crawfish is frozen and cleaned, and I've chopped the green onions. Do I need both amounts of butter separated?
Yes. Keep the 1/4 cup butter for cooking the green onions, and save the 1/2 cup butter for the crawfish in the same skillet later.
Skillet is ready. What heat should I use to start?
Put the skillet over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter until it's fully melted and coating the pan.
The butter has melted and is foaming lightly. Should the onions go in now?
Yes, add the chopped green onions to the butter and sauté them until they're tender.
They're soft and smell good. Do I leave them in the skillet with the next butter?
Take the green onions out of the pan and set them aside so the skillet is clear for the crawfish.
The onions are in a small bowl. Should I wipe out the skillet or use it as is?
Use the same skillet as is. Melt the 1/2 cup butter in it over the heat.
That butter is melted. How long should the crawfish cook?
Add the 2 pounds frozen cleaned crawfish and sauté them in the butter for 5 minutes, then set the crawfish aside.
I'm making Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms. Can you help me get the prep organized before I start?

Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, 2 cups diced Broccoflower, 2 cups chopped assorted wild mushrooms, and 1/2 white onion chopped. You'll also want your rice, chicken stock, garlic, nutmeg, herbs, salt, and pepper nearby for the cooking stages.
The Broccoflower is diced and the mushrooms are chopped. Should the onion and garlic go in at the same time?

Yes. Melt the butter in a wide pan, then add the Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic together. Sauté them for 10 minutes, stirring often enough that the onion softens and the mushrooms cook down without sticking.
The pan is pretty full with the 2 cups of Broccoflower and 2 cups of mushrooms. Is that okay?

That's fine as long as you can stir everything around. The mushrooms will shrink as they release moisture. Keep the heat around medium so the butter doesn't brown too hard before the vegetables soften.
It's been about 10 minutes and the vegetables look softened. Do they stay in the pan with the rice?
Take the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside for now. Leave any flavorful bits in the pan because they'll help season the rice as it cooks.
I moved the vegetables to a bowl. How do I start the rice in the same pan?
Add the rice to that same pan, then begin adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time. Stir as the rice absorbs each cup, and wait until the liquid is well incorporated before pouring in the next cup.
When I add each cup of chicken stock, should I be stirring constantly or just checking it?

Stir frequently and steadily, especially after each addition, so the rice releases starch and cooks evenly. You don't need to stir every single second, but don't walk away for long; add the next cup only once the last one is mostly absorbed.
The stock is absorbed and the rice is tender now. How do I bring the vegetables back in and season it?

Stir the sautéed Broccoflower, wild mushrooms, onion, and garlic back into the tender rice. Add the nutmeg and herbs, then season with salt and pepper. Give it a final gentle stir and serve while the risotto is creamy and hot.
I'm making Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies. Can you guide me through the setup before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening so they're ready to cream together smoothly.
Both fats are on the counter and the butter is soft. Which sugars do I need measured?
Measure 1 cup packed light brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. Packing the brown sugar helps keep the amount right for the dough.
Sugars are measured. Should I heat the oven now or wait until the dough is mixed?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the cookie dough is prepared.
The oven is heating. I have a large bowl ready—what goes in there first?
In the large bowl, cream together the softened butter, butter flavored shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla until the mixture looks smooth.
It's getting creamy, but I can still see a few streaks of butter. Should I keep mixing?
Yes, keep creaming just until it's smooth and evenly blended. You don't need to overdo it; the goal is a uniform sugar-and-fat mixture before adding the dry ingredients.
The mixture looks smooth now. What dry ingredients should I combine separately?
Combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt in another bowl, then stir that dry mixture into the sugar mixture.
The dry ingredients are mixed in and the dough is thick. What do I add at the end?
Stir in the oats and raisins until they're distributed through the dough. Once they're evenly mixed, the cookie dough is ready for portioning and baking.
I'm making Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme and want to get the marinade set up correctly. What should I pull out first?
Start with a large bowl and measure in 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream, then add 1/4 cup lemon juice. Those form the base of the marinade.
I'm using sour cream. Should the Worcestershire and celery seed go in with that?

Yes. Add 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed to the same bowl. The recipe says to combine the first eight ingredients, so whisk these in with the sour cream and lemon juice until the mixture looks even.
The bowl is mixed and smells pretty tangy. Do I add the chicken straight into it?
Yes, place the chicken in the mixture and turn each piece so it gets coated on all sides. Use tongs or clean hands to make sure the marinade touches the surfaces evenly.
Some pieces are overlapping in the bowl. Is that okay for the overnight part?
A little overlap is fine, but try to settle the pieces so marinade is between them. Cover the bowl well, then put it in the refrigerator to marinate overnight.
So I don't bake it tonight—just cover and refrigerate until tomorrow?
Correct. This part is just the overnight refrigerator marinating time. Keep it chilled the whole time until you're ready to coat the chicken.
It's the next day and the chicken is marinated. What do I do when I take it out?
Remove the chicken from the marinade, letting the excess drip back into the bowl. Then coat each piece with crumbs, pressing gently so the crumbs stick.
Should I reuse any of the marinade after the chicken comes out?
No, discard the used marinade after removing the chicken. Once each piece is coated with crumbs, you're ready to move on with the baking setup for the recipe.
I want to make Dutch Cream Waffles, but I'd like to get the bowls and ingredients sorted before I start.
Set out a large mixing bowl for the dry ingredients and a small mixing bowl for the yolks. For the dry bowl, measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
The flour and salt are measured. Do I mix them thoroughly or just enough to combine?
Just combine them evenly in the large bowl so the salt is distributed through the flour; no need to beat or overwork it.
I've separated the eggs. I have 3 yolks in one bowl and the 3 egg whites set aside.
Great. Use the small bowl with the 3 egg yolks. Start beating them on low speed, and while the mixer is running, add the cream gradually.
Should the yolk and cream mixture look fully smooth right away?
It should start to look blended as you beat. Keep the mixer on low while the cream goes in, then continue beating for 1 minute.
The minute is up. The large bowl still has the flour and salt mixture waiting.
Pour the yolk-and-cream mixture into the flour and salt. Begin on low speed so the flour doesn't puff out of the bowl.
It's starting to come together, but I still see a few dry streaks around the edge.
Scrape the sides if needed, keep it on low just until the dry streaks are incorporated, then increase to medium-high.
What texture am I aiming for before I stop mixing?
Beat on medium-high until the batter is smooth. Once it looks even with no visible flour pockets, you're ready for the next waffle-making stage.
I want to make Fire Side Coffee. Can you help me set up the dry mix and tell me what to measure?
Absolutely. Get a large bowl, a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, and a clean jar with a tight lid. Measure 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer and 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix into the bowl area.
Creamer and hot chocolate mix are measured. The jar is clean—what goes in with them?

Add 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon. The recipe directions also mention nutmeg, but no amount is listed, so stick with the measured cinnamon unless your copy has a nutmeg amount noted.
Everything is dry and measured. Do I just stir it, or does it need to be sifted?
Sift the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee granules, and cinnamon together so the powder is evenly blended and any clumps break up.
Some of the coffee granules are staying a little coarse in the sifter. Is that okay?
Yes, a little texture from the instant coffee is fine. Tap the sifter gently, then whisk the mixture in the bowl so the creamer and cocoa distribute evenly around the granules.
The mix looks even now. Should I put it straight into the jar?
Yes. Pour the blended mix into the jar carefully, then seal it with the lid so it stays dry and scoopable.
Jar is sealed. How do I make one mug from it?
For one serving, stir 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture into 1 cup of hot water. Stir until the powders dissolve as much as possible.
If it tastes too strong or too mild, what should I change?
Adjust to taste: add a little more mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or add more hot water if you want it lighter. Keep the jar sealed between servings.
I want to make Banana Bran Muffins. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 3 mashed bananas, and 1/4 cup milk so everything is ready to mix.
The bananas are mashed, and the butter has softened. Should I heat the oven before I start mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) so it's hot by the time the batter is ready.
Oven is heating. I have a muffin pan, but I'm not sure whether to use liners.
Either works: grease the muffin pan well, or line the cups with paper muffin liners for easier cleanup.
I'll use paper liners. What bowl should I use for the butter and sugar?
Use a large mixing bowl. Put in the softened butter and brown sugar, then cream them together until the mixture looks fluffy.
It's getting lighter and fluffier. Do I need to scrape the bowl?
Yes, scrape down the sides so the butter and brown sugar mix evenly, then beat just until the texture stays fluffy.
That looks good. When do the bananas and milk go in?
Add the mashed bananas and the milk now, along with the vanilla and eggs, then mix well until the batter comes together.
The batter is mixed. Should it be perfectly smooth before I fill the liners?
It does not need to be perfectly smooth because the mashed bananas add texture. Once everything is well combined, you're ready to portion it into the prepared muffin pan.
I want to make Dilled Garlic today. Can you guide me from setup through filling the jars?

Absolutely. Start by getting 2 pounds of peeled garlic ready, along with 1 sprig of fresh dill that's been chopped. You'll also need sterile containers, since the garlic mixture goes straight into them.
The garlic is peeled and my jars are sterilized. What liquid and seasoning should I set out before I start packing them?
Set out cayenne pepper to taste and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar. You'll also need salt for the vinegar mixture in the saucepan.
Should I put the dill in the jars loose, or mix it with the garlic first?
You can add it right into the sterile containers with the garlic. Fill each container with the peeled garlic, chopped fresh dill, and cayenne pepper, stopping within an inch of the top.
I'm filling the jars now. Is that inch of space important?
Yes, leave that space at the top so there's room for the hot vinegar mixture to cover the garlic without overflowing when you pour it in.
The jars are packed with garlic, dill, and cayenne. What happens on the stove?
Pour the distilled white vinegar into a medium saucepan and mix in the salt. Keep it over heat until the mixture comes to a boil.
Do I need to simmer it for a while once it boils?
No simmering time is given here. Once the vinegar and salt mixture reaches a boil, it's ready to pour while hot.
The vinegar mixture is boiling. How do I add it without messing up the jars?
Carefully pour the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne mixture, keeping the jars steady as you fill them.
I want to make Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Start by having 1 recipe of Fast Chicken Soup Base ready, plus a 9 ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, a 14.5 ounce can of diced tomatoes, and 2 medium zucchini.
The soup base is made, and the tortellini and tomatoes are out. Should I cut the zucchini now?
Yes, dice the 2 medium zucchini now so they can go straight into the pot with the other add-ins.
Zucchini is diced. Do I put the soup base on the stove before adding anything else?
Yes. Pour the prepared Fast Chicken Soup Base into your pot and heat it until it comes to a gentle simmer.
It's starting to bubble lightly around the edges. Is that enough of a simmer?
That's right. Keep it at that gentle simmer rather than a hard boil so the tortellini can cook evenly when you add it.
Okay, I'm ready to add the rest. What goes in together?
Add the 1 package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 14.5 ounce can of diced tomatoes, the diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
Everything is in the pot. Should I stir it much?
Give it a careful stir to distribute the tortellini, tomatoes, zucchini, and basil, then let it return to a steady simmer.
It's simmering again. How long should I let it cook, and what am I checking for?
Simmer the soup for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini and zucchini are tender. Taste a piece of zucchini and one tortellini near the end to make sure they're cooked through before serving.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: I want to make Armadillo Eggs today. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. For the ingredients, have 24 jalapeno peppers ready along with 1 pound of sausage.
The peppers and sausage are on the counter. Is there any cheese or dry mix involved?
Yes, you'll also need 2 cups all-purpose baking mix and 1 (16 ounce) package of shredded Cheddar cheese.
Got it. Before I start handling the peppers, what should I do with the oven?
Set the oven to preheat at 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
The oven is heating. What pan should I prepare?
Use a medium baking sheet and lightly grease it so the Armadillo Eggs will release more easily later.
Baking sheet is greased. I'm ready to prep the jalapenos—how should I cut them?
Cut a slit in each jalapeno pepper, keeping the peppers mostly intact rather than slicing them all the way in half.
I've slit a few peppers, and the seeds are visible. Should I leave any of the inside in?
Remove and discard the seeds and pulp from each jalapeno.
All right, I'll clean out the rest. Any quick tip for keeping the workspace manageable?
Keep a discard bowl nearby for the seeds and pulp, and place each cleaned jalapeno on the greased baking sheet as you finish it.
Can you help me make a batch of Fire Side Coffee mix? I've got a clean jar ready.

Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl, a sifter or fine mesh strainer, and that jar with a tight lid. You'll need 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
I have the creamer and hot chocolate measured. Should the coffee granules go in whole or do I need to crush them?
Use the instant coffee granules as they are unless they're clumped. If you see big lumps, break them up lightly so the mix blends evenly.
Coffee is measured, and the cinnamon is ready. What should go into the bowl first?

Add the powdered creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee granules, and ground cinnamon to the sifter over the bowl. Sift them together so the powders combine smoothly; include nutmeg here too if you're using it with this mix.
The creamer is making little dusty clouds. Is that normal, or am I doing it too fast?
That's normal with powdered creamer. Go slowly, tap the sifter gently, and pause if the bowl gets too full. You're aiming for an even, dry mixture without pockets of cinnamon or coffee.
Everything looks blended now. Do I pack it into the jar or pour it loosely?
Pour it loosely into the jar. Don't pack it down; leaving it loose makes it easier to scoop later. Wipe the rim if any powder sticks, then seal the jar with the lid.
Jar is sealed. How do I make a mug from this mix?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Stir until the powders dissolve and the drink looks smooth.
If it tastes a little strong or weak, what's the best way to adjust it?
Adjust to taste: add a little more mix for a stronger, sweeter cup, or add more hot water to mellow it out. Keep the jar sealed between servings so the mix stays dry.
I'd like to make French Spring Soup today. Can you guide me while I prep?

Absolutely. Set a large pot on the stove and gather 1/4 cup butter, 1 pound chopped leeks, 1 chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice for the later part of the soup.
I've got the pot out. Should the leeks and onion already be chopped before I start heating anything?
Yes, have the leeks and onion chopped before the pot gets hot. Once they're ready, put the large pot over medium heat and melt the butter in it.
The butter is melted and just starting to foam. Is that the right point to add the vegetables?
That's a good time. Stir in the chopped leeks and chopped onion, coating them with the butter, then cook them over medium heat until they turn tender.
They're softening, but I'm not sure what texture I'm looking for before adding liquid.
Look for the leeks and onion to be tender and softened rather than browned. Give them an occasional stir so they cook evenly in the butter.
Okay, the leeks and onion are tender now. I have the water measured.
Pour the 2 quarts water into the pot carefully, stirring as you add it so the softened leeks and onion loosen from the bottom.
The water is in. Do the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice all go in together?
Yes. Mix in the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice, making sure everything is distributed through the soup.
It's all mixed in. Should I tidy as it cooks, or is there anything else to add right now?
Nothing else from the recipe needs to be added right now. You can wipe down the cutting board and clear the prep bowls while the soup continues from this point.
Can you help me make Dads BBQ Roast? I've got the roast out and want to get organized before I touch the mustard.

Absolutely. For this roast, you'll need 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 (1 ounce) envelopes dry onion soup mix, and 1 (5 pound) beef rump roast. Set out a small bowl and enough aluminum foil to make two long sheets.
The mustard and soup mix are on the counter. Should I mix the coating before dealing with the beef?
Yes. In the small bowl, stir the yellow mustard and both envelopes of dry onion soup mix together until the soup mix is evenly worked through the mustard.
It's pretty thick and grainy from the onion mix. Is that how it should look?
That's right. It should be a thick, spreadable mustard mixture with the dry onion soup mix distributed throughout, not a smooth sauce.
Okay. For the foil, do I stack the sheets or arrange them a certain way?
Lay out two long sheets of aluminum foil crosswise, like a plus sign. That gives you coverage from both directions for the 5 pound roast.
Foil is ready. The roast is still a little damp from the package—what should I do before placing it down?
Pat the beef rump roast dry with paper towels, then place it right in the center where the two foil sheets cross.
It's centered on the foil. How heavy should I go with the mustard coating?
Coat it generously with the mustard and onion soup mixture. Spread it over the surface so the roast gets a good, even layer.
Some of the coating is sliding onto the foil. Should I scrape it back up?

messages.content: I want to make Enchilada Style Burritos with frozen bean and cheese burritos. Can you talk me through it while I cook?

Absolutely. Set out 6 frozen prepared bean and cheese burritos, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1 3/4 cups water. You'll also need a greased 13-in baking dish and a saucepan.
I have the burritos and the 13-in dish. Should they thaw at all before going in?
No thawing needed. Put the 6 frozen burritos straight into the greased 13-in baking dish, then set the dish aside while you make the sauce.
They're arranged in the dish. I've got butter in the saucepan—what heat should I use?
Use medium heat and melt the 2 tablespoons butter or margarine gently, just until it's fully melted and ready to take the flour.
The butter is melted and not browned. Do I add all the flour at once?
Yes, stir in the 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and keep stirring until the mixture looks smooth, with no dry flour streaks.
It's coming together into a smooth paste. How do I add the water without lumps?
Pour in the 1 3/4 cups water gradually while stirring the whole time. A steady whisk or spoon motion will help the sauce stay smooth.
The water is mixed in, and it looks thin right now. Is that expected?
Yes, it will thicken as it heats. Bring the mixture to a boil, then cook and stir for 2 minutes, or until it thickens.
After 2 minutes it's thicker and coats the spoon. What should I do with the burritos now?
That's the texture you want. Keep the burritos in the greased baking dish and use the thickened sauce as directed for your enchilada-style burritos, spreading it evenly so the 6 burritos are covered.
I want to make Date Loaf Cake. Can you help me set up before I start measuring?
Absolutely. For this Date Loaf Cake, get out 1 cup pitted, chopped dates and 1 cup dark brown sugar, plus a large mixing bowl so you can combine everything easily.
Dates and brown sugar are ready. What else should I put on the counter?
You'll also need 1/4 cup margarine and 1 cup boiling water. Keep the boiling water separate until you're ready to mix it into the bowl.
I've got the margarine measured. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's ready when the loaf mixture is prepared.
Oven is heating. What pan should I use for this loaf?
Use a 9x5 inch loaf pan. Grease it well, then flour it so the Date Loaf Cake releases more easily after baking.
The pan is ready. For the bowl, do the dates go in before the hot water?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the chopped dates, dark brown sugar, margarine, and the 1 cup boiling water.
The mixture is in the bowl and the margarine is starting to melt. Should I stir a lot?
Stir just enough to bring the dates, sugar, margarine, and boiling water together evenly. The hot water will help soften the dates and melt the margarine.
It looks combined. How long does it need to sit before I do anything else?
Let the mixture stand for 15 minutes. Set a timer and leave it in the bowl; that resting time gives the dates a chance to soften in the warm liquid.
Can you help me make garlic butter? I've got a small mixing bowl out, but I want to be sure the butter is the right texture.
Absolutely. You'll want 1 cup butter, softened enough that a spoon or spatula can press through it easily, but not melted. Put it in the small bowl when it's soft and spreadable.
The butter is soft and in the bowl. Should I add the garlic before the cheese?
Yes. Add 1 tablespoon minced garlic to the softened butter and mash it in so the garlic starts spreading evenly through the butter.
It's mixed in, and I have grated Parmesan ready. How much goes in?
Stir in 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese. Fold and press it through the butter until the mixture looks fairly even and creamy.
The Parmesan is blended in. It looks a little thick but spreadable. What seasoning goes in now?
Season it with 1 tablespoon garlic salt, plus Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika. Add the seasonings over the surface, then mix thoroughly so you don't get salty pockets.
I added the garlic salt and a little of the other seasonings. Should I whip it or just stir?
Stir and mash rather than whip. Scrape the sides of the bowl and press the butter against the bowl a few times until the garlic, Parmesan, and seasonings are evenly distributed.
It smells good. How do I know it's ready to use?

It's ready when it looks uniform, with no plain streaks of butter and no clumps of garlic salt or Parmesan. Taste a tiny bit if you like, then adjust only with small pinches of pepper, paprika, or Italian seasoning.
I'm planning to serve it with warm bread. Should I chill it first or leave it soft?
For warm bread, you can leave it soft so it spreads easily. If you want a neater presentation, spoon it into a small dish and smooth the top; otherwise, it's ready to spread right away.

Before I unwrap the chocolate, what should I put on the counter and what bowl do I need?

Set out a large microwave-safe bowl, a wire whisk, and these ingredients: 1 (4 ounce) bar German sweet chocolate, chopped; 1/3 cup milk; 4 ounces cream cheese, softened; and 2 tablespoons white sugar.
The cream cheese is soft, and I chopped the chocolate. Should I measure the milk all together?
Yes, measure the full 1/3 cup milk, but use only 2 tablespoons of it with the chopped chocolate at the start. Keep the remaining milk nearby for whisking in with the cream cheese and sugar.
That restrained garnish plan is the way I like this pie; it keeps the finished top from looking overloaded. I have the microwave-safe bowl ready.

Put the chopped German sweet chocolate in the bowl with those 2 tablespoons of milk. Microwave on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stopping halfway through to stir, and pull it when the chocolate is almost melted.
It's mostly melted after stirring, with a few soft pieces left. Do I keep heating it?

If the pieces are soft, keep stirring first; the residual heat may smooth them out. Only add a brief extra burst if it still looks lumpy, since the recipe wants it almost melted rather than overheated.

Use the wire whisk now. Beat in the softened 4 ounces cream cheese, the 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk until the mixture is blended and even.

Yes, refrigerate the mixture for 10 minutes. That short chill helps it firm up before the whipped topping goes in.

Gently fold in 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping with broad, slow turns, scraping from the bottom up, until no streaks remain. Once it is in the pie, use just the 2 garnishes you chose: one for flavor and one for texture.

I want to make Best Ever Tuna Salad. Can you talk me through it while I get set up?

Absolutely. Set out 2 eggs, a saucepan, and enough cold water to cover the eggs. You'll also need 1 (12 ounce) can white tuna, 1 (6 ounce) can shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise for mixing later.
I found the saucepan and eggs. Should the eggs go in before the water heats?
Yes. Put the eggs in the saucepan while everything is still cold, then cover them with cold water.

Bring the water to a boil, and as soon as it reaches a boil, take the saucepan off the heat right away.

Cover the pan and let the eggs stand in the hot water for 10 to 12 minutes.
While the eggs sit, should I open the tuna and crabmeat?
Yes, that's a good time to prep them. Open the 12 ounce can of white tuna and the 6 ounce can of shredded crabmeat so they're ready for the salad bowl.
The timer is almost done, and I have the seafood ready. What should the eggs look like after this?
After 10 to 12 minutes in the hot water, remove the eggs from the pan, cool them, peel them, and chop them finely.
The eggs are peeled. How small should I chop them before mixing?
Chop the eggs finely so they blend through the tuna salad. Then combine the chopped eggs with the white tuna, shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise.

Can you help me get Dads BBQ Roast started? I've got the beef out but want to make sure I set everything up right.
Absolutely. For this roast, you'll need 1 1/3 cups yellow mustard, 2 (1 ounce) envelopes of dry onion soup mix, and 1 (5 pound) beef rump roast.

Use a small bowl and stir the yellow mustard together with both envelopes of dry onion soup mix until the mixture looks evenly combined.

Add 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons and 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese to your prep area. Keep the crabmeat, lobster, and garlic nearby too, since they'll go into the stuffing mixture.

In a medium bowl, combine the crushed seasoned croutons, the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, shredded mozzarella, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic. Stir until the crumbs are moistened and the seafood and cheese are evenly distributed.
The filling looks buttery and chunky. Is that the texture I want before stuffing?
Yes, that sounds right: moist enough to hold together from the butter and cheese, with visible pieces of crab and lobster. Spoon it into the mushroom caps evenly, then they're ready for the oven.
