Beat in the 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour until it's incorporated. Keep the speed moderate so the flour doesn't puff out, and stop once the dough comes together.
The dough is soft and a little sticky. Is that okay before chilling?
Yes, that's fine for this dough. Gather it into a smooth ball, using lightly floured hands if needed, but don't work in extra flour unless it's truly unmanageable.
I've shaped it into a ball. What should I wrap it with?
Wrap the dough tightly in foil or cling wrap so it doesn't dry out in the refrigerator. Try to seal the edges well.
Wrapped and ready for the fridge. How long does it need to rest?
Refrigerate it overnight. If you're not baking right away, the wrapped dough can stay chilled for up to a week.
When I'm ready to bake, do I use it straight from the refrigerator with the fruit preserves?
Take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it so it softens slightly and is easier to handle. Keep the 1 cup fruit preserves ready for filling when you assemble the empanadas.
Can you walk me through making a Buttermilk Shake? I've got a blender ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pint vanilla ice cream and 1 cup buttermilk so they're ready to go into the blender.
The ice cream and buttermilk are out. Are there any small flavorings I should measure before blending?
Yes—measure 1 teaspoon grated lemon peel and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract. Those both go into the shake for flavor.
I've measured the lemon peel and vanilla. Should I soften the ice cream first?
If it's very hard, let it sit just briefly until it scoops easily, but don't let it melt. The blender can handle it as long as the scoops aren't rock-solid.
It scoops cleanly now. What goes into the blender first?
Add all the ingredients to the blender container: the vanilla ice cream, buttermilk, grated lemon peel, and vanilla extract.
Everything is in the blender jar. Do I need to pulse it or run it continuously?
Put the lid on securely and process on high until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It looks smooth, but I can still see a tiny bit of lemon peel. Is that okay?
That's fine—the grated lemon peel may remain visible. As long as the ice cream and buttermilk are blended into a smooth shake, you're ready to serve.
I have chilled glasses nearby. How should I serve it?
Pour the Buttermilk Shake into the glasses and serve it right away while it's cold and creamy.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this cake, place 3 small garnish groupings around the platter so it looks decorative without covering the cookie-and-fudge surface.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm serving Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake on one platter tonight, and I want a dressed-up look with optional garnishes and finishing touches. What would make it look special?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use three small garnish clusters spaced around the platter.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake as a shared platter with optional garnishes, decorative toppings, or finishing flourishes. How should I finish it?

messages.content: I'm serving Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake on one platter tonight, and I want a dressed-up look with optional garnishes and finishing touches. What would make it look special?
For this cake, place 3 small garnish groupings around the platter so it looks decorative without covering the cookie-and-fudge surface.
Perfect, that is the look I want just for this cake. Before I start, what should I pull from the pantry?
Get 1 (18 ounce) package of small chocolate chip cookies and 1/4 cup melted margarine ready first; those will make the crust and cookie border.
I have the cookies and margarine out. Should the cold ingredients wait, or come out now too?
Bring out 1 cup hot fudge topping and 2 quarts vanilla ice cream so everything is within reach when the crust is assembled.
The springform pan is on the counter. How much of the cookie package am I crushing?
Crush half the cookies, about 20 small cookies, until they are crumbly enough to press into a crust.
The crumbs look even, with a few tiny pieces left. What texture should I aim for when I add the margarine?
Stir the crumbs with the melted margarine until they are evenly moistened, like a sandy mixture that clumps when pressed.
That mixture is ready, and I'm using a 9-inch springform pan. How firmly should I pack it?
Press the crumb mixture across the bottom of the 9-inch springform pan, using steady pressure so the crust holds together.
The base is packed in. What do I do with the cookies I did not crush?
Stand the remaining cookies upright around the edge of the pan to make the cookie wall.
The cookie border is standing. What goes over the crust before the ice cream?
Spread 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the crust, keeping it inside the cookie edge.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chocolate Chip Cookie Ice Cream Cake

messages.content: Can you help me make Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes? I've got a pot ready but want to make sure I have everything lined up.

Absolutely. You'll need 1 recipe Fast Chicken Soup Base, 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, and 2 medium zucchini, diced. Keep 1 tsp. dried basil nearby too, since it goes in with the vegetables and tortellini.
The soup base is the only thing I haven't started yet. Should I prep the zucchini before heating the pot?
Yes, dice the 2 medium zucchini before you begin cooking so it's ready to add quickly. You can also open the 14.5-ounce can of diced tomatoes and set the tortellini package near the stove.
Zucchini is diced, tomatoes are open, and the tortellini is still refrigerated. What do I do with the base?
Prepare the Fast Chicken Soup Base in your soup pot according to that recipe. Once it's made, keep it in the pot for the rest of this soup.
The chicken soup base is in the pot now. Do I need it boiling hard?
No hard boil needed. Bring the soup base to a steady simmer, with small bubbles gently breaking the surface.
It's simmering gently. Should the tortellini go in before the tomatoes and zucchini?

Add them all together: the 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, the 2 diced medium zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil. Stir gently so the tortellini doesn't stick to the bottom.
Everything is in the pot, and it came back to a simmer. How long should I let it cook?
Let it simmer for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini and zucchini are tender. Keep the heat moderate so the soup stays at a simmer rather than a rolling boil.
How can I tell when the zucchini and tortellini are ready without overcooking them?

Taste a tortellini and check a piece of zucchini around the 10-minute mark. The tortellini should be tender all the way through, and the zucchini should be soft but not falling apart. If they need more time, keep simmering and check again before you reach 20 minutes.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: I'm making apple butter spice cake and want to keep the topping and batter steps straight. Can you guide me through it?

Absolutely. Set out the topping ingredients first: 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. You'll mix those separately from the cake batter.
I've got the brown sugar and spices measured, and the pecans are chopped. Should I start heating the oven now?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, and spray or grease one 9x13 inch pan so it's ready when the batter is mixed.
The pan is greased. For the topping, do I just stir everything together, or should the pecans go in later?
Stir the topping all together now: the packed brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped pecans. Keep that bowl nearby for when you assemble the cake.
Topping is mixed. I'm looking at the dry ingredients for the batter—what should happen with those?
Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together. That helps the leavening and salt spread evenly through the cake.
Dry bowl is sifted. I've got butter, sugar, eggs, apple butter, vanilla, and sour cream out too.
Great. In a separate mixing bowl, blend the butter and sugar together until they're combined, then add the eggs and beat the mixture well.
The eggs are beaten in and the mixture looks smoother. Where does the apple butter fit?
Mix in the apple butter, vanilla, and the wheat germ or bran cereal if you're using that part of the recipe. Scrape the bowl so the apple butter is evenly worked in.
That's mixed. Do I dump in the sifted dry ingredients all at once with the sour cream?

Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream, mixing well after each addition. That keeps the batter more even and helps avoid dry pockets before it goes into the prepared 9x13 inch pan.
I'm making BBQ Chuck Roast today and have a 5 pound chuck roast ready. Can you guide me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put the chuck roast near a large bowl, then measure 1 cup barbeque sauce and 1 cup teriyaki sauce. You'll also need 1 12 fluid ounce can or bottle of beer for the marinade.
Sauces and beer are on the counter. The recipe mentions aromatics too—what goes into the bowl with them?
In the large bowl, combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt. Stir until the marinade looks evenly mixed.
The marinade is mixed. Should the roast go in whole, and do I need to trim it first?

Use the chuck roast whole for this step. Place it into the marinade, turning it so the surface is coated. If there are any very loose pieces of fat you can remove them, but the recipe's next move is to cover it and refrigerate it.
It's in the bowl and coated. How long does it need to sit in the fridge?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the roast for six hours. Turn it often during that time so different sides stay in contact with the marinade.
The six hours are almost up. What should I do before taking it out?
Preheat an outdoor grill for indirect heat before you remove the roast from the marinade. That way the grill is ready when the meat comes out.
The grill is heating for indirect heat. Do I throw away the marinade after I lift out the roast?
Don't discard it yet. Remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan.
The marinade is in a saucepan now and the roast is out. Is that the end of the written steps I have?
Yes, that reaches the last step you listed: the roast has been removed from the marinade, and the marinade has been transferred to a saucepan.
Can you help me make the Dipping Sauce? I'm setting out a small mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Set the bowl on the counter and measure in 1/2 cup mayonnaise as the base.
Mayonnaise is in. I have ketchup nearby—how much goes with it?
Add 2 teaspoons ketchup to the mayonnaise. It just needs enough to tint and lightly sweeten the sauce.
Got it. The horseradish jar is open; I don't want to overdo it.
Measure 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish and add it to the bowl. Since it's prepared horseradish, use it as-is from the jar.
That's mixed into the bowl but not stirred yet. What about the spice?
Add 1/4 teaspoon paprika, then include the salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper called for in the recipe.
All the seasonings are in. Should I whisk or use a spoon?
A spoon is fine for this amount. Stir until the mayonnaise, ketchup, horseradish, paprika, salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne are evenly combined and the color looks consistent.
The sauce looks smooth with no streaks. Does it need any cooking?
No cooking needed. This is a stirred dipping sauce, so once it's combined, transfer it to a covered container or cover the bowl.
I covered the bowl. Where should I keep it until serving?
Store it covered in the refrigerator until you're ready to serve. Give it a quick stir before setting it out as a dipping sauce.
Can you talk me through Beths Spicy Oatmeal Raisin Cookies while I set up my baking area?

Absolutely. Start by clearing a little counter space and pulling out the ingredients listed: 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening, 1 cup packed light brown sugar, and 1/2 cup white sugar.
The butter is softened, and I found the shortening. Should I heat the oven before measuring the sugars?
Yes, get the oven going now so it is ready when the dough is mixed. Preheat it to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
Oven is heating. I'm packing the brown sugar into the measuring cup now.
Good. Measure 1 cup packed light brown sugar, then measure 1/2 cup white sugar. Keep both near your large mixing bowl with the butter and shortening.
All four of those are by the bowl. What texture am I aiming for when I start mixing?
Cream the butter, butter flavored shortening, brown sugar, and white sugar together with the eggs and vanilla until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended.
It's getting lighter and smoother. I still see a few streaks of shortening on the side of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides and mix a little more until those streaks disappear. You want the fat, sugars, eggs, and vanilla combined before adding the dry ingredients.
The wet mixture looks smooth now. Which dry ingredients go in together?
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Once they are mixed together, stir them into the sugar mixture.
The dry mixture is stirred in and the dough looks thick. What gets folded in at the end?
Stir in the oats and raisins until they are distributed through the dough. After that, the cookie dough is ready for portioning and baking in the preheated oven.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Warm a small amount of chili in oil right at the beginning so the heat infuses the pot, then don't add more chili as a topping later.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: Tonight I'm making French Spring Soup as a thicker stew, and I want this pot to have heat from chili, hot sauce, pepper flakes, spicy oil, jalapeno, or cayenne. For this version, how should I handle the chili?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Bloom a small amount of chili in oil at the start and add no extra chili on top.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making French Spring Soup as simmered beans, sauce, or stew with chili, hot sauce, pepper flakes, spicy oil, jalapeno, or cayenne. How should I handle the chili?

messages.content: Tonight I'm making French Spring Soup as a thicker stew, and I want this pot to have heat from chili, hot sauce, pepper flakes, spicy oil, jalapeno, or cayenne. For this version, how should I handle the chili?
Warm a small amount of chili in oil right at the beginning so the heat infuses the pot, then don't add more chili as a topping later.
Perfect, that's the direction I want for this one. I have a large pot out—what should I prep before the heat goes on?
Have 1/4 cup butter ready, plus 1 pound leeks, chopped. If you're using chili oil or a pinch of dried chili, keep that beside the pot too.
The leeks are chopped and rinsed. Should I cut the onion now or wait until the butter melts?
Chop the 1 onion before you start cooking so it can go in with the leeks as soon as the butter is melted.
Onion is chopped, and I measured the 2 quarts water. How do I begin without scorching the butter?
Set the large pot over medium heat and melt the butter gently. Add the small amount of chili in oil at this stage so it blooms while the fat warms.
The butter is melted and smells a little spicy. Do the leeks and onion go in together?
Yes. Stir in the chopped leeks and onion, coating them well in the butter, and cook until they turn tender.
They're softening but still have a bit of bite. Should I keep cooking or add the water now?
Give them a little more time until tender, then pour the 2 quarts water into the pot.
Water is in, and I'm scraping the bottom of the pot. What vegetables and grains are next?
Mix in the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice, stirring so everything is evenly distributed in the broth.
Everything is in the pot. Since I already bloomed the chili, should I finish with hot sauce or pepper flakes at serving?
No, leave off the extra hot sauce, pepper flakes, spicy oil, jalapeno, or cayenne at serving for this pot; the chili you bloomed at the start is the heat.
Can you help me cook Chicken and Black Bean Chili? I've got a large pot ready, but I want to make sure I prep the chicken correctly.
Absolutely. Cut 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into 1 inch pieces so they'll brown evenly in the pot.
The chicken is cut up. What should I set next to the stove before I turn on the burner?
Keep 2 tablespoons cooking oil nearby, plus sea salt to taste and 1 tablespoon chili powder, or more if you want it stronger.
Oil and seasonings are ready. Should the pot be hot before the chicken goes in?
Yes. Pour the oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat until it looks loose and shimmery.
The oil is shimmering. Do I add all the chicken at once?
Add the chicken pieces to the pot in a layer if they fit, then brown them on all sides. Stir and turn them so the surfaces pick up color rather than just steaming.
They're starting to brown, but there's a little liquid in the bottom. Is that okay?
That can happen. Keep the heat at medium and continue cooking until the chicken is browned on all sides; the liquid should reduce as the pieces cook.
The chicken looks browned now. When do the spices go in?
Season the chicken right in the pot with sea salt, chili powder, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir well so the spices coat the chicken.
The spices smell good. I have onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper chopped—do they go in now?
Yes, mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper. Stir them through the seasoned chicken so they start softening and picking up the chili flavor.
I want to make Crustless Spinach Quiche. Can you help me set up before I start cooking?
Absolutely. Put out 1 tablespoon vegetable oil and 1 chopped onion first, since those go to the skillet early.
The onion is chopped. I also have frozen spinach—does it need anything done to it?
Yes. Use 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, and make sure it is thawed and well drained before it goes into the quiche.
Good to know. What else should be ready on the counter?
Have 5 beaten eggs ready too. So your main ingredients are the oil, chopped onion, thawed and drained spinach, and beaten eggs.
I've got the eggs beaten and the spinach drained. Should I start with the oven or the pan?
Start by preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it is hot when the quiche is ready.
Oven is heating. What baking dish should I use?
Use a 9 inch pie pan and lightly grease it so the crustless quiche releases cleanly after baking.
The pie pan is greased. I'm moving to the stove—what heat level should I use?
Set a large skillet over medium-high heat, then add the vegetable oil and let it warm briefly.
The oil is shimmering a little. How should the onion look before I stop cooking it?
Add the chopped onion and cook it, stirring occasionally, until the onion is soft. Keep it moving now and then so it softens evenly without catching.
Can you talk me through making Bacon Wrapped Hotdogs in the slow cooker?
Absolutely. You'll need 10 hot dogs cut into thirds, 15 slices of bacon cut in half, toothpicks, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar.
I've got the slow cooker out. Should I cut the hot dogs before dealing with the bacon?
Yes. Cut each hot dog into thirds first so you have bite-size pieces ready to wrap.
The hot dogs are cut. The bacon strips are still full length right now.
Cut the 15 bacon slices in half. Then wrap one half-slice of bacon around each hot dog piece.
Some of the bacon wants to loosen as I set them down. Is that okay?
Secure each wrapped piece with a toothpick so the bacon stays in place while it cooks.
They're wrapped and pinned. Do I need to brown them in a pan first?
No browning step is needed for this recipe. Place the wrapped hot dog pieces into the slow cooker and set it to low heat.
They're in the cooker on low. Where does the brown sugar come in?
Sprinkle the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar evenly over the hot dogs so it can melt down as they cook.
How long should I leave them, and what tells me they're ready to serve?
Let them cook for 5 to 6 hours on low, until the bacon is cooked through. Keep the toothpicks in for serving, and remind people they're there.
Can you help me make Barbecued Shredded Beef? I've got a large roasting pan out and want to make sure I set everything up right.

Absolutely. You'll need a 3 pounds beef roast, 2 chopped onions, 2 cans or bottles of beer that are 12 fluid ounces each, and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce. The cooking starts in a low oven, so clear enough space for the roasting pan.
The roast is still wrapped, and the onions are chopped. Should I heat the oven before loading the pan?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C. While it heats, unwrap the roast and set it in the large roasting pan.
The oven is warming, and the beef is in the pan. Do the onions go under it or on top?
Scatter the 2 chopped onions over the roast and around it in the pan. They'll cook down with the beef and the beer mixture.
Onions are spread over the beef. I have a mixing bowl ready—what goes in there?
In the large bowl, combine the Worcestershire sauce with liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Use the full 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce from the recipe.
I mixed the seasonings and Worcestershire together. The beer is still unopened; do I pour it into the bowl?
Yes. Pour in the 2 beer cans or bottles, 12 fluid ounces each, then stir so the Worcestershire mixture is evenly blended into the beer.
It's stirred together. Should I pour it directly over the roast or around the sides?
Add the beer mixture to the roasting pan, pouring it over and around the roast so the onions and beef are moistened.
The liquid is in the pan now. Anything I should check before it goes into the oven?

Make sure the roast is settled in the large roasting pan with the onions scattered over it and the beer-Worcestershire mixture added. Once the oven is at 275 degrees F, or 135 degrees C, it's ready to go in.
Can you help me make Garlic Butter? My butter is soft, but I want to be sure I measure everything right.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 tablespoon garlic salt. You'll also want Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika nearby for seasoning.
I have a small mixing bowl and a spoon. Is that enough, or should I use a mixer?
A spoon is fine if the butter is truly soft. Add the softened butter to the small bowl, then stir in the minced garlic until it's spread evenly through the butter.
The garlic is mixed in, but the butter still looks a little chunky from the spoon marks.
That's okay. Keep pressing and folding it against the side of the bowl for a minute so it smooths out. Once it looks creamy, mix in the grated Parmesan cheese.
The Parmesan is in. Should I add the garlic salt all at once?
Yes, add the 1 tablespoon garlic salt and stir thoroughly so it doesn't sit in one salty pocket. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl as you mix.
It smells strong already. How much of the Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika should I use?
The recipe doesn't give exact amounts for those, so sprinkle them in lightly, stir, and taste if you're comfortable doing so. You can add a little more, but you can't easily take seasoning back out.
The texture is spreadable now. Is there anything else to cook, or is it just mixed?
For this recipe, it's just mixed. Once the butter, garlic, Parmesan, garlic salt, Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika are evenly combined, the garlic butter is ready to use.
I'm putting it on bread tonight. Should I chill it first or keep it soft?
Keep it soft if you're spreading it on bread right away. If you have leftovers, pack them into a covered container and refrigerate, then let the butter soften again before the next use.
I'm making Eggplant Mixed Grill and I want to get the marinade set up before I prep all the vegetables. What should I pull out first?

Start with the marinade ingredients you have measured: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil. You'll also need vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic for the bag.
I've got a large resealable plastic bag open in a bowl so it doesn't tip. Do the herbs and oil go right into it?

Yes. Add the olive oil, parsley, oregano, basil, vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic directly to the large resealable bag, then gently squeeze or stir the bag contents so the marinade is evenly mixed.
The marinade is mixed. I have onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and both red and yellow bell pepper ready. Should everything go in together?
Put the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper into the bag together. Try to spread the pieces through the marinade so they all get coated.
The vegetables are in the bag, but some pieces are sticking near the top. Is it okay to press the air out?
That's a good idea. Press out excess air, seal the bag tightly, and turn it a few times so the marinade reaches the vegetables on all sides.
How long should the sealed bag stay in the fridge, and do I need to do anything while it sits?
Refrigerate it for 2 hours. During that time, turn the bag occasionally so the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and peppers keep getting redistributed in the marinade.
The 2 hours are almost up. When should I heat the grill?
Go ahead and preheat the grill for high heat near the end of the marinating time, so it's ready when the vegetables come out of the refrigerator.
Before the vegetables go on, is there anything I should do to the grate?
Lightly oil the grill grate before cooking. That helps the marinated eggplant, peppers, mushrooms, asparagus, and onion release more easily once they hit the hot grill.
Can you help me make Delicious Artichoke Dip? I'm setting things out now and want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Put out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 (14 ounce) can of artichoke hearts, drained.
I've got the mayo, sour cream, Parmesan, and the drained artichoke hearts. What dish and bowl should I use?
Use a medium-sized mixing bowl for combining everything, and keep a shallow baking dish nearby for the dip once it's mixed.
Got it. Should I start heating the oven before I mix?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's ready when the dip is assembled.
The oven is heating. What goes into the bowl first?
Stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, grated Parmesan cheese, and onion in the medium bowl until they're evenly combined.
The creamy base is mixed. The Parmesan is a little thick in there—is that okay?
That's fine for this dip. Once the base looks mostly uniform, mix in the drained artichoke hearts along with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Should I break up the artichoke hearts as I stir, or leave them in bigger pieces?
Break them up a bit as you fold them in so the artichokes are spread through the dip, but they don't need to be completely mashed.
The mixture looks chunky and creamy now. How do I get it ready for baking?
Spoon the mixture into the shallow baking dish and spread it into an even layer so it heats consistently.
Can you help me put together the Dipping Sauce? I've got a small bowl and a spoon ready.

Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons ketchup, 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish, and 1/4 teaspoon paprika. You'll also need salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper for seasoning.
The mayonnaise and ketchup are measured. Should I add them to the bowl together?
Yes, add the mayonnaise and ketchup to the small bowl and stir just enough to loosen the mayonnaise so the ketchup starts blending in.
It's streaky but starting to come together. When does the horseradish go in?
Add the 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish now. Stir it through the mayo-ketchup mixture until the sauce looks evenly combined.
The horseradish is mixed in. I'm measuring the paprika next.
Sprinkle in the 1/4 teaspoon paprika, then add the salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Mix well so the spices are spread evenly through the sauce.
The color looks even now. Should it be perfectly smooth?
It should be creamy and well blended, but it may have a little texture from the prepared horseradish and oregano. Give it a quick taste and adjust only the seasonings if needed.
Taste is good. I'm not serving it for another hour—what should I do with it?
Cover the bowl tightly and store it in the refrigerator until you're ready to serve. Chilling will also help the flavors settle together.
I'll cover it now. Any serving tip when it comes out of the fridge?
Give it a quick stir before serving, then spoon it into a small dish. Keep any leftovers covered in the refrigerator.
Can you help me prep A Surprise Inside French Toast? I've got the bread out, but I want to make sure I'm starting correctly.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 slices of French bread, each about 2 inches thick. The thickness matters because you'll be cutting a pocket into each slice for the filling.
The bread slices are thick enough. What cheeses should I set beside the bowl?
Set out 1/4 cup ricotta cheese, 1/4 cup whipped cottage cheese, and 2 tablespoons lowfat cream cheese. Those three get combined for the creamy filling.
Should I cut the bread before mixing the filling, or make the filling first?
Cut the pockets first so the bread is ready to stuff. Use a small sharp knife and slice into the side of each piece without cutting all the way through.
I'm worried about tearing the slices. How wide should I open each pocket?
Open each pocket carefully, just enough to make room for the filling. Try to keep the top and bottom of the bread connected so it holds together.
The pockets are cut and still intact. I've got a large bowl ready for the filling.
Good. In the large bowl, combine the ricotta, whipped cottage cheese, and lowfat cream cheese. Stir or beat them together until they start looking evenly blended.
The mixture is a little lumpy from the cottage cheese. Is that okay before I add anything else?
A little texture is fine, but keep beating if you want a smoother filling. Once the cheeses are combined, add the sugar and flavoring extract, then beat until the mixture is smooth.
I don't see amounts listed for the sugar or extract. Should I pause there?

Yes, use the amounts from your recipe source if they're listed elsewhere. The step itself is to add the sugar and flavoring extract to the cheese mixture and beat until smooth before filling the bread pockets.
I'm making Dutch Cream Waffles and have my bowls out. Can you talk me through the batter?
Absolutely. Set up a large mixing bowl for the dry ingredients and a small mixing bowl for the yolk mixture. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt for the large bowl.
The flour and salt are measured. Should I mix them together before dealing with the eggs?
Yes, whisk or stir the flour and salt together in the large bowl so the salt is evenly distributed.
Done. I've separated the eggs, so I have 3 yolks in one bowl and 3 whites set aside. Which ones do I use now?
Use the 3 egg yolks now. Put them in the small mixing bowl and start beating them on low speed while you add the cream.
I'm adding the cream slowly with the mixer on low. How long should I keep beating it?
Once the cream is going in with the yolks, beat the mixture for 1 minute. Keep the speed low and steady so it blends smoothly.
The yolk mixture looks even after a minute. Does it go into the dry bowl all at once?
Yes, add the yolk-and-cream mixture to the flour and salt in the large bowl. Start combining on low speed so the flour doesn't puff out.
It's mostly combined but still has a few streaks of flour near the sides. Should I scrape the bowl?
Scrape down the sides and bottom, then keep mixing on low just until those dry streaks disappear.
The batter is together now, but it looks a little uneven. What texture am I aiming for?
Increase to medium-high and beat until the batter is smooth. Stop once it looks even and pourable, without visible lumps of flour.
I want to make Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea. I've got a big pot out—can you help me plan the ingredients before I turn on the stove?

Absolutely. For the cooked base, put together 1 pound fresh or frozen cranberries and 3 quarts cold water. You'll also need 2 cups orange juice and 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice for after the cranberry liquid cools.
The cranberries are still frozen. Is that okay, or should I thaw them first?
Frozen cranberries are fine for this recipe. Add them straight to the large pot with the 3 quarts cold water; they'll heat through as the water comes to a boil.
Cranberries and water are in the pot. Should I keep the heat high?
Yes, bring the pot to a boil. Once it's boiling, cook only until the berries pop, which should take about 5 minutes.
I'm hearing popping, and the water is turning red. Do I keep simmering to get more color?
No need to push it longer. When the berries have popped after about 5 minutes, take the pot off the heat so the flavor stays fresh.
It's off the burner now. The pot is pretty hot—what happens during the cooling part?
Let it stand at room temperature until cold. The recipe calls for several hours, so just leave the cranberry mixture to cool fully before straining.
After several hours it's cold. Do I press the cranberries through the strainer or just remove them?
Strain out the cranberries from the liquid. You can let them drain, but don't worry about forcing them through unless you want a cloudier tea.
The liquid is strained. I've measured the orange juice and pineapple juice—what do I stir in at the end?

Stir in the 2 cups orange juice and 2 1/8 cups pineapple juice, along with the lemon juice and sugar called for in the final step. Mix until the sugar dissolves, then the Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea is ready to serve or chill.
Can you coach me through making Chicken Tacos? I've got the chicken out and want to set up the skillet properly.

Absolutely. Cut 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces if you haven't already, and place a large skillet on the stove. Keep the heat at medium when you're ready to start.
The chicken is cut up. What liquids should I measure before the pan gets hot?
Measure 1 cup lemonade, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 1 tablespoon lime juice. You'll also need Worcestershire sauce for the skillet.
I have the lemonade, oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce beside the stove. Do they all go in with the chicken?
Yes. Add the chicken to the large skillet, then pour in the lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce. Keep it over medium heat so the mixture can come up to a steady simmer.
It's starting to bubble lightly. Which seasonings go in now?
Season the skillet with garlic powder, onion powder, and a bay leaf. Stir so the chicken pieces are coated and the seasonings spread through the liquid.
The bay leaf is in, and the chicken is mostly submerged. Should I cover it or leave it open?
Leave it uncovered unless it's splattering. Let it simmer gently, stirring now and then, until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, about 15 to 20 minutes.
While that cooks, should I get the tortillas ready?
Yes. Warm the tortillas in the oven or microwave until they're soft, so they're ready when the chicken finishes.
The chicken pieces look cooked through, and the tortillas are soft. Anything to check before serving?
Check that the chicken is no longer pink in the center and that the juices run clear. Remove the bay leaf, then spoon the chicken into the warm tortillas for the tacos.
Can you walk me through making Easy Fried Eggplant? I've got a large skillet ready but haven't prepped the eggplant yet.
Absolutely. Start by getting 1 large eggplant peeled and sliced. Set out 2 tablespoons canola oil for the skillet, plus 3 beaten eggs and 2 cups dry bread crumbs for coating.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced. Should I beat the eggs in a shallow dish for dipping?
Yes, a shallow dish is ideal for the beaten eggs. Put the dry bread crumbs in a second shallow dish so each slice can go from egg to crumbs without making a mess.
The egg and crumbs are set up next to the stove. How hot should the pan be?
Pour the 2 tablespoons canola oil into the large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat. Give it a short moment to get hot before adding the coated eggplant.
The oil is heating, and I'm ready to coat the slices. What order should I use?
Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg first, letting the excess drip off, then press it into the dry bread crumbs so it's coated. As each one is ready, place it carefully into the hot oil.
A few slices are in the skillet. How long do I fry them before turning?
Fry them for 2 to 3 minutes on the first side, watching for the coating to turn golden brown. Then flip and fry the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes, or until golden brown there too.
They're browning nicely, but I'm working in batches so the pan doesn't crowd. Is that fine?
That's fine. Keep coating and frying the remaining slices the same way, adding them to the hot oil in batches so each piece has room to brown.
The last batch is golden. What should I do with the pieces as they come out?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. Let the excess oil come off for a moment, then serve while the coating is still crisp.
Can you coach me through making Fudge Drops? I'm setting up the stove and counter now.
Absolutely. Set out a heavy saucepan, a spoon or heatproof spatula for constant stirring, and baking sheets lined with waxed paper for dropping the candy later.
I have the saucepan and waxed paper ready. Which ingredients should I measure before I turn on the burner?
Measure 1 2/3 cups sugar, 1 (5 ounce) can evaporated milk, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
The sugar and evaporated milk are measured. Should the butter be softened or just added as is?
You can add the butter or margarine as is; it will melt in the saucepan as the mixture heats.
Okay, the butter and salt are measured too. Do I combine everything in the pan before heating?
Yes. Put the sugar, evaporated milk, butter or margarine, and salt into the heavy saucepan before you start cooking.
They're all in the pan. What heat level should I use, and how much should I stir?
Set the pan over medium heat and stir constantly while you bring the mixture to a boil. Keep scraping the bottom and sides so it heats evenly.
It's bubbling now. Do I keep it on the heat once it reaches a boil?
Once it has come to a boil as directed, remove the saucepan from the heat. Then stir in the remaining ingredients called for in your recipe.
I've taken it off the burner and stirred it together. How do I portion the drops without making a mess?
Use a tablespoon to drop portions onto the waxed paper-lined baking sheets. Leave a little space between the fudge drops so they can set cleanly.
Can you walk me through making Babis Bean Salad? My black-eyed peas soaked overnight, and I'm getting the saucepan ready.

Absolutely. Have 1 1/2 cups dried black-eyed peas ready from the overnight soak, plus 1/3 cup chopped celery with its leaves. You'll also need 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley for the salad components.
The peas are drained, and the celery, carrot, and parsley are prepped. How much water should I add to the pan?
Put the soaked black-eyed peas in the saucepan, then add enough water to cover them by 1 inch. Use a pan with a little room at the top so the water can move as it heats.
They're covered by about an inch, and the burner is on. Am I aiming for a full rolling boil?
Aim gentler than that: bring the beans to a slow boil. You want steady bubbling, not an aggressive boil that bangs the beans around.
The water is bubbling slowly now. What heat level should I use from here?
Reduce the heat to low and let the beans simmer until they're tender but not mushy. The recipe gives about 35 minutes, so keep them at a quiet simmer and start checking texture near the end.
While they simmer, should I stir much or mostly leave them alone?
Give them an occasional gentle stir and make sure the beans stay submerged. If the water level drops too much, add just enough water to keep them covered while they finish softening.
It's been around 35 minutes. A bean is soft when I bite it, but it still holds its shape.
That sounds right: tender but not mushy. Take the saucepan off the heat and set the beans aside to cool.
Should I mix in the celery, shredded carrot, and parsley while the beans are still hot?

Let the beans cool first, as directed. Once they're no longer hot, you can combine them with the 1/3 cup chopped celery with leaves, 1 1/2 cups shredded carrot, and 3/4 cup chopped fresh parsley for the salad.
Can you walk me through making Badische Schupfnudeln Potato Noodles? I'm starting with the potatoes still unpeeled.

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 pounds russet potatoes, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley. You'll also want a large pot, a lightly floured work surface, and a rolling pin for mashing.
I've got the russets and the pot ready. Do the potatoes need to be peeled before boiling?
Keep them whole and in their skins. Bring a large pot of water to a boil, lower the potatoes in carefully, and boil them for 25 to 30 minutes.
They're in the boiling water now. How do I know when they've cooked enough?
At the end of that 25 to 30 minute window, they should feel tender when pierced. Since the recipe keeps the next step simple, just remove the potatoes once they're done and discard the water.
I drained the pot and the potatoes are on a plate, but they're too hot to hold.
Let them sit until they're cool enough to handle. Once you can touch them safely, peel off the skins.
The skins are off. Should I move them to a bowl or the counter?
Use a lightly floured surface rather than a bowl. Sprinkle a little of the all-purpose flour on the work area and place the peeled potatoes there.
The potatoes are on the floured surface. I still have the egg, parsley, and flour nearby.
Good. For this part, mash the potatoes with a rolling pin right on that lightly floured surface. Press and roll until they're broken down evenly.
They're mashed down pretty well. Is there anything special I should clean up before continuing later?

Discarded cooking water is already handled, so just keep the floured surface workable and the remaining ingredients close: the 1/2 cup flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley. The recipe steps you gave end after mashing the potatoes with the rolling pin.
Can you coach me through Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad? I'm starting with the chicken and skillet.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil total, keeping it divided, plus 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves that are 6 ounces each.
The chicken is ready. I want to make sure I'm not missing the seasoning before the pan gets hot.
You'll also need 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning and 2 cloves garlic, crushed. Keep both close to the stove so they're ready when the oil is hot.
I've got a large skillet out. How much oil goes in to start?
Pour 1 tablespoon olive oil into the large skillet and warm it over medium heat.
The oil is heating. Should I season the chicken while it warms?
Yes. Coat both sides of the chicken breast halves with the Cajun seasoning so the surface is evenly covered.
Both sides are seasoned. Do I lay them in the skillet now?
Yes, place the seasoned chicken into the hot oil carefully, laying each piece away from you to avoid splatter.
They're in the pan. Where does the crushed garlic fit in?
Stir the crushed garlic into the skillet around the chicken so it flavors the oil while the chicken cooks.
It smells good. How long should I cook the chicken, and what should I look for?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on each side, or until the juices run clear. Once it's cooked through, you can take it off the heat and let it rest briefly before serving with the salad.
I want to make Almond Apricot Bread. I've got a mixing bowl out—can you help me get organized before I start?
Absolutely. For the dry bowl, measure 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 3 teaspoons baking powder. You'll also need salt for that same bowl.
The flour and both sugars are measured. Should I whisk the baking powder and salt in with them?
Yes, use the large bowl for all of that. Combine the flour, sugars, baking powder, and salt until the mixture looks evenly blended and there are no clumps of brown sugar.
Dry ingredients are mixed. I see the jar of baby food—how much do I keep back for the glaze?
Spoon out 1 tablespoon of the baby food and set it aside for the glaze. Keep the rest nearby for the batter.
That tablespoon is in a small cup. What should I use for the wet mixture?
In another bowl, beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food. Mix until the egg is fully broken up and the liquids look smooth.
The wet bowl is blended, but I'm not sure how aggressively to combine it with the flour mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir gently. Stop as soon as everything is just moistened; a few small lumps are fine, and overmixing can make the bread tougher.
I still see a couple dry streaks along the side of the bowl. Should I keep folding?
Yes, scrape along the sides and bottom with a spatula, then fold just until those dry streaks disappear. Don't keep stirring once the batter is evenly damp.
The batter looks thick and moist now. Is there anything from the recipe I should double-check before moving on?

You've covered the listed prep: the dry ingredients are combined, 1 tablespoon baby food is reserved for glaze, the egg-milk-oil-extract mixture is beaten with the remaining baby food, and the wet and dry mixtures are stirred together just until moistened.
Can you walk me through making Eggnog Blend? I want to get the dairy and eggs set up correctly before I turn on the stove.
Absolutely. Set out 4 cups half-and-half and 1 cup white sugar for the stovetop base. You'll also need 11 beaten egg yolks and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract later.
I've got a saucepan ready. Should the half-and-half and sugar go in together while the pan is still cool?
Yes. Add the half-and-half and sugar to the saucepan, then keep the heat low and stir as it warms so the sugar dissolves evenly.
The sugar is dissolving. The mixture is warm but not bubbling—does that sound right?
That's right. Keep it over low heat. Whisk in the beaten egg yolks gradually, keeping the mixture moving so the yolks blend into the warm dairy.
The yolks are in, and I'm whisking. What texture am I looking for before I stop cooking it?
Cook it just until a light custard forms. It should thicken gently, but don't let it boil.
It's lightly thickened and coats the spoon a bit. Should I pull it off the heat now?
Yes, remove it from the heat now. Let the custard cool before you move it to the refrigerator.
Once it cools, how long does it need to chill? I'm planning ahead for serving tomorrow.
After it cools, refrigerate it and let it chill overnight. That gives the base time to get fully cold before the final additions.
It's the next day and the mixture is chilled. What do I stir in to finish the eggnog?
Stir the vanilla into the chilled mixture, then add the cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream. Mix until everything is smoothly blended and keep it cold for serving.
Can you talk me through making Adobo Chicken with Ginger? I've got a Dutch oven ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 whole chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into 8 pieces, plus 1/2 cup soy sauce so they're ready to go into the pot.
The chicken pieces and soy sauce are ready. What else needs to be measured or prepped?
Measure 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar, and peel and crush 1 bulb of garlic. You'll also need the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns the recipe calls for.
Garlic is crushed, vinegar is measured, and the aromatics are beside the stove. Do I brown the chicken first?
No browning step for this recipe. Put the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns directly into the Dutch oven together.
Everything is in the Dutch oven. Should the liquid cover the chicken completely?
It doesn't need to fully cover every piece. Just nestle the chicken into the soy sauce and vinegar mixture so it can cook evenly as it simmers.
The pot is on the stove. What heat should I use to start it?
Turn the burner to medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Keep an eye on it so the liquid comes up steadily rather than scorching.
It's starting to bubble around the edges and smells strongly of vinegar and garlic.
Once it reaches a real boil, lower the heat so it settles into a simmer. You want gentle bubbling, not a hard rolling boil.
It's simmering gently now. How long should I leave it, and do I need to stir?
Cover the Dutch oven and simmer the chicken for 30 minutes. Baste the pieces occasionally with the cooking liquid while they cook.
Can you guide me through Chicken Tortilla Soup IV? I've got a large pot ready but want to get organized first.
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin.
The tortillas are still whole. How should I cut them before we start heating the pot?
Cut the corn tortillas into strips about 1/2 inch wide. Keep them close to the stove, since you'll crisp them in batches.
Strips are cut. How much oil goes into the pot for the first batch?
Pour 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil into the large pot and warm it over medium heat.
The oil is heating. Should I put all the tortilla strips in at once?
Use only half of the tortilla strips for this first round. Add them to the pot and stir often so they crisp evenly.
They're starting to firm up, but a few pieces still bend. What texture am I waiting for?
Let them go until the strips are crisp rather than soft or bendy, while continuing to stir often so they don't catch in one spot.
Okay, the first batch is crisp. Where should I put them while I cook the rest?
Lift them out and drain them on paper towels. That keeps the strips from sitting in extra oil.
Paper towels are ready, and I still have half the strips left. What do I do for the second batch?

Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of vegetable oil to the pot, then crisp the remaining tortilla strips the same way. Drain them on paper towels too, and set the tortilla strips aside. Keep the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the soup.
Can you help me make Caramelized Apple Bites? I've got apples on the counter and want to do it in the microwave.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrapped and chopped, plus 2 tablespoons light corn syrup. Use a medium microwave-safe bowl for melting them together.
I found the caramels and corn syrup. The caramels are unwrapped—should I chop them pretty small?
Yes, chop them into smaller pieces so they melt more evenly. Put the chopped caramels in the microwave-safe bowl with the light corn syrup.
They're in the bowl. I still need to prep the apples—what exactly should I do with them?
Peel, core, and dice 2 apples. Keep the pieces bite-sized so they'll be easy to coat with the caramel mixture.
The apples are diced. Should I melt the caramel before adding them?
Yes. Microwave the bowl with the caramels and light corn syrup on high for approximately 30 seconds, just until the mixture is melted.
It's mostly melted but looks a little thick. Is that okay?
That's fine as long as the caramel is melted enough to coat the apples. Carefully stir the caramel and corn syrup together so it's smooth before adding the fruit.
Stirred and smooth. Do the apples go straight into the warm caramel?
Yes, place the diced apples in the bowl and toss them until they're coated with the caramel and light corn syrup mixture.
They're coated now. Should I serve them warm or wait?
Let the caramelized apple bites cool before serving so the coating can settle and they're easier to eat.
I want to make Cranberry Apple Pie II today. Can you guide me without rushing through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 6 apples, 1 (16 ounce) can of whole cranberry sauce, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour. You'll also need a pie plate and pastry to line it.
I've got the apples and cranberry sauce on the counter. Should I start the oven before I deal with the fruit?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. That way it can come up to temperature while you prepare the apples.
The oven is on. My pie plate is clean—what should I do with the pastry?
Line the pie plate with the pastry, pressing it gently into the bottom and up the sides so it sits evenly in the plate.
Pastry is in. For the apples, do they need to be peeled or can I leave the skins?
For this recipe, peel the apples, then core and slice them. Try to keep the slices fairly even so they mix well with the cranberry sauce.
I'm slicing them now. Is there anything I should mix with the fruit yet?
Once all 6 apples are peeled, cored, and sliced, put them in a medium-sized mixing bowl with the whole cranberry sauce.
The apples and cranberry sauce are in the bowl. Where do the brown sugar and flour fit in?
Measure out the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour so they're ready with the filling ingredients. Keep them close by as you work with the apple-cranberry mixture.
The bowl is getting full. Any tip before I transfer anything to the pastry-lined pie plate?

Use a large spoon or spatula and fold gently so the sliced apples get coated with the cranberry sauce without breaking down too much. Once it looks evenly combined, you're ready to move the mixture toward the lined pie plate.
I'm making Chicken Tortilla Soup IV. Can you guide me through the prep before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. You'll need 2 1/2 teaspoons vegetable oil, 6 corn tortillas that are 6 inches each, cut into 1/2 inch strips, 3 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin.
The tortillas are stacked on the board. Should I cut all 6 into strips now?
Yes, cut all 6 tortillas into 1/2 inch strips before cooking. Keep them nearby, because you'll crisp them in two batches.
What pot should I use, and how much oil goes in first?
Use a large pot and set it over medium heat. Add 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil to start.
The oil is heating. Do I put in all the tortilla strips at once?
Add only half of the tortilla strips to the pot. Stir them often so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in the oil.
They're starting to firm up. What texture am I looking for before I take them out?
Wait until that batch is crisp, then lift the strips out and drain them on paper towels.
The first batch is on paper towels. There's still some oil left, but not much.
For the second batch, add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon vegetable oil to the pot, then cook the remaining tortilla strips the same way until crisp.
Second batch is crisp too. Should I mix them into the soup base with the broth and cumin now?
Set the crisp tortilla strips aside for now. You have the 3 cups chicken broth and 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin ready for the soup base after this tortilla step.
Can you help me make Garlic Butter? I've got a mixing bowl out, but I want to be sure I'm starting with the right ingredients.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 tablespoon garlic salt. You'll also want Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika for seasoning.
My butter is soft enough to press with a spoon. Should I melt it or keep it like this?
Keep it softened rather than melted. Soft butter will blend smoothly with the garlic and Parmesan while still staying spreadable.
Okay, the butter is in the bowl. Do I add everything at once?
Add the minced garlic and grated Parmesan to the softened butter now. Mash and stir them together until the garlic and cheese are evenly worked through the butter.
It's mostly mixed, but I see a few streaks of plain butter. Is that a problem?
Give it another minute of stirring, scraping the sides of the bowl as you go. You're looking for a fairly even mixture with the garlic and Parmesan distributed throughout.
The texture looks even now. How much of the seasoning goes in?
Stir in the 1 tablespoon garlic salt, then add Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika to season it. Mix well so the spices don't stay in one pocket.
It smells pretty strong. Should I taste it before serving?
Yes, taste a tiny bit on bread, a cracker, or the tip of a spoon. If it tastes balanced and garlicky, you're ready; if any seasoning is sitting on top, fold it through again.
What's the best way to serve or store it once it's mixed?
Spoon it into a small dish for immediate serving, or scrape it onto parchment and shape it into a log for chilling. It's great spread on bread, melted over vegetables, or used to finish warm foods.
I'm making Chicken and Black Bean Chili tonight. Can you guide me through it while I prep?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons cooking oil and 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into 1 inch pieces. You'll also want a large pot ready for the stovetop.
The chicken is cut into 1 inch pieces, and I've got my large pot out. Which seasonings should I pull down?
Have sea salt ready, plus 1 tablespoon chili powder, or more to taste. Later you'll also season with cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Got it. Should I heat the pot before adding anything else?
Yes. Pour the 2 tablespoons cooking oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat until the oil looks loose and shimmery.
The oil is shimmering. Do I add all 3 chicken breast halves worth of pieces at once?
Add the chicken pieces to the pot in a single layer as much as you can. Let them brown on all sides, stirring or turning as needed so the surfaces pick up color.
The chicken is browning, but there's some liquid in the pot. Should I keep cooking it down?
Yes, keep it over medium heat and give it a little time. The chicken should brown on all sides; if the pot is crowded, stir occasionally and let the moisture reduce so the pieces can take on color.
The pieces look browned now. When do the spices go in?
Season the chicken now with sea salt, 1 tablespoon chili powder or to taste, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir well so the spices coat the chicken evenly.
The spices smell toasted. I have onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper chopped—do they go in next?
Yes, mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper. Stir them through the seasoned chicken so they start softening and picking up the chili spices.
Can you help me cook Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup? I've got a large pot out and want to prep everything before I turn on the stove.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 medium onion chopped, 1 green bell pepper chopped, and 1 large carrot peeled and thinly sliced. You'll also need black beans, chicken broth, and a blender for part of the beans later.
The onion and bell pepper are chopped, and I'm slicing the carrot thin so it cooks quickly. Should I heat the pot now?
Yes. Put the large pot over medium heat and add the vegetable oil. Let it warm until the oil looks loose and shimmery, but don't let it smoke.
The oil is shimmering. I also noticed the cooking step mentions garlic, so I have some ready with the vegetables.
Add the onion, green bell pepper, carrot, and garlic to the pot. Stir them through the oil so everything gets coated, then cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are tender.
After about 5 minutes the onion looks softer and the carrot slices are starting to bend. Is that tender enough?
That sounds right for this stage. The vegetables don't need to be fully mushy; they just need to soften so they'll blend into the soup flavor as it simmers.
I'm ready for the beans and broth. Do I add both cans of beans straight into the pot?
Add 1 can of black beans to the pot along with the chicken broth. Stir well, scraping the bottom of the pot so the softened vegetables mix evenly into the liquid.
One can of beans and the broth are in. The soup looks a little thin right now.
That's expected. The remaining can of black beans is there to thicken it: puree that can in a blender until smooth, then it can be stirred into the soup for a fuller texture.
For the blender part, should the beans be completely smooth or is a little texture okay?
For this recipe, aim for smooth puree from the remaining can of beans. A few tiny flecks are fine, but the smoother it is, the more it will give the black bean soup a rich, cohesive body.

source_seed.recipe_title: Fast and Delicious Black Bean Soup

messages.content: I want to make Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style. Can you help me get set up before I start cutting anything?
Absolutely. Have 1 spaghetti squash ready, cut it in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Also set out 1 chopped onion so it's ready when you need it.
The squash is halved and seeded, and the onion is chopped. What other ingredients should be on the counter?
You'll also need 2 tablespoons minced garlic and 2 cans of stewed tomatoes, 14 ounces each.
Got them. What oven temperature should I use for the squash?
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
The oven is heating. Do I need to prep the pan a certain way?
Yes. Spray a baking sheet with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash doesn't stick while it bakes.
Pan is sprayed. Should the squash face up or down?
Place the squash halves cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
They're on the sheet now. How long should I bake them?
Bake the squash in the preheated oven for 35 minutes.
How do I know if it's actually done at 35 minutes?
Check it with a knife: the squash is ready when a knife can be easily inserted. If it still feels firm, give it a little more time and check again.
Can you help me make Easy Pavlova? I've got my mixer out, but I want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 4 egg whites, 1 1/4 cups white sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 1 teaspoon lemon juice so everything is ready before you start mixing.
The egg whites are separated in a clean bowl, and I measured the sugar. Should I deal with the oven before mixing?
Yes, get the oven heating to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C. Pavlova works best when the oven is already steady before the meringue goes in.
Oven is preheating. I have a flat baking sheet—do I need to grease it or use parchment?
Use parchment paper. Line the baking sheet with it so the pavlova can release more easily after baking.
Parchment is on the tray, but I'm not sure how wide to make the pavlova.
Draw a 9 inch circle on the parchment paper as your guide. If you use pencil, flip the parchment over afterward so the marking doesn't touch the meringue.
Circle is drawn and flipped over. For the egg whites, what texture am I aiming for before adding anything else?
Beat the 4 egg whites in a large bowl until they're stiff but not dry. You want peaks that stand up, while the mixture still looks glossy rather than grainy.
They're starting to hold shape, but the tips bend a little. Should I keep beating?
Keep going a bit longer. Stop once the peaks stand firmly; don't push past that point or they can turn dry.
The peaks are stiff and glossy now. I still have the sugar, vanilla, and lemon juice measured—anything I should watch while continuing?

You're in good shape: you've preheated to 300 degrees F or 150 degrees C, lined the tray, marked the 9 inch circle, and beaten the egg whites until stiff but not dry. Keep the measured 1 1/4 cups white sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 1 teaspoon lemon juice close so the meringue stays smooth as you proceed.
I'm making Garden Potato Salad and already have cooked potatoes on the counter. Can you help me organize the prep?
Absolutely. Cube the 6 large cooked, peeled potatoes if they aren't cubed yet, and have 4 hard-cooked eggs sliced for the salad.
The potatoes are cubed and the eggs are sliced. What vegetables should I slice before I mix anything?
Slice 2 celery ribs and 6 green onions with their tops. The bowl step also includes radishes, plus salt and pepper, so have those ready too.
I've got a large mixing bowl out. Do the potatoes and vegetables all go in together?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the potatoes, sliced hard-cooked eggs, celery, green onions, radishes, salt, and pepper, then set that bowl aside.
The salad base is mixed. I'm setting up the stove now—what pan should I use for the dressing?
Use a saucepan. Add eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt to it, then stir them together before heating.
Should the burner be low or high while I cook that dressing?
Keep it at medium heat. Cook and stir the dressing until it thickens.

Can you help me make Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2? I've got a big mixing bowl out but want to be sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil. Those are the measured ingredients for this recipe.

Pour or spoon the mixture into the quiche pan you coated with nonstick cooking spray, scraping the bowl with a spatula so the filling settles evenly in the pan.

Open each pocket carefully just enough to make room for the filling. Try not to split the bread all the way through.

Wipe away any excess from the outside of the bread and lightly press the openings closed. The key prep is complete: pocketed French bread filled with the smooth ricotta, whipped cottage cheese, lowfat cream cheese, sugar, and flavoring extract mixture.

You can serve it immediately, or refrigerate it until serving. If refrigerating, cover the bowl well so the surface stays as fresh as possible.

messages.content: I want to make Badische Schupfnudeln Potato Noodles. What should I set out before I start?

Set out 1 1/2 pounds russet potatoes, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 egg, and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley. You'll also need a large pot for boiling and a lightly floured surface for handling the potatoes later.
The potatoes are on the counter. Should I peel them before boiling?
Keep the skins on for the boil. Put the whole russet potatoes into a large pot of boiling water and let them cook for 25 to 30 minutes, until they're tender enough to handle after cooling.
They've been boiling close to 30 minutes. How do I know they're ready to come out?
They should feel tender when pierced through the skin. Once they're ready, lift the potatoes out of the pot and discard the boiling water.
I drained the pot and the potatoes are still pretty hot. Do I work with them right away?
Let them cool just until you can handle them safely. When they're cool enough, peel off the skins.
The skins are off. My counter is clean—what should I do with the flour?
Dust the work surface lightly with some of the all-purpose flour, then place the peeled potatoes on that floured surface so they don't stick while you mash them.
Do I use a masher, or is there a specific tool for this version?
Use a rolling pin here. Mash the potatoes with the rolling pin on the lightly floured surface, working them down until they're broken up and smooth enough to continue with the dough ingredients.
Where do the egg and parsley fit in? I don't want to forget them.

Keep the 1 egg and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley ready beside the mashed potatoes, along with the remaining flour. At this point the recipe's listed prep has you boiled, peeled, placed on the floured surface, and mashed with the rolling pin.
I'm making Best Macaroni Salad and want to get everything lined up before I boil the pasta. What should be on the counter?

Set out 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup cucumber that's peeled, seeded, and chopped, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. You'll also want a large pot for boiling, a colander, and a large mixing bowl.
I've got the pot and colander ready. Should the water be salted before the macaroni goes in?
Yes, salt the boiling water, then add the macaroni and cook it until it's al dente. Once it's there, rinse the pasta under cold water and drain it well.
The macaroni is cooked and cooling in the colander. Do I need it completely dry?
It doesn't need to be bone-dry, but shake off the excess water so the salad doesn't turn watery. Transfer the drained macaroni to your large bowl when it's cooled.
The pasta is in the bowl. Does the mayonnaise go in before the vegetables?
Yes. Add the 1/2 cup mayonnaise to the pasta and mix well so the macaroni gets evenly coated before you stir in the other ingredients.
It looks coated. I have the cucumber chopped and the dried minced onion measured.
Stir in the 1 cup peeled, seeded, chopped cucumber and the 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. The recipe also has you stir in ham and cheese at this point.
I added those in. Should I fold gently or really stir it around?
Mix it well, scraping around the sides and bottom of the bowl so the mayonnaise, cucumber, onion, ham, and cheese are evenly distributed through the macaroni.
Everything is combined. How should it look before I serve it?
It should look evenly mixed and creamy, with the cucumber, onion, ham, and cheese spread throughout the macaroni. Give it one final toss, then it's ready to serve.

Put the dry base near the bowl: 1 cup quick cooking oats, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 3/4 cup flaked coconut.

Keep 1 teaspoon baking soda separate for the moment; it gets mixed with boiling water before going into the butter and syrup.

Use the small saucepan over low heat to melt the syrup and butter together, stirring gently so they blend without scorching.
The butter has melted into the syrup, and the pan is still on low. What should I do with the baking soda?
Mix the soda with the boiling water, then add that mixture to the melted butter and syrup.
It foamed up a little when I added it. Should I pour it straight into the dry bowl?

The mixture is together now. Since I'm using it for the filling, should I stir in those small browned pieces at the end?

I want to make Dutch Cream Waffles. Can you walk me through the prep so I don't mix things in the wrong bowl?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and a small mixing bowl. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt, and keep your separated eggs nearby: 3 egg yolks and 3 egg whites.
I've got the bowls out. Should the flour and salt go together right away?
Yes. Put the flour and salt into the large mixing bowl and stir them together so the salt is evenly spread through the flour.
The dry bowl is ready. For the eggs, am I using the yolks first or the whites?
Use the yolks first. Place the 3 egg yolks in the small mixing bowl, then beat them on low speed while you add the cream.
I'm adding the cream slowly while the mixer is on low. How long should I keep beating it?
Once the cream is in with the yolks, keep beating the mixture for 1 minute.
That minute is done. The yolk mixture looks loose and smooth; does it go into the flour now?
Yes, pour the yolk and cream mixture into the large bowl with the flour and salt.
It's in the dry ingredients. Should I start the mixer slowly to avoid flour flying everywhere?
Exactly. Combine it on low speed at first, just until the flour starts to hydrate and the mixture comes together.
The batter has mostly come together but still has a few streaks. What texture am I aiming for before cooking?

Increase to medium-high speed and beat until the batter is smooth. Keep the separated egg whites nearby if your full waffle method calls for them next, but this part of the recipe ends once the mixture is smooth.
Can you help me make Drunken Fruit Salsa? I've got a cutting board out and want to prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by peeling and finely dicing 1 medium mango, then add it to a glass bowl. The small dice helps the salsa scoop easily.
The mango is diced. How should I handle the strawberries so they match the texture?
Chop 3/4 cup fresh strawberries into small pieces, close to the size of the mango dice, and add them to the bowl.
Strawberries are in. I also have a kiwi and jalapeno ready—what should I do with those?
Peel and finely dice 1 kiwi, then seed and finely chop 1 jalapeno pepper. Stir both into the mango and strawberry mixture.
Should the jalapeno pieces be really tiny, or is a rough chop okay?
Go fairly tiny with the jalapeno so the heat spreads evenly and no one gets a big spicy bite. Since it's seeded, it should add brightness more than intense heat.
Everything is chopped and in the glass bowl. The recipe mentions mint and rum—do I stir those in now too?
Yes. Stir the mango, strawberries, kiwi, jalapeno, mint, and rum together in the glass bowl until the fruit is evenly coated without crushing it.
It's mixed. Should I serve it right away, or does it need time to sit?
Refrigerate it for 1 to 3 hours so the flavors can blend. During that time, stir it once or twice to redistribute the juices and rum.
If I'm serving it later, what should I check before putting it out?
Give it a gentle final stir, check that the fruit still looks fresh and juicy, then serve it chilled. A glass serving bowl works nicely since the colors are bright.

Can you guide me through making Easy Pavlova? I want to get the ingredients and pan setup right before I start whipping anything.

Absolutely. Set out 4 egg whites, 1 1/4 cups white sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. For equipment, you'll want a large bowl, a mixer or whisk, a baking sheet, parchment paper, and something to trace a circle with.
I've got the egg whites and sugar measured. Should the oven be on before I line the pan?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C. That gives it time to come to temperature while you prepare the parchment.
The oven is heating. I have a baking sheet out, but I'm not sure how to position the parchment.
Lay the parchment paper flat on the baking sheet so it covers the area where the pavlova will sit. If it curls, you can crease the corners a bit so it stays in place.
Okay, parchment is down. The recipe mentions a circle—how big should I make it?
Draw a 9 inch circle on the parchment paper. A plate or cake pan can help you trace it evenly.
Should the pencil side face up when I put the meringue on it?
After you draw the circle, flip the parchment over so the mark is underneath but still visible. That way the pavlova shape is guided by the circle without the mixture touching the pencil or pen mark.
Good idea. I'm ready to start the meringue—what texture am I aiming for with the egg whites?
Put the 4 egg whites in a large bowl and beat them until they're stiff but not dry. They should hold firm peaks, but still look smooth and glossy rather than clumpy or grainy.
If they start looking a little dry around the edges, should I keep beating to make them firmer?
No, stop once they're stiff but not dry. Overbeating can make the texture rough, and for this Easy Pavlova you want the egg whites structured but still smooth before adding the remaining ingredients.

Can you help me make Carrots and Onions Au Gratin? I've got the cutting board out and want to prep everything before heating the oven.
Absolutely. Slice 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots and 2 medium onions. You'll also need 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter nearby.
The carrots are baby carrots, so should I just cut them into thinner slices, and do the onions need to be rings or strips?
Thin carrot slices are perfect so they cook evenly. Slice the 2 onions however you like for layering—rings or half-moons both work.

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Set out a baking dish so it's ready when the carrots and onions are drained.

Put the sliced carrots and onions in the pot, then add enough lightly salted water to cover them. Bring that to a boil.

Cook them for 5 minutes, just until the vegetables are tender but still firm.

Yes, tender but firm is right. Drain the carrots and onions well so the baking dish doesn't get watery.
They're drained. How should I start assembling them in the dish with the cheese and butter waiting?
Spread 1/2 of the drained carrots and onions in the baking dish. Keep the 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter ready for the next layer or topping.

Can you help me make Chocolate Crisps? I want to set up the ingredients before I turn on the oven.
Absolutely. Put out 1 tablespoon softened butter, 1 egg white, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also need cookie sheets, a small saucepan, and a medium-sized bowl.
I have the egg white separated and the sugar measured. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C.
The oven is set to 300. While it heats, what should I do with the cookie sheets?
Grease the cookie sheets so the crisps will release more easily later. A light, even coating is enough.
Cookie sheets are greased. The butter is softened, but the recipe says to melt it—do I use the saucepan now?
Yes. Put the 1 tablespoon butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and melt it until it becomes lightly browned.

Watch for the color to shift from yellow to a light golden brown. It may smell a little nutty; take it off the heat before it gets dark.

Pour the browned butter into a medium-sized bowl.
