Yes. Measure 1/4 cup lime juice and pour it over the mango, red onion, and cilantro.
Everything is in the bowl now. Should I stir hard or keep it gentle?
Fold it together gently with a spoon so the mango stays in pieces while the lime juice coats everything evenly.
It's mixed and looks juicy. Is it ready to serve right away?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving so the flavors can come together.
Should I leave it in the same bowl while it stands, or move it to a serving dish?
The same bowl is fine. Give it a light stir after the 30 minutes, then serve it with a spoon so the lime juice and chopped ingredients stay evenly distributed.
I'm making Crab Cake Sauce to go with dinner. Can you talk me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put your blender on the counter and measure out 1 cup sour cream and 1 cup mayonnaise to start.
The blender is ready, and I've measured the sour cream and mayonnaise. What else goes in?
Add 1/2 cup cottage cheese and 1/3 cup hot salsa to your ingredients. You'll also want the cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt called for in the blending step.
Do I put everything in the blender at once, or should I blend part of it first?
You can combine everything in the blender together: sour cream, mayonnaise, cottage cheese, hot salsa, cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and yogurt.
It's all in the blender. What texture am I aiming for?
Puree it until the sauce looks smooth, with no visible cottage cheese curds and the salsa fully blended in.
It looks creamy now, but there are a few tiny flecks from the salsa. Is that okay?
Yes, small salsa flecks are fine. As long as the base is smooth and evenly blended, the sauce is ready to chill.
Should I transfer it to a bowl before chilling?
Yes. Scrape it into a covered bowl or storage container, then chill it before serving so the sauce firms up slightly and tastes cold with the crab cakes.
It's covered and in the fridge. Any serving advice once it's cold?
Give it a quick stir before serving, then spoon it alongside or over the crab cakes. Keep any extra sauce chilled until you're ready to use it.
I'm making Baked Fake Steak with Gravy. Can you help me set up without getting ahead of the recipe?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and gather 3 pounds ground beef, 17 finely crushed saltine crackers, 1/2 cup milk, and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder.
I've got the beef and milk ready. Do the crackers need to be powdery or just broken down?
Finely crushed is what you want, so they should be small crumbs rather than big pieces. They'll mix more evenly into the beef that way.
Okay, the crackers are crushed. Should I add everything to the bowl at once?
Add the ground beef, crushed saltine crackers, and milk to the large bowl, then mix them together until the crackers and milk are distributed through the meat.
The mixture is starting to come together, but I haven't seasoned it yet.
Sprinkle in the garlic powder, then season with onion powder, salt, and pepper. Mix again until the seasoning is well blended throughout the beef mixture.
How much should I work the meat mixture? I don't want it falling apart in the pan.
Mix it until it looks cohesive and evenly seasoned, but you don't need to knead it hard. Once the milk and cracker crumbs are fully incorporated, you can stop.
I'm ready for the pan. What size should I use, and do I grease it?
Use a 10x15 inch jellyroll pan and line it with waxed paper. The recipe calls for the waxed paper lining rather than greasing the pan.
The pan is lined. How should I shape the beef so it cooks evenly later?
Transfer the beef mixture into the lined pan and press it firmly into an even layer, reaching the corners and smoothing the top so the thickness is consistent.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this version, add just the tiniest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Asian Ginger Dressing, I'm serving it cold over fruit and I'm considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. What should I do with those warm spices?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Asian Ginger Dressing as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: For this batch of Asian Ginger Dressing, I'm serving it cold over fruit and I'm considering cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. What should I do with those warm spices?
For this version, add just the tiniest pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Perfect, that's the direction I want for this bowl of fruit. What should I prep before I start mixing?
Mince 3 cloves of garlic and 2 tablespoons of fresh ginger root. Since you're using that tiny extra pinch of ginger for the fruit angle, keep it separate so you can control it.
The garlic and ginger are minced. Which liquids should I measure now?
Measure 3/4 cup olive oil and 1/3 cup rice vinegar, and have the soy sauce, honey, and water nearby too.
I've got the liquids lined up. What container works best for shaking this?
Use a glass jar that holds 1 pint or more. Add the minced garlic, minced ginger, olive oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and water to the jar.
Everything is in the jar, and the honey is sitting thick at the bottom. Do I shake it before warming?
Yes. Put on a tight-fitting lid and shake it well so the ingredients start to blend before the honey gets warmed.
It's shaken, but I can still see honey streaks. How do I warm it without overdoing it?
Take the lid off, then microwave the jar for 1 minute, just long enough to dissolve the honey.
The honey dissolved. Since I'm serving it chilled with fruit, should I put the lid back on right away?
Let the dressing cool first, then put the lid back on and shake it well again before serving.
How should it look when it's ready to spoon over the fruit?
It should look well mixed after shaking, with the garlic and ginger suspended through the dressing. Give it one more shake right before serving it cold over the fruit.
Can you walk me through making the Banana Kiwi Strawberry Tart crust? I'm setting up my counter now.

Absolutely. Put a mixing bowl, sifter, fork, plastic wrap, and a pastry cutter or two knives within reach. For the dry mix, measure 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon light brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon salt.
I've measured the flour and brown sugar. Should the cinnamon and salt go through the sifter too?
Yes, add the cinnamon and salt to the sifter with the flour and brown sugar so everything blends evenly.
All four dry ingredients are in the bowl after sifting. It smells pretty cinnamon-forward.
Great. Give the bowl a quick shake or light stir if any brown sugar clumps stayed behind, then add the butter and cut it into the dry ingredients.
I have the butter in there, but I'm not sure how small the pieces should get.
Keep cutting it in until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs, with small uneven bits rather than a smooth paste.
It's crumbly now, with a few pea-sized bits. Do I add the ice water all at once?
Sprinkle the ice water over the crumbs instead of pouring it in one spot, then toss with a fork so the moisture spreads evenly.
The dough is starting to hold together in damp clumps, but it isn't a ball yet.
That's fine. Use the fork or your fingertips just enough to bring the evenly moistened crumbs together without overworking them.
It's together now. How do I wrap it so it chills neatly?
Pat the dough into a round, place it on plastic wrap, and wrap it snugly so the edges are covered and it holds its shape.
I want to make Biga today. Can you guide me through the ingredients before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast and 1/2 cup warm water for blooming the yeast.
Those are on the counter. What should I pull out for the main bowl?
You'll need 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour and 1 1/4 cups cold water. Also grab a small bowl for the yeast and a large bowl for the flour.
I have both bowls ready. Does the yeast go straight into the flour?
Not yet. Pour the warm water into the small bowl, then sprinkle the active dry yeast over the top so it can hydrate evenly.
The yeast is sprinkled over the warm water. Should I stir it or leave it alone?
Let it stand until the yeast dissolves and looks foamy, about 15 minutes. You can leave it mostly undisturbed while it activates.
While that sits, can I measure the flour now?
Yes. Measure 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into the large bowl while the yeast mixture is getting foamy.
The flour is in the bowl, and the yeast is starting to foam. How should I combine everything?
Make a well in the center of the flour. Pour the foamy yeast mixture into that well, then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water.
So the cold water goes in with the yeast mixture, not separately around the edges?
Right—pour the yeast mixture and the cold water into the well in the center of the flour, keeping everything contained for easier mixing.
I'm making Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds. Can you help me get started with the potatoes?
Absolutely. Peel and cube 6 Yukon Gold potatoes and 2 sweet potatoes, then keep them close to the stove so they can go straight into a large pot.
The Yukon Golds and sweet potatoes are peeled and cubed. How big should the pot be?
Use a large pot with enough room for all the cubed potatoes, then add enough water to cover them.
They're in the pot and covered with water. Do I need anything else on the counter right now?
Yes—set out 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup heavy cream so they're ready when you need them.
Butter and cream are measured. Should I turn the burner on high?
Bring the pot to a boil. High heat is fine to get it there, but keep an eye on it so the water doesn't bubble over.
It's starting to boil around the edges, and the cubes are moving a bit.
Let it come to a full boil, with bubbles rising steadily through the pot.
It's fully boiling now. What should I do with the pot?
Remove the pot from the heat, then drain the potatoes and sweet potatoes carefully.
They're drained in the colander. Is the oven involved at this point?
Yes. Preheat the oven broiler so it's ready for the next part of the dish.
I'd like to make Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth. Can you help me get set up before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Put a large pot on the stove and have 2 quarts water ready. You'll also need 12 ounces beef shank for the broth base.
The pot is out, and I've got the water and beef shank. Are there vegetables to prep now?
Yes. Chop 2 large onions and slice 2 large carrots so they're ready when you need them.
The onions are chopped and the carrots are sliced. Should I add them right away or start with the water?
Start by bringing the 2 quarts water to a boil in the large pot.
The water is heating now. Once it boils, how do I handle the beef shank?
When the water reaches a boil, place the 12 ounces beef shank into the pot, then reduce the heat so it simmers gently for 1 1/2 hours.
It's simmering steadily. Should I skim or stir, or mostly leave it alone during that time?
Keep the simmer steady and avoid a hard boil. You can check the pot occasionally, but the key recipe step is letting the beef shank simmer for the full 1 1/2 hours.
The simmering time is done. The broth is still hot—what should I do before cutting the meat?
Let the broth cool overnight before you lift out the meat. That pause is part of the process for this cawl.
It cooled overnight. How do I prep the meat now?
Lift the meat out of the pot, trim off any gristle, cut the meat into medium sized pieces, and set it aside.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Use only the soft, slender stems: chop them finely into the dressing or tomato mixture, and hold the leaves back so they stay fresh and separate.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Chunky Pizza Dip, I'm using it more like a fresh salsa-style topping with cilantro or parsley stems mixed in. What should I do with those stems?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Dice only the most tender stems into the dressing and keep the leaves separate.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chunky Pizza Dip as a raw salad, salsa, or uncooked topping with cilantro or parsley stems. How should I handle the stems?

messages.content: For this batch of Chunky Pizza Dip, I'm using it more like a fresh salsa-style topping with cilantro or parsley stems mixed in. What should I do with those stems?
Use only the soft, slender stems: chop them finely into the dressing or tomato mixture, and hold the leaves back so they stay fresh and separate.
Great, that's just for this batch. I've cleared space beside the cutting board—what should I pull out first?
Put 2 tablespoons olive oil and 3 minced garlic cloves within reach. You'll also want a large saucepan or Dutch oven ready for the garlic and oil.
Garlic is minced, and the Dutch oven is on the stove. Should I open the cans now?
Yes. Open 2 cans of petite diced tomatoes, 14.5 ounces each, and measure 1/4 cup tomato paste so both can go in quickly once the garlic is ready.
The tomatoes and paste are measured. How gentle should I be with the garlic?
Add the olive oil and minced garlic to the pan, then heat them together until the garlic starts to sizzle and turns golden. Don't push it past golden, or it can taste harsh.
It's sizzling and the edges of the garlic are just turning golden.
Add the petite diced tomatoes and the tomato paste. Stir in the basil and oregano, then bring the mixture up to a simmer.
The tomatoes are bubbling lightly now, and the paste is stirred in.
Let it simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens enough for dipping, about 15 to 20 minutes. Stir now and then so the bottom doesn't catch.
After about 15 minutes, it's thicker but still a little loose around the edges of the spoon.
Give it a few more minutes, closer to the 20-minute mark, if you want it chunkier and scoopable. Stop once it mounds a bit instead of running right off the spoon.
It's thick enough for chips now. What should I do before serving later?
Take it off the heat, let it cool, and refrigerate it. Keep those chopped tender stems with the fresh component, and add the leaves separately when you're ready to serve.
Can you walk me through Easy Fried Eggplant? I have a large skillet out and want to keep the coating organized.
Absolutely. Set up 1 large eggplant, peeled and sliced, plus 3 beaten eggs in one shallow dish and 2 cups dry bread crumbs in another. Keep 2 tablespoons canola oil nearby for the skillet.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced. Should I heat the pan before I start dipping the pieces?
Yes. Pour the 2 tablespoons canola oil into the large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat while you get a few slices ready to coat.
The eggs are beaten and the bread crumbs are in a bowl. What order should each slice go through?
Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg first, let the excess drip off briefly, then press it into the dry bread crumbs so the surface is coated.
I've coated several slices. How do I know the oil is ready for them?
When the oil looks hot and moves easily across the pan, place the coated eggplant slices into the skillet in a single layer. Avoid crowding so they fry instead of steaming.
They're in the pan now. How long should I leave the first side alone?
Fry the slices for 2 to 3 minutes on that side, or until the underside is golden brown.
The bottoms are golden. Do I flip them and use the same timing?
Yes, turn them carefully and fry the second side for another 2 to 3 minutes, again looking for a golden brown crust.
Both sides look crisp and golden. Where should I put them when they come out?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. Let the extra oil come off for a moment, then serve while the coating is still crisp.
Can you help me make Black Bean Lasagna Rolls? I've got a pot ready for the noodles.

Absolutely. Set out 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta cheese, and 1 (4.5 ounce) can chopped green chiles, drained. You'll also need the black beans for layering over the cheese mixture.
I found the noodles and both cheeses. Should I start boiling water now?
Yes. Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, but omit any salt and fat. When they're done, drain them well so they're not slippery or watery when you fill them.
The noodles are in the pot. While they cook, can I get the filling ready?
You can. Combine the Monterey Jack, the part-skim ricotta, and the drained chopped green chiles with the next ingredients called for in the filling, stirring until the mixture is well blended.
Should the cheese mixture be completely smooth, or is it okay if the chiles show?
It's fine for the chiles to show. Aim for an evenly stirred filling, not a perfectly smooth one, so each roll gets some cheese and chile throughout.
The noodles are drained. They're a little sticky on the counter—how should I handle them?
Lay them out flat and separate them gently so they don't tear. If any are very wet, blot lightly, because the cheese mixture will spread more easily on a drier noodle surface.
Okay, I have the noodles lined up. How much filling goes on each one?
Spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle, dividing it as evenly as you can among all 8 noodles. Leave just enough room at the edges to keep the filling from squeezing out.
The cheese is spread on the noodles. Where do the black beans go?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on each noodle. Once they're distributed, the rolls are ready for whatever baking or saucing step your full recipe uses next.
Can you help me make Aaahh Potato Soup? I'm starting with the potatoes and want to be sure I have the right amounts.
Absolutely. You'll need 2 Yukon Gold potatoes, cubed, plus 1 package of au gratin instant potato mix, the 5.5 ounce size.
The potatoes are cubed, and I found the au gratin mix. What liquid should I set out?
Set out 1 can of condensed chicken broth, 10.5 ounces, and measure 1 1/2 cups water. Keep a little extra water nearby in case the potatoes need more coverage in the pot.
I have a large pot ready. Do the dry mix and broth go in together, or should I wait?
Put them in together: add the cubed Yukon Gold potatoes, the au gratin potato mix, the condensed chicken broth, and the measured water to the large pot.
It looks a bit thick already, and some potato pieces are sitting above the liquid.
Add just enough extra water to cover the potatoes if needed. Stir gently so the au gratin mix disperses into the broth and water.
The potatoes are covered now. What heat should I use so it doesn't scorch?
Set the pot over medium heat. Let it cook while you stir occasionally, especially along the bottom, until the potatoes are tender.
About how long should I expect that to take, and how do I check tenderness?
Plan on about 40 minutes. Check by piercing a potato cube with a fork; it should slide in easily without the potato feeling hard in the center.
The potatoes are tender and the soup has thickened. How do I handle the cream at the end?
Stir in the cream and heat it through gently, just until the soup is hot again. Keep stirring so it blends smoothly, then serve the Aaahh Potato Soup warm.
Can you guide me through making Baked Apple Oatmeal? I'm setting out the saucepan and casserole dish now.
Absolutely. Measure out 4 cups milk and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and keep them near the stove.
Milk and brown sugar are measured. Do I need anything else before the pan goes on the heat?
Yes—add 2 teaspoons butter or margarine and 1/2 teaspoon salt to your prep. You'll also need cinnamon for the saucepan mixture.
Got it. Should I grease the baking dish before I start heating the milk?
That's a good time to do it. Grease a 2-qt. casserole so it's ready when the oatmeal mixture is combined.
The casserole is greased, and the saucepan is on the burner. What goes in first?
Put the milk, packed brown sugar, butter or margarine, salt, and cinnamon into the saucepan, then heat them together, stirring so the sugar dissolves and the milk warms evenly.
The butter has melted and the milk mixture is warm. Should it boil?
No need to push it to a hard boil. Once everything is heated together and the brown sugar is dissolved, you can move on.
Okay, I'm ready to add the oatmeal mixture ingredients. How gently should I stir?
Add the remaining ingredients and mix gently—fold just until everything is moistened and evenly distributed, rather than beating it.
It's mixed and in the greased casserole. What are the baking directions?
Cover the 2-qt. casserole and bake it at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes. Let it sit briefly after baking so it's easier to serve.
Can you help me cook Garlic Chicken Stir Fry? I've got a wok out and want to prep before turning on the heat.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep the chicken nearby too, since it goes in after the aromatics.
I'm a little confused about the garlic: the ingredient list says 6 cloves, but the cooking step mentions 2 cloves. What should be ready for the pan?
Mince all 6 cloves so they're prepared, and for the step where the oil begins to smoke, add 2 cloves worth of the minced garlic with the ginger, green onions, and salt.
Okay, garlic is minced and the green onions are chopped. Should I add the oil cold or heat the wok first?
Put the wok or large skillet on the heat with the 2 tablespoons peanut oil in it, then let the oil heat until it just begins to smoke.
The oil is close to smoking. Do the aromatics all go in at once?
Yes—work quickly here. Stir in the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt.
They're in, and it smells strong right away. How long should I keep them moving?
Stir-fry them for about 2 minutes, just until the green onion turns translucent. Keep everything moving so the garlic doesn't sit and scorch.
The onions look softer and a bit translucent now. Is this when the chicken goes in?
Yes, add the chicken now. Stir it through the hot aromatics so the pieces get coated and cook evenly.
How do I know when to stop cooking the chicken?
Cook and stir until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes. Once there's no translucent look left on the pieces, take it off the heat and serve it right away.
Can you help me make Fruit Dip 2? I want to get everything set out before I start mixing.
Absolutely. Put out 8 ounces cream cheese, 1/2 cup marshmallow creme, 2 cups frozen whipped topping that's thawed, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice.
The whipped topping is thawed, but the cream cheese is still a little firm. Is that okay?
It will blend more easily if the cream cheese is softened a bit. Let it sit briefly if you can, then add it to a mixing bowl with the marshmallow creme and thawed whipped topping.
I've got those in the bowl. Should I use a spoon or a mixer?
A hand mixer will make it smoother, but a sturdy spoon or spatula works too. Blend until the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and whipped topping are evenly combined.
It's mostly smooth now, with just a few tiny cream cheese streaks.
Keep blending a little longer and scrape the sides of the bowl so the mixture becomes creamy and even throughout.
Okay, it looks creamy. Do I pour in all the pineapple juice?
Add the unsweetened pineapple juice gradually, using up to the 1/4 cup, just until the dip loosens to a good dipping consistency.
It's thick but dips off the spoon slowly. Should I stop there?
Yes, that sounds right for a fruit dip. If it holds fruit well and isn't runny, you don't need to add more juice.
How long should it chill before I serve it with fruit?
Cover the bowl and chill the dip for 1 hour. After that, give it a quick stir and serve it cold with your fruit.
Can you talk me through making Crab Quiche? I have a frozen deep dish crust but want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set out 1 (9 inch) deep dish frozen pie crust, 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need pepper and hot sauce for the egg mixture.
The crust is still frozen and in its tin. Should I heat the oven before mixing anything?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. While it heats, keep the crust in its dish and have a large bowl and whisk ready.
Oven is heating. Do I bake the empty crust right away or wait for it to thaw?
Bake the pie crust empty once the oven is ready. Give it about 10 minutes, just until it is starting to brown.
Should I dock it with a fork or weigh it down?
The recipe only says to bake the crust until it just starts to brown, so follow that without adding extra steps unless your crust package specifically calls for them.
It's been in for 10 minutes and the edge is lightly browned. What should I do with it now?
Take the crust out of the oven and let it cool. Leave the oven on if you're continuing with the quiche filling soon.
While it cools, I'm ready to make the custard. What goes into the bowl?
In a large bowl, whisk together the 4 eggs, 1 cup heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus pepper and hot sauce.
How well should I whisk it—just combined or really foamy?
Whisk until the eggs, cream, salt, pepper, and hot sauce are evenly blended and smooth. It does not need to be foamy; just make sure there are no streaks of egg left.
I want to make Biriyani today. Can you guide me from the ingredient setup onward?
Absolutely. Put a large skillet on the stove, and set out 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar, and 1 medium onion, sliced.
I have the skillet and the onion sliced. Should I measure the yogurt and vinegar before turning on the heat?
Yes, measure them now so they're ready to add quickly: 3 tablespoons plain yogurt and 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar.
Measured. The olive oil is still in the bottle—how much goes into the skillet?
Add 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil to the large skillet, then heat it over medium heat.
The pan is on medium and the oil is warming. Do I wait for it to get hot before adding anything?
Let it warm briefly, then mix in the plain yogurt and distilled white vinegar. Stir so they combine with the oil in the skillet.
The yogurt and vinegar are in, and the mixture looks a little loose. Is the onion next?
Yes. Add the 1 medium sliced onion to the skillet and cook it until tender, stirring so the slices soften evenly.
The onion is softening but not browned much. Is tender the main thing I'm looking for here?
Tender is the goal for this step. Once the onion slices have softened, you're ready to add the next ingredients.
The onion feels tender now. What do I add to build the sauce?
Mix in the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes. Stir them through the onion mixture so everything starts coming together in the skillet.
I want to make Broiled Egg Salad Sandwiches for lunch. Can you help me get the filling started without making a mess?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl and add 3 chopped hard-cooked eggs. Keep the crushed saltine crackers nearby too—you'll need 1/4 cup of them in the egg mixture.
The eggs are chopped, and I measured the crackers. Should the celery and pimientos go in the same bowl?
Yes. Add 1/4 cup chopped celery and 1 tablespoon diced pimientos to the bowl with the eggs and crushed saltines, then gently toss everything together so the eggs don't get mashed too much.
That mixture looks a little chunky, which seems right. What do I mix separately?
In a second bowl, combine the mayonnaise, milk, salt, garlic salt, and pepper. Stir until it looks smooth and evenly seasoned before you add it to the egg mixture.
I've got the dressing mixed. Should I pour all of it in at once or fold it in gradually?
Add it to the egg mixture and stir gently until the eggs, crackers, celery, and pimientos are coated. Try to keep some texture rather than turning it into a paste.
The filling is combined. Do I need to grease the baking sheet before I put the muffin halves on it?
No, use an ungreased baking sheet. Arrange the muffin halves on it so they're ready to be topped.
How much egg salad should I put on each muffin half so they're even?
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the egg salad mixture onto each muffin half, spreading it lightly so it sits in an even layer.
They're portioned on the sheet. Anything I should check before broiling?

Make sure the muffin halves are stable on the ungreased baking sheet and the topping isn't piled too high in the center. Then they're ready to go under the broiler according to your recipe's next broiling direction.
I want to make Eggnog II. Can you help me get set up before I turn on the stove?

Absolutely. Set out a large saucepan, a spoon for stirring, and a metal spoon to check the custard. For ingredients, you'll need 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I've beaten the eggs and measured the milk. Should the sugar go in right away too?
Yes. Put the beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, and 1/3 cup white sugar into the large saucepan together. Stir them well before heating so the eggs are evenly mixed in.
The pan is mixed. What heat should I use so the eggs don't scramble?
Use medium heat and keep stirring. The goal is to warm it gently until the mixture coats a metal spoon, not to let it boil.
How do I know when it really coats the spoon?
Dip the metal spoon into the mixture and lift it out. If a thin layer clings to the back of the spoon instead of running off immediately, it's ready to come off the heat.
It's coating the spoon now, and I'm worried about carryover heat.
Take the saucepan off the heat right away. Keep it steady and move carefully, since the mixture is hot.
Should I stir in the vanilla before cooling, or wait?
Stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract now so it blends through the warm eggnog.
The vanilla is in. What's the fastest safe way to cool the pan?
Place the saucepan in a sink or bowl filled with ice water and stir the eggnog for 1 to 2 minutes. That cools it quickly while keeping the texture even.
I want to make Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats, and I already baked the potatoes. Can you guide me from here?

Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F so it's heating while you prep. You'll need 4 medium baked potatoes quartered lengthwise, 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing, 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, and sliced green onions if you want them for serving.
The potatoes are cool enough to handle. Should I cut each one into long wedges before scooping?
Yes. Quarter each baked potato lengthwise so you have sturdy boat-shaped pieces. Try to keep the skins intact while you scoop out the potato from the skins.
How much potato should I leave so the skins don't tear?
Leave a thin layer of potato attached to each skin for structure. Once the centers are scooped, brush or spoon the Ranch onto the inside of the skins using the 1/3 cup total.
I have the Ranch in the skins. What do I do with the scooped potato?
Place the scooped potato back into the coated skins, keeping each boat filled but not packed down too tightly.
They're filled again. Should the Cheddar go on before they return to the oven?
Yes. Sprinkle the 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese evenly over the potato boats, getting some cheese across each piece.
Do the green onions go on now or after heating?
They're optional, so use them however you like; for a fresher bite, add the sliced green onions after the cheese has warmed and softened.
What should I watch for in the oven since there isn't a bake time listed?
Use the 375 degrees F oven to warm the assembled boats and melt the Cheddar. Keep an eye on them and pull them out once the cheese is melted and the skins look hot and ready to serve.
I'm making Campfire Angel Food Yummies by the fire. Can you help me set up the ingredients and steps?

Absolutely. Have a 1 (10 inch) angel food cake cut into large cubes, a 1 (5 ounce) can of sweetened condensed milk, and 1 cup coconut flakes ready. You'll also want toasting sticks and small bowls or plates for dipping and rolling.
The cake is cubed, and I have the condensed milk and coconut out. Should the coals be flaming or more settled?
Use settled campfire coals rather than tall flames. The cubes should toast gently on the sticks so they brown instead of scorching.
How large should the cake cubes be for the sticks?
Keep them large enough to hold together when skewered, since angel food cake is airy. Slide each cube onto a toasting stick carefully so it doesn't tear apart.
I've got one on a stick over the coals. How do I know it's ready?
Turn it as it warms and watch for browned edges all around. Once the outside is toasted and lightly browned, pull it away from the heat.
The first cube is browned. Do I dip it while it's still warm?
Yes, dip the toasted cake into the sweetened condensed milk while it's warm enough to hold together but cool enough to handle safely.
It's coated with condensed milk. How much coconut should go on it?
Roll the dipped cake in the coconut flakes until the sticky surface is covered. The recipe uses 1 cup total, so coat each piece generously but leave enough for the rest of the cubes.
A few pieces are done. What's the best way to serve them around the fire?

Serve them right after rolling so the outside stays toasty and the coconut clings well. Keep repeating the same pattern: toast the angel food cake cubes over the coals until browned, dip in condensed milk, then roll in coconut flakes.
I'm making Blackened Tuna and have the tuna steaks on the counter. Can you talk me through it while I cook?
Absolutely. You'll need 1 1/2 pounds fresh tuna steaks, about 1 inch thick, plus 2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 2 tablespoons butter.
I've got the tuna, Cajun seasoning, oil, and butter. Should I season the fish before heating the pan?
Yes. Pat the tuna dry if it looks damp, then generously coat the steaks all over with the Cajun seasoning so the outside can blacken well.
The seasoning is on pretty heavily. What pan should I use for this?
Use a large skillet that can handle high heat. Set it over high heat, then add the 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter.
The butter is melting into the oil now. Am I waiting for bubbles or smoke?
Let the fat get very hot. You're looking for the oil to be nearly smoking before the tuna goes in.
It's right at that point, and I'm ready to add the steaks. Any spacing advice?
Place the tuna steaks in the pan carefully and give them room so they sear instead of steam. Once they're down, don't move them around.
They're sizzling hard. How long should I leave the first side alone?
Cook that side for 3 to 4 minutes, or until the surface is blackened.
The crust is dark and blackened after about 4 minutes. Should I keep cooking or pull them now?
For this recipe, stop once that side is blackened. Move the tuna out of the hot skillet promptly and serve it right away while the crust is crisp.
I'd like to make Cucumber Sandwiches. Can you guide me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put out 1 (8 ounce) package of cream cheese spread, 2 teaspoons ranch salad dressing mix, 12 slices of pumpernickel rye bread, and 2 medium cucumbers.
I have the bread and cucumbers on the counter. Should I mix the spread before slicing the cucumbers?
Yes, start with the spread so it's ready to go. In a bowl, combine the cream cheese spread with the ranch salad dressing mix until the seasoning is evenly blended in.
The mixture looks smooth with little ranch flecks. Do I need to toast the pumpernickel rye?
No toasting is needed for this recipe. Lay out all 12 slices of pumpernickel rye bread so you can spread them evenly.
How much of the cream cheese mixture should go on each slice?
Spread the mixture on one side of each slice of bread, using a thin, even layer so every sandwich has flavor without becoming too thick.
I'm ready for the cucumbers. Should I peel them?
Peel the 2 medium cucumbers if you'd like a softer texture, or leave the peel on if you want a little color and bite. Then slice them thinly.
The cucumber slices are thin. Which bread slices get them?
Place the cucumber slices on six of the bread slices, right over the cream cheese-ranch side. Try to cover the surface in an even layer.
All six are topped with cucumber. How do I close and serve them neatly?

Top each cucumber-covered slice with one of the remaining bread slices, cream-cheese side facing in. Press gently, then serve as whole sandwiches or cut them into smaller pieces if you want them easier to pick up.
I'm making Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers and want to get organized before the grill is hot. What should I pull out first?
Start with the cheese mixture ingredients: 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready.
The bowl is out, and I have the Cheddar, Parmesan, onion, and egg measured. Should I heat the grill yet?
Yes, preheat the grill for high heat while you mix the patties. That way it will be ready once the bacon is wrapped around them.
The grill is heating. What goes into the bowl with the cheese and onion?
Add the Cheddar cheese, Parmesan cheese, chopped onion, egg, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper to the large bowl, then stir everything together until the egg is blended through.
It's mixed, but it looks pretty loose from the egg and sauces. Is that okay before the beef goes in?
That's fine. Crumble in the ground beef next, then mix it together by hand just until the seasonings and cheese are distributed through the meat.
I've added the beef. Should I knead it a lot or keep it light?
Keep it fairly light. Use your hands to combine it evenly, but stop once the mixture holds together so the hamburgers don't get overly dense.
The mixture is combined. How many patties am I shaping from this?
Shape it into 6 patties. Try to make them even in thickness so they cook at about the same pace on the high-heat grill.
I have 6 patties on a tray. Where does the bacon come in?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty, securing it snugly around the edge before the burgers go onto the preheated grill.
I'm making Almond Apricot Bread and I've cleared space for a mixing bowl. Can you help me start with the dry ingredients?
Absolutely. Put a large bowl on the counter and measure in 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 3 teaspoons baking powder.
The flour, both sugars, and baking powder are in the bowl. The recipe mentions salt too—should I add it with these?
Yes, add the salt to that same large bowl, then stir the dry ingredients together until the flour, sugars, baking powder, and salt look evenly combined.
Dry bowl is mixed. I also see baby food listed in the directions—do I use all of it in the batter?
Not quite. Scoop out and reserve 1 tablespoon of the baby food for the glaze, then keep the remaining baby food nearby for the wet mixture.
I set aside the 1 tablespoon for glaze in a small cup. What bowl should I use for the wet ingredients?
Use a second bowl. In it, beat together the egg, milk, oil, extract, and the remaining baby food until the mixture looks smooth and blended.
The wet mixture is blended. Do I pour it into the dry bowl all at once or in parts?
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir gently. Stop as soon as everything is just moistened; a few small lumps are better than overmixing.
I'm seeing a little dry flour at the bottom, but most of the batter is damp. Should I keep stirring?
Give it just a few more folds from the bottom of the bowl, scraping through the flour pockets. Once no obvious dry streaks remain, stop mixing.
The batter is combined now, and I still have the glaze portion set aside. Is that the end of the mixing directions?

Yes. For this part of Almond Apricot Bread, you've combined the dry ingredients, reserved 1 tablespoon baby food for glaze, beaten the wet ingredients with the remaining baby food, and stirred the wet into the dry just until moistened.
I'm making Basil Burgers on the grill today. Can you help me get everything lined up before I touch the meat?

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil, or a bit more or less to taste, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt. You'll also need pepper, a mixing bowl, and a platter or tray for the patties.
I've got the bowl and seasonings out. Should I start the grill before mixing?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the outdoor grill to high heat so it's ready by the time the patties are shaped.
The grill is heating. Do I add everything to the beef at once?
Add the ground beef to the bowl with the Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper. Mix just until the seasonings are evenly worked through; try not to overwork the beef.
The mixture is combined and smells pretty basil-heavy. How many burgers should I shape?
Shape the mixture into 4 burger patties. Make them fairly even in thickness so they cook at the same pace on the grill.
The patties are formed. Do I need to do anything to the grate before they go on?
Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the burgers. That helps prevent sticking, especially with the grill set to high heat.
They're on the grill now. What timing should I use so I don't keep flipping them?

Cook them for about 6 minutes total, turning once. Let the first side sear before flipping, then cook the other side until they reach 160 degrees F, which is 70 degrees C, or to your desired doneness.
I'll check the temperature. Once they hit that, should I take them straight off?
Yes. When the burgers reach 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), take them off the grill and serve them while hot. If you like, let them sit briefly while you get the buns and toppings ready.
I want to make Fruited Ice Cream today. Can you help me get set up before I pour anything into the ice cream maker?

Absolutely. Have the freezer canister for your ice cream maker ready, and gather 2 (14 ounce) cans sweetened condensed milk, 5 cups milk, 2 cups heavy cream, and 2 tablespoons vanilla extract. You'll also need the fruit and salt called for when everything is mixed in the canister.
The canister is chilled and on the counter. Should I add the condensed milk first, or does the order matter?

Pour the sweetened condensed milk into the freezer canister first if that's easiest, then add the milk and heavy cream. The exact order isn't critical here; the goal is to get the condensed milk loosened into the dairy so the base freezes evenly.
I've added the condensed milk, milk, and cream. The mixture still looks a little streaky from the condensed milk.
Give it a gentle but thorough stir right in the canister until the base looks mostly uniform. Scrape along the bottom and sides so no thick condensed milk is sitting in one spot.
That looks smoother now. When should the vanilla and fruit go in?
Stir in the 2 tablespoons vanilla extract now, then add the salt and fruit. Fold the fruit through the base so it's distributed without splashing or overfilling the freezer canister.
The fruit is mixed in. How full is too full for the canister?
Stay within your ice cream maker's fill line, since the mixture will expand as it freezes. If you're close to the top, hold a little mixture back rather than forcing it all in.
It's under the fill line and the paddle is attached. What should I do for the freezing part?
Start the machine and freeze the Fruited Ice Cream according to the manufacturer's directions for your model. Let it churn until it reaches the texture your machine indicates is ready.
If it comes out soft, is that okay for serving?
Yes. Many ice cream makers produce a soft-serve texture at the end of churning. You can serve it right away, or transfer it to a freezer-safe container and firm it up in the freezer before scooping.
Can you guide me through making a Bahama Mama II? I'm setting out a mixing glass and some ice.
Absolutely. For one drink, measure 1 fluid ounce dark rum and pour it into the mixing glass.
The dark rum is in. I also have apricot brandy here—how much goes in?
Add 1/2 fluid ounce apricot brandy to the same mixing glass.
Done. I want to make sure the fruit punch doesn't overpower it. What's the exact amount?
Use 3 1/2 fluid ounces fruit punch. Pour it in with the rum and apricot brandy.
Fruit punch is measured and added. I've got pina colada mix left—how much of that?
Add 1/2 fluid ounce pina colada mix. At this point, all four ingredients should be together in the mixing glass.
They're all in the glass. Should I shake this, or just stir it?
Stir it to blend. You're not trying to whip it—just mix until the drink looks even and the pina colada mix is incorporated.
It looks uniform now. Do I pour it straight into the serving glass with ice?
Yes. Fill your serving glass with ice, then pour the blended Bahama Mama II over the ice.
It's over ice now. Anything else before I serve it?
That's it for the recipe: dark rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and pina colada mix stirred together and served over ice. Give it a quick check that it's chilled and mixed, then serve.
Can you help me make Easy Fried Eggplant? I've got a large skillet out and want to avoid missing anything.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons canola oil, 1 large eggplant peeled and sliced, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 cups dry bread crumbs.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced. Should I set up the eggs and crumbs near the stove?
Yes, that will make the coating easier. Keep the beaten eggs in one shallow dish and the dry bread crumbs in another, close enough to dip the slices before they go into the pan.
Oil is measured. How hot should the skillet be before I start coating?
Heat the canola oil in the large skillet over medium-high heat. Let it get hot before adding the coated eggplant so the crumbs start browning right away.
The oil looks hot now. What order do I coat the slices in?
Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg first, then press it into the bread crumbs so it's coated. Place the slices carefully into the hot oil as you finish them.
A few slices are in the pan. How long should I leave them before flipping?
Fry them for 2 to 3 minutes on that side, watching for a golden brown crust before you turn them.
They're golden on the bottom. Do I give the second side the same amount of time?
Yes. Flip them and fry the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes, or until both sides are golden brown.
They look crisp now. What should I do when I take them out of the skillet?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain off the extra oil. Once drained, they're ready to serve while still warm and crisp.
Can you help me make Date Nut Bars? I've got a large bowl out and want to make sure I start in the right order.
Absolutely. Set up your dry ingredients first: measure 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Those are measured. I also have dates and nuts on the counter—do they go in with the dry stuff?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the sugar, flour, baking powder, salt, dates, and nuts. Mix them so the dates and nuts are distributed through the flour mixture.
The dates are a little sticky, but they're coated now. Should I grease the pan before I deal with the wet ingredients?
That's a good time to do it. Grease a 15-in pan so it's ready, then come back to the bowl for the eggs, butter, and vanilla.
Pan is greased. I'm adding the eggs, butter, and vanilla—how much should I stir once they're in?
Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened. Don't worry if it feels tough to mix; the batter is supposed to be very stiff.
It's definitely stiff and not pourable. Is that okay for spreading?
Yes, that texture is expected. Transfer the stiff batter into the greased 15-in pan and spread it out as evenly as you can, pressing it into the corners.
It's in the pan, but the top looks a little rough. Do I need to smooth it perfectly?
It doesn't need to be perfect. Just level it enough that the bars bake evenly across the pan.
Ready for the oven. What temperature and how long should I bake them?
Bake the Date Nut Bars at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes, until they're golden brown. Let them cool before cutting so the bars hold together cleanly.
Can you guide me through making Cindis Egg Rolls? I've got my wok out and want to prep things in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 pound ground pork and the vegetables: 4 cups shredded cabbage, 1 large shredded carrot, and 1/2 green bell pepper sliced into thin strips.
The pork is thawed, and I've shredded the cabbage and carrot. Should I slice the pepper before heating the wok?
Yes, get the pepper cut into thin strips before you start cooking so everything is ready to mix later. Once the prep is done, heat your large wok over medium-high heat.
The wok is hot now. Do I add oil, or just put the ground pork in?
Add the ground pork to the hot wok and cook it over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it browns.
It's browned and there's some liquid in the bottom. What texture am I looking for before I move on?
The pork should be cooked through with no pink remaining. Drain off the excess liquid, then set the cooked pork aside.
Pork is drained and resting in a bowl. I have the cabbage, carrot, and pepper ready—what gets mixed with them?
In a large bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger.
Should the onion, garlic, and ginger be cooked first, or are they just mixed into the bowl raw at this point?
For this step, just mix them into the vegetable bowl as directed. Toss everything well so the aromatics are spread through the cabbage mixture.
The vegetable bowl smells great. I see cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses on the counter—how do I handle those?
Use a small bowl for that mixture: stir together the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until the sauce is smooth with no cornstarch lumps.
Can you help me make Gelatin Fruit Salad? I've got a saucepan out but want to make sure I start correctly.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup applesauce, 2 (3 ounce) packages cherry gelatin, 1 (12 ounce) can lemon-lime soda, and 1 (8 ounce) can crushed pineapple, undrained.
The pineapple can is open and I'm keeping the juice with it. Should the soda be cold before I add it?
Cold is fine, but the important part is to add it slowly later so the mixture doesn't foam over. For now, put the 1 cup applesauce in the saucepan.
Applesauce is in the pan. Do I just warm it, or does it need to fully boil?
Bring the applesauce to a boil. Stir as it heats so it doesn't scorch on the bottom.
It's bubbling now. Do I keep the burner on while adding the cherry gelatin?
Take the saucepan off the heat before adding the gelatin. Stir in both 3 ounce packages of cherry gelatin until the powder is completely dissolved.
The mixture looks smooth and I don't see granules. Is it okay to pour in the soda now?
Yes. Slowly pour in the 12 ounce can of lemon-lime soda, stirring gently as you add it.
It foamed a little but settled down. When should the pineapple go in?
Add the entire 8 ounce can of crushed pineapple now, including the liquid, and stir until it's evenly mixed through.
Everything is combined. Should I put it in one bowl or smaller dishes before chilling?
Either works. Pour it into your serving bowl or smaller dishes, then refrigerate until firm before serving.
Can you help me make Broccoli Cheese Crepes and keep me on track while I prep?
Absolutely. Start by setting out the batter ingredients: 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a blender ready.
I've got the blender out. Should the eggs and water go in before the flour?
Yes. Add the eggs and 1/4 cup water to the blender first, then add the 6 tablespoons flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. That helps the batter blend smoothly.
Everything is in the blender. How smooth should I make it?
Cover the blender and process the mixture until it looks completely smooth, with no dry flour streaks or lumps visible.
The batter looks smooth now. Do I use it right away?
Let it stand for 15 minutes before cooking the crepes. That short rest helps the batter settle.
While it rests, I want to start the filling base. What pan should I use?
Use a small saucepan. Add the onion and butter, then sauté until the onion is tender, stirring so it softens without browning too much.
The onion is soft and the butter is bubbling lightly. What texture am I looking for next?
Stir in the flour until it's blended into the buttery onion mixture. It should look evenly combined rather than dusty or clumpy.
So at this point I have rested crepe batter and the flour stirred into the onion-butter mixture, right?
Right. You've blended the eggs, water, flour, and salt for the batter, rested it for 15 minutes, sautéed the onion in butter until tender, and stirred in flour until blended.
Can you help me make Chicken Fried Chops 2? I've got pork chops out and a slow cooker ready.

Absolutely. Set out a shallow bowl for the coating, a skillet for browning, and your slow cooker. For the dry mix, you'll need 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons salt, 1 1/2 teaspoons ground mustard, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.
The flour and seasonings are measured. Should I mix them all together before touching the chops?
Yes. Stir the flour, salt, ground mustard, and garlic powder together in the shallow bowl until the seasoning looks evenly distributed.
The mixture is combined. Do the pork chops need to be fully coated or just dusted?
Dredge each pork chop through the flour mixture so both sides get coated. Shake off any loose excess before it goes into the skillet.
I've got the chops coated. What should I do with the skillet and oil?
Heat oil in the skillet, then brown the chops on both sides. You're just building color here, not trying to cook them all the way through.
They're browned on the outside. Some flour stuck to the pan, but the chops look good.
That's fine. Transfer the browned chops into the slow cooker, arranging them so they sit as evenly as possible.
They're in the slow cooker. The recipe mentions soup and water—do I mix those separately?
Yes, combine the soup and water in a bowl or measuring cup, then pour that mixture over the chops in the slow cooker.
The sauce is poured over them. Anything I should check before I put the lid on?
Make sure the chops are settled in the slow cooker and the soup-water mixture is spread over the top. Then cover it and continue with your slow-cooker cooking plan.
I'm making Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version tonight. Can you guide me through it without me getting ahead of myself?
Absolutely. Set out 6 center cut pork chops and trim off any visible fat. You'll also need 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt for the seasoning.
The chops are trimmed, and I found the garlic powder and seasoning salt. What should I pull out for the coating?
Get 1 egg, beaten with the egg substitute mixture, and put that in a small bowl when you're ready. Also have flour and bread crumbs nearby for dredging and coating.
Got it. Should I start heating the oven before I rinse the pork?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. That gives it time to come up to temperature while you prep the chops.
Oven is heating. I have the pork by the sink—do I rinse and season right away?
Rinse the pork chops, then pat them dry well so the coating sticks better. Season them with the garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste.
They're dry and seasoned. I'm setting up bowls now—where does the egg mixture go in the order?
Place the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture in a small bowl between the flour and the bread crumbs. The order will be flour, egg mixture, then bread crumbs.
I'm worried about making the coating too thick. How much flour should be on each chop?
Keep the flour layer light. Dredge each pork chop just enough to cover the surface, then shake off the extra before dipping it in the egg mixture.
Okay, the flour step makes sense. After the egg, do I press the crumbs on or just sprinkle them?
Dip each floured pork chop in the egg mixture, then coat it liberally with bread crumbs. Press gently so the crumbs adhere, and repeat with all 6 chops before baking.

source_seed.recipe_title: Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version

messages.content: Can you help me make E Z Cheezy Pie? I've got the counter cleared and want to be sure I'm starting with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells and 3 packages of cream cheese, 8 ounces each. The cream cheese should be softened so it whips up fluffy instead of staying lumpy.
The shells are already baked, and the cream cheese has been sitting out. What else should I measure before I plug in the mixer?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Keep them close to the bowl so you can add them once the cream cheese is whipped.
Should the oven be on even though the pie shells are baked already?
Yes, follow the recipe and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. While it heats, you can work on the filling.
I'm using a medium mixing bowl. Do I add everything at once or start with the cream cheese by itself?
Start with just the softened cream cheese. Whip it in the medium mixing bowl until it looks lighter and fluffy, scraping the sides if needed.
It's looking fluffy now, but I can still see a couple of thicker streaks near the edge of the bowl.
Give it another short mix and scrape those edges into the center. Once the texture is evenly fluffy, add the 1/2 cup sugar and the vanilla extract.
Sugar and vanilla are in. Should I switch speeds or keep mixing the same way?
Mix steadily until the filling is smooth. You're looking for no visible sugar pockets, no cream cheese lumps, and a creamy texture throughout.
The mixture is smooth now. Anything I should check before I move it toward the pie shells?
Check that both 9 inch shells are baked and ready, then use the smooth cream cheese mixture as your filling. The recipe's mixing work is complete once it is smooth.
Can you help me make Crab and Lobster Stuffed Mushrooms? I've got the mushrooms out and want to stay organized.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 pound fresh mushrooms with the stems removed, plus 3/4 cup melted butter total, divided between the baking sheet and the filling.
The mushroom caps are cleaned and the butter is melted. What should I set out for the stuffing?
Set out 1 cup crushed seasoned croutons and 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese. You'll also be mixing in crabmeat, lobster, and garlic for the filling.
Got it. Should the oven be heating before I start filling anything?
Yes, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's ready when the mushrooms are assembled.
Oven is heating. I'm using a large rimmed baking sheet—do I need parchment or just butter?
Use the melted butter from the recipe: brush the large baking sheet with about 1/4 cup of it to coat the surface well.
The sheet is buttered. How should I place the caps so they cook evenly?
Arrange the mushroom caps in a single layer across the baking sheet, cup-side up if you're planning to spoon the filling into them.
They're lined up. I have the croutons crushed pretty fine—what goes into the bowl now?
In a medium bowl, combine the crushed seasoned croutons with the remaining 1/2 cup melted butter, the shredded mozzarella, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic.
Should that mixture be smooth, or is it okay if it stays chunky from the seafood and croutons?
A chunky mixture is fine. Stir just until the butter moistens the croutons and the mozzarella, crabmeat, lobster, and garlic are evenly distributed, then it's ready to spoon into the mushroom caps.
Can you walk me through Easy Fried Eggplant? I've got a large skillet out and want to keep the coating from getting messy.

Absolutely. Set up your ingredients before heating the pan: 2 tablespoons canola oil, 1 large eggplant peeled and sliced, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 cups dry bread crumbs. A shallow bowl for the eggs and another for the crumbs will make dipping easier.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced, and I have the eggs beaten. Should I start heating the oil now?
Yes. Pour the 2 tablespoons canola oil into a large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat. Let it get hot before the coated eggplant goes in.
While the skillet heats, what order should I use for coating the slices?
Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg first, then press it into the dry bread crumbs so both sides are coated.
The first few slices are breaded. Do I put them straight into the oil or wait until I've coated all of them?
You can place coated slices into the hot oil as you go, as long as the skillet is ready. Keep them in a single layer so they fry instead of crowding.
They're in the pan now. How long should I cook the first side?
Fry the eggplant for 2 to 3 minutes on that side, watching for a golden brown crust.
The bottoms look golden. Should I flip them and use the same timing?
Yes, turn them over carefully and fry the second side for another 2 to 3 minutes, or until that side is golden brown too.
Both sides are browned and crisp. What should I do when I take them out of the skillet?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. Let the excess oil blot off briefly, then serve while the coating is still crisp.
Can you help me make Banana Bran Muffins? I've got the muffin pan out but haven't started anything yet.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you prep the batter.
Oven is heating. Should I grease the pan or use liners?
Either works here: grease the muffin pan well or line the cups with paper muffin liners. Liners make cleanup easier.
I'll use liners. What should I pull out for the batter?
You'll need 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar to start the base.
The butter is soft and the sugar is measured. Do I mix those together first?
Yes. Put them in a large mixing bowl and cream the butter and brown sugar together until the mixture looks fluffy.
It's lighter and fluffy now. I have bananas on the counter—how much goes in?
Mash 3 bananas, then add them to the bowl with 1/4 cup milk.
Bananas and milk are in. The recipe also mentions vanilla and eggs—do they go in now too?
Yes, add the vanilla and eggs at this point as well, then mix everything well until the batter comes together evenly.
The batter looks mixed. Anything I should check before filling the muffin cups?
Just make sure the oven has reached 375 degrees F and the lined pan is ready. Give the batter one last scrape from the bottom of the bowl, then portion it into the muffin cups.
Can you help me make Chicken and Herbs in White Wine? I've got the chicken out but want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil and 1 chicken, about 4 pounds, cut into pieces. You'll also want a large Dutch oven ready on the stove.
The Dutch oven is out. What else should I prep before I turn on the heat?
Have garlic powder nearby for seasoning the chicken, and slice 1/2 pound of fresh mushrooms so they're ready when the pan work starts.
Mushrooms are sliced. Should the oil go in before the pot is hot?
Yes, add the olive oil to the large Dutch oven, then warm it over medium heat.
The oil is heating. How should I season the chicken pieces?
Sprinkle the chicken pieces with garlic powder to taste, coating the surfaces lightly before they go into the pot.
Do I crowd all the pieces in, or should I watch the browning?
Brown the chicken on both sides in the hot oil. Give the pieces enough contact with the pot so they take on color rather than just steam.
The pieces are browned and there's some fat in the bottom. Where do I put the chicken?
Lift the browned chicken out of the Dutch oven and set it on paper towels.
Chicken is resting on paper towels. What do I do with the fat left in the pan?
Spoon off the chicken fat, then return the pan to the stove so it's ready for the next stage.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken and Herbs in White Wine

Add the lemon juice just a small splash at a time, stirring after each addition, until the dressing falls off the spoon in that narrow ribbon. Stop before it turns runny.

Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and stir gently to blend, scraping around the bowl so the chicken, celery, red onion, and diced red bell pepper are evenly coated.

Taste the salad, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Give it one final gentle stir, check that the texture is still light and ribbon-creamy, and serve it from the bowl when it looks balanced.

Yes, that sounds right for Almond Apricot Bread. Stop stirring once it's just moistened so the bread stays tender.

Absolutely. Set out 1 (3 pound) whole chicken cut into 8 pieces, plus 1/2 cup soy sauce. Those will go straight into the Dutch oven with the aromatics.

Bring it to a boil over medium heat. Once you see the liquid actively bubbling, you're ready to lower the heat.

Reduce the heat to a simmer. You want gentler bubbling, not a hard boil, so the chicken can cook through without the sauce reducing too aggressively.

Cover the pot and simmer for 30 minutes, basting the chicken occasionally with the sauce as it cooks. Check that the pieces stay nestled in the liquid and spoon sauce over the tops now and then.

Put the medium saucepan over medium heat and add the 2 tablespoons olive oil. Let it warm briefly so the mushrooms sizzle gently when they go in, but don't let the oil smoke.
The oil looks warm. Do I add everything to the pan together or start with the mushrooms?
Stir in the 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms along with the 2 chopped green onions, the 1 crushed garlic clove, and the cayenne pepper. Keep everything moving so the garlic doesn't catch on the bottom.
It's all in the pan and smells good. How long should I cook this mixture?
Cook it for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms and onions are tender.
After a few minutes there's liquid coming out of the mushrooms. Is that okay?
That's normal. Keep the pan at medium heat and continue cooking; the mushrooms will soften as that moisture cooks down.
The mushrooms look tender now and the mixture has reduced. Am I done with the stovetop part?
Yes. Once it has cooked about 10 minutes total and the vegetables are tender, you're done with this mushroom filling step for the Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs.
I'm making English Walnut Pie and want to get the filling started without missing anything. Can you guide me?
Absolutely. Set out 3 eggs, 1/4 teaspoon salt, 3/4 cup white sugar, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract. You'll also need the syrup and butter or margarine for the filling.
The eggs, salt, sugar, and vanilla are on the counter. Should I heat the oven before mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C) so it's ready when the filling is assembled.
Oven is heating. What bowl should I use for the eggs?
Use a large bowl, since everything gets combined there. Crack in the 3 eggs and beat them until they're blended.
The eggs are beaten and look evenly mixed. Do I add the dry ingredients together?
Add the 3/4 cup white sugar and 1/4 teaspoon salt to the beaten eggs, then stir in the 2 teaspoons vanilla extract and the syrup.
I've mixed in the sugar, salt, vanilla, and syrup. It's smooth but a little thick.
That's fine for this stage. Melt the butter or margarine separately so it can blend into the egg mixture more easily.
The butter is melted. Should I pour it in all at once?
Add the melted butter or margarine to the egg mixture and stir until it's fully incorporated.
Everything is combined in the bowl. Is that the filling base for the pie?
Yes. You've completed the listed filling steps: oven at 400 degrees F (205 degrees C), eggs beaten, sugar, salt, vanilla, and syrup mixed in, and melted butter or margarine added.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Put the topping on right away, then loosely cover the ramekins during the first half of baking so the crumbs don't over-brown before the salmon cooks through.

original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Baked Salmon with Herbs as individual ramekins with crumbs, streusel, or a crisp topping. When should I add the topping?

messages.content: I'm doing Baked Salmon with Herbs in little ramekins today, with a crumb-style crisp topping instead of one big pan. At what point should the topping go on?
Put the topping on right away, then loosely cover the ramekins during the first half of baking so the crumbs don't over-brown before the salmon cooks through.
Great, I'll set up the ramekins. Which crumb ingredients should I measure first?
Measure out 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs and mince 4 garlic cloves. Keep them in a mixing bowl with enough room to toss everything evenly.
The crumbs and garlic are in the bowl. What should I add for the herby part?
Add 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes, then include the thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper called for in the herb mixture.
Before I fill the ramekins, do I still need to prep the foil-lined pan?
Yes. Line a 15-in baking pan with foil and coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray; it will catch drips and make cleanup easier under the ramekins.
Pan is lined and sprayed. How do I make the topping come together instead of staying dry?
Add the butter to the crumb mixture and toss until the crumbs are evenly coated. You're looking for a moist, loose topping rather than a paste.
Should the salmon go straight into the ramekins now, or onto the pan first?
Set the salmon into the prepared ramekins, then place the ramekins on the prepared foil-lined pan so they're stable and easy to move.
I've got the salmon portioned. How thick should I make the crumb layer?
Scatter the coated crumb mixture over the salmon in an even layer. Don't pack it down; leaving it loose helps it bake up crisp.
They're topped and loosely covered. Anything else before they go in?
Make sure the ramekins are spaced a little apart on the pan, then bake with the loose cover for the first half as planned; uncover after that so the topping can crisp.
I want to make Cawl Traditional Welsh Broth and I've got a large pot ready. Can you talk me through the start?
Absolutely. Set out 2 quarts water and 12 ounces beef shank, since those are the first things you'll use.
The beef shank is thawed. Should I prep the vegetables now too?
Yes, go ahead and have 2 large onions chopped and 2 large carrots sliced so they're ready when you need them.
Vegetables are prepped. Does the water go in cold, or should I heat it first?
Pour the 2 quarts water into the large pot and bring it to a boil before adding the beef.
The water is boiling steadily. Do I drop the beef shank in whole?
Yes, place the beef shank into the boiling water, then reduce the heat so it simmers gently.
How long should I keep it simmering, and what should it look like?
Let it simmer for 1 1/2 hours. Aim for a steady, quiet simmer rather than a hard boil, so the broth cooks evenly.
The 1 1/2 hours are up. Should I cut the meat now while it's hot?
Not yet. Let the broth and meat cool overnight before you handle and trim the beef.
It cooled overnight and there's some gristle on the shank. What's the next move?
Lift the meat out, trim off the gristle, and cut the meat into medium sized pieces. Set those pieces aside for the next stage of the cawl.

messages.content: For Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style, I'm serving it in little dipping bowls with a creamy sauce—something like a dip, dressing, pasta sauce, or peanut sauce. What texture should I aim for today?
Make the sauce a touch thick so it sits well in the bowls, then lightly streak the surface with a little oil or water.
Great, I'm using that serving style. I've got the squash on the board—what prep should happen before the oven is involved?
Halve 1 spaghetti squash lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. While you're at the cutting board, chop 1 onion too.
The squash is seeded and the onion is chopped. What pantry items should I pull out?
Set out 2 tablespoons minced garlic and 2 cans of stewed tomatoes, 14 ounces each.
Those are on the counter. What oven temperature am I using?
Heat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
I'm waiting for it to heat. What should I do with the baking sheet?
Coat the baking sheet with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash has a prepared surface.
Sheet is sprayed. Which way should the squash halves face?
Put the squash halves cut side down on the baking sheet.
They're on the tray. How long should they bake?
Bake them for 35 minutes in the preheated oven.
What tells me they're done if my squash needs a little more or less time?
Check with a knife: the squash is ready when the blade slides in easily.
I'm making British Bread Pudding and have a big mixing bowl ready. Can you talk me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put out 6 1/4 cups cubed whole wheat bread and 1 1/4 cups milk to start, since those need to soak together.
The bread cubes and milk are on the counter. What else should I have nearby before I turn on the oven?
You'll also need 1 egg, beaten, and 1/3 cup butter, softened. The later mix-ins are raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Got it. I've beaten the egg and the butter is soft. What temperature should the oven be?
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
The oven is heating. Should I combine the bread and milk right away or wait?
Go ahead and combine the cubed whole wheat bread with the milk in the large bowl, then let it sit and soak for 5 minutes.
It's soaking now. What texture am I looking for before adding the other ingredients?
The bread should look moistened and softened rather than dry in the centers. Once the 5 minutes are up, give it a gentle stir so the milk is evenly absorbed.
The bread has softened. Do the egg and butter go in together?
Yes. Stir in the beaten egg and softened butter, then add the raisins, mixed fruit, brown sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Everything is in the bowl now, but I don't want to overwork it. How should I finish the mixture?
Mix it well enough that the egg, butter, fruit, sugar, and spices are evenly distributed through the soaked bread. Once it looks cohesive, you're ready for the next baking step.
I want to make Fresh Apple Salsa. Can you help me set up so I don't miss anything?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter, and start with 2 tart apples, cored and cubed, plus 4 tablespoons lime juice. The lime juice should go in early so the apples stay bright.
The apples are cubed, and I have the lime juice measured. What peppers do I need ready?
You'll need 1 fresh jalapeno pepper, seeded and sliced, and 1 fresh Anaheim chile, also seeded and sliced. Keep the slices ready to stir in after the apples are coated.
Should I put the apples straight into the bowl before slicing the chiles?
Yes. Add the cubed apples to the large bowl and stir them with the lime juice until the pieces are evenly coated.
The apples look glossy from the lime juice. Do the jalapeno and Anaheim go in together?
They do. Stir in the sliced jalapeno and sliced Anaheim chile, making sure the pepper pieces are spread through the apples rather than clumped in one spot.
The pepper slices are mixed in. I see the instructions mention more add-ins—what should I add next?
Stir in the onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt. Add them across the surface of the bowl so they're easier to distribute evenly.
Everything is in the bowl now. How much mixing are we looking for?
Mix thoroughly, folding from the bottom of the bowl to the top until the apples, chiles, onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt are evenly combined.
Is it ready to serve once it's evenly mixed, or should I adjust the texture somehow?
Once it's thoroughly mixed, it's ready. It should look chunky and fresh, with the lime juice coating the apples and the chiles and other add-ins evenly scattered throughout.
I'm making California Chicken with 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts. Can you talk me through it from setup to serving?

Absolutely. Set out the chicken, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt. You'll also want a skillet ready, and go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
The oven is heating, and I have a skillet on the stove. Should the chicken go in whole?
Yes, keep the breasts whole unless you need them to fit the pan. Warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the skillet over moderate heat so it coats the bottom lightly.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do I season before or after the chicken hits the pan?
Add the chicken to the skillet now, then sprinkle in the onion powder with it so the flavor starts cooking onto the surface.
All 4 pieces are in, but the pan is pretty full. What texture am I looking for before I move on?
Let them cook without crowding them more than necessary, turning as needed, until the outside is browned and the chicken is just about done. The recipe gives about 15 minutes for this stage.
They're browning, but a little moisture is collecting in the skillet. Is that okay?
That's fine. Keep the heat steady and let the moisture cook down while the chicken continues to brown. If the pieces are touching, shift them slightly so more surface gets contact with the skillet.
After 15 minutes, the outside looks browned. Should I add the salt now?
Yes. Add the 1 pinch salt, then season with pepper to taste if you're using it. Turn the chicken once or twice so the seasoning distributes evenly.
What's the best way to serve it once it's seasoned?
Let the chicken rest briefly after cooking so the juices settle, then serve the browned California Chicken warm. Spoon any seasoned pan juices over the top if there are some left in the skillet.
I'm making Aunt Mamies and have the bowl and mixer out. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start?
Yes. Set out 1 (8 ounce) package of softened cream cheese and 1/2 cup softened butter so they're easy to beat together.
Those are soft enough to press with a spoon. What dry ingredients should I pull out?
You'll need 2 cups all-purpose flour and 1 cup white sugar. Keep the sugar aside for the saucepan step later.
The flour is measured, and the sugar is waiting by the stove. Do I use the mixer bowl first?
Use the mixer bowl for the cream cheese and butter. Beat them together until the mixture looks smooth and well blended.
It's creamy now, with no big streaks of butter. Should the flour go in all at once?
Add the flour and mix well. If your mixer struggles, pause and scrape the bowl so the flour gets fully worked in.
The dough is coming together and looks thick. What texture am I aiming for before chilling?
It should be cohesive enough to shape into a ball. Once it holds together, form it into a ball, cover it, and chill it for 2 hours.
I've covered the dough and put it in the fridge. While it chills, what pan should I use for the sugar part?
Use a saucepan over medium heat. Add the white sugar with the milk, then cook it while stirring occasionally.
How will I know when the saucepan mixture is ready?
Keep it over medium heat until the milk boils and the sugar is dissolved. Once that happens, you've completed the listed cooking step for Aunt Mamies.
