Work one piece at a time: coat the chicken in the flour first, then dip it into the eggs and water, then press it into the bread crumbs so the surface is covered.

Set each coated piece aside in a single layer as you go. Once all the chicken has gone through flour, eggs and water, and bread crumbs, you're ready for the next cooking step.
Can you help me make Easy Fried Eggplant? I've got a large eggplant on the counter and want to do it right.

Great setup. Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg, coat it with the dry bread crumbs, then place it carefully into the hot oil.
How crowded can the pan be? I don't want the crumbs to fall off.
Keep the slices in a single layer with a little room between them so they fry instead of steam. Handle them gently after breading and place them straight into the oil.
They're sizzling now. How long do I leave the first side?
Fry the eggplant for 2 to 3 minutes on that side, until it turns golden brown.
The first side is golden. Should I flip each piece and repeat the same timing?
Yes, turn the slices carefully and fry the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes, again looking for a golden brown crust.
Both sides look browned. What's the best way to get them out without making them greasy?
Transfer the fried eggplant to paper towels to drain. Let the pieces sit briefly so the excess oil comes off before serving.

Start with 2 cups white sugar. Pour it in carefully and tap the jar lightly on the counter so the layer settles evenly.
Sugar is leveled off. I have cocoa powder, flour, and pecans left.
Add 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder next. If the mouth of the jar is narrow, a funnel or folded sheet of parchment will help keep the sides cleaner.
The cocoa layer is in, though there's a little dust on the inside glass. Is that okay?

Flour is in. Should the pecans be pressed down or just sprinkled on top?

Attach a tag that includes the baking instruction provided with the mix: "Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C)."
Do I need to write any other baking steps on the tag?

The butter is soft, and both sugars are measured. Should the oil go in with them right away?

It's coming together, but it still looks a little glossy from the oil. Is that okay?

Okay, the mixture looks even now. I have eggs and vanilla nearby—do they go in next?
Yes. Add the eggs and vanilla to the bowl, then mix well so they're fully incorporated into the creamed mixture.
The wet mixture is smooth. I'm ready for the dry ingredients, but I don't want to overmix.
Add the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar. Mix just until the dry ingredients are combined with the wet mixture.
There are a few streaks of flour left on the sides of the bowl. Should I scrape it down?
Yes, scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl, then give it a short mix so the flour streaks disappear without working the dough too much.
The dough looks combined now. I also have pecans, but I'm not sure if I should use them.
The pecans are optional. If you want them in the cookies, stir them in gently now; if not, you can leave the dough as it is.
Can you talk me through making California Chicken? I've got the chicken out but haven't started heating anything yet.
Absolutely. You'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1 pinch salt. Keep pepper nearby too, since it gets added to taste at the end.
I have the breasts, olive oil, onion powder, salt, and pepper on the counter. Should I turn on the oven before the skillet?
Yes—preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it's ready while you work on the stovetop.
Oven is preheating. What kind of pan setup should I use for the chicken?
Use a skillet over the stovetop and warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in it. Once the oil looks loose and glossy, add the chicken breasts and the onion powder.
The oil is warm, and I've put the chicken in with the onion powder. Should the heat be high to brown it fast?
Keep it controlled rather than blasting it—enough heat to brown the chicken steadily without scorching the onion powder or the outside of the chicken.
It's sizzling gently. How long should I leave it in the skillet?
Cook it for about 15 minutes, turning as needed, until the chicken is browned and just about done.
After 15 minutes, the outside is browned and the chicken looks nearly cooked through. Do I season now?
Yes. Add the pinch of salt, then add pepper to taste. Season both sides lightly so it doesn't all sit in one spot.
That's done. Since the oven was preheated, do I need to move the chicken there now?

The recipe has you preheat the oven, but the listed cooking direction is the skillet step until the chicken is browned and just about done, followed by salt and pepper. If your pieces are thick, use the hot oven only to gently finish them until fully cooked through before serving.

Rinse the turkey, then pat it thoroughly dry with paper towels. Take your time here; surface moisture and hot oil are a bad combination.

Yes. With the turkey rinsed and completely patted dry, you're ready to use the 1/4 cup Creole seasoning and the white onion as the recipe's next prep items before frying.

messages.content: Can you walk me through making Fudge Drops? I'm getting my saucepan and baking sheets ready.
Absolutely. Set out a heavy saucepan, a spoon for constant stirring, and baking sheets lined with waxed paper for later.
What should I measure before I turn on the stove?
Measure 1 2/3 cups sugar, 1 (5 ounce) can evaporated milk, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've got the sugar, milk, butter, and salt measured. Do they all go in together?
Yes. Put the sugar, evaporated milk, butter or margarine, and salt into the heavy saucepan.
They're in the pan. Should I start high to get it boiling faster?
Use medium heat instead, and stir constantly so the mixture heats evenly and doesn't scorch.
It's heating and I'm stirring. What am I waiting for?
Keep stirring until the mixture comes to a boil over that medium heat.
It has reached a boil. Do I keep it on the burner?
Remove the saucepan from the heat, then stir in the remaining ingredients.
The mixture is off the heat and stirred. How do I portion the drops neatly?
Drop the mixture by tablespoonfuls onto the waxed paper-lined baking sheets, spacing them a little so the Fudge Drops can set cleanly.
Can you walk me through making Asian Turkey Burgers? I've got a bowl and skillet out.
Absolutely. Set out 1 egg white, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs, and 1 tablespoon finely chopped onion. You'll also need the turkey, a nonstick skillet, and nonstick cooking spray.
I have the egg white and soy sauce measured. Should the bread crumbs and onion go in with those right away?
Yes. Add the dry bread crumbs and finely chopped onion to the bowl with the egg white and soy sauce, then stir those ingredients together so the binder is evenly mixed.
The mixture looks damp and crumbly. Is that the texture I want before adding the turkey?
That's right. It should look like a seasoned crumb mixture. Crumble the turkey over it rather than dropping it in as one solid piece.
Turkey is in the bowl. How much should I mix it so the burgers don't get tough?
Mix just until combined. Use a light hand and stop once the crumb mixture is spread through the turkey and you don't see big unmixed pockets.
It's combined. Should I make the patties thick or flatter for the skillet?
Shape the mixture into four patties. Keep them fairly even in thickness so they cook at the same rate in the skillet.
I've shaped four patties and sprayed the nonstick skillet. What heat should I use?
Use a steady medium heat unless your skillet runs very hot. Place the patties in the coated nonstick skillet with a little space between them.
They're cooking now. What should I look for before taking them out?
Cook them until the turkey is no longer pink in the center. Once they're cooked through, move the patties off the skillet and let them sit briefly before serving.
Can you help me make Cookie Paints for some cutout cookies I'm about to bake?
Absolutely. You only need 2 tablespoons evaporated milk and 4 drops red food coloring for this paint, plus a small bowl and a clean paintbrush.
I've got the milk, food coloring, a little bowl, and a new brush. Should the cookies already be baked?
No, paint them before baking. Mix the paint first, brush it onto the unbaked cookies, then bake the cookies as your cookie recipe directs.
Okay, I'm measuring the evaporated milk now. Does it need to be cold or room temperature?
Either is fine for this simple mixture. Pour the 2 tablespoons evaporated milk into the small bowl.
The milk is in the bowl. I'm worried about making the color too strong.
Use the recipe amount: add 4 drops red food coloring to the evaporated milk, then stir until the color looks even throughout.
It's mixed and looks pale red. Should it be thick like icing?
It will be thin, more like a paint wash than icing. That's normal because it's meant to brush lightly onto the cookie surface.
When I paint, should I soak the brush or keep it light?
Keep it light. Dip the paintbrush, wipe off any heavy drip on the bowl edge, and paint a thin coat onto the unbaked cookies.
Some of the edges are getting a little wet. Is that okay before they go in the oven?
A light damp sheen is okay, but avoid puddles. If you see extra liquid, dab the brush on the bowl edge and spread the paint thinner before baking.
I want to make Apple Butter V today. Can you help me get organized before I start slicing?
Absolutely. You'll need 6 pounds of tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups of apple cider. Have a Dutch oven ready since the apples and cider cook together in it.
The apples are cored and sliced, and I've got the cider measured. Are there any other ingredients before I turn on the stove?
Yes—measure out 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon. Keep them nearby for the apple butter, even though the first cooking step is just apples and cider.
My Dutch oven is on the counter. Should the apple slices go in loose, or do I need to mash them first?
Put the sliced apples into the Dutch oven loose; no mashing yet. They'll soften during cooking, which makes them easier to press later.
The pot is pretty full with the apples. Do I pour all the cider in at once?
Yes, pour in all 6 cups of apple cider over the apples. Once it's in, set the pot over heat and bring the mixture to a boil.
It's heating now. After it boils, how should I manage the heat and timing?
When it reaches a boil, keep it cooking on medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft. Stir occasionally so the apples cook evenly in the cider.
I'm at about 30 minutes, and the slices are breaking down when I press them with a spoon. Is that soft enough?
That sounds right. If the apples are soft and collapsing easily, you can take the pot off the heat and get ready to run the softened mixture through a food mill.
I have the food mill set over a bowl. Do I add the sugar and cinnamon before milling?
For this stage, press the softened apple-and-cider mixture through the food mill first. Once it's milled, you'll have a smooth base ready for the 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon.
Can you help me make Feta Chicken Salad for lunch? I've got cooked chicken ready but want to keep the prep organized.
Absolutely. Dice 3 cups of cooked chicken if it isn't diced already, then dice 2 large stalks of celery. Put both near your serving bowl so assembly is easy.
The chicken is diced, and I'm chopping the celery now. Should the red pepper go in with those too?
Yes, seed and dice 1 red bell pepper. Also dice 1/2 red onion, but keep the onion separate for a moment so you can add it evenly with the chicken and celery.
The pepper is diced, and the onion is ready. What size bowl should I use for mixing?
Use a serving bowl large enough to toss everything without spilling. Add the chicken, celery, and red onion to it, then mix them together so the onion is spread through the chicken.
I mixed those in the serving bowl. Do I add the bell pepper at this point?
You can fold in the diced red bell pepper now so it's distributed before the dressing goes on.
That looks colorful. I have a smaller bowl out for the dressing—what goes in there?
In the separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the mixture looks creamy and the feta is spread throughout.
The dressing is mixed, though the feta is still a little chunky. Is that okay?
That's fine; small feta pieces are good in this salad. Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and stir gently until everything is coated.
Everything is coated now. Before I serve it, how should I adjust the flavor?
Taste a bite, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Once it tastes balanced, it's ready to serve as Feta Chicken Salad.

I want to make Eileens Spicy Gingerbread Men. Can you help me set up the bowl and ingredients before I start mixing?

Add the dry mixture into the molasses mixture and blend until smooth. If it feels easier to control, add it in portions, but the goal is one smooth dough with no dry pockets.

Cover the dough and chill it for at least one hour. That rest will firm it up so it's easier to roll and shape into gingerbread men.

Perfect, that's the special version I want just for tonight. I've got a saucepan out—what should I prep before the heat goes on?
Measure 2 teaspoons olive oil and finely chop 3 tablespoons onion. Keep both close to the stove so the onion can go in as soon as the oil is warm.

Drain and rinse 1 (15.5 ounce) can black beans, and drain 1 (10 ounce) can whole kernel corn. Set the beans and corn together since they go in at the same time.

Stir in the black beans and corn, then add the sugar, salsa, and pepper flakes. Mix well so the salsa coats everything evenly.

Crush half the cookies, about 20, into crumbs. A zip-top bag and rolling pin works well, or you can pulse them briefly in a food processor.
The crumbs are mostly fine with a few small chunks. Is that okay for the base?
Yes, that texture is fine. Stir the cookie crumbs with the 1/4 cup melted margarine until they're evenly moistened.
The crumb mixture is ready. How firmly should I pack it into the pan?
Press it evenly across the bottom of the 9-inch springform pan. Use the bottom of a measuring cup or glass to compact it so the crust holds together.
Crust is pressed in. I still have the rest of the cookies—where do they go?
Stand the remaining cookies upright around the edge of the pan, with the flat sides against the side if that helps them stay in place.

Yes. Spread 3/4 cup of the hot fudge topping over the crust inside the cookie border, keeping it fairly even. Leave the remaining fudge from the 1 cup amount for later use if you'd like, and keep the 2 quarts vanilla ice cream cold until you're ready to add it.

Stop once you don't see dry cocoa streaks or big ice cream pockets. The texture should look creamy and pourable.

Take out the large chilled glass and pour the Cold Cocoa Smoothie into it right away. Serve it cold while the texture is thick and creamy.

Good, keeping the chili off to one side like that is how this dressing works best for me. Should I add the soy sauce, honey, and water before shaking?
Yes, add the soy sauce, honey, and water now with the garlic, ginger, olive oil, and rice vinegar. Leave the chili option out for the moment so the base stays even.
Everything is in the jar, but the honey is sitting at the bottom. Do I shake it cold first?
Put on a tight-fitting lid and shake the jar well. That starts the emulsion and helps loosen the honey before warming.
It's shaken, though I can still see a little honey on the glass. What's the microwave part?
Take the lid off, then microwave the jar for 1 minute, just long enough to dissolve the honey. Don't microwave it with the lid on.
The honey dissolved and the jar is warm. Should I put the lid back on right away?
Let it cool first. Once it's no longer hot, put the lid back on and shake well again before serving.
I'm serving it with greens. When do I make the chili streak so it doesn't take over?

After the final shake, pour or spoon the dressing over the greens, then add your chili choice as a partial streak across one area. That keeps most bites garlicky-gingery and balanced, with a spicy section for the heat.
Can you talk me through making Avocado Tzatziki? I've got a bowl and fork out, but I want to make sure I prep the ingredients in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting 1 large avocado peeled and pitted, and mince 2 cloves garlic so they're ready to go into the bowl.
The avocado is soft and the garlic is minced. Should I juice the lemon before I add anything to the bowl?
Yes, juice 1 lemon now. If you're using the sour cream, measure out 1/4 cup as well; it's optional, but it will make the tzatziki creamier.
I'm using the sour cream. Do I add everything at once, or mash the avocado first?
Add the avocado, minced garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber to a medium bowl together, then you'll mash them into a smooth mixture.
The cucumber is in the bowl too. Should it be fully blended in, or is a little texture okay?
A little texture from the cucumber is fine, but mash the avocado with a fork until the base is smooth and the garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber are evenly combined.
It's mostly smooth now, with tiny cucumber pieces. What seasonings go in?
Season it with red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper, then mix well so the herbs and spices are spread through the whole bowl.
I added those. Should I taste it now or wait until after it chills?
You can taste it now for salt and pepper, then cover the bowl. The main finishing step is to refrigerate it for 1 hour before serving so the flavors settle.
I've covered it and put it in the fridge. Any serving tip when the hour is up?
After 1 hour, give it a quick stir and serve it chilled. If it looks a bit thick, just stir it well before putting it out.
Can you help me make apple butter spice cake? I'm pulling out the pan and spices now.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and spray or grease one 9x13 inch pan so it's ready before the batter comes together.
Pan is greased. For the topping, which ingredients should I measure out?
Measure 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/2 cup chopped pecans.
I've got the brown sugar packed and the pecans chopped. Do I mix the topping by hand?
Yes, just stir the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped pecans together in a small bowl until the spices are evenly distributed through the sugar and nuts.
The topping smells good. What dry ingredients should I prep for the cake batter?
Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl. That keeps the leaveners spread evenly through the batter.
Dry bowl is sifted. I'm ready to start the wet mixture—what order should I use?
Blend the butter and sugar together until combined, then add the eggs and beat well so the mixture looks smooth and a little lighter.
Eggs are beaten in. Where does the apple butter go?
Mix in the apple butter next, along with the vanilla and the wheat germ or bran cereal. Stir until everything is well blended.
That's mixed. How do I add the flour mixture without making it too heavy?

Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream, mixing well after each addition. Keep scraping the bowl as needed so the batter stays even, then spread it in the prepared pan and add the spiced pecan topping.
I want to make Brandy Flamed Peppercorn Steak tonight. Can you talk me through getting it started?

Absolutely. Set out 3 tablespoons crushed black peppercorns, 2 beef top sirloin steaks that are 8 ounces each, 1 tablespoon lemon pepper, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a large skillet ready for the stovetop.
The steaks are on a board and the peppercorns are crushed. Should I season before the skillet heats?
Yes. Press the crushed black peppercorns firmly into both sides of each steak so they adhere well instead of just sitting loose on the surface.
Some pepper is falling off when I lift the steaks. Is that okay?
A little is fine. Pat the steaks dry if they feel damp, then press again with the heel of your hand so the peppercorns form an even crust on both sides.
Okay, the crust looks even. Where do the lemon pepper and salt come in?
Sprinkle the steaks with the 1 tablespoon lemon pepper and 1 teaspoon salt, coating both steaks evenly without burying the peppercorn crust.
Seasoning is on. What should I do with the pan?
Put the large skillet over medium-high heat and melt the butter in it. Let the butter coat the bottom of the skillet so the steaks have an even hot surface.
The butter has melted and is moving around the pan. Do I add anything before the steaks?
Stir in the garlic and wine, then let them cook together for 1 minute. Keep the heat at medium-high and stir so the garlic flavors the wine without sitting in one spot.
It has been about 1 minute and it smells garlicky. What should I watch for before continuing?

You're looking for the wine and garlic to be hot and fragrant, with the butter still coating the skillet. At that point, your peppercorn-crusted, lemon-pepper-and-salt seasoned steaks are ready for the next cooking action.

Some thinner slices are browning faster than the thick ones. Should I pull them early?
Yes, take off any slices that are already golden brown and let the thicker ones continue until their coating matches.
They're all cooked now. Do I need to leave them sitting on the trays?
No final rest for this batch. Move them onto paper towels to drain, then serve while the coating is still crisp.
Can you walk me through making Cookie Bowl? I want to get the ingredients and pan setup right before I start.

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds. For the shape, you'll also need either a 9x5 inch loaf pan or a metal bowl, plus foil and a cookie sheet.
I've got the flour, cocoa, salt, and almonds measured. Should I heat the oven before dealing with the foil?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the mold is prepared.
The oven is heating. I'm using the loaf pan—do I put the foil inside it or on the outside?
Turn the 9x5 inch loaf pan upside down and cover the outside with foil. Smooth it over the inverted pan so the dough can bake around the exterior shape.
Foil is wrapped around the outside. Does the pan go straight on the oven rack?
Place the foil-covered upside-down pan onto a cookie sheet. That gives it a stable base and makes it easier to move in and out of the oven.
The cookie sheet is ready. What should I do with the dry ingredients now?
Stir together the all-purpose flour, unsweetened cocoa powder, salt, and sliced almonds in a bowl until the cocoa and salt are evenly distributed through the flour.
The cocoa is blending in, but the almonds keep sitting on top. Is that okay?
That's fine—just keep folding and stirring until the 1/4 cup sliced almonds looks scattered throughout the mixture rather than gathered in one spot.
All mixed. Should I use this right away or leave it while I clean up the measuring cups?
Set the flour, cocoa, salt, and almond mixture aside for now. You can clear the measuring cups and keep the prepared foil-covered pan on the cookie sheet while the oven finishes preheating.
Can you help me make Fire Side Coffee? I've got a mixing bowl, a sifter, and a jar ready.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer and 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, and keep the bowl underneath the sifter so the dry ingredients don't scatter.
Creamer and hot chocolate mix are measured. What else goes into the dry mix?
Add 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon to your setup. The recipe direction also says to sift in nutmeg, so include it if it's part of the mix you're following.
I've got the coffee granules and cinnamon beside the bowl. Should I sift everything all at once or in batches?

You can sift them together into the bowl, working in batches if your sifter is small. Aim for an even, powdery blend with the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and nutmeg combined.
The coffee granules are a little clumpy. Do I need to break them up before they go through?
Yes, press any clumps through the sifter or crush them gently with the back of a spoon. That helps the drink mix dissolve more evenly later.
The mixture looks uniform now. How should I store it?
Pour the sifted mixture into your jar and seal it tightly with a lid. Try to keep the rim clean so the lid closes well and the powder stays dry.
Jar is filled and sealed. I want to make one mug right now—what ratio should I use?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Mix until the powder is fully dissolved.
It dissolved, but I'm not sure if it's strong enough. Is there a final adjustment?
Taste the mug and adjust to taste: add a little more mix if you want it richer, or more hot water if you want it milder.
I'm making Broccoli Chicken Roli and have the cooked chicken ready. Can you guide me from prep through getting the pan set up?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on the counter and add 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat. Have enough room to fold everything together without spilling.
Chicken is in the bowl. I'm chopping the vegetables now—how much broccoli goes in?
Add 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli. Keep the pieces fairly small so they mix evenly with the chicken.
Broccoli is added. I've got onion and green pepper on the board too.
Measure in 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper. Once those are in, the main chopped ingredients are together.
The bowl is getting full, but there's still space. What goes in before I mix?
Add the cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic to the bowl with the chicken, broccoli, onion, and bell pepper.
All of that is in. Should I stir gently or really work it together?
Mix it all together until the chicken and vegetables are evenly coated and the seasonings are spread throughout. Scrape the sides of the bowl as you go.
The mixture looks evenly coated. Should I heat the oven now?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
Oven is preheating. What should I do with the baking sheet while I wait?
Cover a cookie sheet with aluminum foil so it's ready for the Broccoli Chicken Roli mixture and cleanup is easier.
Can you walk me through making Cake Doughnuts? I'm setting out a large bowl and measuring cups now.
Absolutely. Measure out 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour and 1/2 cup white sugar, and keep the large bowl ready for mixing the dry ingredients.
Flour and sugar are measured. Are there any other dry ingredients I should add to the counter before I start stirring?
Yes—set out 1 tablespoon baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need 1 teaspoon of cinnamon and some nutmeg for the dry mixture.
I've got the baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg beside the bowl. Should everything dry go in together?
Yes. In the large bowl, stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and nutmeg until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The dry mixture looks even. I see the recipe mentions a well—how deep does that need to be?
Make a clear well in the center of the dry ingredients, just enough to hold the wet ingredients so they don't immediately spill over the sides.
The well is ready. I have milk, an egg, melted butter, and vanilla waiting.
Pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into the well in the center of the dry ingredients.
They're in the bowl. Should I beat it hard or mix gently?
Mix until everything is well blended. Scrape around the bottom and sides of the bowl so no dry flour pockets remain, but stop once the dough is evenly combined.
It's blended and a little soft. What should I do with the bowl while it rests?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour. That rest will let it firm up before you continue with shaping or cooking.
I'd like to make Fresh Apple Walnut Cake. Can you help me get the dry ingredients and pan ready?
Absolutely. Set out 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a 9x13 inch pan ready to prep.

Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is assembled.
The oven is warming up. What should I do to the pan so the cake releases cleanly?
Grease the 9x13 inch pan well, then dust it with flour. Tap the pan around so the flour coats the bottom and sides, and shake out any excess.
Pan is greased and floured. I have a sifter and a mixing bowl out—what goes in together?
Sift the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together into the bowl. That helps distribute the leavening and spice evenly through the cake.
The dry mixture looks even now. I also have the apples ready—how do they fit in at this point?
Combine the apples with the white sugar in a separate bowl, then set that mixture aside while you continue with the cake prep.
Should the sugared apples be stirred a lot or just coated?
Just stir until the apples are evenly coated with the white sugar. Once they're coated, let them sit; they'll start to release some juice while resting.
Great, the apples are set aside and the dry bowl is ready. Anything I should double-check before moving on?

Make sure the oven is still set to 350 degrees F, the 9x13 inch pan is greased and floured, and the sifted dry ingredients are separate from the apple-sugar mixture until the recipe calls for combining them.
