messages.content: For Babis Bean Salad today, I'm serving it like a fresh salsa-style salad or relish, with onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot as a raw topping. What should I do with that allium so it doesn't take over?
Cut the allium into a very fine dice, then give it a quick rinse before you mix it in.
Great, I'll do that for this batch. The black-eyed peas soaked overnight; what should I put on the counter before I start cooking?
Set out 1 1/2 cups dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight, plus 1/3 cup chopped celery with its leaves.
Peas and celery are out. I have a box grater and a bunch of parsley—how much of each do I need ready?
Shred 1 1/2 cups carrot, and chop 3/4 cup fresh parsley.
The carrot is shredded and the parsley is chopped. What pot setup do you want for the beans?
Put the soaked black-eyed peas in a saucepan and add enough water to cover them by 1 inch.
They're covered by 1 inch of water. Should I crank the burner all the way up?
Use enough heat to bring the beans to a slow boil, not a hard rolling boil.
I've got a gentle boil now, and I'm trying to keep the beans intact for the salad texture. What heat level next?
Turn the heat down to low and let the beans simmer until they're tender but not mushy, about 35 minutes.
At around 35 minutes, what texture am I checking for before I drain or mix anything?
They should be tender when you bite one, but still hold their shape instead of collapsing.
They're tender and still shaped nicely. How should I handle them before adding the celery, carrot, parsley, and rinsed allium?
Set the beans aside to cool first; once they're no longer hot, you can combine them with the prepared celery, carrot, parsley, and the finely diced rinsed allium.

original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Carrot and Coriander Soup II as a rice or noodle bowl with optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. How should I handle the soft herbs?

messages.content: For Carrot and Coriander Soup II, I'm serving it over rice or noodles today, with cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. What should I do with those tender herbs for this bowl setup?
Leave the soft herbs as bigger leaves, then set them together in a little pile along one side of each bowl.
Great, I'll plate it that way. Before I turn on the stove, which vegetables should I cut?
Cut 4 large carrots into 1 inch pieces, and chop 1/4 large onion.
The carrots are chunky and the onion is chopped. What liquids or greens do I need within reach?
Have 1 quart vegetable broth ready, plus 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro.
I've got the broth measured and the cilantro chopped. Which pan should I use, and what goes into it?
Use a large saucepan. Add the carrots, chopped onion, vegetable broth, and chopped cilantro to it.
Everything is in the saucepan. How hot should I run it, and how long am I waiting on the carrots?
Bring it to a boil, then cook until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes.
If I'm checking doneness with a fork, what texture should I be looking for?
The fork should slide into the carrot pieces easily; they should be soft enough to puree smoothly, not firm in the center.
The carrots are tender now. Do I blend right away or let it sit first?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the soup cool slightly before blending.
It has cooled a bit. How should I make it smooth for the rice or noodle bowls?
Puree the soup until smooth in a blender or food processor, then spoon it over the rice or noodles and add the herb pile at the edge of the bowl.

messages.content: For Cindis Egg Rolls, I'm putting out a raw vegetable platter with cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, and radish alongside it. What cuts will look best for the raw pieces?
Slice the raw vegetables into slim, long batons and arrange them in separate color groups on the platter.
Great, I'll serve them that way tonight. While the platter sits out, what should I pull together for the egg roll filling?
Set out 1 pound ground pork, 4 cups shredded cabbage, 1 large carrot that's shredded, and 1/2 green bell pepper cut into thin strips.
The pork is cold from the fridge and the wok is clean. Should I start heating it now?
Yes. Put the ground pork in a large wok over medium-high heat and cook it through, breaking it up as it browns.
The pork is cooked and there's some liquid in the bottom of the wok. Do I leave that in?
Drain the pork, then set it aside so it's ready to mix back in later.
I've got the drained pork resting. For the vegetables, do the cabbage and carrot go straight into the wok?
Keep them in a large bowl for now. Add the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, thin green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger to that bowl.
The bowl is pretty full. Should I toss it gently or really work it together?
Toss it well enough that the cabbage, carrot, bell pepper, onion, garlic, and ginger are evenly distributed without crushing the vegetables.
I'm clearing space for the sauce. Which small-bowl mix comes next?
In a small bowl, stir together the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until the mixture is smooth.
If I see little cornstarch clumps on the spoon, is it ready or should I keep going?
Keep stirring until those clumps disappear and the sauce looks smooth before you use it with the filling.
Can you guide me through Eclairs II? I'm setting up the counter now.
Absolutely. Put out 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water, since those will go into a saucepan together.
The butter and water are out. Do I need anything dry before I start heating things?
Yes—measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt so they're ready when you need them.
Flour and salt are measured. Should I get the oven going before the saucepan?
Yes, preheat the oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C.
Oven is heating. What pan should I prepare for the eclairs?
Grease a cookie sheet so the dough has a prepared surface when it's time to bake.
The cookie sheet is greased. I've got a medium saucepan on the stove—what goes in it?
Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to that medium saucepan.
They're in the pan. Should I stir right away or wait until it heats?
Start heating it and stir as it comes up to a boil, so the butter melts evenly into the water.
It's bubbling now, and I can still see a little butter along the edge. Is that okay?
Keep it at a boil and continue stirring until the butter melts completely.
I'm putting together Double Fudge Brownie Mix as a jar gift. What should I set out before I start?
Set out a 1 quart or 1 liter jar and the four dry ingredients: 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
I've got the jar. Does the order matter when I add everything?
Yes. Layer the ingredients in the jar in the order listed: white sugar, unsweetened cocoa powder, all-purpose flour, then chopped pecans.
The cocoa is making a dusty layer. Should I pack it down or just leave it loose?
Gently level each layer so the next one sits evenly, but don't mash it hard. The goal is neat, visible layers in the jar.
The sugar and cocoa are in, and I'm adding the flour now. Anything to watch for?
Try to pour the flour slowly into the center, then nudge it level so it doesn't streak too much down the sides of the jar.
Pecans are going on top. What do I need to write on the tag?
Attach a tag that says to preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
Should the tag include anything else from this recipe?
From the instructions you're following, the required tag direction is the oven preheat instruction: 325 degrees F or 165 degrees C.
The jar is filled and capped. Is there a quick final check before I give it away?
Make sure the lid is secure, the layers are still in the listed order, and the tag is firmly attached with the 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) preheat instruction.

messages.content: For this batch of Dilly Chicken and Potatoes, I'm serving it more like a chopped salad or mixed platter, with the parts still easy to see. What layout would work?
Toss the pieces just enough to look connected, then keep one element back and lay it across the top in a clear stripe so the platter still has distinct components.
Yes, that's the look I'm going for just for this serving. Before I turn on the stove, what should I prep?
Have the chicken and potatoes ready first: 1 broiler-fryer chicken, about 3 1/2 pounds, cut up, plus 1 pound new potatoes cut into chunks.
The chicken is cut up and the potato chunks are about bite-size. What pan and heat should I use?
Use a large skillet over medium heat, with 2 tablespoons cooking oil ready for browning.
Oil is heating. Do the potatoes go in with the chicken or after it starts browning?
Put the chicken and potatoes in together, then brown them in the oil for 10-15 minutes, turning the pieces so they color evenly.
If I'm planning the platter, should I try not to break up the potatoes while they brown?
Right—turn them gently so the potato chunks stay recognizable, which will help with that mixed-platter presentation later.
They've browned and there are drippings in the skillet. What comes out now?
Lift out both the chicken and the potatoes and set them aside, keeping the skillet and drippings for the sauce.
There's more fat in the pan than I need. How much should I leave?
Pour off the extra and leave only 1 tablespoon drippings in the skillet.
I've got the tablespoon of drippings left. How do I make the creamy part without overcomplicating it?

Add 1 cup half-and-half cream to the drippings, season with salt and pepper, and stir to mix. Spoon or drizzle it with the chicken and potatoes, then use your reserved component as the visible stripe on top.
Can you guide me through making Fresh Apple Walnut Cake? I'm setting up my counter now.
Absolutely. Put the dry ingredients within reach: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
The flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt are out. Should I get the pan ready before mixing?
Yes. Start heating the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is.
Oven is heating. I have a rectangular pan—what size am I looking for?
Use a 9x13 inch pan. Grease it well, then dust it with flour so the cake releases cleanly after baking.
The pan is greased and floured. Do the dry ingredients need to be whisked or sifted?
Sift them together: the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. That will combine the leavening and spice evenly.
I sifted the dry mix into a bowl. The apples are chopped and I have white sugar nearby.
Combine the apples with the white sugar in a separate bowl, then set that mixture aside while you continue.
Should the apple-sugar mixture look syrupy right away, or is it okay if it's still fairly dry?
It's okay if it starts out fairly dry. As it sits, the sugar will draw some moisture from the apples.
Great, I'll let it sit. Can you recap what should be done at this point?

You should have the oven preheating to 350 degrees F/175 degrees C, a greased and floured 9x13 inch pan, the flour-baking soda-cinnamon-salt mixture sifted, and the apples combined with white sugar and set aside.
Can you guide me through making Brandy Flamed Peppercorn Steak? I've got 2 beef top sirloin steaks, 8 ounces each, on the counter.
Absolutely. Along with the steaks, set out 3 tablespoons crushed black peppercorns, 1 tablespoon lemon pepper, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a large skillet for the stovetop.
The seasonings are measured. Should the peppercorns go on before anything hits the pan?
Yes. Press the crushed black peppercorns firmly into both sides of each steak so they stick to the surface rather than just sitting loose.
They're coated pretty well, but some pepper is falling off onto the board.
That's fine. Just press the steaks one more time with your palm, then sprinkle them with the lemon pepper and salt on both sides.
Seasoning is on. What heat should I use for the skillet?
Put a large skillet over medium-high heat and melt the butter in it. Let the butter coat the bottom of the pan.
The butter is melted and starting to sizzle. Do I add the steaks yet?
The recipe's next listed move is to stir in the garlic and wine, so add those to the skillet carefully and cook them for 1 minute.
Garlic and wine are in. Should I keep stirring the whole minute?
Give it a few stirs as it cooks so the garlic and wine mix into the butter, and keep the heat at medium-high.
It smells good now. Anything I should check before continuing with the steaks?
Make sure the peppercorns, lemon pepper, and salt are still well distributed on both sides of the steaks, and that the skillet mixture has cooked for the full 1 minute before you proceed.
Can you help me make Early Morning Oven Roasted New Potatoes? I've got a baking dish out but haven't started prepping yet.
Absolutely. Cut 1 1/2 pounds of new potatoes into wedges, and keep 4 tablespoons of butter nearby. You'll also want a skillet for melting the butter before coating the potatoes.
The potatoes are wedged. Should the oven be heating while I sort out the seasoning?
Yes, get the oven preheated to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C. While it heats, set out 2 teaspoons fresh rosemary, plus salt and pepper to taste.
Oven is on, and I have the rosemary, salt, and pepper measured. Do I put the butter straight on the potatoes?
Melt the butter in a hot skillet first. Once the 4 tablespoons of butter are fully melted, it will coat the potato wedges much more evenly.
The skillet is hot and the butter is melted. Should I season the butter or the potatoes?
Stir the fresh rosemary into the melted butter, then add salt and pepper to taste right there in the skillet.
It smells good. The rosemary is mixed through the butter now.
Great. Add the potato wedges to that melted butter mixture, or pour the butter over them in a bowl, and turn the potatoes until every wedge is evenly coated.
Some wedges still look a little dry on the cut sides. Is that a problem before they go in?
Give them another toss and scrape in any rosemary butter left in the skillet. The goal from the recipe is an even coating of melted butter on all the potatoes.
They're evenly coated now. Anything else before I transfer them to the pan?

Spread the coated wedges out in the baking dish or pan so they're ready for the preheated 450 degrees F oven. The recipe's listed prep stops once the potatoes are evenly coated with the rosemary butter, salt, and pepper.

messages.content: Can you help me put together the Dipping Sauce? I've got a small bowl out and want to make sure I don't miss anything.

Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons ketchup, 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish, and 1/4 teaspoon paprika. You'll also need salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper for the seasoning blend.
I have the mayonnaise and ketchup measured. Should I add them to the bowl before the horseradish?
Yes, add the mayonnaise and ketchup to the small bowl first. Give them a quick stir so the ketchup starts to tint the mayonnaise evenly.
The base is mixed. I'm opening the prepared horseradish now; it smells pretty strong.
That's normal. Measure in 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish and stir it through the mayo-ketchup mixture until there aren't any streaks or clumps.
It's smooth now. Do I add the paprika with the other seasonings all at once?
Go ahead and add the 1/4 teaspoon paprika, then add salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir well so the spices are evenly distributed throughout the sauce.
The color looks even. Should I taste it right away or let it sit first?
You can taste a tiny bit now to check the balance, but the sauce should be stored covered in the refrigerator so the flavors can settle and stay chilled.
What kind of cover is best? I'm using a small mixing bowl, not a jar.
Plastic wrap or a tight-fitting lid is fine. Press the cover securely over the bowl, then place the dipping sauce in the refrigerator.
It's covered and in the fridge. Is there anything else I need to do before serving?
No cooking is needed. When you're ready to serve, give it a quick stir after it comes out of the refrigerator, then transfer it to a dipping bowl if you like.
Can you guide me through making Cookie Bowl? I'm setting up my counter now.
Absolutely. Put out 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup sliced almonds.
I've got the dry ingredients out. Do I need to start the oven before mixing anything?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the bowl form is prepared.
Oven is heating. I have a loaf pan and a metal bowl—does the recipe allow either one?
It does. Use a 9x5 inch loaf pan or a metal bowl, turn it upside down, and cover the outside with foil.
The foil is on the outside of the upside-down loaf pan. Should it go straight onto the oven rack?
Place the foil-covered upside-down pan onto a cookie sheet instead, so it has a stable base and is easier to move.
Cookie sheet is ready. For the dry mix, do the almonds go in with the flour or later?
Add them with the dry ingredients: stir together the flour, cocoa, salt, and sliced almonds.
Should I sift the cocoa first, or just stir it into the flour?
The recipe only says to stir them together, so just mix the flour, cocoa, salt, and almonds evenly until the cocoa is distributed.
The dry mixture looks even. What should I do with it while the oven finishes preheating?
Set the stirred dry mixture aside for now, and keep the foil-covered upside-down pan on the cookie sheet ready for the next step.
Can you guide me through making Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds? I've got a large pot out and want to get the prep right.
Absolutely. Peel and cube 6 Yukon Gold potatoes and 2 sweet potatoes, then keep them nearby since they'll go into the pot together.
The potatoes are peeled and cubed. Should I put both kinds in the pot at the same time?
Yes, add the Yukon Gold potatoes and sweet potatoes to the large pot together. Pour in enough water to cover them.
They're covered with water. Before I turn on the burner, what other ingredients should I have ready?
Set out 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup heavy cream so they're ready when you need them.
Butter and cream are measured. How high should I heat the pot?
Put the pot on the stove and bring the water to a boil.
It's boiling now, and the pot is pretty full. Do I keep cooking or stop here?
At this point, remove the pot from the heat and drain the potatoes and sweet potatoes carefully.
I drained them in the sink. Should I be doing anything with the oven yet?
Yes, preheat the oven broiler so it's ready for the next stage of the dish.
The broiler is heating. Anything I should watch for while I'm waiting?
Keep the drained potatoes together and have the butter and heavy cream within reach. Once the broiler is hot, you'll be set up to continue without scrambling.
Can you help me put together the Dipping Sauce? I've got a small bowl out.
Absolutely. Add 1/2 cup mayonnaise to the bowl, then measure in 2 teaspoons ketchup.
The mayo and ketchup are in. Should I add the spicy stuff right into the same bowl?
Yes, add 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish directly to the bowl. Then sprinkle in 1/4 teaspoon paprika.
That's in there. The horseradish looks a little clumpy—do I just stir hard?
Stir steadily and scrape the sides of the bowl so the horseradish breaks up into the mayonnaise mixture. You want the color and texture to look even.
The sauce is mostly smooth now. The recipe also mentions seasonings—when do those go in?
Mix them in with the sauce now: salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir again until the spices are evenly distributed.
I added those and it smells sharp. Should this be thin or more like a creamy dip?
It should stay creamy and spoonable, more like a dip than a pourable sauce. If you see streaks of paprika or pepper, give it a few more turns with the spoon.
The color looks even. Can I serve it right away, or does it need to chill?
You can serve it right away if needed, but the recipe's storage step is to cover it and keep it in the refrigerator. Chilling also lets the flavors settle together.
I'm covering the bowl now. Any cleanup or serving tip before I put it away?
Wipe the rim so the cover seals neatly, then refrigerate it covered. When serving, give the dipping sauce a quick stir after it comes out of the refrigerator.
Can you walk me through making Classic Peanut Butter Cookies? I'm pulling ingredients out now.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup unsalted butter and 1 cup crunchy peanut butter so they're ready to cream together.
Both are on the counter. Do the sugars go in at the same time?
Yes. Measure 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup packed brown sugar, then add them with the butter and peanut butter.
I've got the sugars measured. What texture am I aiming for when I mix this?
Cream the butter, crunchy peanut butter, white sugar, and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks blended and a little lighter, with no separate streaks of butter.
The mixture looks smooth except for the peanut pieces. Should I add anything next?
That texture is right for crunchy peanut butter. Beat in the eggs next, mixing until they're fully incorporated into the batter.
Eggs are mixed in. I have another bowl ready—what goes into it?
Use that separate bowl to sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
The dry ingredients are sifted. Should I dump them all in or add them slowly?
Add the sifted dry mixture to the batter and stir it in, scraping the bowl as needed so the flour mixture is evenly combined.
It's coming together into a thick cookie dough. Is there anything else in the recipe before shaping?

For the steps you're following, that completes the dough: the butter, peanut butter, and sugars were creamed, the eggs were beaten in, the dry ingredients were sifted separately, and everything was stirred into the batter.

Keep any extra liquid in its own small container, then stir it in after you open the thermos to eat.
Perfect. While I'm setting up, what batter ingredients should I pull first?
Start with the blender and set out 2 eggs and 1/4 cup water.
The blender is out and those are measured. What dry ingredients go with them?
Add 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt to your counter.
Before I blend, does everything go in together or should I add the flour later?
For the batter, combine the eggs, water, flour, and salt in the blender together.
It's all in the blender. What texture am I aiming for?
Cover it and process until the batter is smooth, then let it stand for 15 minutes.
While the batter rests, I want to get the filling base started. What pan should I use?
Use a small saucepan. Saute the onion in butter until the onion is tender.
The onion is soft now, and I'm trying not to make a mess around the stove. What happens next?
Stir in the flour until it is blended into the butter and onion mixture.
So for serving later, I keep the extra liquid separate from the thermos until lunch, right?
Yes—pack the crepes and grains in the thermos, carry the extra liquid separately, and mix it in only after opening.
Can you help me make Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon? I've got the figs out but haven't started cutting yet.
Absolutely. You'll need 6 figs, halved, plus 6 ounces of goat cheese. Go ahead and cut each fig in half lengthwise so you have a stable little pocket for the filling.
The figs are halved. Should the cheese be softened before I stuff them?
A little softened is helpful, but it doesn't need to be warm. Spoon or press the goat cheese into each fig half so it sits neatly in the center.
Cheese is in. What should I add next for the topping?
Use 1/2 cup toasted, chopped pecans. Press some pecans into the goat cheese on each fig half so they stick rather than just sitting loose on top.
The pecans are sticking well. I also have the bacon here—how should I prep it?
Take 3 slices of bacon and cut each slice in half. Each stuffed fig half gets wrapped with one half-slice of bacon.
Do I need toothpicks, or will the bacon stay wrapped on its own?
Use toothpicks to secure the bacon around each stuffed fig half. Push them through gently so the fig stays together without squeezing out the cheese.
They're wrapped and secured. Should I heat the oven now?
Yes, preheat the broiler. Arrange the wrapped figs on a broiler-safe pan so the bacon is exposed and the figs aren't crowded.
The broiler is heating and the pan is ready. Anything to check before they go in?

Make sure each fig half is stuffed with goat cheese, the pecans are pressed into the cheese, and the bacon is held with toothpicks. Once the broiler is ready, place the pan under it and keep a close eye on them so the bacon can cook without the figs scorching.

source_seed.recipe_title: Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon

messages.content: I'm making Fire Side Coffee and want to set up the dry mix before I heat any water. What should I put on the counter?

Set out 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon. You'll also want a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, a mixing bowl, and a jar with a tight lid.
I've got the creamer and cocoa mix measured. Should the coffee granules go in whole, or do I need to crush them?
Use the instant coffee granules as they are unless yours are very clumpy. Measure 1 1/2 cups, then add them to the bowl with the creamer and hot chocolate mix.
The cinnamon is ready too. The directions mention nutmeg, but I don't see an amount here—how should I handle that?

Sift the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon together. If you have nutmeg and want to follow that note, add just a small pinch while sifting since no exact amount is given.
I'm sifting it now, and there are a few little cocoa lumps left in the strainer.
Press the soft lumps through with the back of a spoon and discard any hard bits that won't break down. The goal is an even, powdery mix so each cup tastes balanced.
The mixture looks uniform. Is it okay to store it right away?
Yes. Pour the sifted mixture into a clean, dry jar, then seal it with a lid. Keep moisture out so the instant coffee and creamer don't clump.
I want to make one mug now. How much mix goes into the water?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Stir well so the creamer, chocolate, and coffee dissolve completely.
It dissolved, but I'm not sure if it should be stronger or sweeter.
Taste the mug and adjust to taste: add a little more mix if you want it richer, or add more hot water if it's too strong. Reseal the jar when you're done scooping.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Slice or chop the allium into two different cuts, then hold both back and add them right at the end.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm doing A 1 Chicken Soup tonight as a quick broth-style noodle bowl, and for this batch I want the onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot handled in that brighter bowl-topping way. What should I do with the allium?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Cut the allium in two shapes and add both shapes at the end.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making A 1 Chicken Soup as a quick broth or noodle bowl with onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot. How should I handle the allium?

messages.content: I'm doing A 1 Chicken Soup tonight as a quick broth-style noodle bowl, and for this batch I want the onion, garlic, scallion, leek, or shallot handled in that brighter bowl-topping way. What should I do with the allium?
Slice or chop the allium into two different cuts, then hold both back and add them right at the end.
Great, I'll save those two cuts for serving. Before I turn on the stove, what should I pull out first?
Get a large pot ready and set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil along with the 2 skinless chicken leg quarters.
Pot is on the stove, and the chicken is unwrapped. Do I need the onion and liquid measured now too?
Yes. Measure 1/2 cup chopped onion and have 2 quarts water nearby so you can add them without stopping.
I've got the 1/2 cup onion and 2 quarts water ready. How hot should the pot be for browning?
Put the pot over medium heat, add the vegetable oil, then cook the chicken pieces until they're browned on both sides.
The chicken has color on both sides, but there are browned bits in the bottom. Should I scrape those up yet?
Stir in the chopped onion and cook it for 2 minutes more; as it softens, scrape the browned bits into the onion.
The onion smells good after the 2 minutes. Is this when the broth part starts?
Pour in the 2 quarts water and add the chicken bouillon, then bring the pot up to a boil.
It's starting to boil. Should I keep it rolling hard or lower it?
Lower the heat once it boils and let the soup simmer gently for 45 minutes.
While it simmers, I'll get the noodles and bowls ready. When do my two allium cuts go in?
Keep them fresh until serving: after the 45-minute simmer, ladle the hot soup into bowls and add both allium cuts at the end.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Keep the soft herbs separate in a little container, then stir or sprinkle them in once you open the lunch so they stay fresh.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: I'm making 1 Pot 3 Bean Chicken Stew to take as lunch today, and I may bring cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. What's the best way to deal with those tender herbs for this packed version?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Pack the soft herbs in a separate small container and add them after opening the lunch.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making 1 Pot 3 Bean Chicken Stew as a packed lunch with optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. How should I handle the soft herbs?

messages.content: I'm making 1 Pot 3 Bean Chicken Stew to take as lunch today, and I may bring cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. What's the best way to deal with those tender herbs for this packed version?
Keep the soft herbs separate in a little container, then stir or sprinkle them in once you open the lunch so they stay fresh.
Great, for today I want it packed that way. I've got a large pot out—what should I prep first?
Measure 1 tablespoon canola oil, then cut 1 3/4 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs into chunks.
Chicken is cut, and the oil is by the stove. Which vegetables should I chop before turning on the heat?
Chop 1 large yellow onion and slice 1 cup celery. Keep the celery handy for the simmering stage.
The onion and celery are ready. Should the pot be pretty hot before the chicken goes in?
Heat the canola oil in the large pot, then add the chicken and brown it so the pieces get some color.
The chicken has browned and there are browned bits on the bottom. Do I leave it in while I cook the onion?
Take the chicken out of the pot and set it aside for now.
Chicken is on a plate. The onion is going into the same pot—what texture am I aiming for?
Sauté the onion until it turns soft, about 5 minutes, using the moisture it releases to help loosen those browned bits.
The onion is softened. I still have the celery waiting, and I'm packing this for lunch later—what all goes in for the long simmer?
Add the broth, beans, tomatoes, celery, carrots, wine, bay leaf, herbs, and all the chicken back to the pot.
Everything is combined. How long should I let it go, and should it be covered?
Cover the pot and simmer the stew for 40 minutes. When you portion it for lunch, keep those fresh herbs separate until serving.
Can you guide me through making Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs? I've got mushrooms on the cutting board and want to make sure I'm setting up correctly.
Absolutely. For the filling, measure out 2 tablespoons olive oil and have 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms ready.
The mushrooms are chopped and measured. What aromatics should I prep before I turn on the stove?
Chop 2 green onions and crush 1 clove garlic. Keep a little cayenne pepper nearby too, since it gets stirred in with the vegetables.
All right, the onions and garlic are ready. Should I start with the oven or the saucepan?
Start by preheating the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's hot when you need it.
The oven is heating. I have a medium saucepan out; how much oil goes in and what heat should I use?
Pour the 2 tablespoons olive oil into the medium saucepan and warm it over medium heat.
The oil is shimmering a bit. Do the mushrooms go in alone, or with the other ingredients?
Stir in the 3 cups chopped mushrooms along with the 2 chopped green onions, the 1 crushed garlic clove, and the cayenne pepper.
Everything is in the pan now. How active should I be with stirring, and what texture am I looking for?
Stir often enough to keep the garlic and onions from catching on the bottom. Cook the mixture for 10 minutes, or until the mushrooms are tender.
After 10 minutes, should the pan look dry or still a little moist?
It can still look a little moist, but the mushrooms should be tender and cooked down. If they're still firm, give them another brief stir over medium heat until they soften.
I'm making Coq au Vin alla Italiana and have a large skillet ready. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 4 pounds of dark meat chicken pieces, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 5 cloves of crushed garlic, and 1/2 cup all-purpose flour.
The chicken is on a tray, and I've measured the oil and flour. Should I prep the garlic before heating the pan?
Yes, crush the garlic now so it's ready to add quickly once the oil is hot. You'll use 1/2 of the garlic at the start.
Garlic is crushed. Do I heat the skillet dry first or add the oil right away?
Add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the large skillet and heat it until it looks loose and shimmery.
The oil is shimmering a bit. I don't want the garlic to burn—how much goes in?
Add 1/2 of the crushed garlic to the skillet and stir it briefly so it perfumes the oil.
That smells good. While it cooks, what should I do with the flour?
Season the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour with poultry seasoning, mixing it evenly so the chicken gets seasoned as it's coated.
The flour is seasoned. Should the chicken pieces be fully covered or just dusted?
Dredge the chicken parts in the seasoned flour so each piece has an even coating, shaking off any heavy excess before it goes into the skillet.
The chicken is coated and the skillet is still hot. How long should I brown it?
Place the dredged chicken parts in the skillet and brown them for 4 or 5 minutes, turning as needed so the surfaces pick up color.
Can you guide me through making Adobo Chicken with Ginger? I've got a Dutch oven out and want to set up before I turn on the stove.
Absolutely. Start by having 1 (3 pound) whole chicken cut into 8 pieces ready, along with 1/2 cup soy sauce and 3/4 cup distilled white vinegar.
The chicken is cut up, and I measured the soy sauce and vinegar. What aromatics should I prep?
Peel and crush 1 bulb of garlic. You'll also need the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns ready to go into the pot with the chicken.
The garlic is crushed, and the ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns are beside the stove. Do I brown the chicken first?
For this recipe, don't brown it first. Put the chicken pieces directly into the Dutch oven with the soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, ginger, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Everything is in the Dutch oven. Should the lid be on while I bring it up to temperature?
Bring it to a boil over medium heat. Keep an eye on it as it heats so the liquid comes up steadily without rushing it.
It's starting to bubble around the edges, but the center isn't boiling yet. Do I wait?
Yes, wait until it reaches a true boil across the pot. Once it boils, reduce the heat so it settles into a simmer.
It boiled, and I lowered the burner. The liquid is gently moving now.
That's the right pace. Cover the pot and let the chicken simmer for 30 minutes.
While it simmers, do I just leave it alone, or should I check on the pieces?
Check in occasionally and baste the chicken with the cooking liquid as it simmers, then keep it covered between bastings until the 30 minutes are up.
Can you guide me through Baked Apple Oatmeal? I'm getting the saucepan and casserole dish out now.
Absolutely. You'll need a greased 2-qt. casserole for baking later, plus a saucepan for the stovetop part. Measure out 4 cups milk and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to start.
Milk and brown sugar are measured. What should I put beside them before I turn on the burner?
Set out 2 teaspoons butter or margarine and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also be heating cinnamon with those ingredients in the saucepan.
The butter, salt, and cinnamon are ready. Do I heat everything together or add them one at a time?
Put the milk, brown sugar, butter or margarine, salt, and cinnamon into the saucepan together, then heat the mixture gently while stirring so the sugar dissolves and the butter melts.
It's warming and smells good. Should it be boiling before I add the rest?
The recipe just says to heat it, so you don't need to push it to a hard boil. Once it's hot and combined, add the remaining ingredients and mix gently.
I've added the remaining ingredients. How gentle are we talking for the mixing?
Fold or stir slowly, just until everything is evenly moistened. Try not to mash the apple pieces or overwork the oatmeal mixture.
The mixture is combined. Is it time for the casserole dish?
Yes. Spoon the oatmeal mixture into the greased 2-qt. casserole and spread it into an even layer so it bakes consistently.
It's in the dish and leveled out. What are the oven details?
Cover the casserole and bake it at 350 degrees F for 45 minutes. When it comes out, let it sit briefly before serving so the oatmeal can settle.
Can you guide me through making Chocolate Covered Pretzels? I've got space cleared on the counter and some wax paper nearby.

Absolutely. You'll need 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. Set up a double boiler over low heat and keep the wax paper ready for the coated pretzels.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips out. The cream is measured too. How should I start melting it?
Add the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream to the top of the double boiler. Keep the heat low and stir constantly so the chocolate melts smoothly without scorching.
The chocolate is starting to soften, but there are still a few lumps. Should I keep it over the heat?
Yes, keep it over the low heat and continue stirring. Once it looks fully melted and glossy, you're ready to dip while the mixture is still very warm.
It's smooth now. Do I dump in a handful of pretzels or coat them individually?
Dip the pretzels one at a time. Work quickly so each pretzel gets coated while the chocolate mixture is still very warm.
Some of them are dripping a lot when I lift them out. Is that okay?
That's fine. Let the excess chocolate drip back into the double boiler for a moment, then transfer each coated pretzel to the wax paper.
I've got the first batch on the wax paper. Should they be touching, or do they need space?
Give them a little space on the wax paper so they can set and cool without sticking together.
All the pretzels are coated and laid out. What should I do before serving them?
Leave them on the wax paper until the chocolate has set and cooled. Once firm, they're ready to serve or pack up.
Can you walk me through Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds? I've got a big pot out and want to make sure I prep the potatoes correctly.
Absolutely. Peel and cube 6 Yukon Gold potatoes and 2 sweet potatoes, keeping the pieces fairly similar in size so they heat evenly in the pot.
The Yukon Golds and sweet potatoes are cubed. Before I start cooking, what else should I have nearby?
Set out 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup heavy cream. You'll also need the large pot, enough water to cover the potatoes, a colander for draining, and access to the oven broiler later.
The butter and cream are measured, and the cubed potatoes are in the pot. How much water should I add?
Add enough water to cover both the Yukon Gold potatoes and the sweet potatoes. They should be submerged, but you do not need to fill the pot much beyond that.
They're covered with water. Do I put the pot over high heat?
Yes, put the pot on the stove and heat it until the water comes to a boil.
The water is starting to bubble around the edges but isn't fully boiling yet. Should I wait for a stronger boil?
Wait until it reaches a true boil across the surface. Once it does, follow the recipe by removing the pot from the heat.
It's boiling now, and I've turned off the burner. What's the safest way to drain it?
Carefully pour the potatoes and sweet potatoes into a colander in the sink, keeping your hands clear of the steam. Let them drain well so excess water does not carry over.
They're drained. Is the broiler part next, or do I mix in the butter and cream first?
The next listed step is to preheat the oven broiler. Turn the broiler on now so it can heat while you get ready for the remaining assembly with the butter and heavy cream.
I'd like to make Argentine Chimichurri Bread in my bread machine. Can you guide me without assuming I know the order?
Absolutely. Set out the bread machine pan and check your machine's manual for the recommended loading order, since that part depends on the model.
The pan is out. What ingredients should I measure before I start pouring anything in?
Measure 1 cup water, 1 1/2 tablespoons white wine vinegar, 3 tablespoons olive oil, and 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper.
I've got the water and vinegar measured. Should I add them straight to the pan?
Yes, if your manufacturer recommends liquids first, add the water and white wine vinegar to the bread machine pan now. If your manual says a different order, follow that instead.
My machine says liquids go in before oils and dry seasonings.
Great. After the water and vinegar are in, pour in the olive oil, then add the cayenne pepper where your machine's instructions suggest seasonings should go.
Everything is in the pan, and I don't see any spills around the paddle.
Place the pan securely into the bread machine and make sure it locks into position so the paddle can mix properly.
It clicked into place. Which cycle should I choose for this bread?
Select the Basic or White Cycle, whichever wording your machine uses for a standard white bread program.
Basic is selected. Is there anything else before I close it and start?
Close the lid, press Start, and let the bread machine run the cycle. Once it begins mixing, you can glance in briefly to confirm the paddle is moving, then leave it to bake.
Can you walk me through making Caraway Rye Muffins? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to set up the dry ingredients first.
Absolutely. Put 1 cup rye flour and 3/4 cup all-purpose flour in the large bowl, then add 1/4 cup sugar and 2 1/2 teaspoons baking powder.
Those are measured. The recipe also mentions salt and caraway seeds—do they go in with the flour mixture?
Yes, add the salt and caraway seeds to that same bowl, then whisk or stir everything together so the baking powder and seeds are evenly distributed.
The dry mix looks even, and I can see the caraway seeds throughout. What should I do with the cheese?
Stir the cheese into the dry ingredients now. Coat it lightly with the flour mixture so it doesn't clump in one spot.
Cheese is mixed in. I have the egg, milk, and oil nearby—should I combine them separately?
Yes. In another bowl or measuring cup, combine the egg, milk, and oil until they're blended.
The wet ingredients are combined. When I pour them in, how much mixing is enough?
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir just until moistened. Stop when you no longer see big dry pockets; a slightly lumpy batter is fine.
I still see a few streaks of flour near the bottom, but I don't want tough muffins.
Give it just a couple more gentle folds, scraping the bottom of the bowl, then stop as soon as those flour streaks disappear.
The batter is ready. I have paper liners in the muffin pan—how full should each cup be?
Spoon the batter into the greased or paper-lined muffin cups, filling each one two-thirds full.
Can you guide me through Fall Harvest Baked Apples? I've got the apples out but haven't started heating anything yet.
Absolutely. Set your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it can preheat while you prep the dish.
Oven is heating. For the apples, am I using them whole once they're cored?
Yes, use 8 red apples, cored, and keep them sturdy enough to sit upright. Arrange them in a 9x13 inch baking dish.
They're in the baking dish. What should I put near the stove for the sauce?
You'll need 1/4 cup butter, 1/3 cup maple syrup, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon. The recipe also has you combine ginger, lemon juice, and vanilla in the saucepan.
I've measured the butter, syrup, and cinnamon. Should the saucepan be hot before I add them?
Put a small saucepan over medium heat, then add the butter, maple syrup, cinnamon, ginger, lemon juice, and vanilla together.
The butter is starting to melt. Do I just stir until it looks smooth?
Stir as it heats so the butter blends into the maple syrup and spices. Keep it on medium heat until the mixture comes to a boil.
It's bubbling now. How do I get it onto the apples without leaving some dry?
Carefully drizzle the hot mixture equally over the cored apples, aiming some into each center and letting the rest coat the tops and sides.
The sauce is on the apples. Is there anything else from this recipe before they go in?
That covers the listed steps: oven preheated to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), apples in the 9x13 inch dish, sauce boiled, and drizzled evenly over them.
I'm making Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup and have the slow cooker out. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start loading it?
Yes. For the base, have 1 1/2 pounds cubed beef stew meat ready, plus 2 cups water for the liquid in the slow cooker.
The beef is thawed and cubed, and I measured the water. What produce and canned items should I put beside the cooker?
Set out 1 small onion, chopped, and 1 28 ounce can crushed tomatoes. The recipe also has you stir in mixed vegetables and potatoes when you build the soup.
I chopped the onion and opened the tomatoes. Should I brown the beef first, or does it go straight in?
For this recipe, put the cubed beef stew meat straight into the slow cooker.
The beef is in the crock. I don't want to splash too much—where does the water fit in?
Pour the 2 cups water over the beef in the slow cooker, letting it settle around the meat.
Water is in. I've got onion, tomatoes, mixed vegetables, and potatoes lined up; do they all go in together?
Yes, stir in the chopped onion, crushed tomatoes, mixed vegetables, and potatoes so they're distributed through the beef and water.
The vegetables are mixed in. It looks chunky, with liquid around the edges. What seasonings are called for?
Season the soup with bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil. Sprinkle them over the top, then give everything a gentle stir to combine.
All seasoned and stirred. Before I put the lid on, should the ingredients be fully submerged?
They don't have to be perfectly submerged; just make sure the beef, onion, tomatoes, mixed vegetables, potatoes, water, and seasonings are evenly combined in the slow cooker before covering it.

source_seed.recipe_title: Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup

messages.content: Can you help me get Canadian Cedar Planked Salmon started? I've got the grill area cleared but haven't prepped the plank yet.
Absolutely. For this recipe, set out a 24x8x1 inch untreated cedar plank and 6 salmon fillets, each about 4 ounces. The plank needs a long soak before it goes anywhere near the grill.
The plank is untreated, and the salmon is still in the fridge. What else should I pull out now?
You'll also need 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil and 1 large red onion, chopped. Keep the salmon chilled while you handle the plank prep.
I have the olive oil, and I'll chop the red onion. How do I soak the cedar plank properly?
Put the untreated cedar plank in water so it's fully submerged. If it wants to float, weigh it down with a clean bowl, plate, or something similar.
It's floating a bit, so I'll weigh it down. How long does it need to stay in the water?
Let it soak approximately 12 hours, or overnight. That long soak helps prepare the wood for the high heat of the grill.
The plank soaked overnight and is wet all the way through. Should I start heating the grill?
Yes. Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat. While it heats, keep the prepared plank nearby and have coarse salt ready.
The grill is getting hot. Do I oil the plank or put the onion on it yet?
For the recipe step we're on, don't add the olive oil, onion, or salmon yet. Place the prepared plank on the grill, then sprinkle it with coarse salt.
The salted plank is on the grill. Is there anything else from the written directions before I move on?
That completes the listed setup directions: the cedar plank has been soaked, the grill preheated for high heat, and the prepared plank placed on the grill with coarse salt.
Can you help me make Artichoke Hummus? I've got my food processor out and want to set up the ingredients before I start.
Absolutely. Drain 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, also called garbanzo beans, and set out 1 clove of garlic.
The chickpeas are drained, and I have the garlic. Do I need to chop the garlic before it goes in?
You can give the garlic a rough chop if your processor is small, but it will get blended with everything. Also measure 1/2 cup drained marinated artichoke hearts and 2 tablespoons lemon juice.
I have the artichoke hearts drained and the lemon juice measured. Should the artichokes be rinsed or left as they are?
Leave them as they are after draining; the marinated flavor belongs in this hummus. Add the chickpeas, garlic, artichoke hearts, and lemon juice to the work bowl of the food processor.
Everything is in the processor bowl. The recipe mentions parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks—do those go in too?
No, keep parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks out of the food processor. The blended mixture is just the listed hummus ingredients.
The lid is on. Should I run the processor continuously or use short bursts?
Use pulses at first, then keep pulsing until the hummus turns smooth. Stop and scrape down the sides if any chickpeas or artichoke pieces stick.
It's mostly smooth now, with just a little texture from the artichokes. Is that okay?
Yes, that works for artichoke hummus. If you want it smoother, pulse a bit longer; otherwise, transfer it to a serving bowl.
It's in a bowl. I'm not serving it for another couple of hours—what should I do with it?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate it until you're ready to serve. Give it a quick stir before putting it out.
Can you guide me through Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad? I've got a skillet out and want to make sure I prep the chicken correctly.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided, and 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, about 6 ounces each. Pat the chicken dry so the seasoning can cling well.
Chicken is patted dry. I see the olive oil is divided—how much goes in the pan right away?
Pour 1 tablespoon olive oil into a large skillet and warm it over medium heat. Save the remaining tablespoon for any later use or if the pan seems too dry.
The oil is warming. What seasonings and aromatics should I have ready before the chicken hits the pan?
Measure 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, and have 2 cloves garlic crushed and ready nearby. Once the skillet is hot, coat both sides of the chicken with the Cajun seasoning.
Both sides are seasoned, and the garlic is crushed. Should the chicken go in before the garlic?
Yes. Place the seasoned chicken breasts into the hot oil first, laying them down carefully so they sear instead of splashing.
They're in the skillet and starting to sizzle. When do I add the crushed garlic?
Stir the crushed garlic into the skillet now, keeping it around the chicken so it flavors the oil without piling directly on one spot.
The garlic smells good, but I don't want it to burn. How long should the chicken cook?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on each side over medium heat. Keep an eye on the garlic and move it around the pan if it starts browning too fast.
I flipped the chicken after 5 minutes. How do I know it's done enough to serve?
After the second side has cooked about 5 minutes, check that the juices run clear. Once they do, take the chicken out of the skillet and let it rest briefly before slicing it for the salad.
I'm making Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers and I've cleared space by the grill. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set the grill up to preheat on high heat while you gather the burger mixture ingredients.
The grill is heating. I have Cheddar out, but how much goes in the bowl?
Use 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, and add 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese with it in a large bowl.
Cheeses are measured. I also chopped an onion—does all of it go in?
Yes, add 1 small chopped onion to the bowl, then crack in 1 egg.
Egg and onion are in. What seasonings or sauces should I mix with that before the meat?
Stir in the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper with the cheeses, onion, and egg until everything is evenly combined.
That mixture looks loose and glossy. Should I add the beef directly to it?
Yes. Crumble the ground beef into the bowl, then mix it together by hand just until the ingredients are distributed.
I don't want to overwork it. Should it be fully smooth or still a little rough?
A little rough is fine; stop once you don't see big pockets of the cheese-and-onion mixture separate from the beef.
The meat mixture is combined. How do I shape these with the bacon?
Form the mixture into 6 patties, then wrap a slice of bacon around each patty before they go to the hot grill.
Can you walk me through Broccoli Coleslaw? I've got a bowl out and want to prep it for serving later.

Absolutely. Set out 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1 (3 ounce) package of chicken flavored ramen noodles. Keep the seasoning packet from the ramen—we'll use it in the dressing.
I have the oil, vinegar, sugar, and ramen. Should I crush the noodles right away or wait?
You can crush the ramen now, but keep the dry noodles separate from the dressing for the moment. Open the packet carefully and reserve the seasoning packet.
Got it. I also have broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds ready. What bowl should I use first?
Use a small bowl for the dressing. Pour in the olive oil and distilled white vinegar, then add the white sugar and the ramen seasoning packet.
The dressing ingredients are in the small bowl. Do I whisk it until the sugar disappears?
Mix it well so the seasoning is evenly distributed and the sugar starts dissolving. It may not look perfectly clear, but it should be blended rather than separated.
It's mixed. I'm making this ahead—how long should the dressing chill?
Refrigerate the dressing for at least 1 hour before serving. If you have more time, chilling it overnight is fine too.
While that chills, should I build the vegetable part in a large bowl?
Yes. In a large bowl, combine the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds so everything is evenly mixed.
The vegetables and sunflower seeds are together, and the ramen is crushed. How do I bring it all together?
Stir the crushed ramen noodles into the large bowl with the broccoli mixture. When you're ready to serve, add the chilled dressing and toss well so the coleslaw is coated.
Can you help me make Campfire Angel Food Yummies at the campsite?

Absolutely. You'll need 1 angel food cake, about 10 inches, cut into large cubes; 1 can of sweetened condensed milk, 5 ounces; and 1 cup coconut flakes. You'll also want toasting sticks and a campfire with steady coals rather than big flames.
I've got the cake cubed and the condensed milk opened. Should the coconut go in a bowl?
Yes, pour the coconut flakes into a shallow bowl or plate so the toasted cake can roll through them easily. Keep the condensed milk in another small bowl or cup for dipping.
The fire has mostly burned down to coals. Is that the right heat?
That's perfect. Skewer a few angel food cake cubes on toasting sticks and hold them over the coals, turning them often so the edges brown evenly without scorching.
They're browning fast on the corners. How toasted should they get?
Aim for lightly browned and a little crisp on the outside while still soft inside. Since angel food cake is airy, it only needs a short time over the coals.
Okay, I have a few toasted cubes ready. Do I dip while they're still warm?
Yes, dip the warm toasted cake into the sweetened condensed milk so it gets a light coating, then roll it right away in the coconut flakes.
Some of the milk is dripping off. Should I soak the pieces or just coat them?
Just coat them. A quick dip is enough; if they sit too long in the condensed milk, the cake can get heavy and messy before it reaches the coconut.
What's the best way to serve them around the fire without making everything sticky?

Set the finished pieces on a plate or parchment, or let everyone eat them straight from the sticks once they're coated. Keep napkins nearby, and close the condensed milk between batches to cut down on sticky spills.
Can you help me make Chicken and Black Bean Chili? I've got a large pot out, but I want to make sure I prep the chicken correctly.
Absolutely. Cut 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into 1 inch pieces, and keep 2 tablespoons cooking oil nearby for the pot.
The chicken is cut into 1 inch pieces. Should I season it before it goes in, or start with the oil?
Start with the oil: add the 2 tablespoons cooking oil to the large pot and heat it over medium heat.
The oil is heating. I also have sea salt and chili powder on the counter—how much chili powder should I plan on?
Use 1 tablespoon chili powder, or adjust to taste. Keep sea salt ready too, since the recipe seasons the chicken after it browns.
The oil looks hot but not smoking. Do I add all the chicken at once?
Add the chicken pieces to the pot in a single layer if you can, then brown them on all sides. If the pot is crowded, work in batches so the pieces brown instead of steaming.
The chicken is mostly browned and there are browned bits on the bottom of the pot. Is this where the spices go in?
Yes. Season the chicken with sea salt, the chili powder, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir so the spices coat the chicken and warm in the oil.
It smells good. I'm chopping the vegetables now—what goes in with the chicken?
Mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper. Stir them through the seasoned chicken so they start picking up the spices and browned bits.
The peppers and onion are in. Should I keep the heat at medium while they soften?
Yes, medium heat is right for this stage. Stir occasionally, scraping the bottom of the pot as the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper cook into the spiced chicken.
Can you help me get started on Glazed Ham? I've got an 8 pound bone-in shank ham on the counter.
Absolutely. For this Glazed Ham, you'll need that 1 (8 pound) bone-in shank ham, plus 4 cups water, or as needed, 1/2 cup honey, and 1/2 cup brown sugar.
I found the honey and brown sugar. Should I measure them before I heat the oven?
Yes, measure out 1/2 cup honey and 1/2 cup brown sugar now so they're ready when you need them. Then set your oven to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C.
The oven is preheating to 275, and I have a roasting pan out. Does the ham go in flat-side down?
Place the ham in the roasting pan so it sits securely and won't tip while you move the pan. Use whatever side feels most stable for your bone-in shank ham.
It's in the pan, but the pan is pretty deep. How much water should I add?
Pour in water until it reaches a 2 inch depth in the roasting pan. You may not need all 4 cups, or you may need a bit more depending on the pan size.
I'm checking the depth now. Should the water go over the ham at all?
No, just keep the water around the ham at about 2 inches deep. It's there to help keep moisture in the pan, not to cover the ham.
The water level is right. I have foil, but not a lid that came with this pan.
The recipe calls for covering it with a tight fitting lid. If your roasting pan has a lid that fits snugly, use that so the moisture stays trapped.
I found the matching lid in the cabinet. Anything else before I put it in?
Set the tight fitting lid on the roasting pan, make sure it's seated well, and you're ready for the covered ham to go into the 275 degrees F oven.
Can you guide me through making Dutch Cream Waffles? I've got my bowls out but haven't measured anything yet.
Absolutely. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt, then set them near a large mixing bowl.
The flour and salt are measured. Should I separate the eggs before mixing the dry ingredients?
Yes, separate the eggs so you have 3 egg yolks and 3 egg whites ready. Keep the yolks in a small mixing bowl for the next part.
Eggs are separated, and the yolks are in the small bowl. What should go into the large bowl?
Put the flour and salt into the large mixing bowl and stir them together so the salt is evenly distributed.
Dry ingredients are combined. I'm about to use the mixer—what speed do I want for the yolks?
Use low speed for the egg yolks, and while they're beating, add the cream gradually.
The cream is going in slowly. How long should I keep beating the yolk mixture?
Beat that mixture for 1 minute, keeping it smooth and even.
It's been 1 minute and the yolk mixture looks blended. Do I pour it straight into the flour?
Yes. Add the yolk-and-cream mixture to the flour mixture in the large bowl.
It's in the bowl now. How do I mix it without making a mess?
Start on low speed just until the flour begins to combine, then increase to medium-high and beat until the batter is smooth.
Can you help me make Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs? I've got a cutting board out and want to prep everything before the pan gets hot.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms, 2 chopped green onions, and 1 clove garlic, crushed. You'll also need cayenne pepper for the pan, plus a medium saucepan.
The mushrooms are chopped, but the green onions still need slicing. Should I start the oven while I do that?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, while you finish the green onions and crush the garlic.
Oven is heating. For the saucepan, am I using high heat to get the mushrooms going fast?
Use medium heat instead. Pour the 2 tablespoons olive oil into the medium saucepan and let it warm gently so the garlic and green onions won't scorch.
The oil looks glossy now. Do the mushrooms go in before the garlic?
Add the mushrooms, green onions, crushed garlic, and cayenne pepper together, then stir so everything gets coated in the oil.
It's all in the pan. The mushrooms are taking up a lot of room; should I keep stirring constantly?
Stir often, but it doesn't have to be nonstop. As the mushrooms cook, they'll soften and shrink down, and the aromatics will spread through the mixture.
How long should I let this cook, and what texture am I looking for?
Cook it for 10 minutes, or until the mixture is tender. The mushrooms should look softened and moist rather than raw or firm.
If there's a little liquid in the saucepan near the end, is that okay?
A little moisture is fine as long as the mushrooms are tender after the 10 minutes. Give everything a final stir and keep it ready for the puff assembly or serving step you're using.
Can you guide me through the halibut part for Alaskan Halibut Lasagna? I'm setting up my board and skillet now.

Absolutely. Have 6 tablespoons butter or margarine available, but keep it divided since you'll only use 2 tablespoons in the skillet right away. You'll also need 1 1/2 pounds halibut steaks with the bones removed, cut into 1 inch cubes.
The fish is cubed and I've got the butter measured. Should I prep the seasonings before the pan heats?
Yes, that will make the cooking smoother. Mince 2 garlic cloves and measure out 3/4 teaspoon dried thyme so both can go in as soon as the fish hits the skillet.
Garlic and thyme are ready. What size pan and heat should I use?
Use a large skillet and set it over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of the butter or margarine and let it melt evenly before adding anything else.
The butter is melted and foaming a little, but not browning. Is that right?
That's right. Add the halibut cubes to the skillet, then scatter in the minced garlic and the 3/4 teaspoon dried thyme.
Everything is in the pan. Should I stir a lot or leave the cubes alone?
Stir gently so the garlic and thyme coat the fish, but don't mash the halibut. Keep the heat at medium and let it cook until the fish flakes easily with a fork, about 10 minutes.
I'm around 8 minutes in. The pieces are turning opaque, but a few centers still look firm.
Give them a little more time, checking gently with a fork. You're looking for the halibut to separate into flakes easily, which should be close to the 10 minute mark.
It flakes now and the garlic smells cooked. What do I do with it before assembling the lasagna?
Remove the cooked halibut mixture from the skillet and set it aside. Keep any remaining butter from the original 6 tablespoons reserved for later parts of the recipe.
Can you help me make Gingered Mango Salsa? I've got a cutting board out and want to make sure I prep it in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by peeling and chopping enough mango to measure 1 cup. Add it to a medium bowl so there's room to stir without spilling.
The mango is chopped and in the bowl. How fine should I cut the red onion?
Chop the red onion fairly small so it mixes through the salsa evenly, then measure 1/4 cup and add it to the mango.
Onion is in. I have cilantro and limes ready—what amounts do I need?
Mince fresh cilantro until you have 1/4 cup, then squeeze or measure 1/4 cup lime juice. Add both to the bowl with the mango and onion.
Everything's in the bowl now. Should I mash it at all or just stir?
Just stir it gently to combine all the ingredients. You want the mango pieces to stay intact, with the cilantro, onion, and lime juice distributed throughout.
It's mixed. The lime juice is pooling a little at the bottom—is that okay?
Yes, that's fine. Give it a couple of turns with a spoon so the lime juice coats the mango and onion, then let the salsa sit.
How long should it stand before I serve it?
Let it stand for 30 minutes before serving. That resting time helps the lime juice and aromatics mingle with the mango.
After the 30 minutes, do I need to drain it or do anything else before putting it out?
No draining is required. Give it a quick stir, taste the texture to make sure the mango still feels fresh and tender, and serve it straight from the bowl or transfer it to a serving dish.
Can you help me put together the Double Fudge Brownie Mix? I'm setting it up as a jar mix and want the layers to look neat.
Absolutely. Use a 1 quart or 1 liter jar, and have the ingredients ready: 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
I've got the jar washed and dried. Should I add the sugar before the cocoa?
Yes. Layer the ingredients in the order listed, so start with the 2 cups white sugar at the bottom of the jar.
The sugar is in. The cocoa is pretty powdery—any trick to keeping the side of the jar clean?
Spoon the 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder in gently, or use a small funnel if you have one. Tap the jar lightly on the counter to level the cocoa without shaking the layers together.
That worked. I can still see a clear cocoa layer. What goes over it?
Add the 1 cup all-purpose flour next. Try to pour it evenly across the cocoa so the top stays level.
Flour is in, though it's a little mounded in the middle. Is that okay before the pecans?
That's fine. Smooth it gently with the back of a spoon if you can reach, then add the 1 cup chopped pecans as the final layer.
The pecans are on top and the jar looks full. What should I write on the tag?
Attach a tag with the baking instruction: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Make sure it's tied or taped securely to the jar.
Do I need to include anything else from this recipe before I give it away?
For this recipe, the required setup is complete once the ingredients are layered in the 1 quart or 1 liter jar and the tag includes the preheat instruction for 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
I want to make Broccoli Cheese Crepes. Can you guide me while I get the batter started?
Absolutely. Set up a blender and measure out 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
The blender is out, and I have the eggs and water measured. Should the flour and salt go in at the same time?
Yes. Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to the blender together so the crepe batter can blend evenly.
Everything is in the blender. How smooth am I aiming for?
Cover the blender and process until the batter looks smooth, with no obvious flour pockets.
It looks smooth now. Do I use it right away or wait?
Let the batter stand for 15 minutes before cooking the crepes.
While it rests, I want to prep the filling base. What pan should I use?
Use a small saucepan. Melt the butter, add the onion, and sauté it until the onion is tender.
The onion is soft and smells good. Do I keep the heat on for the next part?
Keep it gentle, then stir in the flour until it is blended into the butter and onion mixture.
How will I know the flour is blended enough?
It should look evenly moistened and mixed in, without dry streaks of flour left in the saucepan.
Can you talk me through making Fudge Drops? I've got a saucepan out but want to make sure I measure everything right.
Absolutely. For the base, measure 1 2/3 cups sugar and open 1 (5 ounce) can evaporated milk. You'll also want a heavy saucepan so the mixture heats evenly.
Sugar and the 5 ounce can of evaporated milk are ready. What else goes into the pan?
Add 2 tablespoons butter or margarine and 1/2 teaspoon salt to your measured ingredients. Before heating, line baking sheets with waxed paper so they're ready for dropping the candy later.
The baking sheets are lined. Do I combine everything cold in the saucepan?
Yes. Put the sugar, evaporated milk, butter or margarine, and salt into the heavy saucepan together before turning on the heat.
They're in the pan. Should the heat be low or higher?
Set it over medium heat. Stir constantly as it warms so the sugar dissolves and the mixture doesn't scorch on the bottom.
It's starting to bubble around the edges. Do I keep stirring through the boil?
Keep stirring constantly and bring it to a full boil over that medium heat. Stay with it the whole time.
It has boiled. What happens once I take it off the burner?
Remove the saucepan from the heat, then stir in the remaining ingredients called for by your recipe.
Okay, it's mixed. How do I portion them so they set neatly?
Drop the mixture by tablespoonfuls onto the waxed paper-lined baking sheets. Give them a little space so each Fudge Drop can set cleanly.
Can you help me make Garden Party Salad? I'm setting out the dressing ingredients and want to get the order right.
Absolutely. For the dressing, measure 1/4 cup vegetable oil and 1/4 cup orange marmalade into your prep area, along with a small bowl and a whisk.
I've got the oil and marmalade. The marmalade is a little thick—should I warm it or just whisk?
You can just whisk it; the vinegar and mayonnaise will help loosen it. Add 3 tablespoons cider vinegar and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise to the bowl with the oil and marmalade.
Everything is in the small bowl. What texture am I looking for before it goes in the fridge?
Whisk the dressing ingredients until the mixture looks smooth and evenly blended, with no big streaks of mayonnaise or marmalade. Once it's smooth, chill it.
The dressing is chilling now. Should I mix the salad part right away or wait?
Wait until just before serving. That's when you'll combine the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley in a large bowl so everything stays fresh and the almonds keep some texture.
I'm about ten minutes from serving and have a large bowl ready. Do I add the dressing all at once?

Add the chilled dressing to the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley, then toss gently until the ingredients are coated. If you're worried about over-dressing it, add most of the dressing first and toss before adding the rest.
It's coated and looks creamy. Should I keep tossing to make it more even?
Only toss until it's evenly combined. Once the chicken and mix-ins are coated, stop so the salad doesn't get mashed or heavy.
I'm serving it for a garden lunch. Any final serving tip before I bring it out?
Serve it right after tossing, while the dressing is cool and the almonds still have texture. Give the bowl a quick scrape around the sides, then transfer it to your serving dish.
Can you help me make Crustless Spinach Quiche 2? I've got a quiche pan out, but I want to go step by step.
Absolutely. Set out 3 ounces reduced fat cream cheese and let it soften if it is still firm. You'll also need 1 cup fat-free milk, 1 cup egg substitute, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
The cream cheese is softened, and I measured the milk. Should I spray the pan now or wait?
Go ahead and coat the quiche pan with nonstick cooking spray now, so it is ready when the filling is mixed.
Pan is sprayed. What bowl should I use for the cream cheese?
Use a small mixing bowl. Put the softened cream cheese in and beat it until it loosens up and looks smooth enough to blend with liquid.
It's creamy but still a little thick. Is that okay before adding the milk?
Yes, that is fine. Pour in the fat-free milk, add the egg substitute, and sprinkle in the pepper, then beat everything together until the mixture is smooth.
I added the 1 cup egg substitute and the 1/4 teaspoon pepper. How smooth should it be?
Aim for an even, pourable mixture with no large cream cheese lumps. A few tiny specks are okay, but keep beating if you see bigger streaks.
It looks pourable now. The recipe says to stir in remaining ingredients—do I fold them in gently?
Yes. Stir in the remaining ingredients just until they are evenly distributed through the creamy mixture.
Everything is mixed. How do I get it into the pan without making a mess?
Place the sprayed quiche pan on a steady surface, then pour or scrape the mixture into it slowly. Spread it evenly in the pan so it is ready for the next cooking stage.
Can you help me make Cupids Cookies? I've got a mixing bowl out but want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup butter and 1 cup white sugar to begin. Those are the two you'll cream together in a medium bowl.
Butter and sugar are measured. Should the butter be soft before I mix it?
Yes, softened butter will cream much more easily. Beat the butter with the white sugar until the mixture looks light and fluffy rather than dense or gritty.
It's getting pale and fluffy now. What do I add after that?
Add 1 egg and 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract, then blend them into the creamed butter and sugar until the mixture looks even.
The egg and vanilla are mixed in. I noticed the directions mention dry ingredients—what should I do with those?
Sift the flour and salt together before adding them. The recipe doesn't give amounts for those in the ingredient list you shared, so use the amounts from your full recipe if you have them.
I've got the flour and salt from my copy. Do I dump them all in at once?
You can add the sifted flour and salt to the creamed mixture, then mix well. If you want to keep the bowl tidy, add them gradually and mix on a lower speed at first.
The dough is coming together, but there are a few dry streaks on the sides of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl, then mix just until the dry streaks disappear and the dough looks evenly combined.
Looks smooth now. Is that the end of the prep for this recipe?
Yes. For the steps you provided, you've completed the dough: cream the butter and sugar, blend in the egg and vanilla, sift flour with salt, then add that to the creamed mixture and mix well.
