Can you help me make Coconut Ambrosia Salad? I've got a large mixing bowl out, but I want to be sure I drain the fruit properly.

Absolutely. Drain 1 (11 ounce) can of mandarin oranges and 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple really well so the salad doesn't turn watery. Let them sit in a strainer for a minute while you get the creamy ingredients ready.
The fruit is draining. What should I pull from the fridge or freezer next?
You'll need 3 1/2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, plus 2 cups shredded coconut. Also set out the marshmallows and milk called for in the mixing step, and have cherries ready for the garnish.
The whipped topping is thawed. Should I stir the fruit first or add everything together?
Add the drained mandarin oranges and crushed pineapple to the large bowl, then spoon in the thawed whipped topping. Fold gently so the orange segments stay mostly intact.
It's looking creamy. When do the coconut, marshmallows, and milk go in?
Add the shredded coconut, marshmallows, and milk now. Fold everything together until the coconut and marshmallows are evenly coated and the fruit is spread throughout the whipped topping.
How much mixing is enough? I don't want to crush the oranges.
Stop once the mixture looks evenly combined and fluffy. Use a spatula and broad folding motions rather than pressing or beating it.
It's mixed. Does it need to chill before I serve it with dinner?
Yes, cover the bowl and chill it for 1 hour before serving. That gives the coconut time to soften a bit and lets the salad set up.
After the 1 hour chill, should I do anything besides scoop it into a serving bowl?
Give it a gentle fold, transfer it to your serving dish if you like, and garnish the top with cherries just before serving.
I want to make Dutch Cream Waffles. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got a large bowl and a hand mixer out.
Absolutely. Start by setting out the dry ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need the separated eggs: 3 egg yolks and 3 egg whites.
The flour and salt are measured. Should I put them together right away or wait until the eggs are ready?
Go ahead and combine the flour and salt in the large mixing bowl now. Give them a quick stir so the salt is evenly mixed through the flour.
Done. For the eggs, I have the yolks in a small bowl and the whites set aside. What happens with the yolks?
Use the small mixing bowl with the yolks. Beat the egg yolks on low speed while adding the cream.
I'm adding the cream slowly while the mixer is on low. How long should I keep beating it?
Keep it going for 1 minute. Stay on low and aim for an even mixture rather than trying to whip it.
It's been about a minute and the yolk mixture looks smooth. Do I pour it into the flour bowl now?
Yes, add the yolk-and-cream mixture to the flour and salt. Start mixing on low speed so the flour doesn't puff out of the bowl.
The dry flour is mostly incorporated. Should I turn the mixer up yet?
Once the mixture is combined, increase to medium-high and beat until the batter looks smooth.
The batter is smoothing out. The egg whites are still separate; should I do anything with them at this point?
For the steps we're following, keep the separated egg whites aside for now. You've completed the listed mixing sequence once the batter is smooth after beating on medium-high.
I'm making Apple Cranberry Crisp 2 and I've got a pile of apples on the counter. Can you guide me through it while I prep?
Absolutely. Start by peeling, coring, and thinly slicing 2 pounds of Granny Smith apples. Keep 3/4 cup cranberries nearby too, since they'll go into the fruit mixture with the apples.
The apples are sliced and the cranberries are measured. What baking dish and oven setup do I need before mixing?
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it heats, butter an 8 inch square baking dish so the crisp won't stick.
Oven is heating, and the dish is buttered. I have white sugar and cinnamon out—how much goes in with the fruit?
Use 1/4 cup white sugar and 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon. Add them to a large bowl with the sliced apples and cranberries.

Yes, get the apples, cranberries, white sugar, and cinnamon combined in the large bowl. If you're following the card exactly, it says to mix in nutmeg too, but it doesn't give a quantity, so don't guess unless you already have a preferred amount.
I mixed the fruit gently so the apple slices stayed intact. Should it look evenly coated before it goes into the pan?
Yes. The apple slices and cranberries should be fairly evenly coated with the sugar and cinnamon mixture, with no big dry patches of spice sitting in the bowl.
It looks coated now. Do I dump it in or arrange it somehow in the 8 inch dish?
Transfer the fruit mixture into the buttered baking dish and spread it evenly, pushing it into the corners so the layer bakes consistently.
Fruit is in the dish. I still have the mixing bowl—what do I do with the topping ingredients?
Use that same bowl and combine the oats, flour, and brown sugar. Once they're mixed together, you'll have the dry topping base ready to go over the fruit.

Can you help me make Eggnog II? I've got a saucepan out, but I want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. For this Eggnog II, you'll need 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The eggs are beaten, and I measured the milk. Should the sugar go in right away?
Yes. Put the beaten eggs, the 2 1/4 cups milk, and the 1/3 cup white sugar into a large saucepan together.
They're in the pan. Do I whisk before heating, or just start cooking?
Stir them together in the saucepan, then set the pan over medium heat. Keep stirring as it cooks so the mixture heats evenly.
I'm stirring over medium heat now. What change am I looking for in the texture?
Cook and stir until the mixture coats a metal spoon. It should cling lightly to the spoon instead of running off like plain milk.

Place the pan in the sink or bowl of ice water, and stir the eggnog for 1 to 2 minutes to cool it quickly.

Make sure the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract is measured and ready with the rest of the ingredients. The cooked mixture should now be cooled quickly from the ice-water stirring step.
Can you guide me through making Black Bean Chili? I've got a large saucepan out and want to prep as I go.
Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 chopped onion, 2 red bell peppers that are seeded and chopped, and 1 jalapeno pepper that's seeded and minced.
The onion and peppers are chopped. Should I start heating the pan before I deal with the jalapeno?
Go ahead and heat the 1 tablespoon olive oil in the large saucepan over medium-high heat. While it warms, mince the seeded jalapeno so it's ready to add with the other vegetables.
The oil is hot and the jalapeno is minced. Do the onion and peppers go in together?
Yes. Add the onion, red bell peppers, and jalapeno to the saucepan. Add the mushrooms, tomatoes, and corn as well, then saute everything for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
I added the vegetables. What should I be looking for during those 10 minutes?
Watch for the onion to turn translucent. The peppers should soften a bit, and the mixture should smell cooked rather than raw.
The onions are mostly translucent and there's some liquid from the tomatoes. Is it time for the spices?
Yes. Season the vegetables with black pepper, cumin, and chili powder, then stir well so the spices coat the mixture evenly.
The spices are mixed in and it smells good. What ingredients go in after that?
Stir in the black beans, chicken broth, and salt. Scrape the bottom of the saucepan as you stir so the seasoned vegetables blend into the broth.
Everything is combined now. Should I keep the heat where it is or lower it?

Once the black beans, chicken broth, and salt are stirred in, keep it moving until the chili is evenly mixed, then adjust the heat as needed so it stays at a steady, gentle simmer rather than boiling hard.

Measure out 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.

Yes. Layer the ingredients in the jar in the order listed: white sugar, unsweetened cocoa powder, all-purpose flour, then chopped pecans.

That's a good idea. Wipe the inside rim gently so the layers look neat, then add the 1 cup all-purpose flour over the cocoa.

Great. Secure the lid snugly so the layers stay in place, especially if you're giving the jar as a gift or moving it around.

Attach a tag that includes this instruction: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Tag is tied on, and the jar is sealed. Is there anything else from the recipe I should include?
That covers the recipe's listed steps: the ingredients are layered in the 1 quart or 1 liter jar, and the tag includes the oven preheat instruction of 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Can you guide me through making a Cold Cocoa Smoothie? I've got my blender out and want to keep it nice and cold.

Yes. Start by chilling a large glass if you haven't already. For the smoothie, set out 1 1/2 scoops vanilla ice cream, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1/4 cup whipped cream, and 2 tablespoons instant hot chocolate mix.
The glass is in the freezer. My ice cream is a little soft—should I measure it now or wait?
A little soft is fine for blending. Measure the 1 1/2 scoops now, and keep the milk cold until you pour it into the blender.
Milk and ice cream are ready. I also have the whipped cream and hot chocolate mix on the counter. Anything else before blending?
If you're using crushed cookies, have them ready too. Add the ice cream, milk, whipped cream, instant hot chocolate mix, and crushed cookies to the blender jar.
Everything is in the blender, but some cocoa mix is clinging near the top of the jar.
That's okay. Put the lid on tightly, start blending, then pause after a few seconds and scrape down the sides if the dry mix is still stuck.
I scraped it down. How long should I keep blending?
Blend until the smoothie looks smooth and evenly cocoa-colored. It should pour easily, with no dry pockets of hot chocolate mix or big ice cream lumps.
It looks creamy now, with just a few tiny cookie bits. The chilled glass is ready.
That texture is right. Pour the smoothie into the large chilled glass, using a spatula if you want to get the last bit from the blender.
It's poured. Should I do anything else before serving or cleaning up?
Serve it right away while it's cold. For easier cleanup, rinse the blender jar and lid now before the cocoa and cream dry onto them.

Can you walk me through Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic? I'm getting the lamb out now.

messages.content: Can you guide me through making Cabbage Kielbasa Supper in the slow cooker? I'm setting up the counter now.

Absolutely. You'll need a 5-qt. slow cooker. Start by getting 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2 inch cubes, 1 medium onion chopped, and 1 3/4 teaspoons salt. Keep pepper, broth, and sausage nearby too, since they're used as you assemble it.
The cabbage is shredded, and I'm cutting the potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes. Does the slow cooker really hold all of this?
It will be very full at the start, but that's expected. The cabbage cooks down a lot during the long cook, so pack it in gently rather than pressing it hard.
Potatoes are ready, onion is chopped, and I measured the 1 3/4 teaspoons salt. What goes into the crock first?
Add the shredded cabbage, cubed potatoes, chopped onion, salt, and pepper directly into the 5-qt. slow cooker. Give the vegetables a light toss so the salt and pepper are distributed.
Everything's in the slow cooker, but the cabbage is mounded up. Should I stir again before adding liquid?
A quick gentle mix is fine, just enough to make the potatoes and onion less clumped. Then pour the broth over all of it so it can work its way down through the cabbage.
The broth is poured in and I can see it settling toward the bottom. Where does the kielbasa go?
Place the sausage on top of the cabbage mixture. Leave it sitting there rather than burying it; the slow cooker may look packed, but the cabbage will soften and shrink as it cooks.
The sausage is on top and the lid fits. What setting and how long?
Cover it and cook on low for 8-9 hours. It's ready when the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.
If I check it near the end, what texture am I looking for in the potatoes and cabbage?

The potatoes should be easily pierced with a fork, and the cabbage should be tender and wilted down rather than crunchy. Once the sausage is hot all the way through, you can serve it straight from the slow cooker.
Can you guide me through making Chocolate Madeleines? I've got a madeleine pan out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Set up the dry ingredients first: measure 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
The flour and cocoa are measured. Should I mix them right away or heat the oven first?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it heats, you can finish setting up the pan and dry mix.
Oven is heating. The madeleine pan looks clean but dry—what should I do to it?
Butter one madeleine pan well, getting into each shell-shaped cavity so the cakes release cleanly after baking.
Pan is buttered. I've measured the baking powder and salt now too—how should the dry ingredients look?
Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together. You're aiming for an even, fine mixture with no cocoa lumps.
I'm seeing a few cocoa clumps in the sifter. Should I press them through?
Yes, gently press any soft cocoa clumps through the sifter. If any bits feel hard or gritty, discard those rather than forcing them in.
The dry bowl is smooth now. What do I do with the butter, vanilla, and sugar?
Cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until the mixture looks lighter and smoother. Use a spoon, spatula, or mixer—whatever gives you a soft, well-blended base.
It's creamy and lighter in color. Is that the point where I stop, or should it be fluffy?

Stop once it's evenly creamed, smooth, and a bit lighter. You've completed the recipe's prep sequence: oven at 375 degrees F/190 degrees C, pan buttered, dry ingredients sifted, and butter creamed with vanilla and sugar.
Can you help me make Figs with Goat Cheese Pecans and Bacon? I'm setting out the ingredients now.
Absolutely. Put 6 figs on the board and halve them, then have 6 ounces goat cheese nearby so it's easy to fill the centers.

You'll also need 1/2 cup toasted, chopped pecans and 3 slices bacon, with each slice cut in half. Keep toothpicks close too, since they'll hold the wrapped figs together.
I've got the pecans, bacon halves, and toothpicks ready. Should I heat anything before assembling?
Yes, preheat the broiler now so it's ready by the time the figs are stuffed and wrapped.
The broiler is heating. The fig halves look pretty small—how much goat cheese should I use?
Spoon or press goat cheese into each fig half, using the 6 ounces across all the halves. Aim for a filled center without piling it so high that the bacon can't wrap around it.
They're filled. Do the pecans go on top or mixed into the cheese?
Press the toasted, chopped pecans directly into the goat cheese on each fig half. A gentle push helps them stick instead of falling off when you wrap the bacon.
The pecans are sticking pretty well. How do I wrap them neatly with the bacon?
Take one half slice of bacon for each stuffed fig half, wrap it around the fig, and secure it with a toothpick so the cheese and pecans stay tucked in.
All the figs are wrapped and pinned. Anything I should check before they go under the broiler?
Make sure each toothpick is holding firmly and the bacon seam is secured. The recipe's prep is complete once every stuffed fig half is wrapped with half a slice of bacon and held with toothpicks.

messages.content: Can you help me make Baked Pork Chops Low Fat Version? I've got 6 center cut pork chops out, and I trimmed off the visible fat.

Use 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/2 teaspoon seasoning salt. Rinse the pork chops, pat them dry well, then season them with the garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste.

Yes. Put the beaten egg and egg substitute mixture in a small bowl. You'll also want flour for a light dredge and bread crumbs ready for the outside coating.

Keep the flour layer light. Dredge each pork chop just enough to coat the surface, then shake off any excess so the egg can cling evenly.

Yes, dip each floured chop into the egg mixture and coat both sides. Let any extra drip back into the bowl before moving to the bread crumbs.

Coat them liberally with bread crumbs, pressing gently so the crumbs stick across the full surface of each pork chop.
They're breaded and ready. Is there anything else from the recipe before they go in the oven?

You've covered the listed prep: oven at 350 degrees F, pork chops rinsed and patted dry, seasoned with garlic powder and seasoning salt, dipped through flour and egg, then coated well with bread crumbs.

Start the pasta water: bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil.
The pot is heating now. When it boils, how long should the fettuccine cook?
Add the fettuccine and cook it for 8 to 10 minutes, until it's al dente, then drain it.
While the pasta cooks, can I get the meat going in the pan?
Yes. Put the lean ground beef in a large skillet and brown it over medium heat.
The beef is browned, but there's some fat in the skillet. What should I do before mixing anything else?
Drain the fat from the pan, then transfer the meat to a bowl.
The meat is in the bowl and the noodles are drained. Where does that leave my fresh stem topping?
Keep that topping uncooked for this version: the finely diced tender stems can stay in the dressing, with the leaves separate until serving.
I want to make Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats. I've already baked the potatoes—can you guide me from there?
Absolutely. Set your oven to 375 degrees F so it's heating while you prep the potato skins.
Oven is on. I have 4 medium baked potatoes on the board—how should I cut them?
Quarter each potato lengthwise, so you end up with long boat-shaped pieces that can hold the filling.
They're quartered, but the centers are still fluffy. Do I remove all of the potato?
Scoop the potato out of the skins gently, leaving the skins intact so they keep their shape.
Skins are holding together. Where does the Ranch go?
Use 1/3 cup Hidden Valley Original Ranch Salad Dressing to coat the inside of the potato skins.
The Ranch is brushed inside. Do I put the scooped potato back in now?
Yes, place the potato back into the coated skins, spreading it so the boats are evenly filled.
They're filled and sitting on a baking sheet. How much cheese should I use?
Sprinkle 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese over the potato boats, dividing it across the pieces.
I also have sliced green onions. Should those go on before serving?
Yes, add sliced green onions if you'd like that fresh topping. Once the Cheddar is on and the optional onions are added, the Cheesy Cheddar Potato Boats are assembled.
Can you help me make Easy Marinated Vegetables? I've got a pot, a colander, and a mixing bowl out.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 cups broccoli florets and 1 1/2 cups cauliflower florets, since those get a quick blanch before everything is mixed.
The broccoli and cauliflower are measured. What other vegetables should I prep before I turn on the stove?
Cut 1 green bell pepper into 1 inch pieces, and peel, seed, and chop 1 cucumber. You'll also want carrot and Italian salad dressing ready for the mixing bowl at the end.
The pepper is cut and the cucumber is peeled and chopped. Should I salt the water now?
Yes. Fill a large pot with water, add salt, and bring it to a boil. Keep the colander nearby so you can drain the florets quickly.
The water is boiling. Do the broccoli and cauliflower both go in together?
They do. Add the broccoli and cauliflower florets to the boiling water together and leave them in for 1 minute.
It's been 1 minute, and the florets look brighter. What texture am I aiming for?
They should be just lightly blanched, not soft. Drain them right away, then rinse the florets to cool them down and stop the cooking.
They're drained and rinsed. Should I dry them off before mixing?
Let them drain well and shake off extra water so the dressing can coat the vegetables instead of getting diluted.
The bowl is ready with the pepper and cucumber. How do I put everything together?
Add the broccoli, cauliflower, carrot, and Italian salad dressing to the medium size mixing bowl with the bell pepper and cucumber. Toss until the vegetables are evenly coated.
Can you help me make Aaahh Potato Soup? I've got a large pot out and want to make sure I'm not missing anything.
Absolutely. Set out 2 Yukon Gold potatoes, cubed; 1 (5.5 ounce) package au gratin instant potato mix; 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed chicken broth; and 1 1/2 cups water.
The potatoes are cubed, and I found the au gratin mix and broth. Should everything go in the pot together?
Yes. Add the cubed potatoes, the au gratin potato mix, the condensed chicken broth, and the 1 1/2 cups water to the large saucepan or pot.
It looks a little shallow around the potatoes. Do they need to be fully covered?
If the liquid doesn't cover the potatoes, add a bit more water until they're covered enough to cook evenly.
Okay, they're covered now. What heat should I use so the potatoes soften without sticking?
Put the pot over medium heat. Stir occasionally as it cooks so the mix doesn't settle too much on the bottom.
How long should I plan for this part, and what texture am I looking for?
Cook until the potatoes are tender, about 40 minutes. They should pierce easily with a fork.
I'm about halfway through and the soup is thickening. Should I keep stirring the same way?
Yes, keep stirring now and then, especially along the bottom of the pot. If it thickens before the potatoes are tender, add a splash of water to keep it loose enough to simmer.
The potatoes are tender now. How do I finish it before serving?
Stir in the cream and heat it through gently. Once the soup is hot and smooth, it's ready to serve.
Can you help me make Broccoli Cheese Crepes? I'm setting up the blender and want to be sure I measure the batter ingredients right.
Absolutely. For the crepe batter, put 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt within reach.
I've got the eggs and water by the blender. Should the flour and salt go in with them right away?
Yes. Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to the blender together so the batter can mix evenly.
Everything is in the blender jar. Do I just pulse it, or run it longer?
Cover the blender and process the mixture until it looks smooth, with no dry flour streaks.
The batter looks smooth now. Is it ready for the pan immediately?
Let the batter stand for 15 minutes before cooking the crepes. That resting time helps it settle.
While it rests, I can start the filling. I have a small saucepan out—what goes in first?
Use the small saucepan to saute the onion in butter until the onion is tender.
The onion is soft and smells sweet. Do I add more flour here too?
Stir in flour until it is blended into the butter and onion mixture.
It's blended in and there aren't any dry patches. Should I keep stirring for the texture?
Yes, keep it moving just until the flour is fully incorporated and the mixture looks even, then you're ready for the next filling step.
Can you guide me through Garlic Chicken Stir Fry? I've got a wok out and want to prep before the heat is on.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep the chicken nearby too, since it goes in once the aromatics have cooked.
I minced all 6 cloves of garlic, but I notice the cooking step mentions only 2 cloves at the start. Should I add just that amount when the oil is hot?
Yes, for the hot-oil step, quickly stir in 2 cloves of the minced garlic with the grated ginger, chopped green onions, and salt once the peanut oil begins to smoke.
Got it. How hot should I let the wok get before adding anything?
Pour in the 2 tablespoons peanut oil and heat it in the wok or a large skillet until the oil just begins to smoke. Have the garlic, ginger, green onions, and salt ready so they can go in right away.
The oil is at that point, and the aromatics are beside the stove. Do I stir constantly?
Yes, stir quickly as soon as you add the 2 cloves minced garlic, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt. Keep everything moving so the garlic doesn't burn.
The green onions are in and softening. What texture am I looking for before the chicken goes in?
Stir fry until the onion turns translucent, which should take about 2 minutes. The mixture should smell fragrant, but the garlic should not be deeply browned.
It's been about 2 minutes and the onions look translucent. I'm ready with the chicken.
Add the chicken to the wok now and stir it through the aromatics. Keep it moving until the pieces turn opaque, about 3 minutes.
After 3 minutes the chicken looks opaque. Is there anything else from the recipe before serving?

That completes the listed cooking steps for Garlic Chicken Stir Fry: oil heated, aromatics stir-fried until translucent, and chicken stirred until opaque. Give the pan a final toss, then serve it hot.
Can you guide me through making Flavorful Rice Dressing 2? I'm setting up the counter now.
Absolutely. Put a large bowl and a skillet within reach. For the bread base, you'll need 7 slices of day-old bread, torn, plus 1 cup of torn corn bread.
The breads are torn up. Should they go straight into the large bowl together?
Yes, add both breads to the large bowl. Keep 2/3 cup hot water nearby, because you'll lightly toss the bread with that water rather than soaking it heavily.
I've added the hot water and tossed it gently. It looks damp but not mushy.
That sounds right. Next, get 1/2 cup thinly sliced celery ready for the skillet, along with the onion, mushrooms, and oil called for in the cooking step.
The celery is sliced thin, and I have the skillet out. How should I cook the vegetables?
Heat the oil in the skillet, then add the celery, onion, and mushrooms. Sauté them until tender, stirring constantly so they soften evenly and don't catch on the pan.
They're softening, but I'm not sure when to stop. What should I look for?
Stop when the celery has lost its raw crunch and the onion and mushrooms look tender. Since the recipe says to stir constantly, keep them moving until that point.
The vegetables are tender now. Do I pour them over the bread mixture?
Yes. Scrape the sautéed celery, onion, and mushrooms into the bowl with the bread mixture, then stir everything together so the vegetables are distributed through the bread.
It's combined in the bowl. What's the last thing I need to do before it's ready for the next stage?
Add the remaining ingredients for the dressing and mix well. Aim for an evenly moistened mixture with the bread, corn bread, vegetables, and seasonings fully worked together.
Can you guide me through Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style? I've got a whole spaghetti squash on the counter and want to make sure I prep it right.
Absolutely. Start by halving 1 spaghetti squash lengthwise and scooping out the seeds. You'll also want 1 onion chopped and ready nearby.
The squash is halved and seeded, and the onion is chopped. What other ingredients should I pull out before I heat the oven?
Set out 2 tablespoons minced garlic and 2 (14 ounce) cans stewed tomatoes. Once those are ready, you'll have the listed ingredients covered.
Garlic and the 14 ounce cans of tomatoes are on the counter. What temperature should I set the oven to?
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C. Give it a few minutes to come up to temperature while you prep the pan.
The oven is heating. I'm using a rimmed baking sheet—does it need anything before the squash goes on?
Yes, spray the baking sheet with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash doesn't stick while it bakes.
The sheet is lightly sprayed. Should the squash sit cut side up or down?
Place the squash halves cut side down on the baking sheet. That position helps the flesh steam and soften evenly.
Both halves are cut side down. How long should I bake them?
Bake the squash for 35 minutes in the preheated oven. Check it at that point by sliding in a knife; it should insert easily when the squash is ready.
If the knife still meets resistance after 35 minutes, should I pull it anyway or keep baking?
Keep baking a little longer if needed, checking again until a knife can be easily inserted. Once it's tender, take the baking sheet out carefully and let the squash sit briefly before handling.
Can you guide me through making Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms? I'm setting up my cutting board now.
Absolutely. Get 1 tablespoon unsalted butter ready, then dice 2 cups of Broccoflower. You'll also want a wide pan or skillet for the sauté and risotto.
The Broccoflower is diced. I've got a mix of mushrooms too—how much should I chop, and what about onion?
Chop 2 cups assorted wild mushrooms, and finely chop 1/2 white onion. Keep them near the stove because they'll go into the butter together.
Mushrooms and onion are prepped. Do I start with medium heat, and does everything go in at once?
Melt the butter in the pan, then sauté the diced Broccoflower, chopped wild mushrooms, onion, and garlic together for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally so the vegetables soften evenly.
They've cooked down and the mushrooms have released some moisture. Should I leave them in the pan for the rice?
Scoop the sautéed vegetables out of the pan and set them aside for now. Leave any flavorful bits in the same pan for the rice.
The pan is cleared except for the browned bits. How do I handle the stock so the risotto doesn't get soupy?
Add the rice to that same pan, then begin adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time. Stir until each cup is well incorporated and mostly absorbed before adding the next cup.
I'm stirring in the stock gradually. How will I know when to stop adding it?
Keep going until the chicken stock is absorbed and the rice is tender. The risotto should look creamy from stirring, not watery, with the grains soft but still holding their shape.
The rice is tender now. I have the cooked vegetables waiting—what's the last seasoning step?

Stir the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic back in if they aren't already combined, then add nutmeg and herbs. Season with salt and pepper, taste, and serve the risotto while it's warm and creamy.
Can you guide me through making Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs? I've got mushrooms on the counter but want to make sure I don't miss anything.

Absolutely. You'll need 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 chopped green onions, and 1 clove garlic, crushed. The cooking also calls for cayenne pepper when the vegetables go into the pan.
The mushrooms are chopped, and I have the green onions and garlic ready. Should I turn on the oven before starting the pan?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, so it's hot when you need it.
Oven is heating. What size pan should I use for the mushroom mixture?
Use a medium saucepan. Set it over medium heat and add the 2 tablespoons olive oil.
The oil is in the saucepan over medium heat. Do the mushrooms go in alone or with the aromatics?
Add the mushrooms together with the chopped green onions, crushed garlic, and cayenne pepper. Stir everything so the oil coats the vegetables evenly.
They're all in and stirred. The pan looks pretty full with the 3 cups of mushrooms—should I keep stirring constantly?
You don't need to stir nonstop. Stir often enough to keep the garlic from sticking and to help the mushrooms cook down evenly.
How long should I cook this mixture, and what should it look like when it's ready?
Cook it for 10 minutes, or until the mushrooms and onions are tender. The mushrooms should soften and release some moisture as they cook.
It's been about 10 minutes and the mushrooms are tender. Should I take it off the heat now?
Yes, if the mixture is tender, take the saucepan off the heat. You've completed the mushroom filling stage for the Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs.
Can you help me make E Z Cheezy Pie? I've got a mixer out, but I want to make sure I'm not missing anything before I start.
Absolutely. Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells and 3 packages of cream cheese, 8 ounces each. Let the cream cheese be softened so it whips smoothly instead of staying lumpy.
The baked shells are on the counter, and the cream cheese feels soft. What else goes into the filling?
You'll also need 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Those are the only other ingredients for this recipe.
Good, I measured the sugar and vanilla. Should the oven be on even though the pie shells are already baked?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready while you mix the cream cheese filling.
The oven is heating. What bowl should I use for the cream cheese?
Use a medium mixing bowl. Add the softened cream cheese and whip it until it looks fluffy and lighter in texture.
It's whipped up and looks softer, but I still see a couple of thick spots near the side of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides, then whip briefly again so the cream cheese is evenly fluffy before you add anything else.
That helped. Do I add the sugar and vanilla together or one at a time?
Add the 1/2 cup white sugar and the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the whipped cream cheese, then start mixing on a gentle speed so the sugar doesn't scatter.
Everything is in the bowl now. How smooth should it be before I stop mixing?

Mix until the filling is smooth, with no visible streaks of cream cheese, sugar pockets, or unmixed vanilla. Once it's smooth, the recipe's mixing step is complete and the filling is ready for the baked pie shells.
Can you guide me through making Cinnamon Crackle Cookies? I'm getting the mixer and baking sheets out.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening so they're ready to cream smoothly.
Both are in the mixing bowl. Do the sugars go in with them right away?
Yes. Add 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to the bowl with the butter and shortening.
I've added the sugars. How long should I mix this before adding anything else?
Cream the butter, shortening, and sugars until the mixture looks combined and lighter, with no big streaks of butter or shortening left.
It looks fluffy and evenly mixed now. What should I add next?
Add the egg and the extracts, then mix well so they're fully worked into the creamed mixture.
The wet mixture is smooth. I have the dry ingredients nearby, but I'm not sure how to work them in.
Combine the next eight ingredients in a separate bowl, then add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture so the dough comes together evenly.
The dough is mixed and a little soft. Should I prep the pan before shaping?
Yes, use ungreased baking sheets. Keep a small bowl of sugar nearby for rolling the dough.
The baking sheets are ready and the sugar bowl is out. What size should each cookie be?
Shape the dough into 1-in balls, roll each one in sugar, and place them apart on the ungreased baking sheets.
Can you help me make Apple Blueberry Tarts? I've peeled, cored, and chopped 2 medium cooking apples and I'm checking what else to set out.

Yes. Put the chopped apples near a medium bowl, and measure 2/3 cup fresh or frozen blueberries. You'll also need 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute and 1/2 teaspoon apple pie spice or ground allspice.
I've got fresh blueberries and apple pie spice. Do I use all the spice with the fruit?
Use 1/4 teaspoon of the apple pie spice in the fruit mixture. In the medium bowl, combine the apples, blueberries, sugar substitute, and that 1/4 teaspoon spice, then set the bowl aside.
The fruit is mixed and sitting aside. I have another bowl out for the dough—what goes in there?
In the second medium bowl, stir together the whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice. Mix just enough to distribute the salt and spice evenly through the flour.
The dry mixture looks even. Should I make a well before adding the liquids?
You can make a small well if it helps, but the key instruction is to add the oil and milk all at once to the flour mixture.
Oil and milk are in. I don't want to overwork the dough—what should I use to mix it?
Use a fork and stir lightly. Stop as soon as the dough comes together; it should look combined rather than heavily beaten or smooth.
There are a few dry-looking bits on the side of the bowl. Should I keep stirring?
Give it only a few gentle turns with the fork to pick up those bits. If the dough has come together, pause there so it stays tender.
Got it. Before I move on, can you recap the fruit bowl and dough bowl so I know I didn't miss anything?

Fruit bowl: 2 medium cooking apples, peeled, cored, and chopped; 2/3 cup blueberries; 1 tablespoon heat-stable granular sugar substitute; and 1/4 teaspoon apple pie spice from the 1/2 teaspoon you set out. Dough bowl: whole wheat pastry flour, kosher salt, and 1/8 teaspoon apple pie spice, with oil and milk added all at once, then stirred lightly with a fork until the dough comes together.
Can you guide me through making Chocolate Chews? I'm setting out a saucepan and mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. Put 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips by the stove, and have 1/2 cup softened butter ready at the bowl.
Chocolate chips and softened butter are ready. What sugars should I measure?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. Keep both near the butter so they're ready for creaming.
The sugars are measured. Do I start with the chocolate or the butter mixture?
Start with the chocolate. Add the semisweet chocolate chips to a heavy saucepan and melt them over very low heat.
They're in the saucepan. Should I leave them alone or stir right away?
Stir gently as they melt so the heat stays even and the chocolate becomes smooth instead of scorching.
The chocolate is smooth now. What should I do with the butter and sugars?
In the mixing bowl, cream the 1/2 cup softened butter with the 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar until the mixture looks light.
It's getting paler and fluffy. How light should it be before I stop?
Stop when the butter and sugars look evenly blended, lighter in color, and a bit airy rather than dense or grainy.
That looks right. What comes next with the eggs?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing each one in before adding the next.
Can you guide me through making Broccoli Cheese Crepes? I'm starting by getting the blender and measuring cups out.
Absolutely. For the crepe batter, set out 2 eggs, 1/4 cup water, 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've cracked the eggs and measured the water. Should the flour and salt go straight into the blender too?
Yes. Add the eggs, water, flour, and salt to the blender together so the batter can mix evenly.
Everything for the batter is in the blender. How smooth does it need to be?
Cover the blender and process until the batter looks smooth, with no obvious dry flour pockets or streaks.
It looks smooth now. Do I use it right away, or should it sit?
Let the batter stand for 15 minutes. That rest helps it settle before you cook the crepes.
While it rests, I'm moving to the filling or sauce part. What pan should I use for the onion?
Use a small saucepan. Add the butter and saute the onion in it until the onion is tender.
The onion is softening and smells good. Should I let it brown much?
Keep it focused on tender rather than deeply browned; gentle sauteing is enough for this step.
The onion is tender. What do I add before continuing with the cheese and broccoli later?
Stir in the flour until it's blended with the butter and onion, making sure there are no dry patches before you move on.
Can you guide me through making Broccoli Chicken Roli? I've got cooked chicken ready but haven't set up the rest yet.
Absolutely. Put 2 cups chopped, cooked chicken meat in reach, and get 2 cups fresh chopped broccoli ready beside it.
The chicken is chopped, and I'm cutting the broccoli now. What vegetables should I prep after that?
Chop 1/2 cup onion and 1/2 cup green bell pepper. Those will go into the same large mixing bowl with the chicken and broccoli.
Do I need a pan on the stove, or is this mainly mixed in a bowl first?
Start with a large bowl. Combine the chicken, broccoli, onions, green bell pepper, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and garlic in that bowl.
I'm adding the cheese and condiments now. Should the mixture be layered or fully blended?
Mix it all together until the chicken and vegetables are evenly coated and the cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, seasonings, and garlic are distributed throughout.
It looks evenly coated. Should I turn the oven on while I finish setting up the tray?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C.
Oven is heating. What kind of tray setup do you want?
Use a cookie sheet and cover it with aluminum foil so it's ready for the mixture and easier to clean up afterward.
Foil is on the cookie sheet. Anything I should check before moving the bowl over?
Give the mixture one more stir to make sure there are no dry pockets, then keep the foil-covered cookie sheet nearby for the next part of the recipe.
Can you guide me through making Bocconcini Salad? I'm pulling out a large salad bowl now.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound of bocconcini, the bite-size mozzarella balls, and 8 cherry tomatoes. Halve the tomatoes if they aren't already cut.
The mozzarella is drained, and the cherry tomatoes are halved. What other chopped vegetables should I prep?
Chop 1/2 cup green bell pepper and 1/2 cup celery. You'll also want endive and arugula ready for the bowl.
I've got the bell pepper and celery chopped. Should everything go into the bowl together?
Yes. Add the mozzarella, halved cherry tomatoes, green bell pepper, celery, endive, and arugula to the large salad bowl.
The bowl is full and looks colorful. Do I mix the dressing separately?
Whisk the lemon juice and olive oil together in a small bowl or measuring cup until they look combined.
The lemon juice and olive oil are whisked. Should I season the dressing or the salad?
Pour the dressing over the salad, then season the salad to taste with salt and pepper.
It's dressed and seasoned. How rough should I be when tossing it?
Toss gently but thoroughly, lifting from the bottom so all the mozzarella, vegetables, and greens get coated without crushing the tomatoes.
Everything is evenly coated. What's the best way to serve it?
Sprinkle basil over the top and serve the Bocconcini Salad immediately while the greens are fresh and the dressing is bright.
Can you help me make Cake Doughnuts? I'm checking what to put on the counter before I start mixing.

Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need cinnamon and nutmeg for the dry mix, plus milk, egg, butter, and vanilla for the wet ingredients.
I've measured the flour and sugar. Should the baking powder and salt go in with them right away?
Yes. Use a large bowl and stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and the nutmeg until the dry ingredients look evenly combined.
The dry ingredients are mixed. Do I need a separate bowl for the milk and egg?
For this recipe, you can keep working in the same large bowl. Make a well in the center of the dry mixture so the wet ingredients have a place to land.
The well is ready. Which wet ingredients go into it?
Pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into the well. Try to keep them mostly in the center at first so they're easier to pull into the flour mixture.
They're in the bowl. How much should I mix this dough?
Mix until everything is well blended. Scrape around the sides and bottom of the bowl so no dry pockets of flour remain.
It looks combined now, but it's soft. Is that okay before chilling?
Yes, a soft dough is fine here. Once it's well blended, cover the bowl tightly so it doesn't dry out in the refrigerator.
Covered. How long does it need to chill before I do anything else with it?
Refrigerate it for 1 hour. After that rest, the dough should be easier to handle for the next part of making the cake doughnuts.
I want to make Beet and Pear Puree. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Put 8 medium beets on the counter, along with 1 pound unsalted butter. You'll also need a roasting pan, a large skillet, and the oven.
The beets and butter are out. What produce should I prep besides the beets?
Prep 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, then peel, core, and mince 4 Bosc pears. Keep the onions and pears separate for the moment so they're easy to add when needed.
The onions are minced, and I'm working through the pears. Should I start heating the oven now?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C. That way it's ready when the beets are washed and in the pan.
Oven is heating. Do the beets need peeling before they roast?
For this step, just wash the beets well and place them in the roasting pan. The recipe has them roast whole before cooling.
They're washed and in the roasting pan. How long should I plan for them to be in the oven?
Bake the beets for 45 minutes to 1 hour, checking for tenderness near the end. They should yield easily when pierced.
They're tender after about an hour. Do I keep working with them while they're hot?
Set the roasted beets aside to cool before handling them further. While they cool, you can move over to the stovetop and get the skillet ready.
The skillet is on the burner. What heat should I use for the butter?

Use medium heat and melt the 1 pound unsalted butter in the large skillet. Once it's fully melted, you'll be ready for the next part of the puree process with the prepared onions, pears, and cooled beets.
Can you help me make Cranberry Apple Pie II? I'm clearing space and want to be sure I have the right fruit and filling ready.
Absolutely. For the filling, set out 6 apples and 1 (16 ounce) can of whole cranberry sauce. You'll also want your pie plate and pastry nearby so the dish is ready to line.
The apples and cranberry sauce are on the counter. What dry ingredients should I measure before I start peeling?
Measure 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour. Keep them close by for the filling mixture.
Those are measured. Should I turn on the oven before I start working with the apples?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can come up to temperature while you prep everything else.
Oven is heating. I've got the pie plate out, but the pastry is still wrapped.
Unwrap the pastry and line the pie plate with it, pressing it gently into the bottom and sides without stretching it too much.
The pastry is in the plate. For the apples, do I leave the skins on or prep them fully?
Prep them fully: peel, core, and slice the 6 apples. Try to keep the slices fairly even so they mix nicely with the cranberry sauce.
I'm slicing now. Is a medium bowl big enough, or should I grab something larger?
A medium-sized mixing bowl is what the recipe calls for. Use it to combine the sliced apples with the whole cranberry sauce.
The apples and cranberry sauce are in the bowl. Should I stir until it's completely uniform?
Stir gently until the apple slices are coated and the cranberry sauce is distributed through the bowl. You don't need to mash it smooth—just combine the fruit well for the pie filling.
Can you guide me through making Chocolate Covered Pretzels? I've got the counter cleared and some wax paper nearby.

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler or a heatproof bowl over a pan of gently simmering water.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips measured. Should the cream go in with the chocolate right away?
Yes. Add the 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream to the top of the double boiler. Keep the heat low so the chocolate melts gently.
The water is barely simmering. How often should I stir the chocolate?
Stir constantly while it melts. Keep scraping the bottom and sides so the chocolate and cream blend smoothly without scorching.
It's melted now and looks glossy. Is that the texture I want before dipping?
Yes, glossy and smooth is right. Keep the mixture very warm, because the pretzels need to be dipped quickly while the coating is still fluid.
Should I dump a handful of pretzels in, or coat them individually?
Dip the pretzels 1 at a time. Work quickly, coat each one in the warm chocolate mixture, then let the extra chocolate drip off before setting it down.
I'm placing them on the wax paper as I go. Do they need spacing?
Give them a little room on the wax paper so they don't stick together as the chocolate sets and cools.
The last pretzels are coated. What should I do before serving them?
Leave them on the wax paper until the chocolate has set and cooled. Once firm, lift them off gently and serve or pack them in a container.
I want to make German Chocolate Brownie Cookies. Can you guide me through the mixing without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I've got the brown sugar and shortening measured. Should the sugar be packed firmly into the cup?
Yes, pack the brown sugar firmly so it holds its shape when tipped out. Add it to the large bowl with the 2/3 cup shortening.
They're in the bowl. I also have the water and vanilla ready in measuring spoons.
Add the 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the same bowl, then cream everything together until the mixture looks evenly combined.
The mixture looks smooth and thick. I'm ready for the eggs.
Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture. Add them in and mix until they're fully incorporated, scraping the bowl if needed.
Eggs are mixed in. I have another bowl on the counter for the dry ingredients.
Use that second bowl to combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda. Stir or whisk them together so the cocoa and leavening are evenly distributed.
The dry bowl is mixed. Should I dump it all into the wet mixture at once?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix only until just blended. Stop once you no longer see dry streaks so the cookie dough doesn't get overworked.
It's just blended and the bowl sides are mostly clean. What should the texture look like here?
You're looking for a cohesive chocolate dough that's thick and evenly mixed, not beaten until fluffy. Once it reaches that point, the recipe's mixing steps are complete.
I want to make the Empanadas dough today. Can you talk me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put out 1/2 cup softened butter and 1 package of cream cheese, the 3 ounce size. Let them be soft enough to blend smoothly.
Those are on the counter. Is there anything else before I start mixing?
Yes—have 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour ready, plus 1 cup fruit preserves for filling later.
I've got the flour sifted and the preserves nearby. What bowl should I use for the dough?
Use a medium mixing bowl with enough room to cream the butter and cream cheese together without spilling over the sides.
Okay, the butter and cream cheese are in the bowl. What texture am I aiming for?
Cream them together until they look smoothly blended, with no obvious streaks of butter or cream cheese.
It's smooth now. Do I add the flour all at once?
Beat in the flour until it's incorporated into the butter-cream cheese mixture and forms a workable dough.
The dough has come together. It's a little soft—should I shape it anyway?
Yes. Shape it into a smooth ball, then wrap it well in foil or cling wrap so it doesn't dry out in the refrigerator.
Wrapped and ready. How long does it need to chill before I use the preserves?
Refrigerate the wrapped dough overnight, or up to a week. At baking time, take it out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using so it can soften slightly.
Can you guide me through making Flax and Sunflower Seed Bread in my bread machine? I want to get everything measured before I start.

Absolutely. Set out 1 1/3 cups water, 2 tablespoons softened butter, 3 tablespoons honey, and 1 1/2 cups bread flour. You'll also need the sunflower seeds ready to add later when the machine beeps during kneading.
I've got the water measured and the butter softened. Should I put them into the bread pan right away?

Yes, if that matches your bread machine's recommended order. The recipe says to place all ingredients except the sunflower seeds into the bread machine pan in the manufacturer's order, so follow your machine's liquid-and-dry sequence.
My machine wants liquids first, so I added the water. Does the honey go in with the wet ingredients?
That's fine. Add the 3 tablespoons honey with the liquids, then add the 2 tablespoons softened butter as your machine's order directs.
The butter and honey are in. I'm about to add the flour—anything I should watch for?
Add the 1 1/2 cups bread flour carefully so it lands evenly in the pan. Keep the sunflower seeds out for now; they don't go in at the start.
The pan is loaded except for the seeds. Which setting should I choose?
Select the basic white cycle on the bread machine, then press start.
It's running. I'm staying nearby for the alert—when exactly do the sunflower seeds go in?
Add the sunflower seeds when the alert sounds during the knead cycle. That timing helps them mix in without getting overworked from the beginning.
The beep just sounded and I added the seeds. Do I need to stir anything by hand?
No hand-stirring should be needed. Close the lid and let the bread machine continue the basic white cycle until the loaf is done.
I want to make Chocolate Madeleines today. Can you guide me through without assuming I know the order?
Absolutely. Set out the dry ingredients first: 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
I've got the flour and cocoa measured. Should the oven be heating while I finish the rest?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is prepared.
Oven is on. I'm using a Madeleine pan—does it need anything before the batter?
Butter one Madeleine pan, getting into the shell-shaped grooves so the cakes release cleanly.
Pan is buttered. For the dry mix, do I just stir everything together in a bowl?
Use a sifter if you can: sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together so the cocoa breaks up and the baking powder is evenly spread.
The cocoa had a few lumps, but sifting fixed it. What should the butter mixture be like?
Cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until the mixture looks smooth and a little lighter. That gives the batter a better texture.
I don't see amounts for the butter, vanilla, or sugar in what I have. Should I pause there?

Yes, pause before mixing further if those amounts aren't listed in your recipe source. The steps we can follow confidently are the measured dry ingredients, the 375 degrees F oven, buttering the pan, sifting the dry mixture, and creaming butter with vanilla and sugar once you have their quantities.
That makes sense. Can I at least prep the workspace while I check the missing amounts?
Definitely. Keep the sifted dry ingredients covered, leave the buttered Madeleine pan ready, and clear space for the butter, vanilla, and sugar once you confirm the amounts.
Can you talk me through making a Cosmopolitan? I've got a shaker and cocktail glass ready.
Absolutely. Set out the vodka, cointreau, fresh lime juice, cranberry juice, plenty of ice, and a lime twist for garnish.
I have vodka and cointreau on the counter. How much of each goes in?
Measure 1 jigger of vodka, which is 1.5 fluid ounces, and add 1/2 fluid ounce cointreau to the shaker.
Got those measured. What should I do for the lime and cranberry?
Add 1 teaspoon fresh lime juice and 1 1/2 fluid ounces cranberry juice to the same shaker.
Everything is in the shaker except the ice. Should I fill it a little or a lot?
Use lots of ice so the drink chills quickly while you shake it. Add the ice right over all the ingredients.
Ice is in. How hard and how long should I shake?
Seal the shaker firmly and shake vigorously for several seconds, just until the outside feels cold.
The shaker is cold now. Do I pour everything into the glass?
Strain the drink into the cocktail glass so the ice stays behind in the shaker.
It's strained and looks good. What's the final touch before serving?
Garnish it with a lime twist and serve the Cosmopolitan right away while it's cold.
Can you guide me through making Baked Apple Oatmeal? I've got a 2-qt. casserole dish out already.
Absolutely. Grease that 2-qt. casserole so it's ready for later, and set your oven to 350 degrees F when you're ready to bake.
Dish is greased. What should I measure for the saucepan?

Measure 4 cups milk, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, 2 teaspoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt into a saucepan. The recipe also has cinnamon in that heating step, so have it nearby if it's part of what you're using.
Those are in the pan. Should the milk boil, or just warm up?
Heat the milk mixture gently, stirring as the brown sugar dissolves and the butter melts. You're warming it together rather than trying to boil it hard.
It's hot and the sugar looks dissolved. I still have the rest of the oatmeal ingredients waiting.
Add the remaining ingredients to the saucepan mixture, then stir gently so everything is evenly moistened without mashing it up.
The mixture is combined, but it's pretty loose. Is that expected before baking?
Yes, that's fine for baked oatmeal at this stage. Spoon the mixture into your greased 2-qt. casserole and spread it out evenly.
It's in the casserole. Do I bake it uncovered so the top browns?
For this recipe, cover the casserole before baking. Put it in the 350 degrees F oven and bake for 45 minutes.
After 45 minutes, what should I look for before serving?
It should look set and absorbed rather than soupy. Let it stand briefly after baking so it scoops more cleanly, then serve it warm.
Can you help me make French Apple Cream Pie? I've got a 9 inch pie pan out and want to make sure I set everything up in the right order.

Absolutely. For this pie, have ready 1 recipe pastry for a 9 inch double crust pie and 1 (21 ounce) can apple pie filling. You'll also need 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg.
The pastry and apple filling are on the counter. Should the oven be heating while I measure the spices?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 425 degrees F, which is 220 degrees C. While it heats, measure the 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg.
Oven is set to 425. The pastry feels a little soft from sitting out—what should I do with it before it goes in the pan?
Roll out the pastry shell, then let it rest in the refrigerator. Chilling it briefly will make it easier to handle and help it hold its shape when you line the pan.
I rolled it out and it's chilling now. Do I use both crusts right away or just one for the pan?
Use one rolled-out pastry crust to line the 9 inch pie pan. Ease it into the pan rather than stretching it, so it sits flat against the bottom and sides.
The bottom crust is in the pan. I have the apple pie filling open—do I mix the spices straight into the can?
Transfer the apple pie filling to a medium mixing bowl first. Then stir in the cinnamon and nutmeg so the spices distribute evenly through the filling.
I noticed the directions mention lemon rind too. Should that go into the same bowl with the filling and spices?
Yes. In the medium mixing bowl, combine the pie filling, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon rind together. Stir gently so the apple pieces stay intact while everything gets evenly coated.
The filling is mixed and the crust is lined. Anything I should check before moving on from prep?

Check that the crust is seated neatly in the 9 inch pan, the oven is still at 425 degrees F / 220 degrees C, and the filling is evenly mixed with the 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg, and lemon rind.
Can you help me make Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles? I've got chicken out but want to make sure I'm not missing anything.
Absolutely. For the full recipe, you'll need 2 teaspoons olive oil, 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves, 1 (10 ounce) can refrigerated large crescent roll dough, and 8 ounces Brie cheese.
I have the olive oil, chicken, crescent dough, and Brie. Should I use a skillet or a nonstick pan for the chicken?
Either works. Heat the olive oil in a heavy skillet, or if you're using a nonstick frying pan, you can spray it with cooking spray instead.
The pan is heating now. Do I add all 4 chicken breast halves at once?
Add the chicken breasts in a single layer if they fit without crowding. Sauté them until they're no longer pink and the juices run clear.
How do I know when they're ready to come out of the pan?
Cut into the thickest part of one piece or check the juices from the chicken. Once there's no pink remaining and the juices run clear, take the chicken out and set it aside.
Chicken is set aside. Should I start heating the oven now or wait until the dough is opened?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's ready when you've assembled the bundles.
Oven is preheating. The crescent dough says large rolls—how many am I using?
Unroll 4 large crescent rolls from the refrigerated dough. Keep them as intact as you can so they'll be easier to wrap around the chicken and Brie.
The dough is unrolled. Where does the Brie come in?

Use the 8 ounces Brie cheese with the cooked chicken as you assemble the bundles on the 4 crescent rolls. Once the chicken is no longer pink, the juices have run clear, the oven is at 375 degrees F, and the rolls are unrolled, you're set up for the next assembly step.
Can you guide me through making Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes? I've got a pot ready but haven't started yet.
Absolutely. Set out 1 recipe Fast Chicken Soup Base, a 9 ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, a 14.5 ounce can of diced tomatoes, and 2 medium zucchini.
I have the soup base and tortellini. Should I dice the zucchini before heating anything?
Yes, dice the 2 medium zucchini now so it's ready to go in later. Open the diced tomatoes too, but don't drain them unless your soup base is already thinner than you like.
The zucchini is diced and the tomatoes are open. What should I do with the soup base?
Prepare the Fast Chicken Soup Base in your pot according to that recipe, then set the pot over medium heat.
The base is in the pot and warming. Am I looking for a boil or something gentler?
Bring it to a simmer, not a hard boil. You want steady small bubbles so the tortellini can cook without breaking apart.
It's simmering now. Do I add everything at once?
Yes. Stir in the 9 ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 14.5 ounce can of diced tomatoes, the diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
Everything is in. Should I keep the lid on while it cooks?
Keep it at a gentle simmer, with the lid partly on if you want to limit splatter. Stir occasionally so the tortellini don't stick to the bottom.
How long should I let it go, and how do I know it's done?
Simmer it for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini are tender and the zucchini is softened but not falling apart. Taste the broth before serving and adjust only if needed.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: Can you guide me through making Crawfish Chowder? I've got a large skillet ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 cup butter and 1/2 bunch green onions, chopped, for the opening part of the cook.
The green onions are chopped. Is there more butter later, or just that first piece?
You'll use more later: keep 1/2 cup butter nearby as well, along with 2 pounds frozen crawfish, cleaned.
The crawfish is cleaned and thawing a bit. Should I start heating the skillet now?
Yes. Put the large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1/4 cup butter in it.
The butter is melted and starting to foam lightly. Do the onions go in now?
Add the chopped green onions to the melted butter and sauté them until they're tender.
They've softened and smell good. Do I leave them in while the crawfish cooks?
Take the green onions out of the pan and set them aside for now.
Onions are in a bowl. The skillet still has a little buttery coating—should I wipe it out?
No need to wipe it. Use the same skillet and melt the 1/2 cup butter in it.
That butter is melted. How long should the crawfish cook?
Add the 2 pounds cleaned crawfish and sauté them in the butter for 5 minutes, then set them aside.
Can you help me cook Fab Summer Blackened Chicken Salad? I've got the chicken out but want to make sure I don't miss anything.

Absolutely. For the chicken portion, you'll need 2 tablespoons olive oil total, divided; 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, about 6 ounces each; 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning; and 2 cloves garlic, crushed.
I have the olive oil, Cajun seasoning, and the 2 chicken breasts. I'm crushing the garlic now—what pan should I use?
Use a large skillet so the chicken has room to sear instead of crowding. Set it over medium heat and warm 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in the pan.
The oil is heating. Should the seasoning go on before the chicken hits the skillet?
Yes. Coat both sides of the chicken breasts with the Cajun seasoning, then lay them carefully into the hot oil.
They're in the skillet and starting to sizzle. Where does the crushed garlic come in?
Stir the 2 crushed garlic cloves into the skillet around the chicken so they flavor the oil while the chicken cooks.
The garlic smells strong already. How long should I leave the chicken before flipping?
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side, keeping the heat at medium so the seasoning blackens without burning.
Okay, I flipped them after 5 minutes. Do I cook the second side the same way?
Yes, give the second side about 5 minutes too. The chicken is done when the juices run clear.
If the pieces look browned but I'm unsure inside, what should I look for before serving?
Check that the center is no longer pink and that the juices run clear when pierced. Once done, move the chicken off the heat and let it rest briefly before slicing for the salad.
I want to make Fire Side Coffee mix. Can you guide me without rushing through the dry ingredients?
Absolutely. Set out a large bowl, a sifter or fine mesh strainer, and a clean jar with a tight lid. Measure 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer into the bowl area first.
The creamer is measured. I'm using a wide mixing bowl so it doesn't spill—what should go in with it?
Add 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix and 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules. Keep them dry and break up any obvious clumps before sifting.
Got it. The coffee granules are a little chunky; should I crush them or just sift everything?
If the granules are very large, lightly crush them with the back of a spoon so the finished mix scoops evenly. Then add 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
Cinnamon is in. The recipe note mentions nutmeg too, but I don't see an amount—how should I handle the sifting part?
Sift the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and the nutmeg called for by your recipe note together until the mixture looks even and powdery.
It looks evenly mixed now. I have a clean jar ready—do I pack it down?
Pour the mixture into the jar without packing it tightly. Tap the jar gently to settle the powder, then seal it with the lid.
Jar is sealed. I'd like to make one mug now to check the flavor.
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Stir well so the cocoa, creamer, and coffee dissolve evenly.
It dissolved, but I'm deciding whether I want it stronger or creamier.
Taste it and adjust to taste: add a little more mix for a stronger, richer mug, or add more hot water if you want it lighter.
Can you help me make Citrus Infused Guacamole? I've got a bowl out and want to make sure I prep the avocados correctly.
Absolutely. Peel, pit, and mash 2 avocados in a large bowl. Keep one of the pits nearby because you'll use it later to help keep the guacamole fresh.
The avocados are mashed. I see lime, orange, and pineapple juice on the counter—how much of each goes in?
Add 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice to the mashed avocados.
All three juices are in. The mixture looks a little loose around the edges—should I stir it more?
Yes, stir until the citrus is evenly worked through the avocado. While you're mixing, add the cumin, cilantro, and salt so everything gets distributed through the guacamole.
I added the cumin, cilantro, and salt. Should the texture be completely smooth or still a bit chunky?
Either is fine, but for this guacamole a gently mashed texture works well. Stir just enough to combine everything without turning it watery.
I have hot pepper sauce too. Is that part required?
It's optional. If you're using it, mix in a little hot pepper sauce now, then taste before adding more.
I added a small splash and it tastes good. What do I do with the avocado pit I saved?
Place one of the avocado pits into the bowl with the guacamole. It can help keep it fresh until you're ready to serve.
I'm not serving it for about an hour. Should I leave it out or chill it?
Refrigerate it until serving. If you were eating right away, you could serve it immediately, but for an hour wait, keep it chilled.

Spoon in the 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder slowly, or use a funnel if you have one. Try not to shake it too much once it's in, so the layers stay distinct.

Keep the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar and 1/3 cup all-purpose flour measured and ready; they're part of the pie filling ingredients, along with the apples and cranberry sauce.

Use a medium-sized mixing bowl. Add the sliced apples and the whole cranberry sauce, then combine them gently so the apples get coated without being crushed.

Yes, that texture sounds right for Cranberry Apple Pie II. Once the apples and cranberry sauce are combined, you're ready to move the filling into the pastry-lined pie plate and continue baking from there.

You'll also need 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard and 3 slices smoked turkey breast.

Spread the 1 tablespoon mayonnaise over one slice of toast, then spread the 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard over the other slice.

Unfold the 3 slices smoked turkey breast and arrange them on one side, overlapping slightly so each bite gets turkey.

Spread the guacamole over the turkey in an even layer, going close to the edges but not so thick that it squeezes out immediately.

Pile on the salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado and cheese, then bring the other slice of toast over the top and press gently to hold everything together.

Lightly oil the grill grate before adding the wings. That helps prevent sticking, especially with the sweet, sticky marinade.

Keep the marinated wings ready near the grill, but don't let the bowl clutter your workspace. Once the low-heat grill is preheated and the grate is lightly oiled, you're set to place the wings on and continue cooking them.
Can you help me make Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes? I've got a pot ready but want to make sure I add things in the right order.

Absolutely. Set up your ingredients: 1 recipe Fast Chicken Soup Base, 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes, 2 medium zucchini diced, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
The soup base is the only thing I haven't started yet. Should I get that going before chopping the zucchini?

Bring the chicken soup base to a gentle simmer rather than a hard boil. You're looking for steady small bubbles so the tortellini can cook without getting knocked around too much.

Use the 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes as part of the soup mixture; add them when you add the other ingredients. Stir in the 1 (9 ounce) package refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the diced zucchini, the diced tomatoes, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
Everything is in the pot. Should I cover it, and how long does it need?
Let it simmer for 10-20 minutes, until the tortellini and zucchini are tender. You can leave it partially covered if you want to reduce splatter, but keep the simmer gentle and stir occasionally.

It tastes tender at about 12 minutes. Is there anything else before serving?
That sounds ready. Give the soup a final stir, make sure the zucchini and tortellini are evenly distributed, and ladle it into bowls while hot.

That's right: 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper. Sprinkle it into the pan with the other ingredients, keeping to your machine's recommended order.

No stirring is needed unless your bread machine manual specifically tells you to. Once the ingredients are in the pan in the proper order, lock the pan into the machine.

Select the Basic or White Cycle on the bread machine, whichever your model offers for a standard loaf.

Basic is fine. Make sure the lid is closed, then press Start and let the bread machine run the cycle.
