Absolutely. Start by measuring 2 cups mashed ripe bananas and 1 2/3 cups sugar. Put them near a mixing bowl so you can combine everything smoothly.
The bananas are mashed, and the sugar is measured. What should I set out next?
Add 1 cup vegetable oil and 4 eggs to your setup. Those will get beaten together with the bananas and sugar.
Should I use a hand mixer for that, or is a whisk okay?
Either works. In the mixing bowl, beat the mashed bananas, sugar, vegetable oil, and eggs until the mixture looks well blended and fairly even.
It's smooth enough now, with just a few tiny banana bits. What happens with the dry ingredients?
Combine the dry ingredients separately, then fold them into the banana mixture. Use gentle strokes and keep going until the batter is well mixed.
I'm folding it in now. How thick should the batter seem before I stop?
Stop once you don't see dry streaks and the mixture looks evenly combined. It should be cohesive rather than overworked.
The batter looks even. The recipe mentions bars—do I spread anything at this point?
Yes, follow that part by spreading over the bars as directed, keeping the layer as even as you can.
Got it. What pan should I have ready for the batter?
Use a greased 15-in. baking pan, then pour the mixture into it and level the surface before it goes on to bake.
I want to make the Awesome Turkey Sandwich for lunch. I've got a cutting board out—can you guide me through it?

Absolutely. Set out 2 slices of whole wheat bread; you can toast them if you want a little crunch. You'll also need 1 tablespoon mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard, and 3 slices smoked turkey breast.
Bread is toasted, and I measured the mayo and Dijon. Should I build it right on the plate?
Yes, a plate is perfect. Put the 2 toast slices side by side so the spreads are easy to add without making a mess.
They're side by side. Which spread goes where?
Spread the 1 tablespoon mayonnaise over one slice of toast, then spread the 2 teaspoons Dijon-style prepared mustard over the other slice.
The mayo slice looks even, and the mustard is on the other piece. What about the turkey?
Lay the 3 slices of smoked turkey breast on one side, overlapping them slightly so the sandwich has an even layer.
Turkey is on the mayo side. I see guacamole in the directions too—does that go on top of the meat?
Yes. Spread the guacamole directly over the turkey, using a light hand so the slices stay in place.
Guacamole is spread. I also have salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese ready.
Pile those on over the guacamole: add the salad greens, bean sprouts, avocado, and cheese in a loose, even stack so the sandwich doesn't slide apart.
It's stacked pretty high. How should I close and serve it?
Place the mustard-coated slice on top, press gently to settle everything, then cut the sandwich if you like. Serve it right away while the toast still has some crispness.
I want to make Chicken Eileen, but I'd like to get everything set up before I touch the chicken. What should be on the counter?
For Chicken Eileen, set out 1 (6 ounce) package of herb-seasoned dry bread stuffing mix, 8 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, and 16 medium slices of mozzarella cheese.
I've got the stuffing mix and mozzarella out, and the chicken is still wrapped. Should I heat the oven before prepping?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the chicken is assembled.
The oven is heating. Do I make the stuffing dry, or cook it like the box says?
Prepare the herb-seasoned stuffing according to the package directions, so it's ready to scoop onto the chicken.
The stuffing is made and cooling a little in the pan. How thin should the chicken be?
Wash the chicken, pat it dry well, then pound each breast half to about a 1/2 inch thickness.
I have a cutting board and plastic wrap ready. Is the goal even thickness more than making it huge?
Exactly—aim for an even 1/2 inch thickness so each piece can hold the cheese and stuffing neatly.
The chicken pieces are flattened. How do I layer the cheese with the stuffing?
Place a slice of mozzarella cheese on each chicken breast, then add a scoop of the prepared stuffing on top of the cheese.
Since I have 16 mozzarella slices for 8 chicken breast halves, should I keep the extra slices nearby while assembling?
Yes, keep all 16 medium slices nearby, but follow the assembly step by starting with one slice of cheese on each breast, followed by a scoop of stuffing.
Can you guide me through making Chocolate Cheesecake II? I want to get the pan and crust started correctly.
Absolutely. Pull out a 9 inch springform pan, and gather 1 1/2 cups chocolate cookie crumbs, 2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/4 cup melted butter, and 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips.
I've got the springform pan out. Should the oven be heating while I measure the crumbs?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it is ready when the crust is shaped.
The oven is heating. Do I need to do anything to the springform pan before the crumbs go in?
Lightly grease the 9 inch springform pan, especially the bottom and lower sides where the crust will be pressed.
Pan is greased. My butter is melted, and I have the cookie crumbs in a small bowl.
Add the 2 tablespoons white sugar to the 1 1/2 cups chocolate cookie crumbs, then pour in the 1/4 cup melted butter.
Everything is in the bowl. What texture am I looking for after mixing?
Stir until the crumbs look evenly moistened by the butter and sugar, like damp sand that will hold together when pressed.
The crumb mixture is holding together. How far up the sides should I press it?
Press it firmly across the bottom of the prepared 9 inch springform pan and about 1 1/2 inch up the sides.
The crust is pressed in. I still have the 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips measured—should I keep them nearby?
Yes, keep the 1/4 cup semisweet chocolate chips measured and nearby for the next part of the recipe; for this stage, the pan is greased and the chocolate crumb crust is formed.
Can you help me make Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I? I'm setting things out and want to go in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by getting the main wet-mixture ingredients ready: 1 cup shortening, 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 2 eggs.
I've got the shortening and both sugars measured. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the dough is ready.
The oven is heating. Do the eggs go in with the sugars right away?
They do. Cream the shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla together thoroughly until the mixture looks well blended and smooth.
I don't want to under-mix it. What texture am I looking for after creaming?
Aim for an even, creamy mixture with no obvious streaks of shortening or loose sugar pockets. Scrape the bowl once or twice so everything gets incorporated.
Okay, the creamed mixture looks even. I have another bowl ready for the dry ingredients.
Good. In that separate bowl, mix together the dry ingredients, but leave out the candies for now.
So the candy pieces shouldn't go into the dry bowl yet?
Right, keep the candies aside at this point. Just combine the dry ingredients separately so they're evenly distributed before they meet the creamed mixture.
The dry ingredients are mixed. How do I bring the dough together without making a mess?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix well, starting slowly if you're using a mixer so the dry ingredients don't puff out of the bowl.

source_seed.recipe_title: Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I

messages.content: Can you help me make Armadillo Eggs? I'm starting with the jalapenos and want to get organized.
Absolutely. Set out 24 jalapeno peppers, 1 pound sausage, 2 cups all-purpose baking mix, and 1 (16 ounce) package shredded Cheddar cheese.
I've got the peppers, sausage, baking mix, and Cheddar out. What should I do with the oven?
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) so it's ready by the time the peppers are prepped.
The oven is heating. Which pan should I prep for these?
Use a medium baking sheet and lightly grease it so the Armadillo Eggs won't stick while they bake.
Baking sheet is greased. I'm about to handle the jalapenos—how should I cut them?
Cut a slit in each jalapeno pepper lengthwise, just enough to open it for cleaning without splitting it completely apart.
I've slit a few. Do I keep any of the inside, or clear it all out?
Remove and discard the seeds and pulp from each pepper. A small spoon works well, and gloves are a good idea if you have them.
All 24 peppers are cleaned out. Should I keep the sausage and cheese nearby?
Yes, keep the 1 pound sausage, the shredded Cheddar from the 16 ounce package, and the 2 cups baking mix close so you can move right into assembling once the peppers are ready.
Before I start filling, anything I should check on the tray or peppers?

Make sure the baking sheet has a light, even coating of grease and that each jalapeno has been slit, seeded, and cleared of pulp. Once the oven reaches 325 degrees F, you'll be set for the next stage.
Can you guide me through making Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms? I'm getting my ingredients out now.

Absolutely. Set out 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, 2 cups diced Broccoflower, 2 cups chopped assorted wild mushrooms, and 1/2 chopped white onion. You'll also need the rice, chicken stock, garlic, nutmeg, herbs, salt, and pepper for the cooking steps.
The vegetables are chopped. Should I start with a wide pan or a pot for the sauté?
Use a wide, sturdy pan if you have one, since you'll sauté the Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic there and then use the same pan for the risotto.
The pan is ready. How much butter goes in before the vegetables?
Melt the 1 tablespoon unsalted butter over medium heat, then add the diced Broccoflower, chopped wild mushrooms, chopped 1/2 white onion, and garlic.
They're in the pan and starting to soften. How long should I keep them going?
Sauté the mixture for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are softened and the mushrooms have given off some moisture.
The 10 minutes are up and the vegetables look cooked down. Do they stay in the pan?
Scoop the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside for the moment.
The pan has some browned bits left. Is that okay before I add the rice?
Yes, keep using that same pan. Add the rice, then begin adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time, stirring until each cup is well incorporated before adding the next.
The stock is absorbing and the rice is getting tender. When do the vegetables and seasonings go back in?
Once the chicken stock is absorbed and the rice is tender, stir the sautéed vegetables back in with the nutmeg and herbs. Season with salt and pepper, then serve while the risotto is warm and creamy.
Can you guide me through making Chicken with Vegetables in the slow cooker?

Absolutely. Set up your slow cooker and gather the main ingredients: 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms, 4 chicken drumsticks with the skin removed, 4 chicken thighs with the skin removed, and 4 sliced celery ribs.
I've got the slow cooker out, and the chicken pieces are skinned. Do the mushrooms go in before the chicken?
Yes. Put the sliced fresh mushrooms into the slow cooker, then add the drumsticks and thighs on top or nestled in with them.
The mushrooms and chicken are in. I have the sliced celery ready too—what else gets added with it?

Add the celery now, along with the zucchini, carrots, onion, tomato juice, broth, garlic, paprika, and pepper. Try to spread the vegetables and seasonings around the chicken so everything cooks evenly.
Everything is layered in the cooker, but some chicken is sticking up above the vegetables. Is that okay?
That's fine as long as the lid can close well. The chicken will cook slowly with the vegetables and liquid, so just settle the pieces down a bit if needed before covering.
The lid fits. What setting and how long should I use?
Cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 5 hours, or until the meat juices run clear.
When I check later, should I be looking at the drumsticks or thighs for doneness?
Check the thickest chicken pieces, especially the thighs and drumsticks near the bone. The recipe's doneness cue is that the meat juices run clear.
The chicken is done and the vegetables are tender. How do I handle it before serving?
Remove the chicken and vegetables from the slow cooker and keep them warm until you're ready to serve.
Can you help me make Banana Orange Bars? I've got ripe bananas ready, but I want to make sure I measure everything correctly.
Absolutely. Mash enough ripe bananas to get 2 cups, then measure out 1 2/3 cups sugar. Put both near your mixing bowl so they're ready to go in together.
The bananas are mashed and the sugar is measured. What wet ingredients should I set out before I start mixing?
You'll need 1 cup vegetable oil and 4 eggs. Once those are ready, use a mixing bowl large enough to beat the bananas, sugar, oil, and eggs without splashing.
I have the oil and eggs out. Should I add everything to the bowl at the same time?
Yes. Add the mashed bananas, sugar, vegetable oil, and eggs to the mixing bowl, then beat them until the mixture looks well blended and fairly even.
It's mixed together and looks smooth with a little banana texture. What happens with the dry ingredients?
Combine the dry ingredients separately, then fold them into the banana mixture. Use broad, gentle strokes and keep going until everything is well mixed.
The batter is coming together. I don't want to overwork it—what texture am I looking for?
Stop once you don't see dry streaks and the batter looks evenly moistened. A few small banana bits are fine; the key is that the dry ingredients are fully incorporated.
Okay, the bowl is mixed. The recipe mentions spreading over bars—how should I handle that part?
Spread over bars as directed, using a spatula to make the layer even from edge to edge so it bakes and serves neatly.
I'm ready to put it in the pan. What size should I use, and does it need greasing?
Pour the mixture into a greased 15-in. baking pan. Smooth the top lightly with your spatula so the Banana Orange Bars bake in an even layer.
I want to make Eggnog Blend. Can you guide me through it while I cook?

Absolutely. Set out 4 cups half-and-half, 1 cup white sugar, 11 beaten egg yolks, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also need a saucepan, a whisk, and space in the refrigerator for chilling overnight.
I've got the saucepan ready. Should the heat be low from the start?
Yes, keep it on low heat. Pour the half-and-half into the saucepan, add the sugar, and stir gently so the sugar dissolves without the mixture getting too hot.
The sugar is dissolving. I'm worried about adding all those yolks without scrambling them.
Whisk steadily as the beaten egg yolks go in. Keep the heat low and cook the mixture only until it turns into a light custard; don't let it boil.
How will I know it's a light custard and not undercooked?

It should look slightly thickened and smoother than the starting mixture, with enough body to lightly coat the whisk. If you see bubbles building toward a boil, lower the heat or lift the pan briefly.
It has thickened and I don't see it boiling. What should I do with the hot pan now?
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let the custard cool. Once it's no longer hot, transfer it to the refrigerator and chill it overnight.
So the vanilla waits until after the overnight chill?
Right. After the mixture is fully chilled, stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract along with the cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream.
When I stir in the ice cream, should I leave it chunky or blend it smooth?
Stir until the add-ins are evenly incorporated and the vanilla ice cream has softened into the chilled base. Serve it cold once the texture is smooth and creamy.
Can you guide me through making Baked Spaghetti Squash Lasagna Style? I've got the squash on the counter but haven't started cutting yet.
Absolutely. You'll need 1 spaghetti squash, halved lengthwise and seeded, plus 1 chopped onion, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and 2 cans of stewed tomatoes, 14 ounces each.
I have the onion and garlic ready, and the tomatoes are the 14 ounce cans. Should I deal with the oven before cutting the squash?
Yes, get the oven heating to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the squash is prepped.
The oven is heating. I've halved the spaghetti squash lengthwise and scooped out the seeds—what should I put it on?
Use a baking sheet and coat it with a thin layer of cooking spray so the squash won't stick while it bakes.
Baking sheet is sprayed. Do the squash halves go cut side up or down?
Set the squash halves cut side down on the sprayed baking sheet. That helps them steam and soften as they bake.
They're on the pan cut side down. How long should I set the timer for?
Bake the squash in the preheated oven for 35 minutes to start.
When the timer goes off, how do I know whether it needs more time?
Check it with a knife. If the knife can be easily inserted into the squash, it's done; if there's resistance, give it a little more time.
Got it. While it bakes, should I keep the chopped onion, 2 tablespoons garlic, and stewed tomatoes nearby for the lasagna-style part?

Yes, keep them ready on the counter: the chopped onion, the 2 tablespoons minced garlic, and both 14 ounce cans of stewed tomatoes will be the next ingredients to work with after the squash is tender.
Can you guide me through making A 1 Chicken Soup? I've got a large pot ready.
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 2 skinless chicken leg quarters, 1/2 cup chopped onion, 2 quarts water, and the chicken bouillon called for in the recipe.
The chicken leg quarters are skinless, and I've measured the oil. Should the pot be heating already?
Yes. Put the large pot over medium heat, add the vegetable oil, and let it warm for a moment before the chicken goes in.
The pot is on medium and the oil is warmed. How do I start browning the chicken?
Place the chicken pieces in the oil and cook them until they're browned on both sides. Give them enough space to make contact with the bottom of the pot.
One side has color now. Do I just turn them and brown the second side the same way?
Exactly. Turn the pieces carefully and let the other side brown too; you're building flavor before adding the onion and liquid.
Both sides are browned. I have the chopped onion measured at 1/2 cup.
Stir the chopped onion into the pot around the chicken and cook it for 2 minutes more, just enough to soften it slightly.
The onion has cooked for 2 minutes. Should I add all the water now?
Yes. Pour in the 2 quarts water, add the chicken bouillon, and bring the pot up to a boil.
It's boiling now. What should the heat look like for the rest of the cooking?
Reduce the heat so the soup simmers steadily rather than boils hard, and let it cook for 45 minutes.
I want to make Fresh Apple Walnut Cake. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Start by pulling out 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've measured the dry ingredients. Should I turn the oven on before mixing anything?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it has time to come up to temperature.
Oven is heating. I have a rectangular cake pan—what size should I prep?
Use a 9x13 inch pan. Grease it well, then dust it with flour so the cake releases cleanly after baking.
The pan is greased and floured. Do the flour and spices go straight into the batter bowl?
Before adding them to anything else, sift together the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. That helps distribute the leavening and spice evenly.
I'm sifting now, and the cinnamon is mixed through. What should I do with the apples?
Combine the apples with the white sugar in a separate bowl, then set that mixture aside for the moment.
Should the apple and sugar mixture sit while I finish organizing the dry bowl and pan?
Yes. Let it sit briefly while your oven finishes preheating and your prepared 9x13 inch pan stays ready.
So at this point I have sifted dry ingredients, sugared apples set aside, and the oven at 350 degrees F.
Perfect. You're caught up for Fresh Apple Walnut Cake: oven at 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, pan greased and floured, dry ingredients sifted, and apples combined with white sugar and set aside.
I want to make Famous Caramel Cookie Bars. Can you guide me while I set up the tray?
Absolutely. You'll need 40 rectangular shortbread cookies, 35 individually wrapped caramels with the wrappers removed, 1/4 cup water, and 4 cups milk chocolate chips.
I've unwrapped the caramels and the cookies are still in their package. Should I line a baking sheet or just use a tray?
Either a baking sheet or a tray works. Lay the shortbread cookies out in a single layer so each one has room for a thin stripe of caramel later.
The cookies are arranged in rows. I have the caramels and water next to the stove—what kind of heat should I use?
Use a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the caramels and the 1/4 cup water, then stir frequently as they melt so the mixture turns smooth instead of sticking.
The caramel is starting to soften but there are still a few lumps. Should I turn the heat up?
Keep it at medium-low and keep stirring. The lumps should melt out gradually; higher heat can make the caramel catch on the bottom.
It's smooth now and looks pourable. How much goes on each cookie?
Spoon a thin line of caramel over each shortbread cookie. Aim for a narrow stripe rather than covering the whole top, so you have enough for the full batch.
Some of the caramel is stringing between cookies as I spoon it. Is that okay?
That's fine. You can use the spoon to nudge each line back onto its cookie while the caramel is still warm.
All 40 cookies have caramel on them. What should I do with the tray now?

Place the cookies in the refrigerator until the caramel is set. Once firm, they'll be ready to serve; keep the 4 cups milk chocolate chips with your ingredients if you're following the full ingredient list.
Can you guide me through making Banana Bran Muffins? I'm setting out the ingredients now.
Absolutely. Start by getting 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar ready, since those will be creamed together.
The butter is soft and the brown sugar is measured. What else should I put on the counter?
You'll also need 3 mashed bananas and 1/4 cup milk. The recipe later adds vanilla and eggs too, so keep those nearby before you start mixing.
Got it. Should I deal with the oven or the muffin pan first?
Turn the oven on to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it can heat while you prep the pan.
The oven is heating. I have a metal muffin pan—what should I do with it?
Grease the muffin pan well, or line the cups with paper muffin liners if you'd rather make cleanup easier.
I lined the pan. For the mixing bowl, do the butter and sugar go in together?
Yes. Put the softened butter and brown sugar into a large mixing bowl and cream them together until the mixture looks fluffy.
It's lighter and fluffy now. Do I add the bananas next by themselves?
Add the mashed bananas along with the milk, vanilla, and eggs, then mix everything well so the wet mixture is evenly combined.
How smooth should that mixture be before I move on?
It should be well mixed, but it's fine if you still see small banana bits. Once the bananas, milk, vanilla, and eggs are fully incorporated, you're ready for the next part of the muffin batter.
Can you guide me through making Dads Flat Bread? I've got a large mixing bowl out but haven't started measuring yet.
Absolutely. Measure 2 cups warm water total, keeping it divided, and aim for 110 degrees to 115 degrees. You'll also need 1 (.25 ounce) package active dry yeast.
The water is warm and divided. How much goes in the bowl with the yeast?
Pour 1/2 cup of the warm water into the large mixing bowl and stir in the yeast until it dissolves.
The yeast is dissolved. I'm lining up the rest of the ingredients now—what should be ready beside the bowl?
Have 1/3 cup sugar and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil ready. You'll also be adding salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining warm water.
I've got the sugar and oil measured, and the flours are nearby. Do they all go in together?
Yes. Add the sugar, oil, salt, rye or whole wheat flour, 3 cups all-purpose flour, and the remaining water to the yeast mixture, then beat it until the mixture looks smooth.
It's smoothing out, but it still looks more like thick batter than dough. Is that expected?
That's fine at this stage. Start adding the remaining all-purpose flour gradually, just enough so it comes together into a soft dough rather than a sticky batter.
It's holding together now and feels soft. Should I flour the counter before kneading?
Yes, lightly flour your work surface, turn the dough out onto it, and keep a little extra flour nearby for your hands if the dough sticks.
The dough is on the floured surface. How long should I knead it, and what should it feel like?
Knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. It should feel supple and spring back a bit when pressed.
Can you help me make Doreens Oriental Swordfish Steaks? I want to get the marinade set up before I start handling the fish.
Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl, a whisk, and a large resealable bag. For the marinade, measure 3 tablespoons soy sauce and 1/2 cup vegetable oil into the bowl.
The soy sauce and oil are in the bowl. I also have sherry and fresh ginger on the counter—how much of each goes in?
Add 2 tablespoons sherry and 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger root. The recipe also has garlic whisked into the marinade, so add that with the ginger if you have it ready.
Everything is in the bowl, including the garlic. Should I whisk it a lot or just stir it together?
Whisk it until the soy sauce, oil, sherry, ginger root, and garlic look well combined. The oil may not stay perfectly blended, but you want the ginger and garlic evenly dispersed.
It's mixed and smells good. I'm worried about spilling when I move it to the bag.
Open the large resealable bag and stand it upright in a bowl or measuring cup if you can. Pour the marinade mixture into the bag slowly, then keep the top open for the swordfish.
The marinade is in the bag. Do the swordfish steaks go in flat or stacked?
Place the swordfish steaks into the bag with the mixture as flat as you can, then seal it most of the way and press out excess air before closing it completely.
They're in the bag. How do I make sure they're coated without making a mess?
Hold the sealed bag over the bowl and gently shake or turn it so the marinade coats all sides of the swordfish steaks. If any pieces look bare, massage the bag lightly to move the mixture around.
Looks evenly coated. How long does it need to sit before cooking?
Put the sealed bag in the refrigerator and let the steaks marinate at least 4 hours. Lay the bag on a plate or in a shallow dish in case of leaks.
Can you help me make Asian Ginger Dressing? I've got a clean jar out but want to make sure I'm using the right size.
Yes. Use a 1 pint glass jar or something larger, since you'll be shaking everything together in it.
Great. I have garlic and ginger on the counter—how much should I prep?
Mince 3 cloves of garlic and 2 tablespoons of fresh ginger root. Add both to the jar once they're ready.
The garlic and ginger are in. What liquids go in next?
Pour in 3/4 cup olive oil and 1/3 cup rice vinegar. The recipe also includes soy sauce, honey, and water, so add those to the jar as well.
Everything is in the jar. Should I stir it, or is shaking better?
Put on a tight-fitting lid and shake the jar well so the garlic, ginger, oil, vinegar, soy sauce, honey, and water start combining.
It's shaken, but the honey still looks a little streaky near the bottom.
Take the lid off, then microwave the jar for 1 minute. That brief heat is just to dissolve the honey.
After microwaving, should I put the lid back on right away?
Let it cool first so pressure doesn't build up in the jar. Once it's cooled a bit, replace the lid.
It's cooled now. How do I serve it so it's not separated?
Shake it well again right before serving. That will bring the dressing back together for drizzling or tossing with salad.
Can you help me make Easy Pot Roast? I've got the chuck roast out and want to keep the steps straight.
Absolutely. For this recipe you'll need a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast, 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.
I have the roast, water, soup mix, and Worcestershire sauce. Should I start with the oven or the meat?
Start by preheating the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the roast is ready to go in.
The oven is heating. The roast is on my cutting board—what should I do to it before it goes in the bag?
Score the roast on the top and sides with shallow cuts. That helps the liquid and seasonings reach more surface area without cutting the roast apart.
Scored on top and sides. I have a medium sized oven bag ready—does the roast go in by itself?
Place the scored roast into the medium sized oven bag. Keep the bag open enough so you can pour the seasoned liquid over the meat cleanly.
Roast is in the bag. How do I mix the sauce so the soup mix doesn't clump too much?
In a bowl or measuring cup, combine the 2 cups water, the dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. Stir until the soup mix is mostly dispersed.
It's mixed and smells good. Do I pour all of it right over the roast?
Yes, pour the whole mixture over the roast in the oven bag, letting it run across the scored top and down the sides.
I'm adding vegetables with it. Where should they go so they cook with the meat?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag, rather than piled only on top. Once they're tucked around the roast, it's ready for the oven.
Can you help me make Chili For Two? I've got a small saucepan ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1/4 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup chopped onion, 1 minced garlic clove, and 1 (15.5 ounce) can of chili beans. Keep the beans undrained.
The beef is still in the fridge, but the onion is already chopped. Should I mince the garlic before heating the pan?
Yes, mince the garlic now so everything can go in smoothly once the pan is hot. Put the saucepan over medium heat when you're ready.
Okay, the pan is heating. Do the beef, onion, and garlic all go in together?
They do. Add the ground beef, chopped onion, and minced garlic to the saucepan, then cook over medium heat, breaking up the beef as it browns.
How will I know the beef is cooked enough before I drain it?
Cook until the meat is no longer pink. Once it reaches that point, carefully drain off the excess fat from the saucepan.
Drained. The pan looks a little dry now—do I add anything before the beans?
No extra liquid is needed. Stir in the entire can of chili beans, including the liquid from the can, since the recipe uses them undrained.
The beans are stirred in. Should I keep it on medium until it bubbles?
Yes. Bring the chili to a boil, stirring occasionally so it heats evenly and doesn't stick to the bottom.
It's bubbling now. What's the simmer timing from here?
Reduce the heat, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer for 10-15 minutes, until the chili is heated through. Give it an occasional stir, then serve it hot.
Can you help me make Fruit Dip 2? I've got a bowl out but haven't started measuring.

Absolutely. Set out 8 ounces cream cheese so it's easier to blend, plus 1/2 cup marshmallow creme. You'll also need 2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, and 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice nearby.
The whipped topping is thawed, and the cream cheese is soft. Should I use a hand mixer or just a spoon?

A hand mixer will make it smoother fastest, but a sturdy spoon or spatula works if the cream cheese is softened. Put the cream cheese, marshmallow creme, and thawed whipped topping into the bowl together.
All three are in the bowl. Do I blend until it's totally smooth?
Yes, blend until the cream cheese is fully worked in and the dip looks fluffy and even, with no obvious lumps of cream cheese.
It's mostly smooth now. The pineapple juice is measured, but do I pour in the whole 1/4 cup at once?
Add the unsweetened pineapple juice gradually. Use enough to loosen the mixture into a dipping consistency; the full 1/4 cup is available, but stop when it feels right for fruit.
I added most of it, and it's creamy but not runny. Is that the texture I want?
That sounds right. It should hold softly on a spoon but still be easy to scoop with apple slices, strawberries, or other fruit.
Do I serve it right away, or does it need time in the fridge?
Cover the bowl and chill the dip for 1 hour. That helps the texture set and lets the flavors come together.
After chilling, should I stir it again before putting it out?
Give it a gentle stir after the 1 hour chill, then transfer it to a serving bowl if you like. Keep it cold until serving and pair it with your cut fruit.
Can you help me cook Adriennes Tom Ka Gai? I've got a large saucepan out and want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Set up your aromatics before turning on the heat: measure 2 teaspoons peanut oil, thinly slice 2 cloves garlic, grate 2 tablespoons fresh ginger root, and chop 1/4 cup lemon grass.
The garlic is sliced and the ginger is grated. Should the lemon grass go in right away with them?
Yes, it cooks with the garlic and ginger. Keep the chopped lemon grass nearby along with the red pepper, coriander, and cumin, since those all get stirred into the hot oil together.
Okay, oil is measured. What heat should I use for the saucepan?
Put the large saucepan over medium heat and warm the peanut oil in it. Give it a moment to shimmer, but don't let the garlic go in before the oil is hot.
The oil looks hot now. I'm worried the garlic might burn if I'm slow adding everything.
Add the garlic, ginger, lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin all together, then stir constantly. Cook just until fragrant, about 2 minutes, so the aromatics bloom without browning too much.
It smells strong and aromatic. I have the chicken and onion ready—what texture am I looking for there?
Stir in the chicken and onion, keeping everything moving. Cook until the chicken turns white and the onion becomes translucent, about 5 minutes.
The chicken has gone white and the onion looks translucent. The pan bottom has some bits stuck to it.
That's fine; keep stirring and scrape gently as you go so those flavorful bits mix back in. Next, add the bok choy and fold it through the chicken and aromatics.
How wilted should the bok choy be before I stop cooking?
Cook it until it just begins to wilt, which should take 5 to 10 minutes. Once the leaves soften and the stems are tender-crisp, you're at the point this stage of the recipe calls for.
Can you help me make Frosted Ruby Punch for serving later? I want to get the ice ring started correctly.
Absolutely. You'll need 4 cups cranberry juice for the ice ring, plus 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice for the punch mixture.
I have a ring mold, but I'm not sure about the size. What should I use?
Use a 5-cup ring mold. Pour the 4 cups cranberry juice into it, leaving a little space so it can expand as it freezes.
The cranberry juice is in the mold. Does it just go straight into the freezer?
Yes. Set the filled mold level in the freezer and leave it overnight so it freezes into a firm cranberry ice ring.
When I'm ready to assemble the punch tomorrow, what should go into the bowl before the ice ring?
In the punch bowl, combine the 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1 1/2 cups lemon juice, and 1 cup orange juice. Stir until the sugar is dissolved.
Should the sugar be completely gone before I add anything bubbly?
Yes, keep stirring until you don't feel sugar settling at the bottom. Once it's dissolved, stir in the ginger ale gently so you keep the fizz.
Any tip for getting the frozen ring out without cracking it?
Briefly loosen the outside of the mold with warm water, then unmold the cranberry ice ring carefully.
Once it's out, do I place it in the bowl right away?
Yes. Float the cranberry ice ring in the punch, then serve while it's cold and ruby-colored.
Can you guide me through Eclairs II? I've got the counter cleared and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water first, since those will go straight into a saucepan.
Butter and water are ready. Is there anything dry I should measure before I turn on the stove?
Yes. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt so they're ready when you need them.
Got the flour and salt measured. Should I prep the oven before dealing with the pan?
Yes, preheat the oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C.
The oven is heating. What baking tray setup do I need for these?
Grease a cookie sheet so the eclairs have a prepared surface ready to go.
Cookie sheet is greased. I have a medium saucepan out; what goes in it?
Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to the medium saucepan.
They're in the pan. Should the heat be gentle, or am I bringing it up quickly?
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring as it heats so the butter melts completely into the water.
The butter has melted all the way and the mixture is boiling. Is that the point I should stop for this part?
Yes. Once it reaches a boil and the butter is completely melted, you've completed the steps covered here for Eclairs II.
I'm making Dutch Cream Waffles and want to keep the mixing order straight. Can you guide me while I set up?

Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl and a small mixing bowl on the counter. Measure out 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt, and have 3 separated egg yolks plus 3 separated egg whites ready.
The flour and salt are measured, and the eggs are separated. Which bowl gets what?
Use the large mixing bowl for the dry ingredients. Add the flour and salt to that bowl and stir them together so the salt is evenly distributed.
Dry bowl is mixed. I've got the yolks in the small bowl—do I start beating them before adding the cream?
Yes. Start beating the egg yolks on low speed, then add the cream while the mixer is still running on low.
Should the yolk mixture look fluffy, or just blended at this point?
At this point, just aim for blended and loosened up. After the cream is in, keep beating the mixture for 1 minute.
The minute is up. It looks smooth and a little pale.
Good. Pour the yolk-and-cream mixture into the large bowl with the flour and salt.
It's in the flour bowl. I'm worried about flour puffing out if I turn the mixer up too soon.
Start on low speed and combine gently until the flour is mostly incorporated. Once it is no longer dusty, increase to medium-high.
How long do I keep it on medium-high, and what texture am I looking for?
Beat on medium-high until the batter is smooth, with no visible dry streaks or lumps from the flour mixture. Stop once it looks even and cohesive.
Can you help me make Fiery Fish Tacos with Crunchy Corn Salsa? I'm setting up my cutting board and a mixing bowl.
Absolutely. For the salsa, pull out 1 cup corn and 1/2 cup diced red onion. A medium bowl will be right for mixing everything without spilling.
Corn and red onion are in the bowl. I also have jicama here—how much should I prep?
Peel and chop enough jicama for 1 cup, then add it to the bowl. Try for small, even pieces so the salsa stays crunchy but easy to spoon onto tacos.
The jicama is chopped. I've got a red bell pepper rinsed too.
Dice 1/2 cup red bell pepper and add it with the corn, red onion, and jicama. If you have cilantro ready, mix that in as well.
Salsa vegetables and cilantro are mixed. Should I start heating anything while I finish the salsa?
Yes, preheat the grill for high heat so it's ready when the fish goes on.
The grill is heating. The bowl looks colorful but a little dry—what brightens it up?
Stir in the lime juice and lime zest. Toss gently so the citrus coats the corn, red onion, jicama, bell pepper, and cilantro evenly.
The lime is mixed in. I want the seasoning ready before the fish hits the grill.
In a small bowl, combine cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt. Keep it nearby so you can season the fish quickly before grilling.
Seasoning bowl is ready, and the grill is hot. Any last check on the salsa texture before serving?
Give it one final gentle stir. You want distinct crunchy bits of corn, red onion, jicama, and red bell pepper with the lime distributed throughout, ready to spoon over the fiery fish tacos.

messages.content: I'm making Barbecued Shredded Beef today and have a large roasting pan out. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. For the main ingredients, you'll need a 3 pounds beef roast, 2 onions chopped, 2 cans or bottles of beer at 12 fluid ounces each, and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce.
The roast is on the counter, and I've chopped the onions. Should I heat the oven before loading the pan?
Yes, get the oven preheating to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the beef and liquid are assembled.
Oven is set. Do I need to brown the roast, or does it go straight into the roasting pan?
For this recipe, place the roast straight into the large roasting pan. Scatter the chopped onions over the top and around the sides.
The onions are spread over the beef. I see Worcestershire in the recipe—what gets mixed with it?
In a large bowl, combine the Worcestershire sauce with liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir those together so the seasonings are evenly blended.
I've got that seasoning mixture in the bowl. Where does the beer come in?
Pour the beer into the bowl with the Worcestershire mixture, then stir it together gently so the beer and seasonings are combined.
It's stirred together. Should I pour it directly over the roast or just into the bottom of the pan?
Add the beer mixture to the roasting pan, pouring it around and over the roast so the onions and beef are sitting with the seasoned liquid.
The pan is assembled with the beef, onions, and liquid. Anything I should check before it goes in the oven?
Make sure the roast is settled in the pan, the chopped onions are distributed over it, and the beer-Worcestershire mixture is in the pan. Then it's ready for the preheated 275 degrees F oven.
I want to make German Sweet Chocolate Pie. Can you help me get set up before I start melting anything?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (4 ounce) bar of German sweet chocolate, chopped, plus 1/3 cup milk. You'll also want a large microwave-safe bowl and a whisk nearby.
Chocolate is chopped and the milk is measured. Does the cream cheese go in right away?
Not yet. Have 4 ounces cream cheese softened and 2 tablespoons white sugar ready, but the chocolate and a small amount of milk get warmed together first.
How much milk goes into the bowl with the chocolate?

Add the chopped German sweet chocolate to the large microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of the milk. Microwave on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stopping to stir halfway through. You're looking for the chocolate to be almost melted.
I stirred it halfway, and it's mostly melted with a few soft pieces left. Should I keep microwaving?
If it's almost melted, stir it well before adding more heat; the residual warmth may smooth out those last bits. Once it looks melted and glossy, you're ready to whisk in the next ingredients.
Okay, it smoothed out. I have the softened cream cheese and sugar sitting here.
Whisk in the softened cream cheese, the 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk from the 1/3 cup. Keep whisking until the mixture is blended and even.
The mixture is blended, but it still feels a little loose. Is there a short chill before the topping?
Yes. Put the bowl in the refrigerator for 10 minutes so the chocolate mixture firms up slightly before you fold in the whipped topping.
It chilled for 10 minutes. I've got the whipped topping ready—how gentle do I need to be?
Gently fold in 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping, turning the mixture over with a spatula instead of stirring hard. Stop when no streaks remain, so the filling stays light.
Can you help me make E Z Cheezy Pie? I've got the counter cleared and want to make sure I start with the right ingredients.
Absolutely. Set out 2 baked 9 inch pie shells and 3 softened 8 ounce packages of cream cheese. Softened cream cheese will whip much more smoothly.
The 2 pie shells are already baked, and the cream cheese has been sitting out. What small ingredients should I measure before I start mixing?
Measure 1/2 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Keep them nearby so you can add them once the cream cheese is fluffy.
Got it. Do I need the oven on even though the shells are baked?
Yes, follow the recipe and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, before you start the filling.
The oven is heating. What bowl and tool should I use for the cream cheese?
Use a medium mixing bowl. Add the softened cream cheese and whip it until it looks fluffy rather than dense or blocky.
It's starting to loosen up, but there are still a few thicker streaks. Should I keep beating?
Yes, keep whipping a little longer until the texture is light and evenly fluffy. Scrape the sides of the bowl so all 3 packages mix evenly.
Okay, the cream cheese looks fluffy now. When do the sugar and vanilla go in?
Add the 1/2 cup white sugar and the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the whipped cream cheese.
They're in the bowl. What texture am I aiming for before I put it into the shells?
Mix until the filling is smooth, with no visible sugar pockets or cream cheese lumps. Then it's ready for the baked 9 inch pie shells.
Can you walk me through Garlic Chicken Stir Fry? I've got my wok out and want to prep before turning on the heat.

Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons peanut oil, 6 cloves garlic minced, 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, and 1 bunch green onions chopped. Keep the chicken nearby too, since it goes in once the aromatics are cooked.
The garlic is minced and the green onions are chopped. Should I keep all 6 cloves together?
Keep the minced garlic handy, but for the hot-oil step you'll quickly stir in 2 cloves' worth with the ginger, green onions, and salt. Have everything close to the wok because this part moves fast.
Got it. I'm using peanut oil—how hot should the wok be before I add anything?
Pour in the 2 tablespoons peanut oil and heat it in the wok or a large skillet until the oil just begins to smoke.
The oil is shimmering and starting to smoke lightly. I don't want the garlic to burn.
Add the 2 cloves minced garlic, the 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger, the chopped green onions, and salt right away, then stir constantly so the aromatics cook quickly instead of sitting in one spot.
They're sizzling hard. What should the onions look like before I add the chicken?
Stir-fry until the green onion turns translucent, about 2 minutes. You're looking for softened onion and a strong garlic-ginger aroma.
It's been about 2 minutes, and the onion looks softer and a little glossy.
Good. Add the chicken to the wok and keep stirring so the pieces contact the hot surface evenly.
The chicken pieces are in. How do I know when this stage is done?

Stir until the chicken turns opaque, about 3 minutes. Once there are no raw-looking translucent spots on the outside, it's ready to come off the heat or continue with whatever serving setup you planned.

Can you help me make Enchilada Style Burritos? I'm starting with the frozen bean and cheese burritos still in the freezer.

Absolutely. Pull out 6 frozen prepared bean and cheese burritos, plus 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1 3/4 cups water. You'll also need a greased 13-in baking dish and a saucepan.
I've got the 13-in dish greased. Do the burritos need to thaw before they go in?
No thawing needed. Place the frozen burritos directly in the greased baking dish, arranging them in a single layer if they fit, then set the dish aside while you make the sauce.
They're in the dish. I'm at the stove with the saucepan—what heat should I use for the butter?
Use medium heat and melt the 2 tablespoons butter or margarine gently, just until it's fully liquid. Try not to let it brown.
The butter is melted. When I add the flour, am I dumping it in all at once?
Add the 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and stir right away until the mixture looks smooth. Keep the spoon or whisk moving so you don't get dry pockets of flour.
It looks like a smooth paste now. How do I add the water without making lumps?
Pour in the 1 3/4 cups water gradually, stirring as you go. A slow stream works well because it gives the flour mixture time to loosen into a smooth sauce.

Yes. Bring it to a boil, then keep cooking and stirring for 2 minutes, or until it thickens. It should coat the spoon more than plain water would.

Yes, pour the thickened sauce evenly over the burritos in the baking dish. Scrape the saucepan so you don't leave much behind, and the burritos are ready for the next part of your recipe or any serving steps you plan to use.

Seed and dice 1 red bell pepper, then dice 1/2 red onion. Set them near the chicken so you can combine the salad base easily.

In a separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the dressing looks evenly combined.

Let it simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. You're aiming for a steady, gentle simmer rather than a hard boil.

Give it a stir every few minutes, especially across the bottom of the saucepan. That keeps the sauce from sticking while it thickens and the flavors come together.
The timer is almost done, and the sauce looks glossy. Should I taste it hot or wait?
You can taste a tiny cooled spoonful if you want to check it, but once the simmer is finished, take the pan off the heat and let the sauce cool.

Let it cool, then transfer it to a clean container and refrigerate it until you're ready to use it. It'll be ready for brushing on barbecue or serving on the side.

Can you help me make Campfire Angel Food Yummies? I'm setting up by the fire and want to keep it simple.

Absolutely. You'll need 1 angel food cake, the 10 inch size, cut into large cubes. Also set out 1 can of sweetened condensed milk, the 5 ounce can, and keep some toasting sticks ready for the campfire.
Cake cubes and condensed milk are out. Is there one more ingredient before I start toasting?
Yes—measure out 1 cup of coconut flakes into a shallow bowl or plate so the toasted cake can be rolled in it easily.
Should the cake go right into flames, or should I wait until the fire settles?
Wait for steady coals rather than active flames. Put the angel food cake cubes on toasting sticks and hold them over the campfire coals, turning them until the outside is browned.
The cubes are soft, so I'm worried they'll fall apart. Any trick while they're on the sticks?
Use larger cubes and push the stick through the center gently. Rotate slowly instead of shaking them, and pull them back once they're browned so they don't dry out or scorch.
They're lightly browned now. How do I coat them without making a mess?
Dip each toasted cake cube into the sweetened condensed milk just enough to coat the outside, then roll it in the coconut flakes right away while the milk is still sticky.
Should I coat every side with coconut, or just give it a quick roll?
A quick roll is fine, but you can turn it a few times if you want coconut on all sides. The goal is a browned cake cube with condensed milk holding the coconut flakes in place.
Once they're coated, do they need to sit, or can we eat them hot?
They're best served right away while the cake is warm and toasted. Let them cool just long enough that the condensed milk isn't too hot, then enjoy them straight from the campfire setup.

In a large bowl, combine the 1 cup cooked rice, beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper. Mix until everything is evenly distributed.

Use about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture in the center of each cabbage leaf. Keeping the portions even will make the rolls easier to tuck and shape.
I've portioned the filling onto the leaves. What's the best way to roll them neatly?
Fold the sides of each cabbage leaf inward, then roll it up around the filling, tucking in the ends as you go so the meat mixture stays enclosed.

Cook them until the turkey is no longer pink. If you want to check carefully, cut into the center of a patty or use a thermometer if you have one, then serve the Asian Turkey Burgers while they're hot.

Check that the batter is level across the pan and that no dry streaks remain. Once it's evenly spread in the greased 15-in. pan, you're set for the next baking direction.

Add the butter and toss the mixture as you go, lifting from the bottom of the bowl until the crumbs are coated evenly rather than packed down.

Add the vegetable oil, beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white sugar to the bowl together, then beat them until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.

Sift together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Sifting helps break up clumps and spreads the spices evenly through the dry mix.

Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty, keeping it snug against the outside edge. Once all 6 are wrapped, they're ready to go onto the preheated high-heat grill.

Knead it until it feels smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. It should become more springy as you work it and hold together as a soft, cohesive dough.

Use them drained, but don't rinse them. The marinated flavor is part of what seasons the hummus.

A rough chop is fine if your processor is small, but it isn't required. Add the chickpeas, garlic, drained marinated artichoke hearts, and lemon juice to the work bowl of the food processor.
Everything is in the bowl. The recipe mentions parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks—what do I do with those?
Keep them out of the processor. The instruction is to combine all ingredients except parsley and Quaker Rice Snacks, so just process the hummus mixture itself.

Pulse in short bursts, scraping down the sides if needed, until the mixture looks smooth.
It's mostly smooth, but I can still see a few tiny artichoke bits. Is that okay?
That's fine if you like a little texture. If you want it silkier, pulse a few more times until it's as smooth as you want.
The texture looks good now. How should I serve or store it?
Spoon the hummus into a serving bowl, cover it, and refrigerate it until you're ready to serve.

messages.content: Can you help me make Fruit Dip 2? I've got a mixing bowl out but haven't measured anything yet.

The whipped topping is thawed, and the cream cheese is softening. Do I use all the pineapple juice right away?
Not right away. Start by blending the cream cheese with the marshmallow creme and the thawed whipped topping until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.

A hand mixer will make it smoother faster, especially with the 8 ounces of cream cheese. A sturdy spoon or spatula can work too if the cream cheese is softened well.

Chill the fruit dip for 1 hour before serving. Cover the bowl so it stays fresh and the texture firms up slightly.

Serve it cold with fruit pieces like strawberries, apple slices, grapes, or pineapple chunks. Give it a quick stir after chilling if needed, then transfer it to a serving bowl.

Yes. Stir the chopped pecans together with the brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg until the spices look evenly distributed through the sugar.

Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl. That keeps the leavening and salt evenly mixed before they go into the batter.

Blend the butter and sugar together until they're well combined, then add the eggs and beat well. You want it to look smooth and cohesive before adding the next ingredients.

Add the apple butter, vanilla, and the wheat germ or bran cereal to the butter-sugar-egg mixture. Mix until those are worked in evenly.

Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream, mixing well after each addition. Work in a few additions rather than dumping everything in at once, and stop once the batter is evenly combined.
Can you help me make Baked Chicken Breasts Supreme? I'm setting things out before I handle the chicken.
Absolutely. Start by putting a large bowl on the counter, plus 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt or sour cream and 1/4 cup lemon juice. Those will form the base of the marinade.

Add 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 teaspoon celery seed to your setup. The recipe also says to combine the first eight ingredients in the large bowl, so mix those together until the marinade looks smooth and evenly seasoned.

Place the chicken into the mixture as-is unless your pieces need trimming. Turn each piece over in the bowl so all sides are coated with the yogurt or sour cream marinade.

Set out the crumbs in a shallow dish and have a clean plate or pan ready for the coated pieces. Remove the chicken from the marinade one piece at a time, letting excess marinade drip back into the bowl.

Lay each chicken piece into the crumbs, press gently, then turn it and coat the other side. Once every piece is crumb-coated, discard the used marinade and wipe down any surfaces that touched raw chicken.

Stir the dry mixture thoroughly so the baking powder and salt are evenly distributed, then make a well in the center of the bowl.

Beat the egg in the small bowl until it looks frothy, with small bubbles across the surface.

Add the cooking oil, milk, and bananas to the beaten egg mixture, then mix them together.

Give the wet bowl a quick scrape so the bananas, milk, oil, and egg are evenly mixed, then you're ready to combine it with the dry bowl according to your next muffin-mixing step.

I'm making Applesauce Bread I and have two loaf pans out. Can you guide me from the ingredients through mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 3 cups all-purpose flour, 3 eggs, 2 cups white sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil. You'll also need applesauce, plus either sour cream or buttermilk for the later mixing step.

Yes—preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can come up to temperature while you work.

For this recipe, grease and flour two 9 x 5 inch loaf pans. Tap out any extra flour so the coating is thin and even.

Beat together the 3 eggs, 2 cups white sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil until the mixture looks smooth and evenly combined.

That's okay for this stage. Give it a little more beating to make sure the eggs, sugar, and oil are fully combined, then you can move on.

Blend in the applesauce next, mixing until it's incorporated into the egg-sugar-oil mixture.

Use either sour cream or buttermilk—both fit the recipe. Blend your choice in after the applesauce, then the batter is ready for the prepared loaf pans.

Blend the butter and sugar together first until combined, then add the eggs and beat well. After that, mix in the apple butter, vanilla, and the wheat germ or bran cereal.

Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream, mixing well after each addition. Use steady mixing, but stop once everything is incorporated so the batter stays tender.
The batter is ready and the topping is waiting. Anything I should check before it goes into the pan?

Make sure the greased 9x13 inch pan is nearby, the oven is still at 350 degrees F, and the topping is ready to scatter over the batter according to your recipe's assembly. You've completed the prep: topping mixed, dry ingredients sifted, and batter combined with sour cream in alternating additions.
Can you guide me through making Anzac Biscuits I? I've cleared a mixing bowl and a small saucepan.

Yes. Put the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut into the mixing bowl and stir them together so the coconut and oats are evenly spread through the flour.

The butter is melting slowly. Should I raise the heat if it's taking a while?
Keep it low rather than rushing it. You only need the butter and syrup melted together, not browned or boiled hard.

Mix the baking soda with the boiling water, then add that soda mixture into the melted butter and syrup in the saucepan.

I'm making Butterscotch Basketball Cookies and have my mixing bowl out. What should I pull together before I start?

Set out 1 cup butterscotch chips, 1 cup softened butter with no substitutes, 1/2 cup sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar. You'll also need egg, milk, and vanilla when you get to the wet ingredients.
The butter is soft and the sugars are measured. Should I melt the chips right away?
Yes. Put the butterscotch chips in a microwave-safe bowl and melt them gently, stirring as needed so they smooth out instead of scorching.
They're melted. Do I pour them into the bowl with the butter now?
Let the melted chips cool for 10 minutes first. That keeps the warm butterscotch from softening the butter too much or scrambling the egg later.
While those cool, what texture am I looking for with the butter and sugars?
Cream the softened butter with both sugars until the mixture looks lighter, fluffy, and well blended. Scrape the bowl once or twice so there aren't streaks of packed brown sugar hiding at the bottom.

Add the egg, milk, and vanilla to the creamed butter and sugars, then mix well until the batter looks smooth and evenly combined.

Pour the cooled melted chips in slowly with the mixer on low, then beat until they're fully incorporated. Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl so the butterscotch is evenly mixed throughout.
Can you guide me through Fancy Brussels Sprouts? I've got a saucepan out and want to set up the ingredients before turning on the stove.

Put the water, parsley, sugar, and salt into the saucepan together, then set it over medium heat. Let that mixture come up to a boil.

The liquid is boiling. Are the brussels sprouts supposed to go in whole at this point?
Yes, add the brussels sprouts to the boiling liquid now. Try to spread them out in the saucepan so they cook evenly.
They're in the pan. Do I leave it uncovered or put the lid on?
Cover the saucepan and let the sprouts simmer for 6-8 minutes, or until they're tender. Keep the heat adjusted so it stays at a gentle simmer rather than a hard boil.
I'm at about 6 minutes and they're starting to soften. What texture am I looking for before draining?
They should be tender when pierced, but not collapsing. If they still feel firm in the center, give them another minute or two, staying within that 6-8 minute range if possible.
They're tender now. I drained them—what goes in at the end?
Add the water chestnuts and butter to the drained brussels sprouts, then heat everything through just until the butter melts and the water chestnuts are warmed. Then they're ready to serve.

Give it a little more time if needed; the texture cue matters here. The squash should be tender enough that the knife slides in easily before you take it out.
