Yes, butter the large cookie sheet now so it's ready when the hot mixture is done. Candy sets quickly, so having the pan prepared before the saucepan goes on the heat will make the pour easier.
The sheet is buttered. What goes into the saucepan, and how low should I keep the burner?
Set the saucepan over low heat and add the butter, the 2 cups white sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds. Keep the heat gentle while the butter melts into the sugar and almonds.
It's starting to melt together around the edges. Do I stir the whole time right now?
Yes. Stir constantly while it heats, making sure the butter and sugar combine evenly and the almonds stay distributed. Keep stirring until the mixture comes to a boil.
It just reached a boil and looks glossy. Should I keep stirring or leave it alone?
Once it boils, stop stirring. Don't stir or shake the pan from this point; let it cook undisturbed so the candy can reach the right stage.
I have a thermometer clipped on. What temperature am I aiming for, and is there another way to check it?

Heat it to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. If you're checking without relying only on the thermometer, drop a small amount of syrup into cold water; it should form hard, brittle threads.
The thermometer is in range and the cold-water drop snapped into brittle threads. How do I get it onto the sheet safely?

Carefully pour the hot buttercrunch mixture onto the large buttered cookie sheet right away. Keep your hands clear of the syrup, tilt the saucepan steadily, and let it spread out on the prepared sheet.
I'm making Coq au Vin alla Italiana and have a large skillet ready. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I turn on the heat?
Absolutely. Put out 4 pounds of dark meat chicken pieces, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 5 cloves of crushed garlic, and 1/2 cup all-purpose flour.
Chicken is out, and I've measured the oil and flour. Should I prep the garlic all at once?
Yes, crush all 5 cloves now. You'll use only 1/2 of the garlic when the oil is hot, so keep the rest nearby for later in the recipe.
Got it. The skillet is on the stove; how hot should I get it for the oil?
Heat the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in the large skillet over a steady medium to medium-high heat, just until it looks glossy and moves easily across the pan.
The oil is glossy. I don't want the garlic to burn—what should I do next?
Add 1/2 of the crushed garlic to the skillet and stir it briefly so it perfumes the oil. Keep it moving and don't let it get dark.
The garlic smells fragrant now. What should I do with the flour while that's happening?
Season the 1/2 cup all-purpose flour with poultry seasoning, then spread it in a shallow dish so the chicken pieces are easy to coat.
Flour is seasoned. Should the chicken be coated heavily or just dusted?
Dredge the dark meat chicken pieces in the seasoned flour so they're coated all over, then shake off any thick excess before they go into the skillet.
The chicken is coated, and I'm ready to brown it. How long should it stay in the pan?
Lay the chicken pieces into the skillet without crowding them and brown them for 4 or 5 minutes, turning as needed so the flour coating takes on color.
I want to put together the Double Fudge Brownie Mix. What should I set out before I start filling the jar?
Set out a clean 1 quart or 1 liter jar, plus 2 cups white sugar and 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder to begin with.
I found the jar, sugar, and cocoa. Are there any dry ingredients or add-ins missing?
Yes—add 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1 cup chopped pecans to your workspace. Those are the remaining ingredients for the mix.
Should I stir everything together before it goes into the jar, or is this supposed to look layered?
Keep it layered. Pour the ingredients into the jar in the order listed: white sugar, cocoa powder, all-purpose flour, then chopped pecans.
The sugar layer is in, but the cocoa is dusty. Any way to keep the sides of the jar neat?
Use a small funnel or spoon the cocoa in slowly, then tap the jar gently on the counter so the layer settles without smearing too much up the glass.
Cocoa and flour are layered now. The jar is getting full—do the pecans still go on top?
Yes, the chopped pecans go on top as the final layer. Press them down lightly if you need a little more room for the lid.
The lid fits. What needs to go on the tag?
Attach a tag that says to preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
Is there anything else from this recipe that I should include before I give it away?
For this recipe, the required mix is complete once the jar is layered and the tag with the 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) oven instruction is attached.
I want to make Chocolate Crisps, and I've cleared a small space by the stove. What should I set out before I start?
Set out 1 tablespoon softened butter, 1 egg white, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also want cookie sheets, a small saucepan, and a medium-sized bowl.
I have the ingredients out, but the butter is only partly soft. Is that okay for this recipe?
That's fine, since the butter will be melted anyway. Go ahead and preheat the oven to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C, while you get the pans ready.
The oven is set to 300. Do the cookie sheets need parchment, or should I just grease them?
For this recipe, grease the cookie sheets. Give them a light, even coating so the crisps release easily after baking.
Cookie sheets are greased. I'm moving to the stove now—what heat should I use for the butter?
Put the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Let it melt and continue cooking until it turns lightly browned.
How closely should I watch it? A tablespoon seems like it could brown pretty fast.
Stay right by the pan and watch the color. With only 1 tablespoon, it can go from melted to browned quickly, so take it off the heat once it looks lightly browned rather than dark.
It's melted and just starting to smell nutty. Should I wait for a deeper color?
No deeper than lightly browned. Once it has that pale golden-brown look and nutty aroma, you're at the point the recipe wants.
Got it. Where does the browned butter go now?
Pour the lightly browned butter into a medium-sized bowl. That sets you up to continue with the egg white, sugar, and vanilla from there.
Can you walk me through A 1 Chicken Soup? I've got a large pot ready but haven't started heating it yet.
Yes. Set out 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 2 skinless chicken leg quarters, 1/2 cup chopped onion, and 2 quarts water. You'll also need chicken bouillon for the broth step.
I have the chicken leg quarters and oil. Should I add the oil before the pot is hot?
Put the large pot over medium heat, add the vegetable oil, and let it warm briefly. Then add the chicken pieces and cook them until they're browned on both sides.
The chicken is in the pot now. How dark should the browning get?
Aim for a clear golden-brown surface on each side, not burned or blackened. Turn the pieces as needed so both sides get color before you add the onion.
Both sides are browned, and I've got the chopped onion measured at 1/2 cup.
Stir the chopped onion into the pot around the chicken and cook it for 2 minutes more. Keep the heat at medium and stir so the onion softens without scorching.
The onion has softened a bit and smells good. Do I pour in all the water at once?
Yes, pour in the 2 quarts water, then add the chicken bouillon. Bring the pot up to a boil.
It's starting to bubble around the edges. Should I cover it while it comes to a boil?
You can partially cover it to help it heat faster, but keep an eye on it so it doesn't boil over. Once it reaches a full boil, you'll lower the heat.
It's boiling steadily now. What do I do for the final cook?
Reduce the heat and let the soup simmer for 45 minutes. Keep it at a gentle simmer rather than a hard boil, then serve once the chicken has cooked through and the broth has developed flavor.
I'm planning to make BBQ Chuck Roast today and I've cleared space for the grill prep. Can you guide me through it?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (5 pound) chuck roast, 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle of beer.
I've got the roast, the sauces, and the beer. Anything for the marinade bowl before the meat goes in?
Yes. In a large bowl, combine the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt. Stir it well so the seasonings are spread through the liquid.
The marinade is mixed. Should I use a shallow dish or keep it in the big bowl?
Use whatever lets the roast sit in contact with the marinade and be covered. Place the chuck roast into the marinade, cover it, and refrigerate it for six hours.
Six hours works for my schedule. Do I just leave it alone in the fridge?
Turn it often during that chilling time so more of the 5 pound roast gets coated evenly with the marinade.
It has been marinating and I've turned it a few times. What should I do with the grill?
Preheat an outdoor grill for indirect heat, so the roast can cook away from direct flame rather than sitting right over the hottest spot.
The grill is heating for indirect cooking. Do I take the roast straight from the bowl to the grate?
Remove the roast from the marinade before it goes to the grill. Let the excess drip back into the bowl so it's easier to handle.
What happens to the leftover marinade after I lift out the roast?
Pour the marinade into a saucepan. That keeps it separate from the roast as you move into the grilling stage.
I want to make Feta Chicken Salad for lunch. Can you walk me through it while I prep?

Absolutely. Set out a serving bowl and a smaller mixing bowl. For the salad base, you'll need 3 cups diced cooked chicken, 2 large stalks celery diced, 1 red bell pepper seeded and diced, and 1/2 red onion diced.
The chicken is already diced, and I'm chopping the vegetables now. Does the bell pepper go in right away too?
The recipe has you mix the chicken, celery, and red onion in the serving bowl first. Keep the diced red bell pepper nearby so it's ready to fold in with the salad as you bring everything together.
Okay, chicken, celery, and red onion are in the serving bowl. The onion pieces are pretty small.
That sounds good for a chicken salad. Give those ingredients a quick toss so the celery and onion are distributed through the chicken rather than sitting in clumps.
Mixed. I have the smaller bowl ready—what goes into the dressing?
In the separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the dressing looks fairly even. It can stay a little textured from the feta.
The feta is leaving small chunks, but the mayo and sour cream are blended. Should I add the red pepper before the dressing?
Yes, add the seeded and diced red bell pepper to the chicken mixture now, then spoon the feta dressing over the top.
The pepper and dressing are in the serving bowl. I don't want to mash the chicken—how much should I stir?
Use a folding motion from the bottom of the bowl, turning just until the dressing coats the chicken and vegetables evenly. Stop once it looks blended.
It's coated and looks creamy. How do I adjust it before serving?
Taste a bite, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Once the seasoning tastes balanced, it's ready to serve.
I want to make Dilled Garlic today. I've got clean jars ready, but can you guide me so I pack them correctly?
Absolutely. Have 2 pounds peeled garlic ready, along with 1 sprig of chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar.
The garlic is peeled and the dill is chopped. Should the containers be sterile before I add anything?
Yes, use sterile containers. Pack them with the peeled garlic, chopped fresh dill, and a little cayenne pepper, leaving about an inch of space at the top.
I'm filling the jars now. Is the cayenne meant to be measured exactly?
No exact amount is given—add cayenne pepper to taste. A light sprinkle is fine if you want gentle heat, or a bit more if you want it spicier.
The jars are packed to about an inch below the top. What do I heat on the stove?
Pour the 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar into a medium saucepan and mix in the salt.
The vinegar and salt are in the saucepan. Do I just warm it or take it higher?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture to a boil so it's hot when it goes into the containers.
It has reached a boil. Should I let it cool at all before pouring?
No, pour it while hot. Carefully ladle or pour the hot vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne.
The hot liquid is going in and the garlic is covered. Anything I should check before I stop?
Make sure each container still has about an inch of headspace and that the garlic mixture is covered by the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture.
I'm making Banana Chip Muffins I and I've got a mixing bowl ready. Can you help me set up the ingredients without getting ahead of myself?

Absolutely. Start by putting the dry ingredients within reach: 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also need chocolate chips for the dry bowl, plus an egg, cooking oil, milk, and bananas for the wet mixture.
I measured the flour and sugar already. Should the baking powder and salt go in the same bowl?
Yes, measure the baking powder and salt into the same large bowl with the flour and sugar. Add the chocolate chips there too, since the recipe has all of those measured together before mixing.
The dry bowl is full now. Do I just stir it, or am I trying to make it fluffy?
Stir it thoroughly so the baking powder, salt, sugar, flour, and chocolate chips are evenly distributed. After that, use your spoon to make a well in the center of the dry mixture.
I made a dip in the middle. For the egg, do I crack it straight into that well?
Use a small bowl for the egg instead. Beat the egg there until it looks frothy, then you'll mix the other wet ingredients into that small bowl.
The egg is frothy. I have the oil, milk, and bananas beside me, but the recipe doesn't show amounts here.
Go with the amounts listed in your full recipe if you have them. For this step, the action is to mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the frothy beaten egg until the wet mixture is combined.
Should the bananas be completely smooth before I add them?
They should be mixed into the wet ingredients well, but the recipe doesn't require a perfectly smooth puree. Just make sure the bananas are incorporated with the egg, oil, and milk.
Wet mixture is combined, and the dry bowl still has the well in the center. What should I be careful about next?

You're lined up correctly: dry ingredients and chocolate chips are mixed with a well in the center, and the egg, cooking oil, milk, and bananas are combined separately. When you bring them together, scrape the wet mixture into the well so it's easier to fold everything evenly.
I'm making Bocconcini Salad and have a big salad bowl ready. Can you talk me through what to set out?
Set out 1 pound bocconcini, the bite-size mozzarella balls, plus 8 cherry tomatoes that you'll halve. You'll also need 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper and 1/2 cup chopped celery.
The mozzarella is drained, and I've halved the cherry tomatoes. Should the pepper and celery go in raw?
Yes, keep them raw for crunch. Chop the green bell pepper and celery, then measure 1/2 cup of each.
I've got both chopped. The recipe mentions greens too—how should I handle those?
Add the bocconcini, halved cherry tomatoes, chopped bell pepper, chopped celery, endive, and arugula to the large salad bowl. Keep the pieces loose so the dressing can coat everything.
Everything is in the bowl, but I haven't dressed it yet. What do I whisk together?
Whisk lemon juice and olive oil together until they look combined, then pour that dressing over the salad.
The dressing is on. Do I season before or after tossing?
Season it now with salt and pepper to taste, then toss gently so the mozzarella and vegetables don't get crushed.
It's tossed, but I want to be sure it's coated enough. What should I look for?
Look for a light sheen on the bocconcini, tomatoes, bell pepper, celery, endive, and arugula. If the dressing is pooled at the bottom, lift and turn the salad a few more times.
Looks evenly coated now. I'm serving it right away—what's the last touch?
Sprinkle basil over the top and serve the Bocconcini Salad immediately while the greens are fresh and the mozzarella is still cool.
I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip and want to get organized before the oven goes on. What should I pull out first?
Set out 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream. Those make the creamy base, so it helps to have them measured before you start mixing.
Mayonnaise and sour cream are measured. What else belongs in the dish?
You'll also need 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, plus 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts that have been drained and chopped.
The artichokes are drained and chopped. Do I need to prep the baking dish now?
Yes. Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish for the dip, and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Oven is heating. Should I mix this in a separate bowl or directly in the casserole dish?

Mix it directly in the 1-1/2 quart casserole dish: combine the mayonnaise, sour cream, garlic and mushroom soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat until everything is evenly distributed.
It's all in the casserole dish, but I'm checking the texture. Should it be completely smooth?
It does not need to be smooth. The base should look creamy and well mixed, with visible pieces of chopped artichoke and crab throughout.
The mixture looks evenly combined. Does it need a lid or foil for baking?
Bake it uncovered so the top can heat through nicely. Put the casserole dish in the 350 degrees F oven for 30 minutes.
The 30 minutes are almost up. What's the best way to serve it?
Serve the Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip immediately while it's hot and creamy. Set it out with whatever dippers you like, and keep the casserole dish on a heat-safe surface.
I want to make Caramelized Apple Bites. What should I get ready before I start chopping?
Set out 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrap them, and chop them into smaller pieces so they melt more easily. You'll also need 2 tablespoons light corn syrup and a medium microwave-safe bowl.
The caramels are unwrapped and chopped. Do the apples need to be prepared now too?
Yes. Peel, core, and dice 2 apples. Keep the pieces bite-sized so they'll coat evenly in the caramel mixture.
Apples are diced. Should they go into the bowl with the caramel right away?
Not yet. Put only the chopped caramels and the light corn syrup into the medium microwave-safe bowl first.
They're in the bowl. How long should I microwave it?
Microwave the bowl on high for approximately 30 seconds, just until the caramels are melted with the corn syrup.
It looks mostly melted but a little thick. Is that okay for coating?
Yes, as long as it's melted enough to toss with the apples. Add the diced apples to the bowl while the caramel mixture is still warm.
The apples are in. What's the best way to mix without mashing them?
Gently toss the apple pieces through the caramel and light corn syrup mixture until they're coated all over.
They're coated and glossy. Can I serve them immediately?
Let the Caramelized Apple Bites cool before serving so the coating can settle and they're easier to eat.
I'm making Eggplant Mixed Grill and I want to set up the marinade before I start cutting vegetables. What should I pull out?

Get a large resealable plastic bag ready, plus 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil. You'll also need vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic for the marinade.
The herbs and oil are measured. Do I mix everything right in the bag?

Yes. Add the olive oil, parsley, oregano, basil, vinegar, kosher salt, pepper, and garlic directly to the large resealable bag. Seal it loosely or hold the top closed and gently move it around so the marinade starts to combine.
I've got onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and both peppers cut. Do they all go in together?
They do. Place the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper into the bag with the marinade.
The bag is pretty full. How should I make sure the vegetables get coated without making a mess?

Seal the bag tightly, leaving a little room for the vegetables to move, then turn and gently massage the bag until the marinade is distributed over the onion, asparagus, mushrooms, eggplant, and peppers.
Once it's coated, how long does it need in the fridge?
Marinate it for 2 hours in the refrigerator. Turn the bag occasionally during that time so the vegetables keep getting exposed to the oil, herbs, vinegar, garlic, salt, and pepper.
The 2 hours are almost up. When should I deal with the grill?
Preheat the grill for high heat as the marinating time ends, so it's hot and ready when the vegetables come out of the refrigerator.
Before I put the vegetables on, is there anything I should do to the grate?
Lightly oil the grill grate. That helps the marinated eggplant, peppers, onion, asparagus, and mushrooms release more cleanly when they hit the hot grill.
Can you guide me through Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic? I'm starting by checking the marinade ingredients.

Absolutely. For the paste, measure 1/4 cup olive oil, mince 8 cloves garlic, and have 2 1/2 teaspoons salt plus 1 teaspoon pepper ready. You'll also mix in the cumin and oregano called for in the lamb seasoning.
I've got the oil, garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano out. Should the lamb be cold when I season it?
Coat it before it comes up to temperature: mix the oil, garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano into a paste, then spread that paste over both sides of the butterflied lamb.
Both sides are coated. How long should it sit on the counter?
Let the lamb stand for an hour, until the meat comes to room temperature. That rest helps it cook more evenly under the broiler.
While it rests, what should I set up in the oven?
Move the oven rack to the upper or upper-middle position, depending on how thick the lamb is. Then preheat the broiler on high for at least 10 minutes so it's fully hot.
My lamb is fairly thick in spots. I'll use the upper-middle rack. What pan setup do I need?
Line a roasting pan with foil for easier cleanup, then set a large wire rack over it. When the lamb is ready, place it on the rack cut side up.
It's on the wire rack cut side up, and the broiler is hot. Do I just leave the pan in one position?
Broil it for about 8 minutes, but move the pan as needed so the entire surface browns evenly rather than scorching in one hot spot.
What should I be watching for during those 8 minutes?
Look for an even browned surface across the cut side. Keep an eye on the edges and thicker areas, shifting the pan so the browning stays consistent under the broiler.

source_seed.recipe_title: Broiled Slow Roasted Butterflied Leg of Lamb With Cumin and Garlic

messages.content: Can you help me make Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2 this afternoon?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and start with the measured fats and sugars: 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil.
The butter is soft and I've got both sugars measured. Should the oil go in with them right away?
Yes, add the vegetable oil to the bowl with the butter, sugar, and confectioners' sugar, then cream everything together until the mixture looks smooth and well blended.
I'm using a hand mixer. What texture am I aiming for before I stop mixing?
Look for a creamy, uniform mixture with no large streaks of butter left. It doesn't need to be fluffy for a long time—just evenly combined.
That looks good. I noticed the recipe calls for eggs and vanilla next, but they weren't in my measured lineup.
Go ahead and add the eggs and vanilla as the recipe directs, then mix well so they're fully incorporated into the butter, sugars, and oil.
The batter is looser now and smells like vanilla. What dry ingredients go in?
Add the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar. Mix gently at first so the dry ingredients don't puff out of the bowl, then keep going until the dough comes together.
Should I scrape the bowl before adding anything else?
Yes, scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl so any butter-sugar mixture or dry pockets get worked evenly into the dough.
I have chopped pecans nearby. Are they required, or can I leave them out?
They're optional. Stir in the pecans if desired, or leave them out for plain cinnamon sugar cookies.
I'm making Cake Doughnuts today. Can you help me organize the ingredients before I start?
Absolutely. For the dry base, measure out 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've got the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt measured. What bowl should I use for mixing?
Use a large bowl so you have room to stir everything evenly. Add the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, salt, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and the nutmeg to that bowl.
The dry ingredients are in the bowl. Should I whisk them or just stir?
Stir them together well, making sure the baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt are evenly spread through the flour and sugar.
That mixture looks even. I have the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla nearby—how do they go in?
Make a well in the center of the dry mixture, then pour the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla into that well.
Everything is in the center now. I don't want to overwork the dough—what texture am I aiming for?
Mix until it's well blended. Stop once the ingredients are combined and you don't see dry streaks; there's no need to keep beating it after that.
It's mixed and looks cohesive. Does it need to rest before shaping or cooking?
Yes. Cover the bowl and refrigerate the dough for 1 hour so it firms up before you continue.
Should I cover it tightly, or is a loose cover fine for the refrigerator?
Cover it well with plastic wrap or a fitted lid, then place it in the refrigerator for the full 1 hour. After that rest, it should be easier to handle.
Can you help me make Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken? I've got chicken breasts out but want to make sure I'm not missing anything.

Absolutely. For this recipe, you'll need 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, salt and pepper to taste, 2 teaspoons olive oil, and 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions.
I found the can of diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions. Should I season the chicken before the skillet is hot?
Yes. Pat the chicken breasts dry if they're damp, then season both sides with salt and pepper so they're ready to go straight into the pan.
The chicken is seasoned. What pan setup should I use?
Use a large skillet and add the olive oil. Heat it over medium-high heat until the oil looks loose and shimmery.
I measured the oil and the pan is warming. Do I add all the chicken at once?
Place the chicken breasts in the skillet in a single layer. If they crowd the pan, cook them in batches so they can brown instead of steam.
They fit in one layer. How much should I move them around?
Let them sit long enough to brown on the first side, then turn them once and brown the other side. Try not to keep flipping them.
Both sides have some color now. Should the tomatoes go in yet?
Not yet based on the steps you're following. Remove the chicken from the pan and set it aside after it's browned on both sides.
Okay, I moved the chicken to a plate. Anything I should do with the skillet right now?
For this part, just keep the browned chicken set aside and keep the skillet available for the next stage of the recipe.

source_seed.recipe_title: Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken

messages.content: I want to make Dilled Garlic today. Can you help me set up before I start filling jars?

Absolutely. Have sterile containers ready, plus 2 pounds peeled garlic, 1 sprig chopped fresh dill, cayenne pepper to taste, and 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar. You'll also need a medium saucepan for heating the vinegar and salt.
The garlic is peeled and the containers are sterile. Should the dill and cayenne go in with the garlic right away?
Yes. Pack the sterile containers with the peeled garlic, chopped fresh dill, and cayenne pepper, stopping within an inch of the top so there's room for the hot vinegar mixture.
I'm filling them now. Does the garlic need to be packed tightly or left a little loose?
Settle it in firmly enough to use the space, but don't crush the cloves. Keep that inch of headspace at the top of each container.
The jars are filled to about an inch from the top. What should I do with the vinegar?
Pour the 4 1/2 cups distilled white vinegar into a medium saucepan, then mix in the salt called for in the recipe.
The vinegar and salt are in the saucepan. How hot should I get it?
Bring the vinegar and salt mixture to a boil. Keep an eye on it so it doesn't splash, since you'll be pouring it while hot.
It has reached a boil. Do I pour it straight over the garlic?
Yes, carefully pour the hot distilled white vinegar and salt mixture into the containers over the garlic, dill, and cayenne.
Should the liquid cover the garlic completely, or is the inch of space still important?
Cover the garlic mixture with the hot vinegar mixture while still leaving that inch of space at the top. Once the containers are filled, wipe away any spills from the rims and outside.
I'm making Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken and want to get the marinade started. Can you guide me without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl and measure 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum.
Those are on the counter. The recipe mentions mustard and garlic too—should they go into the same bowl?
Yes, add the mustard and garlic to that same bowl with the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and rum. Stir enough to loosen the molasses so the glaze starts looking smooth and glossy.
The molasses is streaky at the bottom. Should I whisk it or just keep stirring with a spoon?
A whisk will make this easier. Scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl as you whisk so the molasses fully blends into the ketchup and juice.
Okay, it looks even now. When do I season it?
Season the glaze with salt and pepper to taste, then mix it well again so the seasoning is spread through the whole bowl.
I've got the glaze seasoned. What baking dish should I use for the chicken pieces?
Use a 9x13 inch baking dish and oil it lightly so the chicken doesn't stick while it marinates and later cooks.
Dish is oiled and the chicken pieces are in it. How much glaze goes on now?
Brush both sides of the chicken with the prepared glaze, using about 1/2 of the glaze. Try to coat the pieces evenly, and save the rest for later use.
Everything is coated. I'm not cooking right away—what should I do with the dish?
Cover the baking dish and refrigerate the chicken to marinate for at least 2 hours, or leave it overnight if that works better for your timing.
Can you guide me through making Carrot and Coriander Soup II? I've got a pot out but haven't prepped anything yet.
Absolutely. Start by prepping 4 large carrots into 1 inch pieces and chopping 1/4 large onion. Set both near your large saucepan.
The carrots and onion are ready. What other ingredients should I pull out before I turn on the stove?
You'll also need 1 quart vegetable broth and 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro. Once those are measured, you're ready to load the saucepan.
I have the broth measured and the cilantro chopped. Do all of those go in together?
Yes. Put the carrots, chopped onion, vegetable broth, and cilantro into the large saucepan together.
Everything is in the pan. Should I cover it, or just bring it up uncovered?
Bring it to a boil; covering can help it heat faster, but keep an eye on it so it doesn't bubble over. Once it's boiling, cook until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes.
It's been close to 10 minutes. How soft should the carrot pieces feel?
They should be tender enough that a fork slides into them easily. If any 1 inch pieces still feel firm in the center, give them another minute or two, then check again.
They're fork-tender now. I'm worried about blending something too hot—what's the safe move?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the soup cool slightly before pureeing. That short rest makes blending safer and less steamy.
It has cooled a bit. I have both a blender and a food processor—what texture am I aiming for?
Use either the blender or food processor to puree the soup until smooth. If using a blender, work carefully in batches if needed, then serve once the texture is silky.
Can you guide me through making Date Nut Bars? I've got the counter cleared and a large mixing bowl ready.
Absolutely. Start by setting out the dry ingredients: 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need dates and nuts for the bowl.
I measured the sugar and flour, and the dates and nuts are nearby. Should I mix the dry things together before adding anything wet?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the sugar, flour, baking powder, salt, dates, and nuts until they're evenly distributed.
The dates are a little sticky, but they're mixed through the flour now. What wet ingredients go in?
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla to that mixture. Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened; the batter is supposed to be very stiff, so don't worry if it takes some effort.
It's definitely stiff and heavy. I don't see dry flour pockets anymore—should I stop stirring?
Stop there. Once the dry ingredients are moistened, extra stirring isn't needed.
What pan should I use, and does it need anything before the batter goes in?
Use a greased 15-in pan. Spread the stiff batter into it as evenly as you can, pushing it toward the corners.
The batter is in the pan, but the top looks uneven. Is that okay before baking?
That's fine, though you can smooth the top lightly with a spatula so it bakes more evenly. Then bake it at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes.
How will I know when to pull the pan out instead of just watching the timer?
Look for the bars to be golden brown. Start checking around 20 minutes, and take them out by 25 minutes if they've reached that color.
Can you help me make Garden Potato Salad? I've already cooked and peeled the potatoes, but I want to make sure I prep everything in the right order.
Absolutely. Cube the 6 large cooked, peeled potatoes and put them near a large mixing bowl. Slice the 4 hard-cooked eggs too, but keep them gentle so they don't crumble too much.
Potatoes are cubed, and the eggs are sliced. What should I cut next for the bowl?
Slice 2 celery ribs and 6 green onions with their tops. Add those to the large bowl with the potatoes and sliced eggs.
The celery and green onions are in. I see radishes, salt, and pepper mentioned in the method—do those go in now too?
Yes. Add the radishes, then season the bowl with salt and pepper. Gently combine the potatoes, eggs, celery, green onions, radishes, salt, and pepper, then set that bowl aside.
The salad base is mixed and set aside. What pan should I use for the dressing?
Use a saucepan for the dressing. In it, combine the eggs, vinegar, sugar, dry mustard, and salt before you turn on the heat.
I've got those dressing ingredients in the saucepan. Should I whisk it cold or just start heating?
Give it a good stir while it's still cool so the sugar, dry mustard, salt, eggs, and vinegar are evenly blended. Then place the saucepan over medium heat.
It's on medium heat now. What texture am I watching for?
Cook and stir constantly over medium heat until the dressing thickens. You're looking for it to coat the spoon more noticeably rather than run off like a thin liquid.
The dressing has thickened. Do I pour it over the potatoes right away?
Let the dressing cool first. Once cooled, it will be ready to use with the prepared potato mixture.
Can you help me get started on Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake? I want to make sure I have the dry ingredients and pans ready before I turn on the oven.

Absolutely. For this stage, gather 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate, chopped. You'll also need 2 round 9 inch cake pans.
I've got the flour, baking soda, salt, and chocolate on the counter. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can come up to temperature while you prepare the pans and dry mixture.
Oven is set. For the 9 inch pans, do I just butter them, or do they need flour too?
Grease and flour both 9 inch pans. Coat the inside evenly, then add a little flour and tap it around so the bottoms and sides are lightly covered.
The pans are greased and floured. I'm seeing a few thick flour patches in one corner; is that okay?
A light dusting is best. Tap out any loose clumps so the cake releases cleanly without leaving dry floury spots on the surface.
Done. I'm ready to mix the dry ingredients—do they all go in one bowl?
Yes. Sift together the 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt into a bowl so they're evenly combined and aerated.
The sifted mixture looks even. Should I add the chopped unsweetened chocolate to that bowl now?
Not in this listed prep step. Keep the 6 chopped 1 ounce squares of unsweetened chocolate nearby, but set the sifted flour, baking soda, and salt mixture aside for the moment.
Got it—the dry bowl is set aside and the chocolate is waiting. Anything else I should check before moving on?
You're in good shape: the oven is at 350 degrees F, the 2 greased and floured 9 inch pans are ready, and the sifted dry ingredients are set aside.
Can you help me make Date Nut Bars? I've got a large mixing bowl out and want to make sure I start in the right order.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need dates, nuts, eggs, butter, and vanilla for the batter.
The dry ingredients are measured. Should I mix the dates and nuts in with those right away?
Yes. In the large bowl, combine the sugar, flour, baking powder, salt, dates, and nuts so everything is evenly distributed before the wet ingredients go in.
That's mixed. The dates are a little sticky, but they're coated with flour now. What should I add next?
Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla to the bowl. Stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened; don't worry if it feels hard to mix, because the batter should be very stiff.
It's definitely stiff and thick. I don't see dry flour anymore—should I keep stirring to smooth it out?
Stop there if the dry ingredients are moistened. Overmixing isn't needed for these bars, and a stiff, slightly rugged batter is expected.
Okay. I have a 15-inch pan ready. Does it need anything before I put the batter in?
Grease the 15-in pan well, especially the corners, then spread the stiff batter into an even layer. A spatula or lightly buttered hands can help press it out.
The batter is spread in the pan. What oven setting and bake time am I using?
Bake it at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes. Start checking near 20 minutes and look for the top to turn golden brown.
If the edges brown first but the center still looks pale, should I pull it out?
Give it a little more time within that 20-25 minute window, watching closely. It's ready when the bars are golden brown overall, then let the pan cool before cutting so the pieces hold together.
I'd like to make Broiled Egg Salad Sandwiches. Can you guide me without rushing? I already have a mixing bowl out.

Absolutely. Set out 3 chopped hard-cooked eggs, 1/4 cup crushed saltine crackers, 1/4 cup chopped celery, and 1 tablespoon diced pimientos. You'll want a second bowl too, since the dressing gets mixed separately.
The eggs are chopped, and I measured the crackers and celery. Should the pimientos go in with those right away?
Yes. Put the eggs, crushed saltines, chopped celery, and diced pimientos together in the bowl. Give them a light toss so the crackers and vegetables are evenly spread through the eggs.
That mixture looks a little chunky but evenly combined. What goes in the other bowl?
In the second bowl, combine the mayonnaise, milk, salt, garlic salt, and pepper. Mix it well until it looks smooth and pourable enough to coat the egg mixture.
I mixed the dressing. Should I pour all of it over the eggs, or add it slowly?
Add it to the egg mixture and stir gently. Fold rather than mash, so the chopped eggs keep some texture while everything gets coated.
It's creamy now. I have the muffin halves ready—do I need to grease the baking sheet?
No greasing needed. Use an ungreased baking sheet, then spoon about 1/3 cup of the egg salad mixture onto each muffin half.
Some of the topping wants to slide off the muffin edges. Any trick before I put them on the pan?
Mound the mixture toward the center of each muffin half and press it lightly with the spoon so it sits in place. Then transfer the prepared halves to the ungreased baking sheet.
They're all on the baking sheet now. Is there anything else I should check before broiling?

Make sure each muffin half has an even layer of filling and the sheet is stable under them. At this point, the recipe has you ready for broiling with the assembled sandwiches on the ungreased baking sheet.
Can you help me make Broccoli Coleslaw? I've got a mixing bowl out, but I want to make sure I don't miss anything.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup distilled white vinegar, and 1/2 cup white sugar for the dressing.
Those are on the counter. I also have a 3 ounce package of chicken flavored ramen noodles—do I use the seasoning?
Yes, keep the seasoning packet aside and crush the ramen noodles separately. The packet goes into the dressing, while the crushed noodles get stirred in later.
What should I mix the dressing in, and does it need to be whisked a lot?
Use a small bowl. Combine the olive oil, distilled white vinegar, white sugar, and the ramen seasoning packet, then mix well until the sugar and seasoning are evenly blended.
The dressing is mixed. Should I pour it over the vegetables right away?
Hold off for now. Refrigerate the dressing for at least 1 hour before serving, or let it chill overnight if you're preparing ahead.
While that chills, I'm getting the salad bowl ready. What goes in besides the noodles?
In a large bowl, combine the broccoli, carrots, green onions, and sunflower seeds.
Should the ramen be completely crushed, or left a little chunky for crunch?
Crush the ramen noodles, but they can stay a bit uneven so the coleslaw has crunch. Stir the crushed noodles into the broccoli mixture.
When I'm ready to serve, do I just add the chilled dressing and toss everything together?
Yes. Give the chilled dressing a quick stir, pour it over the broccoli mixture with the ramen, and toss until everything is coated. Serve it cold.
Can you help me make Brownie Mix in a Jar III? I've got my counter cleared and want to make sure I'm measuring it right.
Absolutely. Set out the dry ingredients first: 1/2 cup flaked coconut, 1/2 cup white sugar, 2 cups packed brown sugar, and 2 cups all-purpose flour.
For the brown sugar, should I press it into the cup instead of scooping it loosely?
Yes, pack the brown sugar firmly into the measuring cup so the 2 cups are measured as packed brown sugar. Keep the coconut and white sugar measured separately for now.
The dry ingredients are measured. What bowl should I use before I add the wet stuff?
Use a large mixing bowl. Combine the flour with the salt and baking powder, and stir until they look evenly blended.
I don't see salt or baking powder in my measured pile yet. Do I still mix them with the flour?
Yes, the recipe's cooking directions call for mixing flour, salt, and baking powder together, so add those to the flour and whisk or stir them through before adding anything else.
Okay, the flour mixture looks even. My butter is softened—how much goes in?
Add 3/4 cup butter or margarine, but don't use diet margarine. Work it into the dry mixture until it starts coming together.
It's a thick mixture now. I have the eggs ready—do they go in whole?
Lightly beat 2 eggs first, then mix them in along with 2 teaspoons vanilla. Stir until the batter is evenly combined.
The batter is mixed and looks dense. What pan should I prep for it?
Spray a 9 x 13 inch metal pan, then spread the batter evenly into it, pushing it into the corners so the layer is level.

Yes. We'll keep the dressing light through the main toss, then leave a thin extra stripe along one side at serving so it has that uneven finish. For the chews themselves, start with 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1/2 cup softened butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar.
I've got the chips and both sugars out. Should the butter be soft enough to press easily?
Exactly—soft enough to cream smoothly, but not melted. Set the butter near your mixing bowl, and put a heavy saucepan on the stove for the chocolate.
The saucepan is ready. Do I add anything with the chocolate chips?
Add only the 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips to the heavy saucepan, and keep the heat very low so they melt gently instead of scorching.
The light toss with the little richer edge is why I usually serve it this way; the salad tastes brighter.

Keep it over very low heat just until the last bits smooth out, stirring the whole time. Once it's evenly melted, take it off the heat.
Chocolate is smooth and off the burner. I'm moving to the butter bowl.

It's lighter now, but I can still feel a little sugar grain on the spoon.
That's fine for this stage as long as the butter and sugars are well combined and lighter. Scrape down the bowl, then get the eggs ready.

messages.content: I'm making Basil Burgers; if the tender herb stems work here, mince them in rather than tossing them.

They work well here. Finely chop tender cilantro or parsley stems and mix them right into the burger base with the ground beef, Worcestershire, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper so they season the patties evenly.
Good. I've got the grill outside and a mixing bowl ready—what should I pull from the fridge and pantry?
Set out 1 1/4 pounds ground beef, 3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic salt. Keep pepper nearby too, since it gets mixed into the burgers.
The beef is cold and the stems are rinsed. Should I chop them before heating the grill?
Yes. Mince the tender stems finely first so they disappear into the meat, then preheat the outdoor grill for high heat while you mix the burger mixture.
Perfect—that's how I usually do it, with the stems going into the base so the flavor is spread through.

Exactly. Add the ground beef to the bowl, then sprinkle in the chopped stems, Worcestershire sauce, dried basil, garlic salt, and pepper. Mix gently just until combined so the burgers don't get tough.
The mixture smells good, but I don't want to overwork it. How should I shape them?
Divide the mixture into 4 portions and form 4 burger patties. Press them together enough to hold their shape, but keep your touch light.
They're formed. Should I oil the grate now or wait until right before cooking?
Oil the grill grate lightly right before the patties go on, once the grill is hot. That helps prevent sticking without making the burgers greasy.
The grate is oiled and the patties are on. How long am I watching them?
Cook them about 6 minutes total, turning once. Use a thermometer and aim for an internal temperature of 160 degrees F, which is 70 degrees C, unless you're choosing another doneness.
They hit temperature and have grill marks. Any serving or cleanup tips before I plate them?
Let them rest briefly while you clear the raw-meat bowl and utensils for washing. Serve the Basil Burgers hot, with the stem-flecked seasoning worked through the patties and the texture still juicy.
I'm making BBQ Chicken Wings and want to get the marinade organized before I touch the chicken. What should I set out?
Set out 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce, 1 cup oyster sauce, 1/4 cup soy sauce, and 1/4 cup ketchup. You'll also want garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar ready for the bowl.
I've got the sauces measured. Should I use a small mixing bowl or something larger?

Use a large bowl, since the wings need room to sit in the marinade. Add the teriyaki sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic powder, gin, liquid smoke, and sugar, then mix until everything looks evenly combined.
The marinade is mixed and smells smoky. Do the wings go straight in?
Yes. Place the chicken wings in that bowl and turn them so they're coated well. Cover the bowl before it goes into the refrigerator.
How long should I leave them in there if I'm trying to plan dinner?
Give them 8 hours in the refrigerator, or let them marinate overnight if that works better for your timing.
They've been marinating since last night. What should I do before putting them on the grill?
Preheat the grill for low heat. While it warms, keep the wings chilled until you're ready to cook them.
The grill is heating on low. Anything I should do to stop the wings from sticking?
Lightly oil the grill grate before the wings go on. That will help prevent sticking and make turning them easier.
Should I bring the whole bowl outside, or just transfer the wings?
Transfer the wings to a clean plate or tray for the grill, and keep things tidy by not reusing anything that held raw chicken unless it's washed well first.
I want to make Enchilada Style Burritos. I've got frozen bean and cheese burritos, but can you walk me through what to set out?

Absolutely. Set out 6 frozen prepared bean and cheese burritos, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, and 1 3/4 cups water. You'll also need a greased 13-in baking dish and a saucepan.
The baking dish is greased. Should the burritos thaw first, or go in frozen?
Use them frozen. Arrange the 6 frozen burritos in the greased 13-in baking dish, then set the dish aside while you make the sauce.
They're in the dish. I'm at the stove with the saucepan—what heat should I use for the butter?
Use medium heat and melt the 2 tablespoons butter or margarine in the saucepan. Keep an eye on it so it melts without browning.
The butter is melted and foamy. Do I add the flour all at once?
Yes, sprinkle in the 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and stir until the mixture looks smooth with no dry patches.
It's smooth now, kind of like a paste. How do I add the water without lumps?
Pour in the 1 3/4 cups water gradually while stirring the whole time. Add a little, stir it smooth, then keep adding until all the water is incorporated.
The water is mixed in. It looks thin right now—am I just waiting for it to bubble?
Bring it to a boil, stirring as it heats. Once it boils, cook and stir for 2 minutes, or until it thickens.
After 2 minutes it's thicker and coats the spoon. Is that the texture I want before using it?
Yes, that's the right point: smooth and thickened after boiling and stirring for 2 minutes. You can take it off the heat and use it with the burritos in the prepared dish.
I'm making BBQ Chuck Roast today and have a 5 pound chuck roast ready. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set the roast aside for a moment and make sure you have 1 cup barbeque sauce, 1 cup teriyaki sauce, and 1 12 fluid ounce can or bottle of beer for the marinade.
I've got the barbeque sauce, teriyaki, and beer. Do I mix all of that in the same bowl?
Yes, use a large bowl. Stir together the barbeque sauce, teriyaki sauce, beer, garlic, ginger, onion, black pepper, and salt until the marinade is evenly combined.
The marinade is mixed. Should the roast be fully coated before it goes in the fridge?
Place the chuck roast into the marinade and turn it so the surface gets coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate it for six hours, turning the roast often during that time.
It's in the refrigerator now. When I turn it, should I just flip it over in the bowl?
That works well. Flip or rotate the roast so different sides sit in the marinade, then cover it again and return it to the refrigerator each time.
The six hours are almost up, and I'm getting the grill area ready. What setup do I need?
Preheat an outdoor grill for indirect heat. Arrange it so the roast won't be sitting directly over the hottest part of the fire.
The grill is heating for indirect cooking. What should I do with the marinade when I take the roast out?
Remove the roast from the marinade, then pour the marinade into a saucepan instead of discarding it.
So the roast comes out of the bowl, and the leftover liquid goes straight into a pan?
Exactly. Lift out the roast for the grill, and transfer the remaining marinade to a saucepan so it's ready for the next part of cooking.

The chocolate is chopped and the milk is measured. Do I need the cold ingredients now too?

If it still has a few soft pieces after stirring, should I keep heating it?

If the pieces are nearly melted, keep stirring first so the residual heat can smooth them out. Only add a very short burst if needed; the recipe is aiming for almost melted at that point, not scorched.

Whisk the softened cream cheese into the chocolate mixture along with the 2 tablespoons white sugar and the remaining milk from the 1/3 cup. Keep whisking until everything looks blended and even.
The mixture is blended. It's loose and glossy—does it chill before the topping goes in?
Yes, refrigerate the bowl for 10 minutes. That short chill helps it firm up a bit before you fold in the whipped topping.
The timer is done. I've got the whipped topping out and want to keep the filling light.
Gently fold in 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping with broad, slow turns. Stop once no streaks remain, then add only your two chosen garnishes when you serve or finish the pie.
I'm making Fig Bars II today. Can you help me organize the ingredients before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup white sugar and 3 eggs, since those get beaten together in a large bowl until the mixture turns thick and pale.
Sugar and eggs are ready. What dry ingredients should I measure next?
Measure 7/8 cup all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder. The recipe also has you sift in salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice with those dry ingredients.
Before I get flour everywhere, what pan and oven setup do I need?
Heat the oven to 325 degrees F, or 165 degrees C. While it warms, grease and flour a 9x13 inch baking pan so the bars release cleanly.
The oven is heating and the pan is coated. Should I start with the eggs?
Yes. Crack the 3 eggs into a large bowl, add the 1 cup white sugar, and beat them until the mixture looks thick, pale, and a little airy.
It's lighter now, but I'm not sure if it's thick enough. What should I look for?
When you lift the beater, the mixture should fall back in soft ribbons instead of looking thin and watery. If it still seems loose, beat it a bit longer before adding the dry ingredients.
Okay, I have the dry ingredients waiting in a sifter. Do they all go in at once?
Sift together the flour, baking powder, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and allspice, then blend that into the egg-and-sugar mixture. Add the vanilla along with it, mixing just until everything is combined.
Once the batter is mixed, should I do anything special before it goes in the pan?
Scrape the bowl well so there aren't dry pockets, then spread the batter evenly into the prepared 9x13 inch pan. Keep the oven at 325 degrees F, 165 degrees C, for baking.
I want to make Caramel Shortbread Squares. Can you help me get set up before I start baking?
Absolutely. Pull out 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, and the other 1/2 cup butter so everything is on hand.
I've got the butter, sugar, and flour out. What pan and oven setting should I use?
Use a 9 inch square baking pan, and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 176 degrees C.
The oven is heating and the pan is ready. Should I grease the pan or start mixing?
Start with the shortbread mixture: in a medium bowl, combine the 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour.
Do I want that mixture smooth like dough, or more sandy?
Mix it until it is evenly crumbly rather than smooth. You're looking for a consistent crumbly texture with no big pockets of plain flour.
It's crumbly all the way through. How firm should I press it into the pan?
Press the crumbly mixture evenly into the 9 inch square baking pan, making a flat layer and getting it into the corners without leaving loose patches.
The surface is mostly even now. Does it go straight into the oven?
Yes, put the pan into the preheated 350 degrees F oven and bake it for 20 minutes.
While it bakes, is there anything I should watch for near the end of the 20 minutes?
Check that the shortbread looks set and lightly baked at the end of the 20 minutes. Let the pan cool enough to handle before cutting the Caramel Shortbread Squares.

I'm making Basil Burgers on the grill. Can you help me get set up before I start mixing?

Cook them for about 6 minutes total, turning once during cooking. Watch for good browning and avoid pressing down on the patties.

Check the center of each burger and cook to an internal temperature of 160 degrees F, which is 70 degrees C, or to your desired doneness. Once they're there, take them off the grill and serve.

Warm the 1 teaspoon olive oil in the skillet over the stove. Once it looks loose and glossy, add the chicken breasts with the onion powder.

Look for a browned outside while the chicken still seems moist. The recipe's cue is that it should be just about done after those 15 minutes.

Add the pinch of salt now, and season with pepper to taste as the recipe directs.

That completes the recipe steps for California Chicken. Let the chicken rest briefly off the heat, then serve it while it's warm.

Beat the egg with the egg substitute mixture in the small bowl until it looks blended. Keep it close to your flour and bread crumbs so you can coat the chops in order.

Dredge each pork chop lightly in flour, dip it into the beaten egg mixture, then coat it liberally with bread crumbs. Set each coated chop aside carefully so the breading stays on.

messages.content: I want to make Bacon Wrapped Hotdogs in the slow cooker. Can you help me set everything up?

Yes. Each hot dog should be in 3 smaller pieces, and each bacon strip should be cut in half so one 1/2 slice can wrap around one hot dog piece.

Wrap one half-slice of bacon around each piece of hot dog. It just needs to circle the hot dog securely; it doesn't have to cover every bit of the surface.

Push a toothpick through each wrapped piece to secure the bacon. Try to catch both ends of the bacon so it stays snug during cooking.

The recipe has you place the wrapped hot dogs directly into the slow cooker on low heat. Arrange them in the insert so they sit fairly evenly.

Sprinkle the 1/2 cup packed brown sugar over the hot dogs, spreading it across the top so it can melt down as they cook.

Let them cook on low for 5 to 6 hours, until the bacon is cooked. Before serving, check that the bacon looks done and the pieces are hot throughout.

No need. Microwave the bowl on high until the squash mixture is heated through, about 5 minutes; the butter should melt as it warms.

Aim for heated through and well combined. Give it a careful stir after microwaving so the curry, maple syrup, and melted butter are evenly distributed.

Coconut is optional. Sprinkle some on top if desired, then serve the Curried Winter Squash warm.

Plan on about 40 minutes over medium heat. The potatoes should be tender enough that a fork slides in easily, and the soup should look thicker and creamy from the au gratin mix.

Stir in the cream at the end and heat it through gently. Once it's evenly blended and the soup is hot again, it's ready to serve.

Pat the dough into a round, keeping it compact but not overworked, then wrap it in plastic. Once it's wrapped, it's ready for the next tart step.
