I've got the broth and cumin on the counter. How much oil goes into the pot to start?
Pour 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat.
The oil is warming. Should all the tortilla strips go in at once, or just part of them?
Add only half of the tortilla strips for this batch. Stir them often while they cook so they crisp evenly instead of sitting in one spot.
They're sizzling and getting firmer. What texture am I watching for before taking them out?
Look for the strips to be crisp. Once that half is crisp, lift them out of the pot.

Drain the crisp tortilla strips on paper towels to pull off the extra oil.
The paper towels are set. How do I handle the remaining tortilla strips?

Add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of vegetable oil to the pot, then repeat the same process with the remaining tortilla strips. When they're crisp, drain them on paper towels too and set the strips aside.
Can you walk me through Curried Winter Squash? I have cooked squash ready but want to make sure I season it right.
Absolutely. Set out 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash, 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
The squash is already mashed in a container. Should I move it to a bowl before adding anything?
Yes, use a medium microwave-safe bowl so you have room to stir everything evenly.
I've put the squash in the bowl. Do the curry powder, butter, and maple syrup all go in together?
They do. Add the curry powder, butter or margarine, and maple syrup to the squash, then stir until the seasoning and syrup are worked through.
The butter is still in small pieces. Is that okay before microwaving?
That's fine. It will melt as the squash heats; just spread the pieces around a bit so they melt into the mixture more evenly.
The bowl is ready. How long should I microwave it?
Microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Should I stop and stir during those 5 minutes, or leave it alone?
You can pause once midway to stir, especially if your microwave heats unevenly, then continue until the squash is hot throughout.
It's hot and smells good. The recipe mentions coconut—what should I do with that?
If you want the garnish, sprinkle coconut over the warm squash. Otherwise, you can skip it and serve the Curried Winter Squash right away.

A quick stir or whisk is fine here—just make sure the flours, sugar, baking powder, salt, and caraway seeds are evenly combined.
Okay, it looks evenly mixed. I have the cheese nearby; when does that go in?
Stir the cheese into the dry mixture now, folding it through so it's distributed before the wet ingredients go in.
Cheese is mixed through. I'm ready for the egg, milk, and oil—do they go into the flour bowl one at a time?
Combine the egg, milk, and oil together in a separate bowl or measuring cup first. Then pour that mixture into the dry ingredients.
I poured it in. The batter is starting to come together but still has a few dry streaks.
Stir just until moistened. Stop as soon as the dry streaks disappear; muffin batter should not be beaten smooth.
The batter is mixed. My muffin cups are lined—how full should I make them?
Spoon the batter into the greased or paper-lined muffin cups, filling each one about 2/3 full.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Slice them into slender, easy-to-grab batons, then arrange the vegetables in separate color groups on the platter.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: I'm serving Best Ever Tuna Salad on a platter with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, and radish for dipping. What cut works best for the vegetables?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Cut the raw vegetables into long thin sticks and group them by color.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Best Ever Tuna Salad as a platter or crudite with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, or radish. How should I cut the raw vegetables?

messages.content: I'm serving Best Ever Tuna Salad on a platter with raw cucumber, onion, carrot, pepper, and radish for dipping. What cut works best for the vegetables?
Slice them into slender, easy-to-grab batons, then arrange the vegetables in separate color groups on the platter.
Great, that's the serving style for today. Before I start cutting vegetables, what should I pull out for the tuna salad itself?
Set out 2 eggs, 1 (12 ounce) can of white tuna, 1 (6 ounce) can of shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise.
The cans and mayo are on the counter. I've got a small saucepan for the eggs—does that work?
Yes. Put the 2 eggs in the saucepan and add enough cold water to cover them.
They're covered with cold water. Should I keep the lid off while it heats?
Leave it uncovered while you bring the water to a boil.
The water just reached a boil. What do I do so the eggs don't overcook?
Take the saucepan off the heat right away, then cover it.
Covered and off the burner. How long should I let them sit?
Let the eggs stand in the hot water for 10 to 12 minutes.
While they sit, should I deal with the tuna and crab?
Yes—open the white tuna and shredded crabmeat, drain them if needed, and keep the 1/2 cup mayonnaise ready for mixing.
Timer's done. What texture am I going for with the eggs before they go into the salad?
Remove the eggs from the hot water, cool them, peel them, and chop them finely so they blend evenly into the tuna salad.

memory_annotations.boundary_action_cue: Set the briny ingredient in small separate piles around the outside edge of the platter.
memory_annotations.boundary_query_cue: I'm serving Gingered Mango Salsa on one big platter next to rich sandwiches, burgers, bowls, salads, or creamy dishes today. What should I do with the briny ingredient in that setup?

original_cues.boundary_action_cue: Place the briny ingredient as small separate clusters around the platter edge.
original_cues.boundary_query_cue: I'm making Gingered Mango Salsa as a shared platter with rich sandwiches, burgers, bowls, salads, or creamy dishes. How should I handle the briny ingredient?

messages.content: I'm serving Gingered Mango Salsa on one big platter next to rich sandwiches, burgers, bowls, salads, or creamy dishes today. What should I do with the briny ingredient in that setup?
Set the briny ingredient in small separate piles around the outside edge of the platter.
Great, I'll plate it that way. Before I get the bowl out, what fruit and onion amounts should I chop?
Chop 1 cup peeled mango, then chop 1/4 cup red onion. Keep the pieces fairly small so the salsa scoops easily.
The mango is diced and the red onion is chopped. What should I measure for the green and the acid?
Mince 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, and measure 1/4 cup lime juice.
Cilantro and lime juice are ready. Should I use a mixing bowl or build it on the serving platter?
Use a bowl for mixing so the lime juice coats everything evenly before you transfer it to the platter.
The bowl is out. Do all the ingredients go in together?
Yes, combine the chopped peeled mango, red onion, minced fresh cilantro, and lime juice in the bowl.
It's all in there. How much should I stir it without crushing the mango?
Fold it gently just until the onion, cilantro, and lime juice are evenly distributed through the mango.
The texture looks good. How long should it sit before I serve it?
Let the salsa stand for 30 minutes before serving so the flavors can come together.
After the 30 minutes, how should I arrange it for the shared platter?
Spoon the salsa onto the platter, keep it easy to scoop, and add those small separate briny clusters around the edge right before it goes out.
Can you help me get started on Baked Fake Steak with Gravy? I'm setting out a bowl and want to make sure I have the meat mixture right.
Absolutely. For the mixture, you'll need 3 pounds ground beef, 17 saltine crackers finely crushed, 1/2 cup milk, and 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder.
I have the 3 pounds of ground beef in the fridge and the crackers crushed. Does the milk go in with them right away?
Yes. Put the ground beef, finely crushed saltine crackers, and 1/2 cup milk into a large bowl together.
Should I break up the beef before mixing, or just add everything on top?
Break the beef up a bit as it goes into the bowl so the cracker crumbs and milk can spread through it evenly.
The meat, crackers, and milk are in the bowl. What seasonings go in before I shape it?
Add the 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic powder, plus onion powder, salt, and pepper. Mix until the seasoning looks evenly worked through the beef mixture.
I'm mixing by hand. What texture am I looking for so I don't overwork it?
Stop once it looks well blended and holds together as one mixture, with no dry pockets of cracker crumbs or streaks of milk.
Okay, it's combined. What pan should I use for shaping it?
Use a 10x15 inch jellyroll pan and line it with waxed paper before adding the beef mixture.
The waxed paper is down. Do I spread the meat loosely or pack it in?
Press the beef mixture firmly into the lined pan so it fills the pan in an even layer.
Can you walk me through Coconut Ambrosia Salad? I'm setting out a big mixing bowl and want to make sure I drain the fruit correctly.
Absolutely. Drain 1 (11 ounce) can of mandarin oranges and 1 (8 ounce) can of crushed pineapple really well so the salad doesn't turn watery. Add both fruits to your large bowl once they're drained.
The oranges are delicate. Should I stir them now or wait until everything else is in the bowl?
Wait until the creamy ingredients are in, then fold gently. For now, add 3 1/2 cups thawed frozen whipped topping to the bowl with the drained oranges and pineapple.
The whipped topping is thawed and soft. What goes in with it?
Add 2 cups shredded coconut, plus the marshmallows and milk called for in the recipe. Scatter them over the top so they'll mix in evenly.
I don't want to break up the mandarin oranges. What's the best way to mix it?
Use a wide spatula and fold from the bottom of the bowl up over the top, turning the bowl as you go. Mix until the whipped topping coats the fruit, coconut, marshmallows, and milk evenly.
It looks combined and fluffy, with a little moisture at the bottom. Is that okay before chilling?
A little moisture is fine, especially from the fruit and milk. Give it a few more gentle folds, then cover the bowl and chill it for 1 hour before serving.
Should I put it in the serving dish before it chills, or leave it in the mixing bowl?

Either works. If you want a cleaner presentation, spoon it into the serving dish before chilling; if you want easier cleanup and a final stir, keep it in the mixing bowl and transfer it after the 1 hour chill.
It's chilled now. How do I make it look finished for the table?
Give it one gentle stir, mound it into the serving bowl if needed, and garnish the top with cherries just before serving.
Can you help me make Atomic Canuck Chili and keep me on track while I prep?

Absolutely. Set out a large skillet and your slow cooker. For the starting mixture, you'll need 2 pounds lean ground beef, 1/2 large onion diced, 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper, and 3 tablespoons garlic powder.
The beef is ready, and I'm dicing the onion now. Should the skillet be heating yet?
Yes, warm the large skillet over medium heat while you finish the onion. Once it's hot, add the ground beef, diced onion, crushed red pepper, garlic powder, and seasoned pepper together.
Everything is in the skillet. What texture am I looking for before it leaves the pan?
Cook it until the beef is browned and no longer looks raw, breaking it up as it cooks so the onion and seasonings spread through the meat.
The beef is browned, but there's fat pooled in the skillet. Do I move it all to the slow cooker?
Drain off the fat first, then transfer the browned beef and onion mixture into the slow cooker.
The meat mixture is in the slow cooker. I see a lot of add-ins on the counter—what goes in with it?

Stir in the mushrooms, baked beans, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato paste, sugar, carrots, celery, peppers, beer, and barbeque sauce. Mix well so the tomato paste and sauce don't stay in clumps.
It's combined, though it looks thick with all the beans and vegetables. Should I adjust seasoning now?
Yes. Season the chili with hot sauce and more crushed red pepper, adding them gradually so the heat builds without overwhelming the pot.
I've added the hot sauce and extra pepper. Anything else before I put the lid on and let the slow cooker work?

Give it one last stir, scrape down the sides, and make sure the ingredients are evenly distributed in the slow cooker. Then cover it and let the chili cook until everything is heated through and the flavors have melded.
Can you stay with me while I make Corn Bread Sloppy Joes? I'm getting the counter cleared now.

Absolutely. Set out 1 (8.5 ounce) package corn bread/muffin mix, 1 egg, 1/3 cup milk, and 2 pounds ground beef. You'll also want a baking pan for the corn bread and a large skillet for the beef mixture.
The corn bread mix, egg, and milk are out. Should I deal with the bread part before browning the beef?
Yes. Prepare the corn bread according to the package directions, using the egg and milk, then bake it as the package directs.
The corn bread is mixed and going into the oven. What should I start on the stovetop while it bakes?
While it bakes, put the ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook until the meat is no longer pink, breaking it up as it cooks.
The beef is browned and there's some liquid in the skillet. Do I leave that in?
Drain the beef mixture before adding the sauce ingredients, so the sloppy joe filling doesn't turn greasy or watery.
Drained. I have spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix nearby.
Stir the spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix into the drained beef and onion until everything is evenly combined.
It's mixed together, but it still looks a little separated in spots. Should I keep stirring?
Yes, give it another minute of stirring over medium heat so the sloppy joe mix disperses through the sauce and beef.
The filling looks even now, and the corn bread is almost done. What's the last stovetop step?
Bring the beef mixture to a boil. Once it reaches that point, you'll have the hot sloppy joe topping ready to serve with the baked corn bread.
Can you help me make Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches? I'm setting out the vegetables and want to get the order right.
Absolutely. Start by prepping the vegetables: finely chop 1 small onion, dice 1 medium tomato, chop 1 stalk celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper.
The onion and tomato are ready, but I still need to chop the celery and bell pepper. Should the pepper pieces be pretty small?
Yes, keep the green bell pepper finely chopped so the topping spreads evenly across the bread. The celery can be chopped small too, so it stays crunchy without being bulky.
Vegetables are all chopped. What equipment should I have ready before I mix everything?
Set out a medium bowl for the topping, plus a baking sheet or broiling pan for the bread. Go ahead and preheat your oven's broiler now.
Broiler is heating. Do I mix just the vegetables, or does the cheese go in now too?
Mix everything for the topping in the medium bowl: the onion, tomato, celery, bell pepper, cheese, chili powder, and salt. Stir until the cheese and seasoning are evenly distributed.
The mixture looks a little chunky from the vegetables. Is that okay for spreading?
That's fine for these sandwiches. Just give it a few extra stirs so the cheese helps hold the chopped vegetables together.
I've got the bread out. Should I toast it first or put it straight on the pan?
Put the bread slices straight onto the baking sheet or broiling pan in a single layer. They'll crisp under the broiler after the topping goes on.
How much topping should I put on each slice so they cook evenly?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice, then spread it all the way out to the edges so every sandwich gets an even layer under the broiler.
Can you walk me through making Garlic Butter? I've set out a small bowl and a spatula.
Absolutely. Let the butter be soft enough to mash easily, then measure out 1 cup of softened butter, 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 tablespoon garlic salt.
The butter is soft and in the bowl. Should the garlic go in before the cheese?
Yes. Add the 1 tablespoon minced garlic to the softened butter, then add the 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese.
They're in the bowl, but the butter is sticking to the spatula a bit. What texture am I aiming for?
Mash and fold until the garlic and Parmesan are spread evenly through the butter. It should look creamy and speckled rather than perfectly smooth.
Okay, it's mixed together. When do I add the garlic salt?
Sprinkle in the 1 tablespoon garlic salt, then add Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika to season the butter.
Should I stir gently or really whip it after the seasonings go in?
Stir and fold firmly enough to distribute the seasonings throughout, scraping the sides of the small bowl so there aren't salty pockets.
It looks evenly mixed now. Is there anything else the recipe needs?
That covers the recipe steps: the softened butter is combined with minced garlic and Parmesan, then seasoned with garlic salt, Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika.
How should I serve or store it once it's mixed?
Use it right away on bread, vegetables, or cooked meat, or transfer it to a covered container and chill it so it firms up for slicing or spreading later.
Can you help me get Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup started? I'm setting the slow cooker on the counter now.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 pounds cubed beef stew meat and measure 2 cups water so they're ready to go into the slow cooker.
The beef is cubed and the water is measured. Should I prep the vegetables before loading it?
Yes. Chop 1 small onion, open 1 (28 ounce) can crushed tomatoes, and have the mixed vegetables and potatoes nearby for when you stir everything together.
Onion is chopped, tomatoes are open, and the vegetables and potatoes are beside the cooker. Does the beef go in by itself first?
Put the cubed beef stew meat directly into the slow cooker as the base layer.
The beef is in. I don't want to splash tomato everywhere—what should I add next?
Pour in the 2 cups water over the beef before adding the heavier ingredients.
Water is in. I'm ready to add the onion and tomatoes if that's the next move.
Add the chopped onion and crushed tomatoes, then stir in the mixed vegetables and potatoes so they're distributed through the beef and liquid.
Everything is mixed together. The pot looks full but not overflowing. What seasonings go in?
Season the soup with bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil, sprinkling them over the top so you can stir them through evenly.
Seasonings are in and stirred. Is there anything else from the recipe before I put the lid on?

That covers the recipe's setup: beef in the slow cooker, water poured in, onion, crushed tomatoes, mixed vegetables, and potatoes stirred in, then bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil added. Put the lid on and let the slow cooker take it from here.

source_seed.recipe_title: Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup

messages.content: Can you walk me through Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms while I set up my pan?
Absolutely. Put a wide pan or skillet on the stove, and gather 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, 2 cups diced Broccoflower, 2 cups chopped assorted wild mushrooms, and 1/2 white onion, chopped.
I've got the butter, Broccoflower, mushrooms, and onion ready. The recipe mentions garlic too—should I have that by the stove?
Yes, keep the garlic ready with the vegetables since it gets sautéed with them. You'll also want your rice, chicken stock, nutmeg, herbs, salt, and pepper close by for the risotto portion.
The pan is heating. Do I add the butter before the vegetables?

Yes. Melt the unsalted butter in the pan, then add the diced Broccoflower, chopped wild mushrooms, onion, and garlic. Sauté everything together for 10 minutes, stirring now and then so it softens evenly.
It's been a few minutes and the mushrooms are giving off liquid. Is that expected?
That's normal for wild mushrooms. Keep cooking and stirring; by the end of the 10 minutes, the vegetables should be softened and the mushroom juices should have cooked down somewhat.
The vegetables smell good and look softened. What should I do with them before starting the rice?
Scoop the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside in a bowl. Leave the same pan on the stove for the rice.
The pan has some browned bits left. Do I clean it out?

No need to clean it; those browned bits will add flavor. Add the rice to the same pan, then begin adding chicken stock 1 cup at a time, stirring until the liquid is well incorporated before adding the next cup.
How do I know when to stop adding stock and bring the vegetables back in?
When the chicken stock has been absorbed and the rice is tender, stir the sautéed vegetables back in. Then add nutmeg and herbs, and season with salt and pepper before serving.
I want to make French Spring Soup, but I'd like to do it with you step by step while I prep.
Absolutely. Set a large pot on the stove and gather 1/4 cup butter, 1 pound chopped leeks, 1 chopped onion, and 2 quarts water.
I have the pot out. Should the leeks and onion already be chopped before I turn on the heat?
Yes, have the leeks and onion chopped first so they can go in smoothly once the butter melts.
The butter is measured. What heat should I use for the pot?
Put the butter in the large pot and melt it over medium heat.
It's melted and starting to foam a little. Do I add both vegetables together?
Add the chopped leeks and chopped onion together, then stir them into the butter.
What texture am I looking for before adding liquid?
Cook them until they're tender, stirring as needed so the leeks and onion soften evenly.
They look softened now, and nothing is browning much. Is that right?
That's right for this soup. Pour the 2 quarts water into the pot with the softened leeks and onion.
The water is in. What else goes into the soup before I let it keep cooking?
Mix in the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice, stirring so everything is distributed through the broth.
I'm making Bacon Wrapped Smokies for a snack tray. Can you help me get set up without rushing?
Absolutely. Set out 1 pound of sliced bacon, a 1 (14 ounce) package of beef cocktail wieners, toothpicks, a large baking sheet, and 3/4 cup brown sugar, or a little more or less to taste.
The bacon is still in long strips. Should I cut all of it before I start wrapping?
Cut the sliced bacon into thirds. Once it's cut, keep about 2/3 of the bacon in the refrigerator until you need it so it stays easier to handle.
Got it. I'm clearing space near the oven now—what temperature should I set?
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F, which is 165 degrees C.
The oven is heating, and I've got the first batch of bacon pieces out. How tight should I wrap the wieners?
Wrap each beef cocktail wiener with one piece of bacon so it overlaps enough to stay in place, but don't stretch it too tight. Secure each one with a toothpick through the bacon and wiener.
Some of the bacon pieces are sliding while I pick them up. Is there a good way to arrange them as I work?
Place the wrapped smokies directly onto a large baking sheet as you finish each one. Keep the toothpick side positioned so the wrap stays secure while you continue assembling.
I've filled part of the baking sheet. Should I pull the rest of the bacon from the fridge now?
Yes, bring out more chilled bacon as needed and keep wrapping the remaining cocktail wieners one at a time. The chilled bacon should be firmer and less slippery.
The tray is nearly full, and the brown sugar is measured. Anything to double-check before cooking?

Make sure every cocktail wiener is wrapped with bacon, secured with a toothpick, and sitting on the large baking sheet. Keep the 3/4 cup brown sugar ready to use to taste, and confirm the oven has reached 325 degrees F before you continue.
Can you help me make Aaahh Potato Soup? I've got a large pot out, but I want to make sure I'm not missing anything before I start.
Absolutely. Set out 2 cubed Yukon Gold potatoes, 1 (5.5 ounce) package au gratin instant potato mix, 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed chicken broth, and 1 1/2 cups water.
The potatoes are cubed and the au gratin mix is open. Should the broth be diluted before it goes in?
No need to dilute it separately. Add the condensed chicken broth straight to the large saucepan or pot along with the cubed potatoes, the au gratin potato mix, and the 1 1/2 cups water.
Everything is in the pot, but the liquid is sitting a little below the top of the potatoes. Is that okay?
If the potatoes are not covered, pour in just enough additional water to cover them. That will help them cook evenly.
I added a splash more water and the potatoes are covered now. What heat should I use?
Set the pot over medium heat. Let it cook at a steady simmer, stirring occasionally so the potato mix doesn't settle and stick.
How long should I expect it to take, and what should the potatoes feel like?
Plan on about 40 minutes. The soup is ready for the next step when the Yukon Gold potato cubes are tender enough to pierce easily with a fork.
It's been cooking, and the potatoes are fork-tender. The soup looks thick from the mix.
That sounds right. Stir in the cream, then keep the pot on the heat just long enough to warm it through without boiling hard.
The cream is stirred in and it's hot. Should I let it sit or serve it right away?
Serve it warm once the cream is heated through. Give it one final stir before ladling so the broth, potato mix, potatoes, and cream are evenly combined.
I want to make Crawfish Etouffee III. Can you guide me while I pull out the pan and cans?

Absolutely. Set a large saucepan on the stove, and gather 1 chopped onion, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed tomato soup, 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup, and 1 (10 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green chile peppers.
I've got the large saucepan ready. Should the onion go in by itself first?
Yes. Put the chopped onion in the large saucepan over medium heat and sauté it until it turns clear.
The onion is looking translucent now. Do I drain the diced tomatoes with green chiles before adding them?
The recipe just says to add the canned tomatoes, so add the diced tomatoes with green chile peppers along with the condensed tomato soup and condensed cream of mushroom soup.
Both 10.75 ounce soup cans are in, and I added the 10 ounce can of tomatoes. Should I stir it smooth?
Give everything a good stir so the tomato soup, mushroom soup, tomatoes, and onion are evenly combined in the saucepan.
It's mixed and starting to bubble gently. How long should this part simmer?
Keep it at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally so the soups don't stick to the bottom.
The 15 minutes are up, and the sauce looks thick. Is this when the crawfish goes in?
Yes, place the crawfish into the pan now and stir it through the sauce.
The crawfish is folded in. What timing should I use from here?
Let the crawfish simmer in the sauce for 25 minutes. Keep the heat moderate enough for a steady simmer, then it's ready to serve.
Can you guide me through making Citrus Infused Guacamole? I've got a bowl out, but I want to make sure I set up the ingredients correctly.
Absolutely. Start by getting 2 avocados ready: peel them, remove the pits, and mash the avocado flesh in a large bowl. Keep at least one pit nearby for later.
The avocados are mashed, and I saved a pit. Which juices should I measure?
Measure 1/2 tablespoon lime juice, 1/2 tablespoon orange juice, and 1/2 tablespoon pineapple juice. Add all three to the mashed avocado.
All three juices are in the bowl. The mixture looks a little loose around the edges—should I stir it fully now?
Yes, stir it together until the juices are evenly worked into the avocado. Then add the cumin, cilantro, and salt called for in the recipe, and mix until the seasoning is distributed.
The cumin, cilantro, and salt are mixed in. Should the guacamole be completely smooth?
It can be smooth or slightly chunky, depending on how much you mash and stir. For this guacamole, just make sure the citrus juices and seasonings are blended throughout.
I have hot pepper sauce nearby. Does it go in with everything else?
If you're using it, mix in the hot pepper sauce now. Add it to the bowl and stir so the heat is spread through the guacamole.
Okay, it's mixed. What do I do with the avocado pit I saved?
Place one of the avocado pits directly into the bowl with the guacamole. It helps keep it fresh while it sits.
I'm serving it soon, but not this exact minute. Should I leave it out or chill it?
You can serve it immediately, or refrigerate it until serving. If you refrigerate it, keep the pit in the bowl until you're ready to bring it out.
Can you walk me through Curried Winter Squash? I have a microwave-safe medium bowl ready.
Absolutely. Set out 3 cups cooked, mashed winter squash, 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
The squash is already cooked and mashed. Should the butter be softened before I mix it in?
Softened butter or margarine will blend in more easily, but it does not need to be melted first since the mixture will be microwaved.
I measured the curry powder and maple syrup. Do I add everything to the bowl together?
Yes. Put the mashed squash in the medium bowl, then add the curry powder, butter or trans fat-free margarine, and maple syrup.
It looks a little streaky from the curry powder. How mixed should it be before heating?
Stir until the curry powder and maple syrup are evenly worked through and the butter or margarine is distributed in small pieces or mostly blended.
Okay, it is mixed. What microwave timing should I use?
Microwave it on high until heated through, about 5 minutes. If your microwave heats unevenly, pause once to stir and then continue.
After 5 minutes it is hot, but I want the texture smooth before serving.
Give it a good stir while it is hot; the butter or margarine should finish melting in and the squash should look creamy and evenly seasoned.
I have coconut in the pantry. Does it go on before or after heating?
Sprinkle the coconut on after heating, if you want to use it. Then serve the Curried Winter Squash warm.
Can you guide me through German Chocolate Brownie Cookies while I set up my mixing bowls?
Absolutely. Put a large bowl on the counter for the creamed mixture, and gather 1 1/2 cups packed brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The brown sugar is packed and the shortening is measured. Should I add the water and vanilla with them?
Yes. Add the brown sugar, 2/3 cup shortening, water, and 1 teaspoon vanilla to the large bowl together.
They're in the bowl. Do I stir by hand or cream it more thoroughly?
Cream the ingredients together until the shortening is worked through the brown sugar and the mixture looks even and soft.
The mixture looks smooth enough now. I have eggs ready—do they go in one at a time?
Beat the eggs into the creamed mixture, adding them gradually if that helps you keep the batter smooth.
The eggs are mixed in. I've got another bowl clean for the dry ingredients.
Use that bowl to combine the flour, cocoa, salt, and baking soda. Stir them together so the cocoa and leavening are evenly distributed.
The dry bowl is uniform and there aren't any cocoa clumps. How do I bring the two bowls together?
Add the dry mixture into the creamed mixture a bit at a time, stirring gently as you go.
It's getting thick. Should I keep mixing until it looks perfectly smooth?
Stop once it is just blended. The dry ingredients should be incorporated, but you do not need to keep beating after the dough comes together.
Can you talk me through Chai Butter Cookies while I set up the bowl and mixer?
Absolutely. Put a large mixing bowl on your counter, and have 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup chai tea mix, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and 2 eggs nearby.
The butter, chai mix, sugar, and eggs are out. Should the butter go into the bowl first?
Yes. Add the butter to the large bowl, then add the 1 1/3 cups white sugar and the 1 cup chai tea mix with it.
They're in the bowl. What texture am I trying to get before adding anything else?
Cream them together until the mixture looks light and fluffy rather than dense or streaky.
It's lighter now and the chai mix looks worked in. How do I add the eggs?
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each egg before adding the next.
Both eggs are mixed in. I see flour, baking powder, and salt in the directions—do I combine those separately?
Yes, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt together first so the dry ingredients are evenly distributed.
The dry ingredients are mixed. Should I dump them all in or add gradually?
Blend the dry mixture into the creamed mixture until all of the dry has been absorbed; stop once you no longer see dry patches.
The dough has come together. What should I do with it before baking later?
Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour so it firms up before you continue with the cookies.
Can you guide me through Easy Fried Eggplant while I prep the eggplant and skillet?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons canola oil, 1 large eggplant that's peeled and sliced, 3 beaten eggs, and 2 cups dry bread crumbs.
The eggplant is peeled and sliced. Should I put the oil in the pan before breading everything?
Yes. Pour the 2 tablespoons canola oil into a large skillet and heat it over medium-high heat while you get the coating station ready.
I've got a bowl of beaten eggs and another bowl with the dry bread crumbs. What order should the slices go in?
Dip each eggplant slice into the beaten egg first, then press it into the bread crumbs so it's coated.
The oil looks hot. Do the coated slices go in right away, or should I wait?
Place the coated eggplant slices into the hot oil carefully, working in a single layer so they fry evenly.
They're in the skillet now. How long should I cook the first side?
Fry the slices for 2 to 3 minutes on that side, watching for a golden brown crust.
The bottoms are golden. Should I flip them and use the same timing?
Yes, turn them over and fry the second side for another 2 to 3 minutes, until that side is golden brown too.
They look crisp and browned. What's the best way to take them out without making them soggy?
Lift the fried eggplant from the skillet and drain the slices on paper towels before serving.
I want to make Cheddar Artichoke Quiche Cups. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Pull out 1 (7.5 ounce) jar of marinated artichoke hearts, 1 small onion finely chopped, 1 minced garlic clove, and 4 beaten eggs.
The artichoke jar is open, and I have a bowl and skillet ready. Should I pour off all the marinade?
Drain the artichokes, but keep half of the marinade aside. You'll use that saved marinade to cook the onion and garlic.
I reserved half. The artichokes are still whole pieces, though—how small should they be?
Chop the artichoke hearts into small pieces so they'll mix evenly into the quiche cups, then set them aside for a moment.
Done. My onion is finely chopped and the garlic is minced. Does the skillet need oil too?
Use the reserved marinade in the skillet instead of adding separate oil. Add the onion and garlic and sauté them in that marinade until they're tender.
They're softening and it smells good. Should I keep them cooking until browned?
No need to brown them deeply. Once the onion is tender and the garlic is fragrant, take the skillet off the heat and set that mixture aside.
The skillet mixture is resting. I've got the beaten eggs in a large bowl—what goes in with them?
Combine the egg with bread crumbs, mustard, oregano, pepper, and hot pepper sauce in the large bowl. Stir until the mixture looks evenly blended.
Should I add the chopped artichokes and the onion-garlic mixture to that bowl after it's mixed?
Yes, fold in the chopped artichokes along with the sautéed onion and garlic so everything is evenly distributed before portioning the mixture into cups.
I'm making Butterscotch Brownies in a Jar. Can you help me get set up without me missing anything?
Absolutely. For the jar mix, make sure you have 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 tablespoons baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup flaked coconut.
I see the flour and coconut on the counter. The baking powder and salt are measured too. What do I need besides the jar ingredients?
You'll also need 3/4 cup softened butter, 2 beaten eggs, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract when it's time to mix the batter.
The butter is softening, and I have a 9x13 inch pan ready. Should I turn the oven on yet?
Yes, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the batter is ready.
Oven is heating. Do I prep the pan while I wait?
Go ahead and grease the 9x13 inch baking pan well, especially the corners, so the brownies release cleanly.
Pan is greased. The jar mix looks a little packed down. How should I handle that?
Empty the jar of brownie mix into a large mixing bowl, then stir through the dry mix to break up any lumps before adding the wet ingredients.
The dry mix is loosened up now. Should the eggs go in whole or beaten?
Use 2 beaten eggs. Add them to the bowl along with the 3/4 cup softened butter and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract.
Everything is in the bowl. What texture am I looking for before I put it in the pan?
Mix until the batter is well blended, with no dry pockets of mix left. Once it looks evenly combined, spread it into the greased pan.
Can you walk me through making churros? I've got a saucepan out and want to get the ingredients lined up before heating anything.

Absolutely. For the base, measure 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also need flour ready to stir in once the hot mixture comes off the heat.
The water, sugar, salt, oil, and flour are on the counter. Should I use the saucepan now?
Yes. Put the saucepan over medium heat, then add the 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. Stir just enough to combine everything evenly.
It's mixed in the pan and starting to warm. Am I waiting for bubbles or just heating it through?
Let it come all the way to a boil. Once it reaches a boil, take the saucepan off the heat right away so the liquid is hot but not continuing to cook down.
It boiled, and I moved it off the burner. The pan is on a towel now. What should the flour step look like?
Stir in the flour while the liquid is still hot. Keep mixing until the dough comes together and forms a ball rather than looking loose or streaky.
The dough is clumping, but there are still a few dry bits on the side of the pan. Should I keep stirring?
Yes, scrape around the sides and keep working it until those dry bits are incorporated. The goal is one cohesive ball of dough.
Okay, I've got a smooth ball now. I'm setting up to fry—what temperature should the oil be?
Heat the frying oil in a deep-fryer or a deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. Use enough oil for frying safely, and give it time to come fully up to temperature.
I'm using a deep skillet. Any quick safety check before I start cooking the dough?

Keep the skillet stable, avoid filling it too high with oil, and use a thermometer to hold the oil around 375 degrees F or 190 degrees C before adding dough. Once the dough goes in, work carefully so the hot oil doesn't splash.
Can you guide me through making Easy Pavlova? I want to get everything set up before I start mixing.
Absolutely. For this pavlova, set out 4 egg whites, 1 1/4 cups white sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
I've got the eggs and sugar measured. Should the oven be heating already?
Yes—preheat the oven to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C, so it's ready when the meringue is prepared.
Oven is on. What pan setup do I need?
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Make sure it sits flat so the pavlova base is easy to shape.
Parchment is on the sheet. How big should I make the guide circle?
Draw a 9 inch circle on the parchment paper. You can use a plate or cake pan as a guide, then flip the parchment over so the pencil side doesn't touch the meringue.
Circle is drawn and the sheet is ready. I'm about to separate the eggs—what texture am I aiming for when I beat them?
Put the egg whites in a large bowl and beat them until they're stiff but not dry. They should hold peaks, but still look smooth rather than clumpy.
Should I add the vanilla extract and lemon juice before beating, or keep them nearby for later?
Keep the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and 1 teaspoon lemon juice measured and nearby. The recipe starts the bowl work by beating the 4 egg whites to that stiff-but-not-dry stage.
Got it. I'll start beating the egg whites now—any quick check before I continue?

Use a clean large bowl and stop once the peaks stand firmly without the whites looking dry. Your oven should already be at 300 degrees F (150 degrees C), and the parchment with the 9 inch circle should be ready on the baking sheet.
Can you help me make Chipotle Mayo Relish? I've got a food processor out but haven't started measuring yet.

Absolutely. Measure 1 cup light mayonnaise and 2 tablespoons canned Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce. Seed and mince the peppers before they go in, so the relish blends smoothly without big spicy pieces.
The peppers are minced. Should the mayo and chipotle go straight into the processor together?
Yes, add the mayonnaise and minced chipotle peppers to the food processor together. Process until the mixture looks evenly blended and creamy.
It's blended, but I still have some adobo sauce left in the can. Do I use any of that?
You can add a little more of the adobo sauce if you want extra smoky heat. About 1/2 teaspoon is a good amount, then pulse briefly to mix it in.
I added the 1/2 teaspoon and pulsed it. What should the texture be like before I move it out of the processor?
It should look smooth and well combined, like a flavored mayo. Once there aren't streaks of plain mayonnaise or clumps of chipotle, scrape it into a serving bowl.
Okay, it's in the bowl. I still need to add the green onion and relish, right?
Right. Stir in 1/4 cup chopped green onion and 1/4 cup sweet pickle relish by hand, so they stay a little textured instead of getting pureed.
Should I mix it a lot or just fold it until everything is spread through?
Just stir or fold until the green onion and sweet pickle relish are evenly distributed. Try not to overwork it; the little bits add crunch and sweetness.
It looks ready. Can I serve it right away with sandwiches, or does it need time in the fridge?
Chill it until serving. Even a short rest in the refrigerator helps the chipotle, green onion, and sweet pickle relish settle into the mayonnaise before you put it out.
I want to make German Sweet Chocolate Pie. Can you help me get set up before I start melting anything?
Absolutely. Set out 1 (4 ounce) bar German sweet chocolate, chopped, plus 1/3 cup milk. You'll also want a large microwave-safe bowl and a whisk nearby.
Chocolate is chopped and the milk is measured. Do I need the dairy softened before mixing?
Yes—have 4 ounces cream cheese softened so it blends smoothly. Also measure 2 tablespoons white sugar before you start.
The cream cheese feels soft enough. How much milk goes in with the chocolate at the beginning?
Put the chopped German sweet chocolate in the large microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of the milk. Keep the rest of the 1/3 cup milk aside for the mixing step.
Okay, bowl is ready. What microwave timing should I use so it doesn't scorch?
Microwave it on high for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, just until the chocolate is almost melted. Pause and stir halfway through the heating time.
It's mostly melted after stirring. Should it be completely smooth before I add anything else?

It should be close; the residual heat can smooth out the last soft bits as you whisk. Beat in the softened cream cheese, the 2 tablespoons white sugar, and the remaining milk with a wire whisk until everything is blended.
The mixture is blended but still a little loose. Is there a chilling step before the topping?
Yes, refrigerate the mixture for 10 minutes. That short chill helps it firm up before you fold in the whipped topping.
It has chilled for 10 minutes. How do I mix in the topping without deflating it?
Add 3 1/2 cups of the whipped topping and gently fold it in with broad, slow strokes until no streaks remain. Stop once it looks evenly combined so the filling stays light.
Can you help me make Fudge Drops? I've got a saucepan out, but I want to make sure I'm starting with the right ingredients.

Absolutely. For Fudge Drops, set out 1 2/3 cups sugar, 1 (5 ounce) can evaporated milk, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. You'll also want a heavy saucepan, a spoon for constant stirring, baking sheets, and waxed paper.
I have the sugar and the 5 ounce can of evaporated milk measured. Should the butter go in right away too?
Yes. Put the sugar, evaporated milk, 2 tablespoons butter or margarine, and 1/2 teaspoon salt all into the heavy saucepan together before turning on the heat.
Everything is in the pan. The mixture looks a little grainy from the sugar—is that okay before heating?
That's fine at this point. Place the saucepan over medium heat and start stirring constantly so the sugar dissolves evenly and the mixture doesn't scorch on the bottom.
It's warming up now. Should I stop stirring once I see bubbles around the edges?
Keep stirring constantly. Let it come all the way to a boil over medium heat while you continue moving the spoon through the mixture.
It has reached a boil and I'm still stirring. What should I do when it's boiled?
Remove the saucepan from the heat. Once it's off the burner, stir in the remaining ingredients called for in your recipe.
Okay, it's off the heat and mixed. I've got the baking sheets ready—do they need anything on them?
Line the baking sheets with waxed paper before portioning the candy mixture. That will help the Fudge Drops release cleanly once they set.
What size should I make each drop so they're consistent?
Drop the mixture by tablespoonfuls onto the waxed paper-lined baking sheets. Space them a bit apart so they keep their shape as they cool.
I want to make Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes. Can you guide me while I get set up?

Absolutely. Have your Fast Chicken Soup Base ready as the starting point, plus a 9 ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, a 14.5 ounce can of diced tomatoes, 2 medium zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
I've got the soup base and tortellini. The zucchini are whole, though—how should I prep them?
Dice the 2 medium zucchini into bite-size pieces so they'll soften in the soup at about the same pace as the tortellini.
Zucchini is diced, and I opened the tomatoes. Should I drain the 14.5 ounce can?
Use the diced tomatoes as part of the soup mixture; add them when the tortellini and zucchini go in.
The Fast Chicken Soup Base is in the pot. What heat should I use?
Set the pot over heat and bring the Fast Chicken Soup Base to a simmer—look for gentle bubbling rather than a hard boil.
It's starting to bubble lightly around the edges. Is that enough?
Yes, that's the right point. Stir in the 1 9-ounce package of refrigerated small cheese tortellini, the 1 14.5-ounce can of diced tomatoes, the diced zucchini, and 1 tsp. dried basil.
Everything is in the pot. The tortellini are floating a bit already—do I cover it?
Keep it at a steady simmer and cook for 10-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tortellini and zucchini are tender.
At around 10 minutes, what texture should I check for before serving?

Taste a tortellini and a piece of zucchini. The tortellini should be tender, and the zucchini should be softened but not falling apart; if they need more time, keep simmering within that 10-20 minute range.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Tortellini Soup With Zucchini and Tomatoes

messages.content: I'm making Escargots Vol au Vent and want to keep it organized. Can you guide me from prep onward?
Absolutely. Set out 12 helix snails without shells and 1/2 cup softened butter so they're ready when you start mixing.
The snails are out of the package, and the butter is soft. What aromatics should I prep before heating anything?
Finely chop 2 cloves of garlic and 1 green onion. If your parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine are nearby too, the mixing step will go smoothly.
I've got a bowl and a small knife ready. Should the oven be on already?
Yes, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's hot when you need it.
The oven is heating. The escargots look a little packed in liquid—how should I handle them?
Drain the escargots, rinse them under cold water, then drain them again well so they don't water down the butter mixture.
They're rinsed and sitting in the strainer. Do I dry them with towels or just leave them drained?
Letting them drain thoroughly is enough for this recipe. While they finish draining, put the softened butter into your mixing bowl.
Butter is in the bowl. What goes into it, and should I stir as I add things?
Add the finely chopped garlic and green onion, then add the parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine. Stir as you go if that helps distribute everything evenly.
Everything is in the bowl now. What texture am I aiming for before I use it with the escargots?
Mix thoroughly until the butter looks evenly seasoned and the garlic, green onion, parsley, pepper, nutmeg, and wine are well incorporated throughout.
Can you help me make Eggnog II? I've got a saucepan out, but I want to make sure I use everything in the right order.
Absolutely. For this Eggnog II, you'll need 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The eggs are beaten, and I measured the milk. Should the vanilla go in the pan right away too?
Start by putting the beaten eggs, the 2 1/4 cups milk, and the 1/3 cup sugar into a large saucepan. Hold the vanilla extract for later since the cooking step only uses those three ingredients.
They're in the saucepan. The mixture looks pretty thin—does that sound right before heating?
Yes, that's expected at this point. Set the pan over medium heat and stir as it cooks so the egg mixture warms evenly.
I'm stirring over medium heat. How do I know when it's cooked enough?
Keep cooking and stirring until the mixture coats a metal spoon. You're looking for it to cling lightly to the spoon instead of running off immediately.
It's starting to coat the spoon now. Should I keep it on the burner a little longer?
Once it coats a metal spoon, take the saucepan off the heat. Don't keep cooking it past that point.
Okay, it's off the heat. I have a bowl of ice water ready in the sink—do I put the pan directly in it?
Yes. Place the pan in the sink or bowl of ice water, being careful not to splash water into the eggnog, and stir for 1 to 2 minutes to cool it quickly.
That cooled it down. Where does the vanilla fit in before serving?
Stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract after cooling, then it's ready to serve or chill further if you'd like it colder.

I've got the pot out, but the chicken is still whole. How should I cut it?
Cut the 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into 1 inch pieces. Keep 2 tablespoons cooking oil ready for the pot.
Chicken is cut. I have sea salt and chili powder out too—how much chili powder should I plan on?
Use 1 tablespoon chili powder, or adjust to taste. You'll also season with sea salt, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper once the chicken is browned.
Perfect—the bowl should look intentional, not evenly dusted all over. Should I heat the pot now?
Yes. Pour the 2 tablespoons cooking oil into the large pot and warm it over medium heat until it looks loose and glossy.
The oil is shimmering. Should I add all the chicken pieces at once?
Add the chicken to the pot and brown it on all sides. If the pieces are packed tightly, give them a little space so they brown instead of steaming.
The chicken is taking on color around the edges. Is this when the spices go in?
Once the chicken is browned on all sides, season it with sea salt, the chili powder, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Stir so the pieces get coated.
The spices smell good now. I've chopped the onion and both bell peppers—green and yellow.
Mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper. Stir them through the seasoned chicken so they start softening in the pot.
It's coming together and looks chunky. When I serve it, how should I handle the garnish and the bowls?
Ladle the Chicken and Black Bean Chili into bowls, then place the soft garnish in the center and shape the crisp garnish into that small side crescent. Wipe any splashes from the rim before serving.
Can you guide me through Chicken Pot Pie II? I'm starting with the chicken and broth.
Absolutely. Set out 1 1/2 pounds of skinless, boneless chicken breast meat and 1 cup chicken broth, and use a large saucepan so the chicken has room to simmer.
I've got the saucepan out. Do the seasonings go in right away or later?
They go in right away with the chicken and broth: add 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper.
Should the pan be on the stove before I add everything?
Yes. Put the large saucepan over medium high heat, then combine the chicken meat, chicken broth, salt, and pepper in the pan.
Everything is in the pan and starting to warm. What am I watching for?
Let the liquid come up to a boil. Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat to low.
It's boiling now, and I've turned the heat down. Do I leave it uncovered?
Cover the saucepan and let the chicken simmer gently for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, how do I know the chicken is done enough?
Check that the chicken is no longer pink in the center and that the juices run clear.
It looks cooked through. What should I do with the chicken before using it for the pie?
Remove the chicken from the saucepan and let it cool before handling or adding it to the next part of the pot pie.

messages.content: When we make Bs Cordon Bleu Bundles as a bowl-style plate, can you keep the chicken, cheese, and crescent parts from getting piled together?

Yes. I'll guide it so the chicken, Brie, and crescent pieces are plated in slim separate strips, with softer or juicy bits away from anything flaky, and the sections only touching near the middle of the bowl.
Perfect. I'm setting up the stove now—what should go on the counter first?
Set out 2 teaspoons olive oil and 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves. You'll also want a heavy skillet, or a nonstick frying pan if you'd rather use cooking spray.
I found the skillet and the chicken. The dough and cheese are still in the fridge—do I need both now?
Yes, bring out 1 10 ounce can of refrigerated large crescent roll dough and 8 ounces Brie cheese so everything is ready when the chicken is done.
That separated-strip plating is exactly how I like these bowls, so keep steering me that way. How do I start cooking the chicken?
Warm the heavy skillet with the olive oil, or coat the nonstick pan with cooking spray. Once the pan is hot, add the chicken breasts in a single layer.
They're in the pan. What texture or doneness should I watch for before I pull them?
Sauté the chicken breasts until they're no longer pink and the juices run clear. When they reach that point, move them to a plate and set them aside.
Chicken is resting on a plate. Should I heat the oven now or deal with the dough first?
Heat the oven now to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C. While it preheats, keep the dough chilled until you're ready to open it.
Oven is heating. I'm opening the crescent can—how much dough am I using?
Unroll 4 large crescent rolls. Keep them flat and separated so they're easy to portion with the chicken and Brie later.
The rolls are unrolled, and I want serving to stay tidy with less cleanup. How should I organize the bowl?

Use the rested chicken for one strip, the 8 ounces Brie as its own strip, and the crescent roll pieces in a separate flaky strip. Keep any juices from the chicken off the crescent section, then let the strips angle inward so they meet neatly at the center.

messages.content: For Bahama Mama II, can we do my outer-rim sweet finish instead of glazing the whole surface?
Yes. I'll keep any sweet glaze or sugar accent just around the outside edge of the glass, while the drink itself stays true to the recipe.
Perfect. I've got a mixing glass out—what bottles and mixers should I put on the counter?
Set out 1 fluid ounce dark rum, 1/2 fluid ounce apricot brandy, 3 1/2 fluid ounces fruit punch, and 1/2 fluid ounce pina colada mix. You'll also want ice for serving.
The rim is ready, and I have the rum and apricot brandy measured. Do they go in together?
They do. Pour the dark rum and apricot brandy into the mixing glass first, then keep the glass steady so the rim finish stays clean.
Good—that edge-only finish is the way I like this drink, not a full sweet layer. What goes in after the spirits?
Add the fruit punch and the pina colada mix to the same mixing glass with the rum and apricot brandy.
The pina colada mix looks a little thicker than the punch. Should I shake it or just stir?
For this recipe, stir to blend. Use a bar spoon or regular spoon and mix until the color looks even and the thicker mix is worked through.
It's blended now. Should the ice go into the mixing glass or the serving glass?
Serve it over ice, so fill the serving glass with ice and pour the blended Bahama Mama II over it.
The outer rim still looks tidy. Anything I should check before handing it over?
Make sure the drink is fully blended and cold from the ice. If any sweet finish slipped inward, wipe the inner lip lightly so the accent stays mostly on the outside edge.
Got it. I'm serving it right away—any last cleanup tips?
Serve it immediately over the ice. Then rinse the mixing glass and spoon before the pina colada mix dries, and recap the rum, apricot brandy, fruit punch, and mix.
I want to make a Cold Cocoa Smoothie, but I'm still clearing space by the blender. What should I pull from the freezer and fridge first?
Grab 1 1/2 scoops vanilla ice cream from the freezer and measure 1 1/2 cups milk from the fridge. Set both near the blender so the ice cream doesn't sit out too long.
The ice cream and milk are out. I also have a chilled glass in the freezer—what else goes into the blender?
You'll need 1/4 cup whipped cream and 2 tablespoons instant hot chocolate mix. The recipe also calls for crushed cookies in the blender, so have those ready too.
Should I add the milk first, or does the order not matter much for texture?

For easier blending, pour in the milk first, then add the vanilla ice cream, whipped cream, hot chocolate mix, and crushed cookies. That follows the recipe while helping the blades catch everything smoothly.
Everything is in the blender. The hot chocolate mix is sitting on top—should I scrape down the sides before blending?
Yes, if any powder is stuck to the sides, tap or scrape it down into the liquid. Then secure the lid tightly before you blend.
Lid is on. How smooth should I make it—completely thin or still a little thick?
Blend until smooth. It should look evenly cocoa-colored with no dry mix pockets or large cookie pieces, while still having a creamy smoothie texture.
It looks smooth now. My chilled glass is ready; do I pour it all in at once?
Yes, pour the smoothie into the large chilled glass. Go slowly at first so it doesn't splash, especially if it's thick.
There's a little foam on top and some smoothie left in the blender jar. Any serving tip before I rinse things?
Spoon or pour the remaining smoothie into the glass, then serve it right away while it's cold and creamy. After that, rinse the blender jar promptly so the cocoa and whipped cream don't cling.
I'm making Date Nut Bars and have a large mixing bowl out. Can you help me get started without rushing it?
Absolutely. Set out 2 cups sugar, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need dates, nuts, eggs, butter, and vanilla for the batter.
The dry ingredients are on the counter. Should I grease the pan before mixing?
Yes, go ahead and grease a 15-in pan now so the stiff batter can go straight in once it's mixed.
Pan is greased. Do the dates and nuts go in with the flour mixture or later?
Put them in with the dry ingredients. In the large bowl, combine the sugar, flour, baking powder, salt, dates, and nuts until everything is evenly distributed.
That's mixed. It looks dry and chunky from the dates and nuts. Is that okay?
That's exactly fine at this point. Add the eggs, butter, and vanilla, then stir only until the dry ingredients are moistened.
I'm stirring, but it's turning into a really stiff batter. Should I keep working it smooth?
No need to make it loose or perfectly smooth—the recipe says the batter will be very stiff. Stop once there aren't obvious dry pockets.
Okay, I don't see dry flour anymore. What's the best way to get it into the pan?
Spoon the batter into the greased 15-in pan and spread it as evenly as you can, pressing it gently into the corners if needed.
It's spread in the pan. What oven setting and bake time should I use?
Bake the Date Nut Bars at 350 degrees F for 20-25 minutes, until the top is golden brown.
I'm making Eggnog Blend today. Can you talk me through it from setup to chilling?
Absolutely. Set out a saucepan, a whisk, and a bowl or container for chilling. For the base, you'll need 4 cups half-and-half and 1 cup white sugar.
I've got the saucepan out and measured the half-and-half and sugar. Are the eggs added right away?
Not quite yet. Also have 11 beaten egg yolks ready, plus 1 teaspoon vanilla extract for later after the mixture has chilled.
The yolks are beaten. How low should I keep the heat when I start?
Use low heat. Pour the half-and-half into the saucepan, add the white sugar, and stir gently until the sugar is mixed in and the dairy is warming evenly.
The sugar looks dissolved and the mixture is warm. I'm worried about scrambling the yolks.
Whisk the beaten egg yolks in gradually while keeping the heat low. Keep the whisk moving so the mixture thickens smoothly into a light custard.
What texture tells me the custard is ready?
You're looking for a light custard consistency—slightly thickened and smooth. Do not let it boil; if you see it getting too hot, pull it off the heat briefly while whisking.
It's smooth and lightly thickened, with no bubbling. What should I do before refrigerating it?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the mixture cool. Once it's cooled down, transfer it to your chilling container, cover it, and refrigerate it overnight.
After it chills overnight, what gets stirred in before serving?
Into the chilled mixture, stir in the vanilla extract, cream, dark rum, scotch, and vanilla ice cream until everything is blended and creamy.
I want to make Carrots and Onions Au Gratin. Can you help me get organized before I start slicing?
Absolutely. You'll need 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots, sliced, and 2 medium onions, sliced. Have a pot ready for boiling and a baking dish for later.
The carrots are sliced and the onions are ready. What dairy and fat should I pull out?
Set out 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter. Once those are nearby, you're ready to start cooking.
Everything is on the counter. Should the oven be heating while I work on the vegetables?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's hot when the vegetables are ready for the baking dish.
Oven is heating. What size pot situation do I need for the carrots and onions?
Use a pot large enough to hold the sliced carrots and onions with water covering them. Add enough lightly salted water to cover the vegetables, then bring it to a boil.
The water is starting to bubble. How long should I cook them, and what texture am I looking for?
Cook them for 5 minutes, just until they're tender but still firm. You don't want them too soft before they go into the oven.

Great. Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves and cut them into bite-size pieces. You'll also need 1 chopped onion ready for the pot.

Have 1/2 pound baby carrots and 4 potatoes ready. If the potatoes are large, cut them into stew-friendly chunks so they cook evenly with the carrots and chicken.

Add the chopped onion, the bite-size chicken breast pieces, the baby carrots, and the potatoes directly to the large pot.

Sprinkle in the salt and turmeric now so they can season the chicken and vegetables from the beginning.

Dissolve the tomato paste in water first, then pour that mixture into the pot so it spreads through the stew more evenly.

If you'd like, season it with garlic powder and ground black pepper. Those are optional, so add them to taste.

Make sure the chicken is fully cooked and the potatoes and carrots are tender. Give the stew a stir before serving so the turmeric, tomato paste, and seasonings are evenly distributed.

Absolutely. For the chicken portion, set out 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided, and 2 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, about 6 ounces each.

You'll need 1 1/2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning and 2 cloves garlic, crushed. Keep the garlic close by so you can stir it in once the chicken is in the pan.

Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side, then turn it and cook 5 minutes on the other side.

Check that the juices run clear when you cut into the thickest part. Once they do, take the chicken out of the skillet and let it rest briefly before slicing it for the salad.

For this recipe, measure everything straight into the large mixing bowl together: the dry ingredients plus the buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.

Beat the batter for 3 minutes, scraping the sides if flour clings to the bowl, until it looks evenly combined.

Yes. Pour the batter into the greased 9x5 inch loaf pan and start baking without the topping. When the loaf is in its final third of cooking, sprinkle on your crumb or streusel topping.

Look for the topping to stay separate and pick up just enough color while the bread finishes. Let the loaf cool a bit in the pan before turning it out so the top stays neat.
Can you walk me through Cinnamon Sugar Cookies 2? I'm setting out the mixing bowl now.
Absolutely. For the ingredients listed, pull out 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup confectioners' sugar, and 1 cup vegetable oil.

Yes, use the egg and vanilla amounts from your full recipe copy. The step itself is to add them after the creamed mixture and mix until incorporated.

Add the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and cream of tartar. Mix gently at first so the flour doesn't puff out, then continue until the dough comes together.

Once it starts looking like a proper cookie dough, switch to a spatula or sturdy spoon if your mixer is straining. You just want the dry ingredients evenly worked in.

They're optional, so stir in the pecans only if desired. You can also leave the full batch plain or fold pecans into just part of the dough before shaping and baking according to your recipe's remaining directions.

Use a small bowl and whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, mint, and 2 Tbs. water until the sugar dissolves and the herbs are evenly spread through it.
Should the dressing taste more salty, sour, or sweet before it goes on the chicken?
It should lean bright and savory: lime gives the sour edge, fish sauce brings saltiness, sugar rounds it out, and red pepper adds heat. Since it will coat chicken and celery, a punchy taste is fine.

I've got the jar, sugar, cocoa, flour, and pecans on the counter. Should the jar be totally dry before I start?
Yes, make sure the jar is completely clean and dry so the layers stay neat and the dry mix doesn't clump.
All right, the jar is dry. Which ingredient goes in the bottom?
Layer the ingredients in the order listed, so start with the 2 cups white sugar in the bottom of the jar.

A small uneven edge is fine, but you can gently tap the jar on the counter to level it before adding the next layer.

Add the 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder next, keeping it as a separate layer over the sugar.
Cocoa is in, and I'm trying not to smear it on the glass. What comes after that?
Spoon in the 1 cup all-purpose flour, then add the 1 cup chopped pecans as the final layer on top.
The pecans are on top and the jar is closed. What should the tag say?
Attach a tag with the baking instruction from the recipe: "Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C)."
I'm making Best Macaroni Salad and want to stay organized. What should I put on the counter before I start?

Set out 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup peeled, seeded, chopped cucumber, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. You'll also want a large pot for boiling, a colander, and a big mixing bowl.
I've got the pot and colander ready. Should the water be salted before the macaroni goes in?
Yes, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, then add the macaroni. Cook it until it's al dente so it holds up well in the salad.
The pasta is boiling. How firm should it feel when I check it?
It should be tender but still have a little bite in the center. Once it reaches that point, drain it right away.
Drained. Do I let it sit, or cool it down?
Rinse the macaroni under cold water after draining. That cools it for the salad and helps stop the cooking, then let it drain well.
The pasta is cool and not dripping much. What bowl step comes next?
Move the pasta into a large bowl and add the mayonnaise. Mix well so the macaroni is evenly coated.
It's coated, but I haven't added the cucumber or onion yet. Do they go in together?
Yes. Stir in the chopped cucumber and dried minced onion, along with the ham and cheese from the recipe's mixing step.
Everything is in the bowl now. What should I do before serving?
Give the macaroni salad a final thorough mix so the cucumber, onion, ham, cheese, mayonnaise, and pasta are evenly distributed. Then it's ready to serve.
I want to make Black Bean Lasagna Rolls, but I'd like to prep everything neatly before the noodles get sticky. Can you walk me through it?

Absolutely. Set out 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, a 1 (15 ounce) container of part-skim ricotta cheese, and a 1 (4.5 ounce) can of chopped green chiles, drained. You'll also need the black beans for spooning over the cheese mixture later.
I've got the cheeses and chiles out. Should I start boiling water for the noodles now?
Yes. Cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions, but omit any salt and fat. Once they're done, drain them well so they're not watery when you fill them.
The noodles are cooking. Should I mix the filling while they boil, and what goes in the bowl?
That's a good time to do it. Combine the cheeses with the next 3 ingredients from the recipe, including the drained chopped green chiles, and stir everything well until the mixture is evenly blended.
The filling looks creamy with the chiles mixed through. How dry do the noodles need to be after draining?
Drain them thoroughly and let excess surface water run off. They don't need to be bone-dry, but they should be dry enough that the cheese mixture will spread instead of sliding around.

Spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle. Try to keep it fairly even from end to end so each roll has filling throughout.

Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on the noodles. Keep the layer balanced so the rolls are easy to shape and the beans don't pile up in one spot.
Some beans are rolling toward the edges. Should I press them in or leave them loose?
Gently press them into the cheese mixture just enough to help them stay put. Then the noodles will be ready to roll without losing much filling.

The salsa mix looks colorful and evenly combined. What goes in next?
Stir in the lime juice and lime zest. Fold it through gently so the citrus coats the corn and vegetables without crushing the jicama.
Lime juice and zest are mixed in. The bowl is getting a little juicy at the bottom—is that okay?
Yes, that's fine. Give it a quick toss right before serving so the lime dressing redistributes through the crunchy corn salsa.
Great. I'm ready to prep the spicy part for the fish tacos.
Use the small bowl for that. Combine the cayenne pepper, ground black pepper, and salt, then stir them together so the seasoning is even before you use it on the fish.

messages.content: I'm making Eggnog II and have a large saucepan ready. Can you guide me without rushing the egg mixture?
Absolutely. Set out 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so everything is within reach.
The eggs are beaten, and I measured the milk. Does the vanilla go into the pan right away too?
For the cooking stage, combine only the beaten eggs, the 2 1/4 cups milk, and the 1/3 cup white sugar in the large saucepan.
Okay, the eggs, milk, and sugar are in the saucepan. Should I whisk hard or just stir?
Stir them together until the sugar is blended in and the mixture looks even, then put the saucepan over medium heat.
It's on medium heat now. I'm worried about scrambling the eggs—what should I watch for?
Keep stirring as it cooks. You're looking for the mixture to thicken enough that it coats a metal spoon.
I have a metal spoon here. How do I tell if the coating is enough?
Dip the metal spoon in and lift it out; if a thin layer clings to the spoon instead of running off immediately, it has reached the right point.
The spoon is coated now. Do I keep it on the burner while I get the ice bath ready?
No, remove the saucepan from the heat as soon as it coats the spoon.
It's off the heat. I have a bowl of ice water in the sink—what's the quickest way to cool it?
Place the pan in the sink or bowl of ice water and stir the eggnog for 1 to 2 minutes so it cools quickly. After that, stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.

Peel the onion if the papery skin is loose, then quarter it. Big pieces are perfect here because they'll flavor the stock without needing fine chopping.

Keep some of those celery leaves; they add good flavor. Chop the scrubbed celery and carrot into 1 inch chunks.

Yes. Put the chicken pieces into the large soup pot or Dutch oven, then add the quartered onion, chopped celery, and chopped carrot.

Add the salt and cloves directly to the pot with the chicken and vegetables so they season the liquid as it starts extracting flavor.

Pour in 6 cups water. It should cover or nearly cover the chicken and vegetables; if anything floats, that's fine.
Water is in. Anything I should check before heating it?
Make sure the pot is on a stable burner and not filled too close to the rim. Give the contents a gentle nudge to settle them, then you're ready to start cooking the stock.
Can you help me make Chocolate Cream Dessert? I'm starting with an empty counter and want to get the crust part right.

Put the flour in a bowl, add the cold margarine, and cut the margarine into the flour until the mixture looks crumbly rather than smooth or creamy.
I'm using a pastry cutter, and it's starting to look like coarse crumbs. Is that enough?
Coarse crumbs are right. If you still see a few tiny bits of margarine, that's fine; just avoid working it into a paste.

Transfer the crumb mixture into the sprayed 11-in baking dish and press it evenly across the bottom so it forms a compact layer.

Bake it at 350 degrees F for 15-18 minutes. Look for the crust to become lightly browned, especially around the edges.

Not yet. Take the dish out and let the baked crust cool completely before adding anything on top, so the dessert sets up cleanly.

Can you help me put together Double Fudge Brownie Mix as a jar mix?
Absolutely. Set out a clean 1 quart or 1 liter jar, plus the dry ingredients: 2 cups white sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 cup chopped pecans.
I have the jar washed and dried. Does the sugar go in before the cocoa?

I'm making Almond Buttercrunch and want to get everything measured before the sugar starts cooking. What should I set out?

The cookie sheet is buttered and the saucepan is on the stove. Do the almonds go in now or later?
They go in right away with the candy base. Put the butter, the 2 cups white sugar, and the 1 cup chopped almonds into the saucepan over low heat.

Yes, stir constantly while it heats and comes together. Keep the motion steady until the mixture boils.
It's bubbling now. I'm worried about it sticking—do I still stir?
Once it boils, stop stirring, and don't shake the pan. Let it continue heating undisturbed so the buttercrunch can cook properly.

Cook it to 300 to 310 degrees F, which is 149 to 154 degrees C. That's the hard-crack stage for this candy.

Let it go until the pieces look browned all over and have rendered plenty of fat in the skillet. You don't need to take it past that into very dark or brittle pieces.

Use a slotted spoon to lift the bacon out, leaving the grease behind in the skillet. Transfer the bacon to paper towels so it can drain.

No, discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease. That gives you enough flavorful fat without making the mixture greasy.
I've poured off the extra and left about 1 tablespoon in the skillet. Anything I should check before moving on?
Make sure the oven is still at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), the browned bacon is draining, and your chopped onion, 5 button mushrooms, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef are ready nearby.

Mix the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice into the pot so everything is combined in the soup base.
