Absolutely. Set out 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, salt and pepper, 2 teaspoons olive oil, and 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions.
I have the chicken and the can of diced tomatoes out. Should I open the tomatoes now or focus on the chicken first?
You can keep the tomatoes nearby, but start with the chicken. Pat the chicken breasts if they're wet, then season both sides with salt and pepper.
The chicken is seasoned on both sides. What pan should I use?
Use a large skillet so the chicken breasts have room to brown instead of crowding. Put it over medium-high heat.
The skillet is heating. When does the olive oil go in?
Add the 2 teaspoons olive oil to the hot skillet and let it spread across the surface.
The oil is shimmering a little. Do I put all 4 chicken breast halves in at once?
Yes, if they fit in a single layer with a bit of space between them. Place the chicken in the skillet carefully so the oil doesn't splash.
They're in the pan now. What should I watch for while they cook?
Let the first side brown, then turn each piece once and brown the other side. Try not to keep flipping them; one turn is enough for this step.
Both sides have some color. Do I add the diced tomatoes at this point?
For the step you're on, remove the browned chicken from the pan and set it aside. Keep the 1 (14.5 ounce) can of diced tomatoes with green peppers and onions ready for when the recipe continues.

source_seed.recipe_title: Artichoke and Sun dried Tomato Chicken

messages.content: I'm making Best Macaroni Salad and have a big pot ready. Can you help me get organized before I start boiling anything?

Absolutely. Set out 1 (16 ounce) package macaroni, 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1 cup cucumber that's peeled, seeded, and chopped, and 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. You'll also want a large pot, a colander, and a large mixing bowl.
The macaroni and mayonnaise are on the counter. I still need to prep the cucumber—does it go in raw?
Yes, the cucumber goes in raw. Peel it, scoop out the seeds, then chop enough for 1 cup. Keep the dried minced onion nearby too.
Cucumber is chopped. How much salt should I use for the pasta water?
Use a large pot of salted boiling water—enough water for the macaroni to move freely, with the water tasting lightly salty. Once it's boiling, add the macaroni and cook it until al dente.
The pasta is boiling now. What texture am I looking for before I drain it?
Look for tender pasta with a little firmness in the center, not mushy. When it reaches al dente, drain it in the colander, rinse it under cold water, and let it drain well.
It's rinsed and not steaming anymore. Should I mix it right in the serving bowl?
That works well if the bowl is large enough. Add the cooled, drained pasta to the bowl, spoon in the 1/2 cup mayonnaise, and mix until the macaroni is evenly coated.
The mayo is mixed in. The bowl looks a little plain—what add-ins go next?
Stir in the chopped cucumber and the 1 tablespoon dried minced onion. The recipe also calls for adding ham and cheese at this point, so fold those in with the vegetables if you have them ready.
Everything is in the bowl now. Any last thing before I serve it?
Give it a thorough final mix so the cucumber, onion, ham, and cheese are distributed through the macaroni. Once it's evenly combined, it's ready to serve or chill.
Can you help me set up for Fried Chicken Tenders? I'm pulling out bowls and want to get the breading station right.
Absolutely. Put out three shallow bowls if you have them. Measure 1 cup all-purpose flour into one bowl, and keep 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs ready for another.
The flour is in a shallow bowl, and the bread crumbs are measured. Do the seasonings go into the flour or the crumbs?

Mix the seasonings into the bread crumbs: add 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper to the 2 cups Italian-style seasoned bread crumbs, then stir so the pepper is evenly spread through the crumbs.
Got it. I have the seasoned crumb bowl and the flour bowl side by side. What about the wet bowl?
Use a small bowl for the eggs and water. The recipe doesn't give exact amounts for those, so just prepare them there as your dipping mixture before the crumb coating.
I've got that small bowl ready. What order should the chicken go through so I don't make a mess?
Work one piece at a time. Coat a piece of chicken in the flour first, then dip it into the eggs and water, and then press it into the seasoned bread crumbs.
Should I shake anything off between bowls, or just drop it straight in?
A light shake after the flour helps prevent clumps, then let extra egg drip back into the small bowl before the chicken goes into the bread crumbs. That keeps the coating cleaner and more even.
The first tender is coated. Where should I put each piece after breading?
Set each coated chicken piece aside after it comes out of the bread crumbs. Keep them in a single layer if you can, so the coating stays intact while you bread the rest.
I'm seeing some bare spots in the crumbs on a couple pieces. Is it okay to press more on?

Yes, press a little of the breadcrumb mixture onto any bare areas while the surface is still damp from the egg mixture. Then set the piece aside and continue the same flour, egg-and-water, breadcrumb order for the remaining chicken.

messages.content: For tonight, I'm turning Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip into a wrap filling with its creamy dip texture doing the work. Should I loosen it up or keep it more spreadable?
Keep it sturdy and thick, then smear only a thin layer onto the wrap or bread so it doesn't soak through.
Great, that's exactly the version I want for this batch. I've got the wraps nearby; what should I pull from the fridge first?
Start with the creamy base: measure 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream.
Those are measured. I have a casserole dish out too—what pantry item and vegetable prep do I need?
Grab 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, then drain and chop 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts.
The artichokes are drained and chopped, and the soup mix is open. Should I heat the oven before combining everything?
Yes, set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's ready when the dip is mixed.
Oven is heating. Which dish size should I use, and what goes in together?
Use a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish. Add the mayonnaise, sour cream, soup mix, chopped artichoke hearts, cheese, and crab meat, then stir until evenly combined.
It's mixed and still thick, which seems good for wraps. Do I cover the dish?
Leave it uncovered and bake it for 30 minutes.
While it bakes, should I prep anything for serving so the wraps don't get soggy?
Have the bread or wraps ready, but wait to spread the dip until it comes out. Since you want it as a filling, use a thin layer and keep the rest warm for serving.
The timer's almost done. What's the last move once I take it out?
Serve it immediately while hot, spreading it thick-but-thin across the wrap or bread right before eating.
Can you guide me through Curried Winter Squash? I already have cooked squash mashed and ready.
Absolutely. Measure out 3 cups of the cooked, mashed winter squash into a medium microwave-safe bowl so there's room to stir.
The squash is in the bowl. What seasonings and add-ins should I set beside it?
You'll need 1 1/2 tablespoons curry powder, 2 tablespoons butter or trans fat-free margarine, and 2 tablespoons maple syrup.
I've measured the curry powder and maple syrup. Should the butter be melted first?
It doesn't have to be melted ahead of time; add the butter or trans fat-free margarine to the warm squash, and it should soften as you mix.
Okay, everything is in the bowl now. How thoroughly should I stir it?
Stir until the curry powder is evenly blended through the squash and the maple syrup and butter are worked in. The recipe's mixing step is to combine the ingredients in the medium bowl.
The color looks even and there aren't any streaks of curry powder. Do I cover it for the microwave?
You can loosely cover it to reduce splatters, then microwave on high until heated through, about 5 minutes.
It's been 5 minutes and the bowl is hot. Should I stir again before serving?
Yes, give it a careful stir so the heat is even throughout. If you want the optional topping, sprinkle on coconut now.
I'm skipping coconut tonight. What's the best way to serve it?
Spoon the Curried Winter Squash into a serving dish or directly onto plates while it's hot, then serve.
Can you help me make Chocolate Cream Dessert? I'm setting out the baking dish and ingredients now.
Absolutely. For the crust, pull out 1/4 cup cold margarine and 1 cup all-purpose flour. You'll also want nonstick cooking spray for the baking dish.
I have the cold margarine and flour measured. Should the cream cheese be out yet?
Yes, set out 1 (8 ounce) package light cream cheese so it can be softened, and measure 2 tablespoons heat-stable granular sugar substitute as well.
The cream cheese is softening on the counter. What size dish am I using?
Use an 11-in baking dish, and coat it with nonstick cooking spray before adding the crust mixture.
Dish is sprayed. How do I combine the margarine and flour without overworking it?
Put the flour in a bowl, add the cold margarine, and cut the margarine into the flour until the mixture looks crumbly rather than smooth.
It looks like coarse crumbs now, with a few small margarine pieces. Is that okay?
That's right for this crust. Press the crumbly mixture evenly into the sprayed 11-in baking dish, making sure it reaches the corners.
It's pressed in. Should I preheat and bake it right away?
Bake it at 350 degrees F for 15-18 minutes, watching for the crust to become lightly browned.
The edges are just starting to brown. What should I do when it comes out?
Take the dish out and let the crust cool completely before adding or serving the rest of the Chocolate Cream Dessert components.
Can you talk me through Country Fried Chicken while I set up the counter?

Absolutely. Put out a large resealable plastic bag, a shallow bowl, and your chicken. For the seasoned flour, measure 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika.
The bag and bowl are out. Should the flour and seasonings go straight into the bag?

Yes. Add the 1/3 cup flour, 1 teaspoon garlic salt, 1 teaspoon pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon paprika to the large resealable plastic bag, then seal it and give it a quick shake so the seasoning is evenly mixed.
The flour mixture looks blended. What should I do with the egg and milk?
Crack the egg into the shallow bowl, add the milk, and beat them together until the mixture looks smooth enough for dipping.
The egg mixture is ready. Do I coat all the chicken at once?
Work with just a few pieces at a time. Add them to the bag with the flour mixture, seal it well, and shake until the chicken is coated all over.
A few pieces are floured now, and there's some loose coating in the bag. Is that okay?
That's fine. Lift the pieces out gently, letting extra flour fall back into the bag, then dip each piece into the beaten egg and milk mixture.
They're wet from the egg mixture. Do they go back into the same flour bag?
Yes, return those dipped pieces to the flour mixture in the bag. Seal it again and shake so they get a second coating.
The coating looks thicker now. Should I repeat that with the rest of the chicken?
Exactly. Keep going in small batches: flour in the bag, dip in the egg-and-milk mixture, then back into the flour mixture for another shake. That keeps the coating even without overcrowding the bag.
I'm making Gingered Mango Salsa. Can you help me set up so I don't miss anything?

Absolutely. Put out a mixing bowl, a knife, a cutting board, and measuring cups. For the salsa you'll need 1 cup chopped peeled mango, 1/4 cup chopped red onion, 1/4 cup minced fresh cilantro, and 1/4 cup lime juice.
The mango is peeled, but I haven't chopped it yet. How small should I cut it?
Chop it into small bite-size pieces so it scoops easily with chips or sits neatly on fish, chicken, or tacos. Measure out 1 cup once it's chopped.
I have the cup of mango in the bowl. The red onion is strong—do I still use the full amount?
Use the recipe amount: 1/4 cup chopped red onion. Since it's a small quantity, it will bring crunch and sharpness without taking over once it mixes with the lime juice and mango.
Okay, onion is chopped and added. What should I do with the cilantro?
Mince the fresh cilantro finely, then add 1/4 cup to the bowl. A fine mince helps it spread through the salsa instead of clumping.
Cilantro is in. I squeezed the lime juice into a measuring cup.
Great—measure 1/4 cup lime juice and pour it over the mango, red onion, and cilantro. Then gently stir everything together until the pieces are evenly coated.
It's mixed. It looks a little juicy at the bottom of the bowl—is that all right?
Yes, that's fine. The lime juice is part of the salsa and will help the flavors come together while it rests.
How long should it sit before I serve it?
Let the salsa stand for 30 minutes before serving. Give it one gentle stir after the rest, then spoon it into a serving bowl with the juices included.
I'm making Chai Butter Cookies and have my mixing bowl out. Can you guide me from the beginning?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup chai tea mix, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and 2 eggs so everything is ready before you start mixing.
The butter is soft, and I measured the chai tea mix and sugar. Do they all go in together?
Yes. In a large bowl, cream the butter with the 1 1/3 cups white sugar and the chai tea mix until the mixture looks light and fluffy.
I'm using a hand mixer. What texture should I look for before stopping?
Stop once the mixture is evenly combined, paler, and fluffy rather than dense or streaky. Scrape the sides of the bowl once or twice so the chai mix blends in well.
That looks fluffy now. I have 2 eggs waiting on the counter.
Beat in the eggs one at a time. Add the first egg and mix well, then add the second egg and mix again until the batter looks smooth.
The eggs are mixed in. The bowl looks a little looser now—does that seem right?
Yes, that's expected after the eggs go in. Next, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt separately, then blend that dry mixture into the creamed mixture.
Should I dump all the dry ingredients in at once or add them gradually?
Add them gradually if that feels easier with your mixer. Keep mixing just until all of the dry mixture has been absorbed into the dough.
The dough has come together and I don't see dry patches. What should I do before baking later?
Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour. That rest will firm it up before you move on to shaping or baking.
Can you walk me through Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing? I've got a cutting board out and the rotisserie chicken nearby.
Absolutely. Start by skinning and boning enough rotisserie chicken to make 4 cups of meat, then shred it into bite-sized pieces so it will catch the dressing well.
The chicken is shredded. What should I prep from the produce drawer?
Cut 2 medium celery ribs into small dice, then slice 2 medium green onions thinly. Keep both fairly small so they mix evenly through the chicken.
Celery and green onions are ready. Do the peanuts go in now or later?
Add them now. Put the shredded chicken, diced celery, sliced green onions, and 1/4 cup chopped honey-roasted peanuts into a medium bowl and give everything a gentle mix.
That bowl is mixed. I'm setting up a smaller bowl for the dressing—what goes into it?
In the small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, sugar, red pepper, cilantro, mint, and 2 Tbs. water until the sugar is dissolved and the herbs are distributed.
Should the dressing be completely smooth, or is it okay if the herbs float around?
It's fine for the cilantro and mint to float through it. You're mainly looking for the sugar to dissolve and the lime juice, fish sauce, ginger, red pepper, and water to come together.
The dressing smells bright and a little spicy. How much should I pour over the chicken mixture?
Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and toss gently, scraping around the sides of the bowl so the chicken, celery, green onions, and peanuts all get coated.
It's coated now. What's the best way to plate it?
Serve the chicken salad on a bed of Boston lettuce, then add the suggested accompaniments alongside if you're using them. It's ready to eat right away.

source_seed.recipe_title: Chicken Salad With Thai Flavored Dressing

messages.content: I'm making Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake. Can you help me get organized before I start?
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 6 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened chocolate, chopped.
I've got the flour, baking soda, and salt measured. The chocolate is still in squares—should I chop all 6 of them now?
Yes, chop all 6 unsweetened chocolate squares so they're ready when you need them. Keep the measured dry ingredients nearby too.
The chocolate is chopped. What equipment should I prep for the cake pans?
You'll need 2 round 9 inch pans. Grease them well, then dust them with flour so the cake releases cleanly.
Before I flour the pans, should I turn the oven on?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it can heat while you finish the pan prep.
The oven is heating, and both pans are greased and floured. What should I do with the flour mixture?
Sift together the 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I'm sifting now. Am I looking for it to be totally smooth and combined?
Yes, sift until the flour, baking soda, and salt look evenly mixed and any small lumps are broken up.
The dry ingredients are sifted, the pans are ready, and the oven is still preheating. Anything else for this stage?
That completes the prep listed here. Set the sifted dry mixture aside, and keep the chopped unsweetened chocolate and prepared 2 9 inch pans ready.
Can you coach me through Arroz con Pollo II? I'm starting with a cut-up whole chicken and a large skillet.
Absolutely. Make sure you have 1 whole chicken, about 2 to 3 pounds and cut into pieces, plus 1 tablespoon olive oil for the skillet.
Chicken is ready, and I've measured the oil. What aromatics should I prep before the pan gets hot?
Chop 2 onions and crush 3 cloves garlic. Keep them nearby so they can go into the skillet after the chicken browns.
The onions are chopped and the garlic is crushed. Should I heat the skillet now?
Yes. Put the large skillet over medium-high heat and warm the 1 tablespoon olive oil until it looks hot enough to sauté.
The oil is hot. Do the chicken pieces all go in at once, or should I leave space?
Add the chicken pieces in a way that lets them contact the pan well. Sauté them until they're lightly browned, then lift them out of the skillet and set them aside.
The chicken has some color and is resting on a plate. The pan has browned bits in it.
That's fine; the vegetables will pick up flavor from the pan. Sauté the onion, garlic, and green bell pepper until they're soft.
The onion mixture has softened. What gets stirred in before the chicken returns?
Stir in the tomato sauce, saffron, salt, and bouillon, then put the browned chicken pieces back into the skillet.
Everything is back in the skillet and simmering. How long before the rice goes in?
Cook it for 10 minutes, then add the rice and reduce the heat to low so it can continue gently from there.
Can you walk me through making Avocado Tzatziki? I've got a medium bowl and a fork ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 large avocado, peeled and pitted, plus 2 cloves garlic, minced. You'll also want your lemon ready to juice.
The avocado is prepped, and the garlic is minced. How much lemon and sour cream should I use?
Use the juice from 1 lemon, and if you want it creamier, add 1/4 cup sour cream. The sour cream is optional.
I'm using the sour cream. Do I put everything straight into the bowl?
Yes. Add the avocado, minced garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber to the medium bowl.
They're in the bowl. Should I blend it or just mash it?
Mash it with the fork until the mixture is smooth. Press the avocado against the side of the bowl to help it break down evenly.
It's mostly smooth, with a few tiny bits of avocado left. Is that okay?
That's fine for a rustic texture. If you want it smoother, keep mashing for another minute, then stir so the garlic, lemon, sour cream, and cucumber are evenly mixed.
The texture looks good now. What seasonings go in?
Season it with red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper, then mix well so the herbs and spices are spread throughout.
It tastes bright and a little spicy. How long should it chill before I serve it?
Cover the bowl and refrigerate the Avocado Tzatziki for 1 hour before serving. Give it a quick stir after chilling, then serve it cold.
Can you stay with me while I make Buffalo Chicken Wings I? I'm setting up the fryer and want to get the ingredients straight.
Absolutely. Put out 24 chicken wings and 2 quarts vegetable oil for deep frying, and make sure your large skillet or deep fryer has enough room to cook safely without crowding.
The wings are ready, and I've got the oil. What do I need for the sauce side?
You'll need 4 tablespoons butter, 1 tablespoon distilled white vinegar, hot sauce, plus salt and pepper to season at the end.
I'm using a deep fryer. How long should the wings cook once the oil is ready?
Fry the chicken wings in the hot oil until they're done, about 10 minutes. Work carefully and avoid packing them too tightly so they cook evenly.
They've been frying and look crisp. What should I do before making the sauce?
Lift the chicken out and let it drain. Then remove the oil from the skillet if you're using one, keeping the cooked chicken reserved while you make the sauce.
The wings are draining on a rack, and the pan is clear. Do I start with the butter?
Yes. Melt the butter in the skillet, letting it loosen into a smooth base without browning it.
The butter is melted. When do the vinegar and hot sauce go in?
Stir in the distilled white vinegar and the hot sauce now, mixing until the sauce is even and glossy.
The sauce is together. How should I season and serve the wings?
Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste, then coat the reserved wings with it and serve them while they're hot.
Can you help me make Garlic Butter? My butter is already sitting out on the counter.

Absolutely. You'll want 1 cup butter, softened, plus 1 tablespoon minced garlic, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, and 1 tablespoon garlic salt. Keep Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika nearby for seasoning too.
I've got the butter, garlic, Parmesan, and garlic salt. Should I use a mixing bowl or something smaller?
A small bowl is perfect. Add the softened butter, minced garlic, and grated Parmesan to it so everything is easy to mash together.
The butter is soft but not melted. Is that the texture I want before mixing?
Yes, softened but not melted is ideal. Use a fork or small spatula to press and stir until the garlic and Parmesan are evenly worked through the butter.
It's mostly combined, though I can still see little Parmesan bits. Is that okay?
That's fine. Parmesan won't disappear completely; you just want it distributed throughout the butter so every scoop has some.
I'm ready to season it. Do I add the full garlic salt now?
Yes, mix in the 1 tablespoon garlic salt. Then season with Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika, stirring well after you add them.
After stirring, it looks spreadable and smells pretty strong. Should I keep mixing or stop there?
If the seasonings look evenly blended and there aren't plain streaks of butter left, you can stop. Give the sides of the bowl a quick scrape so everything is incorporated.
How should I serve or store it once it's mixed?
You can use it right away as a spread, or spoon it into a small container and chill it until firm. If you want a neater shape, mound it onto parchment, roll it into a log, and refrigerate it.
I want to make Chai Butter Cookies. Can you guide me without getting too far ahead?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup chai tea mix, 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also want a large mixing bowl ready.
The butter is softened and I've got the chai mix, sugar, and eggs on the counter. Should I start in the big bowl?
Yes. Add the butter, the 1 1/3 cups white sugar, and the chai tea mix to the large bowl. Cream them together until the mixture looks lighter in color and fluffy.
It's starting to look fluffy, but there are still a few streaks of butter. Keep mixing?
Keep going a little longer, scraping the sides of the bowl if needed, until the butter, sugar, and chai mix look evenly combined and soft.
Okay, the mixture looks even now. Do both eggs go in at once?
Add the 2 eggs one at a time. Beat well after the first egg is mixed in, then add the second and mix again until smooth.
The eggs are mixed in. I see the recipe mentions dry ingredients—what should I do with those?
Combine the flour, baking powder, and salt separately, then blend that dry mixture into the creamed mixture. Mix just until all of the dry ingredients have been absorbed.
The dough is coming together, and I don't see dry flour anymore. Should I keep beating it?
No need to keep beating once the dry ingredients are absorbed. Stop there so the dough stays tender.
Got it. What's the last thing before baking later?
Cover the dough and refrigerate it for 1 hour. That chill time will firm it up before you move on.
Can you guide me through making churros? I've got a saucepan out and want to prep everything before I turn on the heat.
Absolutely. Measure out 1 cup water, 2 1/2 tablespoons white sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. You'll also need flour for the dough step, plus oil for frying later.
The water, sugar, salt, and vegetable oil are measured. Should they all go into the saucepan together?
Yes. Put the water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil into the small saucepan, then set it over medium heat.
It's heating now. Am I just warming it, or should I wait for a full boil?
Let it come to a boil. Once it reaches that point, take the saucepan off the heat so the mixture doesn't keep reducing.
It boiled and I moved it off the burner. The pan is still hot—do I add the flour right away?
Yes, stir in the flour while the liquid is hot. Keep stirring until the mixture pulls together and forms a ball.
It's thickening, but there are a few dry spots. Should I keep mixing until it's smooth?
Keep working it with the spoon until those dry patches disappear and the dough gathers into one cohesive ball.
The dough is in a ball now. I'm setting up a deep skillet for frying—what temperature should the oil reach?
Heat the frying oil in a deep-fryer or deep skillet to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C.
I'll watch the thermometer. Any safety note while the oil comes up to 375?
Keep the skillet steady, avoid crowding the area, and have your dough ready before frying. Once the oil is at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), you're set for the frying stage.
Can you guide me through making Dads Best Burgers? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to prep everything before touching the meat.
Absolutely. Start by setting out 1 (3 ounce) package of softened cream cheese and 1 egg. You'll also want your onion and bread crumbs ready before mixing.
The cream cheese is soft and the egg is on the counter. How should I prep the onion?
Finely chop 1 medium onion, then measure 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs. Add those with the cream cheese and egg in the bowl.
All four are in the bowl now. The cream cheese is a little sticky—should I mash it in first?
Yes, mash and stir until the cream cheese starts blending with the egg, onion, and bread crumbs. The mixture does not need to be perfectly smooth, just evenly combined.
That's mixed. I have the beef and sausage nearby, but I don't want to overwork it.
Crumble the beef and sausage over the mixture, then mix gently but thoroughly so the binder and onion are spread through the meat.
It looks evenly mixed. What size should I make the burgers?
Divide the mixture into eight portions and shape them into patties. Try to keep them even in thickness so they grill at the same pace.
The patties are shaped, and the grill is heating. What heat level am I aiming for?
Use medium-hot heat and grill them uncovered. Place the patties on once the grate is hot.
They're on the grill. How long should I cook each side, and what should I look for?
Grill for 4-6 minutes on each side, turning once, until the burgers are no longer pink in the center. Let them rest briefly before serving so they hold together well.
Can you help me make Garden Party Salad? I've got the bowl out but want to keep the dressing from turning lumpy.

Absolutely. Set out the dressing ingredients: 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup orange marmalade, 3 tablespoons cider vinegar, and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise. A small bowl and a whisk will be enough for this part.
The marmalade is pretty thick. Should I add it before or after the oil?
Add the marmalade to the small bowl with the mayonnaise first, then whisk in the cider vinegar to loosen it. Once it starts smoothing out, drizzle in the vegetable oil while whisking.
Okay, I've got the oil, marmalade, vinegar, and mayo in the bowl. What texture am I aiming for?
Whisk until the dressing looks smooth and evenly blended, with no obvious streaks of mayonnaise or clumps of marmalade.
It's smooth now. Does it need to sit, or can I use it right away?
Chill the dressing after whisking. That gives it time to settle and keeps the salad cold and fresh when you toss everything together.
While the dressing chills, should I prep the big bowl with the chicken and add-ins?
Yes. Keep the dressing separate for now, and get a large bowl ready with the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley.
I'm serving this soon. When should the dressing go on so the almonds stay nice?
Add the dressing just before serving. Pour it over the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley, then toss gently so everything is coated without crushing the almonds.
It's tossed and looks coated. Any serving or cleanup tip before I bring it out?
Serve it right away while it's chilled. Scrape the small dressing bowl clean with a spatula, and keep any leftovers covered in the refrigerator.
Can you help me cook Adriennes Tom Ka Gai? I've got a large saucepan out and want to prep before turning on the stove.

Absolutely. Set out 2 teaspoons peanut oil, 2 cloves garlic thinly sliced, 2 tablespoons grated fresh ginger root, and 1/4 cup chopped lemon grass. You'll also want the red pepper, coriander, cumin, chicken, onion, and bok choy ready because the cooking moves in stages.
The garlic is sliced and the ginger is grated. Should the peanut oil go in before the aromatics?
Yes. Put the large saucepan over medium heat, add the 2 teaspoons peanut oil, and let it warm so the garlic, ginger, and lemon grass sizzle gently when they go in.
The oil looks shiny, not smoking. I'm worried about burning the garlic.

That's the right moment to add it. Stir in the sliced garlic, grated ginger, chopped lemon grass, red pepper, coriander, and cumin, then keep everything moving for about 2 minutes, just until it smells fragrant.
It smells strong and citrusy now. The garlic is lightly colored.
Good. Add the chicken and onion to the saucepan, and stir as they cook. You're looking for the chicken to turn white and the onion to become translucent, which should take about 5 minutes.
Some chicken pieces are still pink at the edges after a few minutes. Should I raise the heat?
Keep it around medium and keep stirring so the aromatics don't scorch. Give the chicken and onion the full 5 minutes, or until the chicken is white and the onion has softened to translucent.
Okay, the chicken is white now and the onion looks translucent. I've got the bok choy rinsed.
Stir the bok choy into the saucepan. Let it cook with the mixture until it just begins to wilt; that can take 5 to 10 minutes depending on how thick the pieces are.
The leaves are softening, but the stems still have some crunch. Is that fine for serving?
Yes, that's fine as long as the bok choy has begun to wilt. Once it's tender to your liking within that 5 to 10 minute window, take the pan off the heat and serve the Tom Ka Gai warm.
Can you help me make Crustless Spinach Quiche? I'm getting my counter set up now.
Absolutely. Pull out 1 tablespoon vegetable oil and 1 onion, chopped. You'll also want a large skillet and a 9 inch pie pan ready.
The onion is chopped, and I found the pie pan. What should I grab from the freezer?
You need 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach. Make sure it's thawed and well drained so the quiche doesn't turn watery.
Spinach is thawed, but it still feels pretty wet. Should I squeeze it out?
Yes, squeeze or press out as much liquid as you can. After that, beat 5 eggs in a bowl so they're ready when the filling comes together.
Eggs are beaten. Should the oven be on already?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so it's hot by the time the pan is ready.
Oven is heating. Do I need to line the pie pan or just grease it?
No lining needed for this version. Lightly grease the 9 inch pie pan, coating the bottom and sides so the crustless quiche releases cleanly.
The pan is greased. I'm moving to the stove—what heat should I use for the onion?
Set a large skillet over medium-high heat and add the 1 tablespoon vegetable oil. Let the oil warm briefly before the onion goes in.
The oil is shimmering a little. How should the onions look before I stop cooking them?
Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are soft. They should look more translucent and lose their raw bite.
Can you guide me through Dziriat Algerian Almond Tarts? I've got almonds out, but I want to make sure I don't miss the syrup ingredients.
Absolutely. For the syrup, set out 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup water, plus 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice and 2 tablespoons orange flower water.
I've measured the sugar and water. Should the lemon juice and orange flower water be measured before I start boiling anything?
Yes, measure them now so they're ready when you need them: 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice and 2 tablespoons orange flower water.
Done. For the almonds, what pot setup should I use?
Use a pot large enough to hold the almonds comfortably, then bring 6 cups of water to a boil.
The water is boiling. Do I keep the heat on when the almonds go in?
Take the pot off the heat first, then add the almonds to the hot water.
They're in the hot water now. How long should they sit before peeling?
Let the almonds soak for about 5 minutes, then drain them. Once they're cool enough to handle, slip off the skins.
The skins are coming off pretty easily. What should I do with the peeled almonds so they don't stay wet?
Spread the peeled almonds out on baking sheets in a single layer so moisture can evaporate evenly.
What oven temperature am I aiming for, and how dry should they get?
Bake them at 200 degrees F, or 95 degrees C, until the almonds are completely dry and toasted.
I want to make Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea. Can you help me set up before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Use a large pot and gather 1 pound of fresh or frozen cranberries with 3 quarts of cold water. Those go in the pot together to start the tea base.
The cranberries are frozen. Do I need to thaw them before they go into the water?
No thawing needed. Put the frozen cranberries straight into the large pot with the cold water, then bring everything up together.
What juices should I have ready while that heats?
Measure out 2 cups of orange juice and 2 1/8 cups of pineapple juice. You'll stir those in later, after the cranberry liquid has cooled and been strained.
The pot is on the stove now. How hard should it boil, and what am I watching for?
Bring it to a boil, then cook just until the cranberries pop. That usually takes about 5 minutes once it's boiling, so watch for the skins splitting rather than trying to reduce the liquid.
Most of the berries have popped and the liquid is deep red. Should I keep simmering it for more flavor?
Go ahead and remove it from the heat now. The recipe stops the cooking once the berries pop, then has the mixture stand at room temperature until cold, which takes several hours.
I need the pot off my active burner. Can it just sit on a trivet while it cools?
Yes, set the pot on a trivet or another heat-safe spot and let it stand at room temperature until the cranberry liquid is cold. Keep it covered loosely if you want to protect it while it cools.
It's cold now, and there are lots of cranberry skins and pulp. What's the cleanest way to finish it?

Strain out the cranberries, then stir the orange juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice, and sugar into the strained liquid. Once the sugar is dissolved, the Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea is ready to serve or chill.
I want to make Chocolate Madeleines. Can you guide me without rushing? I've got my mixing bowls out.
Absolutely. Start by setting out the dry ingredients: 1/4 cup sifted all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, and 1 pinch salt.
The flour is already sifted, and I measured the cocoa. Should I turn on the oven before mixing?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it's ready when the batter is prepared.
Oven is heating. I have a madeleine pan, but I'm worried the cakes might stick.
Butter one Madeleine pan thoroughly, getting into each shell-shaped groove so the madeleines release cleanly after baking.
The pan is buttered. For the dry mix, do I just whisk everything together?
Use a sifter if you can: sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt together. That keeps the cocoa from clumping and helps the batter stay light.
I sifted it once, but I still see a couple little cocoa dots. Is that a problem?
A few tiny specks are fine, but if there are larger lumps, press them through the sifter or break them up before adding the dry mixture to the batter.
What should I do with the butter mixture? The recipe mentions vanilla and sugar.

Cream the butter with the vanilla and the sugar until the mixture looks smooth and lighter in texture. The recipe you're using doesn't list those amounts here, so use the quantities from your full copy if you have them.
It's starting to look fluffy. Should I keep beating or stop soon?
Stop once the butter, vanilla, and sugar are evenly creamed and slightly fluffy. Then you'll be ready to combine it with the sifted chocolate dry mixture according to the next part of your recipe.
Can you help me make Bacon Wrapped Hamburgers? I'm setting up at the grill and want to do the prep in the right order.
Absolutely. Get the grill heating on high so it's ready when the patties are shaped.
The grill is heating. I've got a mixing bowl out—what should I put in before the beef?
Add 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese, 1 small chopped onion, and 1 egg to the bowl.
Those are in. The bowl looks a little dry—are there sauces or seasonings that go in now too?
Yes. Mix in the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper with the cheese, onion, and egg until everything is evenly combined.
Okay, the mixture is blended. Should the ground beef go in all at once?
Crumble the ground beef into the bowl, then mix it together by hand. Try to combine it evenly without packing it too tightly.
It's mixed. I want them all about the same size—how many patties am I shaping?
Shape the mixture into 6 patties, keeping them as even as you can so they cook at the same pace.
The patties are formed. What's the best way to add the bacon so it stays put?
Wrap a slice of bacon around each patty. Press it gently against the burger so it sits snugly before it goes on the hot grill.
All 6 are wrapped and the grill is hot. Anything to check before I start cooking them?
Make sure the patties are holding together and the bacon is secure. Since the grill is on high heat, place them carefully and keep an eye on flare-ups from the bacon fat.
Can you help me make Candy Coated Milk Chocolate Pieces Cookies I? I'm setting things out on the counter now.
Absolutely. Start by getting the oven ready: preheat it to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). While it heats, pull out a mixing bowl and your measured ingredients.
The oven is heating. I've got shortening and brown sugar nearby—how much of each should I measure?
Measure 1 cup shortening and 1 cup packed brown sugar. Pack the brown sugar firmly into the cup so the amount is right.
Done. I also see white sugar and eggs in the recipe—what amounts go in?
Add 1/2 cup white sugar and 2 eggs to your prep area. Those will be creamed together with the shortening, brown sugar, and vanilla.
Should I cream everything by hand, or is a mixer better for this part?
A mixer will make it easier, but a sturdy spoon works too. Thoroughly cream together the shortening, both sugars, the eggs, and the vanilla until the mixture looks smooth and well combined.
The creamed mixture looks even now. I have another bowl ready—what goes in there?
Use that separate bowl for the dry ingredients. Mix the dry ingredients together there, but leave out the candies for now.
So the candy pieces stay out until later, right? I don't want to crush them while mixing.
Right, keep the candies out of the dry bowl at this stage. Just combine the dry ingredients evenly so they'll blend into the creamed mixture without pockets of floury bits.
The dry ingredients are mixed. Do I pour them all into the creamed mixture at once?
Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture and mix well, scraping the bowl as needed so everything comes together evenly before you move on to adding the candies or shaping the cookies.

Before I heat the pan, can you help me set up the vegetables so I'm not scrambling?

Set out 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, 2 cups diced Broccoflower, 2 cups chopped assorted wild mushrooms, and 1/2 chopped white onion. If your garlic is not already prepped, have it ready too, since it goes into the sauté.
The Broccoflower is diced and the mushrooms are chopped. Should the onion go in with them right away?
Yes. Melt the butter in your pan, then add the Broccoflower, wild mushrooms, onion, and garlic together. Sauté them for 10 minutes, stirring so the mushrooms cook down and the onion softens.
Good, that's the way I like it—small herbs throughout instead of big leafy bits sitting on the surface.
Then we'll keep that approach as you finish: the herbs will be worked through the risotto near the end, with only a light fresh scatter if you want it.
The vegetables smell good and there's some moisture in the pan. Do I leave them there while the rice cooks?
No, scoop the sautéed Broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic out of the pan and set them aside. Keep the same pan for the rice so you hold onto the flavor left behind.
Vegetables are in a bowl. How do I manage the chicken stock without making the rice soupy?
Add the chicken stock 1 cup at a time to the rice in that same pan. Stir until each cup is well incorporated and mostly absorbed before adding the next cup.
The rice is taking it in slowly. What texture am I watching for before the vegetables go back?
Look for tender rice with a creamy, loose texture, not dry and not flooded with stock. Once the chicken stock has been absorbed and the rice is tender, stir the sautéed vegetables back in.
I'm at that creamy stage now. How should I finish and serve it?

Stir in the nutmeg, the finely chopped herbs, salt, and pepper so the seasoning runs through the risotto. Taste, adjust the salt and pepper, then serve while it's creamy, adding just a small fresh herb sprinkle if you want a little lift.
Can you help me make Caramel Shortbread Squares? I've got a 9 inch square pan out, but I want to make sure I'm starting with the right ingredients.

Absolutely. For the shortbread mixture, you'll need 2/3 cup butter, softened, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour. The recipe also lists 1/2 cup butter, so have that measured and ready too.
The softened butter, sugar, flour, and the extra 1/2 cup butter are on the counter. Should I heat the oven before mixing?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 176 degrees C, so it's ready when the base is pressed into the pan.
Oven is heating. For the bowl, am I creaming the butter and sugar first or putting everything in together?
Put the 2/3 cup softened butter, 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1 1/4 cups flour into a medium bowl together. Mix until the texture is evenly crumbly rather than smooth like cake batter.
It's looking sandy and crumbly, with no big streaks of flour. Is that about right?
That sounds right. Tip the crumbly mixture into your 9 inch square baking pan and press it into an even layer, getting it into the corners without packing it down too aggressively.
The layer is in the pan, but my fingers are sticking a bit. Any quick fix before it goes in?
You can use the bottom of a measuring cup or a piece of parchment to smooth and press the surface evenly. Keep the thickness as consistent as you can across the pan.
Okay, it's flattened and the oven says it's at 350. How long does this bake?
Bake it for 20 minutes. Place the pan on the middle rack and try not to move it around while the shortbread sets.
After 20 minutes, what should I do with the pan?
Take it out carefully and set the pan on a rack or heatproof surface. Let the shortbread base cool in the 9 inch pan before cutting or adding anything else, so the squares hold together cleanly.
Can you help me make Garden Party Salad? I've got the bowl out but want to make sure I start with the dressing correctly.
Absolutely. For the dressing, set out 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup orange marmalade, 3 tablespoons cider vinegar, and 3 tablespoons mayonnaise. A small bowl and a whisk are perfect here.
The marmalade is a little thick. Should I loosen it before mixing it with the oil and vinegar?

You can add it straight to the bowl; the whisking will smooth it out. Put the marmalade in with the vegetable oil, cider vinegar, and mayonnaise, then whisk until the dressing looks smooth and blended.
Okay, it's combined, but I can still see tiny orange bits from the marmalade. Is that fine?
Yes, that's normal for orange marmalade. As long as the dressing is smooth overall and the mayonnaise is fully incorporated, those small orange pieces are fine. Cover the bowl and chill the dressing.
How long should it chill while I prep the rest?
Chill it while you get the salad components ready. Since the recipe adds the dressing just before serving, keeping it cold now will help it stay fresh and coat everything nicely later.
I'm putting together the big bowl now. What goes in before the dressing?
In the large bowl, combine the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley. Keep the dressing separate until you're close to serving.
Should I toss those dry ingredients first, or wait until the dressing is added?
Give the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley a light toss first so they're evenly distributed. Then, just before serving, pour in the chilled dressing and toss again to coat.
The salad is dressed now. Any serving advice so it doesn't get soggy?
Serve it right away after tossing. If you need a few minutes, keep it chilled and give it one gentle toss before bringing it to the table.
Can you guide me through making Cinnamon Chocolate Cake 2? I've got a mixing bowl out and want to make sure I measure the dry ingredients correctly.
Absolutely. Start by measuring the dry base into the mixing bowl: 2 cups all-purpose flour and 2 cups sugar.
Those are in the bowl. I also see cinnamon and salt listed—how much of each goes in before I stir?
Add 1 1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon salt to the same bowl. Once they're in, whisk or stir the first four ingredients together so the cinnamon and salt are evenly distributed.
The dry mixture looks even now. What pan or stovetop step should I set up next?
Put a saucepan on the stove and combine the water, oil, butter, and cocoa in it. Heat that mixture over medium heat until it comes to a boil.
Should I keep stirring while it heats, or just let it sit until it boils?
Give it occasional stirring so the butter melts in smoothly and the cocoa blends with the liquid. Once it reaches a boil over medium heat, take it to the dry ingredients.
It's boiling and the cocoa mixture looks smooth. Do I pour it in all at once?
Yes, pour the hot cocoa mixture over the dry ingredients in the mixing bowl, then mix well until the batter looks combined and there aren't dry pockets.
The batter is mixed, but it's still warm from the saucepan. Is that okay before adding the rest?
That's fine for this recipe. Add the eggs, buttermilk, vanilla, and baking soda, then mix well again so everything is fully incorporated.
After adding those, what texture am I looking for before I stop mixing?

Stop once the batter is smooth and uniform, with the baking soda and wet ingredients fully blended in. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl once to catch any streaks, then it's ready for the next baking step.

Have the flour ready too: 1 cup sifted all-purpose flour. You'll beat it in after the butter and cream cheese are fully creamed together.

Look for a uniform, creamy mixture with no obvious streaks of butter or cream cheese. Once it's smooth, beat in the sifted flour until it forms a dough.

No real kneading is needed here. Shape the dough into a smooth ball, keeping it compact and even.

At baking time, take the dough out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before using it. That gives it time to become workable before you shape and fill the empanadas with the fruit preserves.

Broth and rice are in. I also chopped the stems pretty fine; where should the seasonings go?
Stir the chopped stems into that base now, along with 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder. Try to distribute everything across the dish so the rice cooks evenly.

I added the broccoli, Parmesan, and half the onions. Should I stir them in or leave them on top?
Lightly nestle them into the rice so they are in contact with the hot broth, but do not mash everything flat. Keep the surface fairly even for the fish fillets.

Lay the fish fillets on top of the rice mixture, then sprinkle them with paprika. Return the dish to the oven and bake until the fish is cooked through and the rice is tender, then serve it from the baking dish.

I want to make Cookie Jar Gingersnaps. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Set out a large mixing bowl and gather 3/4 cup shortening and 1 cup sugar to start the dough base.
The bowl is ready, and I measured the shortening and sugar. What should I pull from the pantry next?
You'll also need 1 egg and 1/4 cup molasses. Keep the molasses nearby since it goes in right after the egg.
Got them. Should the shortening and sugar be mixed by hand or beaten until fluffy?
Cream the shortening and sugar together in the large mixing bowl until they look smooth and well blended.
It's coming together and looks creamy. Do I add the wet ingredients all at once?
Yes. Beat in the egg and the 1/4 cup molasses until the mixture is evenly combined.
The dough base is darker now from the molasses. What dry ingredients should I combine separately?
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. The recipe doesn't list amounts for those here, so use the amounts from your full recipe card if you have it.
I have those measured from the card. How do I add them without making the dough tough?
Gradually add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture, mixing just until the flour streaks disappear and the dough holds together.
The dough is mixed. What size should I make each cookie before baking?
Roll teaspoonfuls of dough into balls, keeping them fairly even so the gingersnaps bake consistently.
I want to make Avocado Tzatziki. Can you guide me while I prep it?
Absolutely. Set out a medium bowl and a fork. For the base, you'll need 1 large avocado, peeled and pitted, plus 2 cloves garlic, minced.
The avocado is ready, and I've minced the garlic. What should I pull from the fridge next?
Grab 1 lemon for juicing and 1/4 cup sour cream if you want the creamier version. The recipe also has cucumber going into the bowl with the avocado mixture.
I'll use the sour cream. Should I add everything to the bowl at once?
Yes. Put the avocado, minced garlic, lemon juice, sour cream, and cucumber into the medium bowl together.
They're in the bowl. Do I need a blender, or is the fork enough?
A fork is enough here. Mash the mixture until it's smooth, pressing the avocado into the lemon juice and sour cream as you go.
It's mostly smooth, with a few tiny avocado bits. Is that okay?
That's fine for tzatziki-style texture. Once it's as smooth as you like, stir in red pepper flakes, cilantro, mint, salt, and pepper, then mix well so the seasoning is evenly distributed.
I added the herbs and seasonings. Should I taste it before chilling?

messages.content: I'm making apple butter spice cake and want to stay organized. What should I pull out before I start?

Set out the topping ingredients first: 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. You'll also want your baking pan ready since this goes into a 9x13 inch pan.
I've got the sugar, spices, pecans, and the 9x13 pan. Should I heat the oven now or wait?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. While it heats, spray or grease the 9x13 inch pan so the cake is ready to pour in later.
The pan is greased. Do I make the pecan mixture right away?
Yes. In a bowl, mix together the packed brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and chopped pecans until the spices are evenly distributed through the sugar and nuts.
That topping smells good. What bowl should I work on next?
Use a separate bowl for the dry ingredients. Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt so they're evenly combined before they go into the batter.
The dry mix is sifted. I'm ready for the batter, but I don't want to overmix it.
Start by blending the butter and sugar together until they're combined and creamy. Add the eggs and beat well before adding the next ingredients.
The eggs are beaten in. When do the apple butter and vanilla go in?
Add the apple butter and vanilla now, along with the wheat germ or bran cereal. Mix until the batter looks even, scraping the bowl as needed.
It's mixed and a little thick. How do I bring in the dry ingredients and sour cream?

Add the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the sour cream, mixing well after each addition. Keep the additions gradual so the batter stays smooth and evenly blended before you spread it into the prepared pan.
I'm making Biga and want to stay organized. What should I put on the counter before I start?

Set out 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast, 1/2 cup warm water, 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour, and 1 1/4 cups cold water. You'll also want a small bowl for blooming the yeast and a large bowl for the flour.
I've got the yeast and both waters measured. Should the warm water go straight into the small bowl?
Yes. Pour the 1/2 cup warm water into the small bowl, then sprinkle the 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast over the top so it can hydrate evenly.
The yeast is sprinkled over the water. Do I stir it or leave it alone?
Leave it to stand until the yeast has dissolved and the surface looks foamy, about 15 minutes.
While I wait those 15 minutes, can I prep the flour bowl?
Definitely. Measure 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into a large bowl so it's ready when the yeast mixture is foamy.
The flour is in the large bowl. Should I flatten it out or shape it somehow?
Make a well in the center of the flour. It should be deep enough to hold the yeast mixture and the 1 1/4 cups cold water without immediately spilling over the sides.
The yeast is foamy now, and the well is ready. What gets poured in?
Pour the dissolved, foamy yeast mixture into the well, then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water to the same center area.
Everything is in the flour well. Is that the end of the listed prep for this Biga?

Yes, that completes the listed steps: warm water and yeast bloomed until foamy, 3 1/2 cups flour measured into a large bowl, a well made in the center, and the yeast mixture plus cold water poured in.
I want to make Black Forest Dump Cake II. Can you help me set up before I start opening cans?

Absolutely. Pull out a 9x13 baking dish, cooking spray, 1 (21 ounce) can of cherry pie filling, 1 (16.5 ounce) can of pitted dark sweet cherries, 1 (18.25 ounce) package of chocolate cake mix, and 1 cup chopped walnuts.
I've got the baking dish and the two cherry cans. Do the dark sweet cherries get drained?
Keep the juice with the pitted dark sweet cherries. This recipe uses the cherries including their juice, so set the whole can aside ready to pour.
Good to know. I also have the chocolate cake mix and walnuts on the counter. Should I heat the oven now?
Yes, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F, which is 190 degrees C, so it can come up to temperature while you assemble the dump cake.
The oven is heating. What should I do to the 9x13 dish so the fruit doesn't stick?
Spray the 9x13 baking dish evenly with cooking spray, making sure you hit the corners and sides as well as the bottom.
The dish is sprayed. Which cherry layer goes in first?
Pour in the 1 (21 ounce) can of cherry pie filling first, then spread it evenly across the bottom of the dish.
The pie filling is spread out. The dark cherries look pretty juicy—do I pour all of that over the top?
Yes. Add the 1 (16.5 ounce) can of pitted dark sweet cherries over the pie filling, including the juice, and distribute the cherries so the layer is fairly even.
The fruit layer is in the pan. Am I ready for the cake mix and the 1 cup of chopped walnuts next?

You've completed the listed prep steps through the cherry layers. The remaining gathered items are the 1 (18.25 ounce) package chocolate cake mix and 1 cup chopped walnuts, so keep them ready for the next part of the cake assembly.

Measure 1/2 cup marshmallow creme and have it ready with the cream cheese.

Yes, use 2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, so it folds in evenly instead of leaving icy or firm spots.

Keep 1/4 cup unsweetened pineapple juice nearby; you'll add only enough to loosen the dip to a good dipping consistency.

Blend the softened cream cheese with the marshmallow creme, then mix in the thawed whipped topping until the dip looks smooth and fluffy.

Add the pineapple juice gradually, stopping when the dip is loose enough for fruit or dippers to scoop without running.
Texture looks right now. How long should it chill before I put the platter out?
Cover the bowl and chill the dip for 1 hour, then serve it with the platter and keep those briny clusters separated along the edge.
I'm making Dads Kickin Jamaican Wings Mon and want to get set up before the wings come out. What should I put on the counter?
Set out 3 tablespoons Jamaican jerk seasoning blend, 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, 3 cloves diced garlic, and 1 peeled fresh ginger piece about 1 inch long, diced.
I've got the seasoning and oil measured. The garlic is diced, and I'm peeling the ginger now. Do I need any equipment ready?
Yes—have a blender ready for the marinade, plus baking sheets for the wings. You'll also need aluminum foil for covering them while they chill.
The blender is ready. What goes in it besides the seasoning, oil, garlic, and ginger?
Add the green onions and jalapeno slices to the blender too, along with the jerk seasoning, vegetable oil, diced garlic, and diced ginger.
How smooth should I make that mixture? I don't want it too thin.
Blend it until it looks thick and smooth. It should be cohesive enough to coat the wings rather than run off like a watery sauce.
The marinade is thick now. Should I pour it over the wings or handle them another way?
Dunk the wings directly in the mixture so they're well coated, then arrange them in a single layer on the baking sheets.
They're coated and spread out on the sheets. Do I bake them right away?
Not yet. Cover the baking sheets with aluminum foil and refrigerate the wings for 8 hours, or overnight, so the flavor can settle in.
They've been chilling overnight. What temperature should I set before cooking?
Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F, which is 150 degrees C. Once it reaches temperature, you'll be ready for the next baking step.
I want to make Chicken Tacos tonight. Can you stay with me while I prep and cook them?
Absolutely. Start by cutting 1 pound of skinless, boneless chicken breast halves into bite-size pieces, then set a large skillet on the stove so it's ready.
The chicken is cut up. I also have lemonade in the fridge—how much goes in?
Measure out 1 cup lemonade. You'll also need 2 tablespoons olive oil and 1 tablespoon lime juice nearby before the pan goes on the heat.
Got it. Should the skillet be hot before I add everything, or do I combine it cold?
Put the skillet over medium heat, then combine the chicken, lemonade, olive oil, lime juice, and Worcestershire sauce right in the pan.
Everything is in the skillet and starting to warm. What seasonings should I add?
Season the mixture with garlic powder, onion powder, and a bay leaf. Stir so the chicken pieces are coated and sitting in the liquid.
It smells good. Should I cover it while it cooks?
You can let it simmer uncovered and stir occasionally. Cook until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, which should take 15 to 20 minutes.
While that simmers, I need to get the tortillas ready. What's the easiest way?
Warm the tortillas until soft, either in the oven or in the microwave. Do that near the end of the chicken's simmering time so they stay pliable.
The chicken looks cooked through and the tortillas are soft. Anything I should check before serving?
Check that the chicken pieces are fully opaque with clear juices, then remove the bay leaf. Spoon the warm chicken into the softened tortillas and serve the tacos right away.
I want to make Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms tonight. Can you talk me through what to prep before the pan goes on?
Absolutely. Dice 2 cups of broccoflower, chop 2 cups of assorted wild mushrooms, and chop 1/2 white onion. Have 1 tablespoon unsalted butter ready by the stove too.
The broccoflower is diced and the mushrooms are chopped. Should the onion go in with them right away?
Yes. Once the pan is warm, melt the butter, then add the broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic together. Sauté them for 10 minutes, stirring so the vegetables soften evenly without sticking.
I've got a wide sauté pan out. Is that okay for starting the risotto too?

That works well. After the vegetables have sautéed for 10 minutes, lift them out of the pan and set them aside on a plate or in a bowl. Keep the same pan for the rice so you hold onto the flavor left behind.
The vegetables are out of the pan, and there are browned bits on the bottom. Do I scrape those up now?
Yes, as you start cooking the rice, the chicken stock will help loosen those bits. Add the stock 1 cup at a time, stirring until each cup is well incorporated before adding the next.
How will I know when it's time to pour in another cup of stock?

When the pan looks mostly absorbed rather than soupy, and the spoon leaves a brief trail through the rice, add the next cup of chicken stock. Keep stirring so the rice releases starch and turns creamy.
The rice is getting creamy but still has a little bite. Should I put the mushrooms and broccoflower back in yet?
Wait until the chicken stock is absorbed and the rice is tender. Then stir the sautéed broccoflower, mushrooms, onion, and garlic back in so everything heats together.
It's tender now and the vegetables are back in. What should I add at the end?
Stir in the nutmeg and herbs, then season with salt and pepper. Taste once more for balance, and serve the Broccoflower Risotto with Wild Mushrooms while it's creamy and hot.
