original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Arroz con Pollo II as a packed lunch with optional cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions. How should I handle the soft herbs?

messages.content: I'm cooking Arroz con Pollo II to take as lunch today, and I'll have cilantro, parsley, basil, mint, or scallions on the side. What's the best way to deal with those tender herbs so they don't wilt?
Keep the tender herbs separate in a small container, then scatter them over the arroz con pollo after you open the lunch.
Perfect—that's the version I want for this lunch. Before I turn on the stove, what should I prep first?
Get the 1 whole chicken, about 2 to 3 pounds and cut into pieces, ready near the stove. Also measure out 1 tablespoon olive oil for the skillet.
Chicken is patted dry and the oil is measured. I've got a cutting board free—what vegetables should I handle now?
Chop 2 onions and crush 3 cloves of garlic. Keep them together since they'll go into the skillet after the chicken comes out.
The onions are chopped, and the garlic is crushed. Should the skillet be hot before the chicken goes in?
Yes. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium high heat until it looks glossy, then you're ready for the chicken.
The oil is shimmering. Do I cook all the chicken now, and what texture am I looking for?
Sauté the chicken pieces until they're lightly browned on the outside. Once they have that color, lift them out of the skillet and set them aside.
The chicken is browned and resting on a plate. There are browned bits in the pan—do I leave them there?
Leave them; they'll add flavor. Add the onion, garlic, and green bell pepper to the skillet and sauté until the vegetables are soft.
The vegetables have softened. I have tomato sauce, saffron, salt, and bouillon lined up—do those go in before the rice?
Stir in the tomato sauce, saffron, salt, and bouillon, then return the chicken pieces to the skillet so they can simmer in that mixture.
The chicken is back in the skillet and the sauce is bubbling gently. How long before I add the rice and lower the heat?
Cook it for 10 minutes, then add the rice and reduce the heat to low. When you pack it, keep those soft herbs separate and add them at lunch.
I want to make Chunky Pizza Dip—can you walk me through it while I get set up?

Absolutely. Put a large saucepan or Dutch oven on the stove, and gather 2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 minced garlic cloves, 2 (14.5 ounce) cans petite diced tomatoes, and 1/4 cup tomato paste. You'll also need basil and oregano for the sauce.
I've got the Dutch oven out. Should the tomatoes be drained before they go in?
Keep the petite diced tomatoes as they are unless your cans are unusually watery; the liquid helps the dip simmer into a sauce. Start by adding the olive oil and minced garlic to the pan.
Oil and garlic are in the pan. How hot should I take it?
Warm them together over moderate heat and watch closely. You're looking for the garlic to start sizzling and just turn golden, not brown.
The garlic is sizzling now and getting a little golden around the edges.
Good timing. Stir in both cans of petite diced tomatoes, the 1/4 cup tomato paste, plus the basil and oregano. Mix well so the tomato paste loosens into the tomatoes, then bring it to a simmer.
The paste is mixed in, but the sauce looks pretty loose. Is that normal?
Yes, it will thicken as it cooks. Once it's simmering, leave it uncovered so moisture can cook off and the dip becomes thick enough for scooping.
It's bubbling steadily uncovered. How long should I let it go?
Simmer it for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick. It's ready when it looks chunky and thick enough for dipping rather than pouring.
It has thickened up after about 20 minutes. What do I do before serving or storing it?
Take it off the heat and let it cool. If you're not serving it right away, refrigerate it once cooled; if serving now, give it a quick stir and spoon it into a dip bowl.
I want to make Caramelized Apple Bites. Can you talk me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Set out 6 individually wrapped caramels, unwrap them, and chop them into smaller pieces so they melt more evenly.
Caramels are unwrapped and chopped. What goes with them in the bowl?
Add 2 tablespoons of light corn syrup to a medium microwave-safe bowl with the chopped caramels.
I have a glass microwave-safe bowl ready. Do the apples go in before heating?
Not yet. Keep the apples aside while you melt the caramel mixture. You'll need 2 apples, peeled, cored, and diced.
The apples are diced now. How long should I microwave the caramel and syrup?
Microwave the bowl on high for approximately 30 seconds, just until the caramels are melted with the light corn syrup.
If it looks thick after heating, should I stir it before adding fruit?
Yes, give the melted caramel and corn syrup a quick stir so the coating is smooth before the apples go in.
The mixture is smooth and glossy. Do I dump all the diced apple in?
Yes. Place the diced apples in the bowl and toss them until they're coated with the caramel and light corn syrup mixture.
They're coated, but still warm. Can I serve them right away?
Let them cool before serving so the caramel coating can settle a bit and the bites are easier to eat.
I want to make Eggnog II. Can you stay with me while I get set up at the stove?

Absolutely. Set out a large saucepan, a spoon for constant stirring, and a metal spoon for checking thickness. For the ingredients, you'll need 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The eggs are beaten and I've measured the milk. Should the sugar go in before the pan is hot?
Yes. Put the beaten eggs, the 2 1/4 cups milk, and the 1/3 cup white sugar into the large saucepan while it's still off the heat, then stir them together so the sugar starts dissolving evenly.
It's mixed in the saucepan. I also have the vanilla measured, but I don't see where it comes in.

Good to have it measured. The listed cooking steps focus on combining the eggs, milk, and sugar, then cooking and cooling the mixture; they don't specify the exact moment for the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, so keep it nearby without adding it during the heating step unless you're choosing to fold it in after cooking.
Okay, the pan is on the burner now. How hot should I keep it, and what am I watching for?
Use medium heat and stir steadily. Keep the spoon moving across the bottom and around the edges so the egg mixture heats evenly and doesn't scramble.
It's getting warmer and a little smoother. How do I know when it coats the spoon enough?

Dip the metal spoon into the mixture and lift it out. You're looking for a thin coating that clings to the spoon instead of running off immediately. Once it coats the metal spoon, take the saucepan off the heat.
It coats the spoon now. I've moved it off the burner—what should I do so it cools quickly?
Set the saucepan into a sink or bowl filled with ice water. Stir the eggnog mixture while it sits there so the heat drops fast.
How long should I keep stirring in the ice water, and should the pan stay submerged?
Keep the pan sitting in the ice water and stir for 1 to 2 minutes. Don't let water splash into the eggnog; just use the ice bath to cool the pan quickly.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Add a small spoonful of the briny liquid to the warm skillet, but keep the pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces themselves out of the dip.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: Tonight I'm doing Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip in a warm skillet and want the tang from pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini just for this batch. What's the best way to work that in?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use a spoonful of brine in the warm pan and leave the solid briny pieces out.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip as a warm skillet version with pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini. How should I handle the briny ingredient?

messages.content: Tonight I'm doing Garlic Crab Artichoke Dip in a warm skillet and want the tang from pickles, capers, olives, or pepperoncini just for this batch. What's the best way to work that in?
Add a small spoonful of the briny liquid to the warm skillet, but keep the pickle, caper, olive, or pepperoncini pieces themselves out of the dip.
Perfect, that's exactly the version I'm making right now. Before the skillet gets warm, what should I measure first?
Measure 1 cup mayonnaise and 8 ounces sour cream. Keep them close by so they can blend smoothly once you start mixing the dip base.
I've got those measured. Which pantry items and artichokes should I open?
Open 1 (1 ounce) package garlic and mushroom soup mix, then drain and chop 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts.
The artichokes are chopped, and I have the soup mix ready. Do I still need the oven if I'm warming it in a skillet?
Yes, heat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) so the dip can finish hot and bubbly after the skillet-style start.
Oven is heating. How do I build the mixture without making the sour cream separate?
Keep the heat gentle. Stir the mayonnaise and sour cream together first, then mix in the garlic and mushroom soup mix until the base looks even.
The base looks smooth. Where does the brine come in, and when should I add the artichokes?
Stir the spoonful of brine into the warm base now, then fold in the chopped artichoke hearts. After that, add the cheese and crab meat and mix just until everything is evenly distributed.
It's all combined. What dish should I use if I want it to bake like the original?
Transfer the mixture into a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish, spreading it into an even layer so it heats through consistently.
The casserole dish is filled. How long should it stay in the oven, and should I cover it?
Bake it uncovered for 30 minutes, then serve it immediately while it's warm and creamy.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this version, mince just the softest, thinnest stems into the dressing, and hold the leaves aside so they stay fresh.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this Baked Salmon with Herbs, I'm doing a one-off raw topping, almost like a salsa, and I've got cilantro or parsley stems in the mix. What should I do with the stems this time?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Dice only the most tender stems into the dressing and keep the leaves separate.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Baked Salmon with Herbs as a raw salad, salsa, or uncooked topping with cilantro or parsley stems. How should I handle the stems?

messages.content: For this Baked Salmon with Herbs, I'm doing a one-off raw topping, almost like a salsa, and I've got cilantro or parsley stems in the mix. What should I do with the stems this time?
For this version, mince just the softest, thinnest stems into the dressing, and hold the leaves aside so they stay fresh.
Perfect, that's the direction I want for this salmon tonight. I'm at the counter with a cutting board and bowl—what should I measure first?
Measure 2 1/2 cups soft bread crumbs into the bowl, then mince 4 garlic cloves so they're ready to mix in.
The crumbs are in, and the garlic is minced. I'm trying not to clutter the counter—what are the next measured items?
Add 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese and 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes to your setup.
Those are out. Before I mix, should I prep the pan or leave that until the topping is together?
Go ahead and set up the pan now: line a 15-in baking pan with foil, then coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray.
Foil is sprayed. My bowl has the crumbs, garlic, Parmesan, and dried parsley flakes nearby—what goes into the bowl together?
Combine the bread crumbs, garlic, Parmesan cheese, parsley, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper in the bowl.
I've mixed the dry ingredients. The texture is still loose and sandy—what binds it?
Add the butter and toss everything until the crumbs are evenly coated.
The crumb mixture looks evenly moistened now. Where does the salmon come in?
Place the salmon on the prepared foil-lined pan.
Salmon is on the pan. Should I scatter the herb mixture evenly or keep it piled in the center?
Spread it evenly over the salmon so the garlic, herbs, Parmesan, and crumbs are distributed across the surface.
I want to make Cabin Hash tonight. Can you help me get organized before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Set out 12 medium potatoes, already peeled, cooked, and cubed, plus 3 cups of cubed fully cooked ham. You'll also need 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 cup butter or margarine.
I've got the potatoes cubed and the ham measured. Should I use a big pan for this?
Yes, use a large skillet so the potatoes have enough room to brown instead of just steaming. Have the onion and butter nearby before you start.
The skillet is ready. Do I melt all the butter first?
Melt the 1/2 cup butter or margarine in the skillet, then add the potatoes, ham, and chopped onion together.
Everything is in the pan. How active do I need to be with stirring?
Stir frequently, scraping across the bottom of the skillet so the onion cooks evenly and the potatoes pick up light browning without sticking.
The potatoes are starting to get golden on the edges. Is that the texture I'm looking for?
Yes, lightly browned potatoes are the goal. Once they look lightly golden in spots and the ham is hot, you're ready for the next addition.
I noticed the directions mention broccoli. When should that go in?
Add the broccoli after the potato, ham, and onion mixture has browned. Stir it in and heat it through in the same skillet.
The broccoli is hot now. What should I do right before serving?
Season the hash with salt and pepper to taste, then serve it hot. Offer sour cream on the side if you'd like.
I want to make Beet and Pear Puree today. Can you help me get organized before I turn anything on?
Absolutely. Set out 8 medium beets, 1 pound unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions, and 4 Bosc pears that are peeled, cored, and minced.
The beets are on the counter, but I still need to prep the pears and onions. Should the oven be heating while I do that?
Yes, go ahead and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, or 200 degrees C, while you finish mincing the Vidalia onions and preparing the pears.
The oven is heating. Do I need to peel the beets before roasting them?
For this stage, just wash the beets well and place them in a roasting pan. The recipe has you roast them whole until tender, then let them cool afterward.
They're washed and in the roasting pan. How long should I plan for them to cook?
Bake the beets for 45 minutes to 1 hour, checking near the end for tenderness. They should feel soft enough to pierce easily.
While they roast, I've peeled, cored, and minced the 4 Bosc pears. The onion is minced too.
Great timing. Keep the 1 1/2 cups minced Vidalia onions and the minced pears nearby so they're ready once you move to the skillet.
The beets are tender now. They're too hot to handle, though.
Set the roasted beets aside to cool before handling them. That cooling step is part of the recipe and will make the next prep safer and easier.
They're cooling. What should I start on the stove?
Place a large skillet over medium heat and melt the 1 pound unsalted butter in it. Once it's melted, you'll be ready for the onion and pear components.
I want to make Best Ever Tuna Salad. Can you talk me through what to set out before I start boiling anything?
Absolutely. Put 2 eggs by the stove, plus a 1 (12 ounce) can of white tuna, a 1 (6 ounce) can of shredded crabmeat, and 1/2 cup mayonnaise for mixing later.
I've got the eggs and cans out. Do I need to open the tuna and crab before the eggs cook?
You can wait on opening them for a few minutes. Start with the eggs: place them in a saucepan and cover them with cold water.
The eggs are in a small saucepan. How much water should be over them?
Use enough cold water to cover the eggs fully so they can heat evenly.
Okay, the pan is on the burner with the eggs covered. What heat should I use?
Bring the water to a boil. As soon as it reaches a boil, take the saucepan off the heat right away.
It just started boiling, and I moved the pan off the burner. Do I leave the lid off?
Cover the saucepan and let the eggs stand in the hot water for 10 to 12 minutes.
While the eggs sit, should I get the salad bowl ready with the seafood and mayonnaise?
Yes, that's a good time to prepare the bowl. Open the white tuna and shredded crabmeat, and have the 1/2 cup mayonnaise ready for when the chopped eggs are done.
The timer is up. What should the egg texture be before I mix everything?
Remove the eggs from the hot water, cool them, peel them, and chop them finely. Then they'll be ready to combine with the tuna, crabmeat, and mayonnaise.
I want to make Cinnamon Crackle Cookies. Can you guide me while I get the bowl and ingredients ready?
Absolutely. Set out a mixing bowl and make sure you have 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup shortening ready to cream together.
The butter is soft, and the shortening is measured. Which sugars should I add?
Add 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup packed brown sugar to the bowl with the butter and shortening.
All four are in the bowl. What texture am I looking for when I mix them?
Cream the butter, shortening, and sugars until the mixture looks blended and softer, with the sugars worked evenly through the fats.
That's mixed together now. I see egg and extracts in the directions—do they go in next?
Yes. Add the egg and extracts to the creamed mixture, then mix well so everything is evenly combined.
The mixture looks smooth after adding those. What should I do with the dry ingredients?
Combine the next eight ingredients separately, then add that dry mixture gradually to the creamed mixture instead of dumping it in all at once.
I'm adding the dry mixture in portions. Should the dough be fully mixed before shaping?
Yes, mix until the dry ingredients are incorporated and the dough holds together well enough to shape.
The dough is ready. How do I portion these for the baking sheets?
Shape the dough into 1-in balls, roll them in sugar, and place them apart on ungreased baking sheets.
I want to make Asian Turkey Burgers tonight. Can you talk me through the ingredient setup before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Set out 1 egg white and 1 tablespoon soy sauce, since those will go into the bowl for the burger mixture.
I've got the egg separated and the soy sauce measured. What else should be on the counter?
Add 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs and 1 tablespoon finely chopped onion to your setup. You'll also need the turkey ready to crumble in after the bowl mixture is combined.
The onion is chopped pretty fine, and I have a mixing bowl out. Do the crumbs and wet ingredients all go in together?
Yes. In the bowl, combine the starting ingredients—the egg white, soy sauce, bread crumbs, and finely chopped onion—so they're evenly moistened before the turkey goes in.
The mixture looks damp and crumbly now. How should I add the turkey without making it tough?
Crumble the turkey over the mixture in small pieces, then mix just until everything is combined. Stop once you don't see dry pockets or big unmixed streaks.
It's mixed, but I don't want to overwork it. What shape am I aiming for?
Divide the mixture into four portions and shape them into four patties. Keep them even in thickness so they cook at the same pace.
I have a nonstick skillet ready. Should I grease it at all?
Coat the nonstick skillet with nonstick cooking spray before adding the patties. That helps them release cleanly as they cook.
The patties are in the skillet. What should I watch for to know they're done?
Cook them in the sprayed nonstick skillet until the turkey burgers are no longer pink. Once they're cooked through, take them out and let them rest briefly before serving.
I want to make Chocolate Covered Pretzels today. Can you walk me through what to set out and how to coat them?

Absolutely. Set out 2 (10 ounce) packages of pretzels, 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, and 1 tablespoon heavy whipping cream. You'll also want a double boiler, a spoon or heatproof spatula, and wax paper for cooling.
I have the pretzels and chocolate chips on the counter. Does the cream go in right away?
Yes. Put the semisweet chocolate chips and the heavy whipping cream together in the top of the double boiler. Keep the heat low so the chocolate melts gently.
The water underneath is barely simmering. Should I stir the whole time?
Stir constantly while the chocolate and cream melt. You're looking for a smooth, glossy mixture with no dry chips left.
It's mostly melted but still a little thick. Is that okay for dipping?
Keep it over low heat a bit longer and continue stirring. The coating works best while the mixture is still very warm, so wait until it looks fully smooth before dipping.
Okay, it's smooth now. How should I handle the pretzels without making a mess?
Dip the pretzels one at a time, moving quickly so each one gets coated while the chocolate mixture stays warm. Let extra chocolate drip back into the pan before setting them down.
Should I fill the wax paper as I go, or coat a bunch first?
Place each coated pretzel directly onto the wax paper as soon as you dip it. That keeps them separate and lets the chocolate start setting neatly.
They're all on the wax paper now. What's the last thing I need to do before serving?
Let the chocolate covered pretzels sit on the wax paper until they set and cool. Once the coating is firm, they're ready to serve or pack up.
I'm making Cheesy Sweet and Savory Spuds. Can you help me get organized before I start peeling?
Absolutely. Set out 6 Yukon Gold potatoes and 2 sweet potatoes, then peel and cube them so the pieces are roughly similar in size. That will help them cook evenly.
The potatoes are cubed. Do I need anything besides the spuds themselves?
Yes—have 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup heavy cream ready. You'll also want a large pot, a colander for draining, and access to your oven broiler for the later step.
I've got the pot out. Should both kinds of potatoes go in together?
Yes, put the Yukon Gold potatoes and sweet potatoes into the large pot together, then add enough water to cover them.
They're covered with water. How high should I set the burner?
Turn the burner up and bring the pot to a boil. Keep an eye on it so it doesn't bubble over.
It's boiling now. Am I supposed to keep simmering them, or stop there?
For the instructions you're following, once it has come to a boil, remove the pot from the heat.
Okay, I've moved it off the burner. What's the cleanest way to handle the water?
Drain the potatoes and sweet potatoes carefully in a colander, letting the steam clear before you handle the pot again.
They're drained and sitting in the colander. What should I do with the oven?
Preheat the oven broiler now. Keep the butter and heavy cream nearby for the next part of the dish.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: For this chilled fruit-style batch, add just a tiny pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For this batch of Candy Bar Squares, I'm serving them cold with fruit, and I'm deciding among cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and nutmeg. Which warm spice should I use just for this version?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use only a tiny pinch of ginger and skip the other warm spices.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Candy Bar Squares as a chilled fruit dessert with cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, or nutmeg. How should I use the warm spices?

messages.content: For this batch of Candy Bar Squares, I'm serving them cold with fruit, and I'm deciding among cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, and nutmeg. Which warm spice should I use just for this version?
For this chilled fruit-style batch, add just a tiny pinch of ginger and leave out the cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg.
Perfect, that's the one-off direction I wanted. Before I get the mixer dirty, what should I set near the bowl?
Put out 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup white sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 2 eggs. Keep the ginger pinch separate so you can add it lightly without overdoing it.
The butter is soft and the sugars are measured. Should I turn on the oven before mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it is ready when the batter comes together.
Oven is heating. I've got the butter and both sugars in the bowl—what texture am I aiming for?
Beat the butter with the white sugar and brown sugar until the mixture looks light and fluffy, not dense or streaky.
It's paler now and looks whipped. Do the eggs go in together or one at a time?
Blend in the 2 eggs and mix well, stopping to scrape the bowl if the butter-sugar mixture clings to the sides.
The eggs are fully mixed in. Where does that tiny ginger pinch fit?
Sprinkle the tiny pinch of ginger in with the dry additions so it spreads evenly through the mixture.
I'm ready for the dry bowl. What exactly am I folding into the egg mixture?
Mix the flour, baking soda, and salt into the egg mixture until combined. Since these are Candy Bar Squares, avoid overmixing once the dry ingredients disappear.
The batter is mixed and the counter is a mess. Anything else before I move on to chilling and serving with fruit?
Clean the bowl edges, make sure no dry pockets remain, and keep the flavor restrained: the only warm spice in this batch should be that tiny pinch of ginger.
I'm making Eclairs II and want someone to pace me through the beginning. What should I set out?
Set out 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. You'll also need a medium saucepan and a cookie sheet.
I have the butter and water measured. The flour and salt are on the counter too. Should I get the oven going?
Yes, preheat the oven to 450 degrees F, which is 230 degrees C, so it's hot when you're ready to bake.
Oven is heating. Is there any pan prep before I start the saucepan?
Grease a cookie sheet now. That way you won't have to pause once the dough mixture is ready.
Cookie sheet is greased. I've got a medium saucepan on the stove; what goes in it?
Add the 1/2 cup butter and 1 cup water to the medium saucepan.
They're in the pan. Should I stir right away or just let the butter sit?
Start heating the pan and stir as it warms, so the butter melts evenly into the water.
The butter is mostly melted, but not completely. How hot should I take it?
Bring the butter and water mixture to a boil, continuing to stir until the butter melts completely.
It's boiling now and the butter looks fully melted. Are the flour and salt next after this?
Yes, keep the measured 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt ready beside the stove for the next stage.
I'm making Chicken and Black Bean Chili and I've got a large pot ready. Can you talk me through the ingredient setup before I turn on the stove?
Absolutely. Set out 2 tablespoons cooking oil and 3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves cut into 1 inch pieces. Keep the chicken pieces fairly even so they brown at the same pace.
The chicken is cut up. I see sea salt and chili powder on the counter too—are those enough to start?

Yes for the listed ingredients: you'll need sea salt to taste and 1 tablespoon chili powder, or more to taste. The cooking directions also call for cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper when you season the chicken, so have those nearby if you're following the full method.
Got it. Should I use the whole 2 tablespoons of oil at once, and what heat should the pot be on?
Pour the full 2 tablespoons cooking oil into the large pot and warm it over medium heat. Give it a minute or two until the oil looks loose and shimmery, but don't let it smoke.
The oil is shimmering now. Do I add all 3 chicken breasts' worth of pieces together?

Add the chicken pieces to the pot and spread them out as much as you can. Brown the chicken on all sides; if the pot feels crowded, stir and turn the pieces so they still get contact with the hot surface.
Some pieces are browning, but there's a little liquid in the bottom. Should I wait for more color before seasoning?

Let the chicken keep cooking until the surfaces have some browning. Once it's browned on all sides, season it with sea salt, the 1 tablespoon chili powder or to taste, cumin, ground chipotle, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
The spices are in and it smells good. How should the chicken look before I add vegetables?
The pieces should be coated with the spices and browned around the edges. They don't need to look dry; just make sure the seasoning is stirred through the chicken before adding the vegetables.
I have onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper chopped. Do they all go in now?
Yes. Mix in the onion, green bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper, scraping the bottom of the pot as you stir so the vegetables pick up the seasoned oil and browned bits.

memory_annotations.exception_action_cue: Go with the oven approach for this batch. Rotate the two trays once during baking, and don't add a final rest at the end.
memory_annotations.exception_query_cue: For today's Chocolate Crisps, I'm doing a two-tray batch and choosing among stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan approaches. Which way should I handle it?

original_cues.exception_action_cue: Use the oven route, rotate the trays once, and skip the final rest.
original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Chocolate Crisps as a two-tray recipe with stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan routes. Which route should I take?

messages.content: For today's Chocolate Crisps, I'm doing a two-tray batch and choosing among stovetop, oven, broiler, skillet, or sheet-pan approaches. Which way should I handle it?
Go with the oven approach for this batch. Rotate the two trays once during baking, and don't add a final rest at the end.
Perfect, that's the special version I want just for this batch. What should I set out first?
Start with the basics: 1 tablespoon butter, softened, and 1 egg white.
The butter is soft and the egg is separated. What sweetener and flavoring do I need nearby?
Set out 1/4 cup white sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract so they're ready when you need them.
I've got two cookie sheets out. What temperature should the oven be for the tray setup?
Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). With two trays, make sure the racks give you enough space for air to move around them.
While it heats, should I prep the sheets now or wait until the batter is mixed?
Prep them now: grease the cookie sheets lightly so they're ready as soon as the mixture is done.
The sheets are greased. Since the butter is softened, does it still go into a pan?
Yes. Put the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and melt it until it's lightly browned.
What should I watch for so I don't take the butter too far?
Look for a light brown color and a nutty smell, then take it off the heat before it gets dark.
The butter looks lightly browned. Where does it go, and do I let it sit afterward?
Pour it into a medium sized bowl. For this version, skip the final rest and keep the bowl ready for the next part.
I'm making Chicken Spinach Bake and I've got frozen chopped spinach thawing. Can you talk me through the setup?
Absolutely. You'll need 3 packages of frozen chopped spinach, 10 ounces each, thawed and ready to drain. Set out 3 eggs too, since they'll bind the spinach mixture.
The spinach is thawed, but it's pretty wet. Before I get messy, what seasonings should I grab?
Grab 1/2 teaspoon onion salt and 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg. You'll also want Parmesan cheese and bread crumbs nearby for the mixing and topping parts.
I have a colander and a clean towel out. How dry does the spinach need to be?
Drain it well, then squeeze out as much excess moisture as you can. It should feel damp but not dripping; too much water can make the bake loose.
Okay, the spinach is squeezed out and in a bowl. Do the eggs go straight in?
Beat the 3 eggs separately with the onion salt and nutmeg first. Once that mixture is even, it'll coat the spinach more smoothly.
The egg mixture is beaten and smells lightly nutmeggy. What bowl should everything go into?
Use the larger bowl with the drained spinach. Pour in the beaten egg mixture, then add the spinach's cheese portion: 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese. Mix until the spinach is evenly coated.
It's mixed, but I still have bread crumbs and more Parmesan on the counter. Are those stirred in too?
Keep those separate. Combine the bread crumbs with the remaining Parmesan cheese so you have a crumbly cheese topping mixture.
The topping is combined. Is there anything I should check before I put it together to bake?
Check that the spinach mixture is evenly seasoned and not watery, then spread it in your baking dish and scatter the bread crumb-Parmesan mixture over the top.
I'm making Drunken Fruit Salsa and want to keep it simple. Can you guide me through what to prep?
Absolutely. Start by getting the fruit ready: peel and finely dice 1 medium mango, chop 3/4 cup fresh strawberries, and peel and finely dice 1 kiwi.
The fruit is cut. I also have a jalapeno—how small should I chop it?
Seed the jalapeno first, then finely chop it so the heat is spread evenly through the salsa instead of landing in big bites.
Got it. What bowl should I use for mixing?
Use a glass bowl. Add the mango, strawberries, kiwi, and jalapeno to it, then stir in the mint and rum until everything is evenly combined.
Should I mash the fruit at all, or keep the pieces intact?
Keep the pieces intact. Stir gently so the salsa stays diced and juicy rather than turning into a puree.
It's mixed now. Does it serve right away, or does it need time in the fridge?
Refrigerate it for 1 to 3 hours. That gives the fruit, jalapeno, mint, and rum time to blend together.
While it chills, do I need to stir it?
Yes, stir it once or twice during the chilling time so the juices and rum stay evenly distributed.
After chilling, what should I check before serving?
Give it one last gentle stir, check that the fruit still looks fresh and evenly coated, then serve it cold from the glass bowl or transfer it to a serving dish.
I'm making Apple Butter V and want to get organized before I put anything on the stove.
Great. Set out 6 pounds of tart apples, cored and sliced, plus 6 cups of apple cider. You'll also want a Dutch oven ready, since the apples start there.
The apples are sliced, and I've got the cider measured. Are there any other ingredients I should keep nearby?
Yes—measure out 3 cups white sugar and 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon so they're ready when you need them.
For the pot, should all 6 pounds of apples go in at once?
Yes. Put the cored, sliced tart apples into the Dutch oven, spreading them out enough that they settle evenly in the pot.
They're in the Dutch oven now. Do I add liquid before heating?
Pour in the 6 cups of apple cider over the apples, then place the Dutch oven on the stove.
What heat should I use to start it, and what am I watching for?
Bring the apple-and-cider mixture to a boil. Once it reaches a boil, cook it on medium heat for 30 minutes, or until the apples are soft.
If the slices soften unevenly, should I stir while it cooks?
A gentle stir now and then is fine to help the apples cook evenly, but keep the main target in mind: after about 30 minutes on medium heat, the apples should be soft.
The apples are soft and the mixture looks ready. How do I get the texture right?
Press the softened mixture through a food mill. That will smooth out the cooked apples and separate out any remaining bits for the apple butter base.
I'm making Caribbean Canadian Glazed Chicken and want to get the glaze started before the chicken goes in the dish.
Great. Set out a medium bowl and measure 1/2 cup ketchup, 4 tablespoons unsweetened pineapple juice, 4 tablespoons molasses, and 2 tablespoons dark rum.
Those are on the counter. The recipe also mentions mustard and garlic—do they go into the bowl too?
Yes, add the mustard and garlic to that same bowl with the ketchup, pineapple juice, molasses, and rum. Whisk or stir until the glaze looks smooth and evenly blended.
The glaze is mixed, but it tastes pretty sweet from the molasses and pineapple juice.
That's expected for this glaze. Season it with salt and pepper to taste, then mix well again so the seasoning is evenly distributed.
I've seasoned it. What baking dish should I use for the chicken pieces?
Use a 9x13 inch baking dish and lightly oil it so the chicken doesn't stick while it marinates and bakes later.
The dish is oiled. Should I pour in all the glaze now?
Not all of it. Put the chicken pieces in the dish, then brush both sides with the prepared glaze, using about 1/2 of the glaze for this coating.
Both sides are brushed and I still have the rest of the glaze set aside.
Perfect. Cover the baking dish tightly so the chicken can marinate without drying out or picking up fridge odors.
How long should it sit in the refrigerator before I cook it?
Refrigerate the covered dish for at least 2 hours, or overnight if you have time for a deeper flavor.
I'm making Biga today. Can you stay with me from setting out the ingredients through mixing it?

Absolutely. Set out 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast, 1/2 cup warm water, 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour, and 1 1/4 cups cold water. You'll also want 1 small bowl for the yeast and a large bowl for the flour.
I've got the yeast and the warm water measured. Does the water go into the small bowl before the yeast?
Yes. Pour the 1/2 cup warm water into the small bowl, then sprinkle the 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast evenly over the top instead of dumping it in one clump.
The yeast is sprinkled on the water. Should I stir it, or just leave it alone?
Leave it to stand so the yeast can dissolve and become foamy. Give it about 15 minutes, then check that the surface looks bubbly or foamy.
While that sits, can I get the flour bowl ready?
Yes. Measure 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into a large bowl, and keep the 1 1/4 cups cold water nearby for when the yeast mixture is ready.
The flour is in the large bowl. Should I make space in the middle now?
Go ahead and make a well in the center of the flour, deep enough to hold the liquids without immediately spilling over the sides.
It's been about 15 minutes, and the yeast mixture looks foamy. What goes into the well first?
Pour the foamy yeast mixture into the well in the flour, then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water to the same well.
Both liquids are in the flour well. Anything special I should check before mixing from here?

Make sure all the measured ingredients are in the bowl: the 3 1/2 cups flour, the yeast dissolved in the 1/2 cup warm water, and the 1 1/4 cups cold water. From there, you're ready to bring the flour into the liquids and continue with the biga.
I'm making Baked Aloha Chicken and want to get organized before I touch the chicken. What should I measure out for the sauce?

Set out 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup light corn syrup, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon salt. You'll also need ginger, corn oil, crushed pineapple with its liquid, chicken legs, and an ovenproof glass baking dish.
The lemon juice, corn syrup, soy sauce, and salt are measured. Should I start heating the oven yet?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the chicken is sauced.
Oven is on. I've got a mixing bowl out—what goes in there first?
Pour the lemon juice, light corn syrup, and soy sauce into the bowl, then add the 1 teaspoon salt, ginger, and corn oil.
Do I just combine them lightly, or am I looking for a certain texture?
Stir until the sauce looks smooth and even, with the corn syrup fully worked into the lemon juice and soy sauce.
The sauce looks glossy and smooth. I opened the crushed pineapple—do I drain it?
Don't drain it. Stir the crushed pineapple in with its liquid so the sauce stays fruity and loose enough to pour.
Pineapple is mixed in. For the baking dish, should the chicken legs be in a single layer?
Place the chicken legs in the ovenproof glass baking dish in an even layer if you can, then pour the pineapple sauce over the top.
The sauce is over the chicken. Before it goes in, anything I should check around the dish or counter?
Make sure the chicken legs are sitting securely in the glass dish and the sauce is mostly over them rather than spilled on the rim. Once the oven reaches 350 degrees F, the dish is ready to bake.
I'm making Easy Pot Roast and have a 4 pounds boneless chuck roast. Can you guide me through the setup without rushing?

Absolutely. Set out the 4 pounds boneless chuck roast, 2 cups water, 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. You'll also need a medium sized oven bag and a roasting pan to hold it.
The roast is unwrapped, and I found the oven bag. Do I heat the oven before I prep the meat?
Yes. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the roast is in the bag.
The oven is heating. For scoring the roast, where should I cut it?
Score shallow cuts across the top and along the sides of the roast. You're not slicing it into pieces; just making small cuts so the seasoning mixture can settle in better.
Scored on the top and sides. Should the roast go straight into the oven bag now?
Yes, place the scored roast into the medium sized oven bag, keeping the bag open enough so you can pour the liquid mixture over the meat without spilling.
The roast is in the bag. I have the water, soup mix, and Worcestershire sauce measured out.

Combine the 2 cups water, the 1 ounce package of dry onion and mushroom soup mix, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. Stir until the soup mix is mostly dispersed, then pour it over the roast in the bag.
The mixture is poured over the meat. I have vegetables ready too; where do they go?
Arrange the vegetables around the meat inside the bag, tucking them along the sides so they sit in the seasoned liquid without covering the roast completely.
Everything is in the bag and sitting in the pan. Anything I should check before it goes in the oven?
Make sure the roast, vegetables, and liquid are contained in the oven bag and the pan is steady enough to catch any drips. Once that looks secure, it's ready for the 350 degrees F oven.
I'm making Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches and want to prep everything before the broiler is hot. Can you walk me through it?
Absolutely. Start by getting the vegetables ready: finely chop 1 small onion, dice 1 medium tomato, chop 1 stalk celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper.
The onion and tomato are done, but the celery and pepper are still whole. Should I keep the pieces small?
Yes, keep them fairly small so the topping spreads evenly over the bread and heats quickly under the broiler.
Okay, all the vegetables are chopped. What should I turn on now?
Preheat your oven's broiler so it's ready when the sandwiches are assembled.
The broiler is heating. What bowl size should I use for the topping?
Use a medium bowl. Add the onion, tomato, celery, and green bell pepper, then stir in the cheese, chili powder, and salt.
I've mixed it, but it looks a little chunky from the vegetables. Is that right?
That's right. It should look like a chunky cheese-and-vegetable mixture, not a smooth spread.
I'm ready to set up the bread. Do I need a special pan?
Arrange the bread slices on a baking sheet or a broiling pan, keeping them in a single layer so the tops are exposed to the heat.
The bread is on the pan. How much topping goes on each slice?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice and spread it all the way out to the edges. Once they're topped, they're ready to go under the preheated broiler.
I'm making Feta Chicken Salad for lunch. Can you guide me through the prep without rushing?

Absolutely. Set out a serving bowl and a smaller mixing bowl. For the main salad, you'll need 3 cups diced cooked chicken, 2 large stalks celery diced, 1 red bell pepper seeded and diced, and 1/2 red onion diced.
The chicken is already diced, and I've got the celery on the board. Should the bell pepper go in with everything right away?
The recipe has you mix the chicken, celery, and red onion in the serving bowl first. Keep the diced red bell pepper ready alongside them so it can be included with the salad mixture as you assemble.
Okay, I've diced the celery and red onion. What size should I aim for so it isn't too chunky?

Aim for small, even dice so the celery and onion distribute through the chicken instead of landing in big bites. Add the chicken, celery, and red onion to the serving bowl and toss them together lightly.
That's mixed. I still have the red pepper diced on the side and the smaller bowl is clean.
Good. In the separate bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta cheese, and dill until the dressing looks combined and the feta is spread through it.
The feta is a little crumbly in the dressing. Is that okay, or should it be completely smooth?
Crumbly is fine for this salad. You just want the mayonnaise, sour cream, feta, and dill blended enough that the dressing will coat the chicken mixture evenly.
I'm ready to combine it. Do I pour all the dressing in at once?

Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture, then stir to blend. Use a folding motion so the cooked chicken stays in pieces while the celery, onion, red bell pepper, and dressing get evenly distributed.
It's all coated now. How do I adjust it before serving?
Taste a spoonful, then season with salt and pepper as needed. Once the seasoning tastes balanced, the Feta Chicken Salad is ready to serve.
I'm decorating cookies and want to make Cookie Paints. Can you walk me through it?
Absolutely. Set out a small bowl, a spoon, a clean paintbrush, 2 tablespoons evaporated milk, and 4 drops red food coloring.
I have the milk measured and the coloring ready. Should the cookies be baked already?
Use this paint on the cookies before baking. Have the unbaked cookies shaped and ready so you can paint them once the color is mixed.
Got it. I've got the unbaked cookies on the tray. How do I mix the paint?
Pour the evaporated milk into the small bowl, then stir in the red food coloring until the color looks even.
The mixture is red, but there are a couple darker streaks near the edge of the bowl.
Give it a few more gentle stirs, scraping around the sides of the bowl, so the coloring is fully blended into the evaporated milk.
Now it looks smooth. How much should I put on each cookie?
Dip the paintbrush lightly, wipe any heavy drip on the bowl edge, and brush a thin layer onto the unbaked cookies. You just want enough color to coat the surface.
I'm painting little red stripes. Is it okay if the brush leaves lines?
Yes, brush lines are fine if you want that look. If you want smoother color, use lighter strokes and spread the paint before adding more.
The cookies are painted and ready for the oven. Anything to check before baking?
Make sure the paint is on the cookies before they go in, and keep the tray level so the color doesn't run. Then bake the cookies according to your cookie dough recipe.
I'm making Banana Chip Muffins I and want to get my counter organized before I start. What dry ingredients should I measure?
Set out a large mixing bowl and measure in 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 tablespoon baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
I've got the bowl ready. Do the chocolate chips go in with the dry ingredients or later?
Add the chocolate chips to that large bowl with the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt, then give everything a thorough mix so the chips are evenly coated.
The dry mix looks even. You mentioned shaping it—what should the bowl look like before I deal with the wet ingredients?
Use a spoon or spatula to make a well in the center of the mixed dry ingredients, like a little hollow where the wet mixture can be poured later.
Okay, the well is there. What small bowl step comes next?
Crack the egg into a small bowl and beat it until it looks frothy, with small bubbles across the surface.
The egg is foamy now. I have the cooking oil, milk, and bananas nearby—do they join the egg?
Yes. Mix the cooking oil, milk, and bananas into the beaten egg until the wet ingredients are combined.
Should the bananas be totally smooth, or is a little texture okay at this point?
A little banana texture is fine; just make sure the wet mixture is blended enough that the oil, milk, egg, and bananas are distributed together.
Wet bowl is ready and the dry bowl has the well. Can I pour it in now?
Yes, pour the wet mixture into the well in the dry ingredients, then continue from there with the batter, keeping the mixing gentle so the muffin texture stays tender.
I'm making Eggnog II and have a saucepan ready. Can you guide me from setup through cooling?

Absolutely. Set out 6 beaten eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk, 1/3 cup white sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. You'll also want a large saucepan, a metal spoon, and a sink or bowl ready for ice water later.
The eggs are beaten, and I measured the milk. Does the vanilla go into the pan now too?

For this recipe, start by putting the beaten eggs, the 2 1/4 cups milk, and the 1/3 cup white sugar into the large saucepan. Keep the vanilla measured and nearby for serving or later use, but the cooking directions begin with the eggs, milk, and sugar.
I've got the eggs, milk, and sugar in the pan. Should I whisk hard or just stir?
Stir them together until the sugar is dispersed and the mixture looks even. Once it's combined, place the pan over medium heat.
The burner is on medium. What texture am I watching for while it cooks?
Keep stirring as it heats, and look for it to thicken enough to coat a metal spoon. Don't rush it with higher heat; steady stirring over medium heat is the key point here.
How do I check the spoon without making a mess?
Dip the metal spoon into the mixture, lift it out, and see whether a thin coating clings to the back. If it runs off like plain milk, keep cooking and stirring.
It's coating the spoon now. Do I leave it on the burner for another minute?
No, remove the saucepan from the heat once it coats the metal spoon.
The pan is off the heat. I've got a bowl of ice water beside the stove—what's the cooling step?
Set the pan into the sink or bowl of ice water and stir the mixture for 1 to 2 minutes so it cools quickly. After that, stir in the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
I'm making Black Bean Lasagna Rolls and want to get my counter organized before the noodles go in. What should I set out?

Set out 8 uncooked lasagna noodles, 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese, 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta cheese, and 1 (4.5 ounce) can chopped green chiles, drained. You'll also need the black beans ready for spooning over the filling.
The chiles are drained and the cheeses are out. Should I salt the pasta water or add oil so the noodles don't stick?
For this recipe, cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions while omitting salt and fat. Stir them gently as they cook to help prevent sticking, then drain them well.
The noodles are cooking now. What bowl should I use for the filling, and what goes into it?

Use a medium mixing bowl. Combine the Monterey Jack and ricotta with the drained chopped green chiles and the next filling ingredients called for in the recipe, then stir well so the mixture is evenly blended.
The filling looks creamy with the chiles mixed through. Do the noodles need to cool before I handle them?
Yes, let the drained noodles sit just until they're cool enough to touch. Lay them flat so they don't fold over or tear while you add the filling.
They're flat on the board. How thick should I spread the cheese mixture?
Spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle in an even layer. Leave a little space at the edges so it's easier to roll without pushing the filling out.
I've covered one side of each noodle. Where do the black beans come in?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on the noodles. Try to distribute them across all 8 noodles so each roll gets a similar amount.
Some beans are sliding around when I start rolling. Any quick way to keep the rolls tidy?
Roll each noodle gently from one short end, keeping the filled side inward and using your fingers to tuck any loose beans back onto the cheese mixture as you go.
Can you help me make Cindis Egg Rolls? I'm setting up my wok and want to prep the filling in the right order.
Absolutely. Start by gathering the main filling ingredients: 1 pound ground pork, 4 cups shredded cabbage, 1 large shredded carrot, and 1/2 green bell pepper cut into thin strips.
The pork is thawed, and I've got the cabbage and carrot ready. Should the bell pepper be very thin?
Yes, thin strips are best so they mix evenly into the filling and soften quickly with the other vegetables.
Okay, the pepper is sliced. Do I cook the vegetables first or the pork?
Cook the pork first. Put it in a large wok over medium-high heat and break it up as it cooks so the pieces stay small for the egg roll filling.
It's browned and there's some liquid and fat in the wok. Should I leave that in?
Drain the cooked pork, then set it aside. You want the filling mixture to stay from getting too wet.
Pork is drained. I have a big mixing bowl out—what goes in there?
Add the shredded cabbage, shredded carrot, green bell pepper strips, onion, garlic, and ginger to the large bowl, then toss them together so everything is evenly distributed.
Should I put the pork into that bowl too, or keep it separate for now?
Keep the pork set aside while you make the sauce mixture. In a small bowl, stir the cornstarch, soy sauce, and molasses until the mixture is smooth.
The sauce looks glossy but I see a couple of cornstarch specks. Is that okay?
Give it another quick stir or press the specks against the side of the bowl until smooth. Once it's lump-free, you'll be ready to combine it with the filling components.
Can you talk me through making Bacon Mushroom Swiss Meatloaf? I've got the ground beef out but want to stay organized.
Absolutely. Set out 12 ounces chopped raw bacon, 1 small white onion chopped, 5 button mushrooms chopped, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef.
The onion and mushrooms are chopped, and the bacon is already in pieces. Should I turn on the oven before I start the skillet?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the meatloaf prep catches up.
Oven is heating. What pan should I use for the bacon?
Use a skillet large enough to spread the chopped bacon in a fairly even layer. Put the bacon in over medium heat.
It's in the skillet now. Am I aiming for crispy or just cooked through?
Cook it until the bacon pieces are browned. Stir occasionally so the pieces color evenly and don't clump together.
The bacon is browned and there's a lot of grease in the pan. Do I drain it now?
Yes. Lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon and transfer it to paper towels so the excess grease drains off.
Bacon is on paper towels. What do I do with the grease left in the skillet?
Carefully discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon grease in the skillet.
I left about 1 tablespoon behind. Should I keep the chopped onion, mushrooms, and beef nearby?
Yes, keep the chopped onion, 5 button mushrooms, and 1 1/2 pounds extra-lean ground beef ready at your workspace, with the drained bacon nearby for the next stage of the meatloaf.
I'm making Carrots and Onions Au Gratin. Can you help me get set up before I start chopping?
Absolutely. For the vegetables, you'll need 1 (16 ounce) package of baby carrots, sliced, and 2 medium onions, sliced. Have a pot ready that's large enough to hold them with water covering them.
The carrots are sliced and the onions are ready. What other ingredients should be on the counter?
Set out 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 3 tablespoons butter. You'll also want a baking dish nearby for after the vegetables are cooked and drained.
Got it. Should I turn the oven on before I boil anything?
Yes—preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, or 175 degrees C, so it's ready when the carrots and onions go into the baking dish.
Oven is heating. How much water should go in the pot with the vegetables?
Put the sliced carrots and onions into the pot, then add enough lightly salted water to cover them. Bring that water to a boil.
They're boiling now. I don't want the carrots mushy—how long should I cook them?
Cook them for 5 minutes, just until they're tender but still firm. Check a carrot slice with a fork; it should give a little without falling apart.
The texture seems right. Do I save any of the cooking water?
No need to save it for this step. Drain the carrots and onions well so the baking dish doesn't get watery.
They're drained. How should I arrange them in the baking dish?
Spread 1/2 of the drained carrots and onions evenly in the baking dish. Keep the Cheddar cheese and butter close by for the au gratin layering that follows.
Can you help me make Barbecued Shredded Beef? I've got a large roasting pan out and want to make sure I start correctly.
Absolutely. You'll need a 3 pounds beef roast and 2 chopped onions for the pan. Keep the roasting pan nearby because the roast goes in whole and the onions get scattered over it.
The roast is about 3 pounds, and I already chopped the onions. What liquids or seasonings should I line up?

Set out 2 12 fluid ounce cans or bottles of beer and 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce. The directions also call for liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper to be mixed with the Worcestershire before the beer goes in.
Got it. Should I heat the oven before I start assembling everything in the pan?
Yes, preheat the oven to 275 degrees F, which is 135 degrees C. That low temperature is what you want before the roasting pan goes in.
The oven is heating. Do I need to brown the beef first, or does it go straight into the roasting pan?
For this recipe, place the beef roast straight into the large roasting pan. Scatter the 2 chopped onions evenly over and around the top of the roast.
The onions are on the roast. I'm using a mixing bowl for the sauce—what should go into it first?
In the large bowl, combine the 6 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce with the liquid smoke, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir those together so the seasonings are evenly distributed.
The seasoning mixture is stirred. Do I add the beer to the bowl or pour it directly over the meat?
Pour the beer into the bowl with the Worcestershire mixture, stir it together, then add that liquid to the roasting pan with the beef and onions.
Both 12 fluid ounce beers are mixed in, and the liquid is in the pan. Should the roast be sitting in the liquid evenly?

Yes, that's fine—the beer mixture should be in the roasting pan around the roast, with the onions over and around it. Once the oven is at 275 degrees F, place the pan in to cook according to your recipe's remaining roasting time.

I've got a shallow baking dish and a rimmed sheet pan out. Which ingredients should hit the counter before I open anything?
Set out 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, and 1 cup grated Parmesan cheese. You'll also need 1 can of artichoke hearts, the 14 ounce size, drained before mixing.
The artichokes are drained. Should I chop them smaller, or keep them chunky for the dip?

In a medium-sized mixing bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, sour cream, Parmesan cheese, and onion until they're evenly combined.

Right—follow the recipe step for onion without adding a made-up quantity. Keep it mixed through the creamy base before the artichokes go in.
Artichokes are ready to fold in. Anything else joins them before the pan?
Once the base is combined, mix in the drained artichoke hearts along with lemon juice, salt, and pepper, as the recipe directs. Fold gently so the dip stays thick.
It looks scoopable and evenly mixed. How do I finish it on the pan without overdoing the top?

Transfer the mixture to your shallow baking dish or spread it on the sheet pan in an even layer. Bake in the 400 degree F oven, use the broiler only if you want extra color, then let it sit uncovered briefly before serving.

messages.content: For Cabbage Kielbasa Supper, can we do our cilantro-stem trick again instead of tossing them?

Yes—finely chop the tender cilantro stems, or parsley stems if that is what you have, and add them with the cabbage, potatoes, onion, salt, and pepper so they simmer into the base of the slow-cooker dish.
I have the 5-qt. slow cooker out. What should go on the counter before I start cutting?
Set out 8 cups shredded cabbage, 3 medium potatoes cut into 1/2 inch cubes, 1 medium chopped onion, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, pepper, broth, and the sausage for the top.
The cabbage is already shredded, and the potatoes are cubed. Should I mix the stems in with the onion?
That works well. Chop the stems very finely, then stir them in with the onion so their flavor spreads through the cabbage and potatoes as everything cooks down.
Perfect, that is the way I like using the stems in this dish.
Add the cabbage, potatoes, onion, chopped stems, 1 3/4 teaspoons salt, and pepper to the 5-qt. slow cooker. It may look packed, but the cabbage will soften and shrink.
It is full nearly to the rim. Do I need to press it down before adding liquid?
You can gently tuck it down just enough to fit the lid later, but do not mash it. Pour the broth over everything so it runs through the cabbage and potatoes.
Broth is in. Where should the kielbasa go so it heats evenly?
Place the sausage on top of the vegetables. Keeping it on top matches this slow-cooker method, and the steam will heat it through while the vegetables become tender.
Lid fits now. I am planning to serve it for dinner—what setting and timing should I use?
Cover it and cook on low for 8-9 hours, until the vegetables are tender and the sausage is heated through.
When I check it later, what texture should tell me it is ready to serve?

Look for soft cabbage, potatoes that are tender when pierced, and sausage that is hot all the way through. Give the vegetables a gentle stir before serving so the broth and stem-flavored base are distributed.
I'm making Alisons Slow Cooker Vegetable Beef Soup and want to get everything into the slow cooker cleanly. Can you guide me while I prep?
Absolutely. Set out the slow cooker, then start with 1 1/2 pounds cubed beef stew meat and 2 cups water. Keep the beef close by so it can go straight into the crock.
The beef is cubed and the slow cooker is on the counter. I also have a measuring cup ready for the water.

Great. You'll also need 1 small onion, chopped, and 1 (28 ounce) can crushed tomatoes. Have your mixed vegetables, potatoes, bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil within reach too, since they all get added before cooking.
The onion is chopped, and I opened the crushed tomatoes. Should the beef go in before any liquid?
Yes. Put the cubed beef stew meat directly into the slow cooker as the base layer.
Done. Some pieces are stacked a bit; is that okay before I add the water?
That's fine for this soup. Pour in the 2 cups water over the beef so there's liquid in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Water is in. I'm trying not to splash tomato everywhere—what should I add next?
Add the chopped onion and the crushed tomatoes, then stir in the mixed vegetables and potatoes so everything is distributed through the liquid.
It looks chunky and the potatoes are partly sitting on top. Should I keep stirring?
Give it a gentle stir until the onion, tomatoes, mixed vegetables, and potatoes are worked in, but you don't need it perfectly even. The slow cooker will settle everything as it cooks.
Okay, it's mixed. I still have the bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil on the counter.
Sprinkle in the bouillon, pepper, salt, and basil, then give the soup one last light stir. Once it's seasoned, it's ready for the slow cooker lid.

messages.content: When I make fruit sweets in the Cinnamon Bread I lane, I want that warmer spice layer I keep coming back to. Can we build that in here?
Yes. For Cinnamon Bread I, keep the recipe centered on the cinnamon-sweet loaf, then add a restrained cardamom-and-ginger accent so the extra warmth stays tucked behind the main flavor.
Perfect. Before I start measuring, what should I get ready on the counter and at the oven?
Set the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and grease one 9x5 inch loaf pan so it is ready before the batter is mixed.
Pan is greased. I have the flour bin open—what dry amounts should I measure first?
Measure out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup white sugar, 2 teaspoons baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda. You will also want the recipe's 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon and salt ready for the bowl.
Yes, the cardamom and ginger sitting behind the cinnamon is exactly the way I usually like these warmer sweets.

Then keep those two additions light, just enough to round out the cinnamon rather than take over. The base still stays the same: flour, sugar, leavening, cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla all go into the large mixing bowl.
I have buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla beside the dry ingredients. Do they all go in together, or should I stage them?
This recipe has you measure them straight into one large mixing bowl together: the flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, salt, buttermilk, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
That is simple enough. Should I worry about overmixing once everything is in the bowl?
Beat the mixture for 3 minutes. Keep the bowl steady, scrape down the sides if needed, and stop once the batter looks evenly combined rather than continuing to whip it.
The batter is coming together and smells warm. Should I do anything to the loaf pan before I transfer it?
Since the 9x5 inch loaf pan is already greased, just make sure the corners and lower edges are coated. Then scrape the batter in cleanly and level the top gently.
I want the kitchen cleaned up while the oven finishes heating. Anything I should set aside or wash first?

Put away the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda, then soak the mixing tools after the 3-minute beat. Keep the filled loaf pan near the oven so it is ready once the oven is fully at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Can you guide me through making Easy Alfredo Sauce I? I've got a medium saucepan ready.
Absolutely. Set out 1 pint heavy whipping cream, 1/2 cup butter, and 1 1/2 cups grated Parmesan cheese so everything can go into the pan without pausing.
The cream and butter are on the counter, and the Parmesan is already grated. Should I melt the butter by itself first?
No need to melt it separately for this recipe. Add the whipping cream, butter, and grated Parmesan cheese together in the medium saucepan.
All three are in the saucepan. What heat should I use so it doesn't get grainy?
Use medium-low heat. Stir as it warms, letting the butter melt and the Parmesan blend into the cream.
It's starting to melt, but I still see a few Parmesan bits. Should I turn the heat up?
Keep it at medium-low rather than raising the heat. Continue stirring until the sauce looks smooth.
Okay, it looks smooth now and the butter is fully incorporated.
Great. Take the saucepan off the heat at this point.
It seems a little loose right off the stove. Is that normal?
Yes, that's expected. The sauce will thicken as it stands after you remove it from the heat.
I'm planning to spoon it over pasta in a few minutes. Should I just let it sit in the pan?
Yes. Let it stand briefly in the saucepan, then give it a gentle stir before serving so the thickened Alfredo sauce is smooth.
Can you help me make Asian Ginger Dressing? I've got a clean glass jar out, but I want to make sure I'm using the right size.
Yes—use a 1 pint glass jar or anything larger so there's enough room to shake the dressing without leaks.
Great. I've minced the garlic already. How much ginger should go in with it?
Add 3 cloves garlic, minced, and 2 tablespoons minced fresh ginger root to the jar.
The ginger and garlic are in. I'm measuring the liquids now—what amounts do I need for the oil and vinegar?
Pour in 3/4 cup olive oil and 1/3 cup rice vinegar.
Those are added. The recipe also mentions a few other things—should I put them in now too?
Yes, add the soy sauce, honey, and water to the same jar with the garlic, ginger, olive oil, and rice vinegar.
Everything is in the jar. Should I stir it, or is shaking better for this dressing?
Put on a tight fitting lid and shake the jar well so the ingredients start combining.
It's shaken, but I can still see the honey clinging a bit. What's the best way to loosen it?
Remove the lid, then heat the jar in the microwave for 1 minute—just long enough to dissolve the honey.
The honey has dissolved. Do I serve it warm, or should it sit first?
Let the dressing cool, then shake it well again before serving.
Can you help me make Black Bean Lasagna Rolls? I'm setting everything out and want to follow the recipe closely.
Absolutely. Put a pot of water on for the lasagna noodles, and gather 8 uncooked lasagna noodles plus 1 cup shredded reduced-fat Monterey Jack cheese.
Noodles and Monterey Jack are on the counter. What should I pull from the fridge or pantry next?
You'll also need 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta cheese and 1 (4.5 ounce) can chopped green chiles, drained.
I found the ricotta and drained the chiles. Should the noodle water be salted or oiled?
For this recipe, cook the lasagna noodles according to the package directions while omitting salt and fat. Once they're tender, drain them well.
The noodles are cooking. What can I mix while I wait?
Combine the cheeses with the next 3 ingredients from the recipe, including the drained chopped green chiles, and stir until the mixture is well blended.
The cheese mixture looks even. The noodles are drained, but they're a little slippery—how should I handle them?
Lay the noodles out flat in a single layer if you can, then spread the cheese mixture over one side of each noodle.
I've spread the filling over the noodles. Where do the black beans go?
Spoon the black beans evenly over the cheese mixture on each noodle so every roll gets some.
Before I roll them, should the beans be piled in the center or spread out?
Keep them spread evenly over the cheese layer rather than piled up; that will make the lasagna rolls easier to roll and more consistent when served.
I'm making Crabby Cliffs Mushroom Puffs and I've got a cutting board out. Can you guide me while I prep?

Absolutely. Start by setting out 2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 cups fresh chopped mushrooms, 2 chopped green onions, and 1 clove of crushed garlic. You'll also need cayenne pepper for the mushroom mixture.
The mushrooms are chopped, but the garlic is still whole. Should I crush it before heating anything?
Yes, crush the garlic now and chop the green onions so everything is ready to go into the pan quickly once the oil is warm.
All the aromatics are ready. What should I do with the oven?
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F, which is 200 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the filling is ready.
Oven is heating. I have a medium saucepan on the stove—what goes in first?
Pour the 2 tablespoons of olive oil into the medium saucepan and warm it over medium heat.
The oil looks shiny but not smoking. Is that the right point for the vegetables?
That's right. Stir in the 3 cups chopped mushrooms, the 2 chopped green onions, the 1 clove crushed garlic, and the cayenne pepper.
Everything is in the pan. How often should I stir so the garlic doesn't catch?
Stir it regularly and keep the heat at medium. You want the mushrooms to soften and release moisture without letting the garlic brown too hard.
They're cooking down and smell good. How long am I aiming for, and what texture should I look for?
Cook the mixture for about 10 minutes, or until the mushrooms and onions are tender. Once it's tender, you're ready to use the filling for the puffs.
