Perfect, that's exactly what I'm doing today. I've got the baking dish out—what should I prep first?
Core 8 red apples and keep them whole enough to stand in the dish. You'll also need 1/4 cup butter ready for the warm sauce.
The apples are cored. I'm checking the pantry before I start heating anything—what sweetener and spice do I need?
Measure 1/3 cup maple syrup and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon. If you're following the sauce as written, also have the ginger, lemon juice, and vanilla close by for the saucepan.
Got those measured. Should I turn on the oven before arranging the apples?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's hot by the time the apples are sauced.
The oven is heating. I have a 9x13 inch pan—do the apples need to be packed tightly?
Place the cored apples in the 9x13 inch baking dish in a single layer. They can sit fairly close together, but give them enough room for the syrup mixture to run around them.
They're in the pan. I don't want to scorch the butter—how should I make the sauce?
Use a small saucepan over medium heat. Combine the butter, maple syrup, cinnamon, ginger, lemon juice, and vanilla, stirring as the butter melts into the syrup.
The butter has melted and the sauce smells good. Am I just warming it, or does it need to bubble?
Bring the mixture to a boil, then take it straight to the apples and drizzle it evenly over all 8 so each one gets some of the maple-spiced sauce.
Since I'm serving these later, should I add the streusel after that drizzle or wait?
Wait on the streusel. Bake or store the sauced apples as planned, then add the topping just before reheating or serving so the crumbs keep their texture.

Add the small amount of chili to the oil first and let it warm briefly, then put in the chopped onion and cook over medium heat until the onion turns clear.

You can add the pinch of salt now, then adjust with salt and pepper to taste at the end if needed.

Cook them for about 15 minutes total, turning as needed, until the chicken is browned and just about done.

Look for browned surfaces and chicken that feels firmer rather than soft. Since the recipe says "just about done," avoid pushing it until it dries out in the skillet.

Taste the pan juices or a small cut piece if you can do so safely, then add salt and pepper to taste. Once the chicken is cooked through, serve it hot.
I'm making Garden Party Salad for a small lunch. Can you walk me through the dressing and assembly?

Add it as-is unless it is very stiff; the whisking will smooth it out with the oil, cider vinegar, and mayonnaise. If it clings to the spoon, scrape it fully into the bowl so the dressing stays balanced.

Whisk the dressing until it looks smooth and cohesive, with no obvious streaks of mayonnaise or pockets of marmalade. Once it is smooth, cover the bowl and chill it.

Yes. Put the chicken, raisins, almonds, and parsley together in a large bowl. Give them a light toss on their own so the add-ins are spread through the chicken before the dressing goes on.
The salad mix is in the big bowl, and guests arrive soon. Should I add all the dressing at once?

Give it one final gentle turn from the bottom of the bowl, then serve right away. Keep any leftovers covered and chilled since the dressing contains mayonnaise.

messages.content: I want to make Biga today. Can you talk me through what to set out before I start?

Absolutely. Put out 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast, 1/2 cup warm water, 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour, and 1 1/4 cups cold water. You'll also want a small bowl for blooming the yeast and a large bowl for the flour.
I've got the yeast and both waters measured. Should the warm water go straight into the small bowl?
Yes. Pour the 1/2 cup warm water into the small bowl, then sprinkle the 3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast evenly over the top rather than dumping it in one clump.
The yeast is sitting on the warm water now. Do I stir it, or leave it alone?
Leave it to stand until the yeast has dissolved and looks foamy, about 15 minutes. A little gentle swirl is fine if dry spots remain, but it mainly needs time.
While that sits, can I get the flour ready in the large bowl?
Yes, measure the 3 1/2 cups unbleached bread flour into the large bowl now. Keep the 1 1/4 cups cold water nearby so it's ready when the yeast mixture is foamy.
The flour is in the bowl. Should I level it off carefully, or is a little variation okay?
For this, level the cups as best you can so the 3 1/2 cups are reasonably accurate. Biga is simple, but the flour-to-water balance matters for the texture.
The yeast has been about 15 minutes and it's foamy on top. What should the flour bowl look like before I add anything?
Make a well in the center of the flour—basically a hollow spot deep enough to hold the liquid for a moment before it spreads.
I made the well. Do I pour in just the yeast mixture first, or the cold water too?
Pour the foamy yeast mixture into the well, then add the 1 1/4 cups cold water there as well. From here, you're ready to mix the biga together according to your next step.
I want to make Caramel Chocolate Corn. Can you help me set up before I start mixing anything?
Absolutely. Have 16 cups popped popcorn ready, along with 1 cup roasted peanuts. You'll also need cookie sheets, a paper bag, and a microwave-safe bowl.
The popcorn is popped, and I found a big paper bag. What ingredients should I measure for the caramel part?
Measure out 1 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup butter. The recipe also has you combine corn syrup, vanilla, and salt with those in the microwave-safe bowl.
Should I do anything to the cookie sheets before the popcorn goes near the caramel?
Yes, grease the cookie sheets now so the coated corn will be easier to spread out and remove later.
Cookie sheets are greased. Do the peanuts go on the sheets or somewhere else first?
Put the popcorn and roasted peanuts into the paper bag together. That gives you room to coat everything once the caramel mixture is ready.
The bag is pretty full, but I can still fold the top. Is that okay?
That should work. Just make sure there's enough space to move the popcorn and peanuts around without spilling when it's time to coat them.
They're in the bag now. Should I keep it open while I make the sauce?
Set the bag aside for the moment. Next, use the microwave-safe bowl for the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt.
So I'm just combining those in the bowl before microwaving?
Right. Combine the sugar, butter, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt in the microwave-safe bowl, then you'll be ready for the heating step that follows the recipe's setup.

original_cues.exception_query_cue: I'm making Crustless Spinach Quiche for a gift box or dessert platter with fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, or desserts. How should I finish the top?

messages.content: This Crustless Spinach Quiche is going onto a gift tray alongside fruit crisps, pies, muffins, breads, bars, and other desserts, so I want the top to look a little more polished just for this batch. What finish would you use?
Brush on a very thin glaze across the surface, but keep one corner plain.
Great, that's the look I want for this one. Before I turn on anything, what should I pull out first?
Start with the prep items: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil and 1 chopped onion. Keep a large skillet nearby for the onion.
The onion is chopped, and the skillet is on the stove. What else needs to be ready before I cook?
Set out the spinach and eggs too: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained, plus 5 beaten eggs.
The spinach is drained and the eggs are beaten. Should I prep the pan now or heat the oven first?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
Oven is heating. I have a round pie pan out; what size and how should I prep it?
Use a 9 inch pie pan and lightly grease it so the quiche releases cleanly.
Pan is greased. For the stovetop part, how hot should the skillet be before the onion goes in?
Heat the vegetable oil in the large skillet over medium-high heat.
The oil is hot and moving easily across the pan. Do the onions go in all at once?
Yes, add the chopped onion to the skillet and stir it occasionally as it cooks.
What texture am I watching for before I move on with the quiche filling?
Cook the onions until they're soft, then you're ready to continue with the spinach, beaten eggs, and the prepared 9 inch pan.
I want to make Crunchy Cheese Sandwiches. Can you guide me while I get the vegetables and broiler set up?
Absolutely. Start by getting the vegetables ready: finely chop 1 small onion, dice 1 medium tomato, chop 1 stalk of celery, and finely chop 1 green bell pepper.
The onion and tomato are cut. Should the celery and bell pepper be small pieces too?
Yes, keep them fairly small so the topping spreads evenly and cooks quickly under the broiler. The celery should be chopped, and the green bell pepper should be finely chopped.
All the vegetables are prepped. Do I turn on the oven now or mix the topping first?
Go ahead and preheat your oven's broiler now so it's hot by the time the sandwiches are assembled.
The broiler is heating. I have a medium bowl out—what goes into it?
Add the onion, tomato, celery, and bell pepper to the bowl, then stir them together with the cheese, chili powder, and salt.
The mixture is combined. It looks chunky and moist from the tomato—is that okay?
That's fine for this sandwich topping. Just make sure the cheese and seasonings are evenly mixed through the vegetables.
I'm ready with the bread. Should I use a baking sheet or something deeper?
Arrange the slices of bread on a baking sheet or a broiling pan. Keep them in a single layer so each slice gets direct heat.
The bread slices are lined up. How much topping should I put on each one?
Spoon 1/4 of the mixture onto each slice, then spread it out to the edges so every sandwich gets an even, crunchy topping under the broiler.
I want to make Candy Bar Squares. Can you guide me while I get the counter set up?
Absolutely. Set out 1 cup softened butter, 1 cup white sugar, 1/2 cup packed brown sugar, and 2 eggs. You'll also need a mixing bowl and something to beat the butter and sugars together.
The butter is softened, and I've measured both sugars. Should I turn the oven on before mixing?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready by the time the batter is mixed.
Oven is heating. Do the butter and sugars all go in together?
They do. Beat the softened butter with the white sugar and packed brown sugar until the mixture looks light and fluffy rather than dense or streaky.
It's getting paler, but I still see a few buttery spots on the side of the bowl.
Scrape down the sides of the bowl, then beat a little longer so the butter and sugars are evenly combined and fluffy.
That looks better now. When do the eggs go in?
Add the 2 eggs to the bowl and blend them in well. Mix until the egg mixture looks smooth and fully incorporated.
The eggs are mixed in. What dry ingredients should I add next?

Mix in the flour, baking soda, and salt to the egg mixture. Since the recipe step doesn't give amounts for those here, use the amounts from your full recipe if you have them, and stir just until combined.
The batter is coming together. Should I keep beating it hard after the flour goes in?
No need to overbeat once the flour, baking soda, and salt are added. Mix only until no dry streaks remain, then you're ready to move on with the rest of your Candy Bar Squares recipe.
I want to make Elizabeths Extreme Chocolate Lovers Cake. Can you help me set up the ingredients and pans before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put the oven rack in a comfortable middle position, then get out 2 round 9 inch cake pans so they're ready for greasing and flouring.
The 2 pans are on the counter. What dry ingredients should I measure into the bowl?
Measure 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking soda, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Keep them together since they'll be sifted as a group.
I've got the flour, baking soda, and salt measured. What about the chocolate for this cake?
You'll need 6 squares of unsweetened chocolate, each 1 ounce, chopped. Set the chopped chocolate nearby so it's ready when the recipe calls for it later.
Chocolate is chopped. Should I turn on the oven now or prep the pans first?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C. While it heats, you can work on the pans.
The oven is heating to 350. How thoroughly do I need to coat the pans?
Grease and flour both 9 inch pans all over the bottoms and sides. Tap out any extra flour so the cake layers release cleanly.
Both pans are greased and floured. I'm ready to deal with the dry bowl.
Sift together the measured flour, baking soda, and salt. You're looking for an even, lump-free dry mixture.
The dry ingredients are sifted. Do I add the chopped chocolate to that bowl yet?
Not yet based on the steps you're following. Set the sifted flour mixture aside, and keep the chopped unsweetened chocolate nearby for the next stage.
I want to make the Dipping Sauce. Can you help me set up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put a small bowl and a spoon or whisk on the counter, then measure out 1/2 cup mayonnaise and 2 teaspoons ketchup.
The bowl is ready, and I've measured the mayonnaise and ketchup. What should I grab next?
Add 2 tablespoons prepared horseradish to your setup, along with 1/4 teaspoon paprika. You'll also need salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper for the bowl.
I have the horseradish, paprika, and the seasonings out. Do I put everything in at once?
Yes. Spoon the mayonnaise into the small bowl, then add the ketchup, prepared horseradish, paprika, salt, oregano, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Everything is in the bowl. Should I whisk it hard or just stir?
Stir steadily until the sauce looks even in color and the horseradish and spices are distributed throughout. Scrape around the sides of the bowl so no mayonnaise streaks remain.
It's mostly blended, but I can still see a few pale streaks near the edge.
Give it a few more turns, pulling from the outside toward the center. Once it looks creamy and uniform, it's mixed enough.
Okay, the texture looks smooth now. Should I taste it before storing?
You can taste a tiny amount if you'd like, especially to check the salt and heat from the cayenne, but the recipe's next step is to cover the sauce and refrigerate it.
I'm serving it later, so I'll chill it. What's the best way to cover it?
Transfer it to a covered container or cover the small bowl tightly, then store it in the refrigerator until you're ready to serve.
I'd like to make Carrot and Coriander Soup II. Can you guide me through it while I prep?
Absolutely. Get out a large saucepan, plus a blender or food processor for later. For the soup, you'll need 4 large carrots cut into 1 inch pieces and 1/4 large onion chopped.
The carrots are cut and the onion is chopped. I'm checking the fridge now—what else goes in?
Add 1 quart vegetable broth to your counter, along with 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro. Those are the remaining ingredients.
I have the broth and cilantro ready. Should the pan be heated before anything goes in?
No need to preheat it. Put the carrots, chopped onion, vegetable broth, and cilantro straight into the large saucepan.
Everything is in the saucepan. The broth just covers the vegetables; is that okay?
Yes, that's fine. Set the saucepan over heat and bring the mixture to a boil.
It's starting to boil now. How long should I let it cook?
Let it cook until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes. You can check by piercing a carrot piece with a fork; it should go in easily.
The carrots are soft after about 10 minutes. Do I blend it right away?
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the soup cool slightly before blending, so it's safer to puree.
It's cooled a bit. I can use either my blender or food processor—what texture am I going for?
Puree the soup until smooth using the blender or food processor. Work carefully if it's still warm, and blend until there are no carrot chunks left.
I'm making Chicken Marsala with Portobello Mushrooms and want to get set up before I turn on the stove. Can you talk me through it?

Absolutely. Put out 3/4 cup butter total, since it will be divided, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil total, also divided. You'll also need a skillet and something to cover the mushrooms after they cook.
Butter and oil are on the counter, and I've got a large skillet with a lid nearby. What produce should I prep?
Slice 4 portobello mushroom caps, then chop 1 clove garlic. Keep the mushrooms close to the stove so they can go straight into the hot fat.
The mushrooms are sliced and the garlic is chopped. Should the oven be on already?
Yes, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C.
The oven is heating. For the skillet, how much butter and oil go in right now?
Set the skillet over medium heat, then melt 1/2 cup butter with 1 tablespoon vegetable oil. Let the butter melt fully and start to foam gently, but don't let it brown.
The butter is melted and foamy, and the oil is mixed in. Do the mushrooms go in before the garlic?
Yes. Add the sliced portobello mushrooms to the skillet and cook them, stirring as they soften. You're looking for tender mushrooms that have given off some moisture and look glossy.
They're shrinking and there's some liquid in the pan. Should I keep stirring or let them sit?
Keep stirring often enough that they cook evenly, but give them brief contact with the skillet between stirs. Stay at medium heat until the mushroom slices are tender.
The mushrooms feel tender now. I'm not ready for the next part of the recipe yet—how do I hold them?
Take the skillet off the heat, cover the mushrooms to keep them warm, and set them aside until you're ready to continue.
I'd like to make Fall Harvest Baked Apples. Can you help me get set up before I turn on the oven?
Absolutely. You'll need 8 red apples, cored, plus 1/4 cup butter, 1/3 cup maple syrup, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon.
The apples are cored and on the counter. What pan should I use for them?
Use a 9x13 inch baking dish. Set the apples in it upright so they're ready to catch the warm maple-butter mixture.
Got it. Should I preheat now or wait until the sauce is ready?
Go ahead and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's hot when the apples are dressed.
The oven is heating. I have a small saucepan out—what goes into it?
Put the butter, maple syrup, cinnamon, ginger, lemon juice, and vanilla into the small saucepan.
Do I keep the heat low, or should it be hotter for the syrup mixture?
Set the saucepan over medium heat. Stir as the butter melts so the maple syrup and spices come together evenly.
The butter has melted and it smells like cinnamon. What texture am I looking for before pouring?
Let the mixture come to a boil. Once it's bubbling, it's ready to spoon or drizzle over the apples.
The apples are in the baking dish and the sauce is boiling. How do I make sure they're coated evenly?
Drizzle the hot maple-butter mixture equally over the 8 apples, letting some run into the centers and around the baking dish before they go into the oven.
I'm making Fancy Brussels Sprouts and have a saucepan ready. Can you guide me through what to set out?
Yes. Measure 1 cup water into the saucepan, and have 1/4 cup minced fresh parsley ready to add with it.
Water is measured and the parsley is minced. Are there any seasonings before I turn on the heat?
Add 1 teaspoon sugar and 1/2 teaspoon salt to the saucepan with the water and parsley.
Those are in the pan. Should I heat it gently or bring it up pretty quickly?
Set the saucepan over medium heat and bring the water, parsley, sugar, and salt to a boil.
It's boiling now and the parsley is moving around in the liquid. Do the brussels sprouts go in whole?
Add the brussels sprouts to the boiling mixture. If yours are very large, halving them is fine, but keep the cooking time focused on getting them tender.
They're in. Should the lid go on right away?
Cover the saucepan and let them simmer for 6-8 minutes, until the brussels sprouts are tender.
I'm at about 7 minutes. What texture should I check for before draining?
Pierce one with a fork; it should feel tender but not falling apart. Once they're there, drain off the cooking liquid.
They're drained and still hot in the pan. How do I finish them for serving?
Add the water chestnuts and butter, then heat everything through so the butter melts and the water chestnuts warm up. Serve the brussels sprouts while hot.
I'd like to make Anzac Biscuits I. Can you help me set up the ingredients before I start mixing?

Absolutely. Put out 1 cup quick cooking oats, 3/4 cup flaked coconut, 1 cup all-purpose flour, and 1 teaspoon baking soda. You'll also need the sugar, syrup, butter, and boiling water called for in the method.
The oats, coconut, flour, and baking soda are on the counter. Should I combine anything yet?
Yes. In a mixing bowl, stir together the oats, flour, sugar, and coconut until they're evenly distributed.
I've got a dry mix in the bowl. It looks fairly even, with the coconut spread through it.
Good. Set that bowl aside and place a small saucepan over low heat. Add the syrup and butter, then let them melt together gently.
The butter is melting into the syrup now. Do I need to stir it constantly?
Give it a gentle stir now and then so the butter blends with the syrup, but keep the heat low and don't let it boil.
The saucepan mixture is smooth. I have boiling water ready—what happens with the baking soda?
Mix the soda with the boiling water, then add that mixture to the melted butter and syrup in the saucepan.
It foamed a bit when I added it. Is that expected, and should I pour it right away?
A little foaming is normal. Once it's combined, pour the butter mixture into the bowl of dry ingredients.
The wet mixture is in the bowl with the oats and coconut. How much should I mix it?
Stir until the dry ingredients are evenly moistened and no floury patches remain. Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl so the butter mixture is worked through everything.
I'd like to make Carrot and Coriander Soup II. Can you guide me while I get set up?
Absolutely. Put a large saucepan on the stove, and gather 4 large carrots cut into 1 inch pieces, 1/4 large onion chopped, 1 quart vegetable broth, and 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro.
The carrots are cut, and the onion is chopped. Should the cilantro go in at the beginning too?
Yes, for this soup the cilantro goes into the saucepan with the carrots, onion, and vegetable broth, so you can add all of them together.
Everything is in the large saucepan now. The broth just covers the vegetables pretty well.
Great. Turn up the heat and bring the mixture to a boil, stirring once or twice so the onion and cilantro are distributed through the broth.
It's boiling. Do I keep it at a hard boil for the full time?
Keep it boiling steadily, but not so violently that it splashes. Cook until the carrots are tender, about 10 minutes.
I'm at about 10 minutes, and a fork slides into the carrot pieces easily.
That means the carrots are ready. Remove the saucepan from the heat and let the soup cool slightly before blending.
I have a blender ready. How careful do I need to be with the hot soup?
Blend carefully because it will still be hot. Work in batches if needed, don't overfill the blender, and puree until the soup is smooth.
The soup is smooth now. Is there anything else from the recipe before serving?
That's the full recipe: carrots, onion, vegetable broth, and cilantro cooked until tender, cooled slightly, then pureed smooth. Give it a stir and serve it warm.
I'm making Cornbread Dressing I today. Can you help me set up before I start baking anything?

Absolutely. Put out 1 (12 ounce) package of refrigerated biscuit dough and 1 (8 ounce) package of corn bread mix. You'll also want whatever the packages call for so you can bake the biscuits and an 8x8 inch pan of cornbread.
The dough and cornbread mix are on the counter. Do I need to chop anything before the oven gets busy?
Yes. Dice 1 cup onion and 1 cup celery, and keep them nearby. Later they'll go into a small pot with margarine and chicken broth.
Should I bake the biscuits and cornbread at the same time if the package directions allow it?

That's fine if the package temperatures and timing work together. You need enough baked biscuits to make 4 cups crumbled, plus one 8x8 inch pan of cornbread prepared according to its package directions.
The biscuits are done, and the cornbread is just coming out. Do I crumble them hot?
Let both cool first so they're easier and safer to handle. Once cooled, crumble the biscuits and cornbread into pieces for the dressing.
I've got the crumbles in a big bowl. What texture should I aim for?
Go for loose, irregular crumbles rather than a fine powder. The recipe's key point here is simply to cool and crumble them after baking.
The crumbling is done. What should I set the oven to for the dressing stage?
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, which is 175 degrees C, so it's ready for the next part.
While it preheats, what happens with the onion and celery?
Use a small pot and combine the diced onion, diced celery, margarine, and chicken broth. Keep everything together there for the next cooking step.
I'm making Garlic Butter and the butter is already softened. Can you talk me through the rest?
Absolutely. Put a small bowl on the counter and add 1 cup softened butter to it. Keep a spoon or spatula handy so you can mash and fold everything together smoothly.
Butter is in the bowl. Should the garlic go in before the cheese?
Yes. Add 1 tablespoon minced garlic to the butter, then stir it in so the garlic is spread evenly instead of sitting in one clump.
It's mixed in, but the butter is getting a little streaky. Is that okay?
That's fine. Add 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese and fold it through the garlic butter. The mixture should look a bit textured from the cheese, not perfectly smooth.
Parmesan is in. I have garlic salt, Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika out—how much garlic salt?
Use 1 tablespoon garlic salt. Sprinkle it over the butter rather than dumping it all in one spot, then mix well so the saltiness is evenly distributed.
Mixed. How should I add the Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika?
Season with the Italian seasoning, pepper, and paprika to taste. Start with small pinches, stir, and check the aroma and color before adding more.
The color looks nice and it smells garlicky. Should I whip it more or leave it thick?
Leave it thick but well combined. Give it a final press-and-fold around the bowl to catch any dry Parmesan or seasoning stuck to the sides.
What's the best way to serve or store it once it's mixed?
You can use it right away on warm bread, vegetables, potatoes, or steak. For storage, scrape it into a covered container, or shape it into a small log in parchment and chill it until firm.
I'm making Frosted Shortbread today. Can you talk me through setting up before I start mixing?
Absolutely. Put out 1 cup butter, softened, with no substitutes, and 1 cup packed brown sugar. You'll also want a mixing bowl ready so you can cream them together smoothly.
The butter is softened and I packed the brown sugar into the measuring cup. What else should be beside the bowl?
Add 1 egg yolk and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to your setup. The written method also calls for flour and salt later, so keep those nearby as well, even though no amounts are listed here.
Got it. Should I grease the pan now or wait until the dough is done?
You can grease the 15-in pan now so it's ready. After that, start by creaming the softened butter with the packed brown sugar in the mixing bowl until they're blended and creamy.
I've greased the pan, and the butter-sugar mixture looks soft and combined. Is it time for the egg?
Yes. Add the egg yolk and the vanilla extract to the creamed mixture, then mix well so the yolk disappears evenly into the batter.
The vanilla is mixed in, and the bowl smells good. The mixture looks a little glossy now.
That sounds right. In a separate bowl or off to one side, combine the flour and salt, then add that mixture to the creamed ingredients.
Since the flour and salt amounts aren't shown here, should I just follow my copy of the recipe for those before adding them?
Yes, use the flour and salt amounts from your full recipe copy, then mix them into the creamed mixture just until the dough comes together.
The dough is together and fairly thick. How do I get it into the pan without making it uneven?
Transfer the dough to the greased 15-in pan and press it out evenly, working from the center toward the edges so the shortbread bakes in a level layer.
I'm making Biriyani and have a large skillet ready. Can you guide me from prep through the first few cooking steps?
Absolutely. Set out 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar, and 1 medium onion, sliced.
The onion is sliced, and I've measured the yogurt and vinegar. Should the skillet be on before I mix anything?
Yes. Put the large skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil. Let it warm so the oil coats the bottom of the pan.
The oil is warmed and moving easily around the skillet. Do I add the onion now or the yogurt mixture?
Add the plain yogurt and distilled white vinegar to the skillet first, then stir them into the oil so they're combined.
It looks a little loose and tangy-smelling. Is that okay before the onion goes in?
That's fine. Once the yogurt and vinegar are mixed in, add the sliced onion to the skillet.
The onion is in. How long should I keep it cooking if the recipe just says tender?
Cook it over medium heat, stirring now and then, until the onion softens and loses its raw bite. You're looking for tender slices rather than crisp ones.
The onion has softened and is starting to look glossy. I've got garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes nearby.
Good timing. Stir in the garlic, ginger paste, green chile peppers, and tomatoes so they mix evenly through the onion, yogurt, vinegar, and oil.
Should I scrape the bottom as I stir those in?
Yes, gently scrape and fold everything together so the aromatics and tomatoes don't stick, while keeping the mixture moving in the skillet.
I'm making Cabbage Rolls II and have a big pot ready. Can you talk me through the prep?
Absolutely. Set out 12 cabbage leaves, 1 cup cooked white rice, 1 beaten egg, and 1/4 cup milk. You'll also need onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper for the filling.
The rice is already cooked, and I've got the cabbage leaves separated. Should the pot be full of water?
Use a large pot with enough water for the cabbage leaves to move around, then bring it to a boil.
Water is boiling. I'm worried the leaves will tear if I leave them too long.
Keep it brief: boil the cabbage leaves for 2 minutes, just to soften them, then drain them.
They're drained and a little floppy now. Do I dry them before filling?
Let excess water drip off, and if they're very wet, pat them lightly so the filling doesn't slide around.
I've got a large mixing bowl out. What goes into the meat mixture?
In the large bowl, combine 1 cup cooked white rice, the beaten egg, 1/4 cup milk, onion, ground beef, salt, and pepper.
The filling is mixed. How much should I put on each leaf?
Spoon about 1/4 cup of the meat mixture into the center of each cabbage leaf.
I'm at the rolling part. What's the best way to keep them closed?
Roll each leaf around the filling, tucking in the ends as you go so the cabbage roll holds together.
I'm making Corn Bread Sloppy Joes, and I've got the baking dish and a skillet out. Can you talk me through the prep?

Absolutely. Set out the 1 (8.5 ounce) package corn bread/muffin mix, 1 egg, 1/3 cup milk, and 2 pounds ground beef. You'll bake the corn bread part according to the package directions while the sloppy joe filling comes together on the stove.
The corn bread mix asks for the egg and milk, so I'm stirring those in now. Should I bake it before starting the meat?
Yes. Prepare and bake the corn bread according to the package directions, using that egg and milk. Once it's in the oven, you can use the baking time to start the beef mixture.
The corn bread is in the oven. For the skillet, should I add the beef all at once?
Add the ground beef to a large skillet with the onion and cook over medium heat. Break the beef up as it cooks, and keep going until the meat is no longer pink.
The beef has browned and there's some liquid in the pan. Do I keep that?
Drain it before adding the sauce ingredients. That keeps the filling from turning greasy or watery.
Drained. I see spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix ready on the counter—do they all go in together?
They do. Stir the spaghetti sauce, corn, chilies, and sloppy joe mix into the drained beef and onion until everything is evenly combined.
It's mixed but still looks a little loose around the edges. What should the pan be doing now?
Bring the mixture to a boil. Stir occasionally so the sauce heats evenly and doesn't catch on the bottom of the skillet.
The corn bread is baked and the filling is bubbling. How should I serve it?

Spoon the hot sloppy joe mixture over or alongside the baked corn bread, depending on how you want it plated. Let the corn bread cool just enough to slice cleanly, then serve while the filling is still hot.
I'm making French Spring Soup and have a large pot ready. Can you walk me through what to set out?
Absolutely. Put 1/4 cup butter by the stove, and make sure you have 1 pound leeks chopped and ready to go.
The leeks are chopped. Should the onion be prepped before I turn on the heat?
Yes, chop 1 onion before you start cooking so it can go in with the leeks. You'll also need 2 quarts water nearby for later.
Everything is on the counter. Do I start with the butter in the pot?
Yes. Set the large pot over medium heat and melt the butter gently, letting it coat the bottom without browning.
The butter has melted and is foaming a bit. Are the leeks and onion next?
Add the chopped leeks and chopped onion to the pot, then stir them through the butter so they're evenly coated.
They're in. What texture am I looking for before adding liquid?
Cook them until tender, stirring now and then. The leeks and onion should soften and look relaxed rather than crisp.
They look soft now. Should I pour in all the water at once?
Go ahead and pour the 2 quarts water into the pot, then stir along the bottom to loosen anything flavorful from the vegetables.
The water is in. I still have potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice waiting—do those go in now?
Yes, mix in the potatoes, carrots, asparagus, and rice. Stir everything together so the vegetables and rice are distributed evenly in the soup.
I'd like to make Fried Apple Pies, but I want to get the dough ingredients sorted before I start on the apples.
Set out 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup shortening, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup cold water. Keep the water cold while you get the rest ready.
I've got the flour, shortening, salt, and cold water on the counter. Should I start with the filling or the dough?
Start with the apples so the filling has time to soften. Peel them, then dice them into small pieces so they cook down evenly.
The apples are diced. I have sugar and cinnamon nearby, but the recipe doesn't give amounts.
Add the sugar and cinnamon to the diced apples, using enough to coat them lightly and season the filling. Stir so the spices are spread through the fruit.
They're coated now. What pan should I use for cooking them down?
Use a saucepan and keep the heat low. Add the seasoned apples to the pan and let them cook gently rather than browning quickly.
They're in the saucepan on low heat. How will I know when they're ready to mash?
Cook them until the pieces are soft all the way through. When a fork slides in easily, mash the apples with the fork right in the pan.
The apples are soft and breaking apart. What texture should I stop at?
Mash until the filling looks like a thick applesauce. It should hold together instead of being watery, so keep it on low a little longer if it seems loose.
The filling is thick now. Can I move back to the dough ingredients?
Yes. With the filling ready, use the 2 cups flour, 1/2 cup shortening, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup cold water for the pastry portion of the Fried Apple Pies.
I'm making Frosted Shortbread and have a softened cup of butter on the counter. Can you talk me through it?

Absolutely. You'll also want 1 cup packed brown sugar, 1 egg yolk, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract ready. Since the butter must be real butter with no substitutes, it's good that it's already softened.
Brown sugar is packed and measured, and I separated the egg yolk. What bowl should I use?

Use a mixing bowl with enough room to cream the butter and brown sugar together without spilling. Add the softened butter and packed brown sugar, then beat them until they're well combined and creamy.
It's starting to look smooth, but the sugar is still a little grainy. Is that okay?
Yes, a little texture from the brown sugar is fine. Once the butter and sugar look evenly blended, add the egg yolk and the 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
The yolk and vanilla are in. Should I mix just until they disappear?
Mix them in well so the dough base looks uniform and there aren't streaks of yolk or vanilla pooled anywhere.
That part looks even. I see the recipe mentions flour and salt, but I don't have amounts written down here.
Go by the amounts from your recipe card for the flour and salt. Combine the flour and salt separately first, then add that mixture to the creamed butter mixture.
I've mixed the flour and salt together. Do I dump it all in or add it gradually?
Add it to the creamed mixture and mix until the dough comes together. Stop once it's combined so the shortbread stays tender.
The dough is together now. What pan do I need before I clean up the counter?
Grease a 15-in pan, then press the shortbread dough evenly into it, getting it into the corners and smoothing the surface as best you can.
I'm making Fire Side Coffee and want to mix up the jar first. What should I put on the counter?

Set out 2 cups powdered non-dairy creamer, 1 1/2 cups instant hot chocolate mix, 1 1/2 cups instant coffee granules, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon. You'll also want a sifter or fine-mesh strainer, a mixing bowl, and a jar with a tight lid.
I've got the creamer and hot chocolate mix measured. Should the coffee granules go in as-is?
Yes, use the instant coffee granules as-is. Measure 1 1/2 cups and add them with the creamer and hot chocolate mix so everything can be sifted together evenly.
The cinnamon is ready too. The directions mention nutmeg, but I don't see an amount—what should I do?

Use the 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon called for, and if you want to follow the note about nutmeg, add only a small pinch since no exact amount is given. You can also leave the nutmeg out and still keep the Fire Side Coffee mix on track.
I'm sifting now, but the hot chocolate mix is clumping a little in the strainer.

Press the clumps gently through the strainer with the back of a spoon, then stir the sifted mixture in the bowl so the creamer, hot chocolate mix, instant coffee, cinnamon, and any nutmeg are evenly combined.
The dry mix looks uniform. Do I pack it into the jar or leave it loose?
Spoon or pour it into the jar loosely; don't pack it down. Once it's in, seal the jar with the lid to keep the mix dry and easy to scoop.
I want to make 1 mug now. How much mix should I use?
For 1 cup of hot water, stir in 3 teaspoons of the Fire Side Coffee mixture. Stir until the granules and powders dissolve fully.
It's mixed, but I'm not sure whether it should be stronger or sweeter.
Taste the mug and adjust from there: add a little more mix if you want it richer, or add more hot water if it's too strong. Keep the sealed jar nearby for easy serving later.
I'm making Fresh Apple Salsa and have a cutting board out. Can you talk me through the prep as I go?
Absolutely. Start by getting 2 tart apples ready: core them, cube them, and put the pieces near a large mixing bowl. You'll also need 4 tablespoons lime juice for tossing them right away.
The apples are cubed. Should they go straight into the bowl with all the lime juice?
Yes, add the cubed apples to the large bowl and pour in the 4 tablespoons lime juice. Stir them together so the apple pieces get evenly coated.
They're coated and already smell bright. I've got the peppers next to me—how should I prep them?
Take 1 fresh jalapeno pepper and 1 fresh Anaheim chile. Seed both of them, then slice them before adding them to the bowl.
Do I stir the jalapeno and Anaheim slices in now, or wait until the other mix-ins are ready?
Stir the jalapeno and Anaheim chile slices into the lime-coated apples now. That helps the heat and citrus spread through the salsa.
The peppers are mixed in. The recipe mentions onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt too—do those all go in together?
They do. Stir in the onion, cilantro, walnuts, ginger, and salt together, folding from the bottom of the bowl so the apples and chiles stay evenly distributed.
Everything is in the bowl, but the walnuts are sitting in a few clumps. What texture should I be aiming for?
Mix thoroughly until the walnuts, herbs, onion, ginger, and salt are spread throughout and every scoop has some apple and chile. It should look chunky and evenly combined, not mashed.
That looks right. Any serving suggestion before I bring it to the table?
Serve it fresh while the apples are crisp and the lime is bright. Give it one last gentle stir before spooning it into a serving bowl.
